+/* ps3recomp - the SPU float compares of SPU_X86_RZ_ALWAYS code against the _ref loops.
+ *
+ * Code built with SPU_X86_RZ_ALWAYS runs with MXCSR at round toward zero, flush to zero and
+ * denormals-are-zero, and there spu_fceq/fcgt/fcmeq/fcmgt use the host's own compares (see
+ * spu_helpers.h). This sets that mode, as spu_float_mode_enter does, and checks the four against
+ * the per-lane _ref definitions on every pair of edge values and on random words.
+ *
+ * Build as lifted SPU code is built:  clang -O2 -mavx2 -mfma -ffp-contract=off -DSPU_X86_RZ_ALWAYS=1
+ * Exit status 0 = no mismatch.
+ */
+#include "../spu_helpers.h"
+#include "../../../tests/spu_ls_watch_fixture.h"
+#include <stdio.h>
+#include <stdlib.h>
+#include <string.h>
+
+#ifndef SPU_X86_RZ_ALWAYS
+#error build with -DSPU_X86_RZ_ALWAYS=1: this tests the forms that define selects
+#endif
+
+static uint64_t s_rng = 0xD1B54A32D192ED03ull;
+static uint64_t rnd(void) { s_rng ^= s_rng << 13; s_rng ^= s_rng >> 7; s_rng ^= s_rng << 17; return s_rng; }
+
+static const uint32_t k_edge[] = {
+    0x00000000u, 0x80000000u, 0x00000001u, 0x80000001u, 0x007FFFFFu, 0x807FFFFFu, 0x00400000u,
+    0x00800000u, 0x80800000u, 0x00800001u, 0x80800001u,
+    0x3F800000u, 0xBF800000u, 0x3F800001u, 0xBF800001u, 0x40000000u, 0xC0000000u,
+    0x7F7FFFFFu, 0xFF7FFFFFu, 0x7F000000u, 0xFF000000u,
+    0x7F800000u, 0xFF800000u,                           /* exponent 255, no fraction: the host's infinity */
+    0x7F800001u, 0xFF800001u, 0x7FC00000u, 0xFFC00000u, /* exponent 255 with a fraction: the host's NaN */
+    0x7FFFFFFFu, 0xFFFFFFFFu, 0x7FBFFFFFu, 0xFFA00000u, 0x7FFFFFFEu,
+};
+enum { K_EDGE = sizeof k_edge / sizeof k_edge[0] };
+
+static unsigned long long s_bad, s_runs;
+static int same(u128 a, u128 b) { return a._u64[0] == b._u64[0] && a._u64[1] == b._u64[1]; }
+static void check(const char* op, u128 a, u128 b, u128 want, u128 got) {
+    s_runs++;
+    if (same(want, got)) return;
+    if (s_bad++ < 12)
+        printf("MISMATCH %s a=%08X %08X %08X %08X b=%08X %08X %08X %08X ref=%08X %08X %08X %08X got=%08X %08X %08X %08X\n", op,
+               a._u32[0], a._u32[1], a._u32[2], a._u32[3], b._u32[0], b._u32[1], b._u32[2], b._u32[3],
+               want._u32[0], want._u32[1], want._u32[2], want._u32[3], got._u32[0], got._u32[1], got._u32[2], got._u32[3]);
+}
+static void all4(u128 a, u128 b) {
+    check("fceq",  a, b, spu_fceq_ref(a, b),  spu_fceq(a, b));
+    check("fcgt",  a, b, spu_fcgt_ref(a, b),  spu_fcgt(a, b));
+    check("fcmeq", a, b, spu_fcmeq_ref(a, b), spu_fcmeq(a, b));
+    check("fcmgt", a, b, spu_fcmgt_ref(a, b), spu_fcmgt(a, b));
+}
+
+int main(int argc, char** argv)
+{
+    const long n = argc > 1 ? atol(argv[1]) : 4000000;
+    _mm_setcsr((_mm_getcsr() & ~0xE040u) | SPU_MXCSR_RZFZ);
+    /* every pair of edge values, in every lane, beside ordinary and beside edge neighbours */
+    for (int i = 0; i < K_EDGE; i++)
+        for (int j = 0; j < K_EDGE; j++)
+            for (int lane = 0; lane < 4; lane++) {
+                u128 a, b;
+                for (int k = 0; k < 4; k++) { a._u32[k] = 0x3F800000u + (uint32_t)k; b._u32[k] = 0x40000000u; }
+                a._u32[lane] = k_edge[i]; b._u32[lane] = k_edge[j];
+                all4(a, b);
+                for (int k = 0; k < 4; k++) { a._u32[k] = k_edge[(i + k) % K_EDGE]; b._u32[k] = k_edge[(j + 3 * k) % K_EDGE]; }
+                all4(a, b);
+            }
+    for (long it = 0; it < n; it++) {
+        u128 a, b;
+        for (int k = 0; k < 4; k++) {
+            const uint32_t ra = (uint32_t)rnd(), rb = (uint32_t)rnd();
+            const int m = (int)(rnd() & 7);
+            a._u32[k] = (m == 0) ? k_edge[rnd() % K_EDGE] : ra;
+            b._u32[k] = (m == 1) ? k_edge[rnd() % K_EDGE] : (m == 2) ? a._u32[k] : (m == 3) ? (a._u32[k] ^ 0x80000000u)
+                      : (m == 4) ? (a._u32[k] + 1u) : rb;
+        }
+        all4(a, b);
+    }
+    printf("%llu checks, %llu mismatches\n", s_runs, s_bad);
+    return s_bad ? 1 : 0;
+}

+/* An aligned load or store is one atomic access (single-copy atomic, as on Cell), an unaligned

+#if defined(__x86_64__) || defined(_M_X64)

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Register cache
+#
+# Every guest load and store has an out-of-line slow path, and the compiler must
+# assume that call can change *ctx: so each ctx->gpr[n] read after a guest memory
+# access is a reload, and each write a store. In a loop that is most of the code.
+# _reg_cache keeps the GPRs, FPRs, CR, XER, LR and CTR in C locals instead. Their
+# address never escapes, so the compiler holds them in host registers across
+# guest memory accesses. *ctx is brought up to date only where something else
+# can look at it:
+#   - a line that passes ctx anywhere (a call, the trampoline drain, a syscall,
+#     an HLE call, a header helper taking ctx) stays exactly as lifted, working
+#     on ctx; the locals that may differ from ctx are written back before it and
+#     every local is reloaded after it (the compiler drops reloads nobody reads);
+#   - a return writes the locals back first.
+# Which locals may differ from ctx at a line is a forward dataflow over the
+# body's labels and gotos. It may include more than needed, which costs a store,
+# never correctness. Off unless PPU_REG_CACHE=1 at lift time: on Windows it made the generated C 43%
+# larger and the build 44% longer with no gain we could measure, so it is opt-in.
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+_RC_FIELD_RE = re.compile(r"ctx->(?:(gpr|fpr)\[(\d+)\]|(cr|xer|lr|ctr)\b)")
+_RC_ESCAPE_RE = re.compile(r"\bctx\b(?!->)")
+_RC_LABEL_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*(\w+):\s*$")
+_RC_GOTO_RE = re.compile(r"\bgoto\s+(\w+)\s*;")
+_RC_RETURN_RE = re.compile(r"\breturn\s*;")
+_RC_MIN_LINES = 16   # small bodies gain little, and setjmp_patch.py matches TOC stubs by shape
+
+
+def _rc_local(m) -> str:
+    if m.group(1):
+        return ("_g" if m.group(1) == "gpr" else "_fp") + m.group(2)
+    return "_c_" + m.group(3)
+
+
+def _rc_field(local: str) -> str:
+    if local.startswith("_g"):
+        return f"ctx->gpr[{local[2:]}]"
+    if local.startswith("_fp"):
+        return f"ctx->fpr[{local[3:]}]"
+    return "ctx->" + local[3:]
+
+
+def _rc_sort_key(local: str):
+    if local.startswith("_g"):
+        return (0, int(local[2:]))
+    if local.startswith("_fp"):
+        return (1, int(local[3:]))
+    return (2, local)
+
+
+def _rc_writes(text: str, locals_: set) -> set:
+    """Locals the (cache-form) line may assign or hand out the address of."""
+    out = set()
+    for loc in locals_:
+        if loc not in text:
+            continue
+        e = re.escape(loc)
+        if (re.search(r"\b" + e + r"\b\s*(?:<<|>>|[-+*/%&|^])?=(?!=)", text)
+                or re.search(r"&\s*" + e + r"\b", text)
+                or re.search(r"\b" + e + r"\b\s*(?:\+\+|--)", text)
+                or re.search(r"(?:\+\+|--)\s*" + e + r"\b", text)):
+            out.add(loc)
+    return out
+
+
+def _reg_cache(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]:
+    """Cache the scalar register file in locals (see above). `lines` is a body as
+    _function_def_lines emits it, without the PPU_MM_SNAP line or the closing brace.
+    Returns it unchanged when the pass does not apply."""
+    if os.environ.get("PPU_REG_CACHE") != "1" or len(lines) < _RC_MIN_LINES:
+        return lines
+    if re.search(r"ctx->(?:gpr|fpr)\[(?!\d+\])", "\n".join(lines)):
+        return lines   # an index the pass cannot name a local for
+    locals_ = set()
+    for l in lines:
+        for m in _RC_FIELD_RE.finditer(l):
+            locals_.add(_rc_local(m))
+    if not locals_:
+        return lines
+
+    n = len(lines)
+    cache = [_RC_FIELD_RE.sub(_rc_local, l) for l in lines]
+    verbatim = [bool(_RC_ESCAPE_RE.search(c)) for c in cache]
+    writes = [set() if verbatim[i] else _rc_writes(cache[i], locals_) for i in range(n)]
+    labels = {}
+    for i, l in enumerate(lines):
+        m = _RC_LABEL_RE.match(l)
+        if m:
+            labels[m.group(1)] = i
+    gotos = [[labels[t] for t in _RC_GOTO_RE.findall(l) if t in labels] for l in lines]
+    for i, l in enumerate(lines):
+        if any(t not in labels for t in _RC_GOTO_RE.findall(l)):
+            return lines   # a goto the pass cannot follow
+        # A line kept as lifted must leave the locals valid on every goto out of it:
+        # it may not write a field, and its calls must not fall through to a goto.
+        # The jump-table switch qualifies (its call is `default: ...; return;`).
+        if verbatim[i] and gotos[i]:
+            if _rc_writes(cache[i], locals_) or not l.strip().startswith("switch ("):
+                return lines
+
+    # Forward dataflow: which locals may differ from ctx on entry to each line.
+    dirty_in = [None] * n
+    dirty_in[0] = frozenset()
+    work = [0]
+    while work:
+        i = work.pop()
+        d = dirty_in[i]
+        out = frozenset() if verbatim[i] else d | writes[i]
+        succ = list(gotos[i])
+        s = lines[i].strip()
+        if i + 1 < n and s != "return;" and not re.fullmatch(r"goto\s+\w+\s*;", s):
+            succ.append(i + 1)
+        for j in succ:
+            nd = out if dirty_in[j] is None else dirty_in[j] | out
+            if nd != dirty_in[j]:
+                dirty_in[j] = nd
+                work.append(j)
+
+    def flush(ds) -> str:
+        return " ".join(f"{_rc_field(x)} = {x};" for x in sorted(ds, key=_rc_sort_key))
+
+    reload_all = " ".join(f"{x} = {_rc_field(x)};" for x in sorted(locals_, key=_rc_sort_key))
+    out_lines = [f"    auto {x} = {_rc_field(x)};" for x in sorted(locals_, key=_rc_sort_key)]
+    end_dirty = frozenset()
+    for i in range(n):
+        d = dirty_in[i]
+        if d is None:   # unreachable: leave it as lifted, in cache form
+            out_lines.append(cache[i] if not verbatim[i] else lines[i])
+            continue
+        if verbatim[i]:
+            if d:
+                out_lines.append(f"    {{ {flush(d)} }}  /* reg cache: write back */")
+            out_lines.append(lines[i])
+            out_lines.append(f"    {{ {reload_all} }}  /* reg cache: reload */")
+            end_dirty = frozenset()
+            continue
+        c = cache[i]
+        if _RC_RETURN_RE.search(c):
+            ds = d | writes[i]
+            if ds:
+                c = _RC_RETURN_RE.sub(lambda _m: f"{{ {flush(ds)} return; }}", c)
+        out_lines.append(c)
+        end_dirty = d | writes[i]
+    # Falling off the end of the body returns too.
+    s = lines[-1].strip()
+    if end_dirty and s != "return;" and not re.fullmatch(r"goto\s+\w+\s*;", s):
+        out_lines.append(f"    {{ {flush(end_dirty)} }}  /* reg cache: write back at exit */")
+    return out_lines

+def _const_value(insns, at, reg, depth=0):
+    """The constant `reg` holds right after instruction `at`, when its definition chain
+    is lis/li/addi/ori from immediates within `insns` (in address order); else None."""
+    def imm(s):
+        try:
+            return int(s.strip(), 0)
+        except ValueError:
+            return None

+    if not a or a[0] != reg or depth > 4:
+        return None

+    if m in ('lis', 'li') and len(a) == 2:
+        v = imm(a[1])
+        if v is None:

+                prev = w
+                break
+        if prev is None:
+            return None
+        base = _const_value(insns, prev, src, depth + 1)
+        if base is None:

+        return ((base + v) if m == 'addi' else (base | (v & 0xFFFF))) & 0xFFFFFFFF

+/*
+ * rsx_upscale.c - finds and starts the vendor back ends (gt5_upscale.h), Direct3D 12: the temporal
+ * upscaler and the frame generators.
+ *
+ * Each is an optional plug-in looked for next to the executable:
+ *   gt5_upscale_dlss.dll  NVIDIA DLSS (the upscaler) and DLSS Frame Generation; built on the player's PC
+ *                         by scripts\add_dlss.ps1 against NVIDIA's SDK
+ *   gt5_upscale_fsr.dll   AMD FSR 3 frame generation; built by scripts\add_fsr.ps1 against AMD's SDK
+ * Neither SDK is part of this project. A plug-in that is not there, not loadable, or not usable on this
+ * graphics card: the renderer carries on as it is and the menu's choices for it stay greyed out, with
+ * the reason (rsx_upscale_caps, rsx_fg_method_available) and a line in the log.
+ *
+ * A plug-in of interface version 1 (DLSS from before frame generation) still loads: it has no fg_ calls.
+ *
+ * rsx_upscale_load and rsx_upscale_unload run on the renderer's thread; what the load found does not
+ * change afterwards, so the questions (caps, available) may be asked from any thread.
+ */
+#ifdef _WIN32
+#include <stdio.h>
+#include <string.h>
+#include <windows.h>
+#include <d3d12.h>
+
+#include "gt5_upscale.h"
+#include "rsx_upscale.h"
+
+enum { PLUG_DLSS = 0, PLUG_FSR = 1, PLUG_COUNT = 2 };
+typedef struct {
+    const char*  method;           /* the frame generator's name in LD_FRAMEGEN */
+    const wchar_t* file;
+    const char*  what;             /* for the log */
+    const char*  get_it;           /* the launcher's button */
+    HMODULE      mod;
+    const gt5_upscale_api* api;    /* loaded and started */
+    gt5_upscale_caps caps;         /* its upscaler */
+    gt5_fg_caps  fg;               /* its frame generator */
+} plug_t;
+static plug_t s_plug[PLUG_COUNT] = {
+    { "dlss", L"gt5_upscale_dlss.dll", "the DLSS plug-in", "Get NVIDIA DLSS", NULL, NULL, {0}, {0} },
+    { "fsr",  L"gt5_upscale_fsr.dll",  "the FSR plug-in",  "Get AMD FSR 3",   NULL, NULL, {0}, {0} },
+};
+static int s_tried;
+static volatile LONG s_done;       /* the load has finished: the answers below are final */
+static gt5_fg_caps s_no_caps;
+
+/* The folder of the executable, with a trailing backslash. */
+static int exe_dir(wchar_t* out, size_t cap)
+{
+    const DWORD n = GetModuleFileNameW(NULL, out, (DWORD)cap);
+    if (!n || n >= cap) return 0;
+    wchar_t* cut = wcsrchr(out, L'\\');
+    if (!cut) return 0;
+    cut[1] = 0;
+    return 1;
+}
+
+/* One plug-in: found, loaded, started, asked what it can do. */
+static void plug_load(plug_t* p, ID3D12Device* device, const wchar_t* dir, const wchar_t* logs)
+{
+    wchar_t path[MAX_PATH + 40];
+    memset(&p->caps, 0, sizeof p->caps);
+    memset(&p->fg, 0, sizeof p->fg);
+    _snwprintf(path, MAX_PATH + 40, L"%ls%ls", dir, p->file);
+    path[MAX_PATH + 39] = 0;
+    if (GetFileAttributesW(path) == INVALID_FILE_ATTRIBUTES) {
+        fprintf(stderr, "[upscale] no %s next to the game (%ls): the launcher's \"%s\" adds it\n", p->what + 4, p->file, p->get_it);
+        snprintf(p->caps.message, sizeof p->caps.message, "%s is not installed: the launcher's \"%s\" adds it", p->what, p->get_it);
+        snprintf(p->fg.message, sizeof p->fg.message, "not installed: the launcher's \"%s\" adds it", p->get_it);
+        return;
+    }
+    /* The plug-in's own neighbours (the vendor's DLLs) are found beside it. */
+    p->mod = LoadLibraryExW(path, NULL, LOAD_WITH_ALTERED_SEARCH_PATH);
+    if (!p->mod) {
+        const DWORD e = GetLastError();
+        fprintf(stderr, "[upscale] %s could not be loaded (error %lu)\n", p->what, e);
+        snprintf(p->caps.message, sizeof p->caps.message, "%s could not be loaded (Windows error %lu)", p->what, e);
+        snprintf(p->fg.message, sizeof p->fg.message, "%s", p->caps.message);
+        return;
+    }
+    gt5_upscale_get_fn get = (gt5_upscale_get_fn)(void*)GetProcAddress(p->mod, GT5_UPSCALE_GET_NAME);
+    const gt5_upscale_api* api = get ? get() : NULL;
+    if (!api || api->api_version < GT5_UPSCALE_API_VERSION_MIN || api->api_version > GT5_UPSCALE_API_VERSION || !api->init) {
+        fprintf(stderr, "[upscale] %s is from another version of the game (interface %u, wanted %u to %u): "
+                        "run \"%s\" again\n", p->what, api ? api->api_version : 0u, GT5_UPSCALE_API_VERSION_MIN,
+                GT5_UPSCALE_API_VERSION, p->get_it);
+        snprintf(p->caps.message, sizeof p->caps.message, "%s is from another version of the game: run \"%s\" in the launcher again",
+                 p->what, p->get_it);
+        snprintf(p->fg.message, sizeof p->fg.message, "%s", p->caps.message);
+        FreeLibrary(p->mod); p->mod = NULL;
+        return;
+    }
+    if (!api->init(device, logs, &p->caps)) {
+        fprintf(stderr, "[upscale] %s could not start: %s\n", p->caps.name[0] ? p->caps.name : p->what,
+                p->caps.message[0] ? p->caps.message : api->last_error ? api->last_error() : "");
+        if (!p->caps.message[0]) snprintf(p->caps.message, sizeof p->caps.message, "%s could not start", p->what);
+        snprintf(p->fg.message, sizeof p->fg.message, "%s", p->caps.message);
+        p->caps.available = 0;
+        FreeLibrary(p->mod); p->mod = NULL;
+        return;
+    }
+    p->api = api;
+    /* its upscaler (a plug-in may have none: the calls are NULL) */
+    if (!api->optimal || !api->create || !api->evaluate || !api->destroy) p->caps.available = 0;
+    if (p->caps.available)
+        fprintf(stderr, "[upscale] %s is available on this graphics card\n", p->caps.name);
+    else if (api->create)
+        fprintf(stderr, "[upscale] %s is not available here: %s\n", p->caps.name, p->caps.message);
+    /* its frame generator (interface version 2) */
+    if (api->api_version < 2u) {
+        snprintf(p->fg.message, sizeof p->fg.message, "%s is from before frame generation: run \"%s\" in the launcher again",
+                 p->what, p->get_it);
+        fprintf(stderr, "[upscale] %s has no frame generation (interface version %u): \"%s\" in the launcher rebuilds it\n",
+                p->what, api->api_version, p->get_it);
+        return;
+    }
+    if (!api->fg_caps || !api->fg_create || !api->fg_evaluate || !api->fg_destroy || !api->fg_state || !api->last_error) {
+        snprintf(p->fg.message, sizeof p->fg.message, "%s has no frame generation", p->what);
+        return;
+    }
+    if (!api->fg_caps(&p->fg)) {
+        memset(&p->fg, 0, sizeof p->fg);
+        snprintf(p->fg.message, sizeof p->fg.message, "%s did not say whether it can make frames", p->what);
+    }
+    if (p->fg.available && p->fg.max_generated < 1u) p->fg.max_generated = 1u;
+    if (p->fg.available)
+        fprintf(stderr, "[framegen] %s%s%s is available on this graphics card (up to %u made frame%s for each drawn one)\n",
+                p->fg.name, p->fg.version[0] ? " " : "", p->fg.version, p->fg.max_generated, p->fg.max_generated == 1u ? "" : "s");
+    else
+        fprintf(stderr, "[framegen] %s is not available here: %s\n", p->fg.name[0] ? p->fg.name : p->what, p->fg.message);
+}
+
+int rsx_upscale_load(ID3D12Device* device)
+{
+    if (s_tried) return s_plug[PLUG_DLSS].api != NULL && s_plug[PLUG_DLSS].caps.available;
+    s_tried = 1;
+    wchar_t dir[MAX_PATH];
+    if (device && exe_dir(dir, MAX_PATH)) {
+        /* The back ends want a folder they may write to: the game's logs folder (..\logs from the executable). */
+        wchar_t logs[MAX_PATH + 16];
+        _snwprintf(logs, MAX_PATH + 16, L"%ls..\\logs", dir);
+        logs[MAX_PATH + 15] = 0;
+        CreateDirectoryW(logs, NULL);
+        for (int i = 0; i < PLUG_COUNT; i++) plug_load(&s_plug[i], device, dir, logs);
+    } else {
+        for (int i = 0; i < PLUG_COUNT; i++) {
+            snprintf(s_plug[i].caps.message, sizeof s_plug[i].caps.message, "no Direct3D 12 device");
+            snprintf(s_plug[i].fg.message, sizeof s_plug[i].fg.message, "no Direct3D 12 device");
+        }
+    }
+    InterlockedExchange(&s_done, 1);
+    return s_plug[PLUG_DLSS].api != NULL && s_plug[PLUG_DLSS].caps.available;
+}
+
+const gt5_upscale_api* rsx_upscale_api(void)
+{
+    return s_plug[PLUG_DLSS].api && s_plug[PLUG_DLSS].caps.available ? s_plug[PLUG_DLSS].api : NULL;
+}
+const gt5_upscale_caps* rsx_upscale_caps(void) { return &s_plug[PLUG_DLSS].caps; }
+
+static plug_t* plug_of(const char* method)
+{
+    if (!method) return NULL;
+    for (int i = 0; i < PLUG_COUNT; i++)
+        if (!_stricmp(method, s_plug[i].method)) return &s_plug[i];
+    return NULL;
+}
+
+const gt5_upscale_api* rsx_fg_provider(const char* method)
+{
+    const plug_t* p = plug_of(method);
+    return p && s_done && p->api && p->fg.available ? p->api : NULL;
+}
+
+const gt5_fg_caps* rsx_fg_provider_caps(const char* method)
+{
+    const plug_t* p = plug_of(method);
+    return p && s_done ? &p->fg : &s_no_caps;
+}
+
+int rsx_fg_method_available(const char* method, char* why, unsigned why_size)
+{
+    const plug_t* p = plug_of(method);
+    if (why && why_size) why[0] = 0;
+    if (!p) { if (why && why_size) snprintf(why, why_size, "not a frame generator of this version"); return 0; }
+    if (!s_done) { if (why && why_size) snprintf(why, why_size, "not looked for yet"); return 0; }
+    if (p->api && p->fg.available) return 1;
+    if (why && why_size) snprintf(why, why_size, "%s", p->fg.message[0] ? p->fg.message : "not available");
+    return 0;
+}
+
+void rsx_upscale_unload(ID3D12Device* device)
+{
+    InterlockedExchange(&s_done, 0);
+    for (int i = 0; i < PLUG_COUNT; i++) {
+        if (s_plug[i].api && s_plug[i].api->shutdown) s_plug[i].api->shutdown(device);
+        s_plug[i].api = NULL;
+        memset(&s_plug[i].caps, 0, sizeof s_plug[i].caps);
+        memset(&s_plug[i].fg, 0, sizeof s_plug[i].fg);
+        /* The DLLs stay loaded: NGX keeps threads of its own for a moment after shutdown. */
+    }
+}
+#endif /* _WIN32 */

+ * answer the same without trying again. */

+int rsx_fg_method_available(const char* method, char* why, unsigned why_size);
+
+#ifdef __cplusplus
+}
+#endif
+#endif /* _WIN32 */
+#endif /* RSX_UPSCALE_H */

+/* Windows: cellAudio's real mixing thread and device thread on the real default output device, with
+ * the real event queues (sys_event.c) and a stand-in for GT5's sound tick thread -- no game needed.
+ *
+ *   test_audio_device [seconds] [--tone] [--stall-at <s> --stall-ms <ms>] [--switch-every <s>]
+ *
+ * It opens cellAudio as GT5 does (Init, an 8-channel port of 16 blocks, its own notify queue), and its
+ * "tick thread" is func_00C0E35C's loop: receive with a 1 s timeout, write the next block on each tick,
+ * and on any error remove the queue and end, as GT5 does. Every second it prints the ticks, the longest
+ * gap between two, and the device in use. It plays silence unless --tone (a quiet 440 Hz tone).
+ *  - Switch the Windows default output device, disable or unplug the one in use, plug a headset in:
+ *    the log says "[cellAudio] sound device now ..." / "lost" / "back", the ticks go on, and the
+ *    longest gap stays small (a few ms; the switch itself never holds the ticks up).
+ *  - AUDIO_FOLLOW_TEST=<s>: every <s> seconds the device is dropped as if lost and reopened <s>/2 later.
+ *  - --switch-every <s>: every <s> seconds a default-device change is announced as Windows would, with
+ *    the device playing marked as another one, so the default (the same device) is opened and swapped
+ *    in while the old one plays out: the hand-over between two working devices.
+ *  - --stall-at 3 --stall-ms 1500: the mixing thread is held 1.5 s (its lock taken), as a stall of the
+ *    PC did. With AUDIO_TICK_GUARD=0 the tick thread times out and removes its queue (GT5's one-second
+ *    bursts); with the guard it waits on and the ticks resume.
+ * Exit code 0 when the tick thread is still running at the end, 1 when it ended.
+ *
+ * Build (from ps3recomp, an x64 Native Tools prompt; clang-cl or cl):
+ *   clang-cl /std:c17 /O2 /D_CRT_SECURE_NO_WARNINGS /I include /I runtime/settings
+ *     libs/audio/tests/test_audio_device.c runtime/syscalls/sys_event.c runtime/settings/gt5_settings.c
+ *     ole32.lib user32.lib /Fe:test_audio_device.exe
+ */
+#include "../cellAudio.c"
+#include <assert.h>
+
+int64_t sys_event_queue_receive(ppu_context* ctx);   /* runtime/syscalls/sys_event.c */
+
+/* ---- what the rest of the runtime would provide ---- */
+uint8_t* vm_base;
+uint32_t ppu_vm_size;
+uint32_t ppu_hle_inject_base;
+int g_resv_store_active;
+uint32_t g_ww_lo, g_ww_hi;
+void ppu_resv_break_store(uint64_t ea) { (void)ea; }
+void ps3_ww_report_inline(uint32_t a, uint64_t v, int w) { (void)a; (void)v; (void)w; }
+int spu_coh_is_reserved(uint32_t a) { (void)a; return 0; }
+void spu_coh_notify_write(uint32_t a) { (void)a; }
+void spu_coh_notify_write_ppu(uint32_t a) { (void)a; }
+void spu_coh_ppu_after(uint32_t a) { (void)a; }
+void spu_lockline_lock(void) {}
+void spu_lockline_unlock(void) {}
+int ps3_ab_on(const char* what) { (void)what; return -1; }
+void ps3_hle_register_ctx(uint32_t nid, const char* name, void (*fn)(ppu_context*)) { (void)nid; (void)name; (void)fn; }
+/* sys_event.c's neighbours, none of them on the paths used here */
+void ppu_thread_note_block(uint64_t tid) { (void)tid; }
+void ydkj_release_pending_threads(void) {}
+int spu_dispatch_frame_by_queue(uint32_t q, uint32_t f) { (void)q; (void)f; return 0; }
+int ps3_log_verbose(void) { return 0; }
+void ppu_dump_guest_stack(ppu_context* c, const char* t) { (void)c; (void)t; }
+size_t spu_elf_image_size(const uint8_t* image, size_t max_avail) { (void)image; (void)max_avail; return 0; }
+int spu_workload_dispatch_async(const uint8_t* image, uint32_t size, uint32_t arg) { (void)image; (void)size; (void)arg; return 0; }
+uint32_t g_spu_pending_evt[3];
+int g_spu_pending_evt_valid;
+int64_t lv2_usec_deadline(uint64_t usec) { (void)usec; return 0; }
+int lv2_deadline_passed(int64_t deadline) { (void)deadline; return 1; }
+
+static const uint64_t kKey = 0x48DA6C685BCC82DULL;   /* GT5's tick queue key */
+static uint32_t s_q, s_port;
+static volatile LONG s_ticks, s_tick_thread_alive = 1, s_stalling, s_stall_over;
+static volatile LONGLONG s_last_tick_us, s_gap_max_us, s_gap_max_all_us;
+static int s_tone;
+
+static void put_be_f32(uint32_t ea, float f)
+{
+    uint32_t v; memcpy(&v, &f, 4);
+    vm_write32(ea, v);
+}
+
+/* The next block of the ring, in order, as GT5's writer does. */
+static void write_block(uint64_t n)
+{
+    static double phase;
+    const AudioPortSlot* p = &s_ports[s_port];
+    const uint32_t base = (uint32_t)p->port_addr + (uint32_t)(n % 16) * CELL_AUDIO_BLOCK_SAMPLES * 8 * 4;
+    for (uint32_t s = 0; s < CELL_AUDIO_BLOCK_SAMPLES; s++) {
+        const float v = s_tone ? (float)(0.05 * sin(phase)) : 1e-9f;   /* never all zero: a real writer */
+        phase += 2.0 * 3.14159265358979 * 440.0 / 48000.0;
+        for (uint32_t c = 0; c < 8; c++) put_be_f32(base + (s * 8 + c) * 4, c < 2 ? v : 0.0f);
+    }
+}
+
+/* GT5's tick thread (func_00C0E35C), with the block writer as its one listener. */
+static unsigned __stdcall tick_thread(void* arg)
+{
+    (void)arg;
+    ppu_context* ctx = (ppu_context*)calloc(1, sizeof *ctx);
+    uint64_t written = 2;
+    cellAudioSetNotifyEventQueue(kKey);
+    for (;;) {
+        ctx->gpr[3] = s_q; ctx->gpr[4] = 0; ctx->gpr[5] = 1000000;   /* 1 s, as GT5 */
+        const int64_t rc = sys_event_queue_receive(ctx);
+        if (rc != 0) {
+            printf("[test] tick thread: receive returned 0x%llX: removing its queue and ending, as GT5 does\n",
+                   (unsigned long long)rc);
+            cellAudioRemoveNotifyEventQueue(kKey);
+            break;
+        }
+        const LONGLONG now = (LONGLONG)audio_now_us();
+        if (s_last_tick_us) {
+            const LONGLONG gap = now - s_last_tick_us;
+            if (gap > s_gap_max_us) s_gap_max_us = gap;
+            const int held = InterlockedExchange(&s_stall_over, 0) || s_stalling;   /* the held stretch's gap */
+            if (gap > s_gap_max_all_us && !held) s_gap_max_all_us = gap;
+        }
+        s_last_tick_us = now;
+        InterlockedIncrement(&s_ticks);
+        write_block(written++);
+    }
+    InterlockedExchange(&s_tick_thread_alive, 0);
+    free(ctx);
+    return 0;
+}
+
+/* audio_apply_volume on its own: the curve, the glide, the registry change. */
+static void volume_unit_test(void)
+{
+    static float b[CELL_AUDIO_BLOCK_SAMPLES * 2];
+    const int last_i = CELL_AUDIO_BLOCK_SAMPLES * 2 - 1;
+    const float* o = b;
+    float last = 1.0f;
+    for (int i = 0; i <= last_i; i++) b[i] = 1.0f;
+    gt5_setting_set("GT5_VOLUME", "50");
+    for (int k = 0; k < 12; k++) {
+        o = audio_apply_volume(b, CELL_AUDIO_BLOCK_SAMPLES);
+        assert(last - o[last_i] <= 0.2001f);                  /* glides: at most 0.2 a block */
+        last = o[last_i];
+    }
+    assert(fabsf(last - 0.25f) < 1e-4f);                      /* 50 -> 0.25 (-12 dB) */
+    assert(b[last_i] == 1.0f);                                /* the mix itself untouched */
+    gt5_setting_set("GT5_VOLUME", "0");
+    for (int k = 0; k < 12; k++) o = audio_apply_volume(b, CELL_AUDIO_BLOCK_SAMPLES);
+    assert(o[last_i] == 0.0f);
+    gt5_setting_set("GT5_VOLUME", "");                        /* back to 100 (not set) */
+    for (int k = 0; k < 12; k++) o = audio_apply_volume(b, CELL_AUDIO_BLOCK_SAMPLES);
+    assert(o == b);                                           /* full volume: the mix as it is */
+    printf("[test] volume: 50 -> 0.25 with a glide of at most 0.2 a block, 0 -> silence, unset -> the mix itself: passed\n");
+    /* This program has no window, so with "mute when in the background" on it is always behind one. */
+    if (audio_window_in_front() == 0) {
+        gt5_setting_set("GT5_MUTE_BACKGROUND", "1");
+        for (int k = 0; k < 12; k++) o = audio_apply_volume(b, CELL_AUDIO_BLOCK_SAMPLES);
+        assert(o[last_i] == 0.0f);
+        gt5_setting_set("GT5_MUTE_BACKGROUND", "");
+        for (int k = 0; k < 12; k++) o = audio_apply_volume(b, CELL_AUDIO_BLOCK_SAMPLES);
+        assert(o == b);
+        printf("[test] mute when in the background: muted behind another window, back when off: passed\n");
+    } else {
+        printf("[test] mute when in the background: not tested (no foreground window to be behind)\n");
+    }
+}
+
+int main(int argc, char** argv)
+{
+    int seconds = 20, stall_at = 0, stall_ms = 0, switch_every = 0;
+    for (int i = 1; i < argc; i++) {
+        if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--tone")) s_tone = 1;
+        else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--switch-every") && i + 1 < argc) switch_every = atoi(argv[++i]);
+        else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--stall-at") && i + 1 < argc) stall_at = atoi(argv[++i]);
+        else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--stall-ms") && i + 1 < argc) stall_ms = atoi(argv[++i]);
+        else seconds = atoi(argv[i]);
+    }
+    if (!s_tone) _putenv("PS3_MUTE=1");      /* silence at the device unless asked for the tone */
+    if (!getenv("PS3_VERBOSE")) _putenv("PS3_VERBOSE=0");   /* no line per event wait */
+    setvbuf(stdout, NULL, _IONBF, 0);
+    setvbuf(stderr, NULL, _IONBF, 0);
+    if (vm_init() != 0) { printf("vm_init failed\n"); return 2; }
+    gt5_settings_init(NULL);
+    volume_unit_test();
+
+    assert(cellAudioInit() == CELL_OK);
+    s_q = sys_event_queue_create_direct(kKey, 8);
+    assert(s_q);
+    vm_write64(0x20000, 8);    /* nChannel */
+    vm_write64(0x20008, 16);   /* nBlock */
+    assert(cellAudioPortOpen((void*)(uintptr_t)0x20000, (void*)(uintptr_t)0x20100) == CELL_OK);
+    s_port = vm_read32(0x20100);
+    write_block(0); write_block(1);         /* two ahead, as GT5 starts */
+    HANDLE th = (HANDLE)_beginthreadex(NULL, 0, tick_thread, NULL, 0, NULL);
+    while (!s_notify_queues[0].in_use) Sleep(1);
+    assert(cellAudioPortStart(s_port) == CELL_OK);
+
+    LONG last_ticks = 0;
+    u64 last_us = audio_now_us();
+    for (int t = 1; t <= seconds; t++) {
+        if (stall_ms && t == stall_at) {
+            printf("[test] holding the mixing thread %d ms\n", stall_ms);
+            InterlockedExchange(&s_stalling, 1);
+            mutex_lock(&s_audio_mutex);
+            Sleep((DWORD)stall_ms);
+            InterlockedExchange(&s_stall_over, 1);   /* the next gap is the held stretch's */
+            mutex_unlock(&s_audio_mutex);
+            InterlockedExchange(&s_stalling, 0);
+            t += stall_ms / 1000;
+        } else {
+            Sleep(1000);
+        }
+        if (switch_every && t % switch_every == 0) {
+            /* As if Windows' default had moved to another device: the device thread sees a default that
+             * isn't the one playing and opens it (here the same device again), the mixing thread swaps. */
+            lstrcpynW(s_dev_playing, L"(another device)", 256);
+            s_nc.lpVtbl->OnDefaultDeviceChanged(&s_nc, eRender, eConsole, NULL);
+        }
+        const LONG ticks = s_ticks;
+        const u64 now_us = audio_now_us();
+        const audio_dev* d = s_dev;
+        printf("[test] %2d s: %6.1f ticks/s (187.5 is real time), longest gap %5.1f ms, device %s, tick thread %s\n",
+               t, (ticks - last_ticks) * 1e6 / (double)(now_us - last_us),
+               (double)InterlockedExchange64(&s_gap_max_us, 0) / 1000.0,
+               d ? d->name : "(none: clock)", s_tick_thread_alive ? "running" : "ENDED");
+        last_ticks = ticks;
+        last_us = now_us;
+    }
+    const int alive = s_tick_thread_alive;
+    printf("[test] longest gap between ticks outside the held stretch: %.1f ms; tick thread %s\n",
+           (double)s_gap_max_all_us / 1000.0, alive ? "still running" : "ended");
+    cellAudioQuit();
+    (void)th;
+    return alive ? 0 : 1;
+}

diff --git a/libs/hardware/wheel.h b/libs/hardware/wheel.h

+/*
+ * ps3recomp - steering wheel emulation (Logitech G27 on cellUsbd)
+ *
+ * Gran Turismo 5 and 6 drive their Logitech wheels themselves: the game
+ * registers a USB device driver with cellUsbd, reads the wheel's HID reports
+ * off its interrupt IN endpoint and writes Logitech force-feedback commands to
+ * its interrupt OUT endpoint. cellUsbd.c presents one emulated G27 to the
+ * game; this header joins it to the two halves behind it:
+ *
+ *   wheel_g27.c       the G27 itself: USB descriptors, the 11-byte input
+ *                     report, and the force-feedback command decoder, which
+ *                     keeps four effect slots plus the default spring.
+ *   wheel_host_win.c  the PC wheel: DirectInput (Windows), polled on a thread
+ *                     of its own, whose effects follow the decoder's slots. Or
+ *                     the mouse, in races (PS3_MOUSE_STEER=1).
+ *
+ * Everything is off unless a wheel is found on the host (PS3_WHEEL=off turns
+ * it off even then) or mouse steering is on, so a player with a pad sees no
+ * change.
+ */
+#ifndef PS3RECOMP_WHEEL_H
+#define PS3RECOMP_WHEEL_H
+
+#include "ps3emu/ps3types.h"
+
+#ifdef __cplusplus
+extern "C" {
+#endif
+
+/* G27 buttons, by the PS3 function each one has (bit = 1 << index). The order
+ * is the G27's own report order, which a G29/G923 also uses for DirectInput
+ * button numbers 0-22, so "host button i -> WHEEL_BTN i" is the default map. */
+enum {
+    WHEEL_BTN_CROSS = 0, WHEEL_BTN_SQUARE, WHEEL_BTN_CIRCLE, WHEEL_BTN_TRIANGLE,
+    WHEEL_BTN_R1, WHEEL_BTN_L1, WHEEL_BTN_R2, WHEEL_BTN_L2,
+    WHEEL_BTN_SELECT, WHEEL_BTN_START, WHEEL_BTN_R3, WHEEL_BTN_L3,
+    WHEEL_BTN_GEAR1, WHEEL_BTN_GEAR2, WHEEL_BTN_GEAR3, WHEEL_BTN_GEAR4,
+    WHEEL_BTN_GEAR5, WHEEL_BTN_GEAR6, WHEEL_BTN_GEAR_R,
+    WHEEL_BTN_PLUS, WHEEL_BTN_MINUS, WHEEL_BTN_DIAL_CW, WHEEL_BTN_DIAL_CCW,
+    WHEEL_BTN_COUNT
+};
+
+typedef struct WheelInput {
+    int   connected;
+    float steer;        /* -1 (full left) .. +1 (full right) over the host wheel's range */
+    float throttle;     /* 0 released .. 1 floored */
+    float brake;
+    float clutch;
+    int   hat;          /* 0 = up, 1 = up-right ... 7 = up-left, -1 = centred */
+    u32   buttons;      /* 1 << WHEEL_BTN_* */
+    int   shifter;      /* an H-shifter is attached (or PS3_WHEEL_SHIFTER=1) */
+    int   steer_g27;    /* steer is the G27's own position, not a PC wheel's (mouse steering) */
+} WheelInput;
+
+/* ---- the force-feedback model the decoder keeps (wheel_g27.c) ---- */
+
+enum {
+    WHEEL_FX_NONE = 0,
+    WHEEL_FX_CONSTANT,  /* level */
+    WHEEL_FX_SPRING,    /* condition: center, deadband, k_neg/k_pos, sat */
+    WHEEL_FX_DAMPER,    /* condition: k_neg/k_pos, sat */
+    WHEEL_FX_FRICTION,  /* condition: k_neg/k_pos, sat */
+    WHEEL_FX_SQUARE,    /* periodic: magnitude, offset, period_ms */
+    WHEEL_FX_SAW_UP,
+    WHEEL_FX_SAW_DOWN,
+    WHEEL_FX_TRIANGLE,
+};
+
+typedef struct WheelEffect {
+    int   type;         /* WHEEL_FX_* */
+    int   playing;
+    float level;        /* constant: -1..+1 (byte 0x80 = 0). + pushes the rim LEFT on a
+                         * G27: GT5 sends 0x90-0xF0 to pull a wheel held right back to
+                         * the centre, below 0x80 for one held left. It goes to
+                         * DirectInput with the same sign (a force from the right). */
+    float center;       /* condition: -1..+1 (rim position) */
+    float deadband;     /* condition: half width, 0..1 */
+    float k_neg, k_pos; /* condition: -1..+1 left / right of the dead band */
+    float sat;          /* condition: 0..1 */
+    float magnitude;    /* periodic: 0..1 */
+    float offset;       /* periodic: -1..+1 */
+    u32   period_ms;    /* periodic */
+} WheelEffect;
+
+#define WHEEL_FFB_SLOTS 4
+
+typedef struct WheelFfb {
+    u32         gen;            /* bumped on every change */
+    WheelEffect slot[WHEEL_FFB_SLOTS];
+    WheelEffect def_spring;     /* the wheel's own centring spring (cmd 0x0E) */
+    int         def_spring_on;  /* cmd 0x04 / 0x05 */
+    int         range_deg;      /* rotation the game asked for (0xF8 0x81 ...), 0 = never */

+static void osk_post(u32 status)
+{
+    for (int slot = 0; slot < CELL_SYSUTIL_MAX_CALLBACKS; slot++)
+        cellSysutilQueueEvent(slot, status, 0);
+}
+
+/* Called from cellSysutilCheckCallback, on the thread the title pumps sysutil from. */
+void cellOskDialog_tick(void)
+{
+    if (s_osk_post_loaded) { s_osk_post_loaded = 0; osk_post(OSK_EV_LOADED); }
+    if (s_osk_post_finished) {
+        s_osk_post_finished = 0;
+        if (s_osk_separate)
+            osk_post(s_osk_result == CELL_OSK_DIALOG_INPUT_FIELD_RESULT_CANCELED ? OSK_EV_CANCELED : OSK_EV_ENTERED);
+        osk_post(OSK_EV_FINISHED);
+    }
+    if (s_osk_post_unloaded) { s_osk_post_unloaded = 0; osk_post(OSK_EV_UNLOADED); }
+}

+static LRESULT CALLBACK osk_wndproc(HWND w, UINT m, WPARAM wp, LPARAM lp)
+{
+    switch (m) {
+    case WM_COMMAND:
+        if (LOWORD(wp) == IDOK || LOWORD(wp) == IDCANCEL) {
+            if (LOWORD(wp) == IDOK) {
+                HWND e = GetDlgItem(w, OSK_ID_EDIT);
+                const int n = GetWindowTextW(e, (WCHAR*)s_result_text, CELL_OSK_MAX_TEXT_LENGTH + 1);
+                s_result_length = n > 0 ? (u32)n : 0;
+                s_osk_result = n > 0 ? CELL_OSK_DIALOG_INPUT_FIELD_RESULT_OK
+                                     : CELL_OSK_DIALOG_INPUT_FIELD_RESULT_NO_INPUT_TEXT;
+            } else {
+                s_result_length = 0;
+                s_result_text[0] = 0;
+                s_osk_result = s_osk_abort ? CELL_OSK_DIALOG_INPUT_FIELD_RESULT_ABORT
+                                           : CELL_OSK_DIALOG_INPUT_FIELD_RESULT_CANCELED;
+            }
+            DestroyWindow(w);
+            return 0;
+        }
+        break;
+    case WM_CLOSE:
+        SendMessageW(w, WM_COMMAND, IDCANCEL, 0);
+        return 0;
+    case WM_DESTROY:
+        PostQuitMessage(0);
+        return 0;
+    }
+    return DefWindowProcW(w, m, wp, lp);
+}

+    s_osk_abort = 0;

+/*
+ * gt5_menu_vk.h - the in-game settings menu on the Vulkan renderer (rsx_vulkan_backend.c).
+ *
+ * The menu itself (input, sizes, pages, saving) is the one the Direct3D 12 renderer has (gt5_menu.h);
+ * this is only how a Vulkan renderer hands it a device and a swap chain and puts it on the screen.
+ * Include <vulkan/vulkan.h> (with VK_NO_PROTOTYPES, as the renderer does) before this file. A build
+ * without the menu links gt5_menu_stub.c, which answers "no menu" to all of it.
+ *
+ * How it is drawn. The menu is laid out in the window's pixels and drawn, on the window's thread,
+ * into an image of its own the size of the swap chain's (an overlay, transparent where there is no
+ * menu), with its own command buffers submitted on the renderer's queue. Whoever presents -- the
+ * thread that draws the frames, or the frame generation presenter -- puts that overlay over the
+ * swap chain image after copying the frame into it: one more render pass, gt5_menu_vk_composite.
+ *
+ * Threads.
+ *     gt5_menu_vk_init, gt5_menu_vk_frame, gt5_menu_vk_shutdown   the window's thread (it runs the
+ *                                                                 window's messages and draws)
+ *     gt5_menu_vk_swapchain                                       whoever made the swap chain, with
+ *                                                                 the GPU idle and no present running
+ *     gt5_menu_vk_composite                                       whoever presents, under the lock
+ *                                                                 that keeps presents one at a time
+ * The queue is the renderer's: every submission the menu makes goes through queue_lock(1) ... (0).
+ */
+#ifndef GT5_MENU_VK_H
+#define GT5_MENU_VK_H
+
+#ifdef __cplusplus
+extern "C" {
+#endif
+
+typedef struct gt5_menu_vk_init_info {
+    void*                     hwnd;             /* the window (Windows: its HWND; the menu takes its messages
+                                                   through gt5_menu_wndproc) */
+    VkInstance                instance;
+    VkPhysicalDevice          physical_device;
+    VkDevice                  device;
+    VkQueue                   queue;            /* the queue the swap chain is presented on */
+    uint32_t                  queue_family;
+    PFN_vkGetInstanceProcAddr get_instance_proc_addr;   /* every Vulkan function the menu calls comes from it */
+    void                    (*queue_lock)(int take);     /* 1: the queue is the menu's until 0 */
+    uint32_t                  width, height;    /* the swap chain's size now (for the log; the swap chain itself
+                                                   comes with gt5_menu_vk_swapchain) */
+    const char*               version;          /* shown on the About page; NULL = $GT5_VER */
+    const char*               title;            /* the game's name there; NULL = $PS3_TITLE */
+} gt5_menu_vk_init_info;
+
+/* Sets up the registry if nobody has, Dear ImGui, the fonts and the menu's Vulkan objects. 1 on
+ * success; on failure the menu stays off and every other call does nothing. The swap chain comes next,
+ * with gt5_menu_vk_swapchain. */
+int  gt5_menu_vk_init(const gt5_menu_vk_init_info* info);
+/* The GPU must be idle (or the menu's own work finished: it waits for its fences). */
+void gt5_menu_vk_shutdown(void);
+
+/* A swap chain was made (or made again): its images, their format and size. They must have been made
+ * with VK_IMAGE_USAGE_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_BIT. count 0: there is none (the window went), nothing is put
+ * over the picture until there is. The overlay follows the swap chain's size. Call with the GPU idle and
+ * no present running. */
+void gt5_menu_vk_swapchain(VkFormat format, uint32_t width, uint32_t height, uint32_t count, const VkImage* images);
+
+/* Window's thread, once a frame (cheap when the menu is closed and nothing changed): builds the menu
+ * when it is open or the corner readout is on, and draws it into the overlay. Also where a changed
+ * setting gets written to settings.bat, half a second after the last change. 1 when there is something
+ * to show. */
+int  gt5_menu_vk_frame(void);
+
+/* Whoever presents, after the frame was copied into swap chain image `image_index` (left in
+ * VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL by a transfer): records into cb the render pass that puts the
+ * menu over it, which leaves the image in VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_PRESENT_SRC_KHR. Returns 1 when it did; 0 when
+ * there is nothing to show (or no swap chain the menu knows): the caller then makes its own barrier to
+ * PRESENT_SRC_KHR as before. */
+int  gt5_menu_vk_composite(VkCommandBuffer cb, uint32_t image_index);
+
+#ifdef __cplusplus
+}
+#endif
+#endif /* GT5_MENU_VK_H */

+/*
+ * gt5_menu_vk_stub.c - "there is no menu" for the Vulkan renderer's calls (gt5_menu_vk.h), in a build
+ * whose game has no gt5_menu_vk.cpp.
+ *
+ * A file of its own, beside gt5_menu_stub.c, for the reason that one gives: a library member is pulled
+ * into the exe only for a name nothing else defined. The game's gt5_menu_vk.cpp defines these when it is
+ * built with the Vulkan renderer and the menu; when it isn't, only this member comes in, and the other
+ * menu calls stay with whoever has them (the game's menu, or gt5_menu_stub.c).
+ *
+ * Only with the Vulkan renderer (PS3RECOMP_RSX_VULKAN, which also brings its headers); empty otherwise.
+ */
+#if defined(PS3RECOMP_RSX_VULKAN)
+#define VK_NO_PROTOTYPES
+#include <vulkan/vulkan.h>
+#include "gt5_menu_vk.h"
+
+int  gt5_menu_vk_init(const gt5_menu_vk_init_info* info) { (void)info; return 0; }
+void gt5_menu_vk_shutdown(void) {}
+void gt5_menu_vk_swapchain(VkFormat format, uint32_t width, uint32_t height, uint32_t count, const VkImage* images)
+{ (void)format; (void)width; (void)height; (void)count; (void)images; }
+int  gt5_menu_vk_frame(void) { return 0; }
+int  gt5_menu_vk_composite(VkCommandBuffer cb, uint32_t image_index) { (void)cb; (void)image_index; return 0; }
+#else

+/* user32's per-monitor DPI call, where Windows has it (10 1607+): the process is per-monitor aware
+ * (boot_main.cpp), so window sizes are real pixels and the frame around a window depends on its monitor. */
+typedef BOOL (WINAPI* null_adjust_dpi_fn)(LPRECT, DWORD, BOOL, DWORD, UINT);
+static void null_adjust_rect(RECT* r, DWORD style, DWORD ex, UINT dpi)
+{

+    if (f == (null_adjust_dpi_fn)-1) f = (null_adjust_dpi_fn)(void*)GetProcAddress(GetModuleHandleA("user32.dll"), "AdjustWindowRectExForDpi");

+/* The game's icon: drawn here, nothing copied. A rounded square in the menu's dark slate with three
+ * slanted bars in its blue, shortest at the top, like a mark for speed. Each pixel is the coverage of
+ * 4x4 samples, so the edges are smooth at every size. */
+static HICON null_icon(int size)
+{
+    if (size < 16) size = 16;
+    if (size > 256) size = 256;
+    BITMAPV5HEADER bh;
+    memset(&bh, 0, sizeof bh);
+    bh.bV5Size = sizeof bh; bh.bV5Width = size; bh.bV5Height = -size; bh.bV5Planes = 1; bh.bV5BitCount = 32;
+    bh.bV5Compression = BI_BITFIELDS;
+    bh.bV5RedMask = 0x00FF0000; bh.bV5GreenMask = 0x0000FF00; bh.bV5BlueMask = 0x000000FF; bh.bV5AlphaMask = 0xFF000000;
+    void* bits = NULL;
+    HDC dc = GetDC(NULL);
+    HBITMAP colour = CreateDIBSection(dc, (BITMAPINFO*)&bh, DIB_RGB_COLORS, &bits, NULL, 0);
+    ReleaseDC(NULL, dc);
+    if (!colour || !bits) return NULL;
+    HBITMAP mask = CreateBitmap(size, size, 1, 1, NULL);
+    unsigned* px = (unsigned*)bits;
+    const float s = (float)size, rad = s * 0.22f;
+    for (int y = 0; y < size; y++)
+        for (int x = 0; x < size; x++) {
+            float cover = 0.0f, bar = 0.0f;
+            for (int sy = 0; sy < 4; sy++)
+                for (int sx = 0; sx < 4; sx++) {
+                    const float u = ((float)x + ((float)sx + 0.5f) / 4.0f) / s, v = ((float)y + ((float)sy + 0.5f) / 4.0f) / s;
+                    /* the rounded square, 1/16 in from the edges */
+                    const float m = 1.0f / 16.0f, r = rad / s;
+                    float dx = u < m + r ? m + r - u : u > 1.0f - m - r ? u - (1.0f - m - r) : 0.0f;
+                    float dy = v < m + r ? m + r - v : v > 1.0f - m - r ? v - (1.0f - m - r) : 0.0f;
+                    if (u < m || u > 1.0f - m || v < m || v > 1.0f - m || dx * dx + dy * dy > r * r) continue;
+                    cover += 1.0f;
+                    /* three bars, slanted by a quarter of their height, right-aligned */
+                    for (int b = 0; b < 3; b++) {
+                        const float y0 = 0.30f + 0.15f * (float)b, y1 = y0 + 0.10f;
+                        if (v < y0 || v > y1) continue;
+                        const float slant = (y1 - v) * 0.5f;
+                        const float x1 = 0.80f + slant, x0 = 0.62f - 0.16f * (float)b + slant;
+                        if (u >= x0 && u <= x1) bar += 1.0f;
+                    }
+                }
+            const float a = cover / 16.0f, t = cover > 0.0f ? bar / cover : 0.0f;
+            /* slate (27,34,48) to blue (64,140,230), premultiplied by the coverage */
+            const float rr = (27.0f + (64.0f - 27.0f) * t) * a, gg = (34.0f + (140.0f - 34.0f) * t) * a,
+                        bb = (48.0f + (230.0f - 48.0f) * t) * a;
+            px[y * size + x] = ((unsigned)(a * 255.0f + 0.5f) << 24) | ((unsigned)(rr + 0.5f) << 16) |
+                               ((unsigned)(gg + 0.5f) << 8) | (unsigned)(bb + 0.5f);
+        }
+    ICONINFO ii;
+    memset(&ii, 0, sizeof ii);
+    ii.fIcon = TRUE; ii.hbmColor = colour; ii.hbmMask = mask;
+    HICON icon = mask ? CreateIconIndirect(&ii) : NULL;
+    DeleteObject(colour);
+    if (mask) DeleteObject(mask);
+    return icon;
+}

+/* ---- [win] the window's place, kept in settings.bat ---------------------------------------------- */
+
+/* The window as it is now, if it is a plain window (not borderless, maximized or minimized): its outer
+ * rectangle in screen pixels, as GT5_WINDOW_PLACE "x,y,w,h". */
+static void null_place_save(HWND hwnd)
+{
+    if (!null_start_on() || !hwnd || IsIconic(hwnd) || IsZoomed(hwnd) || !IsWindowVisible(hwnd)) return;
+    const LONG_PTR style = GetWindowLongPtrA(hwnd, GWL_STYLE);
+    if (!(style & WS_CAPTION)) return;
+    RECT r;
+    if (!GetWindowRect(hwnd, &r) || r.right - r.left < 64 || r.bottom - r.top < 64) return;
+    char b[64];
+    snprintf(b, sizeof b, "%ld,%ld,%ld,%ld", (long)r.left, (long)r.top, (long)(r.right - r.left), (long)(r.bottom - r.top));
+    gt5_setting_set("GT5_WINDOW_PLACE", b);
+}
+static int null_place_load(RECT* out)
+{
+    char b[64];
+    long x, y, w, h;
+    gt5_setting_stored("GT5_WINDOW_PLACE", b, sizeof b);
+    if (sscanf(b, "%ld,%ld,%ld,%ld", &x, &y, &w, &h) != 4 || w < 64 || h < 64) return 0;
+    RECT r = { x, y, x + w, y + h };
+    /* only if it still lies mostly on a monitor (one may have been unplugged since) */
+    MONITORINFO mi;
+    memset(&mi, 0, sizeof mi);
+    mi.cbSize = sizeof mi;
+    if (!GetMonitorInfoA(MonitorFromRect(&r, MONITOR_DEFAULTTONULL), &mi)) return 0;
+    RECT in;
+    if (!IntersectRect(&in, &r, &mi.rcWork) || (in.right - in.left) * 2 < w || (in.bottom - in.top) * 2 < h) return 0;
+    *out = r;
+    return 1;
+}
+
+/* A monitor's scaling (96 = 100 %), before any window is on it. */
+static UINT null_monitor_dpi(HMONITOR mon)
+{
+    typedef HRESULT (WINAPI* get_dpi_mon_fn)(HMONITOR, int, UINT*, UINT*);
+    static get_dpi_mon_fn f = (get_dpi_mon_fn)-1;
+    if (f == (get_dpi_mon_fn)-1) {
+        HMODULE m = LoadLibraryExA("shcore.dll", NULL, LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_SYSTEM32);
+        f = m ? (get_dpi_mon_fn)(void*)GetProcAddress(m, "GetDpiForMonitor") : NULL;
+    }
+    UINT x = 96, y = 96;
+    if (!f || !mon || FAILED(f(mon, 0 /* MDT_EFFECTIVE_DPI */, &x, &y)) || x < 48) x = 96;
+    return x;
+}

+/* [win] The window when it first opens (PS3_WINDOW_START): hidden until it is where it belongs. */
+static void null_window_place(HWND hwnd, u32 render_w, u32 render_h)
+{
+    char mode[32], size[32], first[16];
+    gt5_setting_stored("GT5_LAUNCH_WINDOW", mode, sizeof mode);
+    gt5_setting_stored("PS3_WINDOW_SIZE", size, sizeof size);
+    gt5_setting_stored("GT5_WINDOW_FIRST", first, sizeof first);
+    if (!first[0]) {
+        /* The first start of this version: the old default (a window, no size chosen) becomes borderless
+         * full screen, once; what the player picks after that stays. */
+        if (!size[0] && (!mode[0] || !_stricmp(mode, "windowed"))) {
+            gt5_setting_set("GT5_LAUNCH_WINDOW", "borderless");
+            snprintf(mode, sizeof mode, "borderless");
+            fprintf(stderr, "[win] first start: borderless full screen\n");
+        }
+        gt5_setting_set("GT5_WINDOW_FIRST", "done");
+        if (gt5_settings_path()[0] && GetFileAttributesA(gt5_settings_path()) != INVALID_FILE_ATTRIBUTES) gt5_settings_save();
+    }
+    POINT pt = { 0, 0 };
+    GetCursorPos(&pt);
+    HMONITOR mon = MonitorFromPoint(pt, MONITOR_DEFAULTTOPRIMARY);   /* where the player is: the launcher's Play */
+    MONITORINFO mi;
+    memset(&mi, 0, sizeof mi);
+    mi.cbSize = sizeof mi;
+    const LONG_PTR style = GetWindowLongPtrA(hwnd, GWL_STYLE);
+    if (!_stricmp(mode, "borderless")) {
+        GetMonitorInfoA(mon, &mi);
+        SetWindowLongPtrA(hwnd, GWL_STYLE, (style & ~(LONG_PTR)WS_OVERLAPPEDWINDOW) | WS_POPUP);
+        SetWindowPos(hwnd, NULL, mi.rcMonitor.left, mi.rcMonitor.top, mi.rcMonitor.right - mi.rcMonitor.left,
+                     mi.rcMonitor.bottom - mi.rcMonitor.top, SWP_FRAMECHANGED | SWP_NOZORDER | SWP_NOACTIVATE);
+        ShowWindow(hwnd, SW_SHOW);
+        fprintf(stderr, "[win] borderless full screen, %ldx%ld\n", (long)(mi.rcMonitor.right - mi.rcMonitor.left),
+                (long)(mi.rcMonitor.bottom - mi.rcMonitor.top));
+        return;
+    }
+    /* A window (or a maximized one, which goes back to this): where it was last, else centred on the
+     * mouse's monitor; PS3_WINDOW_SIZE, else its last size, else the 1280x720 it had at 100 % scaling
+     * at this monitor's scaling (what it looked like before the game was DPI aware). */
+    RECT last;
+    const int have_last = null_place_load(&last);
+    if (have_last) mon = MonitorFromRect(&last, MONITOR_DEFAULTTONEAREST);
+    GetMonitorInfoA(mon, &mi);
+    const UINT dpi = null_monitor_dpi(mon);
+    u32 cw = render_w, ch = render_h;
+    ps3_display_window_size(render_w, render_h, &cw, &ch);
+    if (!size[0]) {
+        /* [win] the shape of the frame the renderer will draw (boot_main.cpp: the 1080p mode's size when the
+         * game is offered it, which a wide mode can't make wider than 1920; else this 720p size), so that a
+         * window shows the picture without bars inside it */
+        extern int cellVideoOut_offers_1080(void);   /* cellVideoOut.c */
+        u32 fw = cw, fh = ch;
+        if (cellVideoOut_offers_1080()) ps3_display_render_size(1920, 1080, &fw, &fh);
+        if (fw && fh) cw = (u32)((double)ch * (double)fw / (double)fh + 0.5);
+    }
+    LONG ww, wh;
+    if (!size[0] && have_last) {
+        ww = last.right - last.left; wh = last.bottom - last.top;
+    } else {
+        if (!size[0]) { cw = (u32)((cw * dpi + 48u) / 96u); ch = (u32)((ch * dpi + 48u) / 96u); }
+        RECT r = { 0, 0, (LONG)cw, (LONG)ch };
+        null_adjust_rect(&r, (DWORD)WS_OVERLAPPEDWINDOW, 0, dpi);
+        ww = r.right - r.left; wh = r.bottom - r.top;
+    }
+    const LONG aw = mi.rcWork.right - mi.rcWork.left, ah = mi.rcWork.bottom - mi.rcWork.top;
+    if (ww > aw || wh > ah) {           /* larger than the screen: the same shape, as large as fits */
+        const double k = (double)aw / ww < (double)ah / wh ? (double)aw / ww : (double)ah / wh;
+        ww = (LONG)(ww * k); wh = (LONG)(wh * k);
+    }
+    LONG x = have_last ? last.left : mi.rcWork.left + (aw - ww) / 2;
+    LONG y = have_last ? last.top : mi.rcWork.top + (ah - wh) / 2;
+    if (x + ww > mi.rcWork.right) x = mi.rcWork.right - ww;
+    if (y + wh > mi.rcWork.bottom) y = mi.rcWork.bottom - wh;
+    if (x < mi.rcWork.left) x = mi.rcWork.left;
+    if (y < mi.rcWork.top) y = mi.rcWork.top;
+    SetWindowPos(hwnd, NULL, x, y, ww, wh, SWP_NOZORDER | SWP_NOACTIVATE);
+    const int max = !_stricmp(mode, "max");
+    ShowWindow(hwnd, max ? SW_SHOWMAXIMIZED : SW_SHOW);
+    fprintf(stderr, "[win] %s at %ld,%ld %ldx%ld (%s, %u dpi)\n", max ? "maximized window" : "window", (long)x, (long)y,
+            (long)ww, (long)wh, have_last ? "where it was last" : "centred", dpi);
+}
+
+/* [win] The Vulkan renderer's window (an SDL window, rsx_vulkan_win32.c) is placed, kept and remembered
+ * exactly as this one: PS3_WINDOW_START, the same placement, place in settings.bat and icon. */
+int   rsx_null_window_start_on(void) { return null_start_on(); }
+void  rsx_null_window_place(void* hwnd, u32 render_w, u32 render_h) { null_window_place((HWND)hwnd, render_w, render_h); }
+void  rsx_null_window_place_save(void* hwnd) { null_place_save((HWND)hwnd); }
+void* rsx_null_window_icon(int size) { return (void*)null_icon(size); }

+/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ * [win] Quitting
+ * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/
+
+/* Any thread. Ends the process cleanly; returns only to a second caller, which then waits for the first.
+ * What TerminateProcess alone used to skip:
+ *   - a save in flight (cellSaveData, ps3_savedata_busy): waited for, up to save_wait_ms;
+ *   - the C library's buffers of every open file: the game's own files (cellFs: fwrite without a flush,
+ *     ppu_fs.cpp) and the logs (fflush(NULL));
+ *   - the pads' motors, left running: stopped first, before the save wait, and for good
+ *     (cellPad_rumble_stop_all: every XInput and Sony pad, and nothing more is sent after it);
+ * (settings.bat is written on the window's thread before this: null_quit_go.) TerminateProcess stays the
+ * last step: exit() would run the C library's and the DLLs' teardown under the game's threads, which
+ * are still running. PS3_EXIT_CLEAN=0: TerminateProcess at once, as before (the motors still stop).
+ * This is the one place every way out of a running game on Windows ends in (the window's own quit, a
+ * window closed any other way, Vulkan's window included, via boot_main.cpp, the session ending, the
+ * renderer giving up): the pads' motors are stopped here and nowhere else on those ways. */
+void rsx_null_backend_quit_now(int code, int save_wait_ms)
+{
+    static volatile LONG once;
+    if (InterlockedExchange(&once, 1)) { for (;;) Sleep(1000); }
+    {
+        extern void cellPad_rumble_stop_all(void);   /* cellPad.c (cellPad.h) */
+        cellPad_rumble_stop_all();
+    }
+    if (null_clean_on()) {
+        extern int ps3_savedata_busy(void);          /* cellSaveData.c */
+        const ULONGLONG t0 = GetTickCount64();
+        int waited = 0;
+        while (ps3_savedata_busy() && GetTickCount64() - t0 < (ULONGLONG)(save_wait_ms > 0 ? save_wait_ms : 0)) { Sleep(20); waited = 1; }
+        fprintf(stderr, "[quit] ending cleanly%s; files flushed\n",
+                waited ? (ps3_savedata_busy() ? " (a save was still being written after the wait)" : " (after a save finished)") : "");
+    } else {
+        fprintf(stderr, "[quit] PS3_EXIT_CLEAN=0: ending at once\n");
+    }
+    fflush(NULL);
+    TerminateProcess(GetCurrentProcess(), (UINT)code);
+}
+
+static DWORD WINAPI null_quit_thread(LPVOID unused)
+{
+    (void)unused;
+    rsx_null_backend_quit_now(0, 10000);
+    return 0;
+}
+
+/* Window thread: the player has said Yes (or nothing asks). The window goes at once; the game keeps
+ * ticking while a save in flight finishes, then the process ends (null_quit_thread). */
+static void null_quit_go(HWND hwnd)
+{
+    if (s_state.quitting) return;
+    s_state.quitting = 1;
+    fprintf(stderr, "[quit] the player quit\n");
+    if (!null_clean_on()) {                     /* as before: boot_main ends it at the next pump */
+        s_state.window_closed = 1;
+        DestroyWindow(hwnd);
+        return;
+    }
+    null_place_save(hwnd);
+    if (gt5_settings_dirty()) gt5_settings_save();
+    ShowWindow(hwnd, SW_HIDE);
+    HANDLE t = CreateThread(NULL, 0, null_quit_thread, NULL, 0, NULL);
+    if (t) CloseHandle(t);
+    else rsx_null_backend_quit_now(0, 0);
+}
+
+/* Window thread: ask "Quit the game?" in the game's own overlay. 1: it asks (its Yes posts
+ * GT5_MENU_QUIT_MSG); 0: nobody asks, quit now. */
+static int null_quit_ask(HWND hwnd)
+{
+    if (!null_overlay_on()) return 0;
+    if (IsIconic(hwnd)) ShowWindow(hwnd, SW_RESTORE);    /* the taskbar's Close on a minimized game */
+    const int r = gt5_menu_ask_quit();
+    return r == 1;
+}
+
+/* The messages this file shows: one window, a few plain words, in the player's language. */
+static void null_tell(int what)
+{
+    const int zh = null_zh();
+    const wchar_t* text;
+    if (what == 1)

+/* Window thread. what 1: Direct3D 12 couldn't start (boot_main.cpp); 2: the renderer stopped for good, a
+ * graphics driver reset or a card that hung or went away (rsx_live_draw.c). The window goes, one plain
+ * message says so, and the game ends cleanly. */
+void rsx_null_backend_fatal(int what)
+{
+    static int said;
+    if (said) return;
+    said = 1;
+    fprintf(stderr, "[win] %s: telling the player, then quitting\n",
+            what == 1 ? "Direct3D 12 couldn't start" : "the renderer stopped for good");
+    if (s_state.hwnd) ShowWindow(s_state.hwnd, SW_HIDE);
+    null_tell(what);
+    if (gt5_settings_dirty()) gt5_settings_save();
+    s_state.quitting = 1;
+    /* exit codes 20 / 21: the player has been told (3 is abort()'s, boot_main.cpp) */
+    rsx_null_backend_quit_now(what == 1 ? 20 : 21, 3000);
+}

+ * The runtime's input code and renderer call the menu (gt5_menu.h). This file goes into the runtime

+ * runtime calls: the game's exe has gt5_menu.cpp among its own objects, so every name here is already

+/*
+ * rsx_present_fit.h - [win] [fill] where the frame goes in the window, and [winf] with which filter, for the
+ * Vulkan renderer's step into the window (the DirectX 12 engine has the same rules in rsx_live_draw.c, ld_win_rect,
+ * ld_rs_present_draw and ld_rs_draw). Plain C, no dependencies: the renderer, its tests and the demos use it alike.
+ *
+ *   fw x fh   the frame (the game's picture)
+ *   fill      LD_FILL's part of it (x0, y0, x1, y1 as fractions of the frame), or NULL for all of it
+ *   tw x th   the window's drawing area (the swap chain image)
+ *   fit       PS3_PRESENT_FIT: the picture in its own shape, the largest rectangle of the frame's shape
+ *             centred in the window, when the two shapes differ by more than 1 %; else (or 0) all of it
+ * Out: src = x0, y0, x1, y1 in frame pixels; dst = x0, y0, x1, y1 in window pixels. Returns 1 when there are
+ * bars (the rest of the window is to be black).
+ */
+#ifndef RSX_PRESENT_FIT_H
+#define RSX_PRESENT_FIT_H
+
+#include <stdint.h>
+
+static inline int rsx_present_fit_rects(uint32_t fw, uint32_t fh, const float* fill, uint32_t tw, uint32_t th, int fit,
+                                        int32_t src[4], int32_t dst[4])
+{
+    src[0] = 0; src[1] = 0; src[2] = (int32_t)fw; src[3] = (int32_t)fh;
+    if (fill) {
+        int32_t s[4];
+        s[0] = (int32_t)(fill[0] * (float)fw + 0.5f); s[1] = (int32_t)(fill[1] * (float)fh + 0.5f);
+        s[2] = (int32_t)(fill[2] * (float)fw + 0.5f); s[3] = (int32_t)(fill[3] * (float)fh + 0.5f);
+        if (s[0] < 0) s[0] = 0;
+        if (s[1] < 0) s[1] = 0;
+        if (s[2] > (int32_t)fw) s[2] = (int32_t)fw;
+        if (s[3] > (int32_t)fh) s[3] = (int32_t)fh;
+        if (s[2] - s[0] >= 16 && s[3] - s[1] >= 16) { src[0] = s[0]; src[1] = s[1]; src[2] = s[2]; src[3] = s[3]; }
+    }
+    dst[0] = 0; dst[1] = 0; dst[2] = (int32_t)tw; dst[3] = (int32_t)th;
+    if (!fit || !fw || !fh || !tw || !th) return 0;
+    const double pic = (double)fw / (double)fh, tgt = (double)tw / (double)th;
+    const double off = tgt / pic - 1.0;
+    if (off <= 0.01 && off >= -0.01) return 0;          /* within 1 %: the whole window */
+    if (tgt > pic) {                                     /* wider: bars left and right */
+        const int32_t w = (int32_t)((double)th * pic + 0.5);
+        dst[0] = ((int32_t)tw - w) / 2; dst[2] = dst[0] + w;
+    } else {                                             /* taller: bars above and below */
+        const int32_t h = (int32_t)((double)tw / pic + 0.5);
+        dst[1] = ((int32_t)th - h) / 2; dst[3] = dst[1] + h;
+    }
+    return 1;
+}
+
+/* [winf] The filter of the step into the window, chosen as the DirectX 12 renderer's ld_rs_draw chooses it for
+ * that step (point = 2), from the rects above. Out: the shader's eight constants (vulkan/rsx_vk_winf.frag):
+ *   [0..3] r, the frame's part shown as uv (x0, y0, x1, y1); [4..5] fp, uv per window pixel;
+ *   [6] n: -1 a magnification (ratio < 0.999) while filling or fitting: Catmull-Rom over 4x4 texels;
+ *          1 about 1:1 (or a magnification with neither): one bilinear tap;
+ *          2..8 a reduction by up to n: n x n bilinear taps (a box);
+ *   [7] flags: 1 every tap kept inside r (fill: the rest of the frame is GT5's black margin);
+ *              2 a reduction by 2-4 takes a tent over +-1 window pixel (2n x 2n taps) instead of the box (tent).
+ * ratio is frame pixels per window pixel, the larger of the two directions. */
+static inline void rsx_present_filter(uint32_t fw, uint32_t fh, const int32_t src[4], const int32_t dst[4], int fill,
+                                      int fit, int tent, float out[8])
+{
+    const float dw = (float)(dst[2] - dst[0]), dh = (float)(dst[3] - dst[1]);
+    out[0] = (float)src[0] / (float)fw; out[1] = (float)src[1] / (float)fh;
+    out[2] = (float)src[2] / (float)fw; out[3] = (float)src[3] / (float)fh;
+    out[4] = dw > 0.0f ? (out[2] - out[0]) / dw : 0.0f;
+    out[5] = dh > 0.0f ? (out[3] - out[1]) / dh : 0.0f;
+    const float rx = dw > 0.0f ? (float)(src[2] - src[0]) / dw : 1.0f, ry = dh > 0.0f ? (float)(src[3] - src[1]) / dh : 1.0f;
+    const float ratio = rx > ry ? rx : ry;
+    int n = 1;
+    if (ratio > 1.001f) {                                  /* ceil(ratio - 0.001) */
+        const float c = ratio - 0.001f;
+        n = (int)c;
+        if ((float)n < c) n++;
+    }
+    if (n > 8) n = 8;
+    float flags = 0.0f;
+    if (fill) { flags += 1.0f; if (ratio < 0.999f) n = -1; }
+    else if (ratio < 0.999f && fit) n = -1;
+    if (tent && n >= 2 && n <= 4) flags += 2.0f;           /* above 4x: the box (a tent would be 2n x 2n taps) */
+    out[6] = (float)n; out[7] = flags;
+}
+

+#version 450
+// The step into the window ([winf]): one triangle over the viewport (the picture's rectangle in the
+// swap chain image); uv runs over r, the frame's part shown.
+layout(push_constant) uniform C { vec4 r; vec2 fp; float n; float cl; } c;
+layout(location = 0) out vec2 uv;
+void main()
+{
+    vec2 q = vec2((gl_VertexIndex << 1) & 2, gl_VertexIndex & 2);
+    gl_Position = vec4(q * 2.0 - 1.0, 0.0, 1.0);
+    uv = c.r.xy + (c.r.zw - c.r.xy) * q;
+}

+#version 450
+// The DirectX 12 renderer's window filter (rsx_live_draw.c ld_rs_blit_pso, point = 2), the same math:
+//   n < 0: a magnification, Catmull-Rom over the 4x4 texels round each pixel, clamped to the rect r;
+//   cl & 2: a reduction by n (2..4), a tent over +-1 window pixel (2n x 2n bilinear taps, triangle weights);
+//   else n x n bilinear taps (a box; one tap for n = 1). cl & 1 keeps every tap inside r (LD_FILL).
+layout(push_constant) uniform C { vec4 r; vec2 fp; float n; float cl; } c;
+layout(set = 0, binding = 0) uniform sampler2D t0;
+layout(location = 0) in vec2 uv;
+layout(location = 0) out vec4 o;
+void main()
+{
+    vec2 lo = min(c.r.xy, c.r.zw), hi = max(c.r.xy, c.r.zw);
+    if (c.n < 0.0) {
+        vec2 sz = vec2(textureSize(t0, 0));
+        ivec2 t_lo = ivec2(floor(lo * sz + 0.001)), t_hi = max(ivec2(ceil(hi * sz - 0.001)) - 1, t_lo);
+        vec2 p = uv * sz - 0.5, b = floor(p), f = p - b;
+        vec2 w0 = f * (-0.5 + f * (1.0 - 0.5 * f)), w1 = 1.0 + f * f * (-2.5 + 1.5 * f);
+        vec2 w2 = f * (0.5 + f * (2.0 - 1.5 * f)), w3 = f * f * (-0.5 + 0.5 * f);
+        vec4 wx = vec4(w0.x, w1.x, w2.x, w3.x), wy = vec4(w0.y, w1.y, w2.y, w3.y);
+        vec4 a = vec4(0.0);
+        for (int y = 0; y < 4; y++)
+            for (int x = 0; x < 4; x++)
+                a += texelFetch(t0, clamp(ivec2(b) + ivec2(x - 1, y - 1), t_lo, t_hi), 0) * (wx[x] * wy[y]);
+        o = clamp(a, 0.0, 1.0);
+        return;
+    }
+    int fl = int(c.cl + 0.5);
+    vec2 hs = vec2(0.0);
+    if ((fl & 1) != 0) hs = 0.5 / vec2(textureSize(t0, 0));
+    vec4 a = vec4(0.0);
+    int k = int(c.n);
+    if ((fl & 2) != 0) {
+        int m = 2 * k;
+        float ws = 0.0;
+        for (int y = 0; y < m; y++)
+            for (int x = 0; x < m; x++) {
+                vec2 t = ((vec2(x, y) + 0.5) / float(m) - 0.5) * 2.0;
+                float wt = (1.0 - abs(t.x)) * (1.0 - abs(t.y));
+                vec2 q = uv + t * c.fp;
+                if ((fl & 1) != 0) q = clamp(q, lo + hs, hi - hs);
+                a += textureLod(t0, q, 0.0) * wt;
+                ws += wt;
+            }
+        o = a / ws;
+        return;
+    }
+    for (int y = 0; y < k; y++)
+        for (int x = 0; x < k; x++) {
+            vec2 q = uv + ((vec2(x, y) + 0.5) / c.n - 0.5) * c.fp;
+            if ((fl & 1) != 0) q = clamp(q, lo + hs, hi - hs);
+            a += textureLod(t0, q, 0.0);
+        }
+    o = a / (c.n * c.n);
+}
