+/*
+ * gt5_upscale.h - the renderer's interface to a temporal upscaler (anti-aliasing / upscaling from
+ * jittered frames, depth and motion vectors) and, since interface version 2, to a frame generator (the
+ * frame between two drawn ones, from the same kind of inputs), Direct3D 12.
+ *
+ * The renderer knows only this header. A back end is an optional plug-in DLL looked for next to gt5.exe:
+ *   gt5_upscale_dlss.dll  NVIDIA DLSS: the upscaler, and DLSS Frame Generation (scripts\add_dlss.ps1)
+ *   gt5_upscale_fsr.dll   AMD FSR 3: frame generation only (scripts\add_fsr.ps1)
+ * Neither vendor's SDK is part of this project and their files never are; a plug-in is built on the
+ * player's PC against the SDK that the launcher fetches from the vendor's own repository. Without a
+ * plug-in the game is the same program with that plug-in's choices greyed out.
+ *
+ * Every call is made on the renderer's thread, with the recording thread idle (neither vendor's
+ * library is thread safe).
+ *
+ * The Vulkan renderer speaks to the same DLLs through a second entry set, gt5_upscale_vk.h
+ * ("gt5_upscale_get_vk"); a plug-in built without it is used by Direct3D 12 only.
+ */
+#ifndef GT5_UPSCALE_H
+#define GT5_UPSCALE_H
+
+#ifdef _WIN32
+#include <windows.h>
+#include <d3d12.h>
+/* The modes, flags and the caps / state structs, shared with the Vulkan interface (gt5_upscale_vk.h). */
+#include "gt5_upscale_types.h"
+
+#ifdef __cplusplus
+extern "C" {
+#endif
+
+#define GT5_UPSCALE_API_VERSION     2u
+#define GT5_UPSCALE_API_VERSION_MIN 1u   /* the oldest a loader still takes: a version 1 plug-in has no fg_ calls */
+
+typedef struct gt5_upscale_frame {
+    ID3D12GraphicsCommandList* list;   /* a real, open list; the back end changes its state freely      */
+    ID3D12Resource* color;             /* render size, NON_PIXEL_SHADER_RESOURCE                        */
+    ID3D12Resource* depth;             /* render size, a float depth copy, NON_PIXEL_SHADER_RESOURCE    */
+    ID3D12Resource* motion;            /* R16G16_FLOAT, pixels this frame -> last, NON_PIXEL_SHADER_RESOURCE */
+    ID3D12Resource* output;            /* output size, created with ALLOW_UNORDERED_ACCESS, UNORDERED_ACCESS */
+    unsigned render_w, render_h;       /* the part of the inputs that holds the frame                   */
+    float    jitter_x, jitter_y;       /* this frame's sub-pixel offset, in render pixels               */
+    float    mv_scale_x, mv_scale_y;   /* multiplies the vectors into render pixels (0 = 1)             */
+    float    frame_ms;                 /* time since the last evaluated frame                           */
+    int      reset;                    /* 1: nothing from earlier frames may be used (cut, new scene)   */
+} gt5_upscale_frame;
+
+/* ---- frame generation (interface version 2) ------------------------------------------------------- *
+ * The generator NEVER presents and never sees the swap chain: it writes the made frame into a texture
+ * of the renderer's on a command list of the renderer's. Showing it, and when, is the presenter's.     */
+
+/* (fg_create's flags GT5_FG_* and gt5_fg_caps: gt5_upscale_types.h) */
+
+/*
+ * One drawn frame. The call makes the frame(s) BETWEEN the frame of the call before and this one, so
+ * the first call after fg_create, and any call with reset, makes nothing useful: the back end then
+ * writes a copy of this frame into output[0], and the renderer shows nothing extra for that pair.
+ *
+ *   color     out_w x out_h, R8G8B8A8_UNORM: the picture that is interpolated. The renderer gives the
+ *             picture WITHOUT the HUD and puts the HUD on the made frame itself.
+ *   hudless   NULL in that case. Only when color is the finished picture with the HUD: the same frame
+ *             without it, same size and format.
+ *   depth     R32_FLOAT, 0 near .. 1 far unless GT5_FG_DEPTH_INVERTED; its top-left render_w x render_h
+ *             is the frame.
+ *   motion    R16G16_FLOAT: for each pixel
+ *             of THIS frame, where its surface was in the frame BEFORE minus where it is now, times
+ *             mv_scale = pixels of the render size; the camera's motion included, no jitter. Its
+ *             top-left render_w x render_h is the frame.
+ *   output[k] out_w x out_h, R8G8B8A8_UNORM, created with ALLOW_UNORDERED_ACCESS, k < generated: made
+ *             frame k is the frame at (k + 1) / (generated + 1) of the way from the frame before.
+ * States: color, hudless, depth and motion in NON_PIXEL_SHADER_RESOURCE (that state alone: with a
+ * rectangle smaller than the picture NVIDIA's generator moves color out of that state and back itself),
+ * output[] in UNORDERED_ACCESS; all are left in those states.
+ *
+ * The 3D picture inside the display picture is rect_*: outside it the back end leaves this frame's own
+ * pixels. The top-left texel of depth and motion is the top-left pixel of the rectangle.
+ */
+typedef struct gt5_fg_frame {
+    ID3D12GraphicsCommandList* list;   /* a real, open list; the back end changes its state freely      */
+    ID3D12Resource* color;
+    ID3D12Resource* hudless;           /* may be NULL                                                   */
+    ID3D12Resource* depth;
+    ID3D12Resource* motion;
+    ID3D12Resource* output[3];
+    unsigned generated;                /* how many of output[] to fill, 1 .. caps.max_generated         */
+    unsigned rect_x, rect_y, rect_w, rect_h;   /* the 3D picture inside color / output                  */
+    unsigned render_w, render_h;       /* the part of depth and motion that holds the frame             */
+    float    mv_scale_x, mv_scale_y;   /* multiplies the vectors into render pixels (0 = 1)             */
+    float    jitter_x, jitter_y;       /* this frame's sub-pixel offset in render pixels (0: none)      */
+    float    frame_ms;                 /* time since the frame of the call before                       */
+    unsigned long long frame_id;       /* +1 with every call; a gap is a reset                          */
+    int      reset;                    /* 1: this frame has nothing to do with the one before (a cut, a
+                                          new scene, frames left out). Must be given.                   */
+    int      not_game;                 /* 1: a menu, a video                                            */
+    /* The camera of this frame; no jitter in any of it. cam_ok 0: none of it is known (the back end
+     * then works from the vectors alone and puts plausible values where it must). */
+    int      cam_ok;
+    float    cam_near, cam_far;        /* the planes the depth was made with, in the world's units      */
+    float    cam_fov_y;                /* vertical field of view of the 3D rectangle, radians           */
+    float    cam_aspect;               /* width / height of the view                                    */
+    float    cam_pos[3], cam_right[3], cam_up[3], cam_fwd[3];   /* world space; the axes of length 1    */
+    /* row-major, for row vectors (clip = view * view_to_clip), depth 0..1, clip w = the view distance;
+     * clip space is that of the 3D rectangle (x, y in -1..1 across it, y up) */
+    float    view_to_clip[16], clip_to_view[16];
+    float    clip_to_prev_clip[16], prev_clip_to_clip[16];   /* identity when the frame before is not known */
+} gt5_fg_frame;
+
+/* (gt5_fg_state, what the generator holds: gt5_upscale_types.h) */
+
+/* In version 2 any of optimal / create / evaluate / destroy may be NULL (a plug-in with no upscaler)
+ * and any of the fg_ calls may be NULL (no frame generator); init, shutdown and last_error are always
+ * there. The fg_ members are read only when api_version >= 2. */
+typedef struct gt5_upscale_api {
+    unsigned api_version;              /* GT5_UPSCALE_API_VERSION (the one the plug-in was built with)  */
+    /* Once. dir: a folder the back end may write its own logs and caches to. 1 when caps were filled
+     * (available or not); 0 when the back end could not even start. */
+    int  (*init)(ID3D12Device* device, const wchar_t* dir, gt5_upscale_caps* caps);
+    /* The render size for an output size and a mode. 1 on success. */
+    int  (*optimal)(unsigned out_w, unsigned out_h, gt5_upscale_mode mode, unsigned* render_w, unsigned* render_h);
+    /* Makes (or remakes) the upscaler for these sizes. list: a real, open list the back end may record
+     * its set-up into; execute it before the first evaluate. preset: 0 = the back end's default for the
+     * mode, else its own number for a model variant (DLSS: 10 = J, 11 = K, 12 = L, 13 = M). 1 on success. */
+    int  (*create)(ID3D12GraphicsCommandList* list, unsigned render_w, unsigned render_h, unsigned out_w,
+                   unsigned out_h, gt5_upscale_mode mode, unsigned flags, int preset);
+    /* One frame. 1 on success. The list's state (heaps, root signatures, pipeline, targets) is the back
+     * end's afterwards: set your own again. */
+    int  (*evaluate)(const gt5_upscale_frame* frame);
+    /* Releases what create() made. Only once the lists that used it have finished on the GPU. */
+    void (*destroy)(void);
+    void (*shutdown)(ID3D12Device* device);
+    /* The last failure, as text for the log ("" when none). */
+    const char* (*last_error)(void);
+
+    /* ---- interface version 2 ---- */
+    /* After init(). 1 when caps were filled (available or not). */
+    int  (*fg_caps)(gt5_fg_caps* caps);
+    /* Makes (or remakes) the generator. out_w x out_h: the size of color and output; rect_w x rect_h: the
+     * size of the 3D picture inside them; render_w x render_h: the largest size depth and motion will
+     * have; max_generated: the most frames one call will be asked for; flags: GT5_FG_*. list: a real,
+     * open list the back end may record its set-up into; execute it before the first fg_evaluate.
+     * 1 on success. */
+    int  (*fg_create)(ID3D12GraphicsCommandList* list, unsigned out_w, unsigned out_h, unsigned rect_w,
+                      unsigned rect_h, unsigned render_w, unsigned render_h, unsigned max_generated,
+                      unsigned flags);
+    /* One drawn frame: records the generator's passes into frame->list. 1 on success; the list's state
+     * is the back end's afterwards. The textures must stay as they are until the list has run. */
+    int  (*fg_evaluate)(const gt5_fg_frame* frame);
+    /* What fg_create made. 1 when there is a generator. */
+    int  (*fg_state)(gt5_fg_state* state);
+    /* Releases what fg_create made. Only once the lists that used it have finished on the GPU. */
+    void (*fg_destroy)(void);
+} gt5_upscale_api;
+
+/* The one function a plug-in DLL exports. */
+typedef const gt5_upscale_api* (*gt5_upscale_get_fn)(void);
+#define GT5_UPSCALE_GET_NAME "gt5_upscale_get"
+
+#ifdef __cplusplus
+}
+#endif
+#endif /* _WIN32 */
+#endif /* GT5_UPSCALE_H */

+/*
+ * gt5_upscale_types.h - what the renderer's interfaces to a temporal upscaler and a frame generator have in
+ * common, whichever graphics API they speak: the quality modes, the flags, and the structs that say what a back
+ * end can do and what it holds. gt5_upscale.h (Direct3D 12) and gt5_upscale_vk.h (Vulkan) both include it; the
+ * layouts are exactly those interface version 2 always had, so a plug-in built before this split still loads.
+ * No platform header is needed here.
+ */
+#ifndef GT5_UPSCALE_TYPES_H
+#define GT5_UPSCALE_TYPES_H
+
+#ifdef __cplusplus
+extern "C" {
+#endif
+
+/* Quality modes: how much smaller than the output the frame is drawn. */
+typedef enum gt5_upscale_mode {
+    GT5_UPSCALE_NATIVE = 0,        /* drawn at the output's size: anti-aliasing only (DLAA)            */
+    GT5_UPSCALE_QUALITY = 1,       /* about 67% of the output's width and height                       */
+    GT5_UPSCALE_BALANCED = 2,      /* about 58%                                                        */
+    GT5_UPSCALE_PERFORMANCE = 3,   /* 50%                                                              */
+    GT5_UPSCALE_ULTRA_PERFORMANCE = 4 /* 33%                                                           */
+} gt5_upscale_mode;
+
+/* What the frames given to evaluate() are like. */
+#define GT5_UPSCALE_HDR             0x01u  /* colour is linear HDR (off: 8-bit display-referred colour) */
+#define GT5_UPSCALE_MV_OUTPUT_SIZE  0x02u  /* motion vectors at the output's size (off: the render size) */
+#define GT5_UPSCALE_MV_JITTERED     0x04u  /* motion vectors include the jitter                          */
+#define GT5_UPSCALE_DEPTH_INVERTED  0x08u  /* depth 1 = near                                             */
+#define GT5_UPSCALE_AUTO_EXPOSURE   0x10u
+
+typedef struct gt5_upscale_caps {
+    int      available;            /* 1: create() can be called                                         */
+    int      needs_driver;         /* 1: the graphics driver is too old; min_driver_* says which is     */
+    unsigned min_driver_major, min_driver_minor;
+    int      init_result;          /* the back end's own result code, for the log                       */
+    char     name[48];             /* "NVIDIA DLSS", for the menu                                       */
+    char     message[200];         /* why not, in a sentence, when available is 0                       */
+} gt5_upscale_caps;
+
+/* What the frames given to fg_evaluate() are like (fg_create's flags). The game today: none of them. */
+#define GT5_FG_HDR              0x01u  /* the pictures are linear HDR (off: 8-bit sRGB-encoded, as presented) */
+#define GT5_FG_DEPTH_INVERTED   0x02u  /* depth 1 = near (off: 0 near .. 1 far)                               */
+#define GT5_FG_DEPTH_INFINITE   0x04u  /* the far plane is at infinity                                        */
+#define GT5_FG_MV_JITTERED      0x08u  /* the vectors include the jitter (ours do not)                        */
+
+typedef struct gt5_fg_caps {
+    int      available;            /* 1: fg_create can be called                                        */
+    int      needs_driver;         /* 1: the graphics driver is too old; min_driver_* says which is     */
+    unsigned min_driver_major, min_driver_minor;
+    int      init_result;          /* the back end's own result code, for the log                       */
+    unsigned max_generated;        /* made frames a drawn frame (AMD FSR 3.1: 1; DLSS: what NGX reports) */
+    int      wants_camera;         /* 1: the matrices and axes of the frame are used; 0: only near, far
+                                      and the field of view are                                         */
+    char     name[48];             /* "AMD FSR 3", "NVIDIA DLSS Frame Generation", for the menu         */
+    char     version[48];          /* "3.1.6", "310.9.16": for the log                                  */
+    char     message[200];         /* why not, in a sentence a player can read, when available is 0     */
+} gt5_fg_caps;
+
+/* What the generator holds, for the menu's state line and the log. */
+typedef struct gt5_fg_state {
+    unsigned out_w, out_h, rect_w, rect_h, render_w, render_h, max_generated;
+    unsigned memory_mb;                /* video memory the generator's own textures take (0: not known) */
+} gt5_fg_state;
+
+/* The camera of one frame, for a frame generator; no jitter in any of it (the members gt5_fg_frame has
+ * always had, in that order). cam_ok 0: none of it is known (the back end then works from the vectors alone
+ * and puts plausible values where it must). Matrices row-major, for row vectors (clip = view * view_to_clip),
+ * depth 0..1, clip w = the view distance; clip space is that of the 3D rectangle (x, y in -1..1 across it,
+ * y up). */
+typedef struct gt5_fg_camera {
+    int      cam_ok;
+    float    cam_near, cam_far;        /* the planes the depth was made with, in the world's units      */
+    float    cam_fov_y;                /* vertical field of view of the 3D rectangle, radians           */
+    float    cam_aspect;               /* width / height of the view                                    */
+    float    cam_pos[3], cam_right[3], cam_up[3], cam_fwd[3];   /* world space; the axes of length 1    */
+    float    view_to_clip[16], clip_to_view[16];
+    float    clip_to_prev_clip[16], prev_clip_to_clip[16];   /* identity when the frame before is not known */
+} gt5_fg_camera;
+
+#ifdef __cplusplus
+}
+#endif
+#endif /* GT5_UPSCALE_TYPES_H */

new file mode 100644

+++ b/libs/video/gt5_upscale_vk.h
@@ -0,0 +1,122 @@
+/*
+ * gt5_upscale_vk.h - the Vulkan renderer's interface to a temporal upscaler and a frame generator: the same
+ * plug-in DLLs as Direct3D 12's (gt5_upscale.h), through a second entry set, "gt5_upscale_get_vk".
+ *   gt5_upscale_dlss.dll  NVIDIA DLSS (Super Resolution, DLAA) and DLSS Frame Generation, through NGX's Vulkan calls
+ *   gt5_upscale_fsr.dll   AMD FSR 3 frame generation, through AMD's Vulkan back end
+ * A plug-in built without Vulkan headers has no such entry: the Vulkan renderer then leaves its choices greyed.
+ *
+ * Differences from Direct3D 12 that the calls carry:
+ *   - the vendor's library may need instance and device extensions, which only the renderer can enable, when it
+ *     makes them: instance_extensions is asked before the instance is made, device_extensions before the device
+ *     (both before init). The renderer enables those the driver has, and tells init which it could not;
+ *   - images are handed over as image + view + format + size + usage. The renderer keeps every image in
+ *     VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_GENERAL: each is in that layout when a call starts and must be in it when the call ends
+ *     (the renderer puts a full memory barrier before and after each call);
+ *   - work is recorded into the renderer's command buffer, outside a render pass. Its pipeline, descriptor
+ *     sets and push constants are the back end's afterwards: the renderer binds its own again.
+ * Every call is made on the renderer's thread (neither vendor's library is thread safe).
+ */
+#ifndef GT5_UPSCALE_VK_H
+#define GT5_UPSCALE_VK_H
+
+#include <stddef.h>             /* wchar_t */
+#include <vulkan/vulkan.h>
+#include "gt5_upscale_types.h"
+
+#ifdef __cplusplus
+extern "C" {
+#endif
+
+#define GT5_UPSCALE_VK_API_VERSION 1u
+
+/* One of the renderer's images. view: 2D, level 0, layer 0, colour aspect (depth comes as an R32_SFLOAT colour
+ * image holding 0 near .. 1 far). usage: what the image was made with (the output has STORAGE). */
+typedef struct gt5_vk_image {
+    VkImage           image;
+    VkImageView       view;
+    VkFormat          format;
+    unsigned          w, h;
+    VkImageUsageFlags usage;
+} gt5_vk_image;
+
+/* The renderer's device, for init. */
+typedef struct gt5_vk_device {
+    VkInstance                instance;
+    VkPhysicalDevice          physical_device;
+    VkDevice                  device;
+    VkQueue                   queue;
+    unsigned                  queue_family;
+    PFN_vkGetInstanceProcAddr get_instance_proc_addr;
+    PFN_vkGetDeviceProcAddr   get_device_proc_addr;
+    unsigned                  api_version;          /* the instance's VkApplicationInfo.apiVersion */
+    unsigned                  missing_extensions;   /* how many of the extensions asked for the driver lacked */
+} gt5_vk_device;
+
+/* One frame for the upscaler (gt5_upscale_frame's fields, as Vulkan images). color, depth and motion: their
+ * top-left render_w x render_h is the frame; motion R16G16_SFLOAT, pixels this frame -> the one before, no jitter;
+ * output R8G8B8A8_UNORM at the output size, with STORAGE usage. */
+typedef struct gt5_upscale_vk_frame {
+    VkCommandBuffer cmd;
+    gt5_vk_image    color, depth, motion, output;
+    unsigned        render_w, render_h;
+    float           jitter_x, jitter_y;     /* this frame's sub-pixel offset, in render pixels (y down)        */
+    float           mv_scale_x, mv_scale_y; /* multiplies the vectors into render pixels (0 = 1)              */
+    float           frame_ms;
+    int             reset;
+} gt5_upscale_vk_frame;
+
+/* One drawn frame for a generator (gt5_fg_frame's fields, as Vulkan images; see gt5_upscale.h for each). The

+/*
+ * ps3recomp - the Vulkan renderer's window on Windows: what needs <windows.h>, which
+ * rsx_vulkan_backend.c keeps out (it declares the few user32 calls it makes by hand).
+ *
+ *   rsx_vk_win32_hwnd       the HWND behind the SDL window
+ *   rsx_vk_win32_hook       the in-game menu sees the window's messages first, as it does in the
+ *                           DirectX 12 window's procedure (rsx_null_backend.c, null_wndproc): its key,
+ *                           F11 / Alt+Enter, and every key and click while it is open. SDL's own
+ *                           window procedure gets the rest, unchanged.
+ *   rsx_vk_win32_unhook     SDL's procedure back (before the window goes)
+ *   rsx_vk_win32_cpu_cores  CPU cores busy since the last call (process time over wall time)
+ *   rsx_vk_win32_ask_quit   Esc: "Quit the game?" in the menu's overlay (the window's X asks it too)
+ *   rsx_vk_win32_place      [win] the window placed, kept and remembered as the DirectX 12 one is
+ *   rsx_vk_plugins_*        [up] the DLSS / FSR plug-ins' Vulkan entry sets: loaded before the instance (their
+ *                           extensions), started once the device is there; rsx_vk_upscaler, rsx_vk_fg_provider
+ *
+ * Built only with the Vulkan renderer on Windows (PS3RECOMP_RSX_VULKAN); elsewhere this file is empty.
+ */
+#if defined(_WIN32) && defined(PS3RECOMP_RSX_VULKAN)
+
+#ifndef WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
+#define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
+#endif
+#include <windows.h>
+#include <stdio.h>
+#include <stdlib.h>
+#include <string.h>
+#include <SDL2/SDL.h>
+#include <SDL2/SDL_syswm.h>
+#include "gt5_menu.h"
+#include "gt5_settings.h"
+
+static HWND    s_hwnd;
+static WNDPROC s_sdl_proc;
+static int     s_quitting;   /* the player said Yes to "Quit the game?": the close goes through */
+
+/* "Quit the game?" in the menu's overlay (gt5_menu_ask_quit), as the DirectX 12 window asks it
+ * (rsx_null_backend.c): the window's X, Alt+F4 and the taskbar's Close here, Esc in the renderer
+ * (rsx_vk_win32_ask_quit). Its Yes comes back as GT5_MENU_QUIT_MSG: the window goes, the settings are
+ * written, and SDL is told the window closed, which ends the game cleanly (boot_main.cpp:
+ * rsx_null_backend_quit_now). PS3_QUIT_OVERLAY=0: as before (the X closes at once, Esc asks in SDL's
+ * box). */
+static int vk_quit_overlay_on(void)
+{
+    const char* e = getenv("PS3_QUIT_OVERLAY");
+    return !(e && e[0] == '0' && e[1] == 0);
+}
+
+/* [win] rsx_null_backend.c: the DirectX 12 window's own placement, place in settings.bat and icon. */
+int   rsx_null_window_start_on(void);
+void  rsx_null_window_place(void* hwnd, unsigned render_w, unsigned render_h);
+void  rsx_null_window_place_save(void* hwnd);
+void* rsx_null_window_icon(int size);
+
+/* [win] PS3_WINDOW_START: a borderless window is the whole of a monitor whatever moves or sizes it (the
+ * launcher from outside, Win+Shift+arrow, a change of scaling): the monitor its new rectangle mostly lies
+ * on. As the DirectX 12 window's WM_WINDOWPOSCHANGING (rsx_null_backend.c). */
+static void vk_keep_borderless(HWND hwnd, WINDOWPOS* p)
+{
+    if (!rsx_null_window_start_on() || IsIconic(hwnd)) return;
+    const LONG_PTR style = GetWindowLongPtrW(hwnd, GWL_STYLE);
+    if (!(style & WS_POPUP) || (style & WS_CAPTION) || (style & WS_MINIMIZE) ||
+        ((p->flags & SWP_NOSIZE) && (p->flags & SWP_NOMOVE))) return;
+    RECT cur, want;
+    GetWindowRect(hwnd, &cur);
+    want.left = (p->flags & SWP_NOMOVE) ? cur.left : p->x;
+    want.top = (p->flags & SWP_NOMOVE) ? cur.top : p->y;
+    want.right = want.left + ((p->flags & SWP_NOSIZE) ? cur.right - cur.left : p->cx);
+    want.bottom = want.top + ((p->flags & SWP_NOSIZE) ? cur.bottom - cur.top : p->cy);
+    if (want.left <= -30000 || want.top <= -30000) return;
+    MONITORINFO mi;
+    memset(&mi, 0, sizeof mi);
+    mi.cbSize = sizeof mi;
+    if (!GetMonitorInfoW(MonitorFromRect(&want, MONITOR_DEFAULTTONEAREST), &mi)) return;
+    p->x = mi.rcMonitor.left; p->y = mi.rcMonitor.top;
+    p->cx = mi.rcMonitor.right - mi.rcMonitor.left; p->cy = mi.rcMonitor.bottom - mi.rcMonitor.top;
+    p->flags &= ~(UINT)(SWP_NOMOVE | SWP_NOSIZE);
+}
+
+static LRESULT CALLBACK vk_win_proc(HWND hwnd, UINT msg, WPARAM wp, LPARAM lp)
+{
+    LRESULT r;
+    if (msg == GT5_MENU_QUIT_MSG) {                     /* the overlay's Yes */
+        if (!s_quitting) {
+            s_quitting = 1;
+            fprintf(stderr, "[quit] the player quit\n");
+            rsx_null_window_place_save(hwnd);           /* [win] where it opens next (a plain window only) */
+            if (gt5_settings_dirty()) gt5_settings_save();
+            ShowWindow(hwnd, SW_HIDE);
+        }
+        return CallWindowProcW(s_sdl_proc, hwnd, WM_CLOSE, 0, 0);   /* SDL_QUIT: the game ends */
+    }
+    if (msg == WM_EXITSIZEMOVE) rsx_null_window_place_save(hwnd);   /* [win] dragged or resized: opens there next */
+    if (msg == WM_WINDOWPOSCHANGING) vk_keep_borderless(hwnd, (WINDOWPOS*)lp);
+    if (msg == WM_CLOSE && !s_quitting && vk_quit_overlay_on()) {
+        if (IsIconic(hwnd)) ShowWindow(hwnd, SW_RESTORE);   /* the taskbar's Close on a minimized game */
+        if (gt5_menu_ask_quit() == 1) return 0;            /* it asks; 2 (asked already) or 0 (it can't): close */
+    }
+    if (gt5_menu_wndproc(hwnd, msg, wp, lp, &r)) return r;   /* the menu's key, and everything while it is open */
+    return CallWindowProcW(s_sdl_proc, hwnd, msg, wp, lp);
+}
+
+/* Esc with the menu closed (rsx_vulkan_backend.c): 1 when the overlay now asks "Quit the game?". The
+ * question takes the keys from here on, Esc's release too, so SDL is told Esc went up now: else it
+ * would take the next Esc for a key held down (a repeat) and never ask again. */
+int rsx_vk_win32_ask_quit(void)
+{
+    if (!s_hwnd || s_quitting || !vk_quit_overlay_on() || gt5_menu_ask_quit() != 1) return 0;
+    CallWindowProcW(s_sdl_proc, s_hwnd, WM_KEYUP, VK_ESCAPE, (LPARAM)0xC0010001u);   /* scan code 1, released */
+    return 1;
+}
+
+void* rsx_vk_win32_hwnd(void* sdl_window)
+{
+    SDL_SysWMinfo info;
+    SDL_VERSION(&info.version);
+    if (!sdl_window || !SDL_GetWindowWMInfo((SDL_Window*)sdl_window, &info) || info.subsystem != SDL_SYSWM_WINDOWS) return NULL;
+    return (void*)info.info.win.window;
+}
+
+int rsx_vk_win32_hook(void* hwnd)
+{
+    if (!hwnd || s_hwnd) return s_hwnd == (HWND)hwnd;
+    /* SDL's windows are Unicode windows: the W calls, so nothing is translated on the way through. */
+    WNDPROC old = (WNDPROC)GetWindowLongPtrW((HWND)hwnd, GWLP_WNDPROC);
+    if (!old) return 0;
+    s_sdl_proc = old;
+    s_hwnd = (HWND)hwnd;
+    if (!SetWindowLongPtrW(s_hwnd, GWLP_WNDPROC, (LONG_PTR)vk_win_proc)) { s_hwnd = NULL; s_sdl_proc = NULL; return 0; }
+    return 1;
+}

+/* [win] PS3_WINDOW_START (default 1; 0 = as before): the SDL window, made hidden, is placed and shown as the
+ * DirectX 12 window is (rsx_null_backend.c, null_window_place): borderless full screen on the monitor the
+ * mouse is on (GT5_LAUNCH_WINDOW=borderless, the default, and the first start's migration), maximized, or
+ * a window of PS3_WINDOW_SIZE / its last size / 1280x720 at 100 % scaled to the monitor's scaling, where
+ * it was last or centred; the game's icon. Its procedure is subclassed from here on, so the place is kept
+ * (WM_EXITSIZEMOVE) and a borderless window stays the whole monitor. Returns 0 when it did nothing (the
+ * switch off): the caller shows the window. */
+int rsx_vk_win32_place(void* sdl_window, unsigned render_w, unsigned render_h)
+{
+    HWND hwnd = (HWND)rsx_vk_win32_hwnd(sdl_window);
+    if (!hwnd) return 0;
+    rsx_vk_win32_hook(hwnd);
+    if (!rsx_null_window_start_on()) return 0;
+    HICON big = (HICON)rsx_null_window_icon(GetSystemMetrics(SM_CXICON));
+    HICON sm = (HICON)rsx_null_window_icon(GetSystemMetrics(SM_CXSMICON));
+    if (big) SendMessageW(hwnd, WM_SETICON, ICON_BIG, (LPARAM)big);
+    if (sm) SendMessageW(hwnd, WM_SETICON, ICON_SMALL, (LPARAM)sm);
+    rsx_null_window_place(hwnd, render_w, render_h);
+    return 1;
+}
+
+void rsx_vk_win32_unhook(void)
+{
+    if (!s_hwnd) return;
+    if (IsWindow(s_hwnd) && (WNDPROC)GetWindowLongPtrW(s_hwnd, GWLP_WNDPROC) == vk_win_proc)
+        SetWindowLongPtrW(s_hwnd, GWLP_WNDPROC, (LONG_PTR)s_sdl_proc);
+    s_hwnd = NULL;
+    s_sdl_proc = NULL;
+}
+
+/* Cores busy (process time / wall time) since the call before; -1 the first time. */
+float rsx_vk_win32_cpu_cores(void)
+{
+    static double cpu0;
+    static ULONGLONG t0;
+    FILETIME a, b, k, u;
+    const ULONGLONG now = GetTickCount64();
+    if (!GetProcessTimes(GetCurrentProcess(), &a, &b, &k, &u)) return -1.0f;
+    const double cpu = ((double)(((unsigned long long)k.dwHighDateTime << 32) | k.dwLowDateTime) +
+                        (double)(((unsigned long long)u.dwHighDateTime << 32) | u.dwLowDateTime)) * 1e-7;
+    float cores = -1.0f;
+    if (t0 && now > t0) cores = (float)((cpu - cpu0) * 1000.0 / (double)(now - t0));
+    cpu0 = cpu;
+    t0 = now;
+    return cores;
+}
+
+/* ---- [up] the vendor plug-ins' Vulkan entry sets (gt5_upscale_vk.h) ------------------------------------------------
+ * The same DLLs the Direct3D 12 renderer finds (rsx_upscale.c), next to the executable:
+ *   gt5_upscale_dlss.dll  NVIDIA DLSS (the upscaler) and DLSS Frame Generation
+ *   gt5_upscale_fsr.dll   AMD FSR 3 frame generation
+ * through their "gt5_upscale_get_vk". On Vulkan the vendor's library may need instance and device extensions, which
+ * only the renderer can enable when it makes them, so the plug-ins are loaded BEFORE the instance (rsx_vk_plugins_
+ * preload), asked for those (..._instance_extensions, ..._device_extensions) and started once the device is there
+ * (rsx_vk_plugins_init). A plug-in that is not there, from before Vulkan, or not usable: the renderer carries on and
+ * the choices stay greyed with the reason. Renderer thread only. */
+#include "gt5_upscale_vk.h"
+
+enum { VKP_DLSS = 0, VKP_FSR = 1, VKP_COUNT = 2 };
+static struct {
+    const char* method;            /* the frame generator's name in LD_FG_METHOD */
+    const wchar_t* file;
+    const char* what;              /* for the log */
+    const char* get_it;            /* the launcher's button */
+    HMODULE mod;
+    const gt5_upscale_vk_api* api; /* loaded; started when inited */
+    int inited;
+    gt5_upscale_caps caps;
+    gt5_fg_caps fg;
+} s_vkp[VKP_COUNT] = {
+    { "dlss", L"gt5_upscale_dlss.dll", "the DLSS plug-in", "Get NVIDIA DLSS", NULL, NULL, 0, {0}, {0} },
+    { "fsr",  L"gt5_upscale_fsr.dll",  "the FSR plug-in",  "Get AMD FSR 3",   NULL, NULL, 0, {0}, {0} },
+};
+static int s_vkp_tried;
+
+int rsx_vk_plugins_preload(void)
+{
+    if (s_vkp_tried) { int n = 0; for (int i = 0; i < VKP_COUNT; i++) n += s_vkp[i].api != NULL; return n; }
+    s_vkp_tried = 1;
+    { const char* e = getenv("VK_UPSCALE"); if (e && e[0] == '0') { fprintf(stderr, "[upscale] off (VK_UPSCALE=0)\n"); return 0; } }
+    wchar_t dir[MAX_PATH];
+    const DWORD n = GetModuleFileNameW(NULL, dir, MAX_PATH);
+    wchar_t* cut = n && n < MAX_PATH ? wcsrchr(dir, L'\\') : NULL;
+    if (!cut) return 0;
+    cut[1] = 0;
+    int found = 0;
+    for (int i = 0; i < VKP_COUNT; i++) {
+        wchar_t path[MAX_PATH + 40];
+        _snwprintf(path, MAX_PATH + 40, L"%ls%ls", dir, s_vkp[i].file);
+        path[MAX_PATH + 39] = 0;
+        if (GetFileAttributesW(path) == INVALID_FILE_ATTRIBUTES) {
+            snprintf(s_vkp[i].caps.message, sizeof s_vkp[i].caps.message, "%s is not installed: the launcher's \"%s\" adds it", s_vkp[i].what, s_vkp[i].get_it);
+            snprintf(s_vkp[i].fg.message, sizeof s_vkp[i].fg.message, "not installed: the launcher's \"%s\" adds it", s_vkp[i].get_it);
+            continue;
+        }
+        s_vkp[i].mod = LoadLibraryExW(path, NULL, LOAD_WITH_ALTERED_SEARCH_PATH);
+        if (!s_vkp[i].mod) {
+            const DWORD e = GetLastError();
+            fprintf(stderr, "[upscale] %s could not be loaded (error %lu)\n", s_vkp[i].what, e);
+            snprintf(s_vkp[i].caps.message, sizeof s_vkp[i].caps.message, "%s could not be loaded (Windows error %lu)", s_vkp[i].what, e);
+            snprintf(s_vkp[i].fg.message, sizeof s_vkp[i].fg.message, "%s", s_vkp[i].caps.message);
+            continue;
+        }
+        gt5_upscale_get_vk_fn get = (gt5_upscale_get_vk_fn)(void*)GetProcAddress(s_vkp[i].mod, GT5_UPSCALE_GET_VK_NAME);
+        const gt5_upscale_vk_api* api = get ? get() : NULL;
+        if (!api || api->api_version != GT5_UPSCALE_VK_API_VERSION || !api->init || !api->instance_extensions ||
+            !api->device_extensions || !api->shutdown || !api->last_error) {
+            fprintf(stderr, "[upscale] %s has no Vulkan entry set%s (interface %u): \"%s\" in the launcher builds it again\n",
+                    s_vkp[i].what, get ? " of this version" : "", api ? api->api_version : 0u, s_vkp[i].get_it);
+            snprintf(s_vkp[i].caps.message, sizeof s_vkp[i].caps.message, "%s is from before Vulkan: run \"%s\" in the launcher again",
+                     s_vkp[i].what, s_vkp[i].get_it);
+            snprintf(s_vkp[i].fg.message, sizeof s_vkp[i].fg.message, "%s", s_vkp[i].caps.message);
+            /* (the DLL stays loaded: the Direct3D 12 renderer is not in this run) */
+            continue;
+        }
+        s_vkp[i].api = api;
+        found++;
+    }
+    return found;
+}
+
+/* The extensions the loaded plug-ins name, each once, into out (at most cap). */
+static unsigned vkp_merge(const char** out, unsigned n, unsigned cap, unsigned count, const char* const* names)
+{
+    for (unsigned k = 0; k < count && names; k++) {
+        if (!names[k] || !names[k][0]) continue;
+        unsigned j = 0;
+        while (j < n && strcmp(out[j], names[k])) j++;
+        if (j == n && n < cap) out[n++] = names[k];
+    }
+    return n;
+}
+unsigned rsx_vk_plugins_instance_extensions(const char** out, unsigned cap)
+{
+    unsigned n = 0;
+    for (int i = 0; i < VKP_COUNT; i++) {
+        if (!s_vkp[i].api) continue;
+        unsigned c = 0; const char* const* names = NULL;
+        if (s_vkp[i].api->instance_extensions(&c, &names)) n = vkp_merge(out, n, cap, c, names);
+    }
+    return n;
+}
+unsigned rsx_vk_plugins_device_extensions(VkInstance instance, VkPhysicalDevice phys, PFN_vkGetInstanceProcAddr gipa,
+                                          const char** out, unsigned cap)
+{
+    unsigned n = 0;
+    for (int i = 0; i < VKP_COUNT; i++) {
+        if (!s_vkp[i].api) continue;
+        unsigned c = 0; const char* const* names = NULL;
+        if (s_vkp[i].api->device_extensions(instance, phys, gipa, &c, &names)) n = vkp_merge(out, n, cap, c, names);
+    }
+    return n;
+}
+
+void rsx_vk_plugins_init(const gt5_vk_device* dev)
+{
+    wchar_t dir[MAX_PATH], logs[MAX_PATH + 16] = L".";
+    const DWORD n = GetModuleFileNameW(NULL, dir, MAX_PATH);
+    wchar_t* cut = n && n < MAX_PATH ? wcsrchr(dir, L'\\') : NULL;
+    if (cut) {
+        cut[1] = 0;
+        _snwprintf(logs, MAX_PATH + 16, L"%ls..\\logs", dir);
+        logs[MAX_PATH + 15] = 0;
+        CreateDirectoryW(logs, NULL);
+    }
+    for (int i = 0; i < VKP_COUNT; i++) {
+        if (!s_vkp[i].api || s_vkp[i].inited) continue;
+        const gt5_upscale_vk_api* api = s_vkp[i].api;
+        if (!api->init(dev, logs, &s_vkp[i].caps)) {
+            fprintf(stderr, "[upscale] %s could not start on Vulkan: %s\n", s_vkp[i].what,
+                    s_vkp[i].caps.message[0] ? s_vkp[i].caps.message : api->last_error());
+            if (!s_vkp[i].caps.message[0]) snprintf(s_vkp[i].caps.message, sizeof s_vkp[i].caps.message, "%s could not start", s_vkp[i].what);
+            snprintf(s_vkp[i].fg.message, sizeof s_vkp[i].fg.message, "%s", s_vkp[i].caps.message);
+            s_vkp[i].caps.available = 0;
+            s_vkp[i].api = NULL;
+            continue;
+        }
+        s_vkp[i].inited = 1;
+        if (!api->optimal || !api->create || !api->evaluate || !api->destroy) s_vkp[i].caps.available = 0;
+        if (s_vkp[i].caps.available)
+            fprintf(stderr, "[upscale] %s is available on this graphics card (Vulkan)\n", s_vkp[i].caps.name);
+        else if (api->create)
+            fprintf(stderr, "[upscale] %s is not available here (Vulkan): %s\n", s_vkp[i].caps.name, s_vkp[i].caps.message);
+        if (!api->fg_caps || !api->fg_create || !api->fg_evaluate || !api->fg_destroy || !api->fg_state) {
+            snprintf(s_vkp[i].fg.message, sizeof s_vkp[i].fg.message, "%s has no frame generation", s_vkp[i].what);
+            continue;
+        }
+        if (!api->fg_caps(&s_vkp[i].fg)) {
+            memset(&s_vkp[i].fg, 0, sizeof s_vkp[i].fg);
+            snprintf(s_vkp[i].fg.message, sizeof s_vkp[i].fg.message, "%s did not say whether it can make frames", s_vkp[i].what);
+        }
+        if (s_vkp[i].fg.available && s_vkp[i].fg.max_generated < 1u) s_vkp[i].fg.max_generated = 1u;
+        if (s_vkp[i].fg.available)
+            fprintf(stderr, "[framegen] %s%s%s is available on this graphics card (Vulkan; up to %u made frame%s for each drawn one)\n",
+                    s_vkp[i].fg.name, s_vkp[i].fg.version[0] ? " " : "", s_vkp[i].fg.version, s_vkp[i].fg.max_generated,
+                    s_vkp[i].fg.max_generated == 1u ? "" : "s");
+        else
+            fprintf(stderr, "[framegen] %s is not available here (Vulkan): %s\n", s_vkp[i].fg.name[0] ? s_vkp[i].fg.name : s_vkp[i].what,
+                    s_vkp[i].fg.message);
+    }
+}
+
+const gt5_upscale_vk_api* rsx_vk_upscaler(void)
+{
+    return s_vkp[VKP_DLSS].api && s_vkp[VKP_DLSS].inited && s_vkp[VKP_DLSS].caps.available ? s_vkp[VKP_DLSS].api : NULL;
+}
+const gt5_upscale_caps* rsx_vk_upscaler_caps(void) { return &s_vkp[VKP_DLSS].caps; }
+const gt5_upscale_vk_api* rsx_vk_fg_provider(const char* method)
+{
+    for (int i = 0; i < VKP_COUNT; i++)
+        if (method && !_stricmp(method, s_vkp[i].method))
+            return s_vkp[i].api && s_vkp[i].inited && s_vkp[i].fg.available ? s_vkp[i].api : NULL;
+    return NULL;
+}
+const gt5_fg_caps* rsx_vk_fg_caps(const char* method)
+{
+    static gt5_fg_caps none;
+    for (int i = 0; i < VKP_COUNT; i++)
+        if (method && !_stricmp(method, s_vkp[i].method)) return &s_vkp[i].fg;
+    return &none;
+}
+void rsx_vk_plugins_shutdown(void)
+{
+    for (int i = 0; i < VKP_COUNT; i++) {
+        if (s_vkp[i].api && s_vkp[i].inited) s_vkp[i].api->shutdown();
+        s_vkp[i].inited = 0;
+        s_vkp[i].api = NULL;
+        /* the DLLs stay loaded: NGX keeps threads of its own for a moment after its shutdown */
+    }
+}

+/*
+ * rsx_cull_tags.c -- draws whose triangles an SPU job did NOT cull, and the facing rule the job would
+ * have applied, so the draw can be culled by the graphics card instead.
+ *
+ * GT5's geometry job w018CAD00 culls each batch's triangles on the SPU (facing, off screen, depth,
+ * no sample covered) and writes the draw itself (GT5/src/native/native_w018CAD00.c). With GT5_CULL=1
+ * a native version keeps every triangle of a batch that lies wholly inside the depth range and tags
+ * the draw: index address, index count, the first triangle, the SPU's facing rule. The card rejects
+ * off-screen and pixel-less triangles by itself; facing it rejects only with the draw's cull state, and
+ * that state is the game's, set for the PS3 where the SPU had already removed the back faces. So at
+ * the draw (BEGIN/END, rsx_dispatch.c) the effective cull is the union of the game's and the SPU's:
+ *   game culls the SPU's winding (or both)  -> as the game set it
+ *   game culls nothing                      -> cull enabled, the face that is the SPU's winding under
+ *                                              the game's own FRONT_FACE (front face left as it is)
+ *   game culls the other winding            -> the PS3 drew nothing (SPU and RSX together): no draw
+ * GT5_CULL=2 tags draws only to count the game's state against the SPU's rule ("[cull-draw]"); draws of
+ * the job's other cull routine (rule bit 4) are always report only. The first 24 lookups that find no
+ * tag while tags exist are printed with both sides' values ("[cull-draw] miss").
+ *
+ * Winding. The SPU culls area > 0 in its screen space (flip: area < 0), area = (x1-x0)(y2-y0) -
+ * (x2-x0)(y1-y0) after its viewport scale (sx, sy). The RSX takes winding in window space after its
+ * own VIEWPORT_SCALE (rx, ry) with y downwards whatever the window origin (RPCS3's finding; the D3D12
+ * and Vulkan backends take FRONT_FACE as is, validated). Both come from the same clip space, so the SPU
+ * culls RSX-clockwise triangles when sign(sx*sy) * (flip ? -1 : 1) == sign(rx*ry), else counter-clockwise.
+ * "[cull-draw]" in compare mode shows whether the game's own cull state agrees with this rule on the
+ * draws where it culls at all.
+ *
+ * The table: one entry per 128-byte unit of index address (the job's ring allocations are 128-byte
+ * units, so two live draws never share a slot unless 16 MB of ring lie between them); a seqlock per
+ * entry, written by SPU worker threads, read by the walker. A draw takes a tag only when address,
+ * index count and its first triangle (read from guest memory) all match, so a stale entry left by
+ * an older pass of the ring, or another job's draw at the same address, is never taken.
+ */
+#include "rsx_dispatch.h"
+#include "rsx_vertex_fetch.h"   /* cellGcmResolveLocated */
+#include <stdio.h>
+#include <stdlib.h>
+#include <string.h>
+#ifdef _WIN32
+#  include <windows.h>
+#endif
+
+extern u8* vm_base;
+extern u32 ppu_vm_size;
+
+#define CT_BITS 17u
+#define CT_N    (1u << CT_BITS)
+typedef struct { volatile u32 ver; u32 addr; u32 count; u32 info; } ct_entry;   /* info = first3 (22 bits) | rule << 22 */
+static ct_entry* s_ct;
+
+/* counters: [0] tags put [1] put over another live address [2] put while a writer held the slot
+ * [3] draws looked up [4] found [5] address matched, count or first triangle did not [6] forced
+ * [7] skipped (game culls the other winding) [8..19] compare table: SPU rule (CW, CCW, two-sided)
+ * x game (off, CW, CCW, both) [20] RSX viewport scale zero */
+static unsigned long long s_ct_stat[32];
+/* [24..31] draws of the job's other cull routine (rule bit 4, report only): SPU CW x game (off, CW, CCW,
+ * both), then SPU CCW x game */
+/* the last tags put, for the miss lines (written without care for races: diagnostics only) */
+static u32 s_ct_last[8][2];
+static volatile u32 s_ct_last_n;
+#define CT_ADD(k) __atomic_fetch_add(&s_ct_stat[k], 1ull, __ATOMIC_RELAXED)
+
+int rsx_cull_draw_hook_impl(u32* regs, u32 index_count, u32 saved[3]);
+extern int (*g_rsx_cull_draw_hook)(u32* regs, u32 index_count, u32 saved[3]);
+
+static inline u32 ct_slot(u32 addr) { return (((addr & 0x7FFFFFFFu) >> 7) ^ ((addr >> 31) << 16)) & (CT_N - 1u); }
+
+static int ct_ready(void)
+{
+    if (__atomic_load_n(&s_ct, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) return 1;
+    ct_entry* t = (ct_entry*)calloc(CT_N, sizeof(ct_entry));
+    if (!t) return 0;
+    ct_entry* expect = NULL;
+    if (!__atomic_compare_exchange_n(&s_ct, &expect, t, 0, __ATOMIC_ACQ_REL, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) { free(t); return 1; }
+    __atomic_store_n(&g_rsx_cull_draw_hook, rsx_cull_draw_hook_impl, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
+    return 1;
+}
+
+/* SPU worker side (GT5's native): rule bits 0 two-sided, 1 flip, 2 SPU x scale < 0, 3 SPU y scale < 0,
+ * 8-9 mode (1 the card culls, 2 report only). first3 = i0 << 20 ^ i1 << 10 ^ i2 of the draw's first
+ * triangle. */
+void rsx_cull_tag_put(u32 index_addr, u32 index_count, u32 first3, u32 rule)
+{
+    if (!ct_ready()) return;
+    ct_entry* e = &s_ct[ct_slot(index_addr)];
+    u32 v = __atomic_load_n(&e->ver, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
+    if ((v & 1u) || !__atomic_compare_exchange_n(&e->ver, &v, v + 1u, 0, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE, __ATOMIC_RELAXED)) {
+        CT_ADD(2);
+        return;                                   /* another writer has this slot this instant: no tag */
+    }
+    if (e->addr && e->addr != index_addr) CT_ADD(1);
+    e->addr = index_addr; e->count = index_count; e->info = (first3 & 0x3FFFFFu) | (rule << 22);
+    __atomic_store_n(&e->ver, v + 2u, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
+    CT_ADD(0);
+    const u32 k = __atomic_fetch_add(&s_ct_last_n, 1u, __ATOMIC_RELAXED) & 7u;
+    s_ct_last[k][0] = index_addr; s_ct_last[k][1] = index_count;
+}
+
+/* GT5_CULL's first misses: a draw whose index address no tag has, while tags exist. Both sides' values. */
+static void ct_miss(u32 addr, u32 count, u32 slot_addr, u32 slot_count)
+{
+    static int shown;
+    static unsigned long long misses;
+    if (shown >= 24 || !__atomic_load_n(&s_ct_stat[0], __ATOMIC_RELAXED)) return;
+    misses++;
+    if (shown >= 8 && misses % 5000u) return;          /* the first 8, then every 5000th: most misses are the PPU's own draws */
+    shown++;
+    const u32 ea = cellGcmResolveLocated((addr >> 31) == 0, addr & 0x7FFFFFFFu);
+    u32 i0 = 0xFFFFFFFFu, i1 = 0xFFFFFFFFu, i2 = 0xFFFFFFFFu;
+    if (ea && vm_base && (!ppu_vm_size || (u64)ea + 6u <= ppu_vm_size)) {
+        const u8* q = vm_base + ea;
+        i0 = ((u32)q[0] << 8) | q[1]; i1 = ((u32)q[2] << 8) | q[3]; i2 = ((u32)q[4] << 8) | q[5];
+    }
+    const u32 n = s_ct_last_n;
+    fprintf(stderr, "[cull-draw] miss %d: draw index offset %08X location %u (key %08X, ea %08X) count %u first %u %u %u | slot %u holds %08X count %u | "
+            "last tags (key count):", shown, addr & 0x7FFFFFFFu, addr >> 31, addr, ea, count, i0, i1, i2, ct_slot(addr), slot_addr, slot_count);
+    for (u32 j = 0; j < 8 && j < n; j++) { const u32 k = (n - 1u - j) & 7u; fprintf(stderr, " %08X %u", s_ct_last[k][0], s_ct_last[k][1]); }
+    fprintf(stderr, "\n");
+    fflush(stderr);
+}
+
+static int ct_find(u32 addr, u32 count, u32* rule)
+{
+    if (!s_ct) return 0;
+    const ct_entry* e = &s_ct[ct_slot(addr)];
+    for (int tries = 0; tries < 4; tries++) {
+        const u32 v1 = __atomic_load_n(&e->ver, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
+        if (v1 & 1u) continue;
+        const u32 a = e->addr, c = e->count, info = e->info;
+        __atomic_thread_fence(__ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
+        if (__atomic_load_n(&e->ver, __ATOMIC_RELAXED) != v1) continue;
+        if (a != addr) { ct_miss(addr, count, a, c); return 0; }
+        if (c != count) { CT_ADD(5); return 0; }
+        /* the first triangle in guest memory: 16-bit big-endian indices */
+        const u32 ea = cellGcmResolveLocated((addr >> 31) == 0, addr & 0x7FFFFFFFu);
+        if (!ea || !vm_base || (ppu_vm_size && (u64)ea + 6u > ppu_vm_size)) { CT_ADD(5); return 0; }
+        const u8* p = vm_base + ea;
+        const u32 i0 = ((u32)p[0] << 8) | p[1], i1 = ((u32)p[2] << 8) | p[3], i2 = ((u32)p[4] << 8) | p[5];
+        if ((((i0 << 20) ^ (i1 << 10) ^ i2) & 0x3FFFFFu) != (info & 0x3FFFFFu)) { CT_ADD(5); return 0; }
+        *rule = info >> 22;
+        return 1;
+    }
+    return 0;
+}
+
+static void ct_report(void)
+{
+#ifdef _WIN32
+    static ULONGLONG next;
+    const ULONGLONG now = GetTickCount64();
+    if (now < next) return;
+    const int first = next == 0;
+    next = now + 5000;
+    if (first) return;
+#else
+    return;
+#endif

+            "cull set %llu, not drawn %llu | game cull off/CW/CCW/both: SPU CW %llu/%llu/%llu/%llu, SPU CCW %llu/%llu/%llu/%llu, "
+            "two-sided %llu/%llu/%llu/%llu | viewport scale 0: %llu | other routine (report only): SPU CW %llu/%llu/%llu/%llu, "
+            "SPU CCW %llu/%llu/%llu/%llu\n",
+            s[0], s[1], s[2], s[3], s[4], s[5], s[6], s[7], s[8], s[9], s[10], s[11], s[12], s[13], s[14], s[15],
+            s[16], s[17], s[18], s[19], s[20], s[24], s[25], s[26], s[27], s[28], s[29], s[30], s[31]);
+    fflush(stderr);
+}
+
+static inline float ct_f(u32 u) { float f; memcpy(&f, &u, 4); return f; }
+
+/* The walker, at BEGIN_END(0) of an indexed TRIANGLES draw with index_count indices: 0 = leave the draw
+ * alone, 1 = cull registers changed (old values in saved[], the dispatcher restores them after the
+ * draw), 2 = do not draw. Methods: 0x181C index offset, 0x1820 index location/format, 0x183C cull
+ * enable, 0x1830 cull face, 0x1834 front face, 0x0A30/0x0A34 viewport scale x/y. */
+int rsx_cull_draw_hook_impl(u32* regs, u32 index_count, u32 saved[3])
+{
+    ct_report();
+    const u32 fmt = regs[0x1820 >> 2];
+    if (((fmt >> 4) & 0xFu) != 1u) return 0;                     /* 16-bit indices only */
+    const u32 addr = (regs[0x181C >> 2] & 0x7FFFFFFFu) | ((fmt & 1u) << 31);
+    CT_ADD(3);
+    u32 rule = 0;
+    if (!ct_find(addr, index_count, &rule)) return 0;
+    CT_ADD(4);
+    const u32 en = regs[0x183C >> 2] & 1u, face = regs[0x1830 >> 2], front = regs[0x1834 >> 2];
+    /* what the game culls, in RSX windings */
+    const int ccw_front = front == 0x0901u;
+    int g_cw = 0, g_ccw = 0;
+    if (en) {
+        if (face == 0x0408u) g_cw = g_ccw = 1;
+        else if (face == 0x0405u) { if (ccw_front) g_cw = 1; else g_ccw = 1; }   /* BACK */
+        else if (face == 0x0404u) { if (ccw_front) g_ccw = 1; else g_cw = 1; }   /* FRONT */
+    }
+    const int gi = g_cw && g_ccw ? 3 : g_cw ? 1 : g_ccw ? 2 : 0;
+    const int mode = (int)(rule >> 8) & 3;
+    if (rule & 1u) { CT_ADD(16 + gi); return 0; }             /* two-sided: the SPU culled no facing */
+    const float rx = ct_f(regs[0x0A30 >> 2]), ry = ct_f(regs[0x0A34 >> 2]);
+    if (rx == 0.0f || ry == 0.0f || rx != rx || ry != ry) { CT_ADD(20); return 0; }
+    const int spu_sign = (((rule >> 2) & 1u) ^ ((rule >> 3) & 1u) ^ ((rule >> 1) & 1u)) ? -1 : 1;
+    const int rsx_sign = ((rx < 0.0f) ^ (ry < 0.0f)) ? -1 : 1;
+    const int spu_cw = spu_sign == rsx_sign;                    /* the SPU culls RSX-clockwise triangles */
+    if (rule & 0x10u) { CT_ADD((spu_cw ? 24 : 28) + gi); return 0; }   /* the other cull routine: report only */
+    CT_ADD((spu_cw ? 8 : 12) + gi);
+    if (mode != 1) return 0;
+    if (spu_cw ? g_cw : g_ccw) return 0;                        /* the game culls them already */
+    if (spu_cw ? g_ccw : g_cw) { CT_ADD(7); return 2; }         /* the PS3 drew none of them */
+    saved[0] = regs[0x183C >> 2]; saved[1] = face; saved[2] = front;
+    regs[0x183C >> 2] = 1u;
+    regs[0x1830 >> 2] = (spu_cw == ccw_front) ? 0x0405u : 0x0404u;   /* BACK is clockwise when CCW is front */
+    CT_ADD(6);
+    return 1;
+}

+/* One lock per group of lines (SPU_LOCKLINE_STRIPES, default 1).
+ *
+ * Every lock-line transaction used to take one process-wide lock: in a GT5
+ * race seven SPU workers and the PPU threads spent about 6 % of the workers'
+ * time and 8 % of the PPU threads' spinning on it, almost all of it waiting
+ * while some other line's transaction ran. What the lock has to give is per
+ * line: a GETLLAR copy, a PUTLLC compare-and-commit, a PUT or PPU store into a
+ * reserved line and its notify must not interleave with another transaction on
+ * the SAME 128-byte line. So the lines are spread over LL_STRIPES locks by a
+ * hash of the line address, and a transaction takes the lock of its line
+ * (spu_lockline_lock_line), or of every line it spans (spu_lockline_lock_span).
+ * spu_lockline_lock() still excludes everybody -- it takes every stripe, in
+ * order -- so a caller that touches several lines or the shared lists keeps
+ * exactly the old exclusion. The shared state the transactions touch besides
+ * their line: the list of reserving contexts (pushed with a compare-and-swap,
+ * only removed under spu_lockline_lock), the reserved-line bitmap (atomic OR),
+ * the holder counts and the LR counter (atomic), the watch and kick lists
+ * (changed only under spu_lockline_lock).
+ *
+ * Mode 0 maps every line to stripe 0: one lock, as before. The mode may change
+ * while the game runs (PS3_AB_WHAT=llock): a locker reads the mode, takes the
+ * stripe that mode names and reads the mode again; the changer takes every
+ * stripe before it writes the mode. While anybody holds a stripe the mode
+ * cannot change, so all holders agree on it. Stripes are always taken in
+ * ascending order. SPU_COH_CLEAR_MARKS (which clears bitmap bits outside the
+ * atomic OR) keeps mode 0. */
+#define LL_STRIPES 32u
+#define LL_STRIPE_SHIFT 27u                       /* 32 - log2(LL_STRIPES) */
+typedef struct { volatile long v; char pad[128 - sizeof(long)]; } ll_stripe_t;
+static __declspec(align(128)) ll_stripe_t s_ll[LL_STRIPES];
+static volatile long s_ll_mode = -1;              /* -1 not read yet, 0 one lock, 1 a lock per group of lines */
+static int s_ll_allow = 1;                        /* 0: the environment keeps mode 0 (A/B cannot turn it on) */
+static int s_ll_sleep = -1;
+static unsigned long s_ll_flips;
+static inline unsigned ll_stripe(uint32_t ea) { return (uint32_t)((ea >> 7) * 0x9E3779B1u) >> LL_STRIPE_SHIFT; }

+/* The stripes of every line in [ea, ea + size), as a bit mask. */
+static inline uint32_t ll_span_mask(uint32_t ea, uint32_t size)
+{
+    const uint64_t first = (uint64_t)ea >> 7, last = ((uint64_t)ea + (size ? size : 1) - 1) >> 7;

+static inline int ll_acquire_mask(uint32_t mask_striped)
+{
+    for (;;) {

+static void ll_stat_sum(ll_tstat* cur)
+{
+    memset(cur, 0, sizeof *cur);
+    const long n = s_ll_nthr < 128 ? s_ll_nthr : 128;
+    for (long i = 0; i < n; i++) {
+        const ll_tstat* t = s_ll_thr[i];
+        if (!t) continue;
+        cur->acq += t->acq; cur->cont += t->cont; cur->wait += t->wait; cur->hold += t->hold;
+        cur->n_line += t->n_line; cur->n_span += t->n_span; cur->n_all += t->n_all;
+        for (int k = 0; k < LL_SITES; k++) if (t->site[k].caller) {
+            int j = 0;
+            while (j < LL_SITES && cur->site[j].caller && cur->site[j].caller != t->site[k].caller) j++;
+            if (j == LL_SITES) continue;
+            cur->site[j].caller = t->site[k].caller;
+            cur->site[j].acq += t->site[k].acq; cur->site[j].cont += t->site[k].cont;
+            cur->site[j].wait += t->site[k].wait; cur->site[j].hold += t->site[k].hold;
+        }
+        for (int k = 0; k < LL_LINES; k++) if (t->line[k].acq) {
+            int j = 0;
+            while (j < LL_LINES && cur->line[j].acq && cur->line[j].line != t->line[k].line) j++;
+            if (j == LL_LINES) continue;
+            cur->line[j].line = t->line[k].line; cur->line[j].acq += t->line[k].acq; cur->line[j].cont += t->line[k].cont;
+        }
+    }

+static __declspec(noinline) void ll_stat_lock(int kind, uint32_t mask, uint32_t line, void* caller)
+{
+    ll_tstat* t = ll_tself();
+    const unsigned long long t0 = __rdtsc();
+    const int waited = ll_acquire_mask(mask);
+    const unsigned long long t1 = __rdtsc();
+    if (!t) return;
+    t->acq++; t->cont += waited; t->wait += t1 - t0;
+    if (kind == 0) t->n_line++; else if (kind == 1) t->n_span++; else t->n_all++;
+    int k = (int)(((uintptr_t)caller >> 2) * 0x9E3779B1u >> 27) & (LL_SITES - 1);
+    for (int i = 0; i < LL_SITES && t->site[k].caller && t->site[k].caller != (uintptr_t)caller; i++) k = (k + 1) & (LL_SITES - 1);
+    if (!t->site[k].caller) t->site[k].caller = (uintptr_t)caller;
+    if (t->site[k].caller == (uintptr_t)caller) { t->site[k].acq++; t->site[k].cont += waited; t->site[k].wait += t1 - t0; t->held_site = k; }
+    else t->held_site = -1;
+    if (kind == 0) {
+        ll_lstat* L = &t->line[(line >> 7) * 0x9E3779B1u >> 26];
+        if (L->line != line && L->acq < 8) { L->line = line; L->acq = 0; L->cont = 0; }
+        if (L->line == line) { L->acq++; L->cont += waited; }
+    }
+    t->t_held = __rdtsc();
+}
+static __declspec(noinline) void ll_stat_unlock(uint32_t mask)
+{
+    ll_tstat* t = t_ll;
+    if (t && t->t_held) {
+        const unsigned long long h = __rdtsc() - t->t_held;
+        t->hold += h;
+        if (t->held_site >= 0) t->site[t->held_site].hold += h;
+        t->t_held = 0;
+    }
+    ll_release_mask(mask);
+    if (t && (t->acq & 1023) == 0) ll_stat_print();
+}

+void spu_lockline_lock_line(uint32_t ea)
+{

+/* ===========================================================================
+ * Holder counts
+ *
+ * Marks are never cleared, so in a GT5 race some 700 thousand stores a second
+ * land on marked lines, and fewer than 20 thousand of them end anybody's
+ * reservation. Each one still walked every SPU context and every watch under
+ * the lock, and the PPU store paths walked every PPU context as well: about a
+ * fifth of the game's main thread. This table counts, per hashed line, the
+ * contexts whose coh_hold_line is that line plus the watches on it; a writer
+ * that finds the count at zero has nobody to tell and skips both walks.
+ *
+ * Only the owning thread moves its own coh_hold_line (GETLLAR sets it, a
+ * committed PUTLLC or unregistering clears it), so the count can only be too
+ * high -- a context whose reservation a notifier ended still counts until it
+ * reserves elsewhere, and two lines sharing a slot add up -- and too high only
+ * costs a walk. The lock-free GETLLAR (spu_coh_reserve_fast) counts itself
+ * before its fence and copy; a writer stores, fences, then reads the count.
+ * That is the same store-buffering shape as the reservation itself: either
+ * the writer sees the count or the reader's copy sees the write.
+ * SPU_COH_HOLD=0 turns the skip off (the count is still kept).
+ * ===========================================================================*/
+#define COH_HOLD_SLOTS (1u << 14)
+static volatile long s_coh_hold[COH_HOLD_SLOTS];
+static unsigned long long s_coh_skipped;
+static inline volatile long* coh_hold_slot(uint32_t line)
+{
+    return &s_coh_hold[(line >> SPU_COH_LINE_SHIFT) & (COH_HOLD_SLOTS - 1u)];
+}
+static inline void coh_hold_set(spu_context* c, uint32_t line)
+{
+    const uint32_t old = c->coh_hold_line;
+    if (old == line) return;
+    __atomic_fetch_add(coh_hold_slot(line), 1, __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST);
+    c->coh_hold_line = line;
+    if (old) __atomic_fetch_sub(coh_hold_slot(old), 1, __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST);
+}
+void spu_coh_hold_drop(spu_context* c)
+{
+    if (!c) return;
+    const uint32_t old = c->coh_hold_line;
+    if (!old) return;
+    c->coh_hold_line = 0;
+    __atomic_fetch_sub(coh_hold_slot(old), 1, __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST);
+}
+static int coh_hold_skip_on(void)
+{
+    static int on = -1;
+    if (on < 0) { const char* e = getenv("SPU_COH_HOLD"); on = !(e && *e == '0'); }
+    return on;
+}
+/* After the writer's fence: nobody holds or watches this line. */
+static inline int coh_nobody_holds(uint32_t line)
+{

+/* ===========================================================================
+ * Versioned lines (SPU_LL_LAZY, rpcs3cmp lead 4)
+ *
+ * Every write a notifier reports (a PUTLLC or PUTLLUC commit, an MFC PUT or SDCRZ, a PPU store or
+ * stwcx. to a marked line, an HLE write) adds one to its line's version, under the line's lock-line
+ * lock, after the data is stored and before anyone is looked for. An SPU's GETLLAR of a marked line
+ * can then hold its reservation "lazily" (spu_channels.c): it reads the version, copies the line, and
+ * neither counts itself as a holder nor joins the walk; its PUTLLC fails if the version moved, and
+ * the lost-reservation event is raised where the SPU can look for it (its next GETLLAR, PUTLLC,
+ * PUTLLUC, RdEventStat read or count, WrEventAck, WrEventMask) instead of by the writer. A reservation
+ * whose SPU has the event enabled (event mask bit 0x400, needed both to take it as an interrupt and to
+ * sleep on it) is never lazy: WrEventMask turns a lazy one into an ordinary one under the line's lock.
+ *
+ * One 32-bit version per line, 2^20 slots indexed by line number, so two lines share a slot only 128 MB
+ * apart; a write to one then fails a lazy PUTLLC on the other (a spurious lost reservation, which the
+ * guest's retry loop absorbs). Slots are only ever added to, atomically (lines of one slot can sit
+ * under different stripe locks).
+ * ===========================================================================*/

+uint32_t spu_ll_version(uint32_t ea) { return __atomic_load_n(ll_ver_slot(ea & ~127u), __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE); }
+/* Returns the version before the bump. */
+static inline uint32_t ll_ver_bump(uint32_t line) { return __atomic_fetch_add(ll_ver_slot(line), 1u, __ATOMIC_ACQ_REL); }

+ * plain store; this keeps the notify for lines an SPU actually holds and gives the rest the plain
+ * path back. A PUTLLC still compares the whole line, so a store that slips past an unmarked line
+ * still fails the reservation it races with.
+ * EXPERIMENTAL, off: SPU_COH_CLEAR_MARKS=1 turns it on. Tested 2026-11-06, GT5 froze for good
+ * (0 fps) on the car-colour screen, where the car model loads on the SPUs; with marks kept it
+ * did not. A wakeup is probably lost somewhere a notify used to guarantee it -- not found yet. */
+static unsigned long long s_coh_unmarked;
+static void spu_coh_maybe_unmark(uint32_t line, const void* self)
+{
+    static int on = -1;
+    if (on < 0) on = getenv("SPU_COH_CLEAR_MARKS") ? 1 : 0;
+    if (!on) return;
+    for (spu_coh_watch* w = s_coh_watches; w; w = w->next)
+        if (w->line == line) return;
+    const uint32_t l = line >> SPU_COH_LINE_SHIFT;
+    const unsigned char bit = (unsigned char)(1u << (l & 7));
+    if (!(s_coh_bitmap[l >> 3] & bit)) return;
+    s_coh_bitmap[l >> 3] &= (unsigned char)~bit;
+    spu_coh_writer_fence();
+    for (spu_coh_entry* entry = __atomic_load_n(&s_coh_ctxs, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE); entry; entry = entry->next) {
+        const spu_context* c = entry->ctx;
+        if (c && spu_coh_holds(c, line)) {        /* self, or a fast-path reader that just published */
+            s_coh_bitmap[l >> 3] |= bit;
+            (void)self;
+            return;
+        }
+    }
+    s_coh_unmarked++;
+}

+/* Lines whose PPU stores must reach a host-side scheduler at once: the request
+ * line of each live SPURS instance (wklReadyCount1 and wklSignal1 live there).
+ * The scheduler wakes immediately on an SPU commit to that line (the PUTLLC
+ * commit hook), but a PPU store -- GT5 kicks its job chains from the main
+ * thread -- waited for the scheduler's 1 ms poll, 1-2 ms with the 1 ms timer,
+ * several times a frame. spu_coh_ppu_after runs the hook for these lines after
+ * the store's lock is released. SPU_COH_PPU_KICK=0 turns it off. */
+#define SPU_KICK_LINES 8
+static uint32_t s_kick_lines[SPU_KICK_LINES];
+static volatile long s_kick_n;
+static void (*s_ppu_kick_hook)(uint32_t line);
+void spu_coh_kick_line_add(uint32_t line, void (*hook)(uint32_t))
+{
+    static int on = -1;
+    if (on < 0) { const char* e = getenv("SPU_COH_PPU_KICK"); on = !(e && *e == '0'); }
+    if (!on) return;
+    line &= ~127u;
+    spu_lockline_lock();

+    int have = 0;
+    for (long i = 0; i < n; i++) if (s_kick_lines[i] == line) have = 1;
+    if (!have && n < SPU_KICK_LINES) {
+        s_kick_lines[n] = line;
+        s_ppu_kick_hook = hook;
+        __atomic_store_n(&s_kick_n, n + 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
+    }
+    /* Marked, so every PPU store to it takes the coherent path that ends here. */
+    spu_coh_reserve(NULL, line);
+    spu_lockline_unlock();
+}
+/* After a PPU store to a marked line, with no lock held. */
+void spu_coh_ppu_after(uint32_t ea)
+{
+    const long n = __atomic_load_n(&s_kick_n, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
+    if (!n) return;
+    const uint32_t line = ea & ~127u;
+    for (long i = 0; i < n; i++)
+        if (s_kick_lines[i] == line) { s_ppu_kick_hook(line); return; }
+}

+/* A store by a PPU thread (lifted guest code or an HLE writer). The same as

+/* Native forms of the two interpreted pieces of the WWS job manager's interrupt path.
+ *
+ * Sony's WWS job manager (in GT5 the policy module j75BFE68A, loaded at LS 0xA00) takes an SPU
+ * interrupt for every DMA-list stall-and-notify -- two per job and two more per run that flushes
+ * shared buffers, each delivered twice -- and its handler is the part of it the runtime cannot run
+ * as lifted code:
+ *
+ *   - the handler entry, LS 0xA2C..0xA5C (13 instructions). Only the vector word the manager writes
+ *     at LS 0 at run time points there, so no lift has it. Today: a dispatch miss, 15
+ *     micro-interpreter steps, then the full interpreter (spu_step) from the stqx at 0xA68 until it
+ *     rejoins the lifted loop at 0xA60.
+ *   - the code the handler WRITES at LS 0x3FEC0 and calls twice per interrupt: 76 `stqa` saving
+ *     r0..r75 to 0x3F9C0.., later 76 `lqa` restoring them, each followed by `bi $r79`. Today: a
+ *     dispatch miss through the full resolver, then the micro-interpreter, both times.
+ *
+ * Here both are done directly, and only when the local store holds exactly the instruction words
+ * they are made of (the 13 entry words; the 76 generated words and the `bi`); otherwise 0 is
+ * returned and the caller interprets as before. So the guest sees the same thing instruction for
+ * instruction: the same registers, the same local-store bytes, the same next pc. Nothing depends on
+ * the title: the words are checked, not the image.
+ *
+ * Self-contained (spu_context fields only) so the stand-alone check (perf1 unit\test_wws_irq_native.c)
+ * includes this very file. The caller must not use it while a local-store watch or probe is armed
+ * (they would miss these accesses) and must set the trampoline after a return of 1. */
+#ifndef SPU_WWS_IRQ_NATIVE_H
+#define SPU_WWS_IRQ_NATIVE_H
+
+#include <stdint.h>
+
+#define SPU_WWS_IRQ_ENTRY  0xA2Cu
+#define SPU_WWS_IRQ_STUB   0x3FEC0u
+
+static inline uint32_t spu_wwsn_be32(const uint8_t* p)
+{
+    return ((uint32_t)p[0] << 24) | ((uint32_t)p[1] << 16) | ((uint32_t)p[2] << 8) | p[3];
+}
+
+/* stqa / lqa: the quadword in local-store (big-endian) order: each 32-bit lane byte-swapped. One
+ * 16-byte shuffle where SSSE3 is compiled in (the runtime is built with SSE4.1), four byte swaps
+ * otherwise; the same bytes either way. */
+#if defined(__SSSE3__)
+#include <tmmintrin.h>
+static inline __m128i spu_wwsn_swap(__m128i v)
+{
+    return _mm_shuffle_epi8(v, _mm_set_epi8(12, 13, 14, 15, 8, 9, 10, 11, 4, 5, 6, 7, 0, 1, 2, 3));
+}
+static inline void spu_wwsn_st(spu_context* ctx, uint32_t lsa, const u128* r)
+{
+    _mm_storeu_si128((__m128i*)&ctx->ls[lsa & SPU_LS_MASK & ~0xFu], spu_wwsn_swap(_mm_loadu_si128((const __m128i*)r)));
+}
+static inline void spu_wwsn_ld(const spu_context* ctx, uint32_t lsa, u128* r)
+{
+    _mm_storeu_si128((__m128i*)r, spu_wwsn_swap(_mm_loadu_si128((const __m128i*)&ctx->ls[lsa & SPU_LS_MASK & ~0xFu])));
+}
+#else
+static inline void spu_wwsn_st(spu_context* ctx, uint32_t lsa, const u128* r)
+{
+    uint8_t* p = &ctx->ls[lsa & SPU_LS_MASK & ~0xFu];
+    for (int k = 0; k < 4; k++) {
+        const uint32_t w = r->_u32[k];
+        p[4 * k] = (uint8_t)(w >> 24); p[4 * k + 1] = (uint8_t)(w >> 16);
+        p[4 * k + 2] = (uint8_t)(w >> 8); p[4 * k + 3] = (uint8_t)w;
+    }
+}
+
+static inline void spu_wwsn_ld(const spu_context* ctx, uint32_t lsa, u128* r)
+{
+    const uint8_t* p = &ctx->ls[lsa & SPU_LS_MASK & ~0xFu];
+    for (int k = 0; k < 4; k++) r->_u32[k] = spu_wwsn_be32(p + 4 * k);
+}
+#endif
+
+static inline void spu_wwsn_splat(u128* r, uint32_t v)
+{
+    r->_u32[0] = r->_u32[1] = r->_u32[2] = r->_u32[3] = v;
+}
+
+/* LS 0xA2C..0xA5C of the job manager (raw words, as in its image):
+ *   lnop; nop; stqa $78,0x1530; il $78,0; hbrr 0xA6C,0xA60;
+ *   stqa $76,0x3FE80; stqa $77,0x3FE90; stqa $78,0x3FEA0; stqa $79,0x3FEB0;
+ *   ila $76,0x3FEC0; lqa $77,0xA40; ila $78,0x130; ila $79,0x804        -> on at 0xA60 */
+static const uint32_t k_spu_wws_irq_entry[13] = {
+    0x00200000u, 0x40200000u, 0x2082A64Eu, 0x4080004Eu, 0x1200048Cu, 0x20FFD04Cu, 0x20FFD24Du,
+    0x20FFD44Eu, 0x20FFD64Fu, 0x43FF604Cu, 0x3081484Du, 0x4200984Eu, 0x4204024Fu,
+};
+
+/* Returns 1 with ctx->pc = 0xA60 when LS 0xA2C holds the entry above, else 0 (nothing changed). */
+static inline int spu_wws_irq_entry_native(spu_context* ctx)
+{
+    const uint8_t* l = &ctx->ls[SPU_WWS_IRQ_ENTRY];
+    for (int i = 0; i < 13; i++)
+        if (spu_wwsn_be32(l + 4 * i) != k_spu_wws_irq_entry[i]) return 0;
+    spu_wwsn_st(ctx, 0x1530, &ctx->gpr[78]);        /* stqa $78,0x1530 */
+    spu_wwsn_splat(&ctx->gpr[78], 0);               /* il   $78,0      */
+    spu_wwsn_st(ctx, 0x3FE80, &ctx->gpr[76]);       /* stqa $76..$79   */
+    spu_wwsn_st(ctx, 0x3FE90, &ctx->gpr[77]);
+    spu_wwsn_st(ctx, 0x3FEA0, &ctx->gpr[78]);
+    spu_wwsn_st(ctx, 0x3FEB0, &ctx->gpr[79]);
+    spu_wwsn_splat(&ctx->gpr[76], 0x3FEC0);         /* ila  $76,0x3FEC0 */
+    spu_wwsn_ld(ctx, 0xA40, &ctx->gpr[77]);         /* lqa  $77,0xA40   */
+    spu_wwsn_splat(&ctx->gpr[78], 0x130);           /* ila  $78,0x130   */
+    spu_wwsn_splat(&ctx->gpr[79], 0x804);           /* ila  $79,0x804   */
+    ctx->pc = 0xA60;
+    return 1;
+}
+
+/* What LS 0x3FEC0 holds: 1 the save code, 2 the restore code, 0 anything else. Word j of quadword
+ * m (m = 0..18, j = 0..3) is `stqa`/`lqa` of register 4m+j at 0x3F9C0 + 16*(4m+j) -- the handler
+ * makes it from the four words at 0xA40 / 0xAD0 by subtracting 0x804 per quadword -- and
+ * 0x3FFF0 holds `bi $79`. Nothing after that `bi` runs, so nothing after it is checked. */
+/* The two codes as bytes (76 words and the `bi`), made once: the check is then two 308-byte compares
+ * at most instead of 77 words assembled from bytes, on every one of the two calls per interrupt. */
+static uint8_t s_wwsn_img[2][0x134];
+static volatile int s_wwsn_img_ready;
+static void spu_wwsn_img_make(void)
+{
+    for (int k = 0; k < 2; k++) {
+        const uint32_t base = (k ? 0x30FFD04Cu : 0x20FFD04Cu) - 19u * 0x804u;
+        for (uint32_t r = 0; r < 77; r++) {
+            const uint32_t w = r < 76 ? base + r * 0x201u : 0x35002780u;
+            s_wwsn_img[k][4 * r] = (uint8_t)(w >> 24); s_wwsn_img[k][4 * r + 1] = (uint8_t)(w >> 16);
+            s_wwsn_img[k][4 * r + 2] = (uint8_t)(w >> 8); s_wwsn_img[k][4 * r + 3] = (uint8_t)w;
+        }
+    }
+    __atomic_store_n(&s_wwsn_img_ready, 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);   /* the same bytes from every thread */
+}
+static inline int spu_wws_irq_stub_kind(const uint8_t* ls)
+{
+    const uint8_t* p = ls + SPU_WWS_IRQ_STUB;
+    if (!__atomic_load_n(&s_wwsn_img_ready, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) spu_wwsn_img_make();
+    /* Word 0 says which one it could be (stqa $0 or lqa $0 at 0x3F9C0), as before. */
+    const int kind = p[0] == s_wwsn_img[0][0] ? 1 : p[0] == s_wwsn_img[1][0] ? 2 : 0;
+    if (!kind) return 0;
+    return memcmp(p, s_wwsn_img[kind - 1], sizeof s_wwsn_img[0]) == 0 ? kind : 0;
+}
+
+/* Returns 1 with ctx->pc = $79 (the `bi`) when LS 0x3FEC0 holds the save or restore code, else 0. */
+static inline int spu_wws_irq_stub_native(spu_context* ctx)
+{
+    const int kind = spu_wws_irq_stub_kind(ctx->ls);
+    if (!kind) return 0;
+    if (kind == 1)
+        for (uint32_t r = 0; r < 76; r++) spu_wwsn_st(ctx, 0x3F9C0u + 16u * r, &ctx->gpr[r]);
+    else
+        for (uint32_t r = 0; r < 76; r++) spu_wwsn_ld(ctx, 0x3F9C0u + 16u * r, &ctx->gpr[r]);
+    ctx->pc = ctx->gpr[79]._u32[0] & SPU_LS_MASK & ~3u;
+    return 1;
+}
+
+#endif /* SPU_WWS_IRQ_NATIVE_H */

+/* ---- [res] Resolution: the game's screen-sized targets drawn at a scale ----------------------------------------
+ * The DirectX 12 renderer's resolution scale (rsx_live_draw.c, "Internal resolution scale", g_rs_* / ld_rs_*) for a
+ * backend that says it can (rsx_draw_backend.rs_max_dim: Vulkan). LD_RES_TARGET=<lines> (the menu's Resolution row:
+ * 720, 1080, 1440, 2160, 2880; scale = lines / the video mode's height) or LD_RES_SCALE=<s> (0.25 .. 8), read at
+ * every flip through the settings registry and applied between two frames (eng_rs_flip).
+ * Every guest-side number stays the guest's: a surface keeps its guest size in w / h (the clip times the antialias
+ * grid), and addresses, pitches, clips and texture sizes are untouched; its image is w x h times eng_surface.rs.
+ * Which surfaces: eng_rs_pick, DirectX 12's rule (screen-sized ones: at least 4/5 of the mode's height and half its
+ * width in pixels, not both sides powers of two). Shadow maps, cube faces, the mirror, bloom, particle and text
+ * targets stay at the guest's size. Then, as DirectX 12 does:
+ *   - a draw runs at its colour target's scale (eng_rs_pass: a pass that writes no colour may run at guest size, with
+ *     a colour target of the engine's own); its viewport, scissor and clears are scaled, polygon offset's slope with
+ *     them, and a program that reads WPOS gets a variant that divides it back (fp_alpha.w = 1 / scale);
+ *   - a zeta has an entry per scale it is drawn at (eng_zdepth.rs), all one guest size; a read of the address takes
+ *     the entry with the newest of what it reads (eng_rs_zread), and a clear clears them all;
+ *   - textures read a scaled surface by normalized coordinates (texel coordinates are divided by the guest
+ *     texture's size; a depth compare's by the bound map's, so they are multiplied by the scale): windows, regions,
+ *     feedback copies and depth copies are taken at the scaled size;
+ *   - what goes to guest memory (2D transfers, a surface or zeta read in another format) is reduced to the guest
+ *     size: the texel under each guest texel's centre for small rectangles and for depth, a box for large colour
+ *     ones; what comes from guest memory is enlarged, each guest texel to its block;
+ *   - the frame is the scanout at the scale (present_frame); the backend filters it into the window;
+ *   - a change of scale makes the surfaces it moves again (what they show drawn across: color_target_blit) and lets
+ *     go of the zeta entries of scales nothing is drawn at any more.
+ * Left as DirectX 12 leaves them: cube faces and the mirror (never scaled; a scaled face is refused), a 2x2 sample
+ * grid (counts as twice the scale; LD_RES_AA=1 multiplies it too), a 2x1 grid (multiplied).
+ * Not here, though DirectX 12 has them: LD_RES_SCENE (Photo Mode's small 3D window made as sharp as the window it is
+ * shown in: it needs the scene / HUD line, which comes with DLSS), the upscaler's own scene scale, LD_RES_OUT (the
+ * window's size is the backend's, which filters any frame size into it).
+ * With no scale asked for, every rs is exactly 1.0f, eng_rs_hs / eng_rs_he return their argument and none of the
+ * new branches is taken. A backend that leaves rs_max_dim 0 (VK_RES_SCALE=0 on Vulkan): no scale, as before.
+ * ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ */
+#define ENG_RS_MAX_TEXELS  (7680ull * 4320ull)     /* one image: no more than an 8K frame (DirectX 12's limit) */
+#define ENG_RS_MIN_SCALE   0.25f
+#define ENG_RS_MAX_SCALE   8.0f
+#define ENG_RS_LOC_DEAD    0xFFFFFFFFu             /* a zeta entry a change of scale let go */
+static struct {
+    float user;               /* the scale in force (1: none) */
+    int   on;                 /* user != 1 */
+    float want;               /* what the settings ask for, applied at the next flip */
+    unsigned gen; int have_gen;
+    int   read;               /* the switches below were read */
+    int   aa_mul, depth_rule, zsync, passlog;
+    u32   min_w, min_h;
+    u32   skip[16], n_skip, only[16], n_only;
+    u32   cycle_ms;           /* LD_RES_CYCLE=<seconds> (tests) */
+    unsigned long long cycle_at;
+    int   cycle_up;
+    u32   logs, pass_logs, read_logs, fail_logs;
+    u32   frame_w, frame_h;   /* the frame last presented at a scale (its log line) */
+    /* [up] The 3D scene at a scale of its own (rsx_live_draw.c g_rs_scene_*): while scene_on, the surface at this
+     * address and guest size is made at scene_rs whatever eng_rs_pick says, and passes into it with the clip
+     * scene_cw x scene_ch run at that scale. Every other surface gets exactly what it got. scene_owner: 1 the
+     * upscaler (its render size), 2 LD_RES_SCENE (the 3D picture as sharp as the window it is shown in). */
+    int   scene_on, scene_owner, scene_follow;
+    float scene_rs;
+    u32   scene_loc, scene_off, scene_w, scene_h, scene_cw, scene_ch;
+} s_rs = { .user = 1.0f, .want = 1.0f, .scene_rs = 1.0f, .scene_follow = -1 };
+#define eng_rs_log(...) do { if (s_rs.logs < 64u) { s_rs.logs++; fprintf(stderr, "[res-scale] " __VA_ARGS__); } } while (0)
