+/* spu_jcap.h -- job capture: what one SPU job sees of the world, written to a file a stand-alone
+ * harness can replay (the replay library: GT5 native round, n_jobmgr\replay\jcap_replay.c).
+ *
+ *   SPU_JOB_CAPTURE=<image>[,<image>...]   images to capture: w018CAD00, w01695680, j75BFE68A, jD58063CD, ...
+ *                                          ("*" = every image, "w*" / "j*" = every job / chain image)
+ *   SPU_JOB_CAPTURE_DIR=<dir>              where the files go (default %TEMP%\gt5_jcap)
+ *   SPU_JOB_CAPTURE_N=<n>                  captures per image (default 8)
+ *   SPU_JOB_CAPTURE_SKIP=<n>               jobs of each image passed over before the first capture (default 0)
+ *   SPU_JOB_CAPTURE_EVERY=<k>              then capture every k-th job of the image (default 1)
+ *
+ * What a "job" is, by the image's kind:
+ *   1  a WWS job (w-images): the job manager's call into the job (the `bisl` at LS 0x327C of j75BFE68A,
+ *      return address 0x3280) up to the job's return there: through the manager's drain, or (GT5's jobs: their
+ *      crt returns through a computed link, LS 0x40DC, where nothing is lifted, so the drain unwinds and the
+ *      run's driver re-dispatches) when the pc first reaches 0x3280 again (flag SPU_JCAP_F_UNWOUND);
+ *   2  a SPURS job-chain job (the sound j-images): spu_run_spurs_job's run of the job;
+ *   3  a policy-module run (j75BFE68A, the WWS job manager itself): one spu_run_policy_module run, with
+ *      every job it ran inside it.
+ * At the start: the 128 registers, the 256 KB local store and the context's other fields. During the job, in
+ * order: every channel write (with the MFC command's parameters), channel read (with the value read) and
+ * channel count, each DMA transfer the MFC made for it (GET: the bytes that landed in local store; PUT: the
+ * bytes sent), each lock-line command (the line before and after), the context fields after each operation,
+ * and each interrupt taken. At the end: the registers, local store and fields again.
+ * Off (no SPU_JOB_CAPTURE): one test of g_spu_jcap_on in spu_wrch / spu_rdch / spu_rchcnt / the MFC transfer
+ * and lock-line paths, nothing else. On: dispatch and channel short paths are off for the whole run
+ * (g_spu_dfast = 0, g_spu_ch_inline = 0) so every dispatch and channel access reaches the hooks.
+ *
+ * File layout (all integers little-endian; local store bytes as the SPU sees them, big-endian words;
+ * a register is the runtime's u128: _u32[0] is the preferred word):
+ *   spu_jcap_file_header
+ *   entry registers   u128[128]
+ *   entry irq_gpr     u128[128]   (the register copy of an interrupt in progress; irq_saved says if it counts)
+ *   entry local store 256 KB
+ *   records           n_records x (spu_jcap_rec + payload)
+ *   exit block        (when flags & SPU_JCAP_F_COMPLETE): spu_jcap_state, u128[128], 256 KB local store
+ * The header's crc32 covers all of it; a reader refuses a file whose size, CRC or record chain is off.
+ */
+#ifndef SPU_JCAP_H
+#define SPU_JCAP_H
+#include <stddef.h>
+#include <stdint.h>
+
+#ifdef __cplusplus
+extern "C" {
+#endif
+
+#define SPU_JCAP_MAGIC    "GT5JCAP1"
+#define SPU_JCAP_VERSION  2u          /* 2: RESTART records, F_UNWOUND, the end at 0x3280 outside the drain */
+
+/* The WWS job manager's return point after its call of a job (j75BFE68A: `bisl $0,$5` at 0x327C). */
+#define SPU_JCAP_WWS_RETURN 0x3280u
+
+enum {
+    SPU_JCAP_KIND_WWS_JOB    = 1,
+    SPU_JCAP_KIND_CHAIN_JOB  = 2,
+    SPU_JCAP_KIND_POLICY_RUN = 3,
+};
+
+#define SPU_JCAP_F_COMPLETE   1u      /* the exit block is present */
+#define SPU_JCAP_F_TRUNCATED  2u      /* records stopped at the size cap: not replayable to the end */
+#define SPU_JCAP_F_ABORTED    4u      /* the run ended without the job's return (a halt, the run's end) */
+#define SPU_JCAP_F_UNWOUND    8u      /* the job came back outside its drain: its return landed where nothing is
+                                         lifted (a WWS job's computed link, LS 0x40DC), the drain unwound the host
+                                         frames (RESTART record), and the job ended when the pc reached 0x3280 */
+
+/* The context's fields besides registers and local store (spu_context.h names). */
+typedef struct spu_jcap_state {
+    uint32_t pc, status, stop_code, int_enable;
+    uint32_t srr0, event_status, event_mask, decrementer;
+    uint32_t mfc_lsa, mfc_eah, mfc_eal, mfc_size;
+    uint32_t mfc_tag, mfc_tag_mask, mfc_tag_status, atomic_stat;
+    uint32_t resv_ea, resv_valid, list_stall_mask, list_stall_stat;
+    uint32_t irq_saved, irq_resume_pc, irq_stall_seen, host_depth;
+    uint32_t steps, policy_mode, drain_ret_pc, spu_id;
+    uint32_t out_mbox_count, out_mbox_value, out_intr_mbox_count, out_intr_mbox_value;
+    uint32_t in_mbox_count, in_mbox_value, sig1_count, sig1_value;
+    uint32_t sig2_count, sig2_value, image_id, resident_ovl;
+    uint32_t resident_task, module_img_a00, park_on_empty_inmbox, spu_group_id;
+} spu_jcap_state;                                   /* 44 words */
+
+/* One resident code slot of the context (spu_context.resident_code[]), with its image's name. */
+typedef struct spu_jcap_slot {
+    uint32_t lsa, size, source_ea, image_id;
+    int32_t  verify_state, source_index;
+    char     name[16];                              /* "w018CAD00"; "" for an empty slot */
+} spu_jcap_slot;
+
+typedef struct spu_jcap_file_header {
+    char     magic[8];                              /* SPU_JCAP_MAGIC */
+    uint32_t version, header_size;                  /* SPU_JCAP_VERSION, sizeof(spu_jcap_file_header) */
+    char     image[16];                             /* the captured image ("w018CAD00") */
+    char     ctx_image[16];                         /* name of the context's image_id at the start ("j75BFE68A") */
+    char     ovl_image[16];                         /* name of resident_ovl ("" if none) */
+    uint32_t kind, seq;                             /* SPU_JCAP_KIND_*; this image's capture number (0..) */
+    uint32_t job_no;                                /* which job of this image it was, counting from 1 */
+    uint32_t flags;                                 /* SPU_JCAP_F_* */
+    uint32_t entry_pc, return_pc;                   /* kind 1: the job's entry and 0x3280; else 0 */
+    uint32_t mxcsr;                                 /* host MXCSR at the start (the SPU float mode) */
+    uint32_t wid, spu_num;                          /* LS 0x1DC / 0x1C8 of a WWS context; job-chain: 0 */
+    uint32_t n_records;
+    uint64_t records_bytes;                         /* bytes of the record section */
+    uint64_t t_start_ns, t_end_ns;                  /* host time (information only) */
+    uint32_t entry_fn_addr;                         /* kind 2/3: LS address of the entry function the runner called */
+    uint32_t crc32;                                 /* CRC-32 (zlib's) of the whole file, this field taken as 0 */
+    uint32_t reserved[6];
+    spu_jcap_slot  slots[4];                        /* resident_code[0..3] at the start */
+    spu_jcap_state entry;
+} spu_jcap_file_header;
+
+/* Every record: this head, then `len` payload bytes. */
+typedef struct spu_jcap_rec {
+    uint16_t type, flags;
+    uint32_t len;
+    uint32_t a, b;
+} spu_jcap_rec;
+
+enum {
+    /* wrch: a = channel, b = value word 0. Payload spu_jcap_wrch. Followed by its XFER / ATOMIC records,
+     * then POST. */
+    SPU_JCAP_R_WRCH   = 1,
+    /* rdch: a = channel, b = value word 0. Payload spu_jcap_rdch. Then POST. */
+    SPU_JCAP_R_RDCH   = 2,
+    /* rchcnt: a = channel, b = the count. Payload spu_jcap_opctx. Then POST. */
+    SPU_JCAP_R_RCHCNT = 3,
+    /* One transfer the MFC made: a = command, b = size. Payload spu_jcap_xfer + `size` bytes when
+     * flags & SPU_JCAP_XF_DATA (GET: local store after; PUT: local store before). */
+    SPU_JCAP_R_XFER   = 4,
+    /* A lock-line command (GETLLAR, PUTLLC, PUTLLUC, PUTQLLUC): a = command, b = effective address. Payload
+     * spu_jcap_atomic: the 128-byte local-store line before and after. */
+    SPU_JCAP_R_ATOMIC = 5,
+    /* The context's fields after an operation. Payload spu_jcap_post. */
+    SPU_JCAP_R_POST   = 6,
+    /* An interrupt taken: a = srr0 (the interrupted pc), b = the handler's address. Payload spu_jcap_irq. */
+    SPU_JCAP_R_IRQ    = 7,
+    /* The last record: a = number of records before it. */
+    SPU_JCAP_R_END    = 8,
+    /* The run's driver (spu_run_with_halt) took over: a = how (2: a non-local return, spu_restart_dispatch,
+     * landed in its `case 2`; 3: one landed in its carry-on loop; 4: its drain emptied with the SPU still
+     * running and the loop carries on), b = pc. Payload spu_jcap_opctx (pc, lr = drain_ret_pc, host_depth,
+     * int_enable as the driver found them). */
+    SPU_JCAP_R_RESTART = 9,
+};
+
+#define SPU_JCAP_XF_DATA  1u        /* the bytes follow */
+#define SPU_JCAP_XF_PUT   2u        /* main memory was written (else read) */
+
+typedef struct spu_jcap_opctx { uint32_t pc, lr, host_depth, int_enable; } spu_jcap_opctx;
+typedef struct spu_jcap_wrch {
+    uint32_t value[4];                              /* the u128 written (_u32[0..3]) */
+    uint32_t mfc_lsa, mfc_eah, mfc_eal, mfc_size, mfc_tag, mfc_tag_mask, pad[2];   /* staged MFC parameters */
+    spu_jcap_opctx at;
+} spu_jcap_wrch;
+typedef struct spu_jcap_rdch { uint32_t value[4]; spu_jcap_opctx at; } spu_jcap_rdch;
+typedef struct spu_jcap_xfer { uint32_t lsa, ea_hi, ea_lo; int32_t result; } spu_jcap_xfer;
+typedef struct spu_jcap_atomic {
+    uint32_t lsa, atomic_stat, handled, pad;        /* handled: the command was a lock-line one */
+    uint8_t  before[128], after[128];               /* local store line at lsa & ~127 */
+} spu_jcap_atomic;
+typedef struct spu_jcap_post {
+    uint32_t event_status, event_mask, mfc_tag_status, mfc_tag_mask;
+    uint32_t atomic_stat, list_stall_mask, list_stall_stat, srr0;
+    uint32_t int_enable, decrementer, status, irq_stall_seen;
+    uint32_t resv_valid, resv_ea, stop_code, pad;
+} spu_jcap_post;
+typedef struct spu_jcap_irq { uint32_t event_status, event_mask, list_stall_stat, host_depth; } spu_jcap_irq;
+
+/* CRC-32 as zlib's crc32() (reflected 0xEDB88320): crc = spu_jcap_crc32(0, p, n); continue with the result. */
+static inline uint32_t spu_jcap_crc32(uint32_t crc, const void* data, size_t n)
+{
+    static const uint32_t k[16] = {
+        0x00000000u, 0x1DB71064u, 0x3B6E20C8u, 0x26D930ACu, 0x76DC4190u, 0x6B6B51F4u, 0x4DB26158u, 0x5005713Cu,
+        0xEDB88320u, 0xF00F9344u, 0xD6D6A3E8u, 0xCB61B38Cu, 0x9B64C2B0u, 0x86D3D2D4u, 0xA00AE278u, 0xBDBDF21Cu };
+    const uint8_t* p = (const uint8_t*)data;
+    crc = ~crc;
+    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; i++) {
+        crc ^= p[i];
+        crc = (crc >> 4) ^ k[crc & 15];
+        crc = (crc >> 4) ^ k[crc & 15];
+    }
+    return ~crc;
+}
+
+/* ---- the runtime side (spu_jcap.c) ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
+#ifndef SPU_JCAP_FORMAT_ONLY
+struct spu_context;
+/* -1 not read yet, 0 off, 1 on. A plain global: every hook is `if (__builtin_expect(g_spu_jcap_on > 0, 0))`
+ * and nothing else while capture is off; spu_jcap_init() settles it. */
+extern int g_spu_jcap_on;
+/* A hooked function split for that: its original body always inlined into the hooked entry, the capture
+ * path in a separate cold function. */
+#if defined(__GNUC__) || defined(__clang__)
+#define SPU_JCAP_BODY static inline __attribute__((always_inline))
+#define SPU_JCAP_COLD static inline __attribute__((noinline, cold))
+#else
+#define SPU_JCAP_BODY static __forceinline
+#define SPU_JCAP_COLD static __declspec(noinline)
+#endif
+int  spu_jcap_init(void);
+/* Is a capture recording this context on this thread? */
+int  spu_jcap_active(const struct spu_context* ctx);
+/* Inside a recorded channel write (between spu_jcap_op_wrch and spu_jcap_op_post) on this thread? */
+int  spu_jcap_in_op(void);
+
+/* Start points. Each returns quickly when the context's job is not to be captured. */
+void spu_jcap_dispatch(struct spu_context* ctx);              /* top of spu_ib_full: a WWS job entry? */
+void spu_jcap_run_begin(struct spu_context* ctx, int kind, uint32_t entry_fn_addr);   /* kinds 2, 3 */
+void spu_jcap_run_end(struct spu_context* ctx, int halted);  /* after spu_run_with_halt */
+/* spu_drain_call_full on its way out: the WWS job's return? */
+void spu_jcap_drain_leave(struct spu_context* ctx, uint32_t return_pc);
+/* The pc is at SPU_JCAP_WWS_RETURN outside the job's drain (top of spu_ib_full, or the interpreter about to
+ * run it): the end of a WWS job whose host frames were unwound. */
+void spu_jcap_reached(struct spu_context* ctx);
+/* spu_run_with_halt took over: 2 (`case 2`), 3 (a non-local return in its loop), 4 (its loop carries on). */
+void spu_jcap_restart(struct spu_context* ctx, int landing);
+
+/* The operations (called only while spu_jcap_active). */

+/* A hit is now proven with a byte compare against a copy of the bytes it was
+ * computed from, not a fresh content hash. The hash read the whole image on
+ * every job start too, eight bytes per step: 4% of GT5's sound-job thread,
+ * which runs short of real time. memcmp is exact and several times faster.
+ * SPU_FP_HASHCHECK=1 restores the content-hash check. */
+/* 64 slots: GT5 has more than 8 job images in use during a race, so with 8 the
+ * round-robin slots kept being replaced, and every miss copied and hashed the
+ * whole image again (3% of the sound-job thread in fingerprinting plus much of
+ * its memcpy, 12 Nov). */
+/* Round 9 (15 Nov 2026): on x86-64 a hit is proven by a CRC32C of the image instead -- four interleaved
+ * streams over its four quarters (crc32 issues one a cycle with a 3-cycle latency), 128 bits in all --
+ * compared with the CRC of the copy the fingerprint was computed from. That reads the image once, not the
+ * image and the copy. GT5 on 4 E-cores checks ~2,200 images a second, 33.6 KB on average: 6.4-7.7 us
+ * each with memcmp, 3.3-4.5 us with the CRC (alternated in one race), ~7 ms of CPU a second less, most
+ * of it on the sound job chain's thread. SPU_FP_CHECK=memcmp restores the byte compare; PS3_AB_WHAT=fpcrc
+ * alternates the two; SPU_FP_STATS=1 logs the checks' cost every 10 s. */
+#if defined(__x86_64__) || defined(_M_X64)
+#include <immintrin.h>
+#define SPU_FP_HAVE_CRC 1
+__attribute__((target("sse4.2")))
+static void spu_fp_crc4(const uint8_t* p, size_t n, uint64_t out[2])
+{
+    const size_t q = (n / 32) * 8;   /* bytes per stream, a multiple of 8 */
+    uint64_t c0 = 0xFFFFFFFFu, c1 = 0x12345678u, c2 = 0x9ABCDEF0u, c3 = 0x0F1E2D3Cu;
+    const uint8_t *p0 = p, *p1 = p + q, *p2 = p + 2 * q, *p3 = p + 3 * q;
+    for (size_t i = 0; i < q; i += 8) {
+        uint64_t d0, d1, d2, d3;
+        memcpy(&d0, p0 + i, 8); memcpy(&d1, p1 + i, 8); memcpy(&d2, p2 + i, 8); memcpy(&d3, p3 + i, 8);
+        c0 = _mm_crc32_u64(c0, d0); c1 = _mm_crc32_u64(c1, d1); c2 = _mm_crc32_u64(c2, d2); c3 = _mm_crc32_u64(c3, d3);
+    }
+    for (size_t i = 4 * q; i < n; i++) c0 = _mm_crc32_u8((uint32_t)c0, p[i]);
+    out[0] = c0 | (c1 << 32);
+    out[1] = (c2 | (c3 << 32)) ^ (uint64_t)n;
+}
+#else
+#define SPU_FP_HAVE_CRC 0
+static void spu_fp_crc4(const uint8_t* p, size_t n, uint64_t out[2]) { (void)p; out[0] = out[1] = n; }
+#endif
+static int spu_fp_check_crc(void)
+{
+    if (!SPU_FP_HAVE_CRC) return 0;
+    static int mode = -1;
+    if (mode < 0) { const char* e = getenv("SPU_FP_CHECK"); mode = (e && !strcmp(e, "memcmp")) ? 0 : 1; }
+    extern int ps3_ab_on(const char* what);
+    static signed char listed = -1;
+    if (listed < 0) listed = (signed char)(ps3_ab_on("fpcrc") >= 0);
+    if (listed) { const int ab = ps3_ab_on("fpcrc"); if (ab >= 0) return ab; }
+    return mode;
+}

+/* The context a job runs in, one per host thread and reused job after job. Each job used to
+ * get a fresh 256 KB local store from calloc, built there, copied into a stack-local context
+ * that spu_context_init had just zeroed (local store included), and freed: a megabyte of
+ * memory traffic per job. Now the job is built in the context's own store, zeroed once by the
+ * init. A job that starts another on the same thread (none is known to) gets its own. */
+static SPURS_JOB_TLS spu_context* t_job_ctx;
+static SPURS_JOB_TLS int t_job_ctx_busy;
+/* Zeroing the whole 256 KB store for every job was ~12 us on a small core, and an audio chain runs
+ * 13 jobs every 5.33 ms. A job's bytes stay inside its own regions (binary, buffers, stack: LS 0 to
+ * the end of the last region) and the context block under the top of the store, so the context
+ * remembers where the last job's regions ended, and the next job zeroes from the end of its own
+ * binary (which the load overwrites) to there, and the top block: the store then reads exactly as
+ * a fully zeroed one. SPURS_JOB_LS_CHECK=1 proves the premise, checking before each job that the
+ * rest of the store is still zero (and zeroing all of it when it is not); SPURS_JOB_LS_FULL=1 zeroes
+ * all of it every time. */

+/* sys_mmapper_enable_page_fault_notification (lv2 327)
+ *
+ * r3 = start of an area from sys_mmapper_allocate_address
+ * r4 = event queue that receives a page-fault event for that area
+ *
+ * On a PS3 a thread that touches an unmapped page of the area stops and the
+ * queue gets an event naming it and the address; the owner maps memory and
+ * resumes the thread. GT5's packed file system asks for this twice (func_00C057A0
+ * with its "PDIPGFSX" queue, func_00C078F0) and ignores the result.
+ *
+ * Here sys_mmapper_allocate_address commits the whole area up front, so no
+ * access in it can fault and no such event can ever be due: checking the
+ * arguments the way lv2 does and remembering the pair is the whole of the
+ * behaviour. Errors: CELL_EINVAL when start is not the start of an area,
+ * CELL_ESRCH when the queue does not exist, CELL_EBUSY when the queue is
+ * already registered, CELL_EAGAIN when the table is full. */
+#define PF_NOTIFY_MAX 16
+static struct { uint32_t start, queue; } s_pf_notify[PF_NOTIFY_MAX];
+static int s_pf_notify_n = 0;
+#ifdef _WIN32
+static SRWLOCK s_pf_lock = SRWLOCK_INIT;
+#define PF_LOCK()   AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&s_pf_lock)
+#define PF_UNLOCK() ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&s_pf_lock)
+#else
+static pthread_mutex_t s_pf_lock = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;
+#define PF_LOCK()   pthread_mutex_lock(&s_pf_lock)
+#define PF_UNLOCK() pthread_mutex_unlock(&s_pf_lock)
+#endif
+
+static int64_t sys_mmapper_enable_page_fault_notification_handler(ppu_context* ctx)
+{
+    uint32_t start = LV2_ARG_U32(ctx, 0);
+    uint32_t queue = LV2_ARG_U32(ctx, 1);
+    if (!sys_mmapper_is_area_start(start))
+        return (int64_t)(int32_t)CELL_EINVAL;
+    if (queue == 0 || queue > SYS_EVENT_QUEUE_MAX || !g_sys_event_queues[queue - 1].active)
+        return (int64_t)(int32_t)CELL_ESRCH;
+    int64_t rc = CELL_OK;
+    PF_LOCK();
+    for (int i = 0; i < s_pf_notify_n; i++)
+        if (s_pf_notify[i].queue == queue) { rc = (int64_t)(int32_t)CELL_EBUSY; break; }
+    if (rc == CELL_OK) {
+        if (s_pf_notify_n < PF_NOTIFY_MAX) {
+            s_pf_notify[s_pf_notify_n].start = start;
+            s_pf_notify[s_pf_notify_n].queue = queue;
+            s_pf_notify_n++;
+        } else {
+            rc = (int64_t)(int32_t)CELL_EAGAIN;
+        }
+    }
+    PF_UNLOCK();
+    fprintf(stderr, "[mmapper] page-fault events for 0x%08X go to queue %u (none can occur: the area is backed)%s\n",
+            start, queue, rc == CELL_OK ? "" : " -- refused");
+    return rc;
+}

+/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ * sys_memory_allocate_from_container (lv2 350)
+ *
+ * r3 = size
+ * r4 = container id
+ * r5 = flags (page size: 0x400 = 1 MB, 0x200 = 64 KB, 0 = 1 MB)
+ * r6 = pointer to receive the address (u32*)
+ *
+ * Was unregistered, so the catch-all answered CELL_OK and wrote nothing. GT5
+ * calls it once, when it sets up the music decoder (func_009772A8, after
+ * cellSysmoduleLoadModule(0x53)): a 1 MB container, then 512 KB from it with
+ * 64 KB pages, and the address read back from a stack word it had zeroed. It
+ * built the decoder's heap at guest address 0. Now it gets real memory.
+ *
+ * The memory comes from the user range like sys_memory_allocate's and is
+ * charged to the container, not to the main pool: the container already
+ * stands for that much memory. sys_memory_free gives it back to the container.
+ * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/
+int64_t sys_memory_allocate_from_container(ppu_context* ctx)
+{
+    uint32_t size     = LV2_ARG_U32(ctx, 0);
+    uint32_t cid      = LV2_ARG_U32(ctx, 1);
+    uint64_t flags    = LV2_ARG_U64(ctx, 2);
+    uint32_t addr_out = LV2_ARG_PTR(ctx, 3);
+
+    uint32_t alignment = flags == SYS_MEMORY_PAGE_SIZE_64K ? 0x10000u
+                       : (flags == SYS_MEMORY_PAGE_SIZE_1M || flags == 0) ? 0x100000u : 0u;
+    if (!alignment)
+        return (int64_t)(int32_t)CELL_EINVAL;
+    if (!size || (size & (alignment - 1u)))
+        return (int64_t)(int32_t)CELL_EALIGN;
+    if (cid == 0 || cid > SYS_MEMORY_CONTAINER_MAX)
+        return (int64_t)(int32_t)CELL_ESRCH;
+
+    bump_lock();
+    sys_mem_container_info* c = &g_sys_mem_containers[cid - 1];
+    if (!c->active) {
+        bump_unlock(); return (int64_t)(int32_t)CELL_ESRCH;
+    }
+    if (size > c->total_size - c->used_size) {
+        bump_unlock(); return (int64_t)(int32_t)CELL_ENOMEM;
+    }
+    int slot = -1;
+    for (int i = 0; i < SYS_MEMORY_ALLOC_MAX; ++i)
+        if (!g_sys_mem_allocs[i].active) { slot = i; break; }
+    uint32_t addr = slot < 0 ? 0 : user_address(size, alignment);
+    if (!addr || vm_commit(addr, size) != CELL_OK) {
+        bump_unlock(); return (int64_t)(int32_t)CELL_ENOMEM;
+    }
+    memset(vm_to_host(addr), 0, size);
+    sys_mem_alloc_info* a = &g_sys_mem_allocs[slot];
+    a->active = 1; a->addr = addr; a->size = size;
+    a->container_id = (int32_t)cid; a->page_size = alignment;
+    c->used_size += size;
+    if (addr + size > g_sys_mem_bump_ptr) g_sys_mem_bump_ptr = addr + size;
+    bump_unlock();
+    fprintf(stderr, "[sys_memory] allocate_from_container(size=0x%X, cid=%u, flags=0x%llX) -> 0x%08X\n",
+            size, cid, (unsigned long long)flags, addr);
+    if (addr_out) write_be32(addr_out, addr);
     return CELL_OK;
 }

+/* Is addr the first byte of an area sys_mmapper_allocate_address handed out?
+ * (sys_mmapper_enable_page_fault_notification, lv2_register.c, accepts only
+ * such an address.) */
+int sys_mmapper_is_area_start(uint32_t addr)
+{

-/* ===========================================================================
- * Channel-stall contract (faithful-adopt, from canersaka's fork).
- *
- * A blocking spu_rdch on an empty read channel parks the SPU host thread on a
- * per-SPU CV until a producer (mailbox/signal write, event raise) calls
- * spu_ch_wake -- never fabricating a value. Under SPU_LOCKSTEP the wait
- * releases the run token first (block_begin) so a peer SPU that must post the
- * awaited data is never blocked on this ctx. A 10 ms re-poll is the missed-wake
- * safety net. Opt-in (env SPU_CH_BLOCK=1), default OFF while the producers
- * (mailbox/signal writes, MFC tag-status event raise) are being wired -- until
- * then blocking a read whose producer is missing would hang, so default stays
- * legacy non-blocking with zero regression, exactly like the lockstep gate.
- * ===========================================================================*/
-/* Set by runtime/spu/spu_raw.c once a raw SPU exists. A raw SPU runs on its own

- * RdInMbox must PARK, not fabricate a zero -- there is no scheduler above it to
- * retry. Off unless a raw SPU is actually created, so no other port changes. */
-int g_spu_force_ch_block = 0;

-/* Would rdch complete right now? Plain reads + the 10 ms re-poll cover cross-

-/* MFC_LLR_LOST_EVENT (0x400) -- the only producer for it.
- *
- * The SPU "wait until another processor touches this variable" idiom is: GETLLAR
- * the 128-byte line, set the event mask to Lr, then block in

- * bit, so an SPU using it waited forever -- ps1_netemu's GPU core (SPU 4) parks
- * at pc=0x0A5E8 with evmask=0x400 exactly here while the PPU spins waiting on the
- * SPU. Deadlock, and the reason the PS1 core never starts.
- *
- * Losing a reservation means the reserved line changed, and GETLLAR already
- * snapshots it, so compare against that snapshot rather than hooking every store.
- * ponytail: polled, not store-hooked -- one 128-byte memcmp per 10 ms poll on an
- * already-blocked SPU, and nothing at all on the PPU store path. The ceiling is
- * one poll of wake latency, and an A-B-A write that restores the same bytes
- * between polls is missed; hook the writers if either ever matters.
- */

-    }

-/* Report a CROSS-IMAGE match: the registry served a function some other image
- * registered at this address, because one side's image_id was the 0 wildcard.
- *
- * This is a real hazard, reported with evidence by @canersaka (#59): SPURS job
- * chains load job binaries into descriptor-assigned LS slots, so the same binary
- * can sit at different addresses on different rounds. If the lift was fixed-base
- * and the exact match misses, the wildcard can serve ANOTHER image's function at
- * that address -- the job then runs the wrong program end to end, returns
- * cleanly, and the only symptom is something three layers downstream that never
- * happens. Their words: one log line would have saved a day.
- *
- * Logging, not refusing. Refusing the wildcard outright was measured and does
- * NOT survive contact: a dormant task image can register spans overlapping the
- * resident kernel's low LS range, so a legitimate service-to-kernel yield gets
- * falsely rejected. Telling resident from dormant needs residency tracking the
- * registry does not have. So this reports and keeps going.
- *
- * Deduped per (addr, from, to): spu_lookup runs millions of times a second, and
- * a substitution that repeats every dispatch would bury the log it is meant to
- * make readable. */

-/* ---- Dispatch cache (on by default; SPU_DISPATCH_CACHE=0 turns it off) -----
- * Indirect dispatch and interpreter rejoin resolve the same few targets
- * millions of times a second, and each resolution re-derives ownership: the
- * resident code slots (verifying a pending load), then the task, overlay and
- * primary registries, each a hash-chain walk. The answer changes only when one
- * of its inputs does, so remember it per host thread, keyed by everything the
- * resolver reads:
- *  - the target and the context's image, resident overlay and resident task;
- *  - the registry, by its append-only count (any registration drops every
- *    entry);
- *  - the context's resident code slots, by dcache_residency, which
- *    spu_overlay_note_get (their only runtime writer) bumps on every change;
- *  - the context's lifetime, by dcache_id: a context re-initialised at the
- *    same address starts with id 0 and takes a fresh one.
- * A verified slot is not re-compared, as without the cache (verify once per
- * load); a store by SPU code into a verified span is not tracked, the same as
- * there. Misses (NULL) are not cached, so a rejected or unlifted target is
- * resolved every time, as before. SPU_DISPATCH_CACHE=shadow runs the full
- * resolver on every hit, counts disagreements and returns its answer. */

-/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
- * Micro-interpreter for RUNTIME-GENERATED stub code (SMC).
- *
- * The WWS jobmanager's interrupt handler GENERATES a register save/restore
- * stub above the static image (LS 0x3FEC0: a chain of stqd/lqd plus a `bi`
- * terminator, written at interrupt entry) and calls it. No lift can exist for
- * bytes that only come into being at runtime, so when the indirect dispatch
- * finds no registered function we interpret the LIVE LS bytes directly for
- * the small instruction set such stubs use, and exit back into lifted code at
- * the first branch (trampoline re-dispatch). Returns 1 if it executed to a
- * branch, 0 on an unknown opcode (caller falls through to BRANCH-TO-0). */
-static int spu_smc_microstep(spu_context* ctx)
-{
-    uint32_t pc = ctx->pc & SPU_LS_MASK & ~3u;
-    /* Straight runs of quadword loads and stores (lqa/stqa/lqd/stqd) go through
-     * a tight loop: no decode chain, no per-access probe. The WWS handler's
-     * generated save and restore stubs are 76 of them and a `bi`, run on every
-     * stall-and-notify interrupt -- ~40k stubs a second on God of War:
-     * Ascension's serial EDGE chain, ~7% of its time at ~25 ns an instruction
-     * the generic way. Only while every LS diagnostic is off (they read 0 once
-     * the first access has read their switches); otherwise the generic path
-     * below runs them. */

+/*
+ * ps3recomp - SPU channel + indirect-branch runtime glue
+ *
+ * Implements the externs the SPU lifter (tools/spu_lifter.py) emits:
+ *   - spu_rdch / spu_rchcnt / spu_wrch : SPU channel access. MFC channels are
+ *     routed to the DMA engine (spu_dma.h); mailboxes, signal notification,
+ *     events and the decrementer use the spu_context channel fields.
+ *   - spu_indirect_branch : resolves ctx->pc to a lifted spu_func_* via a
+ *     registry that generated code populates by calling spu_recomp_register().
+ *
+ * The MFC engine state is kept per spu_context here (spu_context.h does not
+ * embed one), in a small lazily-populated registry.
+ */
+
+#include "spu_coh_bitmap.h" /* ppu_st_page_all: the lifted stores' page gate */
+/* The PUT path asks this once or twice per 128-byte line it writes, 256 times
+ * for a 16 KB transfer. spu_coh_is_reserved (spu_coherency.c) is a call to
+ * exactly this inline test. */
+#define MFC_COH_IS_RESERVED(a) spu_coh_line_reserved(a)
+#include "spu_dma.h"
+#include "spu_coherency.h" /* lock-line lock + PPU-write coherence bitmap */
+#include "spu_helpers.h"   /* spu_splat_u32 / spu_ls_read128 (SMC microstep) */
+#include "spu_lockstep.h"

+#include <stdint.h>

+/* setjmp/longjmp also save and restore the signal mask on POSIX: one
+ * sigprocmask system call per halt, stack reset or task resume. These frames
+ * never cross a signal handler, so the mask is the same at both ends. */
+#if defined(_WIN32)
+#define SPU_SETJMP(env) setjmp(env)
+#define SPU_LONGJMP(env, v) longjmp(env, v)
+#else
+#define SPU_SETJMP(env) _setjmp(env)

+#endif

+/* The SPU decrementer ticks at the PS3 timebase, 79.8 MHz -- the same clock
+ * sys_time_get_timebase_frequency reports to the PPU. Titles calibrate real
+ * delays against it, so the rate has to be right, not merely non-zero. */
+#define SPU_DECREMENTER_HZ  79800000ull
+
+static uint64_t spu_host_ns(void)
+{
+#ifdef _WIN32
+    static LARGE_INTEGER s_freq;
+    LARGE_INTEGER c;
+    if (!s_freq.QuadPart) QueryPerformanceFrequency(&s_freq);
+    QueryPerformanceCounter(&c);
+    /* Split the divide to keep the multiply from overflowing: QPC counters are
+     * large enough that (count * 1e9) wraps a u64 within hours of uptime. */
+    return (uint64_t)(c.QuadPart / s_freq.QuadPart) * 1000000000ull
+         + (uint64_t)(c.QuadPart % s_freq.QuadPart) * 1000000000ull
+           / (uint64_t)s_freq.QuadPart;
+#elif defined(__APPLE__)
+    /* SPU_RdDec reads this on every decrementer read. Darwin builds
+     * CLOCK_MONOTONIC from gettimeofday and the boot time, at microsecond
+     * resolution; CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW is the mach continuous-time counter in
+     * nanoseconds, at about half the cost. Both are monotonic, count across
+     * sleep and start from an arbitrary origin, and the decrementer only ever
+     * subtracts two readings of this one function. */
+    return clock_gettime_nsec_np(CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW);
+#else
+    struct timespec ts;
+    clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &ts);
+    return (uint64_t)ts.tv_sec * 1000000000ull + (uint64_t)ts.tv_nsec;
+#endif
+}
+
+/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ * Clean SPU job abort (longjmp). The `br .` halt idiom and other terminal
+ * spins can't be escaped by setting a status flag (lifted code never checks
+ * it), so spu_halt() longjmps back to spu_run_with_halt() in the dispatcher.
+ * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/
+#if defined(_MSC_VER)
+#  define SPU_TLS __declspec(thread)
+#else
+#  define SPU_TLS __thread
+#endif
+/* Called after an SPU atomic commits a 128-byte line, with the lock-line lock
+ * released. cellSpurs sets it so a PPU blocked in cellSpursEventFlagWait wakes
+ * when a task sets the flag, instead of on its next 2 ms poll. */
+void (*g_spu_line_commit_hook)(uint32_t line) = 0;
+/* spu_workload.c: wakes tasks parked in WAIT_SIGNAL on that line's taskset. */
+void spu_taskset_line_committed(uint32_t line);
+/* SPU_LS_WATCH=0x1BE80[,0x927D80...]: watch up to 4 16-byte LS lines (reads
+ * and writes) in every SPU image. See spu_ls_watch_hit2 for the fast path. */
+#define SPU_WATCH_MAX 4
+int g_spu_ls_watch_n = -1;
+static unsigned s_spu_ls_watch[SPU_WATCH_MAX];
+unsigned* spu_ls_watch_list(int* out_n)
+{
+    if (g_spu_ls_watch_n < 0) {
+        int n = 0; const char* e = getenv("SPU_LS_WATCH");
+        while (e && *e && n < SPU_WATCH_MAX) {
+            s_spu_ls_watch[n++] = (unsigned)strtoul(e, (char**)&e, 0) & ~0xFu;
+            while (*e == ',' || *e == ' ') e++;
+        }
+        g_spu_ls_watch_n = n;
+    }
+    *out_n = g_spu_ls_watch_n;
+    return s_spu_ls_watch;
+}
+void spu_ls_watch_slow(uint32_t lsa, int is_write, const uint8_t* p, uint32_t pc, uint32_t lr)
+{
+    int n; spu_ls_watch_list(&n);
+    if (!n) return;
+    uint32_t a = lsa & (SPU_LS_MASK & ~0xFu);
+    for (int i = 0; i < g_spu_ls_watch_n; i++) {
+        if (s_spu_ls_watch[i] == a) {
+            fprintf(stderr, "[spu-watch %s 0x%05X pc=0x%05X lr=0x%05X] "
+                "%02X%02X%02X%02X %02X%02X%02X%02X %02X%02X%02X%02X %02X%02X%02X%02X\n",
+                is_write ? "WR" : "rd", a, pc, lr,
+                p[0],p[1],p[2],p[3], p[4],p[5],p[6],p[7],
+                p[8],p[9],p[10],p[11], p[12],p[13],p[14],p[15]);
+            fflush(stderr);
+            break;
+        }
+    }
+}

+static SPU_TLS jmp_buf s_spu_halt_env;
+static SPU_TLS int     s_spu_halt_armed = 0;
+
+/* Call right after a setjmp returned 0. On 64-bit Windows longjmp unwinds every
+ * host frame between it and its setjmp (RtlUnwindEx, a function-table lookup
+ * and a virtual unwind per frame), several microseconds per jump; with the
+ * buffer's Frame zeroed it restores the registers directly. These jumps --
+ * a halt back to spu_run_with_halt, an iret back to the drain loop that took
+ * the interrupt -- only cross C frames of this runtime and of lifted code,
+ * which have no destructors or __finally blocks to run. SPU_LONGJMP_UNWIND=1
+ * keeps the unwinding jump. */
+void spu_jmp_no_unwind(void* env)
+{
+#if defined(_WIN64) && defined(_MSC_VER)
+    static int s_unwind = -1;
+    if (s_unwind < 0) {
+        int u = getenv("SPU_LONGJMP_UNWIND") ? 1 : 0;
+        /* Control Flow Guard on for the process (Windows Security's Exploit protection can force it on
+         * every program) makes the CRT's longjmp refuse a buffer whose Frame is 0: it ends the process
+         * on the spot, fast fail 13, exit code 0xC0000409, a second after the game starts (#31). Then
+         * keep the unwinding jump. */
+        typedef BOOL (WINAPI *get_policy_fn)(HANDLE, int, void*, SIZE_T);
+        get_policy_fn get_policy = (get_policy_fn)(void*)GetProcAddress(
+            GetModuleHandleA("kernel32.dll"), "GetProcessMitigationPolicy");
+        DWORD cfg = 0;   /* PROCESS_MITIGATION_CONTROL_FLOW_GUARD_POLICY; bit 0 EnableControlFlowGuard */
+        if (!u && get_policy && get_policy(GetCurrentProcess(), 7 /* ProcessControlFlowGuardPolicy */,
+                                           &cfg, sizeof cfg) && (cfg & 1)) {
+            u = 1;
+            fprintf(stderr, "[spu] Control Flow Guard is on for this process: SPU jumps unwind\n");
+        }
+        s_unwind = u;
+    }
+    if (!s_unwind) ((_JUMP_BUFFER*)env)->Frame = 0;
+#else
+    (void)env;
+#endif
+}

+/* A non-local return replaces the old host call chain without changing
+ * any architectural registers, local store, or pending guest work. */
+void spu_restart_dispatch(spu_context* ctx)
+{
+    g_spu_trampoline_fn = 0;
+    if (s_spu_halt_armed) SPU_LONGJMP(s_spu_halt_env, 2);
+    fprintf(stderr, "[spu] non-local return outside execution driver at 0x%05X\n", ctx->pc);
+    ctx->status = SPU_STATUS_STOPPED_BY_HALT;
+}

+/* SPU->PPU outbound-mailbox delivery hook. The SPU writing WrOutMbox /
+ * WrOutIntrMbox must wake PPU code blocked on the SPURS event queue bound to
+ * the SPU thread group (e.g. cellSpursInitialize). lv2_register.c installs a
+ * handler that maps spu_group_id -> connected event queue and pushes an event.
+ * NULL until installed (plain SPU jobs with no PPU listener stay a no-op). */
+int (*g_spu_user_event_hook)(spu_context*, uint32_t) = NULL;
+void (*g_spu_out_mbox_hook)(uint32_t group_id, uint32_t spu_id,
+                            int is_intr, uint32_t value) = 0;

+/* Every MFC PUT an SPU completes, if anyone is listening. Installed by the GCM
+ * layer (libs/video/cellGcmSys.c), which needs it to find the RSX pushbuffer:
+ * a title whose SPUs build the command stream never tells libgcm where that
+ * stream is, so the only evidence is the DMA that writes it. NULL until
+ * installed, so a title with no SPU-built FIFO pays nothing. */
+void (*g_spu_put_hook)(uint32_t ea, uint32_t size) = 0;
+/* Every GET, as spu_overlay_note_get sees it (SPU_WWSPROF sets it; NULL otherwise). */
+extern void (*g_spu_get_hook)(uint32_t size);
+void (*g_spu_get_hook)(uint32_t size) = 0;

+void spu_halt(spu_context* ctx)
+{
+    /* Register/context dump at halt-asserts: the WWS job's parameter guard
+     * (heqi 0x1650 in job_wws_7BD900) checks (r12 bit0) & (r9 16-aligned) &
+     * (r15 != 0) -- job descriptor/ABI values our execute path must supply.
+     * Dump the low registers + the job's parameter area so a firing assert
+     * names exactly which input is wrong. */
+    { static int _n = 0;
+      if (_n < 6 && ctx->status == SPU_STATUS_STOPPED_BY_HALT) { _n++;
+        fprintf(stderr, "[spu-halt] img=%d pc=0x%05X regs:", ctx->image_id,
+                ctx->pc & SPU_LS_MASK);
+        for (int r = 3; r <= 16; r++)
+            fprintf(stderr, " r%d=%08X", r, ctx->gpr[r]._u32[0]);
+        fprintf(stderr, " r80=%08X r85=%08X\n",
+                ctx->gpr[80]._u32[0], ctx->gpr[85]._u32[0]);
+        fflush(stderr);
+      } }
+    if (s_spu_halt_armed) { s_spu_halt_armed = 0; SPU_LONGJMP(s_spu_halt_env, 1); }
+}
+
+/* Diagnostic: dump the taskset-policy scheduler's working tables (LS 0x2700..)
+ * at func_00000E60 entry, to reverse why it computes "no runnable task". Env
+ * YDKJ_E60. Called from the lifted taskset policy. */
+void spu_dbg_e60(spu_context* ctx)
+{
+    static int s_e = -1; if (s_e < 0) s_e = getenv("YDKJ_E60") ? 1 : 0;
+    if (!s_e) return;
+    static int _d = 0; if (!PS3_LOG_FIRST(_d, 6)) return;
+    const uint8_t* L = ctx->ls;
+    #define RD(o) (((uint32_t)L[(o)]<<24)|((uint32_t)L[(o)+1]<<16)|((uint32_t)L[(o)+2]<<8)|L[(o)+3])
+    fprintf(stderr, "[E60] r20=%08X r24=%08X | run2700=%08X ready2710=%08X pend2720=%08X en2730=%08X sig2740=%08X wait2750=%08X x2770=%08X\n",
+            ctx->gpr[20]._u32[0], ctx->gpr[24]._u32[0],
+            RD(0x2700), RD(0x2710), RD(0x2720), RD(0x2730), RD(0x2740), RD(0x2750), RD(0x2770));
+    #undef RD
+    fflush(stderr);
+}
+
+/* SPU `stop` / stop-and-signal. A real SPU stop HALTS the core; the previous
+ * lifted emission only did `status=...; return;`, which unwound ONE frame and
+ * let the caller's service loop keep running -- so a SPURS policy doing
+ * stop-and-signal in a loop spun millions of times instead of yielding. Halt the
+ * host SPU thread (longjmp to spu_run_with_halt) so the job stops AT the stop,
+ * with ctx->status + the outbound mailbox value available for the dispatcher to
+ * service. Env YDKJ_STOP_NOHALT restores the old (looping) behavior for A/B. */
+void spu_stop(spu_context* ctx)
+{
+    /* A lifted `stop` sets status and RETURNS to its caller -- for a SPURS
+     * policy this is stop-and-signal: it returns up into the kernel/policy
+     * service loop, which continues (i.e. the SPU "resumes" past the stop). That
+     * resume-by-return behavior is correct; the previous spin was caused by the
+     * lack of (a) a PPU listener for the outbound mailbox and (b) mailbox
+     * backpressure -- both handled in the channel write path, not here. So by
+     * default DO NOT halt. Env YDKJ_STOP_HALT forces a hard halt (longjmp) for
+     * A/B experiments (it makes the kernel terminate, which the game restarts). */
+    static int s_halt = -1;
+    if (s_halt < 0) s_halt = getenv("YDKJ_STOP_HALT") ? 1 : 0;
+    ctx->status = SPU_STATUS_STOPPED_BY_STOP;
+    if (s_halt) spu_halt(ctx);
+}
+
+/* SPU_FLOAT_RZ=1: SPU code runs with FPCR at round toward zero with flush-to-zero, so the
+ * single-precision helpers take their native form (spu_helpers.h, spu__nv_rz). The mode is set
+ * on entry to spu_run_with_halt and the caller's FPCR is put back on the way out: a run can
+ * happen synchronously on a PPU thread (a workload dispatched from the PPU caller), whose
+ * lifted floating point must keep round to nearest with denormals. Double precision restores
+ * the default around itself inside a run. On x86 with AVX2 the same is done with MXCSR, where the
+ * generated code gets about three times the throughput; a translation unit built without AVX2
+ * takes the exact scalar forms, which hold under this mode too. So on x86 the mode is on unless
+ * SPU_FLOAT_RZ=0, which code built with SPU_X86_RZ_ALWAYS must not be given.
+ * Returns the mode to restore, or ~0 when nothing was changed. */
+static uint64_t spu_float_mode_enter(void)
+{
+#if defined(__aarch64__) && defined(__ARM_NEON) && !defined(SPU_SCALAR_HELPERS)
+    static int s_on = -1;
+    int on = __atomic_load_n(&s_on, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
+    if (on < 0) {
+        const char* e = getenv("SPU_FLOAT_RZ");
+        on = e && e[0] == '1' && !e[1];
+        __atomic_store_n(&s_on, on, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
+    }
+    if (!on) return ~0ull;
+    uint64_t v;
+    __asm__ volatile("mrs %0, fpcr" : "=r"(v));
+    if (v == SPU_FPCR_RZFZ) return ~0ull;   /* nested run: the outer one restores */
+    __asm__ volatile("msr fpcr, %0" :: "r"((uint64_t)SPU_FPCR_RZFZ));
+    return v;
+#elif defined(__x86_64__) || defined(_M_X64)
+    static int s_on = -1;
+    int on = __atomic_load_n(&s_on, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
+    if (on < 0) {
+        const char* e = getenv("SPU_FLOAT_RZ");
+        on = !(e && e[0] == '0' && !e[1]);
+        __atomic_store_n(&s_on, on, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
+    }
+    if (!on) return ~0ull;
+    const unsigned v = _mm_getcsr();
+    if ((v & 0xE040u) == 0xE040u) return ~0ull;   /* nested run: the outer one restores */
+    _mm_setcsr(v | 0xE040u);
+    return v;
+#else
+    return ~0ull;
+#endif
+}
+static void spu_float_mode_leave(uint64_t outer)
+{
+#if defined(__aarch64__) && defined(__ARM_NEON) && !defined(SPU_SCALAR_HELPERS)
+    if (outer != ~0ull) __asm__ volatile("msr fpcr, %0" :: "r"(outer));
+#elif defined(__x86_64__) || defined(_M_X64)
+    if (outer != ~0ull) _mm_setcsr((unsigned)outer);
+#else
+    (void)outer;
+#endif
+}
+
+/* An external stop (raw SPU SPU_RunCntl = 0) halts the SPU at its next
+ * channel operation. The SPU itself never sees the request; the host thread
+ * that runs it leaves through the spu_run_with_halt landing pad, which is what
+ * the stopping side waits for. */
+static void spu_honour_stop_request(spu_context* ctx)
+{
+    if (!ctx->stop_request) return;
+    ctx->status = SPU_STATUS_STOPPED;
+    spu_halt(ctx);
+}
+
+/* Run a lifted SPU entry with a halt landing pad. Returns 1 if the job halted
+ * (via spu_halt), 0 if it returned normally. */
+int spu_run_with_halt(void (*entry)(spu_context*), spu_context* ctx)
+{
+    const uint64_t fpcr_outer = spu_float_mode_enter();   /* not modified after setjmp */
+    int halted = 0;
+    /* Job-args probe: image-1 (the WWS job binary) entries arrive at the crt
+     * with r3/r4 zeroed in SOME runs while the jm2 runner sets them -- count
+     * and stamp every image-1 run here to find the argless caller. */
+    if (ctx->image_id == 1) {
+        static int _n = 0;
+        if (_n < 12) { _n++;
+            fprintf(stderr, "[rwh] #%d img=1 ctx=%p r3=%08X r4=%08X entry=%p\n",
+                    _n, (void*)ctx, ctx->gpr[3]._u32[0], ctx->gpr[4]._u32[0],
+                    (void*)entry);
+            fflush(stderr); }
+    }
+    /* Also discard any saved register file keyed to this context pointer:
+     * contexts are stack locals, so the address recurs and a stale save from
+     * an earlier run would be restored over this job's arguments. */
+    { extern void spu_irq_regs_forget(spu_context*); spu_irq_regs_forget(ctx); }
+    ctx->steps = 0;   /* fresh run: step 0 is the entry */
+    if (g_spu_direct < 0) spu_direct_init();   /* PS3_SPU_DIRECT, spu_context.h */
+    /* The host stack is empty here by definition, so no lifted caller frame
+     * is live. A persistent context (a SPURS policy module re-entered every
+     * scheduling quantum) otherwise carries the depth its last quantum
+     * halted at: two frames per quantum for an idle job manager, and the
+     * recursion guard halted the SPU at 2000 after a few minutes of idling. */
+    ctx->host_depth = 0;
+    ctx->irq_frame = 0;
+    ctx->drain_ret_pc = 0;
+    /* Nest-safe: a job run synchronously from inside another SPU's execution
+     * re-enters here on the same host thread. The halt target is per-thread,
+     * so save the outer one and put it back on the way out -- otherwise the
+     * outer run's next halt longjmps into this (by then dead) frame, and a
+     * stack-local job context skips its coherency unregister (GH3: crashes in
+     * spu_coh_notify_write on a freed stack). */
+    jmp_buf outer_env; const int outer_armed = s_spu_halt_armed;
+    if (outer_armed) memcpy(outer_env, s_spu_halt_env, sizeof(jmp_buf));
+    s_spu_halt_armed = 1;
+    g_spu_trampoline_fn = 0;                        /* no stale transfer pending */
+    /* Lockstep gate (env SPU_LOCKSTEP, default off): join the round-robin
+     * ring and BLOCK until this ctx holds the run token, so only one lifted SPU
+     * executes at a time. No-op when unarmed. The thread-local halt env above
+     * makes a token pause/resume mid-run safe. */
+    yz_lockstep_register(ctx);
+    switch (SPU_SETJMP(s_spu_halt_env)) {
+    case 1:
+        halted = 1;
+        g_spu_trampoline_fn = 0;
+        break;
+    case 2:
+        /* A one-way guest stack reset invalidates every lifted host caller.
+         * Re-enter its target with the same guest state on the driver stack. */
+        if (__builtin_expect(g_spu_jcap_on > 0, 0)) spu_jcap_restart(ctx, 2);   /* SPU_JOB_CAPTURE */
+        ctx->host_depth = 0;
+        g_spu_trampoline_fn = 0;
+        spu_indirect_branch(ctx);
+        SPU_DRAIN(ctx);
+        break;
+    default:
+        spu_jmp_no_unwind(s_spu_halt_env);
+        /* SPU_DRAIN trampoline model: the top-level entry runs until its first
+         * cross-function tail transfer, which sets g_spu_trampoline_fn and
+         * returns; the drain loop re-enters each queued target until the SPU
+         * halts (stop -> longjmp) or the trampoline empties. Nested brsl/bisl
+         * calls drain inside their own call brackets (see the lifter). */
+        entry(ctx);
+        /* The switch is read once: this runs after every module run, and an
+         * uncached getenv here was ~3% of a SPURS workload's SPU time. */
+        { static int _e = 0;
+          static int aw = -1; if (aw < 0) aw = getenv("SPU_ARGWATCH") ? 1 : 0;
+          if (aw && _e < 8) { _e++;
+              fprintf(stderr, "[argwatch] after entry(): img=%d pc=0x%05X "
+                      "r2=0x%08X r3=0x%08X r4=0x%08X\n", ctx->image_id,
+                      (uint32_t)ctx->pc & SPU_LS_MASK, ctx->gpr[2]._u32[0],
+                      ctx->gpr[3]._u32[0], ctx->gpr[4]._u32[0]);
+              fflush(stderr); } }
+        SPU_DRAIN(ctx);
+    }
+    /* A policy module only leaves through exit-to-kernel, which halts. An iret that
+     * unwound to this driver also discarded the host frame of whatever call the
+     * interrupted code was inside, so that callee's plain return lands here: empty
+     * trampoline, still running, pc at the lost caller's continuation. Ending the
+     * run there strands the lane's claimed jobs and stalls every other lane behind
+     * them (GT5: a compiled Wws job returning to the manager at 0x3280). Carry on. */
+    while (!halted && ctx->policy_mode && (ctx->status & SPU_STATUS_RUNNING)) {
+        const int how = SPU_SETJMP(s_spu_halt_env);
+        if (how == 1) { halted = 1; g_spu_trampoline_fn = 0; break; }
+        spu_jmp_no_unwind(s_spu_halt_env);
+        /* SPU_JOB_CAPTURE: 3 = a non-local return landed here, 4 = the drain emptied and the driver carries on */
+        if (__builtin_expect(g_spu_jcap_on > 0, 0)) spu_jcap_restart(ctx, how == 2 ? 3 : 4);
+        ctx->host_depth = 0;
+        ctx->irq_frame = 0;
+        ctx->drain_ret_pc = 0;
+        g_spu_trampoline_fn = spu_indirect_branch;
+        SPU_DRAIN(ctx);
+    }
+    yz_lockstep_unregister(ctx);   /* leave the ring; hand the token onward */
+    s_spu_halt_armed = outer_armed;
+    if (outer_armed) memcpy(s_spu_halt_env, outer_env, sizeof(jmp_buf));
+    spu_float_mode_leave(fpcr_outer);
+    return halted;
+}
+
+/* ===========================================================================
+ * One private MFC engine per live virtual context. Persistent policy contexts
+ * outnumber physical SPUs even when their scheduling quanta run sequentially.
+ * Registry nodes have stable addresses and survive a quantum, including stalled
+ * lists and tag state. The registry lock protects lookup/publication/removal;
+ * the context's single execution owner protects its engine after lookup.
+ * Release is permitted only after that owner has stopped using the context.
+ * ===========================================================================*/
+typedef struct spu_mfc_slot {
+    spu_context* ctx;
+    mfc_engine mfc;
+    struct spu_mfc_slot* next;
+} spu_mfc_slot;
+
+static spu_mfc_slot* s_mfc_slots;
+static SRWLOCK s_mfc_claim_lock = SRWLOCK_INIT;
+
+/* SPU_PCSAMPLE=<secs>: every <secs>, print image and pc of every context
+ * holding an MFC slot -- i.e. every live SPU that has done DMA. Answers
+ * "which SPU task never returned, and where is it" without a debugger. */
+static DWORD WINAPI spu_pcsample_thread(LPVOID p)
+{
+    const DWORD ms = (DWORD)(uintptr_t)p;
+    for (;;) {
+        Sleep(ms);
+        int i = 0;
+        AcquireSRWLockShared(&s_mfc_claim_lock);
+        for (spu_mfc_slot* slot = s_mfc_slots; slot; slot = slot->next, i++) {
+            spu_context* c = slot->ctx;
+            if (c) fprintf(stderr, "[pcsample] slot=%d img=%d spu=0x%X pc=0x%05X lr=0x%05X"
+                                   " r3=0x%08X r81=0x%08X r84=0x%X r13=0x%08X r14=0x%08X\n",
+                           i, c->image_id, c->spu_id, (unsigned)(c->pc & SPU_LS_MASK),
+                           (unsigned)(c->gpr[0]._u32[0] & SPU_LS_MASK), c->gpr[3]._u32[0],
+                           c->gpr[81]._u32[0], c->gpr[84]._u32[0], c->gpr[13]._u32[0], c->gpr[14]._u32[0]);
+        }
+        ReleaseSRWLockShared(&s_mfc_claim_lock);
+        fflush(stderr);
+    }
+}
+
+/* Default-off memoization of the last virtual owner used by this host thread.
+ * Engines remain registry-owned, not host-thread or physical-SPU-owned. A hit
+ * borrows exactly the same pointer as the locked path; both require the owner
+ * to stop before release/range cleanup. No context layout or memory is touched.
+ *
+ * Cleanup publishes a new generation before freeing any slot. A stale TLS
+ * pointer is compared only after an acquire generation load and is never
+ * dereferenced on mismatch. Other owners' cleanup conservatively drops hits.
+ * Capture generations under the registry lock so a miss cannot bless an old
+ * pointer with a generation published by concurrent cleanup. Saturation disables
+ * hits permanently rather than permitting a generation-wrap ABA. */
+static _Atomic(uint64_t) s_mfc_cache_generation = 1;
+static SPU_TLS struct {
+    spu_context* ctx;
+    mfc_engine* engine;
+    uint64_t generation;
+} s_mfc_recent;
+static int spu_mfc_cache_enabled(void)
+{
+    static atomic_int cached;
+    int value = atomic_load_explicit(&cached, memory_order_relaxed);
+    if (!value) {
+        /* On unless SPU_MFC_LOOKUP_CACHE=0. Without it every MFC channel access takes the registry
+         * lock, about six a transfer: in a GT5 race eight SPU threads spent 65-78% of their CPU in
+         * that lock, the sound job fell behind real time and the RSX parked 1500 times a second. */
+        const char* flag = getenv("SPU_MFC_LOOKUP_CACHE");
+        value = flag && !strcmp(flag, "0") ? 1 : 2;
+        atomic_store_explicit(&cached, value, memory_order_relaxed);
+    }
+    return value == 2;
+}
+static void spu_mfc_cache_remember(spu_context* ctx, mfc_engine* engine)
+{
+    /* Caller holds either registry lock; removal cannot interleave here. */
+    s_mfc_recent.ctx = ctx;
+    s_mfc_recent.engine = engine;
+    s_mfc_recent.generation = atomic_load_explicit(&s_mfc_cache_generation, memory_order_relaxed);
+}
+static void spu_mfc_cache_invalidate(void)
+{
+    /* Caller holds the writer lock. Keep UINT64_MAX as a permanent slow mode. */
+    uint64_t generation = atomic_load_explicit(&s_mfc_cache_generation, memory_order_relaxed);
+    if (generation != UINT64_MAX)
+        atomic_store_explicit(&s_mfc_cache_generation, generation + 1, memory_order_release);
+}
+
+static mfc_engine* mfc_for(spu_context* ctx)
+{
+    int cache_enabled = spu_mfc_cache_enabled();
+    if (cache_enabled) {
+        uint64_t generation = atomic_load_explicit(&s_mfc_cache_generation, memory_order_acquire);
+        if (generation != UINT64_MAX && generation == s_mfc_recent.generation &&
+            ctx == s_mfc_recent.ctx)
+            return s_mfc_recent.engine;
+    }
+    /* Looked up once. mfc_for runs on every MFC channel access, and with
+     * SPU_PCSAMPLE unset `started` never became 1, so every access paid a
+     * getenv: a tenth of all samples in a Twisted Metal profile. */
+    { static volatile LONG checked = 0;
+      if (!checked && !InterlockedExchange(&checked, 1)) {
+          const char* e = getenv("SPU_PCSAMPLE");
+          if (e) CreateThread(NULL, 0, spu_pcsample_thread, (LPVOID)(uintptr_t)(atoi(e) * 1000), 0, NULL);
+      } }
+    AcquireSRWLockShared(&s_mfc_claim_lock);
+    for (spu_mfc_slot* slot = s_mfc_slots; slot; slot = slot->next) {
+        if (slot->ctx == ctx) {
+            if (cache_enabled) spu_mfc_cache_remember(ctx, &slot->mfc);
+            ReleaseSRWLockShared(&s_mfc_claim_lock);
+            return &slot->mfc;
+        }
+    }
+    ReleaseSRWLockShared(&s_mfc_claim_lock);
+
+    /* A concurrent miss may publish while the read lock is released. Recheck
+     * under the writer lock before creating this context's private engine. */
+    AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&s_mfc_claim_lock);
+    for (spu_mfc_slot* slot = s_mfc_slots; slot; slot = slot->next) {
+        if (slot->ctx == ctx) {
+            if (cache_enabled) spu_mfc_cache_remember(ctx, &slot->mfc);
+            ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&s_mfc_claim_lock);
+            return &slot->mfc;
+        }
+    }
+    spu_mfc_slot* slot = (spu_mfc_slot*)malloc(sizeof(*slot));
+    if (!slot) {
+        fprintf(stderr, "[SPU] cannot allocate private MFC engine for context %p\n", (void*)ctx);
+        fflush(stderr);
+        abort(); /* Shared fallback state would silently corrupt DMA completion. */
+    }
+    slot->ctx = ctx;
+    mfc_engine_init(&slot->mfc);
+    slot->next = s_mfc_slots;
+    s_mfc_slots = slot;
+    if (cache_enabled) spu_mfc_cache_remember(ctx, &slot->mfc);
+    ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&s_mfc_claim_lock);
+    return &slot->mfc;
+}
+
+/* mfc_for for the channel layer, which is about to read and write the context
+ * anyway: the engine mfc_for found last time is kept in the context itself
+ * (spu_context.h: mfc_engine_ptr and its two guards), so the common case is
+ * three fields of the context in hand instead of this thread's memo and the
+ * flag that enables it.
+ *
+ * The rules are the memo's. The fields are written from this thread's memo
+ * right after mfc_for refreshed it, so they carry a generation the engine was
+ * known good at; they are trusted only while that is still the registry's
+ * generation (nothing has been released since) and while mfc_engine_owner is
+ * this context's own address (a copied structure does not carry the engine
+ * over). mfc_for itself still never touches the context: its callers include
+ * cleanup of contexts whose memory is gone.
+ *
+ * SPU_MFC_CTX_CACHE=0 never writes the fields, which sends every access
+ * through mfc_for as before. SPU_MFC_LOOKUP_CACHE=0 (take the registry lock on
+ * every access) has no memo to copy from, so it turns this off as well. */
+static int spu_mfc_ctx_cache_enabled(void)
+{
+    static atomic_int cached;
+    int value = atomic_load_explicit(&cached, memory_order_relaxed);
+    if (!value) {
+        const char* flag = getenv("SPU_MFC_CTX_CACHE");
+        value = flag && !strcmp(flag, "0") ? 1 : 2;
+        atomic_store_explicit(&cached, value, memory_order_relaxed);
+    }
+    return value == 2;
+}
+static mfc_engine* mfc_for_ctx_slow(spu_context* ctx)
+{
+    mfc_engine* engine = mfc_for(ctx);
+    if (spu_mfc_ctx_cache_enabled() && s_mfc_recent.ctx == ctx && s_mfc_recent.engine == engine) {
+        ctx->mfc_engine_ptr = engine;
+        ctx->mfc_engine_generation = s_mfc_recent.generation;
+        ctx->mfc_engine_owner = ctx;
+    }
+    return engine;
+}
+static inline mfc_engine* mfc_for_ctx(spu_context* ctx)
+{
+    if (ctx->mfc_engine_owner == ctx) {
+        const uint64_t generation = atomic_load_explicit(&s_mfc_cache_generation, memory_order_acquire);
+        if (generation == ctx->mfc_engine_generation && generation != UINT64_MAX)
+            return (mfc_engine*)ctx->mfc_engine_ptr;
+    }
+    return mfc_for_ctx_slow(ctx);
+}
+
+void spu_mfc_release(spu_context* ctx)
+{
+    if (!ctx) return;
+    AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&s_mfc_claim_lock);
+    for (spu_mfc_slot** link = &s_mfc_slots; *link; link = &(*link)->next) {
+        if ((*link)->ctx != ctx) continue;
+        spu_mfc_slot* slot = *link;
+        *link = slot->next;
+        spu_mfc_cache_invalidate();
+        free(slot);
+        break;
+    }
+    ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&s_mfc_claim_lock);
+}
+
+/* Exit safety net for contexts unwound off a departing thread's stack.
+ * Pointer comparisons suffice: the abandoned context need not be readable. */
+void spu_mfc_forget_range(uintptr_t lo, uintptr_t hi)
+{
+    AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&s_mfc_claim_lock);
+    for (spu_mfc_slot** link = &s_mfc_slots; *link;) {
+        spu_mfc_slot* slot = *link;
+        uintptr_t owner = (uintptr_t)slot->ctx;
+        if (owner >= lo && owner < hi) {
+            *link = slot->next;
+            spu_mfc_cache_invalidate();
+            free(slot);
+        } else {
+            link = &slot->next;
+        }
+    }
+    ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&s_mfc_claim_lock);
+}
+
+/* ===========================================================================
+ * Atomic reservation (GETLLAR / PUTLLC / PUTLLUC) -- real lock-line semantics
+ *
+ * Multiple SPU kernel threads (the SPURS workload runtime runs several SPUs on
+ * one shared lock-free queue) issue GETLLAR/PUTLLC on the SAME 128-byte lines.
+ * Without honoring the reservation, two SPUs both "claim" the same slot and the
+ * queue corrupts (observed: the 2nd claim returns garbage [1,1,1,1] -> the SPU
+ * traps). PUTLLC must FAIL when the line changed since GETLLAR. We implement the
+ * compare-and-swap under one global lock across all SPU host threads.
+ * ===========================================================================*/
+extern uint8_t* vm_base;
+
+/* The spinlock guarding all atomic line ops now lives in spu_coherency.c as
+ * spu_lockline_lock/unlock. It used to be a file-static here, which serialized
+ * SPU against SPU but left the PPU free to store into a line in the middle of
+ * a PUTLLC's compare-and-commit -- the update the SPU was about to make would
+ * be written over, and the SPU would never learn the line had changed. Same
+ * lock, same critical sections, now shared with the PPU store paths. */
+
+/* Total PUTLLC attempts (all SPUs). The PM flow trace (spurs_policy.c) reads
+ * the delta across one policy run to find the run that performed a claim. */
+volatile unsigned g_spu_putllc_count = 0;
+/* PUTLLCs that hit the WATCHED sync line (g_barrier_sync_watch) -- isolates the
+ * work-run on the stalled job queue from the dozen idle jobmanager instances. */
+volatile unsigned g_spu_putllc_sync_hit = 0;
+
+/* Lowest LS address treated as "not job code". Jobs load at 0 and
+ * their stacks top out well below this; a branch at or above it with no
+ * lifted code is a runaway, not a service call. */
+#define SPU_JM2_KERNEL_BASE 0x15000u
+
+/* Link-register value handed to a SPURS job so its final `bi $r0` lands
+ * somewhere we recognise. The real job manager passes a return address into
+ * itself; we have no manager, so we pass this and treat arriving here as job
+ * completion. Chosen above the context/descriptor we park near the top of LS. */
+#define SPU_JOB_RETURN_LS   0x3FF00u
+
+/* SPU_LL_LAZY (versioned lines, spu_coherency.c): a lazy reservation whose line has been written is
+ * lost now -- the event its writer would have raised, raised where the SPU looks: its next GETLLAR,
+ * PUTLLC, PUTLLUC, RdEventStat read or count, WrEventAck or WrEventMask. */
+static inline void spu_ll_settle(spu_context* ctx)
+{
+    if (__builtin_expect(ctx->resv_lazy != 0, 0)) {
+        if (ctx->resv_valid && spu_ll_version(ctx->resv_ea) != ctx->resv_ver) {
+            ctx->resv_valid = 0;
+            SPU_EVENT_SET(ctx, SPU_EVENT_LR);
+            __atomic_fetch_add(&g_spu_lr_raise, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
+        }
+        if (!ctx->resv_valid) ctx->resv_lazy = 0;
+    }
+}
+/* The SPU has just enabled the lost-reservation event (WrEventMask): from here on the event must be
+ * raised by the writer (it can be taken as an interrupt, and an SPU may sleep on it), so a lazy
+ * reservation becomes an ordinary one -- counted and listed under the line's lock, after which every
+ * writer of the line walks it -- or, if the line moved meanwhile, is lost now. */
+static void spu_ll_make_eager(spu_context* ctx)
+{
+    const uint32_t ea = ctx->resv_ea;
+    spu_lockline_lock_line(ea);
+    if (ctx->resv_valid && spu_ll_version(ea) != ctx->resv_ver) {
+        ctx->resv_valid = 0;
+        SPU_EVENT_SET(ctx, SPU_EVENT_LR);
+        __atomic_fetch_add(&g_spu_lr_raise, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
+    } else if (ctx->resv_valid) {
+        spu_coh_reserve(ctx, ea);
+    }
+    ctx->resv_lazy = 0;
+    spu_lockline_unlock_line(ea);
+}
+
+/* Returns 1 if `cmd` is an atomic line op and was handled here, else 0. */
+SPU_JCAP_BODY int spu_mfc_atomic_body(spu_context* ctx, uint32_t cmd);
+SPU_JCAP_COLD int spu_mfc_atomic_cap(spu_context* ctx, uint32_t cmd);
+/* SPU_JOB_CAPTURE (spu_jcap.c): a captured job's lock-line commands, with the line before and after.
+ * Off: one test of the plain global, then the body (always inlined here) as before. */
+static int spu_mfc_atomic(spu_context* ctx, uint32_t cmd)
+{
+    if (__builtin_expect(g_spu_jcap_on > 0, 0)) return spu_mfc_atomic_cap(ctx, cmd);
+    return spu_mfc_atomic_body(ctx, cmd);
+}
+SPU_JCAP_COLD int spu_mfc_atomic_cap(spu_context* ctx, uint32_t cmd)
+{
+    if (!spu_jcap_active(ctx)) return spu_mfc_atomic_body(ctx, cmd);
+    spu_jcap_atomic_pre(ctx, cmd);
+    const int handled = spu_mfc_atomic_body(ctx, cmd);
+    spu_jcap_atomic_post(ctx, cmd, handled);
+    return handled;
+}
+SPU_JCAP_BODY int spu_mfc_atomic_body(spu_context* ctx, uint32_t cmd)
+{
+    /* Classify FIRST. Every MFC_Cmd write lands here, and only the switch at
+     * the bottom used to filter -- so the uncommitted-EA guard below reported
+     * ORDINARY DMA as `[spu-atomic]`. A plain put (0x20) to a garbage EA read
+     * as an atomic spin, which is a genuinely misleading place to start
+     * debugging from. Non-atomic commands belong to the DMA engine. */
+    if (cmd != MFC_GETLLAR_CMD && cmd != MFC_PUTLLC_CMD &&
+        cmd != MFC_PUTLLUC_CMD && cmd != MFC_PUTQLLUC_CMD)
+        return 0;
+
+    uint32_t ea  = ctx->mfc_eal & ~(uint32_t)(MFC_ATOMIC_LINE - 1);
+    /* The MFC ignores the low 7 bits of an atomic command's LSA (the transfer is one aligned line).
+     * Masked only to the LS, an LSA in the last 128 bytes read and wrote past LS into the context. */
+    uint32_t lsa = ctx->mfc_lsa & SPU_LS_MASK & ~(uint32_t)(MFC_ATOMIC_LINE - 1);
+    uint8_t* ls  = &ctx->ls[lsa];
+    uint8_t* mem = vm_base + ea;
+
+    { static int s_t = -1; if (s_t < 0) s_t = getenv("SPU_POLLTRACE") ? 1 : 0;
+      if (s_t) { static uint64_t s_n = 0; static uint32_t s_lastea = 0;
+        if ((++s_n % 2000000) == 0 || ea != s_lastea) {
+          if ((s_n % 2000000) == 0)
+            fprintf(stderr, "[atomcnt] %llu atomic ops; last cmd=0x%X ea=0x%08X\n",
+                    (unsigned long long)s_n, cmd, ea);
+          s_lastea = ea; } } }
+    /* SPU_ATOMTRACE=1 keeps the old 40-line cap; =<N> raises it. A busy image
+     * (FMOD) exhausts 40 before a quieter one issues its first atomic, which
+     * reads as "that image never does atomics" when it simply never got a line. */
+    { static int s_at = -1;
+      if (s_at < 0) { const char* e = getenv("SPU_ATOMTRACE");
+                      int v = e ? atoi(e) : 0; s_at = e ? (v > 1 ? v : 40) : 0; }
+      if (s_at) { static int _a=0; if (PS3_LOG_FIRST(_a, s_at))
+        fprintf(stderr, "[atom] cmd=0x%02X ea=0x%08X (img=%d)\n", cmd, ea, ctx->image_id); } }
+    /* cri task (img22) atomic on the taskset: dump the loaded bitset line so we can
+     * see if the task reads MY taskset (0x4005E000) with my READY bit, or elsewhere. */
+    { static int s_ct=-1; if(s_ct<0) s_ct=getenv("SPU_ATOMTRACE")?1:0;
+      if(s_ct && ctx->image_id==22 && cmd==0xD0 && mfc_ea_range_committed(ea,16)) {
+        static int _c=0; if(PS3_LOG_FIRST(_c, 24)){
+          uint8_t* m=vm_base+ea;
+          #define BW(o) (((uint32_t)m[o]<<24)|((uint32_t)m[o+1]<<16)|((uint32_t)m[o+2]<<8)|m[o+3])
+          fprintf(stderr,"[cri-atom] GETLLAR ea=0x%08X line[0..0x30]: %08X %08X %08X %08X | %08X %08X %08X %08X | %08X %08X %08X %08X\n",
+            ea, BW(0),BW(4),BW(8),BW(0xC), BW(0x10),BW(0x14),BW(0x18),BW(0x1C), BW(0x20),BW(0x24),BW(0x28),BW(0x2C));
+          #undef BW
+        } } }
+    /* YDKJ_CRI_R4: dump the CellSpursTaskset bitsets when the policy atomically
+     * touches my taskset (0x0F000000), to watch the task-activation state machine
+     * (why task0 isn't selected+first-run). running@0 ready@0x10 pending@0x20
+     * enabled@0x30 signalled@0x40 waiting@0x50 (each 16B; word0 = MSB, task0=bit127). */
+    { static int s_td = -1; if (s_td < 0) s_td = (getenv("YDKJ_CRI_CHAIN") && getenv("SPU_ATOMTRACE")) ? 1 : 0;
+      if (s_td && ea >= 0x0F000000u && ea < 0x0F001900u) {
+        extern uint8_t* vm_base;
+        static int _t=0; if (vm_base && PS3_LOG_FIRST(_t, 24)) {
+            uint8_t* t = vm_base + 0x0F000000u;
+            #define TW(o) (((uint32_t)t[o]<<24)|((uint32_t)t[o+1]<<16)|((uint32_t)t[o+2]<<8)|t[o+3])
+            fprintf(stderr, "[tset] %s run=%08X rdy=%08X pnd=%08X ena=%08X sig=%08X wait=%08X | wid=%08X last=%02X\n",
+                    cmd==0xD0?"GET":cmd==0xB4?"PUT":"?", TW(0x00), TW(0x10), TW(0x20), TW(0x30), TW(0x40), TW(0x50), TW(0x74), t[0x73]);
+            #undef TW
+        }
+      } }
+
+    /* Guard atomic line ops against an uncommitted/garbage EA (e.g. a SPURS
+     * policy computing a lock-line address from an incomplete instance context).
+     * Same rationale as the DMA EA guard: a bad guest atomic must not segfault
+     * the host. GETLLAR returns a zeroed line (no reservation); PUTLLC fails. */
+    if (!mfc_ea_range_committed(ea, MFC_ATOMIC_LINE)) {
+        static int s_w = 0;
+        if (PS3_LOG_FIRST(s_w, 16))
+            fprintf(stderr, "[spu-atomic] cmd=0x%X ea=0x%08X pc=0x%05X img=%d uncommitted -- skipped\n",
+                    cmd, ea, (uint32_t)ctx->pc & SPU_LS_MASK, ctx->image_id);
+        if (cmd == MFC_GETLLAR_CMD) {
+            spu_ll_settle(ctx);
+            memset(ls, 0, MFC_ATOMIC_LINE);
+            ctx->resv_ea = ea; ctx->resv_valid = 0; ctx->resv_lazy = 0; ctx->atomic_stat = 4;
+        } else {
+            ctx->atomic_stat = 1;   /* PUTLLC failure (line "moved") */
+        }
+        return 1;
+    }
+
+    /* SPU_ATOM_EA=<hex>: log every lock-line atomic touching that EA`s 128B line.
+     * SPU_ATOM_FULL=1 additionally dumps 32 bytes of the line before and after.
+     *
+     * Built into ONE buffer and written with a single fprintf: several SPU host
+     * threads and the PPU all write stderr, so a dump split across many fprintf
+     * calls comes out shredded and unreadable exactly when it matters. */
+    { static int s_ae = -1; static uint32_t s_aea;
+      if (s_ae < 0) { const char* e = getenv("SPU_ATOM_EA");
+        s_aea = e ? (uint32_t)strtoul(e, 0, 16) & ~127u : 0; s_ae = s_aea ? 1 : 0;
+        if (s_ae == 1) { extern uint32_t g_barrier_sync_watch;
+            g_barrier_sync_watch = s_aea;   /* arm PUTLLC OK/FAIL verdict log */
+            ppu_st_page_all(PPU_ST_PAGE_WATCH, 1); } }
+      if (s_ae == 1 && ((uint32_t)ea & ~127u) == s_aea) {
+          static int _n = 0, s_cap = -1;
+          /* SPU_ATOM_EA_MAX=<n>: lines to print (default 48, 0 = unlimited). */
+          if (s_cap < 0) { const char* m = getenv("SPU_ATOM_EA_MAX"); s_cap = m ? atoi(m) : 48; }
+          if (!s_cap || PS3_LOG_FIRST(_n, s_cap)) {
+              extern uint8_t* vm_base;
+              const uint8_t* r = vm_base + ((uint32_t)ea & ~127u);
+              static int s_af = -1;
+              if (s_af < 0) { const char* f = getenv("SPU_ATOM_FULL"); s_af = f ? (atoi(f) > 1 ? 2 : 1) : 0; }
+              char buf[1024]; int p = 0;
+              /* lr (gpr[0]) as well as pc: these atomics sit in generic helpers,
+               * so pc names the HELPER and only lr names the real caller. */
+              p += snprintf(buf + p, sizeof buf - p,
+                            "[atom-ea] cmd=0x%X img=%d pc=0x%05X lr=0x%05X ea=0x%08X",
+                            cmd, ctx->image_id, (uint32_t)ctx->pc & SPU_LS_MASK,
+                            ctx->gpr[0]._u32[0] & SPU_LS_MASK, (uint32_t)ea);
+              int nb = s_af == 2 ? 128 : s_af ? 64 : 8;   /* 64 covers +0x30 pendingRecv; =2 the whole line */
+              p += snprintf(buf + p, sizeof buf - p, " RAM=");
+              for (int i = 0; i < nb && p < (int)sizeof buf - 4; i++)
+                  p += snprintf(buf + p, sizeof buf - p, "%02X%s", r[i],
+                                (i % 4 == 3) ? " " : "");
+              if (cmd == MFC_PUTLLC_CMD) {
+                  p += snprintf(buf + p, sizeof buf - p, " STORE=");
+                  for (int i = 0; i < nb && p < (int)sizeof buf - 4; i++)
+                      p += snprintf(buf + p, sizeof buf - p, "%02X%s", ls[i],
+                                    (i % 4 == 3) ? " " : "");
+              }
+              fprintf(stderr, "%s\n", buf); fflush(stderr);
+          }
+      } }
+    /* Bink sync-line atomic trace (armed by the PPU-side producer probe). */
+    { extern uint32_t g_barrier_sync_watch;
+      uint32_t b = g_barrier_sync_watch;
+      if (b && ea >= (b & ~127u) && ea < ((b + 0xC0 + 127) & ~127u)) {
+          static int _n = 0;
+          if (PS3_LOG_FIRST(_n, 64))
+              fprintf(stderr, "[sync-atomic] %s img=%d pc=0x%05X ea=0x%08X\n",
+                      cmd == MFC_GETLLAR_CMD ? "GETLLAR" :
+                      cmd == MFC_PUTLLC_CMD ? "PUTLLC" : "PUTLLUC",
+                      ctx->image_id, (uint32_t)ctx->pc, ea);
+      } }
+    switch (cmd) {
+    case MFC_GETLLAR_CMD:
+        /* Lockstep tick: a guest GETLLAR..PUTLLC poll loop is intra-function
+         * (all gotos), so it never crosses the SPU_DRAIN tick site -- without a
+         * tick here a polling SPU would hold the run token forever while the
+         * peer that must WRITE the line waits for it (canersaka ticks the
+         * GETLLAR fast+slow paths for exactly this reason). */
+        yz_lockstep_tick(ctx);
+        spu_ll_settle(ctx);                        /* the reservation this one replaces */
+        /* SPU_LL_LAZY: on a marked line, with the lost-reservation event not enabled, the
+         * reservation is the line's version and the copy: no lock, no count, no walk (see
+         * spu_ll_settle and spu_coherency.c). */
+        const int llar_lazy = spu_ll_lazy_on() && !(ctx->event_mask & SPU_EVENT_LR) && spu_coh_is_reserved(ea);
+        uint32_t llar_ver = 0;
+        int llar_fast = 0;
+        if (llar_lazy) {
+            __atomic_store_n(&ctx->resv_valid, 0, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
+            spu_coh_hold_drop(ctx);                /* an ordinary reservation it replaces stops counting */
+            llar_ver = spu_ll_version(ea);         /* before the copy (acquire) */
+        } else {
+            ctx->resv_lazy = 0;
+            /* A registered holder re-reading an already marked line -- every
+             * policy-module poll -- publishes its reservation and copies without
+             * the lock; any write the copy misses ends that reservation (see
+             * spu_coh_reserve_fast). Anything else takes the lock as before. */
+            llar_fast = spu_coh_reserve_fast(ctx, ea);
+        }
+        if (!llar_fast && !llar_lazy) {
+            spu_lockline_lock_line(ea);
+            /* Tell the PPU store paths this line is live, so a store into it goes
+             * through the lock and raises SPU_EVENT_LR here instead of landing
+             * unannounced. Nothing else about this transaction changes. */
+            spu_coh_reserve(ctx, ea);
+        }
+
+        /* ONE read of guest memory, then the snapshot from that copy.
+         *
+         * This used to memcpy from `mem` twice -- once to the local store, once
+         * to resv_line -- and a PPU store landing BETWEEN the two reads gave the
+         * SPU a stale line and a fresh snapshot. That is a permanent deadlock,
+         * and it is the one this port spent a session chasing: the SPU compares
+         * its (stale) copy, finds produced == consumed, and sleeps on
+         * MFC_LLR_LOST_EVENT; spu_resv_lost_poll then compares memory against a
+         * snapshot that ALREADY has the new value, finds no difference, and
+         * never raises the event. Measured at a freeze: mirror 0x9E, snapshot
+         * 0x9F, memory 0x9F, and the SPU polling rchcnt 1.6 billion times.
+         *
+         * Hardware cannot produce that state: GETLLAR is a single atomic
+         * 128-byte read, so the reserved data and the reservation come from the
+         * same instant. Copying the snapshot from `ls` restores that property,
+         * and a store that lands after the read now leaves BOTH stale -- which
+         * is what makes the lost-reservation event fire. */
+        memcpy(ls, mem, MFC_ATOMIC_LINE);              /* line -> local store */
+        /* Snapshot from `ls`, NOT a second read of `mem`. Hardware GETLLAR is a
+         * single atomic 128-byte read, so the reserved data and the reservation
+         * come from the same instant. Reading guest memory twice lets a PPU store
+         * land between them, leaving the SPU a STALE line and a FRESH snapshot --
+         * and then both halves of the wait fail: the SPU compares its stale copy,
+         * sees produced == consumed and sleeps on MFC_LLR_LOST_EVENT, while the
+         * reservation poll compares memory against a snapshot that already holds
+         * the new value, finds no difference, and never raises the event. Nobody
+         * wakes anybody. Snapshotting from `ls` makes a later store leave BOTH
+         * stale, which is exactly what makes the lost-reservation event fire. */
+        memcpy(ctx->resv_line, ls, MFC_ATOMIC_LINE);   /* snapshot for compare */
+        /* MFC_RdAtomicStat after a GETLLAR reads 4 (GETLLAR complete), not 0:
+         * Havok's SPU allocator (GH3 collide task, LS 0xA66C) re-issues the
+         * GETLLAR until that bit is set, and spun forever on 0. PUTLLUC is 2. */
+        if (llar_lazy) {
+            ctx->resv_ea = ea; ctx->resv_ver = llar_ver; ctx->resv_lazy = 1;
+            __atomic_store_n(&ctx->resv_valid, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
+        } else if (!llar_fast) { ctx->resv_ea = ea; ctx->resv_valid = 1; }   /* the fast path published it already */
+        ctx->atomic_stat = 4;
+        ctx->dbg_getllar++;
+        /* A GETLLAR re-issued millions of times on one line is an SPU spin-wait
+         * that nobody is releasing (a ticket lock, a counter barrier). Say so
+         * once per line with the line's head, so the stuck word is visible
+         * without a per-function probe. */
+        { static SPU_THREAD_LOCAL uint32_t t_ea; static SPU_THREAD_LOCAL unsigned long t_n;
+          if (ea != t_ea) { t_ea = ea; t_n = 0; }
+          else if (++t_n == 4000000) {
+              const uint8_t* m = vm_base + ea;
+              fprintf(stderr, "[spu-spin] img=%d pc=0x%05X lr=0x%05X GETLLAR ea=0x%08X x4M; line:"
+                              " %02X%02X%02X%02X %02X%02X%02X%02X %02X%02X%02X%02X %02X%02X%02X%02X\n",
+                      ctx->image_id, (unsigned)(ctx->pc & SPU_LS_MASK), ctx->gpr[0]._u32[0] & SPU_LS_MASK, ea,
+                      m[0],m[1],m[2],m[3], m[4],m[5],m[6],m[7], m[8],m[9],m[10],m[11], m[12],m[13],m[14],m[15]);
+          } }
+        if (!llar_fast && !llar_lazy) spu_lockline_unlock_line(ea);
+        /* SPU_LLARWATCH=<hex EA>: every GETLLAR of that line, with the LSA it
+         * used and the first word as it lands in BOTH places.
+         *
+         * The deadlock this settles: at a freeze the reservation snapshot holds
