+/* Counters, per host thread (no shared line is written on the hot path). They
+ * live in a block on the heap that is never freed, not in thread-local
+ * storage: the printer reads every thread's block, and the thread-local copy
+ * of a thread that has ended is freed memory (the first version of these
+ * lines printed such garbage). */
+#define DFC_IMGS 64
+typedef struct {
+    int img; uint32_t src_ea;
+    unsigned long long all, toggle, drains;   /* dispatches; of them toggle-to-next; full drains from one */
+} spu_dfast_img;
+typedef struct {
+    unsigned long long ib_plain, ib_irq, ib_svc, ib_task, ib_cold, ib_null, ib_reset, ib_full_off;
+    unsigned long long hit, neg_hit, miss, nocache, flush, states, tagcalls;
+    unsigned long long drain[2];              /* spu_drain_call: plain returns, full drains */
+    unsigned long long disp_all, disp_toggle, drain_toggle;   /* SPU_DISPATCH_STAT's toggle-to-next count */
+    spu_dfast_img img[DFC_IMGS];
+} spu_dfast_counts;
+#define DFC_SUMMED (offsetof(spu_dfast_counts, img) / sizeof(unsigned long long))
+/* spu_drain.c: this thread's {plain returns, full drains}, pointing into its block (NULL until it has one). */
+extern SPU_THREAD_LOCAL unsigned long long* g_spu_dfc_drain_p;
+/* 1 while SPU_DISPATCH_STAT is set: the dispatcher and the drain then look for the
+ * interrupt-toggle idiom (spu_dfast_note_*). Read by spu_drain.c. */
+int g_spu_dfast_diag = -1;
+#define SPU_DFC_THREADS 256
+static spu_dfast_counts* volatile s_dfc_thr[SPU_DFC_THREADS];
+static volatile long s_dfc_nthr;
+static volatile long long s_dfc_shadow_bad;
+static int s_dfc_period = -1;            /* SPU_DISPATCH_STAT seconds; 0 = no printing */
+static volatile long long s_dfc_next_ms;
+static volatile long s_dfc_printing;
+static spu_dfast_counts s_dfc_spill;     /* threads past SPU_DFC_THREADS share this one (counts racy, never garbage) */
+
+/* The cache proper. key = tag << 16 | lsa >> 2 (0 = empty: tags start at 1);
+ * fd = the function's offset from s_dc2_base, or DC2_NULL for "nothing lifted". */
+typedef struct { uint32_t key; int32_t fd; } spu_dc2_ent;
+typedef struct { uint32_t id, residency, rgen; int image, ovl, task; } spu_dc2_tuple;
+#define DC2_ENTRIES 4096u
+#define DC2_STATES  1024u                /* interned key halves per thread; full at 3/4 -> start over */
+#define DC2_NULL    INT32_MIN
+typedef struct {
+    spu_dc2_tuple memo;                  /* the last key half looked at, and its tag (0 = none) */
+    uint32_t memo_tag;
+    uint32_t nstates;
+    spu_dfast_counts* n;                 /* this thread's counters (heap; NULL until the first full dispatch) */
+    spu_dc2_ent ent[DC2_ENTRIES];
+    spu_dc2_tuple st[DC2_STATES];
+    uint8_t st_used[DC2_STATES];
+} spu_dc2;
+static SPU_TLS spu_dc2 t_dc2;
+static const char* const s_dc2_base = (const char*)(void*)spu_lifted_lookup_full;
+
+/* [spu-static]'s recorder (below) is fed from the dispatcher's per-dispatch note. */
+static int spu_tl_enabled(void);
+static void spu_tl_note_lookup(const spu_context* ctx, uint32_t pc);
+static int s_tl_on;
+static SPU_NOINLINE_COLD int spu_dfast_diag_init(void)
+{
+    if (s_dfc_period < 0) { const char* e = getenv("SPU_DISPATCH_STAT"); s_dfc_period = e ? atoi(e) : 0; }
+    const int on = s_dfc_period > 0 || spu_tl_enabled() > 0;
+    __atomic_store_n(&g_spu_dfast_diag, on, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
+    return on;
+}
+static SPU_NOINLINE_COLD spu_dfast_counts* spu_dfast_alloc(spu_dc2* d)
+{
+    spu_dfast_counts* n = (spu_dfast_counts*)calloc(1, sizeof *n);
+    const long i = __atomic_fetch_add(&s_dfc_nthr, 1, __ATOMIC_ACQ_REL);
+    if (!n || i >= SPU_DFC_THREADS) { free(n); n = &s_dfc_spill; }
+    else __atomic_store_n(&s_dfc_thr[i], n, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
+    g_spu_dfc_drain_p = &n->drain[0];
+    if (g_spu_dfast_diag < 0) spu_dfast_diag_init();
+    return d->n = n;
+}
+static inline spu_dfast_counts* spu_dfc(spu_dc2* d)
+{
+    spu_dfast_counts* n = d->n;
+    return __builtin_expect(n != 0, 1) ? n : spu_dfast_alloc(d);
+}
+
+/* ---- The interrupt-toggle idiom (SPU_DISPATCH_STAT only) -----------------------------
+ * The job code wraps each DMA set-up in `bid` / `bie` to the very next instruction;
+ * the lift turns each into a full dispatch. Counted per image: dispatches whose pc
+ * follows such a branch (the word at pc-4 is `bi` with the D or E bit through a
+ * register that holds pc), and full drains of spu_drain_call that start with one
+ * pending (the branch sat in a called function). Exact and read-only. */
+static inline uint32_t spu_dfast_be32(const uint8_t* p) { return (uint32_t)p[0] << 24 | (uint32_t)p[1] << 16 | (uint32_t)p[2] << 8 | p[3]; }
+static inline int spu_toggle_to_next(const spu_context* c, uint32_t pc)
+{
+    if (pc < 4 || (pc & 3) || pc >= SPU_LS_SIZE) return 0;
+    const uint32_t w = spu_dfast_be32(c->ls + pc - 4);
+    return (w >> 21) == 0x1A8u && (w & 0xC0000u) && (c->gpr[(w >> 7) & 0x7F]._u32[0] & 0x3FFFCu) == pc;
+}
+static spu_dfast_img* spu_dfast_img_of(spu_dfast_counts* n, const spu_context* c, uint32_t pc)
+{
+    int img = c->image_id; uint32_t src = 0;
+    for (unsigned s = 0; s < 4; ++s)
+        if (c->resident_code[s].image_id && pc - c->resident_code[s].lsa < c->resident_code[s].size) {
+            img = c->resident_code[s].image_id; src = c->resident_code[s].source_ea; break;
+        }
+    if (img == c->image_id && c->resident_ovl) img = c->resident_ovl;
+    unsigned k = (uint32_t)img * 0x9E3779B1u >> 26;
+    for (unsigned probe = 0; probe < DFC_IMGS; probe++, k = (k + 1) & (DFC_IMGS - 1)) {
+        spu_dfast_img* e = &n->img[k];
+        if (e->all == 0 && e->img == 0) { e->img = img; e->src_ea = src; }
+        if (e->img == img) { if (src && !e->src_ea) e->src_ea = src; return e; }
+    }
+    return NULL;
+}
+static SPU_NOINLINE_COLD void spu_dfast_note_dispatch(spu_context* ctx)
+{
+    spu_dfast_counts* n = spu_dfc(&t_dc2);
+    const uint32_t pc = ctx->pc & SPU_LS_MASK;
+    const int t = spu_toggle_to_next(ctx, pc);
+    n->disp_all++; n->disp_toggle += (unsigned)t;
+    spu_dfast_img* e = spu_dfast_img_of(n, ctx, pc);
+    if (e) { e->all++; e->toggle += (unsigned)t; }
+    if (s_tl_on > 0) spu_tl_note_lookup(ctx, pc);
+}
+/* spu_drain.c: a drain about to take its full loop with a transfer pending. */
+void spu_dfast_note_drain(spu_context* ctx)
+{
+    const uint32_t pc = ctx->pc & SPU_LS_MASK;
+    if (!spu_toggle_to_next(ctx, pc)) return;
+    spu_dfast_counts* n = spu_dfc(&t_dc2);
+    n->drain_toggle++;
+    spu_dfast_img* e = spu_dfast_img_of(n, ctx, pc);
+    if (e) e->drains++;
+}
+
+static SPU_NOINLINE_COLD void spu_dfast_print(void)
+{
+    if (s_dfc_period < 0) spu_dfast_diag_init();
+    if (s_dfc_period <= 0) return;
+#ifdef _WIN32
+    const long long now = (long long)GetTickCount64();
+#else
+    struct timespec ts; clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &ts);
+    const long long now = (long long)ts.tv_sec * 1000 + ts.tv_nsec / 1000000;
+#endif
+    const long long next = s_dfc_next_ms;
+    if (!next) { s_dfc_next_ms = now + 1000ll * s_dfc_period; return; }
+    if (now < next || __atomic_exchange_n(&s_dfc_printing, 1, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) return;
+    if (s_dfc_next_ms == next) {
+        static spu_dfast_counts prev, cur; static long long prev_ms;
+        memset(&cur, 0, sizeof cur);
+        const long nt = s_dfc_nthr < SPU_DFC_THREADS ? s_dfc_nthr : SPU_DFC_THREADS;
+        for (long i = -1; i < nt; i++) {
+            const spu_dfast_counts* c = i < 0 ? &s_dfc_spill : __atomic_load_n(&s_dfc_thr[i], __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
+            if (!c) continue;
+            const unsigned long long* a = (const unsigned long long*)c; unsigned long long* b = (unsigned long long*)&cur;
+            for (size_t k = 0; k < DFC_SUMMED; k++) b[k] += a[k];
+            for (int k = 0; k < DFC_IMGS; k++) {
+                const spu_dfast_img* e = &c->img[k];
+                if (!e->all && !e->drains) continue;
+                int j = 0;
+                while (j < DFC_IMGS && (cur.img[j].all || cur.img[j].drains) && cur.img[j].img != e->img) j++;
+                if (j == DFC_IMGS) continue;
+                cur.img[j].img = e->img; if (e->src_ea) cur.img[j].src_ea = e->src_ea;
+                cur.img[j].all += e->all; cur.img[j].toggle += e->toggle; cur.img[j].drains += e->drains;
+            }
+        }
+        const double s = prev_ms ? (double)(now - prev_ms) / 1000.0 : (double)s_dfc_period;
+#define DFC(f) ((double)(cur.f - prev.f) / s)
+        fprintf(stderr, "[spu-dfast] per s: dispatches plain %.0f, full %.0f (interrupt return %.0f, service pc %.0f, "
+                "task %.0f, not cached %.0f, nothing lifted %.0f, job return or stack reset %.0f, switched off %.0f); "
+                "lookups hit %.0f, hit-nothing %.0f, miss %.0f, uncached %.0f; drains plain %.0f, full %.0f; "
+                "states %llu, start-overs %llu, threads %ld, shadow mismatches %lld\n",
+                DFC(ib_plain), DFC(ib_irq) + DFC(ib_svc) + DFC(ib_task) + DFC(ib_cold) + DFC(ib_null) + DFC(ib_reset) + DFC(ib_full_off),
+                DFC(ib_irq), DFC(ib_svc), DFC(ib_task), DFC(ib_cold), DFC(ib_null), DFC(ib_reset), DFC(ib_full_off),
+                DFC(hit), DFC(neg_hit), DFC(miss), DFC(nocache), DFC(drain[0]), DFC(drain[1]),
+                cur.states, cur.flush, nt, (long long)__atomic_load_n(&s_dfc_shadow_bad, __ATOMIC_RELAXED));
+        /* The toggle-to-next share, per image: busiest first. */
+        {
+            char buf[1600]; int p = 0;
+            const double all = DFC(disp_all), tog = DFC(disp_toggle);
+            p += snprintf(buf + p, sizeof buf - p, "[spu-dfast] per s: dispatches %.0f, after a bid/bie to the next "
+                          "instruction %.0f (%.1f %%); full drains %.0f, started by one in a called function %.0f; "
+                          "by image (dispatches/toggle/drains):", all, tog, all > 0 ? 100.0 * tog / all : 0.0,
+                          DFC(drain[1]), DFC(drain_toggle));
+            static spu_dfast_img pimg[DFC_IMGS];
+            for (int r = 0; r < 10; r++) {
+                int best = -1; double bt = -1;
+                for (int j = 0; j < DFC_IMGS; j++) {
+                    if (!cur.img[j].all && !cur.img[j].drains) continue;
+                    const spu_dfast_img* q = NULL;
+                    for (int k = 0; k < DFC_IMGS; k++) if ((pimg[k].all || pimg[k].drains) && pimg[k].img == cur.img[j].img) q = &pimg[k];
+                    const double t = (double)(cur.img[j].all - (q ? q->all : 0));
+                    if (t > bt && cur.img[j].img != INT32_MIN) { bt = t; best = j; }
+                }
+                if (best < 0 || bt <= 0) break;
+                const spu_dfast_img* q = NULL;
+                for (int k = 0; k < DFC_IMGS; k++) if ((pimg[k].all || pimg[k].drains) && pimg[k].img == cur.img[best].img) q = &pimg[k];
+                char name[24];
+                if (cur.img[best].src_ea) snprintf(name, sizeof name, "w%08X", cur.img[best].src_ea);
+                else snprintf(name, sizeof name, "img%d", cur.img[best].img);
+                p += snprintf(buf + p, sizeof buf - p, " %s %.0f/%.0f/%.0f", name,
+                              (double)(cur.img[best].all - (q ? q->all : 0)) / s,
+                              (double)(cur.img[best].toggle - (q ? q->toggle : 0)) / s,
+                              (double)(cur.img[best].drains - (q ? q->drains : 0)) / s);
+                cur.img[best].img = INT32_MIN;            /* printed (cur is rebuilt every time) */
+                if (p > (int)sizeof buf - 64) break;
+            }
+            if (__atomic_load_n(&g_spu_dfast_diag, __ATOMIC_RELAXED) > 0) fprintf(stderr, "%s\n", buf);
+            /* keep this window's per-image totals for the next difference */
+            memset(pimg, 0, sizeof pimg);
+            for (long i = -1; i < nt; i++) {
+                const spu_dfast_counts* c = i < 0 ? &s_dfc_spill : __atomic_load_n(&s_dfc_thr[i], __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
+                if (!c) continue;
+                for (int k = 0; k < DFC_IMGS; k++) {
+                    const spu_dfast_img* e = &c->img[k];
+                    if (!e->all && !e->drains) continue;
+                    int j = 0;
+                    while (j < DFC_IMGS && (pimg[j].all || pimg[j].drains) && pimg[j].img != e->img) j++;
+                    if (j == DFC_IMGS) continue;
+                    pimg[j].img = e->img; pimg[j].all += e->all; pimg[j].toggle += e->toggle; pimg[j].drains += e->drains;
+                }
+            }
+        }
+#undef DFC
+        fflush(stderr);
+        prev = cur; prev_ms = now;
+        s_dfc_next_ms = now + 1000ll * s_dfc_period;
+    }
+    __atomic_store_n(&s_dfc_printing, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
+}
+
+/* ---- [spu-static]: what still runs without static code (always on) ------------------------------
+ * The goal is that every SPU instruction the game runs is lifted code reached by a branch the lifter
+ * resolved. What is still dynamic is counted here, by image and reason, and printed every 5 s
+ * (SPU_STATIC_STAT=<seconds> another period, 0 off):
+ *
+ *   [spu-static] 5 s: interpreted N (<image> <reason> <n>, ...), looked up N (cache N, full N),
+ *                unknown images N; since start: interpreted N, unknown images N
+ *
+ * interpreted -- control reached code the runtime ran some other way than as lifted code:
+ *   "no lifted entry"   a branch to a pc with no lifted function, run by the interpreter until it
+ *                       rejoins lifted code (spu_smc_microstep -> spu_interp_run_until): the static
+ *                       answer is an entry there (GT5: scripts/spu_static_entries.txt)
+ *   "generated code"    bytes the SPU wrote itself, run by the micro-interpreter to their branch
+ *                       (the job manager's register stubs at 0x3FEC0 when their words do not match the
+ *                       native forms in spu_wws_irq_native.h)
+ *   "nothing to run"    no lifted function and nothing the interpreters could run: the SPU halts
+ *   "unlifted local store"  SPU_INTERP_UNLIFTED (off by default)
+ *   "unlifted program"  a whole SPU program interpreted (lv2 RD_SPU_INTERP, off by default)
+ *   "data word"         a word of data inside an executable range reached as an instruction
+ *                       (spu_unsupported: the lifted code goes on, as before, and is wrong from there)
+ * looked up -- branches whose target the runtime resolved while the game ran (spu_indirect_branch:
+ *   "cache" = the dispatch cache's plain path, "full" = the whole dispatcher), from the per-thread
+ *   dispatch counters above; every branch the lifter (or GT5's build-time direct branches) resolved
+ *   never gets here.
+ * unknown images -- SPU programs and jobs the game started that have no lifted code (a dispatch MISS,
+ *   an SPU thread image that is not in the registry).
+ *
+ * SPU_TARGET_LOG=<file>: the recorder. Every (image, target) the runtime looked up or interpreted,
+ * deduplicated and counted, written to <file> at every line and at exit, one per line in the form of
+ * GT5's scripts/spu_static_entries.txt: `<image> <address> <how> <count>`, <how> = interpreted /
+ * generated / missing / unlifted / dataword / lookup. Lookups are counted per thread (no shared write on
+ * the dispatch path); everything else is rare and takes a lock. Off: one load and a branch per dispatch,
+ * the same test the dispatch statistics already make. */
+enum { ST_NOENTRY, ST_STUB, ST_MISS, ST_UNLIFTED, ST_PROGRAM, ST_DATAWORD, ST_ANY, ST_NREASON, ST_LOOKUP = ST_NREASON };
+static const char* const k_st_reason[ST_NREASON] = {
+    "no lifted entry", "generated code", "nothing to run", "unlifted local store", "unlifted program", "data word",
+    "any-address form" };
+static const char* const k_st_how[ST_NREASON + 1] = {
+    "interpreted", "generated", "missing", "unlifted", "program", "dataword", "anyaddr", "lookup" };
+typedef struct { int img; uint32_t src, reason; unsigned long long n; } spu_st_ent;
+#define SPU_ST_ENTS 128
+static spu_st_ent s_st[SPU_ST_ENTS], s_st_prev[SPU_ST_ENTS];
+static volatile long s_st_lock;
+static unsigned long long s_st_total, s_st_unknown, s_st_total_prev, s_st_unknown_prev, s_st_lost;
+static unsigned long long s_st_any, s_st_any_prev;   /* entries into an any-address form (not "interpreted") */
+static int s_st_quiet;                    /* default: a line only when a count that should be 0 grew, and at exit */
+static int s_st_period = -1;              /* seconds, 0 = off */
+static long long s_st_next_ms, s_st_prev_ms;
+static volatile long s_st_printing;
+static unsigned long long s_st_look_prev[2];
+/* the recorder */
+static int s_tl_on = -1;                  /* SPU_TARGET_LOG: -1 not read, 0 off, 1 on (declared above) */
+static char s_tl_path[520];
+typedef struct { int img; uint32_t src, pc, how; unsigned long long n; } spu_tl_ent;
+#define SPU_TL_ENTS 8192u
+typedef struct { spu_tl_ent e[SPU_TL_ENTS]; uint32_t used, full; } spu_tl_tab;
+#define SPU_TL_THREADS 256
+static spu_tl_tab* volatile s_tl_thr[SPU_TL_THREADS];
+static volatile long s_tl_nthr;
+static spu_tl_tab s_tl_shared;            /* the rare kinds, under s_st_lock */
+static SPU_TLS spu_tl_tab* t_tl;
+static volatile long long s_tl_lost;
+
+static inline void spu_st_lock(void) { while (__atomic_exchange_n(&s_st_lock, 1, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) { } }
+static inline void spu_st_unlock(void) { __atomic_store_n(&s_st_lock, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE); }
+static long long spu_st_now_ms(void)
+{
+#ifdef _WIN32
+    return (long long)GetTickCount64();
+#else
+    struct timespec ts; clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &ts);
+    return (long long)ts.tv_sec * 1000 + ts.tv_nsec / 1000000;
+#endif
+}
+/* The image that owns pc for this context, in the resolver's order (spu_lifted_lookup_full): the first
+ * resident code slot holding pc (its image, and the main-memory address its code came from), else the
+ * resident overlay or task, else the context's image. */
+static void spu_st_owner(const spu_context* c, uint32_t pc, int* img, uint32_t* src)
+{
+    *img = c ? c->image_id : -1; *src = 0;
+    if (!c) return;
+    for (unsigned s = 0; s < 4; ++s)
+        if (c->resident_code[s].image_id && pc - c->resident_code[s].lsa < c->resident_code[s].size) {
+            *img = c->resident_code[s].image_id; *src = c->resident_code[s].source_ea; return;
+        }
+    if (c->resident_task) *img = c->resident_task;
+    else if (c->resident_ovl) *img = c->resident_ovl;
+}
+static void spu_tl_add(spu_tl_tab* t, int img, uint32_t src, uint32_t pc, unsigned how)
+{
+    const uint64_t h = ((uint64_t)(uint32_t)img << 32 ^ src ^ (uint64_t)pc << 13 ^ how) * 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15ull;
+    uint32_t i = (uint32_t)(h >> 51) & (SPU_TL_ENTS - 1);
+    for (uint32_t probe = 0; probe < SPU_TL_ENTS; probe++, i = (i + 1) & (SPU_TL_ENTS - 1)) {
+        spu_tl_ent* e = &t->e[i];
+        if (e->n && e->img == img && e->src == src && e->pc == pc && e->how == how) { e->n++; return; }
+        if (!e->n) {
+            if (t->used >= SPU_TL_ENTS * 3 / 4) { t->full = 1; __atomic_add_fetch(&s_tl_lost, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED); return; }
+            e->img = img; e->src = src; e->pc = pc; e->how = how; t->used++;
+            __atomic_store_n(&e->n, 1ull, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);   /* fields first: the writer reads n first */
+            return;
+        }
+    }
+}
+static SPU_NOINLINE_COLD int spu_tl_init(void)
+{
+    const char* e = getenv("SPU_TARGET_LOG");
+    if (e && *e) { snprintf(s_tl_path, sizeof s_tl_path, "%s", e); }
+    __atomic_store_n(&s_tl_on, e && *e ? 1 : 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
+    if (e && *e) fprintf(stderr, "[spu-static] recording every target looked up or interpreted to %s\n", s_tl_path);
+    return s_tl_on;
+}
+static int spu_tl_enabled(void) { const int v = __atomic_load_n(&s_tl_on, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE); return v < 0 ? spu_tl_init() : v; }
+/* A lookup by the dispatcher (only while the recorder is on: spu_dfast_note_dispatch). */
+static SPU_NOINLINE_COLD void spu_tl_note_lookup(const spu_context* ctx, uint32_t pc)
+{
+    spu_tl_tab* t = t_tl;
+    if (!t) {
+        const long i = __atomic_fetch_add(&s_tl_nthr, 1, __ATOMIC_ACQ_REL);
+        if (i >= SPU_TL_THREADS) { __atomic_add_fetch(&s_tl_lost, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED); return; }
+        t = (spu_tl_tab*)calloc(1, sizeof *t);
+        if (!t) return;
+        __atomic_store_n(&s_tl_thr[i], t, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
+        t_tl = t;
+    }
+    int img; uint32_t src;
+    spu_st_owner(ctx, pc, &img, &src);
+    spu_tl_add(t, img, src, pc & SPU_LS_MASK, ST_LOOKUP);    /* the writer reads it unlocked: counts may lag */
+}
+/* Everything that is not lifted code reached by a lifted or looked-up branch: counted by (image, reason). */
+static void spu_st_note_key(int img, uint32_t src, uint32_t pc, unsigned reason)
+{
+    const int tl = spu_tl_enabled() > 0;
+    spu_st_lock();
+    if (reason == ST_ANY) s_st_any++; else s_st_total++;
+    int k = 0;
+    while (k < SPU_ST_ENTS && s_st[k].n && !(s_st[k].img == img && s_st[k].src == src && s_st[k].reason == reason)) k++;
+    if (k < SPU_ST_ENTS) { if (!s_st[k].n) { s_st[k].img = img; s_st[k].src = src; s_st[k].reason = reason; } s_st[k].n++; }
+    else s_st_lost++;
+    if (tl) spu_tl_add(&s_tl_shared, img, src, pc, reason);
+    spu_st_unlock();
+}
+void spu_static_note(const spu_context* ctx, uint32_t pc, unsigned reason)
+{
+    int img; uint32_t src;
+    spu_st_owner(ctx, pc & SPU_LS_MASK, &img, &src);
+    spu_st_note_key(img, src, pc & SPU_LS_MASK, reason);
+}
+/* lv2's whole-program interpreter (no context of the runtime's yet): by program entry. */
+void spu_static_note_program(int img, uint32_t entry) { spu_st_note_key(img, 0, entry & SPU_LS_MASK, ST_PROGRAM); }
+/* An SPU program or job the game started that has no lifted code (spu_workload.c, lv2). */
+void spu_static_note_unknown(void)
+{
+    spu_st_lock(); s_st_unknown++; spu_st_unlock();
+}
+/* spu_helpers.h's spu_unsupported (a `.word` the lifter kept as data) reaches this through a hook, so
+ * lifted code that is linked without this file still builds. */
+static void spu_st_dataword(const spu_context* ctx, uint32_t pc) { spu_static_note(ctx, pc, ST_DATAWORD); }
+__attribute__((constructor)) static void spu_st_hook_init(void) { g_spu_dataword_hook = spu_st_dataword; }
+
+/* The name of an image for the log: a Wws job's code by its main-memory address (GT5 names the lift
+ * w<address>), anything else by its workload registration name, else its id. */
+const char* spu_workload_name_of(int image_id);   /* spu_workload.c */
+static void spu_st_name(int img, uint32_t src, char* out, size_t n)
+{
+    if (src) { snprintf(out, n, "w%08X", src); return; }
+    const char* nm = img > 0 ? spu_workload_name_of(img) : NULL;
+    if (nm && *nm) {
+        size_t k = strcspn(nm, ".");
+        if (k > 12 && !strncmp(nm, "spu_", 4)) k = 12;       /* spu_<sha256>: the first bytes are enough */
+        snprintf(out, n, "%.*s", (int)k, nm);
+        return;
+    }
+    snprintf(out, n, "img%d", img);
+}
+static int spu_tl_cmp(const void* a, const void* b)
+{
+    const spu_tl_ent* x = (const spu_tl_ent*)a; const spu_tl_ent* y = (const spu_tl_ent*)b;
+    if (x->img != y->img) return x->img < y->img ? -1 : 1;
+    if (x->src != y->src) return x->src < y->src ? -1 : 1;
+    if (x->pc != y->pc) return x->pc < y->pc ? -1 : 1;
+    return x->how < y->how ? -1 : x->how > y->how;
+}
+static int spu_tl_same(const spu_tl_ent* x, const spu_tl_ent* y)
+{
+    return x->img == y->img && x->src == y->src && x->pc == y->pc && x->how == y->how;
+}
+static void spu_tl_write(void)
+{
+    if (spu_tl_enabled() <= 0) return;
+    const long nt = s_tl_nthr < SPU_TL_THREADS ? s_tl_nthr : SPU_TL_THREADS;
+    size_t cap = SPU_TL_ENTS * (size_t)(nt + 1), cnt = 0;
+    spu_tl_ent* all = (spu_tl_ent*)malloc(cap * sizeof *all);
+    if (!all) return;
+    spu_st_lock();
+    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < SPU_TL_ENTS; i++) if (s_tl_shared.e[i].n) all[cnt++] = s_tl_shared.e[i];
+    spu_st_unlock();
+    for (long t = 0; t < nt; t++) {
+        const spu_tl_tab* tab = __atomic_load_n(&s_tl_thr[t], __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
+        if (!tab) continue;
+        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < SPU_TL_ENTS && cnt < cap; i++) {
+            if (!__atomic_load_n(&tab->e[i].n, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) continue;
+            all[cnt++] = tab->e[i];
+        }
+    }
+    qsort(all, cnt, sizeof *all, spu_tl_cmp);
+    char tmp[540]; snprintf(tmp, sizeof tmp, "%s.tmp", s_tl_path);
+    FILE* f = fopen(tmp, "w");
+    if (f) {
+        fprintf(f, "# SPU_TARGET_LOG: every SPU code address the runtime looked up or could not run as lifted code\n"
+                   "# <image> <address> <how> <count>; how = interpreted (no lifted entry: add the line to GT5\\scripts\\\n"
+                   "# spu_static_entries.txt), generated (code the SPU wrote), missing, unlifted, program, dataword,\n"
+                   "# lookup (lifted code reached through the dispatcher). Lost (tables full): %lld\n",
+                (long long)__atomic_load_n(&s_tl_lost, __ATOMIC_RELAXED));
+        for (size_t i = 0; i < cnt;) {
+            size_t j = i; unsigned long long n = 0;
+            while (j < cnt && spu_tl_same(&all[j], &all[i])) n += all[j++].n;
+            char nm[48]; spu_st_name(all[i].img, all[i].src, nm, sizeof nm);
+            fprintf(f, "%s %08X %s %llu\n", nm, all[i].pc, all[i].how <= ST_NREASON ? k_st_how[all[i].how] : "?", n);
+            i = j;
+        }
+        fclose(f);
+        remove(s_tl_path);
+        rename(tmp, s_tl_path);
+    }
+    free(all);
+}
+static void spu_st_atexit(void);
+
+/* Called often from somewhere that runs whatever the SPUs do (the SPURS coordinator's passes); prints
+ * when a period has passed. Returns at once otherwise. */
+int spu_static_report_due(void)
+{
+    if (s_st_period < 0) {
+        /* SPU_STATIC_STAT unset: quiet (checked every 5 s, printed only when "interpreted" or "unknown images"
+         * grew; the totals once at exit); 1: every 5 s; N > 1: every N s; 0: nothing */
+        const char* e = getenv("SPU_STATIC_STAT");
+        const int v = e ? atoi(e) : 5;
+        s_st_quiet = !e;
+        s_st_period = v == 1 ? 5 : v;
+        if (s_st_period > 0) atexit(spu_st_atexit);
+    }
+    return s_st_period > 0 && (!s_st_next_ms || spu_st_now_ms() >= s_st_next_ms);
+}
+void spu_static_report(void)
+{
+    if (!spu_static_report_due()) return;
+    const long long now = spu_st_now_ms();
+    if (!s_st_next_ms) { s_st_next_ms = now + 1000ll * s_st_period; s_st_prev_ms = now; return; }
+    if (__atomic_exchange_n(&s_st_printing, 1, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) return;
+    if (now >= s_st_next_ms) {
+        /* looked up: the dispatcher's own per-thread counts (spu_dfast_counts) */
+        unsigned long long plain = 0, full = 0;
+        const long nt = s_dfc_nthr < SPU_DFC_THREADS ? s_dfc_nthr : SPU_DFC_THREADS;
+        for (long i = -1; i < nt; i++) {
+            const spu_dfast_counts* c = i < 0 ? &s_dfc_spill : __atomic_load_n(&s_dfc_thr[i], __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
+            if (!c) continue;
+            plain += c->ib_plain;
+            full += c->ib_irq + c->ib_svc + c->ib_task + c->ib_cold + c->ib_null + c->ib_reset + c->ib_full_off;
+        }
+        spu_st_ent cur[SPU_ST_ENTS];
+        spu_st_lock();
+        memcpy(cur, s_st, sizeof cur);
+        const unsigned long long tot = s_st_total, unk = s_st_unknown, anyn = s_st_any;
+        spu_st_unlock();
+        if (s_st_quiet && tot == s_st_total_prev && unk == s_st_unknown_prev) {
+            /* quiet: nothing that should be 0 grew -- no line (the totals come at exit) */
+            s_st_next_ms = now + 1000ll * s_st_period;
+            spu_tl_write();
+            __atomic_store_n(&s_st_printing, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
+            return;
+        }
+        char buf[1600]; int p = 0;
+        const double s = (double)(now - s_st_prev_ms) / 1000.0;
+        p += snprintf(buf + p, sizeof buf - p, "[spu-static] %.0f s: interpreted %llu", s, tot - s_st_total_prev);
+        /* this period's reasons, the largest first */
+        unsigned long long d[SPU_ST_ENTS];
+        int any = 0;
+        for (int k = 0; k < SPU_ST_ENTS; k++) {
+            unsigned long long was = 0;
+            for (int j = 0; j < SPU_ST_ENTS && s_st_prev[j].n; j++)
+                if (s_st_prev[j].img == cur[k].img && s_st_prev[j].src == cur[k].src && s_st_prev[j].reason == cur[k].reason) { was = s_st_prev[j].n; break; }
+            d[k] = cur[k].n - was;
+        }
+        for (int r = 0; r < 8; r++) {
+            int best = -1;
+            for (int k = 0; k < SPU_ST_ENTS; k++) if (cur[k].n && d[k] && cur[k].reason != ST_ANY && (best < 0 || d[k] > d[best])) best = k;
+            if (best < 0) break;
+            char nm[48]; spu_st_name(cur[best].img, cur[best].src, nm, sizeof nm);
+            p += snprintf(buf + p, sizeof buf - p, "%s%s %s %llu", any ? ", " : " (", nm,
+                          cur[best].reason < ST_NREASON ? k_st_reason[cur[best].reason] : "?", d[best]);
+            any = 1; d[best] = 0;
+        }
+        if (any) p += snprintf(buf + p, sizeof buf - p, ")");
+        /* the any-address entries: lifted code, but where the fast lift could have an entry (SPU_TARGET_LOG) */
+        p += snprintf(buf + p, sizeof buf - p, ", any-address %llu", anyn - s_st_any_prev);
+        any = 0;
+        for (int r = 0; r < 4; r++) {
+            int best = -1;
+            for (int k = 0; k < SPU_ST_ENTS; k++) if (cur[k].n && d[k] && cur[k].reason == ST_ANY && (best < 0 || d[k] > d[best])) best = k;
+            if (best < 0) break;
+            char nm[48]; spu_st_name(cur[best].img, cur[best].src, nm, sizeof nm);
+            p += snprintf(buf + p, sizeof buf - p, "%s%s %llu", any ? ", " : " (", nm, d[best]);
+            any = 1; d[best] = 0;
+        }
+        if (any) p += snprintf(buf + p, sizeof buf - p, ")");
+        p += snprintf(buf + p, sizeof buf - p, ", looked up %llu (cache %llu, full %llu), unknown images %llu; "
+                      "since start: interpreted %llu, any-address %llu, unknown images %llu\n",
+                      (plain + full) - (s_st_look_prev[0] + s_st_look_prev[1]), plain - s_st_look_prev[0],
+                      full - s_st_look_prev[1], unk - s_st_unknown_prev, tot, anyn, unk);
+        fputs(buf, stderr);
+        fflush(stderr);
+        memcpy(s_st_prev, cur, sizeof cur);
+        s_st_total_prev = tot; s_st_unknown_prev = unk; s_st_any_prev = anyn;
+        s_st_look_prev[0] = plain; s_st_look_prev[1] = full;
+        s_st_prev_ms = now;
+        s_st_next_ms = now + 1000ll * s_st_period;
+        spu_tl_write();
+    }
+    __atomic_store_n(&s_st_printing, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
+}
+
+/* At exit: the totals since start, one line (and the recorder's file). */
+static void spu_st_atexit(void)
+{
+    unsigned long long plain = 0, full = 0;
+    const long nt = s_dfc_nthr < SPU_DFC_THREADS ? s_dfc_nthr : SPU_DFC_THREADS;
+    for (long i = -1; i < nt; i++) {
+        const spu_dfast_counts* c = i < 0 ? &s_dfc_spill : __atomic_load_n(&s_dfc_thr[i], __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
+        if (!c) continue;
+        plain += c->ib_plain;
+        full += c->ib_irq + c->ib_svc + c->ib_task + c->ib_cold + c->ib_null + c->ib_reset + c->ib_full_off;
+    }
+    fprintf(stderr, "[spu-static] at exit, since start: interpreted %llu, any-address %llu, looked up %llu "
+            "(cache %llu, full %llu), unknown images %llu\n", s_st_total, s_st_any, plain + full, plain, full, s_st_unknown);
+    fflush(stderr);
+    if (spu_tl_enabled() > 0) spu_tl_write();
+}
+
+static inline uint32_t spu_dc2_hash(const spu_dc2_tuple* t)
+{
+    uint64_t h = ((uint64_t)t->id << 32 | t->residency) * 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15ull;
+    h ^= ((uint64_t)(uint32_t)t->image << 32 | (uint32_t)t->ovl) * 0xC2B2AE3D27D4EB4Full;
+    h ^= ((uint64_t)(uint32_t)t->task << 32 | t->rgen) * 0x165667B19E3779F9ull;
+    return (uint32_t)(h >> 40);
+}
+/* The tag of this key half: interned on first sight, the whole cache started
+ * over when the table is three quarters full (so no tag is ever reused while
+ * an entry filed under it remains). Sets the memo. */
+static SPU_DC2_NOINLINE uint32_t spu_dc2_tag(spu_dc2* d, const spu_dc2_tuple* t)
+{
+    if (__builtin_expect((++spu_dfc(d)->tagcalls & 0x3FFu) == 0, 0)) spu_dfast_print();   /* state changes: about one a job */
+    uint32_t i = spu_dc2_hash(t) & (DC2_STATES - 1);
+    for (;;) {
+        if (!d->st_used[i]) break;
+        const spu_dc2_tuple* s = &d->st[i];
+        if (s->id == t->id && s->residency == t->residency && s->rgen == t->rgen &&
+            s->image == t->image && s->ovl == t->ovl && s->task == t->task) {
+            d->memo = *t; d->memo_tag = i + 1;
+            return i + 1;
+        }
+        i = (i + 1) & (DC2_STATES - 1);
+    }
+    if (d->nstates >= DC2_STATES * 3 / 4) {
+        memset(d->ent, 0, sizeof d->ent);
+        memset(d->st_used, 0, sizeof d->st_used);
+        d->nstates = 0;
+        spu_dfc(d)->flush++;
+        i = spu_dc2_hash(t) & (DC2_STATES - 1);
+    }
+    d->st_used[i] = 1; d->st[i] = *t; d->nstates++; spu_dfc(d)->states++;
+    d->memo = *t; d->memo_tag = i + 1;
+    return i + 1;
+}
+static inline uint32_t spu_dc2_current_tag(spu_dc2* d, spu_context* c, uint32_t rgen)
+{
+    uint32_t id = c->dcache_id;
+    if (__builtin_expect(!id, 0)) id = spu_dcache_sign(c);
+    const uint32_t tag = d->memo_tag;
+    if (__builtin_expect(tag && d->memo.id == id && d->memo.residency == c->dcache_residency &&
+                         d->memo.image == c->image_id && d->memo.ovl == c->resident_ovl &&
+                         d->memo.task == c->resident_task && d->memo.rgen == rgen, 1))
+        return tag;
+    spu_dc2_tuple t;
+    t.id = id; t.residency = c->dcache_residency; t.rgen = rgen;
+    t.image = c->image_id; t.ovl = c->resident_ovl; t.task = c->resident_task;
+    return spu_dc2_tag(d, &t);
+}
+static SPU_DC2_NOINLINE spu_lifted_fn spu_dc2_miss(spu_dc2* d, spu_context* c, uint32_t lsa, uint32_t rgen)
+{
+    const spu_lifted_fn fn = spu_lifted_lookup_full(c, lsa);
+    if (lsa >= SPU_LS_SIZE || (lsa & 3)) { spu_dfc(d)->nocache++; return fn; }
+    long long off = DC2_NULL;
+    if (fn) {
+        off = (long long)((const char*)(void*)fn - s_dc2_base);
+        if (off <= (long long)DC2_NULL || off > (long long)INT32_MAX) { spu_dfc(d)->nocache++; return fn; }
+    }
+    /* The resolver may have verified a pending code slot, which changes the
+     * signature: file the answer under the state as it stands now (with the
+     * registry count read before the resolve), as the cache above does. */
+    const uint32_t tag = spu_dc2_current_tag(d, c, rgen);
+    spu_dc2_ent* e = &d->ent[((lsa >> 2) ^ (tag * 0x9E3779B1u)) & (DC2_ENTRIES - 1)];
+    e->key = tag << 16 | lsa >> 2;
+    e->fd = (int32_t)off;
+    spu_dfc(d)->miss++;
+    return fn;
+}
+static SPU_NOINLINE_COLD spu_lifted_fn spu_dc2_shadow(spu_dc2* d, spu_context* c, uint32_t lsa, spu_lifted_fn got)
+{
+    (void)d;
+    const spu_lifted_fn full = spu_lifted_lookup_full(c, lsa);
+    if (full != got && __atomic_fetch_add(&s_dfc_shadow_bad, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED) < 16)
+        fprintf(stderr, "[spu-dfast] shadow mismatch img=%d ovl=%d task=%d lsa=0x%05X cached=%p full=%p\n",
+                c->image_id, c->resident_ovl, c->resident_task, lsa, (void*)got, (void*)full);
+    return full;
+}
+/* The fast path's lookup: the same answer as spu_lifted_lookup_full. */
+static inline spu_lifted_fn spu_dc2_lookup(spu_context* c, uint32_t lsa, int mode)
+{
+    spu_dc2* const d = &t_dc2;
+    /* Read before the resolver walks the registry: an entry is never keyed by
+     * a count newer than the registry it saw. */
+    const uint32_t rgen = __atomic_load_n(&s_registry_count, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
+    const uint32_t tag = spu_dc2_current_tag(d, c, rgen);
+    const spu_dc2_ent* e = &d->ent[((lsa >> 2) ^ (tag * 0x9E3779B1u)) & (DC2_ENTRIES - 1)];
+    if (__builtin_expect(e->key == (tag << 16 | lsa >> 2) && lsa < SPU_LS_SIZE && !(lsa & 3), 1)) {
+        const int32_t fd = e->fd;
+        spu_lifted_fn fn = fd == DC2_NULL ? NULL : (spu_lifted_fn)(void*)(s_dc2_base + fd);
+        if (fn) spu_dfc(d)->hit++; else spu_dfc(d)->neg_hit++;
+        if (__builtin_expect(mode == 2, 0)) fn = spu_dc2_shadow(d, c, lsa, fn);
+        return fn;
+    }
+    return spu_dc2_miss(d, c, lsa, rgen);
+}
+
+spu_lifted_fn spu_lifted_lookup(const spu_context* ctx, uint32_t lsa)
+{
+    {
+        const int m = spu_dfast_mode();
+        if (m > 0 && ctx) return spu_dc2_lookup((spu_context*)ctx, lsa, m);
+    }
+    const int mode = spu_dcache_mode();
+    if (!mode || !ctx) return spu_lifted_lookup_full(ctx, lsa);
+    spu_context* c = (spu_context*)ctx;
+    uint32_t id = c->dcache_id;
+    if (!id) id = spu_dcache_sign(c);
+    /* Read before the resolver walks the registry: an entry is never keyed by
+     * a count newer than the registry it saw. */
+    const uint32_t rgen = __atomic_load_n(&s_registry_count, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
+    spu_dcache_ent* e = &t_dcache[((lsa >> 2) ^ (id * 0x9E3779B1u)) & (SPU_DCACHE_ENTRIES - 1)];
+    if (e->fn && e->id == id && e->lsa == lsa && e->rgen == rgen &&
+        e->residency == c->dcache_residency && e->image == c->image_id &&
+        e->ovl == c->resident_ovl && e->task == c->resident_task) {
+        if (mode == 2) {
+            __atomic_fetch_add(&s_dcache_hits, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
+            const spu_lifted_fn full = spu_lifted_lookup_full(ctx, lsa);
+            if (full != e->fn) {
+                if (__atomic_fetch_add(&s_dcache_shadow_bad, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED) < 16)
+                    fprintf(stderr, "[spu-dcache] shadow mismatch img=%d ovl=%d task=%d lsa=0x%05X "
+                            "cached=%p full=%p\n", c->image_id, c->resident_ovl, c->resident_task,
+                            lsa, (void*)e->fn, (void*)full);
+                e->fn = NULL;
+                return full;
+            }
+            spu_dcache_shadow_stats();
+        }
+        return e->fn;
+    }
+    if (mode == 2) {   /* shared counters only in shadow mode: they would bounce between SPU threads */
+        __atomic_fetch_add(&s_dcache_misses, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
+        spu_dcache_shadow_stats();
+    }
+    const spu_lifted_fn fn = spu_lifted_lookup_full(ctx, lsa);
+    if (fn) {
+        /* The resolver may have verified a pending slot, which changes the
+         * signature: the entry records the one it resolved against, read
+         * after it, and goes in the slot that signature selects. */
+        id = c->dcache_id;
+        if (!id) id = spu_dcache_sign(c);
+        e = &t_dcache[((lsa >> 2) ^ (id * 0x9E3779B1u)) & (SPU_DCACHE_ENTRIES - 1)];
+        e->fn = fn; e->id = id; e->lsa = lsa; e->rgen = rgen;
+        e->residency = c->dcache_residency; e->image = c->image_id;
+        e->ovl = c->resident_ovl; e->task = c->resident_task;
+    }
+    return fn;
+}
+
+/* ---- Swappable code overlays (see spu_context.resident_ovl) --------------
+ * A title registers each runtime-streamed overlay's SOURCE content EA with
+ * the image id its lifted functions were registered under. The MFC GET path
+ * marks that overlay resident in the streaming context; dispatch retries a
+ * primary-image miss against the resident overlay's registry. */
+typedef struct { uint32_t src_ea; int image_id; uint8_t sig[16]; int has_sig; uint32_t span;
+                 uint32_t load_lsa; unsigned code_count; spu_overlay_code_segment* code; } spu_ovl_src;
+/* 6 FMOD codec/DSP overlays + up to 89 WWS job-code modules (all stream into
+ * the same job code buffer at LS 0x4000, dispatched by content signature). */
+#define SPU_OVL_SRC_MAX 128
+static spu_ovl_src s_ovl_src[SPU_OVL_SRC_MAX];
+static int s_ovl_src_count = 0;
+
+/* Every MFC GET is checked against the registered sources, and a job that
+ * streams its data in small pieces issues thousands of GETs a frame against
+ * up to SPU_OVL_SRC_MAX sources. A GET under 512 bytes can only match a
+ * source by EA (signature entries need >= 512 bytes), so keep every
+ * registered source EA in an insert-only open-addressed set and skip the
+ * scan for a small GET whose EA was never registered.
+ *
+ * The set is a superset of the EA-keyed entries the scan can see: it has
+ * four times as many slots as there can be sources (so an insert always
+ * finds a slot, and a probe always reaches an empty one), nothing is ever
+ * removed, and an EA is inserted before the source count that publishes its
+ * entry is release-stored. spu_overlay_note_get acquire-loads the count
+ * before probing, so any entry the scan would visit is already in the set. */
+#define SPU_OVL_EA_SET 512u
+static uint32_t s_ovl_ea_set[SPU_OVL_EA_SET];
+static uint8_t s_ovl_ea_used[SPU_OVL_EA_SET];
+static unsigned spu_ovl_ea_slot(uint32_t ea) { return (ea * 0x9E3779B1u) >> 23; }
+static void spu_ovl_ea_add(uint32_t ea)
+{
+    for (unsigned i = spu_ovl_ea_slot(ea), n = 0; n < SPU_OVL_EA_SET; ++n, i = (i + 1) & (SPU_OVL_EA_SET - 1)) {
+        if (__atomic_load_n(&s_ovl_ea_used[i], __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) {
+            if (s_ovl_ea_set[i] == ea) return;
+            continue;
+        }
+        s_ovl_ea_set[i] = ea;
+        __atomic_store_n(&s_ovl_ea_used[i], 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
+        return;
+    }
+}
+static int spu_ovl_ea_known(uint32_t ea)
+{
+    for (unsigned i = spu_ovl_ea_slot(ea), n = 0; n < SPU_OVL_EA_SET; ++n, i = (i + 1) & (SPU_OVL_EA_SET - 1)) {
+        if (!__atomic_load_n(&s_ovl_ea_used[i], __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) return 0;
+        if (s_ovl_ea_set[i] == ea) return 1;
+    }
+    return 1;   /* full (cannot happen): never filter */
+}
+
+/* SPU_OVL_SIG_SCAN=1 (off by default): a GET of 512 bytes or more compared its first 16 bytes with
+ * every signature source in turn -- 89 WWS job modules and the FMOD overlays, on every such GET.
+ * Now every source is also filed in an insert-only index under its key (the first 8 signature bytes,
+ * or its EA), and the GET looks at the sources filed under its own key only, in source order, with
+ * the very same test and the same action as the scan: a source under another key cannot match
+ * (another signature differs in its first 8 bytes; another EA is another EA). Filed before the count
+ * that publishes the source is release-stored, so every source the scan could see is in the index. */
+#define SPU_OVL_IDX 512u
+static uint64_t s_ovl_idx_key[SPU_OVL_IDX];
+static uint16_t s_ovl_idx_src[SPU_OVL_IDX];
+static uint8_t  s_ovl_idx_used[SPU_OVL_IDX];          /* 0 empty, 1 signature key, 2 EA key */
+static unsigned spu_ovl_idx_slot(uint64_t key) { return (unsigned)((key * 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15ull) >> 55); }
+static void spu_ovl_idx_add(int kind, uint64_t key, int src)   /* registration (one thread at a time) */
+{
+    for (unsigned i = spu_ovl_idx_slot(key), n = 0; n < SPU_OVL_IDX; ++n, i = (i + 1) & (SPU_OVL_IDX - 1)) {
+        if (__atomic_load_n(&s_ovl_idx_used[i], __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) continue;
+        s_ovl_idx_key[i] = key; s_ovl_idx_src[i] = (uint16_t)src;
+        __atomic_store_n(&s_ovl_idx_used[i], (uint8_t)kind, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
+        return;
+    }
+}
+/* The sources filed under (kind, key) with index < nsrc, ascending, appended to out[*n]. */
+static void spu_ovl_idx_find(int kind, uint64_t key, int nsrc, int* out, int* n)
+{
+    for (unsigned i = spu_ovl_idx_slot(key), k = 0; k < SPU_OVL_IDX; ++k, i = (i + 1) & (SPU_OVL_IDX - 1)) {
+        const uint8_t u = __atomic_load_n(&s_ovl_idx_used[i], __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
+        if (!u) return;
+        if (u != kind || s_ovl_idx_key[i] != key || s_ovl_idx_src[i] >= nsrc) continue;
+        int j = (*n)++;
+        while (j > 0 && out[j - 1] > s_ovl_idx_src[i]) { out[j] = out[j - 1]; j--; }
+        out[j] = s_ovl_idx_src[i];
+    }
+}
+static uint64_t spu_ovl_sig_key(const uint8_t* b) { uint64_t k; memcpy(&k, b, 8); return k; }
+static int s_ovl_sig_scan = -1;   /* a file static so the stand-alone harness can compare both */
+static int spu_ovl_sig_scan(void)
+{
+    if (s_ovl_sig_scan < 0) { const char* e = getenv("SPU_OVL_SIG_SCAN"); s_ovl_sig_scan = e && *e == '1'; }
+    return s_ovl_sig_scan;
+}
+
+void spu_overlay_register_source(uint32_t content_ea, int image_id)
+{
+    if (s_ovl_src_count < SPU_OVL_SRC_MAX) {
+        spu_ovl_ea_add(content_ea);
+        s_ovl_src[s_ovl_src_count].src_ea = content_ea;
+        s_ovl_src[s_ovl_src_count].image_id = image_id;
+        s_ovl_src[s_ovl_src_count].has_sig = 0;
+        spu_ovl_idx_add(2, content_ea, s_ovl_src_count);
+        __atomic_store_n(&s_ovl_src_count, s_ovl_src_count + 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
+    }
+}
+
+/* Register a bounded code image that may coexist with other streamed images.
+ * Its functions must be translated at the local-store addresses used by the title. */
+void spu_overlay_register_region(uint32_t content_ea, uint32_t span, int image_id)
+{
+    if (!span || span > SPU_LS_SIZE || s_ovl_src_count >= SPU_OVL_SRC_MAX) return;
+    spu_overlay_register_source(content_ea, image_id);
+    s_ovl_src[s_ovl_src_count - 1].span = span;
+}
+
+/* Residency proves which load happened, not what the bytes are: the source EA
+ * could hold different content than was lifted. Compare the lifted segments
+ * once per load, at the first dispatch into the span, instead of at every
+ * transfer. Any later GET into the span resets the slot to pending (contiguous
+ * continuation) or clears it (anything else), see spu_overlay_note_get. */
+enum { SPU_OVERLAY_PENDING = 1, SPU_OVERLAY_VERIFIED, SPU_OVERLAY_REJECTED };
+#define SPU_OVERLAY_CODE_SEGMENTS 8u
+int spu_overlay_register_verified_region(uint32_t content_ea, uint32_t load_lsa,
+    uint32_t span, int image_id, const spu_overlay_code_segment* code, unsigned count)
+{
+    if (!span || load_lsa >= SPU_LS_SIZE || span > SPU_LS_SIZE - load_lsa || image_id <= 0 ||
+        !code || !count || count > SPU_OVERLAY_CODE_SEGMENTS || s_ovl_src_count >= SPU_OVL_SRC_MAX)
+        return 0;
+    size_t total = 0;
+    for (unsigned i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
+        const spu_overlay_code_segment* c = &code[i];
+        if (!c->bytes || !c->size || c->lsa < load_lsa || c->size > span ||
+            c->lsa - load_lsa > span - c->size) return 0;
+        total += c->size;
+    }
+    spu_overlay_code_segment* copy = (spu_overlay_code_segment*)malloc(count * sizeof *copy + total);
+    if (!copy) return 0;
+    uint8_t* bytes = (uint8_t*)(copy + count);
+    for (unsigned i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
+        copy[i] = code[i];
+        memcpy(bytes, code[i].bytes, code[i].size);
+        copy[i].bytes = bytes;
+        bytes += code[i].size;
+    }
+    spu_overlay_register_region(content_ea, span, image_id);
+    spu_ovl_src* o = &s_ovl_src[s_ovl_src_count - 1];
+    o->load_lsa = load_lsa; o->code = copy; o->code_count = count;
+    return 1;
+}
+
+static int spu_overlay_resident_verified(spu_context* ctx, unsigned slot)
+{
+    int* state = &ctx->resident_code[slot].verify_state;
+    if (*state == SPU_OVERLAY_PENDING) {
+        const spu_ovl_src* o = &s_ovl_src[ctx->resident_code[slot].source_index];
+        int match = 1;
+        for (unsigned i = 0; match && i < o->code_count; ++i)
+            match = !memcmp(ctx->ls + o->code[i].lsa, o->code[i].bytes, o->code[i].size);
+        *state = match ? SPU_OVERLAY_VERIFIED : SPU_OVERLAY_REJECTED;
+        spu_dcache_residency_changed(ctx);   /* the verify state is part of the signature */
+    }
+    return *state == SPU_OVERLAY_VERIFIED;
+}
+
+/* Register one-way runtime entries that replace the guest call stack.
+ * Matching the resolved function, not just its LS address, avoids affecting
+ * unrelated overlays using the same address. Entries have one registration
+ * writer and are immutable after publication. */
+static struct { uint32_t entry; int image_id; } s_stack_reset[16];
+unsigned g_spu_stack_reset_count;
+/* Nonzero at (entry >> 2) & 1023 of every registered entry, so SPU_DIRECT
+ * (spu_context.h) can tell with one load that a transfer needs the drain's
+ * stack-reset check. Collisions only cost a trampoline step. */
+uint8_t g_spu_stack_reset_hint[1024];
+void spu_register_stack_reset_entry(uint32_t entry, int image_id)
+{
+    /* Registrations have one writer; publish a complete new slot before a
+     * reader observes its count, including registration during a live run.
+     * The hint byte is written before that release store for the same reason:
+     * a reader that sees the new count must also see the hint. */
+    unsigned n = __atomic_load_n(&g_spu_stack_reset_count, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
+    if (n < 16) {
+        s_stack_reset[n].entry = entry & SPU_LS_MASK;
+        s_stack_reset[n].image_id = image_id;
+        g_spu_stack_reset_hint[((entry & SPU_LS_MASK) >> 2) & 1023u] = 1;
+        __atomic_store_n(&g_spu_stack_reset_count, n + 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
+    }
+}
+
+#if defined(_MSC_VER)
+static __declspec(noinline) void spu_check_stack_reset_scan(spu_context*, void (*)(spu_context*));
+#else
+static __attribute__((noinline, cold)) void spu_check_stack_reset_scan(spu_context*, void (*)(spu_context*));
+#endif
+/* Also called before direct trampoline transfers: generated calls can enter
+ * a stack-switching routine without going through spu_indirect_branch. */
+void spu_check_stack_reset(spu_context* ctx, void (*fn)(spu_context*))
+{
+    /* Runs on every drain transfer: test the registry before the
+     * thread-local halt state, which is a function call on Darwin, and keep
+     * the scan out of line so the common return needs no frame. */
+    if (!spu_stack_reset_needed(ctx)) return;
+    spu_check_stack_reset_scan(ctx, fn);
+}
+
+static void spu_check_stack_reset_scan(spu_context* ctx, void (*fn)(spu_context*))
+{
+    if (!s_spu_halt_armed) return;
+    const unsigned count = __atomic_load_n(&g_spu_stack_reset_count, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
+    for (unsigned i = 0; i < count; ++i)
+        if (ctx->pc == s_stack_reset[i].entry &&
+            fn == spu_lookup(ctx->pc, s_stack_reset[i].image_id)) {
+            g_spu_trampoline_fn = 0;
+            SPU_LONGJMP(s_spu_halt_env, 2);
+        }
+}
+
+/* SPURS taskset TASK entries (see spu_context.resident_task). A taskset can hold
+ * several tasks whose lifts share the SAME LS base -- the co-resident task-code
+ * region -- so no LS address identifies which task owns it. The title registers
+ * each task's ELF ENTRY point with the image id its functions were registered
+ * under; spu_indirect_branch adopts that image the moment the policy branches
+ * into the entry from outside the region. This is what lets each such task be
+ * registered under its own real image id instead of the id-0 wildcard, so a
+ * dormant co-resident task can no longer shadow the one the policy launched. */
+#define SPU_TASK_ENTRY_MAX 16
+static struct { uint32_t entry; int image_id; } s_task_entry[SPU_TASK_ENTRY_MAX];
+static int s_task_entry_count = 0;
+void spu_taskset_register_task_entry(uint32_t entry, int image_id)
+{
+    if (s_task_entry_count < SPU_TASK_ENTRY_MAX) {
+        s_task_entry[s_task_entry_count].entry = entry & SPU_LS_MASK;
+        s_task_entry[s_task_entry_count].image_id = image_id;
+        s_task_entry_count++;
+    }
+}
+static int spu_taskset_task_image(uint32_t entry)
+{
+    for (int i = 0; i < s_task_entry_count; i++)
+        if (s_task_entry[i].entry == entry) return s_task_entry[i].image_id;
+    return 0;
+}
+/* Resume PCs and even fresh entry PCs overlap between task ELFs. The
+ * taskset policy's TaskInfo identifies which ELF it has actually loaded. */
+static struct { uint32_t elf_ea; int image_id, policy_image_id; }
+    s_task_elf[SPU_TASK_ENTRY_MAX];
+static int s_task_elf_count;
+void spu_taskset_register_task_elf(uint32_t elf_ea, int image_id, int policy_image_id)
+{
+    if (s_task_elf_count < SPU_TASK_ENTRY_MAX) {
+        s_task_elf[s_task_elf_count].elf_ea = elf_ea & ~7u;
+        s_task_elf[s_task_elf_count].image_id = image_id;
+        s_task_elf[s_task_elf_count++].policy_image_id = policy_image_id;
+    }
+}
+static int spu_taskset_resident_image(const spu_context* ctx)
+{
+    const uint8_t* p = ctx->ls + 0x2794; /* SpursTasksetContext.taskInfo.elf */
+    uint32_t elf = (((uint32_t)p[0] << 24) | ((uint32_t)p[1] << 16) |
+                    ((uint32_t)p[2] << 8) | p[3]) & ~7u;
+    for (int i = 0; i < s_task_elf_count; ++i)
+        if (s_task_elf[i].elf_ea == elf &&
+            s_task_elf[i].policy_image_id == ctx->resident_ovl)
+            return s_task_elf[i].image_id;
+    return 0;
+}
+/* Lowest LS address of the shared task-code region: the taskset tasks all lift
+ * at LS 0x3000 (below it is the SPURS kernel/policy/context, 0x290..0x2FFF). */
+#define SPU_TASKSET_TASK_LO 0x3000u
+
+/* Content-signature variant: FMOD COPIES codec overlays to the heap before
+ * streaming them into the swap slot, so the source EA is unknowable ahead of
+ * time -- match the first 16 bytes of the streamed content instead. */
+void spu_overlay_register_sig(const uint8_t sig[16], int image_id)
+{
+    if (s_ovl_src_count < SPU_OVL_SRC_MAX) {
+        s_ovl_src[s_ovl_src_count].src_ea = 0;
+        s_ovl_src[s_ovl_src_count].image_id = image_id;
+        memcpy(s_ovl_src[s_ovl_src_count].sig, sig, 16);
+        s_ovl_src[s_ovl_src_count].has_sig = 1;
+        spu_ovl_idx_add(1, spu_ovl_sig_key(sig), s_ovl_src_count);
+        __atomic_store_n(&s_ovl_src_count, s_ovl_src_count + 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
+    }
+}
+
+/* Called from the MFC GET path after the copy: ls points at the JUST-COPIED
+ * bytes. EA match first (exact, cheap), then content signature for sizeable
+ * chunks (overlay bodies are >= 0x500 bytes). */
+/* SPU_DUMP_OVL=<dir>[,<lsa>]: write out every distinct code body streamed into
+ * LS <lsa> (default 0x5000, the job code buffer), so job bodies the title
+ * keeps in its own data can be lifted. A body larger than one DMA arrives as
+ * consecutive GETs (contiguous EA and LS); those are appended to the same
+ * file. One file per source EA: ovl_<ea>.bin. */
+static void spu_ovl_dump(spu_context* ctx, uint32_t ea, uint32_t lsa, const uint8_t* ls, uint32_t size)
+{
+    static int s_on = -1; static char s_dir[400]; static uint32_t s_lsa = 0x5000;
+    if (s_on < 0) { const char* e = getenv("SPU_DUMP_OVL"); s_on = e && *e;
+        if (s_on) { snprintf(s_dir, sizeof s_dir, "%s", e);
+                    char* c = strchr(s_dir, ','); if (c) { *c = 0; s_lsa = (uint32_t)strtoul(c + 1, 0, 0); } } }
+    if (!s_on) return;
+    static uint32_t s_seen[256]; static unsigned s_n;
+    static SPU_TLS uint32_t t_src, t_next_ea, t_next_lsa;
+    FILE* f = NULL; char path[512];
+    if (lsa == s_lsa && size >= 256) {
+        for (unsigned i = 0; i < s_n; i++) if (s_seen[i] == ea) { t_src = 0; return; }
+        if (s_n < 256) s_seen[s_n++] = ea;
+        t_src = ea;
+        snprintf(path, sizeof path, "%s/ovl_%08X.bin", s_dir, ea);
+        f = fopen(path, "wb");
+        fprintf(stderr, "[spu-ovl-dump] img=%d body ea=0x%08X size=%u -> %s\n", ctx->image_id, ea, size, path);
+    } else if (t_src && ea == t_next_ea && lsa == t_next_lsa) {
+        snprintf(path, sizeof path, "%s/ovl_%08X.bin", s_dir, t_src);
+        f = fopen(path, "ab");
+    } else { t_src = 0; return; }
+    if (f) { fwrite(ls, 1, size, f); fclose(f); }
+    t_next_ea = ea + size; t_next_lsa = lsa + size;
+}
+
+/* SPU_GET_LOG=<dir>,<lsa lo>,<lsa hi>: write each distinct GET of 256 bytes or more
+ * that lands in that LS window to <dir>/get_<ea>_<lsa>_<size>.bin and log it. Finds the
+ * job bodies a policy module streams in, and the addresses they run at. */
+static void spu_get_log(spu_context* ctx, uint32_t ea, uint32_t lsa, const uint8_t* ls, uint32_t size)
+{
+    static int s_on = -1; static char s_dir[400]; static uint32_t s_lo, s_hi;
+    if (s_on < 0) {
+        const char* e = getenv("SPU_GET_LOG"); s_on = 0;
+        if (e && *e) {
+            snprintf(s_dir, sizeof s_dir, "%s", e);
+            char* c = strchr(s_dir, ',');
+            if (c) { *c = 0; s_lo = (uint32_t)strtoul(c + 1, &c, 0); if (*c == ',') s_hi = (uint32_t)strtoul(c + 1, 0, 0); }
+            s_on = s_hi > s_lo;
+        }
+    }
+    if (!s_on || size < 256 || lsa < s_lo || lsa >= s_hi) return;
+    enum { N = 1024 };
+    static uint32_t s_ea[N], s_lsa[N], s_sz[N]; static long s_n;
+    long n = __atomic_load_n(&s_n, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
+    for (long i = 0; i < n && i < N; i++)
+        if (s_ea[i] == ea && s_lsa[i] == lsa && s_sz[i] == size) return;
+    n = __atomic_fetch_add(&s_n, 1, __ATOMIC_ACQ_REL);
+    if (n >= N) return;
+    s_ea[n] = ea; s_lsa[n] = lsa; s_sz[n] = size;
+    char path[512];
+    snprintf(path, sizeof path, "%s/get_%08X_%05X_%u.bin", s_dir, ea, lsa, size);
+    FILE* f = fopen(path, "wb");
+    if (f) { fwrite(ls, 1, size, f); fclose(f); }
+    fprintf(stderr, "[spu-get] img=%d pc=0x%05X ea=0x%08X -> LS 0x%05X size=%u first %02X%02X%02X%02X\n",
+            ctx->image_id, (uint32_t)ctx->pc & SPU_LS_MASK, ea, lsa, size, ls[0], ls[1], ls[2], ls[3]);
+}
+
+/* SPU_LOCKGUARD=<hex ea>: the word at that EA is a ticket lock (serving,next
+ * halfwords). Log any SPU write that moves either halfword by anything other
+ * than 0 or +1 -- a stale whole-line store rolling the lock back. `src` is the
+ * new bytes for [ea, ea+size). */
+void spu_lockguard_check(spu_context* ctx, uint32_t ea, const uint8_t* src, uint32_t size, const char* what)
+{
+    static int64_t s_g = -2;
+    if (s_g == -2) { const char* e = getenv("SPU_LOCKGUARD"); s_g = e ? (int64_t)strtoul(e, 0, 16) : -1; }
+    if (s_g < 0 || !vm_base) return;
+    uint32_t g = (uint32_t)s_g;
+    if (g < ea || g + 4 > ea + size) return;
+    const uint8_t* o = vm_base + g; const uint8_t* n = src + (g - ea);
+    unsigned os = (o[0] << 8) | o[1], on = (o[2] << 8) | o[3];
+    unsigned ns = (n[0] << 8) | n[1], nn = (n[2] << 8) | n[3];
+    int bad = !(ns == os || ns == ((os + 1) & 0xFFFF)) || !(nn == on || nn == ((on + 1) & 0xFFFF));
+    if (bad) { static int c; if (PS3_LOG_FIRST(c, 32))
+        fprintf(stderr, "[lockguard] %s img=%d pc=0x%05X ea=0x%08X size=%u: %04X/%04X -> %04X/%04X\n",
+                what, ctx ? ctx->image_id : -1, ctx ? (unsigned)(ctx->pc & SPU_LS_MASK) : 0u,
+                ea, size, os, on, ns, nn); }
+}
+
+void spu_overlay_note_get(spu_context* ctx, uint32_t ea, const uint8_t* ls, uint32_t size)
+{
+    if (__builtin_expect(g_spu_get_hook != 0, 0)) g_spu_get_hook(size);
+    uint32_t lsa = (uint32_t)(ls - ctx->ls);
+    spu_ovl_dump(ctx, ea, lsa, ls, size);
+    spu_get_log(ctx, ea, lsa, ls, size);
+    for (unsigned slot = 0; slot < 4; ++slot) {
+        if (!ctx->resident_code[slot].image_id) continue;
+        uint32_t base = ctx->resident_code[slot].lsa;
+        uint32_t end = base + ctx->resident_code[slot].size;
+        if (lsa < end && lsa + size > base) {
+            if (lsa < base || ea != ctx->resident_code[slot].source_ea + (lsa - base)) {
+                ctx->resident_code[slot].image_id = 0;
+                spu_dcache_residency_changed(ctx);
+            } else if (ctx->resident_code[slot].verify_state) {
+                ctx->resident_code[slot].verify_state = SPU_OVERLAY_PENDING;
+                spu_dcache_residency_changed(ctx);
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    int nsrc = __atomic_load_n(&s_ovl_src_count, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
+    if (size < 512 && !spu_ovl_ea_known(ea)) return;
+    int cand[SPU_OVL_SRC_MAX], ncand = 0;
+    const int scan = spu_ovl_sig_scan();
+    if (!scan) {
+        if (size >= 512) spu_ovl_idx_find(1, spu_ovl_sig_key(ls), nsrc, cand, &ncand);
+        if (spu_ovl_ea_known(ea)) spu_ovl_idx_find(2, ea, nsrc, cand, &ncand);   /* merged in source order */
+    }
+    for (int c = 0; c < (scan ? nsrc : ncand); c++) {
+        const int i = scan ? c : cand[c];
+        const spu_ovl_src* o = &s_ovl_src[i];
+        int hit = o->has_sig ? (size >= 512 && memcmp(ls, o->sig, 16) == 0)
+                             : (o->src_ea == ea);
+        if (hit) {
+            if (o->span) {
+                if (lsa + o->span > SPU_LS_SIZE) return;
+                /* Verified code was lifted for one load address. */
+                if (o->code && lsa != o->load_lsa) continue;
+                for (unsigned slot = 0; slot < 4; ++slot) {
+                    if (ctx->resident_code[slot].image_id && ctx->resident_code[slot].lsa != lsa)
+                        continue;
+                    ctx->resident_code[slot].lsa = lsa;
+                    ctx->resident_code[slot].size = o->span;
+                    ctx->resident_code[slot].source_ea = ea;
+                    ctx->resident_code[slot].image_id = o->image_id;
+                    ctx->resident_code[slot].verify_state = o->code ? SPU_OVERLAY_PENDING : 0;
+                    ctx->resident_code[slot].source_index = i;
+                    spu_dcache_residency_changed(ctx);
+                    return;
+                }
+                fprintf(stderr, "[spu-ovl] no free resident code span for image %d\n", o->image_id);
+                return;
+            }
+            if (ctx->resident_ovl != o->image_id) {
+                ctx->resident_ovl = o->image_id;
+                { static int _n = 0; if (PS3_LOG_FIRST(_n, 32))
+                    fprintf(stderr, "[spu-ovl] img=%d streamed overlay src=0x%08X "
+                            "-> LS 0x%05X size=%u -> resident ovl image %d%s\n",
+                            ctx->image_id, ea, (uint32_t)(ls - ctx->ls), size,
+                            ctx->resident_ovl, o->has_sig ? " (sig match)" : ""); }
+            }
+            return;
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+/* Match a 16-byte module header against the registered content signatures.
+ * Returns the overlay image id, or 0 if none. Used by the WWS job-code dispatch
+ * path: the job manager streams a module into the code buffer via a DMA LIST
+ * (per-element GETs the single-transfer note_get hook doesn't see as one >=512
+ * chunk), so resident_ovl is set at branch-in time by matching the buffer head. */
+int spu_overlay_match_sig(const uint8_t hdr[16])
+{
+    const int nsrc = __atomic_load_n(&s_ovl_src_count, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
+    if (!spu_ovl_sig_scan()) {   /* the first signature source in order that matches, through the index */
+        int cand[SPU_OVL_SRC_MAX], ncand = 0;
+        spu_ovl_idx_find(1, spu_ovl_sig_key(hdr), nsrc, cand, &ncand);
+        for (int c = 0; c < ncand; c++)
+            if (memcmp(hdr, s_ovl_src[cand[c]].sig, 16) == 0) return s_ovl_src[cand[c]].image_id;
+        return 0;
+    }
+    for (int i = 0; i < nsrc; i++) {
+        const spu_ovl_src* o = &s_ovl_src[i];
+        if (o->has_sig && memcmp(hdr, o->sig, 16) == 0)
+            return o->image_id;
+    }
+    return 0;
+}
+
+/* HLE of the taskset Policy Module's task-syscall entry (LS 0xA70). A SPURS task
+ * (e.g. the cri_mpv task, image 22) reads syscallAddr from its SpursTasksetContext
+ * (LS 0x27C4) and branches to it to perform a task syscall (EXIT/YIELD/WAIT/POLL).
+ * The real kernel has the PM code resident at 0xA70; we don't, so we plant 0xA70 as
+ * syscallAddr (in the cri dispatch) and INTERCEPT a branch to it here to HLE the
+ * syscall. num = r3&0xF (0x10 bit = the "2" variant), args in r4. Adopted from the
+ * JonathanDC64/ps3recomp fork (aaea4158) which uses this to run SPURS tasks clean. */
+/* Write the event bits a PPU-side Set owed this wait object into guest memory,
+ * at object+0x00 (events) and every object+0x30 slot (pendingRecv).
+ *
+ * Called from the WAIT_SIGNAL handler immediately before control returns to the
+ * guest. Doing it at Set time loses a race: the guest reads object+0x30 the
+ * instant it resumes, and a task that took the latched-wake path was never
+ * parked for the Set to target. Here the guest demonstrably has not read yet.
+ *
+ * ponytail: fills all 16 slots rather than the one the guest picked -- the slot
+ * index is derived from state we do not model, and a wrong slot delivers
+ * nothing. Narrow it if a title ever cares which slot fired. */
+static void spu_ef_deliver_owed(spu_context* ctx, uint32_t wobj)
+{
+    (void)ctx;
+    static int s_od = -1;
+    if (s_od < 0) s_od = getenv("SPURS_EF_OBJ_DELIVER") ? 1 : 0;
+    if (!s_od || !wobj || !vm_base) return;
+    extern uint16_t spu_ef_bits_take(uint32_t);
+    uint16_t bits = spu_ef_bits_take(wobj);
+    if (!bits) return;
+    uint8_t* m = vm_base + wobj;
+    m[0] = (uint8_t)(bits >> 8); m[1] = (uint8_t)bits;          /* +0x00 events */
+    for (uint32_t s = 0; s < 16; s++) {                          /* +0x30 slots */
+        m[0x30 + 2*s]     = (uint8_t)(bits >> 8);
+        m[0x30 + 2*s + 1] = (uint8_t)bits;
+    }
+    { static int _n = 0; if (PS3_LOG_FIRST(_n, 8))
+        fprintf(stderr, "[spu] delivered owed bits=0x%04X to object 0x%08X \n",
+                (unsigned)bits, wobj); }
+}
+
+void spu_spurs_taskset_syscall(spu_context* ctx)   /* non-static: also called by the pure interpreter (spu_interp.c) */
+{
+    uint32_t raw = ctx->gpr[3]._u32[0];
+    uint32_t num = raw & 0x0F;
+    /* SPU_SYSCALL_IMG=<n>: every syscall of image n, uncapped (the 24-line
+     * budget is spent by FMOD's WAIT_SIGNAL loop long before a later task). */
+    static int s_si = -2;
+    if (s_si == -2) { const char* e = getenv("SPU_SYSCALL_IMG"); s_si = e ? atoi(e) : -1; }
+    { static int _n = 0; if (PS3_LOG_FIRST(_n, 24) || ctx->image_id == s_si)
+        fprintf(stderr, "[spu] SPURS taskset syscall num=%u (raw=0x%X args=0x%08X) image=%d link/r0=0x%05X wobj@2FDC=0x%02X%02X%02X%02X\n",
+                num, raw, ctx->gpr[4]._u32[0], ctx->image_id, ctx->gpr[0]._u32[0] & SPU_LS_MASK,
+                ctx->ls[0x2FDC], ctx->ls[0x2FDD], ctx->ls[0x2FDE], ctx->ls[0x2FDF]); }
+    /* The task-API argument is passed in LOCAL STORE at 0x2FD0, not in r4: the
+     * caller does shufb(arg,...) -> stqd 0x2FD0 and only then sets r3 = number
+     * (see func_00026DE0 / func_000272AC in image 22). Logging r4 shows caller
+     * leftovers and hides what the task actually asked for. */
+    { static int s_sa = -1; if (s_sa < 0) s_sa = getenv("YDKJ_SYSCALL_ARG") ? 1 : 0;
+      if (s_sa) { static int _n = 0; if (PS3_LOG_FIRST(_n, 40)) {
+        const uint8_t* a = &ctx->ls[0x2FD0];
+        fprintf(stderr, "[spu] syscall num=%u LS[0x2FD0]=%02X%02X%02X%02X %02X%02X%02X%02X"
+                        " %02X%02X%02X%02X %02X%02X%02X%02X img=%d\n",
+                num, a[0],a[1],a[2],a[3], a[4],a[5],a[6],a[7],
+                a[8],a[9],a[10],a[11], a[12],a[13],a[14],a[15], ctx->image_id);
+        fflush(stderr); } } }
+    /* NOTE (YDKJ cri_mpv): the cri task's BOOTSTRAP (func_00003040) calls the
+     * task-API syscall and EXPECTS IT TO RETURN, then branches to the real task
+     * entry (0x3050). Halting on num=0 here kills the task at bootstrap before it
+     * runs. So for image 22 we DON'T halt on num=0 -- we return so the bootstrap
+     * continues to the decode entry. (A genuine end-of-task EXIT would re-enter and
+     * spin; if that happens, gate a real halt after the task has done work.)
+     * For non-cri images keep the fork's EXIT=halt semantics. Env YDKJ_CRI_EXIT_HALT
+     * forces the old halt behaviour for comparison. */
+    /* The cri bootstrap calls EXIT once and EXPECTS IT TO RETURN, then branches to
+     * the real task entry -- so image 22 cannot halt on the first one. But a task
+     * that has since done work and calls EXIT again means it: returning there makes
+     * it re-enter and spin (observed: 6x num=0 from link 0x26E18 once the task is
+     * woken). Honour the first call, halt on the rest. Each task runs on its own
+     * host thread, so a thread-local count is per task. */
+    static _Thread_local int s_exit_seen = 0;
+    if (num == 0 && ctx->image_id == 22 && !getenv("YDKJ_CRI_EXIT_HALT")) {
+        if (s_exit_seen++ == 0) { ctx->gpr[3]._u32[0] = 0; return; }   /* bootstrap */
+        { static int _n = 0; if (PS3_LOG_FIRST(_n, 8))
+            fprintf(stderr, "[spu] cri task EXIT #%d -- halting (was spinning)\n",
+                    s_exit_seen); }
+        ctx->status = SPU_STATUS_STOPPED_BY_STOP;
+        spu_halt(ctx);
+        return;
+    }
+    if (num == 0 && (ctx->image_id != 22 || getenv("YDKJ_CRI_EXIT_HALT"))) {
+        ctx->status = SPU_STATUS_STOPPED_BY_STOP;
+        spu_halt(ctx);          /* longjmp out to spu_run_with_halt; post-run writes exit code */
+        return;
+    }
+    /* WAIT_SIGNAL(2): REAL semantics (RPCS3 spursTasksetProcessSyscall) --
+     * consume the task's bit in the guest taskset's `signalled` bitset, or
+     * SLEEP this task's host thread until _cellSpursSendSignal /
+     * cellSpursEventFlagSet delivers one (the FMOD mixer's flag-A wait path:
+     * the task registers its wait slot in the flag struct with atomics, then
+     * syscalls WAIT_SIGNAL; the PPU-side Set satisfies the slot and signals).
+     * Returning "success" here without waiting made the task spin on empty
+     * work state forever -- the LBP boot deadlock. taskset/taskId come from
+     * the SpursTasksetContext this runtime planted at LS 0x2700. */
+    if (num == 2) {
+        uint32_t ts  = ((uint32_t)ctx->ls[0x27BC] << 24) | ((uint32_t)ctx->ls[0x27BD] << 16) |
+                       ((uint32_t)ctx->ls[0x27BE] << 8)  |  (uint32_t)ctx->ls[0x27BF];
+        uint32_t tid = ((uint32_t)ctx->ls[0x27D4] << 24) | ((uint32_t)ctx->ls[0x27D5] << 16) |
+                       ((uint32_t)ctx->ls[0x27D6] << 8)  |  (uint32_t)ctx->ls[0x27D7];
+        /* The guest names its wait OBJECT in the task-API argument at LS 0x2FD0
+         * (low nibble is flags). It reads its received event bits from
+         * object+0x30, so this is both who to wake and where to deliver. */
+        uint32_t wobj = (((uint32_t)ctx->ls[0x2FDC] << 24) |
+                         ((uint32_t)ctx->ls[0x2FDD] << 16) |
+                         ((uint32_t)ctx->ls[0x2FDE] << 8)  |
+                          (uint32_t)ctx->ls[0x2FDF]) & ~0xFu;
+        /* SPURS_EF_SPU_REPLY=1 -- DIAGNOSTIC BISECT, NOT A FIX.
+         *
+         * The guest task is supposed to set its SPU->PPU flag (object+0x100)
+         * when a work cycle completes; it never does, so the PPU blocks on that
+         * flag forever and can never enqueue the next unit of work. That is a
+         * cycle: we cannot see what the PPU would do next without breaking it.
+         *
+         * On RE-ENTRY to WAIT_SIGNAL for the same object the previous cycle has
+         * finished, so set the flag on the task`s behalf and watch where the PPU
+         * goes. This FABRICATES guest state -- the repo`s own history says faked
+         * success is the most expensive kind of bug (see the unresolved-NID note
+         * in ppu_hle.cpp), so it stays opt-in and must never become the default.
+         * If the PPU advances, the answer is what the task must do to earn it. */
+        { static int s_rp = -1;
+          if (s_rp < 0) { const char* e = getenv("SPURS_EF_SPU_REPLY");
+                          s_rp = e ? atoi(e) : 0; }   /* 2 = reply on EVERY entry */
+          if (s_rp && wobj) {
+              static uint32_t seen[8]; static int seen_n = 0;
+              int again = 0;
+              for (int i = 0; i < seen_n; i++) if (seen[i] == wobj) { again = 1; break; }
+              if (s_rp >= 2) again = 1;   /* force: answer "would the PPU move at all?" */
+              if (!again) { if (seen_n < 8) seen[seen_n++] = wobj; }
+              else {
+                  extern void spurs_ef_set_from_spu(uint32_t, uint16_t);
+                  spurs_ef_set_from_spu(wobj + 0x100u, 1);
+                  static int _n = 0;
+                  if (PS3_LOG_FIRST(_n, 8))
+                      fprintf(stderr, "[spu] SPU-REPLY: set flag 0x%08X for object "
+                                      "0x%08X (cycle complete)\n", wobj + 0x100u, wobj);
+              }
+          } }
+
+        if (ts) {
+            extern int spu_taskset_wait_signal(uint32_t, uint32_t);
+            /* Park = OS-level wait on this SPU's host thread. Under the lockstep
+             * gate the thread HOLDS the global run token here; parking without
+             * releasing it starves every other lifted SPU (observed: FMOD task 1
+             * parks in WAIT_SIGNAL holding the token -> the mixer never runs
+             * again -> the PPU audio pump blocks forever on flag 0x94F600). */
+            /* Publish that this task is parked so a PPU-side event-flag Set can
+             * reach it even though it registered no wait slot in the flag. */
+            extern void spu_taskset_parked_add(uint32_t, uint32_t, uint32_t);
+            extern void spu_taskset_parked_del(uint32_t, uint32_t);
+            extern int spu_taskset_consume_wake(uint32_t);
+            if (spu_taskset_consume_wake(ts)) {   /* a Set beat us to the park */
+                spu_ef_deliver_owed(ctx, wobj);
+                ctx->gpr[3]._u32[0] = 0;
+                return;
+            }
+            yz_lockstep_block_begin(ctx);
+            spu_taskset_parked_add(ts, tid, wobj);
+            spu_taskset_wait_signal(ts, tid);
+            spu_taskset_parked_del(ts, tid);
+            yz_lockstep_block_end(ctx);
+            spu_ef_deliver_owed(ctx, wobj);
+        }
+        ctx->gpr[3]._u32[0] = 0;
+        return;
+    }
+    /* EXIT(0, cri bootstrap)/YIELD(1)/POLL(3)/RECV_WKL_FLAG(4):
+     * report success and resume (return -> lifted caller continues at its link). */
+    ctx->gpr[3]._u32[0] = 0;
+}
+
+/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ * Micro-interpreter for RUNTIME-GENERATED stub code (SMC).
+ *
+ * The WWS jobmanager's interrupt handler GENERATES a register save/restore
+ * stub above the static image (LS 0x3FEC0: a chain of stqd/lqd plus a `bi`
+ * terminator, written at interrupt entry) and calls it. No lift can exist for
+ * bytes that only come into being at runtime, so when the indirect dispatch
+ * finds no registered function we interpret the LIVE LS bytes directly for
+ * the small instruction set such stubs use, and exit back into lifted code at
+ * the first branch (trampoline re-dispatch). Returns 1 if it executed to a
+ * branch, 0 on an unknown opcode (caller falls through to BRANCH-TO-0). */
+static SPU_TLS int t_spu_st_handoff;   /* set when the micro-interpreter hands to the full one */
+static int spu_smc_microstep(spu_context* ctx)
+{
+    uint32_t pc = ctx->pc & SPU_LS_MASK & ~3u;
+    /* Straight runs of quadword loads and stores (lqa/stqa/lqd/stqd) go through
+     * a tight loop: no decode chain, no per-access probe. The WWS handler's
+     * generated save and restore stubs are 76 of them and a `bi`, run on every
+     * stall-and-notify interrupt -- ~40k stubs a second on God of War:
+     * Ascension's serial EDGE chain, ~7% of its time at ~25 ns an instruction
+     * the generic way. Only while every LS diagnostic is off (they read 0 once
+     * the first access has read their switches); otherwise the generic path
+     * below runs them. */
+    const int ldst_fast = g_spu_ls_watch_n == 0 && g_spu_ls_probe == 0 &&
+                          g_spu_smc_watch == 0 && ctx->image_id != 2;
+    for (int steps = 0; steps < 4096; steps++) {
+        if (ldst_fast) {
+            for (; steps < 4096; steps++, pc = (pc + 4) & SPU_LS_MASK) {
+                uint32_t wf;
+                memcpy(&wf, ctx->ls + pc, 4);
+                wf = SPU_BSWAP32(wf);
+                const uint32_t op9f = wf >> 23, op8f = wf >> 24;
+                uint32_t a;
+                if (op9f == 0x041 || op9f == 0x061)                   /* stqa / lqa: LSA = I16 << 2 */
+                    a = ((wf >> 7) & 0xFFFF) << 2;
+                else if (op8f == 0x24 || op8f == 0x34)                /* stqd / lqd */
+                    a = ctx->gpr[(wf >> 7) & 0x7F]._u32[0] + ((uint32_t)((int32_t)(wf << 8) >> 22) << 4);
+                else
+                    break;
+                uint8_t* p = ctx->ls + (a & SPU_LS_MASK & ~15u);
+                u128* r = &ctx->gpr[wf & 0x7F];
+                if (op9f == 0x041 || op8f == 0x24) {
+                    const uint32_t q[4] = { SPU_BSWAP32(r->_u32[0]), SPU_BSWAP32(r->_u32[1]),
+                                            SPU_BSWAP32(r->_u32[2]), SPU_BSWAP32(r->_u32[3]) };
+                    memcpy(p, q, 16);
+                } else {
+                    uint32_t q[4];
+                    memcpy(q, p, 16);
+                    for (int k = 0; k < 4; k++) r->_u32[k] = SPU_BSWAP32(q[k]);
+                }
+            }
+            if (steps >= 4096) break;
+        }
+        uint32_t w = ((uint32_t)ctx->ls[pc] << 24) | ((uint32_t)ctx->ls[pc+1] << 16) |
+                     ((uint32_t)ctx->ls[pc+2] << 8) | ctx->ls[pc+3];
+        uint32_t op11 = w >> 21, op9 = w >> 23, op8 = w >> 24, op7 = w >> 25;
+        uint32_t rt = w & 0x7F, ra = (w >> 7) & 0x7F, rb = (w >> 14) & 0x7F;
+        int32_t  i10 = (int32_t)(w << 8) >> 22;               /* bits 14-23 sext */
+        int32_t  i16 = (int32_t)(int16_t)((w >> 7) & 0xFFFF);
+        (void)rb;
+
+        if (op11 == 0x1A8 || op11 == 0x1A9 || op11 == 0x1AA || op11 == 0x1AB) {
+            /* bi / bisl / iret / bisled (+E/D interrupt bits) */
+            if (op11 == 0x1AB &&                       /* bisled: only on event */
+                (ctx->event_status & ctx->event_mask) == 0) { pc += 4; continue; }
+            if (w & 0x40000) ctx->int_enable = 1;
+            else if (w & 0x80000) ctx->int_enable = 0;
+            uint32_t tgt = (op11 == 0x1AA) ? ctx->srr0
+                                           : ctx->gpr[ra]._u32[0];
+            if (op11 == 0x1A9 || op11 == 0x1AB)
+                ctx->gpr[rt] = spu_make_preferred_u32((pc + 4) & SPU_LS_MASK);   /* the link: word 0, the rest zero */
+            ctx->pc = tgt & SPU_LS_MASK & ~3u;
+            g_spu_trampoline_fn = spu_indirect_branch;
+            return 1;
+        }
+        if (op11 >= 0x128 && op11 <= 0x12B) {
+            /* biz / binz / bihz / bihnz rt,ra (+E/D bits, taken-only) */
+            uint32_t cv = ctx->gpr[rt]._u32[0];
+            int taken;
+            switch (op11) {
+            case 0x128: taken = (cv == 0); break;                     /* biz  */
