+/* DualSense and DualShock 4, read directly as HID: XInput can't see them without
+ * a translator in between. USB and Bluetooth reports both, analog sticks and triggers.
+ * The rumble goes back as an output report (ds_rumble_write); no lights or audio are
+ * sent. Like the keyboard it counts only while this process has the foreground, and
+ * an XInput pad on port 0 still wins. PAD_NO_DUALSENSE=1 turns it off. */
+#ifdef _WIN32
+typedef struct { DWORD cbSize; GUID guid; DWORD flags; ULONG_PTR reserved; } ds_iface_data;
+typedef struct { DWORD cbSize; WCHAR path[1]; } ds_iface_detail;
+typedef struct { ULONG size; USHORT vendor, product, version; } ds_hid_attrs;
+static PadHostState s_ds_state;
+static SRWLOCK s_ds_lock = SRWLOCK_INIT;
+static volatile LONG s_ds_live;
+/* The controller being read, for the rumble's own handle: its path, which one, how it is connected. */
+static WCHAR s_ds_path[512];
+static volatile LONG s_ds_gen;        /* goes up with each controller opened */
+static volatile LONG s_ds_dualsense;
+static volatile LONG s_ds_bt = -1;    /* 0 USB, 1 Bluetooth, -1 not known yet (from its first report) */
+
+static HANDLE ds_open(int* is_dualsense)
+{
+    static HMODULE hid, setup;
+    if (!hid) hid = LoadLibraryA("hid.dll");
+    if (!setup) setup = LoadLibraryA("setupapi.dll");
+    if (!hid || !setup) return INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE;
+    void (WINAPI *get_guid)(GUID*) = (void (WINAPI*)(GUID*))(void*)GetProcAddress(hid, "HidD_GetHidGuid");
+    BOOLEAN (WINAPI *get_attrs)(HANDLE, ds_hid_attrs*) = (BOOLEAN (WINAPI*)(HANDLE, ds_hid_attrs*))(void*)GetProcAddress(hid, "HidD_GetAttributes");
+    void* (WINAPI *get_devs)(const GUID*, const WCHAR*, HWND, DWORD) = (void* (WINAPI*)(const GUID*, const WCHAR*, HWND, DWORD))(void*)GetProcAddress(setup, "SetupDiGetClassDevsW");
+    BOOL (WINAPI *enum_ifaces)(void*, void*, const GUID*, DWORD, ds_iface_data*) = (BOOL (WINAPI*)(void*, void*, const GUID*, DWORD, ds_iface_data*))(void*)GetProcAddress(setup, "SetupDiEnumDeviceInterfaces");
+    BOOL (WINAPI *get_detail)(void*, ds_iface_data*, ds_iface_detail*, DWORD, DWORD*, void*) = (BOOL (WINAPI*)(void*, ds_iface_data*, ds_iface_detail*, DWORD, DWORD*, void*))(void*)GetProcAddress(setup, "SetupDiGetDeviceInterfaceDetailW");
+    BOOL (WINAPI *destroy)(void*) = (BOOL (WINAPI*)(void*))(void*)GetProcAddress(setup, "SetupDiDestroyDeviceInfoList");
+    if (!get_guid || !get_attrs || !get_devs || !enum_ifaces || !get_detail || !destroy) return INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE;
+    GUID guid;
+    get_guid(&guid);
+    void* devs = get_devs(&guid, NULL, NULL, 0x12 /* DIGCF_PRESENT | DIGCF_DEVICEINTERFACE */);
+    if (devs == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) return INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE;
+    HANDLE found = INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE;
+    ds_iface_data id;
+    id.cbSize = sizeof id;
+    for (DWORD i = 0; found == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE && enum_ifaces(devs, NULL, &guid, i, &id); i++) {
+        union { ds_iface_detail d; char raw[1024]; } u;
+        u.d.cbSize = 8;   /* sizeof(SP_DEVICE_INTERFACE_DETAIL_DATA_W) on x64 */
+        if (!get_detail(devs, &id, &u.d, sizeof u, NULL, NULL)) continue;
+        HANDLE h = CreateFileW(u.d.path, GENERIC_READ, FILE_SHARE_READ | FILE_SHARE_WRITE, NULL, OPEN_EXISTING, 0, NULL);
+        if (h == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) continue;
+        ds_hid_attrs a;
+        a.size = sizeof a;
+        const int sony = get_attrs(h, &a) && a.vendor == 0x054C;
+        if (sony && (a.product == 0x0CE6 || a.product == 0x0DF2)) { *is_dualsense = 1; found = h; }
+        else if (sony && (a.product == 0x05C4 || a.product == 0x09CC)) { *is_dualsense = 0; found = h; }
+        else CloseHandle(h);
+        if (found != INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) {
+            AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&s_ds_lock);
+            wcsncpy(s_ds_path, u.d.path, sizeof s_ds_path / sizeof s_ds_path[0] - 1);
+            s_ds_path[sizeof s_ds_path / sizeof s_ds_path[0] - 1] = 0;
+            ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&s_ds_lock);
+            InterlockedExchange(&s_ds_dualsense, *is_dualsense);
+            InterlockedExchange(&s_ds_bt, -1);
+            InterlockedIncrement(&s_ds_gen);
+        }
+    }
+    destroy(devs);
+    return found;
+}
+
+static void ds_parse(const u8* b, DWORD n, int dualsense)
+{
+    /* Where the sticks and buttons sit in this report. */
+    u32 st, tr, bt;
+    /* Windows hands back every report at the device's longest length: 64 bytes on USB, 78 on Bluetooth.
+     * A Bluetooth pad nobody has switched to full reports (Steam does) sends the simple 0x01 at 78, and
+     * taken for USB its triggers read as buttons and its face buttons as trigger pressure. */
+    if (dualsense && b[0] == 0x01 && n >= 11 + 40 && n <= 64) { st = 1; tr = 5; bt = 8; }   /* USB */
+    else if (dualsense && b[0] == 0x31 && n >= 12) { st = 2; tr = 6; bt = 9; }          /* Bluetooth, full */
+    else if (b[0] == 0x01 && n >= 10) { st = 1; tr = 8; bt = 5; }                       /* DS4 USB, Bluetooth simple */
+    else if (!dualsense && b[0] == 0x11 && n >= 12) { st = 3; tr = 10; bt = 7; }        /* DS4 Bluetooth, full */
+    else return;
+    const u8 b0 = b[bt], b1 = b[bt + 1];
+    u16 btns = 0;
+    static const u16 hat[8] = {
+        CELL_PAD_CTRL_UP, CELL_PAD_CTRL_UP | CELL_PAD_CTRL_RIGHT, CELL_PAD_CTRL_RIGHT,
+        CELL_PAD_CTRL_DOWN | CELL_PAD_CTRL_RIGHT, CELL_PAD_CTRL_DOWN, CELL_PAD_CTRL_DOWN | CELL_PAD_CTRL_LEFT,
+        CELL_PAD_CTRL_LEFT, CELL_PAD_CTRL_UP | CELL_PAD_CTRL_LEFT };
+    if ((b0 & 0xF) < 8) btns |= hat[b0 & 0xF];
+    if (b0 & 0x10) btns |= CELL_PAD_CTRL_SQUARE;
+    if (b0 & 0x20) btns |= CELL_PAD_CTRL_CROSS;
+    if (b0 & 0x40) btns |= CELL_PAD_CTRL_CIRCLE;
+    if (b0 & 0x80) btns |= CELL_PAD_CTRL_TRIANGLE;
+    if (b1 & 0x01) btns |= CELL_PAD_CTRL_L1;
+    if (b1 & 0x02) btns |= CELL_PAD_CTRL_R1;
+    if (b1 & 0x04) btns |= CELL_PAD_CTRL_L2;
+    if (b1 & 0x08) btns |= CELL_PAD_CTRL_R2;
+    if (b1 & 0x10) btns |= CELL_PAD_CTRL_SELECT;
+    if (b1 & 0x20) btns |= CELL_PAD_CTRL_START;
+    if (b1 & 0x40) btns |= CELL_PAD_CTRL_L3;
+    if (b1 & 0x80) btns |= CELL_PAD_CTRL_R3;
+    PadHostState st_new;
+    memset(&st_new, 0, sizeof st_new);
+    st_new.connected = 1;
+    st_new.buttons = btns;
+    {   /* the round dead zone, as every controller's (PAD_STICK_DEADZONE) */
+        const float dz = pad_stick_dz_new();
+        pad_stick(pad_u8_axis(b[st]), pad_u8_axis(b[st + 1]), dz, &st_new.analog_lx, &st_new.analog_ly);
+        pad_stick(pad_u8_axis(b[st + 2]), pad_u8_axis(b[st + 3]), dz, &st_new.analog_rx, &st_new.analog_ry);
+    }
+    st_new.trigger_l2 = b[tr]; st_new.trigger_r2 = b[tr + 1];
+    st_new.press_up       = (btns & CELL_PAD_CTRL_UP)       ? 255 : 0;
+    st_new.press_down     = (btns & CELL_PAD_CTRL_DOWN)     ? 255 : 0;
+    st_new.press_left     = (btns & CELL_PAD_CTRL_LEFT)     ? 255 : 0;
+    st_new.press_right    = (btns & CELL_PAD_CTRL_RIGHT)    ? 255 : 0;
+    st_new.press_triangle = (btns & CELL_PAD_CTRL_TRIANGLE) ? 255 : 0;
+    st_new.press_circle   = (btns & CELL_PAD_CTRL_CIRCLE)   ? 255 : 0;
+    st_new.press_cross    = (btns & CELL_PAD_CTRL_CROSS)    ? 255 : 0;
+    st_new.press_square   = (btns & CELL_PAD_CTRL_SQUARE)   ? 255 : 0;
+    st_new.press_l1       = (btns & CELL_PAD_CTRL_L1)       ? 255 : 0;
+    st_new.press_r1       = (btns & CELL_PAD_CTRL_R1)       ? 255 : 0;
+    AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&s_ds_lock);
+    s_ds_state = st_new;
+    ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&s_ds_lock);
+}
+
+static DWORD WINAPI ds_thread(LPVOID unused)
+{
+    (void)unused;
+    for (;;) {
+        int dualsense = 0;
+        HANDLE h = ds_open(&dualsense);
+        if (h == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) { Sleep(3000); continue; }
+        printf("[cellPad] %s found: reading it directly\n", dualsense ? "DualSense" : "DualShock 4");
+        fflush(stdout);
+        u8 buf[128];
+        DWORD n;
+        while (ReadFile(h, buf, sizeof buf, &n, NULL)) {
+            if (s_ds_bt < 0) InterlockedExchange(&s_ds_bt, n > 64 ? 1 : 0);   /* USB reports are 64 bytes */
+            ds_parse(buf, n, dualsense);
+            InterlockedExchange(&s_ds_live, 1);
+        }
+        InterlockedExchange(&s_ds_live, 0);
+        CloseHandle(h);
+    }
+    return 0;
+}
+
+/* The rumble of a DualSense / DualShock 4 read directly: an output report on a handle of its own.
+ *   DualShock 4, USB:       report 0x05, 32 bytes: [1] what to set (1 = the motors), [4] the right
+ *                           (small, fast) motor, [5] the left (large) one.
+ *   DualShock 4, Bluetooth: report 0x11, 78 bytes: [1] 0xC4 (HID, with a CRC; 4 ms), [3] what to set,
+ *                           [6] right, [7] left, [74-77] the CRC-32 of 0xA2 and bytes 0-73, low first.
+ *   DualSense, USB:         report 0x02, 48 bytes: [1] 0x03 (the motors as a DualShock 4's, haptics
+ *                           off), [3] right, [4] left.
+ * As Sony's own Linux driver (hid-playstation) and SDL lay them out; the lights are left alone. A
+ * DualSense over Bluetooth is left still: the two descriptions of its report disagree by a byte.
+ * Untried here (no Sony controller on the test PC). PAD_DS_RUMBLE=0 sends nothing. */
+static u32 ds_crc32(u32 crc, const u8* p, size_t n)
+{
+    crc = ~crc;
+    while (n--) {
+        crc ^= *p++;
+        for (int k = 0; k < 8; k++) crc = (crc >> 1) ^ (0xEDB88320u & (0u - (crc & 1u)));
+    }
+    return ~crc;
+}
+
+/* The report for these motor levels (fast: the small motor, slow: the large one) into buf (78 bytes or
+ * more, zeroed here); its length, 0 = none. */
+static int ds_rumble_report(int dualsense, int bt, u8 fast, u8 slow, u8* buf)
+{
+    memset(buf, 0, 78);
+    if (!dualsense && !bt) { buf[0] = 0x05; buf[1] = 0x01; buf[4] = fast; buf[5] = slow; return 32; }
+    if (dualsense && !bt) { buf[0] = 0x02; buf[1] = 0x03; buf[3] = fast; buf[4] = slow; return 48; }
+    if (!dualsense && bt) {
+        buf[0] = 0x11; buf[1] = 0xC4; buf[3] = 0x01; buf[6] = fast; buf[7] = slow;
+        const u8 hdr = 0xA2;   /* the Bluetooth HID header, part of the sum */
+        const u32 crc = ds_crc32(ds_crc32(0, &hdr, 1), buf, 74);
+        buf[74] = (u8)crc; buf[75] = (u8)(crc >> 8); buf[76] = (u8)(crc >> 16); buf[77] = (u8)(crc >> 24);
+        return 78;
+    }
+    return 0;
+}
+
+typedef struct { USHORT usage, usage_page, in_len, out_len, feature_len, reserved[17], counts[10]; } ds_hidp_caps;
+static HANDLE s_dsw = INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE;   /* the rumble's handle (the rumble thread's only) */
+static LONG   s_dsw_gen;
+static USHORT s_dsw_len;                       /* the controller's output report length, 0 = not known */
+
+/* 1 when the report went out. On the rumble thread only. */
+static int ds_rumble_write(u8 fast, u8 slow)
+{
+    static HMODULE hid;
+    static BOOLEAN (WINAPI *get_pp)(HANDLE, void**);
+    static BOOLEAN (WINAPI *free_pp)(void*);
+    static LONG (WINAPI *get_caps)(void*, ds_hidp_caps*);
+    static BOOLEAN (WINAPI *set_out)(HANDLE, void*, ULONG);
+    static unsigned said;
+    if (!hid && (hid = LoadLibraryA("hid.dll")) != NULL) {
+        get_pp = (BOOLEAN (WINAPI*)(HANDLE, void**))(void*)GetProcAddress(hid, "HidD_GetPreparsedData");
+        free_pp = (BOOLEAN (WINAPI*)(void*))(void*)GetProcAddress(hid, "HidD_FreePreparsedData");
+        get_caps = (LONG (WINAPI*)(void*, ds_hidp_caps*))(void*)GetProcAddress(hid, "HidP_GetCaps");
+        set_out = (BOOLEAN (WINAPI*)(HANDLE, void*, ULONG))(void*)GetProcAddress(hid, "HidD_SetOutputReport");
+    }
+    if (!InterlockedCompareExchange(&s_ds_live, 0, 0) || s_ds_bt < 0) return 0;
+    const LONG gen = s_ds_gen;
+    if (s_dsw == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE || gen != s_dsw_gen) {
+        if (s_dsw != INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) CloseHandle(s_dsw);
+        WCHAR path[512];
+        AcquireSRWLockShared(&s_ds_lock);
+        memcpy(path, s_ds_path, sizeof path);
+        ReleaseSRWLockShared(&s_ds_lock);
+        s_dsw = CreateFileW(path, GENERIC_WRITE, FILE_SHARE_READ | FILE_SHARE_WRITE, NULL, OPEN_EXISTING, 0, NULL);
+        s_dsw_gen = gen;
+        s_dsw_len = 0;
+        void* pp = NULL;
+        if (s_dsw != INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE && get_pp && get_caps && free_pp && get_pp(s_dsw, &pp)) {
+            ds_hidp_caps caps;
+            memset(&caps, 0, sizeof caps);
+            if (get_caps(pp, &caps) == 0x00110000L /* HIDP_STATUS_SUCCESS */) s_dsw_len = caps.out_len;
+            free_pp(pp);
+        }
+        if (s_dsw == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE && said++ < 3)
+            fprintf(stderr, "[cellPad] the %s can't be written to (error %lu): no rumble\n",
+                    s_ds_dualsense ? "DualSense" : "DualShock 4", GetLastError());
+    }
+    if (s_dsw == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) return 0;
+    u8 rep[600];
+    memset(rep, 0, sizeof rep);
+    const int n = ds_rumble_report(s_ds_dualsense, s_ds_bt, fast, slow, rep);
+    if (!n) {
+        if (said++ < 3) fprintf(stderr, "[cellPad] a DualSense over Bluetooth doesn't rumble here\n");
+        return 0;
+    }
+    /* Windows takes a report at the controller's own output length: the rest stays zero. */
+    const DWORD len = s_dsw_len >= n && s_dsw_len <= sizeof rep ? s_dsw_len : (DWORD)n;
+    DWORD wrote = 0;
+    BOOL ok = WriteFile(s_dsw, rep, len, &wrote, NULL);
+    if (!ok && set_out) ok = set_out(s_dsw, rep, (ULONG)n);
+    if (!ok && said++ < 3)
+        fprintf(stderr, "[cellPad] the %s's rumble report (%d of %lu bytes) was refused (error %lu)\n",
+                s_ds_dualsense ? "DualSense" : "DualShock 4", n, (unsigned long)len, GetLastError());
+    return ok ? 1 : 0;
+}
+
+/* With Steam open, its desktop layout makes this pad a mouse and keyboard for anything that isn't a
+ * Steam game: R2 left click, L2 right click, right stick moves the cursor, Cross presses Enter. A
+ * trigger press with the cursor outside the window clicks whatever is there, the window loses focus
+ * and the pad stops counting, in the middle of a corner. So while the pad is in use the cursor stays
+ * on the picture, and five seconds after its last use the mouse is free again. PAD_NO_CURSOR_GUARD off.
+ *
+ * That clip held the user's own mouse too, for whole races: a right stick held up for throttle
+ * counts as use. So by default nothing is clipped. Steam's mouse comes in through SendInput, which
+ * marks every event injected; a low-level mouse hook drops injected mouse events while the pad has
+ * been used in the last five seconds and this game's window is in front, and lets everything else
+ * through. The real mouse moves and clicks freely. PAD_CURSOR_CLIP=1 clips as before. */
+static unsigned long long pad_now_ms(void);
+static volatile LONG64 s_pad_last_use_tick;      /* GetTickCount64 at the pad's last use, 0 = never */
+static volatile LONG s_pad_mouse_hook, s_pad_mouse_dropped;
+static LRESULT CALLBACK pad_mouse_ll(int code, WPARAM wp, LPARAM lp)
+{
+    if (code == HC_ACTION) {
+        const MSLLHOOKSTRUCT* m = (const MSLLHOOKSTRUCT*)lp;
+        const LONG64 last = s_pad_last_use_tick;
+        if ((m->flags & (LLMHF_INJECTED | LLMHF_LOWER_IL_INJECTED)) && last &&
+            GetTickCount64() - (ULONGLONG)last < 5000) {
+            HWND fg = GetForegroundWindow();
+            DWORD pid = 0;
+            if (fg) GetWindowThreadProcessId(fg, &pid);
+            if (pid == GetCurrentProcessId()) {
+                InterlockedIncrement(&s_pad_mouse_dropped);
+                return 1;
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    return CallNextHookEx(NULL, code, wp, lp);
+}
+static DWORD WINAPI pad_mouse_hook_thread(LPVOID unused)
+{
+    (void)unused;
+    /* Every mouse event on the desktop waits for this hook, so it must never wait for a busy game:
+     * a hook that misses Windows' timeout lags the user's whole mouse. Its work is a few compares. */
+    SetThreadPriority(GetCurrentThread(), THREAD_PRIORITY_TIME_CRITICAL);
+    HHOOK h = SetWindowsHookExW(WH_MOUSE_LL, pad_mouse_ll, GetModuleHandleW(NULL), 0);
+    if (!h) {
+        fprintf(stderr, "[pad] mouse hook not installed (error %lu); Steam's pad mouse is not filtered\n", GetLastError());
+        return 0;
+    }
+    fprintf(stderr, "[pad] the mouse is never held; Steam's pad-driven mouse is ignored while the pad drives the game\n");
+    MSG msg;
+    while (GetMessageW(&msg, NULL, 0, 0) > 0) {}
+    UnhookWindowsHookEx(h);
+    return 0;
+}
+static void pad_cursor_guard(const PadHostState* hs)
+{
+    static int mode = -1, clipped;   /* 0 off, 1 drop injected mouse input, 2 clip the cursor */
+    static unsigned long long last_use, last_clip;
+    static unsigned set_gen;
+    if (set_gen != gt5_settings_gen()) {
+        set_gen = gt5_settings_gen();
+        const int m = getenv("PAD_NO_CURSOR_GUARD") ? 0 : gt5_setting_bool("PAD_CURSOR_CLIP", 0) ? 2 : 1;
+        if (mode == 2 && m != 2 && clipped) { ClipCursor(NULL); clipped = 0; }
+        mode = m;
+    }
+    if (!mode) return;
+    const unsigned long long now = pad_now_ms();
+    if (hs && (hs->buttons || hs->trigger_l2 > 16 || hs->trigger_r2 > 16 ||
+               abs((int)hs->analog_lx - 128) > 48 || abs((int)hs->analog_ly - 128) > 48 ||
+               abs((int)hs->analog_rx - 128) > 48 || abs((int)hs->analog_ry - 128) > 48))
+        last_use = now;
+    if (mode == 1) {
+        if (!hs) return;
+        if (last_use == now) s_pad_last_use_tick = (LONG64)GetTickCount64();
+        if (!InterlockedCompareExchange(&s_pad_mouse_hook, 1, 0)) {
+            HANDLE t = CreateThread(NULL, 64 * 1024, pad_mouse_hook_thread, NULL, 0, NULL);
+            if (t) CloseHandle(t);
+        }
+        return;
+    }
+    if (hs && last_use && now - last_use < 5000) {
+        if (clipped && now - last_clip < 250) return;
+        HWND fg = GetForegroundWindow();
+        RECT r; POINT o = { 0, 0 };
+        if (fg && GetClientRect(fg, &r) && ClientToScreen(fg, &o) && r.right > 0 && r.bottom > 0) {
+            OffsetRect(&r, o.x, o.y);
+            ClipCursor(&r);
+            clipped = 1; last_clip = now;
+        }
+    } else if (clipped) {
+        ClipCursor(NULL);
+        clipped = 0;
+    }
+}
+
+static int pad_poll_dualsense(void)
+{
+    static int started = 0;
+    if (!started) {
+        started = 1;
+        if (!getenv("PAD_NO_DUALSENSE")) {
+            HANDLE t = CreateThread(NULL, 64 * 1024, ds_thread, NULL, 0, NULL);
+            if (t) CloseHandle(t);
+        }
+    }
+    /* PAD_DS_REPORT_FILE=<file>: a test's DualSense, one input report as hex, through the same
+     * parser as the real one, with no window focus needed. */
+    { static const char* sim = (const char*)-1;
+      if (sim == (const char*)-1) sim = getenv("PAD_DS_REPORT_FILE");
+      if (sim) {
+          FILE* f = fopen(sim, "r");
+          if (f) {
+              u8 rep[128]; memset(rep, 0, sizeof rep);
+              unsigned v; int i = 0;
+              while (i < 128 && fscanf(f, "%2x", &v) == 1) rep[i++] = (u8)v;
+              fclose(f);
+              if (i >= 11) ds_parse(rep, (DWORD)i, 1);
+          }
+          AcquireSRWLockShared(&s_ds_lock);
+          s_host_state[0] = s_ds_state;
+          ReleaseSRWLockShared(&s_ds_lock);
+          return 1;
+      } }
+    { static int tr = -1, was = -1;
+      if (tr < 0) tr = getenv("PAD_TRACE") ? 1 : 0;
+      const int f = pad_host_window_focused();
+      if (tr && f != was) {
+          /* Title, window class and program: an untitled window took focus in a user's session and
+           * the title alone could not say whose it was. */
+          char title[80] = "", cls[64] = "", exe[MAX_PATH] = "";
+          HWND fg = GetForegroundWindow();
+          if (fg) {
+              GetWindowTextA(fg, title, sizeof title);
+              GetClassNameA(fg, cls, sizeof cls);
+              DWORD pid = 0; GetWindowThreadProcessId(fg, &pid);
+              HANDLE ph = pid ? OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, FALSE, pid) : NULL;
+              if (ph) { DWORD len = sizeof exe; QueryFullProcessImageNameA(ph, 0, exe, &len); CloseHandle(ph); }
+          }
+          const char* base = strrchr(exe, '\\');
+          fprintf(stderr, "[pad] t=%llu window %s, foreground now '%s' class '%s' program '%s'\n", pad_now_ms(),
+                  f ? "focused" : "LOST FOCUS", title, cls, base ? base + 1 : exe);
+      }
+      was = f; }
+    /* PAD_BACKGROUND=1 (play.bat): the pad keeps driving the game while another window has focus.
+     * A focus grab by something untitled left the pad dead for the rest of a race. Test runs leave
+     * it off, so the user's controller never reaches a game running behind their windows. */
+    static int bg; static unsigned bg_gen;
+    if (bg_gen != gt5_settings_gen()) { bg_gen = gt5_settings_gen(); bg = gt5_setting_bool("PAD_BACKGROUND", 0); }
+    const int focused = pad_host_window_focused();
+    if (!InterlockedCompareExchange(&s_ds_live, 0, 0) || (!focused && !bg)) {
+        pad_cursor_guard(NULL);
+        return 0;
+    }
+    /* The keyboard joins in pad_merge_keys, which leaves out the keys Steam's desktop mode (among
+     * others) makes of pad buttons: merged blindly, Cross also pressed Enter, which is Start here. */
+    AcquireSRWLockShared(&s_ds_lock);
+    s_host_state[0] = s_ds_state;
+    ReleaseSRWLockShared(&s_ds_lock);
+    pad_cursor_guard(focused ? &s_host_state[0] : NULL);   /* never clip the cursor over someone else's window */
+    return 1;
 }

+/* The motors (see the Rumble section): what they should do, sent from a thread of their own when it

+static SRWLOCK s_rumble_lock = SRWLOCK_INIT;
+static u16     s_xi_sent_lo[PAD_MAX_HOST_PORTS], s_xi_sent_hi[PAD_MAX_HOST_PORTS];
+static int     s_ds_sent;   /* small (fast) motor << 8 | large (slow) motor last sent to a DualSense / DualShock 4 */
+
+/* 1 while a motor turns or the game asks for one to. */
+static int pad_rumble_sync(void)
+{
+    const int off = pad_rumble_off(pad_now_ms());
+    int busy = 0;
+    AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&s_rumble_lock);
+    for (int i = 0; i < PAD_MAX_HOST_PORTS; i++) {
+        if (s_rumble[i].lo || s_rumble[i].hi) busy = 1;
+        if (!s_xi_connected[i]) { s_xi_sent_lo[i] = s_xi_sent_hi[i] = 0; continue; }
+        const u16 lo = off ? 0 : s_rumble[i].lo, hi = off ? 0 : s_rumble[i].hi;
+        if (lo == s_xi_sent_lo[i] && hi == s_xi_sent_hi[i]) continue;
+        XINPUT_VIBRATION vib;
+        vib.wLeftMotorSpeed = lo;
+        vib.wRightMotorSpeed = hi;
+        if (p_xi_set_state && p_xi_set_state((DWORD)i, &vib) == ERROR_SUCCESS) {
+            s_xi_sent_lo[i] = lo;
+            s_xi_sent_hi[i] = hi;
+        }
+    }
+    /* A DualSense / DualShock 4 read directly is port 0 while no XInput pad is. A level it refuses is
+     * not sent again until the game asks for another. */
+    const int ds_port0 = !s_xi_connected[0] && InterlockedCompareExchange(&s_ds_live, 0, 0);
+    const int want = !ds_port0 || off || !s_cfg.ds_rumble ? 0 : ((s_rumble[0].hi >> 8) << 8) | (s_rumble[0].lo >> 8);
+    if (want != s_ds_sent && (ds_port0 || s_ds_sent)) {
+        ds_rumble_write((u8)(want >> 8), (u8)want);
+        s_ds_sent = want;
+    }
+    for (int i = 0; i < PAD_MAX_HOST_PORTS; i++) if (s_xi_sent_lo[i] || s_xi_sent_hi[i]) busy = 1;
+    if (s_ds_sent) busy = 1;
+    ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&s_rumble_lock);
+    return busy;
+}
+
+static DWORD WINAPI pad_rumble_thread(LPVOID unused)
+{
+    (void)unused;
+    for (;;) {
+        const int busy = pad_rumble_sync();
+        if (s_rumble_dead) return 0;
+        /* While anything turns: a look every 100 ms (the menu, a stall); else only when asked. */
+        WaitForSingleObject(s_rumble_wake, busy ? 100 : INFINITE);
+    }
+}
+
+static void pad_rumble_kick(void)
+{
+    static volatile LONG started;
+    if (!InterlockedCompareExchange(&started, 1, 0)) {
+        s_rumble_wake = CreateEventW(NULL, FALSE, FALSE, NULL);
+        HANDLE t = s_rumble_wake ? CreateThread(NULL, 64 * 1024, pad_rumble_thread, NULL, 0, NULL) : NULL;
+        if (t) CloseHandle(t);
+        else fprintf(stderr, "[cellPad] no rumble thread (error %lu)\n", GetLastError());
+    }
+    if (s_rumble_wake) SetEvent(s_rumble_wake);
+}

+/* Every motor off, now and for good: the game is ending (exit, the window closed, a crash). Not under
+ * the rumble thread's lock if that is held (a crash inside it): the XInput pads are told anyway. */
+void cellPad_rumble_stop_all(void)

+    }
+    if (s_rumble_wake) SetEvent(s_rumble_wake);

+};
+#define KBS_KEYS 4
+static u16 s_kbs_keys[KBS_COUNT][KBS_KEYS];   /* the keys of each button, 0 = empty slot */
+
+static int kbs_key(const char* s)
+{
+    if (s[0] && !s[1]) {
+        const char c = (char)toupper((unsigned char)s[0]);
+        if (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') return SDL_SCANCODE_A + (c - 'A');
+        if (c == '0') return SDL_SCANCODE_0;
+        if (c >= '1' && c <= '9') return SDL_SCANCODE_1 + (c - '1');
+    }
+    if ((s[0] == 'F' || s[0] == 'f') && isdigit((unsigned char)s[1])) {
+        char* end; const long n = strtol(s + 1, &end, 10);
+        if (!*end && n >= 1 && n <= 12) return SDL_SCANCODE_F1 + (int)n - 1;
+        if (!*end && n >= 13 && n <= 24) return SDL_SCANCODE_F13 + (int)n - 13;
+    }
+    if (!strncasecmp(s, "Num", 3) && isdigit((unsigned char)s[3]) && !s[4])
+        return s[3] == '0' ? SDL_SCANCODE_KP_0 : SDL_SCANCODE_KP_1 + (s[3] - '1');
+    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof kbs_names / sizeof kbs_names[0]; i++)
+        if (!strcasecmp(s, kbs_names[i].name)) return kbs_names[i].key;
+    return 0;
+}
+
+static const char* kbs_key_name(int k, char buf[8])
+{
+    if (k >= SDL_SCANCODE_A && k <= SDL_SCANCODE_Z) { buf[0] = (char)('A' + (k - SDL_SCANCODE_A)); buf[1] = 0; return buf; }
+    if (k >= SDL_SCANCODE_1 && k <= SDL_SCANCODE_9) { buf[0] = (char)('1' + (k - SDL_SCANCODE_1)); buf[1] = 0; return buf; }
+    if (k == SDL_SCANCODE_0) return "0";
+    if (k >= SDL_SCANCODE_F1 && k <= SDL_SCANCODE_F12) { snprintf(buf, 8, "F%d", k - SDL_SCANCODE_F1 + 1); return buf; }
+    if (k >= SDL_SCANCODE_F13 && k <= SDL_SCANCODE_F24) { snprintf(buf, 8, "F%d", k - SDL_SCANCODE_F13 + 13); return buf; }
+    if (k >= SDL_SCANCODE_KP_1 && k <= SDL_SCANCODE_KP_9) { snprintf(buf, 8, "Num%d", k - SDL_SCANCODE_KP_1 + 1); return buf; }
+    if (k == SDL_SCANCODE_KP_0) return "Num0";
+    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof kbs_names / sizeof kbs_names[0]; i++)
+        if (kbs_names[i].key == k) return kbs_names[i].name;
+    snprintf(buf, 8, "sc%d", k);
+    return buf;
+}
+
+static char* kbs_trim(char* s)
+{
+    while (*s == ' ' || *s == '\t') s++;
+    char* e = s + strlen(s);
+    while (e > s && (e[-1] == ' ' || e[-1] == '\t' || e[-1] == '\r' || e[-1] == '\n')) *--e = 0;
+    return s;
+}
+
+static int kbs_has(const u16* keys, int n, int k)
+{
+    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) if (keys[i] == k) return 1;
+    return 0;
+}

+/* PS3_KEYS, read once: the Windows kb_init's rules and log line. */
+static void kbs_init(void)
+{
+    for (int b = 0; b < KBS_COUNT; b++) { memset(s_kbs_keys[b], 0, sizeof s_kbs_keys[b]); s_kbs_keys[b][0] = kbs_btn[b].def; }
+    const char* e = getenv("PS3_KEYS");
+    if (!e || !*e) return;
+    int bound[KBS_COUNT];
+    u16 keys[KBS_COUNT][KBS_KEYS];
+    memset(bound, 0, sizeof bound);
+    memset(keys, 0, sizeof keys);
+    char buf[1024];
+    snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, "%s", e);
+    for (char* item = buf; item && *item; ) {
+        char* next = strchr(item, ',');
+        if (next) *next++ = 0;
+        char* colon = strchr(item, ':');
+        if (colon) {
+            *colon = 0;
+            const char* bn = kbs_trim(item);
+            int b = -1;
+            for (int i = 0; i < KBS_COUNT; i++) if (!strcasecmp(bn, kbs_btn[i].name)) b = i;
+            if (b < 0) {
+                if (*bn) fprintf(stderr, "[keys] PS3_KEYS: no button called '%s', left out\n", bn);
+            } else {
+                int n = 0;
+                if (!bound[b]) memset(keys[b], 0, sizeof keys[b]);
+                else while (n < KBS_KEYS && keys[b][n]) n++;   /* the same button again: more keys */
+                bound[b] = 1;
+                for (char* k = colon + 1; k; ) {
+                    char* slash = strchr(k, '/');
+                    if (slash) *slash++ = 0;
+                    const char* kn = kbs_trim(k);
+                    const int key = *kn && strcasecmp(kn, "none") ? kbs_key(kn) : -1;
+                    if (key == SDL_SCANCODE_ESCAPE)
+                        fprintf(stderr, "[keys] PS3_KEYS: Esc stays the quit key, left out of %s\n", kbs_btn[b].name);
+                    else if (!key)
+                        fprintf(stderr, "[keys] PS3_KEYS: no key called '%s' (for %s), left out\n", kn, kbs_btn[b].name);
+                    else if (key > 0 && n < KBS_KEYS && !kbs_has(keys[b], n, key))
+                        keys[b][n++] = (u16)key;
+                    k = slash;
+                }
+            }
+        } else if (*kbs_trim(item)) {
+            fprintf(stderr, "[keys] PS3_KEYS: '%s' isn't button:key, left out\n", kbs_trim(item));
+        }
+        item = next;
+    }
+    for (int b = 0; b < KBS_COUNT; b++) if (bound[b]) memcpy(s_kbs_keys[b], keys[b], sizeof keys[b]);
+    /* A default key a binding took leaves its old button. */
+    for (int b = 0; b < KBS_COUNT; b++) {
+        if (bound[b]) continue;
+        for (int k = 0; k < KBS_KEYS; k++) {
+            const int key = s_kbs_keys[b][k];
+            for (int o = 0; key && o < KBS_COUNT; o++)
+                if (bound[o] && kbs_has(s_kbs_keys[o], KBS_KEYS, key)) s_kbs_keys[b][k] = 0;
+        }
+    }
+    char line[1400] = "";
+    size_t len = 0;
+    for (int b = 0; b < KBS_COUNT; b++) {
+        char part[96] = "";
+        size_t pl = 0;
+        for (int k = 0; k < KBS_KEYS; k++) {
+            const int key = s_kbs_keys[b][k];
+            if (!key) continue;
+            char nb[8];
+            pl += (size_t)snprintf(part + pl, sizeof part - pl, "%s%s", pl ? "/" : "", kbs_key_name(key, nb));
+            if (pl >= sizeof part) pl = sizeof part - 1;
+        }
+        if (pl || bound[b])
+            len += (size_t)snprintf(line + len, sizeof line - len, " %s%s=%s", kbs_btn[b].name, bound[b] ? "" : "(default)",
+                                    pl ? part : "none");
+        if (len >= sizeof line) len = sizeof line - 1;
+    }
+    fprintf(stderr, "[keys] PS3_KEYS:%s\n", line);
+    pad_sym_bump();   /* [glyphs] the keyboard's symbols name the keys bound now */
+}

+static unsigned long long kbs_now_ms(void)
+{
+    struct timespec ts;
+    clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &ts);
+    return (unsigned long long)ts.tv_sec * 1000ull + (unsigned long long)(ts.tv_nsec / 1000000);
+}

+/* PS3_KEYS_TEST_FILE: the held keys (a flag per key id), or NULL when the real keyboard is read. */
+static const unsigned char* kbs_test_keys(void)
+{
+    static int on = -1;
+    static char path[512];
+    static unsigned char held[KBS_IDS];
+    static unsigned long long until;
+    static int timed;
+    if (on < 0) {
+        const char* e = getenv("PS3_KEYS_TEST_FILE");
+        on = e && *e;
+        if (on) snprintf(path, sizeof path, "%s", e);
+    }
+    if (!on) return NULL;
+    const unsigned long long now = kbs_now_ms();
+    if (timed) {
+        if (now < until) return held;
+        timed = 0;
+        memset(held, 0, sizeof held);
+        fprintf(stderr, "[keys] test: released\n");
+    }
+    FILE* f = fopen(path, "rb");
+    if (!f) return held;
+    char text[256] = "";
+    const int got = fgets(text, sizeof text, f) != NULL;
+    fclose(f);
+    if (!got) text[0] = 0;
+    unsigned char now_held[KBS_IDS];
+    memset(now_held, 0, sizeof now_held);
+    int ms = 0;
+    char names[256];
+    snprintf(names, sizeof names, "%s", kbs_trim(text));
+    int ntok = 0;
+    for (char* tok = text; *tok; ntok++) {
+        while (*tok && strchr(" \t\r\n", *tok)) tok++;
+        if (!*tok) break;
+        char* end = tok;
+        while (*end && !strchr(" \t\r\n", *end)) end++;
+        const char after = *end;
+        *end = 0;
+        if (ntok && strspn(tok, "0123456789") == strlen(tok)) {
+            ms = atoi(tok);   /* a number after the keys: how long to hold them */
+        } else {
+            for (char* k = tok; k; ) {
+                char* plus = strchr(k, '+');
+                if (plus) *plus++ = 0;
+                const int key = *k ? kbs_key(k) : 0;
+                if (key > 0 && key < KBS_IDS) now_held[key] = 1;
+                else if (*k) fprintf(stderr, "[keys] test: no key called '%s'\n", k);
+                k = plus;
+            }
+        }
+        *end = after;
+        tok = end;
+    }
+    if (ms > 0) {
+        f = fopen(path, "wb");
+        if (f) fclose(f);
+        memcpy(held, now_held, sizeof held);
+        timed = 1;
+        until = now + (unsigned long long)ms;
+        fprintf(stderr, "[keys] test: %s\n", names);
+    } else if (memcmp(held, now_held, sizeof held)) {
+        memcpy(held, now_held, sizeof held);
+        fprintf(stderr, "[keys] test: holding '%s'\n", names);
+    }
+    return held;
+}
+
+static int kbs_down(int k, const unsigned char* test, const Uint8* keys, int nkeys, Uint32 mouse)
+{
+    if (test) return k < KBS_IDS && test[k];
+    switch (k) {
+    case KBS_SHIFT:  return keys[SDL_SCANCODE_LSHIFT] || keys[SDL_SCANCODE_RSHIFT];
+    case KBS_CTRL:   return keys[SDL_SCANCODE_LCTRL] || keys[SDL_SCANCODE_RCTRL];
+    case KBS_ALT:    return keys[SDL_SCANCODE_LALT] || keys[SDL_SCANCODE_RALT];
+    case KBS_MOUSE4: return (mouse & SDL_BUTTON_X1MASK) != 0;
+    case KBS_MOUSE5: return (mouse & SDL_BUTTON_X2MASK) != 0;
+    default:         return k < nkeys && keys[k];
+    }
+}

+static void pad_poll_keyboard_sdl(PadHostState* hs)
+{
+    static int off = -1;
+    if (off < 0) { off = getenv("PAD_NO_KEYBOARD") ? 1 : 0; if (!off) kbs_init(); }
+    if (off) return;
+    const unsigned char* test = kbs_test_keys();
+    if (!test && !SDL_WasInit(SDL_INIT_VIDEO)) return;
+
+    pad_host_release(hs);   /* nothing held over from a pad that just went away, or a lost focus */
+    hs->connected = 1;
+    if (g_pad_intercept || (!test && !SDL_GetKeyboardFocus())) return;
+
+    int nkeys = 0;
+    const Uint8* keys = test ? NULL : SDL_GetKeyboardState(&nkeys);
+    if (!test && (!keys || nkeys <= SDL_SCANCODE_RALT)) return;
+    const Uint32 mouse = test ? 0 : SDL_GetMouseState(NULL, NULL);
+    u16 btns = 0;
+    unsigned dirs = 0;      /* stick directions, 1 << (b - KBS_LS_UP) */
+    for (int b = 0; b < KBS_COUNT; b++)
+        for (int k = 0; k < KBS_KEYS && s_kbs_keys[b][k]; k++)
+            if (kbs_down(s_kbs_keys[b][k], test, keys, nkeys, mouse)) {
+                if (b < KBS_LS_UP) btns |= kbs_btn[b].btn;
+                else               dirs |= 1u << (b - KBS_LS_UP);
+                break;
+            }
+    #define KBS_DIR(b) (dirs & (1u << ((b) - KBS_LS_UP)))
+
+    const u16 pressed = btns;  /* what the keys pressed, for the trace below */
+    const u16 stick = kb_arrows(&btns);
+    hs->buttons   = btns;
+    hs->analog_lx = (u8)(((stick & CELL_PAD_CTRL_LEFT) || KBS_DIR(KBS_LS_LEFT)) ? 0 :
+                         ((stick & CELL_PAD_CTRL_RIGHT) || KBS_DIR(KBS_LS_RIGHT)) ? 255 : 128);
+    hs->analog_ly = (u8)(((stick & CELL_PAD_CTRL_UP) || KBS_DIR(KBS_LS_UP)) ? 0 :
+                         ((stick & CELL_PAD_CTRL_DOWN) || KBS_DIR(KBS_LS_DOWN)) ? 255 : 128);
+    hs->analog_rx = (u8)(KBS_DIR(KBS_RS_LEFT) ? 0 : KBS_DIR(KBS_RS_RIGHT) ? 255 : 128);
+    hs->analog_ry = (u8)(KBS_DIR(KBS_RS_UP) ? 0 : KBS_DIR(KBS_RS_DOWN) ? 255 : 128);
+    #undef KBS_DIR
+    hs->trigger_l2 = (u8)((btns & CELL_PAD_CTRL_L2) ? 255 : 0);
+    hs->trigger_r2 = (u8)((btns & CELL_PAD_CTRL_R2) ? 255 : 0);
+    hs->press_up       = (btns & CELL_PAD_CTRL_UP)       ? 255 : 0;
+    hs->press_down     = (btns & CELL_PAD_CTRL_DOWN)     ? 255 : 0;
+    hs->press_left     = (btns & CELL_PAD_CTRL_LEFT)     ? 255 : 0;
+    hs->press_right    = (btns & CELL_PAD_CTRL_RIGHT)    ? 255 : 0;
+    hs->press_triangle = (btns & CELL_PAD_CTRL_TRIANGLE) ? 255 : 0;
+    hs->press_circle   = (btns & CELL_PAD_CTRL_CIRCLE)   ? 255 : 0;
+    hs->press_cross    = (btns & CELL_PAD_CTRL_CROSS)    ? 255 : 0;
+    hs->press_square   = (btns & CELL_PAD_CTRL_SQUARE)   ? 255 : 0;
+    hs->press_l1       = (btns & CELL_PAD_CTRL_L1)       ? 255 : 0;
+    hs->press_r1       = (btns & CELL_PAD_CTRL_R1)       ? 255 : 0;
+
+    { static int said = 0;
+      if (!said && btns) { said = 1;
+          printf("[cellPad] keyboard active on port 0\n");
+          fflush(stdout); } }
+    /* Tests and PS3_KEYS_TRACE=1: what the keys pressed, at each change (the Windows line). */
+    { static int tr = -1;
+      static unsigned prev, lines;
+      if (tr < 0) tr = test || getenv("PS3_KEYS_TRACE");
+      const unsigned all = pressed | (dirs << 16);
+      if (tr && all != prev && lines < 5000) {
+          char out[400] = "";
+          size_t n = 0;
+          for (int b = 0; b < KBS_COUNT; b++) {
+              const int on = b < KBS_LS_UP ? (pressed & kbs_btn[b].btn) != 0 : (int)((dirs >> (b - KBS_LS_UP)) & 1);
+              if (on) n += (size_t)snprintf(out + n, sizeof out - n, " %s", kbs_btn[b].name);
+              if (n >= sizeof out) n = sizeof out - 1;
+          }
+          lines++;
+          prev = all;
+          fprintf(stderr, "[keys] t=%llu pad:%s\n", kbs_now_ms(), n ? out : " nothing");
+      } }
+}

+/* What readers see: the last complete sweep. A sweep first marks every port released, then fills in
+ * the pads, so a thread reading s_host_state during another thread's sweep saw every button up. */
+/* The keyboard beside a controller on port 0 (Arpadiam, 16 Nov 2026: the keys did nothing while a
+ * pad was connected): buttons from both, each stick and trigger from whichever is pushed further.
+ * Steam's desktop layout, among others, turns a controller's buttons into keys while it runs (Cross
+ * into Enter, which is Start here; the d-pad into the arrows): a key that goes down within 60 ms of a
+ * controller button is taken for that echo, and the keyboard is left out until its keys are all up.
+ * PS3_KEYS_WITH_PAD=0: the keyboard is off while a controller is on port 0, as before. */
+#if defined(_WIN32) || (PAD_BACKEND_SDL2 && !defined(__ANDROID__))
+static void pad_merge_keys(PadHostState* hs, const PadHostState* kb)
+{
+    static int on = -1, echo;
+    static u16 pad_prev, kb_prev;
+    static unsigned long long pad_down_ms, kb_down_ms;
+    if (on < 0) { const char* e = getenv("PS3_KEYS_WITH_PAD"); on = !(e && *e == '0'); }
+    if (!on) return;
+    const unsigned long long now = pad_now_ms();
+    const u16 kbb = kb->connected ? kb->buttons : 0;
+    const int kb_used = kbb || kb->analog_lx != 128 || kb->analog_ly != 128 || kb->analog_rx != 128 || kb->analog_ry != 128;
+    const int pad_new = (hs->buttons & ~pad_prev) != 0, kb_new = (kbb & ~kb_prev) != 0;
+    if (pad_new) pad_down_ms = now;
+    if (kb_new) kb_down_ms = now;
+    pad_prev = hs->buttons;
+    kb_prev = kbb;
+    if (!kb_used) echo = 0;
+    else if (!echo && ((kb_new && pad_down_ms && now - pad_down_ms <= 60) || (pad_new && kbb && now - kb_down_ms <= 60))) {
+        echo = 1;
+        static unsigned said;
+        if (said++ < 20) fprintf(stderr, "[keys] keys pressed with a controller button (Steam's desktop layout?): the keyboard waits until they're released\n");
+    }
+    if (echo || !kb_used) return;
+    hs->buttons |= kbb;
+    #define PAD_FURTHER(f) if (abs((int)kb->f - 128) > abs((int)hs->f - 128)) hs->f = kb->f
+    PAD_FURTHER(analog_lx); PAD_FURTHER(analog_ly); PAD_FURTHER(analog_rx); PAD_FURTHER(analog_ry);
+    #undef PAD_FURTHER
+    #define PAD_MAX(f) if (kb->f > hs->f) hs->f = kb->f
+    PAD_MAX(trigger_l2); PAD_MAX(trigger_r2);
+    PAD_MAX(press_right); PAD_MAX(press_left); PAD_MAX(press_up); PAD_MAX(press_down); PAD_MAX(press_triangle);
+    PAD_MAX(press_circle); PAD_MAX(press_cross); PAD_MAX(press_square); PAD_MAX(press_l1); PAD_MAX(press_r1);
+    #undef PAD_MAX
+}
+#endif
+
+/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ * Triggers: throttle and brake while the game drives (PAD_TRIGGERS)
+ *
+ * GT5 accelerates on Cross and brakes on Square, by how hard they are pressed: a PS3 pad's face buttons
+ * are pressure-sensitive. No PC controller's face buttons are, so a pad player had on/off throttle and
+ * brake, with the analog triggers on the gear shifts (R2 / L2). That is the default, as the game has it.
+ * With Triggers set to "Throttle and brake" (PAD_TRIGGERS=drive), while the game drives a car, a
+ * controller's right trigger feeds the pressure of the button the game accelerates with and the left
+ * trigger that of the brake button, the bumpers press the buttons it shifts up and down with, and what
+ * a bumper or trigger pressed before that nothing presses now (and that the game gives a job: in its
+ * default layout L1 looks back, R1 works the lights) moves to the stick press on the same side. That
+ * is the layout GT5 itself uses for its 0-400 m drag mode (throttle R2, brake L2, shift R1 / L1, look
+ * back L3). The face buttons keep pressing what they pressed, fully.
+ *
+ * Which buttons, and when the game is driving, come from GT5 itself (GT5/src/gt5_padmap.cpp): it reads
+ * a controller for a car through its button assignment, every frame, in one function (its menus read
+ * the controller elsewhere), and that says so here (cellPad_drive_frame) each time, with the buttons of
+ * the assignment the player has and whether it is a race or a replay. So the triggers follow a layout
+ * changed in the game's own options, and when the game stops driving (the menus, replays, dialogs) the
+ * controller is as on a PS3 pad within a few frames: the triggers don't press Cross or Square there. The
+ * same on the race's pause screen, where the race input runs on: the race engine's pause flag says so
+ * (cellPad_race_pause, below).
+ * A trigger, bumper or stick press held as the driving ends is left out until it is let go, so a held
+ * trigger doesn't press something on the screen that comes up. The in-game menu always gets the
+ * PS3 pad's layout (it pages with L1 / R1). Keys, the mouse and a wheel are not affected. Without
+ * GT5's word (another title, the function not found) nothing changes. Each change of layout is one
+ * "[pad] ... controller N:" line in the log.
+ * -------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
+
+/* What GT5 last said: its buttons, as bit indexes + 1 (0 = none), 5 bits each, accel | brake << 5 |
+ * up << 10 | down << 15, then the pressure at which it reads full throttle << 20 and full brake << 28
+ * (0 = on / off), and every button with a job << 36. One 64-bit word, so a reader never sees half. */
+static volatile unsigned long long s_drive_map;
+static volatile unsigned long long s_drive_ms;        /* pad_now_ms of its last driving read, 0 = none yet */
+static volatile unsigned           s_drive_gap = 33;  /* ms between two of them, smoothed */
+static volatile unsigned long long s_drive_other_ms;  /* [win] pad_now_ms of its last read in another mode (a replay) */
+static volatile int                s_drive_pad;       /* [win] the last driving read was a port with a pad on it */
+
+static unsigned pad_bit_index(unsigned bit) { return bit & 0xFFFF ? (unsigned)__builtin_ctz(bit & 0xFFFF) + 1 : 0; }
+
+void cellPad_drive_frame(int play, unsigned accel, unsigned brake, unsigned up, unsigned down,
+                         unsigned accel_full, unsigned brake_full, unsigned jobs)
+{
+    const unsigned long long map = (unsigned long long)pad_bit_index(accel) | (unsigned long long)pad_bit_index(brake) << 5 |
+                                   (unsigned long long)pad_bit_index(up) << 10 | (unsigned long long)pad_bit_index(down) << 15 |
+                                   (unsigned long long)(accel_full & 0xFF) << 20 | (unsigned long long)(brake_full & 0xFF) << 28 |
+                                   (unsigned long long)(jobs & 0xFFFF) << 36;
+    __atomic_store_n(&s_drive_map, map, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
+    if (!play) {   /* [win] a replay (mode 2) or another mode: said by GT5_MENU_PAUSE's log */
+        __atomic_store_n(&s_drive_other_ms, pad_now_ms(), __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
+        return;
+    }
+    __atomic_store_n(&s_drive_pad, (accel || brake || jobs) ? 1 : 0, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);   /* [win] the player's port has a pad */
+    const unsigned long long now = pad_now_ms(), was = __atomic_load_n(&s_drive_ms, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
+    if (was && now > was && now - was < 1000) s_drive_gap = (s_drive_gap * 7 + (unsigned)(now - was)) / 8;
+    __atomic_store_n(&s_drive_ms, now, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
+}
+
+/* The game drove within the last few of its frames (at least 150 ms, so a slow frame doesn't flip the
+ * layout; at most 600 ms, so a screen that stops the driving gets the PS3 layout soon). */
+static int pad_driving(unsigned long long now)
+{
+    const unsigned long long at = __atomic_load_n(&s_drive_ms, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
+    if (!at) return 0;
+    if (now <= at) return 1;
+    unsigned win = s_drive_gap * 4;
+    if (win < 150) win = 150;
+    if (win > 600) win = 600;
+    return now - at < win;
+}
+
+/* [pause] The race's pause, as GT5's race engine has it. Its pause screen keeps the race input running (the
+ * race reads the pad on, for the button that ends the pause: D54), so that alone can't tell paused from
+ * running. GT5/src/gt5_padmap.cpp reads the engine's own pause getter's fields with every driving update()
+ * and says so here before the buttons: 1 paused, 0 running, -1 not known (the getter or the race engine not
+ * found, or not seen yet in this race). */
+static volatile int s_race_pause = -1;
+
+void cellPad_race_pause(int state)
+{
+    __atomic_store_n(&s_race_pause, state < 0 ? -1 : state ? 1 : 0, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
+}
+
+/* 1 paused, 0 running, -1 not known or no race being driven. Any thread. */
+int cellPad_race_pause_state(void)
+{
+    if (!pad_driving(pad_now_ms())) return -1;
+    return __atomic_load_n(&s_race_pause, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
+}
+
+int cellPad_race_paused(void) { return cellPad_race_pause_state() == 1; }
+
+typedef struct {
+    u16 accel, brake, up, down;   /* CELL_PAD_CTRL_* bits, 0 = none */
+    u8  accel_full, brake_full;   /* pressure at which the game reads it fully, 0 = it reads on / off */
+    u16 jobs;
+} PadDriveMap;
+
+static void pad_drive_map(PadDriveMap* m)
+{
+    const unsigned long long v = __atomic_load_n(&s_drive_map, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
+    #define PAD_BIT(i) ((i) ? (u16)(1u << ((i) - 1)) : (u16)0)
+    m->accel = PAD_BIT((unsigned)(v & 31));
+    m->brake = PAD_BIT((unsigned)((v >> 5) & 31));
+    m->up = PAD_BIT((unsigned)((v >> 10) & 31));
+    m->down = PAD_BIT((unsigned)((v >> 15) & 31));
+    #undef PAD_BIT
+    m->accel_full = (u8)((v >> 20) & 0xFF);
+    m->brake_full = (u8)((v >> 28) & 0xFF);
+    m->jobs = (u16)((v >> 36) & 0xFFFF);
+}
+
+/* ---- [win] the race holds still while the in-game menu is open (GT5_MENU_PAUSE) --------------------------
+ * GT5_MENU_PAUSE (default on; 0 = off: the race went on behind the menu, the car coasting). When the in-game
+ * menu or its "Quit the game?" opens (g_gt5_menu_pause_want, gt5_menu.cpp) while GT5 is driving - its race
+ * input (cellPad_drive_frame) ran in a race or the 0-400 m mode a moment ago, for a port with a pad whose
+ * assignment gives Start a job (by default: pause) - Start is pressed for the game on port 0, through
+ * the pad's own path (pad_game_press: in the report the game reads, while the menu keeps every real input
+ * from it). [pause] That GT5 paused is known from its race engine's pause flag coming on (cellPad_race_pause:
+ * its race input runs on at its pause screen, D54); if it stays off for two seconds (the countdown, the
+ * finish: Start does nothing there) nothing is undone. When the menu closes, it was this that paused the
+ * race and the flag is still on, the resume button is pressed the same way (GT5_MENU_PAUSE_RESUME: start
+ * (default), circle, cross, triangle, select or a CELL_PAD_CTRL_* mask), and the flag going off says that GT5
+ * resumed. Nothing is pressed in a replay (its input runs in mode 2), at GT5's menus (no race input), when
+ * the player had paused it already (the flag is on: the menu then leaves it paused), when the flag can't be
+ * read (another release, or not seen yet in this race: a pause nothing could tell or undo), or for a race
+ * driven with a wheel alone (Start on the pad isn't read then). Each step is one "[pause]" line in the log.
+ * It runs from the game's own pad reads (cellPadGetData, which GT5's pause screen keeps making) and its
+ * race input.
+ *
+ * [fix3] How long a press is. GT5 reads the pad in one place (its pad manager, EU 1.00 0xBFBAA8, the only call
+ * of cellPadGetData: ports 0-6 in turn, once a game frame, the report kept whatever its len), and its race
+ * did not pause on a Start held 141 ms (about 8 of those reads, D52) while a 300 ms one through PAD_FILE did,
+ * from the same reader, with the same bytes otherwise (the menu's blanking aside). So a press is as long as
+ * a deliberate press on a pad: GT5_MENU_PAUSE_PRESS_MS (default 300, 50-2000) and at least 10 new reports,
+ * let go after at most 700 ms more; presses 200 ms apart. A "[pause] ... let go after" line says how long
+ * each was and how many new reports carried it. */
+#define PAD_PAUSE_VERDICT_MS 2000   /* GT5 paused if its pause flag comes on within this of Start */
+#define PAD_RESUME_VERDICT_MS 3000  /* ... and resumed if it goes off within this of the resume button */
+#define PAD_PRESS_REPORTS 10        /* new reports a press is in, at least */
+#define PAD_PRESS_GAP_MS 200        /* up between two presses, at least */
+
+static volatile int                s_gp_mask;       /* buttons pressed for the game on port 0, 0 = none */
+static volatile unsigned long long s_gp_from;       /* pad_now_ms when that began */
+static volatile int                s_gp_reports;    /* reports with something new (len > 0) that carried it */
+static volatile unsigned long long s_gp_up_ms;      /* pad_now_ms when the last one was let go */
+static volatile int                s_gp_ms = 300;   /* [fix3] how long it is held: GT5_MENU_PAUSE_PRESS_MS */
+
+/* A new press only once the last one is up and the game has seen it up for a moment: two presses that
+ * touch are one press to the game (the resume button right after the pause's Start would do nothing). */
+static int pad_game_press_ready(unsigned long long now)
+{
+    return !__atomic_load_n(&s_gp_mask, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) && now - __atomic_load_n(&s_gp_up_ms, __ATOMIC_RELAXED) >= PAD_PRESS_GAP_MS;
+}
+
+/* Press mask for the game on port 0: in every report it reads for GT5_MENU_PAUSE_PRESS_MS and at least
+ * PAD_PRESS_REPORTS new reports (at most 700 ms longer), then let go. Real input stays shut out meanwhile while
+ * the menu has it. */
+static void pad_game_press(u16 mask)
+{
+    {   /* [fix3] the press's length */
+        char b[16];
+        gt5_setting_str("GT5_MENU_PAUSE_PRESS_MS", b, sizeof b);
+        int ms = b[0] ? atoi(b) : 300;
+        if (ms < 50) ms = 50;
+        if (ms > 2000) ms = 2000;
+        __atomic_store_n(&s_gp_ms, ms, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
+    }
+    __atomic_store_n(&s_gp_reports, 0, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
+    __atomic_store_n(&s_gp_from, pad_now_ms(), __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
+    __atomic_store_n(&s_gp_mask, (int)mask, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
+}
+
+static int pad_menu_pause_on(void)
+{
+    static int on = 1; static unsigned gen = ~0u;
+    if (gen != gt5_settings_gen()) { gen = gt5_settings_gen(); on = gt5_setting_bool("GT5_MENU_PAUSE", 1); }
+    return on;
+}
+
+/* GT5_MENU_PAUSE_RESUME: the button that ends GT5's pause screen, and its name for the log. */
+static u16 pad_resume_button(const char** name)
+{
+    char b[32];
+    gt5_setting_str("GT5_MENU_PAUSE_RESUME", b, sizeof b);
+    static const struct { const char* n; u16 m; } k[] = {
+        { "start", CELL_PAD_CTRL_START }, { "circle", CELL_PAD_CTRL_CIRCLE }, { "cross", CELL_PAD_CTRL_CROSS },
+        { "triangle", CELL_PAD_CTRL_TRIANGLE }, { "select", CELL_PAD_CTRL_SELECT } };
+    for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof k / sizeof k[0]; i++)
+        if (pad_ieq(b, k[i].n)) { *name = k[i].n; return k[i].m; }
+    const unsigned long v = b[0] ? strtoul(b, NULL, 0) : 0;
+    if (v && v <= 0xFFFF) { static char hex[16]; snprintf(hex, sizeof hex, "0x%04lX", v); *name = hex; return (u16)v; }
+    *name = "start";
+    return CELL_PAD_CTRL_START;
+}
+
+static volatile int s_mp_busy;
+static int s_mp_state;                  /* 0 idle, 1 Start pressed: did it pause?, 2 paused by the menu, 3 resume pressed: did it resume? */
+static unsigned long long s_mp_t;       /* when that state began */
+static int s_mp_want_seen, s_mp_pending;
+static const char* s_mp_resume_name = "start";
+
+static void pad_menu_pause_tick(void)
+{
+    if (__atomic_exchange_n(&s_mp_busy, 1, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) return;   /* one thread at a time; the next read does it */
+    const unsigned long long now = pad_now_ms();
+    const int want = __atomic_load_n(&g_gt5_menu_pause_want, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) != 0;
+    const int opened = want && !s_mp_want_seen;
+    s_mp_want_seen = want;
+    if (opened && s_mp_state != 0) s_mp_pending = 1;   /* served once the last pause or resume has settled */
+    if (!want) s_mp_pending = 0;
+    const unsigned long long drive = __atomic_load_n(&s_drive_ms, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
+    switch (s_mp_state) {
+    case 0:
+        if ((opened || (s_mp_pending && want)) && !pad_game_press_ready(now)) { s_mp_pending = 1; break; }   /* after the last press */
+        if (opened || (s_mp_pending && want)) {
+            s_mp_pending = 0;
+            const unsigned long long other = __atomic_load_n(&s_drive_other_ms, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
+            PadDriveMap m;
+            pad_drive_map(&m);
+            const char* why = NULL;
+            if (!pad_menu_pause_on()) why = "(GT5_MENU_PAUSE=0)";
+            else if (!drive && !other) why = "and the game's race input isn't known";
+            else if (!pad_driving(now)) why = other && now - other < 600 ? "in a replay" : "away from a race";
+            else if (cellPad_race_pause_state() == 1) why = "while the race is paused already (its pause screen stays)";   /* [pause] Start would resume it */
+            else if (cellPad_race_pause_state() < 0) why = "and the race's pause can't be read";   /* [pause] a pause it couldn't undo */
+            else if (!__atomic_load_n(&s_drive_pad, __ATOMIC_RELAXED)) why = "while the race is driven without a pad (a wheel alone)";
+            else if (!(m.jobs & CELL_PAD_CTRL_START)) why = "and Start has no job in the game's buttons";
+            if (why) {
+                fprintf(stderr, "[pause] menu open %s: nothing pressed\n", why);
+            } else {
+                pad_game_press(CELL_PAD_CTRL_START);
+                s_mp_state = 1; s_mp_t = now;
+                fprintf(stderr, "[pause] menu open in a race: Start pressed for the game (%d ms)\n",
+                        __atomic_load_n(&s_gp_ms, __ATOMIC_RELAXED));
+            }
+        }
+        break;
+    case 1:   /* did GT5 pause? [pause] its race engine's pause flag comes on */
+        if (cellPad_race_pause_state() == 1) {
+            s_mp_state = 2;
+            fprintf(stderr, "[pause] the game paused: its pause flag came on %lld ms after Start\n", (long long)(now - s_mp_t));
+        } else if (now - s_mp_t > PAD_PAUSE_VERDICT_MS) {
+            s_mp_state = 0;
+            fprintf(stderr, "[pause] the game didn't pause (its pause flag stayed off %u ms after Start): nothing to undo\n",
+                    (unsigned)PAD_PAUSE_VERDICT_MS);
+        }
+        break;
+    case 2:   /* paused by the menu: resumed when it closes, [pause] if it is still paused */
+        if (!want && pad_game_press_ready(now)) {
+            const int ps = cellPad_race_pause_state();
+            if (ps == 1) {
+                const u16 b = pad_resume_button(&s_mp_resume_name);
+                pad_game_press(b);
+                s_mp_state = 3; s_mp_t = now;
+                fprintf(stderr, "[pause] menu closed: %s pressed for the game to resume (%d ms)\n", s_mp_resume_name,
+                        __atomic_load_n(&s_gp_ms, __ATOMIC_RELAXED));
+            } else {
+                s_mp_state = 0;
+                fprintf(stderr, "[pause] menu closed: nothing pressed, %s\n",
+                        ps == 0 ? "the race runs already" : "the race isn't being driven now");
+            }
+        }
+        break;
+    case 3: {   /* did GT5 resume? [pause] its pause flag goes off */
+        const int ps = cellPad_race_pause_state();
+        if (ps == 0) {
+            s_mp_state = 0;
+            fprintf(stderr, "[pause] the game resumed: its pause flag went off %lld ms after %s\n", (long long)(now - s_mp_t),
+                    s_mp_resume_name);
+        } else if (now - s_mp_t > PAD_RESUME_VERDICT_MS) {
+            s_mp_state = 0;
+            if (ps == 1)
+                fprintf(stderr, "[pause] the game didn't resume within %u ms of %s: it stays on its pause screen\n",
+                        (unsigned)PAD_RESUME_VERDICT_MS, s_mp_resume_name);
+            else
+                fprintf(stderr, "[pause] the race wasn't driven again within %u ms of %s\n", (unsigned)PAD_RESUME_VERDICT_MS,
+                        s_mp_resume_name);
+        }
+        break;
+    }
+    default:
+        s_mp_state = 0;
+        break;
+    }
+    __atomic_store_n(&s_mp_busy, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
+}
+
+/* At the end of a port 0 report: what pad_game_press holds, put in after the menu's shutting out. */
+static void pad_game_press_apply(CellPadData* data, u32 setting)
+{
+    const int mask = __atomic_load_n(&s_gp_mask, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
+    if (!mask) return;
+    data->button[CELL_PAD_BTN_OFFSET_DIGITAL1] |= (u16)(mask & 0xFF);
+    data->button[CELL_PAD_BTN_OFFSET_DIGITAL2] |= (u16)((mask >> 8) & 0xFF);
+    if (setting & CELL_PAD_SETTING_PRESS_ON) {
+        if (mask & CELL_PAD_CTRL_CIRCLE) data->button[CELL_PAD_BTN_OFFSET_PRESS_CIRCLE] = 255;
+        if (mask & CELL_PAD_CTRL_CROSS) data->button[CELL_PAD_BTN_OFFSET_PRESS_CROSS] = 255;
+        if (mask & CELL_PAD_CTRL_TRIANGLE) data->button[CELL_PAD_BTN_OFFSET_PRESS_TRIANGLE] = 255;
+        if (mask & CELL_PAD_CTRL_SQUARE) data->button[CELL_PAD_BTN_OFFSET_PRESS_SQUARE] = 255;
+    }
+    if (data->len > 0) __atomic_add_fetch(&s_gp_reports, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
+    const unsigned long long held = pad_now_ms() - __atomic_load_n(&s_gp_from, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
+    const int ms = __atomic_load_n(&s_gp_ms, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
+    const int reports = __atomic_load_n(&s_gp_reports, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
+    if ((reports >= PAD_PRESS_REPORTS && held >= (unsigned long long)ms) || held > (unsigned long long)ms + 700u) {
+        /* let go: the next report has it up (one thread lets go and says so) */
+        if (__atomic_exchange_n(&s_gp_mask, 0, __ATOMIC_ACQ_REL)) {
+            __atomic_store_n(&s_gp_up_ms, pad_now_ms(), __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
+            fprintf(stderr, "[pause] 0x%04X let go after %llu ms, in %d new reports\n", (unsigned)mask, held, reports);
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+/* The pressure word a button reports, NULL for one with none (L3, R3, Start, Select). L2 and R2 report
+ * the triggers' fields. */
+static u8* pad_press_field(PadHostState* hs, u16 bit)
+{
+    switch (bit) {
+    case CELL_PAD_CTRL_UP:       return &hs->press_up;
+    case CELL_PAD_CTRL_DOWN:     return &hs->press_down;
+    case CELL_PAD_CTRL_LEFT:     return &hs->press_left;
+    case CELL_PAD_CTRL_RIGHT:    return &hs->press_right;
+    case CELL_PAD_CTRL_TRIANGLE: return &hs->press_triangle;
+    case CELL_PAD_CTRL_CIRCLE:   return &hs->press_circle;
+    case CELL_PAD_CTRL_CROSS:    return &hs->press_cross;
+    case CELL_PAD_CTRL_SQUARE:   return &hs->press_square;
+    case CELL_PAD_CTRL_L1:       return &hs->press_l1;
+    case CELL_PAD_CTRL_R1:       return &hs->press_r1;
+    case CELL_PAD_CTRL_L2:       return &hs->trigger_l2;
+    case CELL_PAD_CTRL_R2:       return &hs->trigger_r2;
+    default:                     return NULL;
+    }
+}
+
+/* Presses a button with pressure v (1-255); a button without a pressure word just goes down. */
+static void pad_press(PadHostState* hs, u16 bit, u8 v)
+{
+    if (!bit || !v) return;
+    hs->buttons |= bit;
+    u8* p = pad_press_field(hs, bit);
+    if (p && *p < v) *p = v;
+}
+
+/* A trigger's travel (0-255) as the pressure that gives the game the same share of throttle or brake:
+ * a little taken off the bottom (a trigger resting just off zero) and the top (one that never quite
+ * reaches 255), then scaled to `full`, the pressure the game reads as fully pressed. full = 0: the game
+ * reads the button on / off, pressed past a quarter of the trigger's travel. */
+static u8 pad_trigger_press(u8 t, u8 full)
+{
+    const int lo = 8, hi = 247;
+    if (t <= lo) return 0;
+    if (!full) return t > 64 ? 255 : 0;
+    const int span = t >= hi ? hi - lo : t - lo;
+    const int v = (span * full + (hi - lo) - 1) / (hi - lo);   /* rounded up: the lightest touch counts */
+    return (u8)(v < 1 ? 1 : v > 255 ? 255 : v);
+}
+
+/* The physical controls whose job changes with the layout, for the hold-over check. */
+enum { PH_RT = 1, PH_LT = 2, PH_RB = 4, PH_LB = 8, PH_LS = 16, PH_RS = 32 };
+static int      s_trig_layout[PAD_MAX_HOST_PORTS];   /* 1: throttle and brake */
+static unsigned s_trig_block[PAD_MAX_HOST_PORTS];    /* PH_* held over a layout change, left out until let go */
+
+/* One controller's state, as the backends make it (a PS3 pad's layout), in the layout in force. */
+static void pad_triggers_apply(int port, PadHostState* hs, int racing, const PadDriveMap* m)
+{
+    const u16 b = hs->buttons;
+    const u8 rt = hs->trigger_r2, lt = hs->trigger_l2;
+    const unsigned held = (rt > 8 ? PH_RT : 0) | (lt > 8 ? PH_LT : 0) |
+                          ((b & CELL_PAD_CTRL_R1) ? PH_RB : 0) | ((b & CELL_PAD_CTRL_L1) ? PH_LB : 0) |
+                          ((b & CELL_PAD_CTRL_L3) ? PH_LS : 0) | ((b & CELL_PAD_CTRL_R3) ? PH_RS : 0);
+    if (racing != s_trig_layout[port]) {
+        s_trig_layout[port] = racing;
+        /* Only on the way out of a race: a throttle held into one is just the throttle. */
+        s_trig_block[port] = racing ? 0 : held;
+        static unsigned said;
+        if (said < 400) {
+            said++;
+            fprintf(stderr, "[pad] t=%llu controller %d: %s%s\n", pad_now_ms(), port,
+                    racing ? "triggers are throttle and brake (the game is driving)"
+                           : cellPad_race_pause_state() == 1 ? "as on a PS3 pad (the race is paused)" : "as on a PS3 pad",
+                    s_trig_block[port] ? "; a control held over waits to be let go" : "");
+        }
+    }
+    s_trig_block[port] &= held;
+    const unsigned block = s_trig_block[port];
+    if (!racing) {
+        if (block & PH_RT) { hs->trigger_r2 = 0; hs->buttons &= (u16)~CELL_PAD_CTRL_R2; }
+        if (block & PH_LT) { hs->trigger_l2 = 0; hs->buttons &= (u16)~CELL_PAD_CTRL_L2; }
+        if (block & PH_RB) { hs->press_r1 = 0; hs->buttons &= (u16)~CELL_PAD_CTRL_R1; }
+        if (block & PH_LB) { hs->press_l1 = 0; hs->buttons &= (u16)~CELL_PAD_CTRL_L1; }
+        if (block & PH_LS) hs->buttons &= (u16)~CELL_PAD_CTRL_L3;
+        if (block & PH_RS) hs->buttons &= (u16)~CELL_PAD_CTRL_R3;
+        return;
+    }
+    hs->buttons &= (u16)~(CELL_PAD_CTRL_L1 | CELL_PAD_CTRL_R1 | CELL_PAD_CTRL_L2 | CELL_PAD_CTRL_R2 |
+                          CELL_PAD_CTRL_L3 | CELL_PAD_CTRL_R3);
+    hs->press_l1 = hs->press_r1 = 0;
+    hs->trigger_l2 = hs->trigger_r2 = 0;
+    /* A job the assignment gives no button keeps its control's PS3 button (and pressure). */
+    const u16 accel = m->accel ? m->accel : CELL_PAD_CTRL_R2, brake = m->brake ? m->brake : CELL_PAD_CTRL_L2;
+    const u16 up = m->up ? m->up : CELL_PAD_CTRL_R1, down = m->down ? m->down : CELL_PAD_CTRL_L1;
+    if (!(block & PH_RT)) pad_press(hs, accel, m->accel ? pad_trigger_press(rt, m->accel_full) : pad_trigger_press(rt, 255));
+    if (!(block & PH_LT)) pad_press(hs, brake, m->brake ? pad_trigger_press(lt, m->brake_full) : pad_trigger_press(lt, 255));
+    if ((b & CELL_PAD_CTRL_R1) && !(block & PH_RB)) pad_press(hs, up, 255);
+    if ((b & CELL_PAD_CTRL_L1) && !(block & PH_LB)) pad_press(hs, down, 255);
+    /* A bumper's or trigger's button that nothing presses now and that the game gives a job: the stick
+     * press on its side (L1 before L2, R1 before R2). The stick presses' own jobs (horn, wipers in GT5's
+     * default layout) are then off the controller, as in the game's drag-mode layout. */
+    const u16 made = accel | brake | up | down;
+    u16 left = 0, right = 0;
+    if ((m->jobs & CELL_PAD_CTRL_L1) && !(made & CELL_PAD_CTRL_L1)) left = CELL_PAD_CTRL_L1;
+    else if ((m->jobs & CELL_PAD_CTRL_L2) && !(made & CELL_PAD_CTRL_L2)) left = CELL_PAD_CTRL_L2;
+    if ((m->jobs & CELL_PAD_CTRL_R1) && !(made & CELL_PAD_CTRL_R1)) right = CELL_PAD_CTRL_R1;
+    else if ((m->jobs & CELL_PAD_CTRL_R2) && !(made & CELL_PAD_CTRL_R2)) right = CELL_PAD_CTRL_R2;
+    if ((b & CELL_PAD_CTRL_L3) && !(block & PH_LS)) pad_press(hs, left ? left : CELL_PAD_CTRL_L3, 255);
+    if ((b & CELL_PAD_CTRL_R3) && !(block & PH_RS)) pad_press(hs, right ? right : CELL_PAD_CTRL_R3, 255);
+}
+
+/* Pad buttons the mouse presses at GT5's menus while it steers in races (wheel_host_win.c: left button
+ * Cross, right Circle, the wheel the d-pad's up/down), added to port 0 at each poll. */
+static volatile unsigned s_mouse_btns;
+void cellPad_set_mouse_buttons(unsigned btns) { s_mouse_btns = btns; }
+
+/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ * The in-game menu's controller (F1, or the pad chord)
+ *
+ * The menu used to read the first connected port, and the keyboard always marks port 0 connected:
+ * a controller on XInput slot 2-4 (Steam's virtual pad beside another, ViGEm) could neither open nor
+ * drive it, nor could a wheel. Now it reads every controller at once (buttons of all, each stick and
+ * trigger from whichever is pushed furthest), the keyboard as before, and the PC wheel's buttons and
+ * d-pad. Always in the PS3 pad's layout, whatever the trigger layout in a race. PAD_MENU_ALL_PADS=0:
+ * the first connected port, as before.
+ * -------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
+static void pad_menu_add(gt5_menu_pad* mp, const PadHostState* p)
+{
+    mp->buttons |= p->buttons;
+    #define PAD_FURTHER(f, s) if (abs((int)p->s - 128) > abs((int)mp->f - 128)) mp->f = p->s
+    PAD_FURTHER(lx, analog_lx); PAD_FURTHER(ly, analog_ly); PAD_FURTHER(rx, analog_rx); PAD_FURTHER(ry, analog_ry);
+    #undef PAD_FURTHER
+    if (p->trigger_l2 > mp->l2) mp->l2 = p->trigger_l2;
+    if (p->trigger_r2 > mp->r2) mp->r2 = p->trigger_r2;
+}
+
+static void pad_menu_feed(const PadHostState* raw, const PadHostState* kb, int kb_apart)
+{
+    gt5_menu_pad mp;
+    memset(&mp, 0, sizeof mp);
+    mp.lx = mp.ly = mp.rx = mp.ry = 128;
+    int any = 0;
+    for (int i = 0; i < PAD_MAX_HOST_PORTS; i++) {
+        if (!raw[i].connected) continue;
+        pad_menu_add(&mp, &raw[i]);
+        any = 1;
+        if (!s_cfg.menu_all) {
+            if (i == 0 && kb_apart && kb->connected) pad_menu_add(&mp, kb);   /* port 0 had the keys merged */
+            break;
+        }
+    }
+    if (s_cfg.menu_all) {
+        if (kb_apart && kb->connected) { pad_menu_add(&mp, kb); any = 1; }
+#if defined(_WIN32) || (PAD_BACKEND_SDL2 && !defined(__ANDROID__))
+        const unsigned wb = wheel_host_pad_buttons();
+        if (wb) { mp.buttons |= (unsigned short)wb; any = 1; }
+#endif
+    }
+    mp.connected = any;
+    gt5_menu_feed_pad(&mp);
+}
+
+/* PAD_FILE (tests): a line "pad <buttons> <ms> [lx ly rx ry [lt rt]]" is a controller on port 0 for ms
+ * milliseconds, as if one were plugged in: buttons in PAD_SCRIPT's mask encoding as that controller has
+ * them (a PS3 pad's layout: R2 / L2 are its triggers), sticks 0-255 (128 at rest), triggers 0-255 (a
+ * trigger past 30 also sets its R2 / L2 bit, as an Xbox pad's does; an R2 / L2 bit with no value is a
+ * full pull). It goes through everything a real controller does, the trigger layout included, so a
+ * test can pull the right trigger halfway and read what the game makes of it:
+ *     echo pad 0 3000 128 128 128 128 0 128 > pad.txt     (3 s of the right trigger at half)
+ * The line is taken and the file emptied; a new "pad" line replaces the one held. The other PAD_FILE
+ * lines (cellPadGetData) are pressed after the trigger layout, straight into what the game reads. */
+static int pad_file_pad(unsigned long long now, PadHostState* out)
+{
+    static int on = -1;
+    static char path[512];
+    static unsigned long long until;
+    static PadHostState held;
+    if (on < 0) {
+        const char* e = getenv("PAD_FILE");
+        on = e && *e;
+        if (on) snprintf(path, sizeof path, "%s", e);
+    }
+    if (!on) return 0;
+    FILE* f = fopen(path, "rb");
+    if (f) {
+        char line[160] = "";
+        const int got = fgets(line, sizeof line, f) != NULL;
+        fclose(f);
+        const char* p = line;
+        while (*p == ' ' || *p == '\t') p++;
+        if (got && (p[0] | 0x20) == 'p' && (p[1] | 0x20) == 'a' && (p[2] | 0x20) == 'd' && (p[3] == ' ' || p[3] == '\t')) {
+            char* rest;
+            const unsigned mask = (unsigned)strtoul(p + 3, &rest, 0) & 0xFFFFu;
+            int ms = 0, v[6] = { 128, 128, 128, 128, 0, 0 };
+            const int n = sscanf(rest, "%d %d %d %d %d %d %d", &ms, &v[0], &v[1], &v[2], &v[3], &v[4], &v[5]);
+            for (int i = 0; i < 6; i++) v[i] = v[i] < 0 ? 0 : v[i] > 255 ? 255 : v[i];
+            if (n >= 1 && ms > 0) {
+                pad_host_release(&held);
+                held.connected = 1;
+                held.buttons = (u16)mask;
+                held.analog_lx = (u8)v[0]; held.analog_ly = (u8)v[1];
+                held.analog_rx = (u8)v[2]; held.analog_ry = (u8)v[3];
+                held.trigger_l2 = (u8)(v[4] ? v[4] : (mask & CELL_PAD_CTRL_L2) ? 255 : 0);
+                held.trigger_r2 = (u8)(v[5] ? v[5] : (mask & CELL_PAD_CTRL_R2) ? 255 : 0);
+                if (held.trigger_l2 > 30) held.buttons |= CELL_PAD_CTRL_L2;
+                if (held.trigger_r2 > 30) held.buttons |= CELL_PAD_CTRL_R2;
+                #define PAD_FULL(bit, f) held.f = (held.buttons & (bit)) ? 255 : 0
+                PAD_FULL(CELL_PAD_CTRL_UP, press_up); PAD_FULL(CELL_PAD_CTRL_DOWN, press_down);
+                PAD_FULL(CELL_PAD_CTRL_LEFT, press_left); PAD_FULL(CELL_PAD_CTRL_RIGHT, press_right);
+                PAD_FULL(CELL_PAD_CTRL_TRIANGLE, press_triangle); PAD_FULL(CELL_PAD_CTRL_CIRCLE, press_circle);
+                PAD_FULL(CELL_PAD_CTRL_CROSS, press_cross); PAD_FULL(CELL_PAD_CTRL_SQUARE, press_square);
+                PAD_FULL(CELL_PAD_CTRL_L1, press_l1); PAD_FULL(CELL_PAD_CTRL_R1, press_r1);
+                #undef PAD_FULL
+                until = now + (unsigned long long)ms;
+                fprintf(stderr, "[cellPad] PAD_FILE controller for %d ms: buttons 0x%04X, sticks %d,%d %d,%d, "
+                                "triggers L %d R %d\n", ms, mask, v[0], v[1], v[2], v[3], held.trigger_l2, held.trigger_r2);
+            }
+            FILE* w = fopen(path, "wb");
+            if (w) fclose(w);
+        }
+    }
+    if (!until || now >= until) return 0;
+    *out = held;
+    return 1;
+}
+
+/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ * [glyphs] Button symbols ("Button symbols" setting, GT5/src/gt5_glyphs.cpp): the device used last, the
+ * Xbox control that presses a PS3 button now, and the key that does. Any thread may ask.
+ *
+ * The device is what made the last new press: a button, a trigger pulled most of the way or a stick
+ * pushed most of the way, on a controller or the keyboard. A key that goes down within 60 ms of a
+ * controller button is Steam's desktop layout echoing it (as in pad_merge_keys) and doesn't count; a
+ * wheel and the mouse don't change it. Before anything is pressed: an XInput controller if one is in,
+ * else a DualSense / DualShock 4 read directly, else the keyboard.
+ * -------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
+static volatile int s_sym_device;        /* CELL_PAD_SYM_DEV_*, 0 = nothing pressed yet */
+static volatile int s_sym_racing = -1;   /* the trigger layout is throttle and brake now */
+
+static unsigned pad_sym_far(const PadHostState* p)
+{
+    #define PAD_SYM_FAR(v) ((v) < 128 - 96 || (v) > 128 + 96)
+    return (unsigned)PAD_SYM_FAR(p->analog_lx) | (unsigned)PAD_SYM_FAR(p->analog_ly) << 1 |
+           (unsigned)PAD_SYM_FAR(p->analog_rx) << 2 | (unsigned)PAD_SYM_FAR(p->analog_ry) << 3 |
+           (unsigned)(p->trigger_l2 > 160) << 4 | (unsigned)(p->trigger_r2 > 160) << 5;
+    #undef PAD_SYM_FAR
+}
+
+static int pad_sym_kind(int port)
+{
+#if PAD_BACKEND_XINPUT
+    return s_xi_connected[port] ? CELL_PAD_SYM_DEV_XBOX : CELL_PAD_SYM_DEV_PLAYSTATION;   /* else the DualSense read directly */
+#elif PAD_BACKEND_SDL2
+    return s_sdl_ps[port] ? CELL_PAD_SYM_DEV_PLAYSTATION : CELL_PAD_SYM_DEV_XBOX;
+#else
+    (void)port;
+    return CELL_PAD_SYM_DEV_XBOX;
+#endif
+}
+
+/* From pad_poll_backend: raw = the controllers as on a PS3 pad, ctl = which ports have one, kb = the keys. */
+static void pad_sym_note(const PadHostState* raw, const int* ctl, const PadHostState* kb, unsigned long long now, int racing)
+{
+    static u16 prev_b[PAD_MAX_HOST_PORTS], kb_prev;
+    static unsigned prev_far[PAD_MAX_HOST_PORTS], kb_far_prev;
+    static unsigned long long pad_edge_ms;
+    int dev = 0;
+    for (int i = 0; i < PAD_MAX_HOST_PORTS; i++) {
+        const int on = ctl[i] && raw[i].connected;
+        const u16 b = on ? raw[i].buttons : 0;
+        const unsigned pushed = on ? pad_sym_far(&raw[i]) : 0;
+        if ((b & (u16)~prev_b[i]) || (pushed & ~prev_far[i])) { dev = pad_sym_kind(i); pad_edge_ms = now; }
+        prev_b[i] = b;
+        prev_far[i] = pushed;
+    }
+    const u16 kbb = kb->connected ? kb->buttons : 0;
+    const unsigned kfar = kb->connected ? pad_sym_far(kb) : 0;
+    if (!dev && ((kbb & (u16)~kb_prev) || (kfar & ~kb_far_prev)) && !(pad_edge_ms && now - pad_edge_ms <= 60))
+        dev = CELL_PAD_SYM_DEV_KEYBOARD;
+    kb_prev = kbb;
+    kb_far_prev = kfar;
+    if (dev && dev != s_sym_device) { s_sym_device = dev; pad_sym_bump(); }
+    if (racing != s_sym_racing) { s_sym_racing = racing; pad_sym_bump(); }
+}
+
+unsigned cellPad_symbol_gen(void) { return __atomic_load_n(&s_sym_gen, __ATOMIC_RELAXED); }
+
+int cellPad_symbol_device(void)
+{
+    const int d = s_sym_device;
+    if (d) return d;
+#if PAD_BACKEND_XINPUT
+    for (int i = 0; i < PAD_MAX_HOST_PORTS; i++) if (s_xi_connected[i]) return CELL_PAD_SYM_DEV_XBOX;
+#endif
+#ifdef _WIN32
+    if (InterlockedCompareExchange(&s_ds_live, 0, 0)) return CELL_PAD_SYM_DEV_PLAYSTATION;
+#endif
+#if PAD_BACKEND_SDL2
+    for (int i = 0; i < PAD_MAX_HOST_PORTS; i++) if (s_sdl_controllers[i]) return pad_sym_kind(i);
+#endif
+    return CELL_PAD_SYM_DEV_KEYBOARD;
+}
+
+int cellPad_symbol_xbox(unsigned bit)
+{
+    static const struct { u16 bit; u8 sym; } k_std[] = {
+        { CELL_PAD_CTRL_CROSS, CELL_PAD_SYM_A }, { CELL_PAD_CTRL_CIRCLE, CELL_PAD_SYM_B },
+        { CELL_PAD_CTRL_SQUARE, CELL_PAD_SYM_X }, { CELL_PAD_CTRL_TRIANGLE, CELL_PAD_SYM_Y },
+        { CELL_PAD_CTRL_L1, CELL_PAD_SYM_LB }, { CELL_PAD_CTRL_R1, CELL_PAD_SYM_RB },
+        { CELL_PAD_CTRL_L2, CELL_PAD_SYM_LT }, { CELL_PAD_CTRL_R2, CELL_PAD_SYM_RT },
+        { CELL_PAD_CTRL_L3, CELL_PAD_SYM_LS }, { CELL_PAD_CTRL_R3, CELL_PAD_SYM_RS },
+        { CELL_PAD_CTRL_SELECT, CELL_PAD_SYM_VIEW }, { CELL_PAD_CTRL_START, CELL_PAD_SYM_MENU },
+        { CELL_PAD_CTRL_UP, CELL_PAD_SYM_DPAD }, { CELL_PAD_CTRL_DOWN, CELL_PAD_SYM_DPAD },
+        { CELL_PAD_CTRL_LEFT, CELL_PAD_SYM_DPAD }, { CELL_PAD_CTRL_RIGHT, CELL_PAD_SYM_DPAD },
+    };
+    const u16 shoulders = CELL_PAD_CTRL_L1 | CELL_PAD_CTRL_R1 | CELL_PAD_CTRL_L2 | CELL_PAD_CTRL_R2 |
+                          CELL_PAD_CTRL_L3 | CELL_PAD_CTRL_R3;
+    if (s_sym_racing == 1) {
+        /* Throttle and brake on the triggers (pad_triggers_apply): the bumpers shift, a shoulder button's
+         * job nothing else does moves to the stick press on its side, the face buttons are as they were. */
+        PadDriveMap m;
+        pad_drive_map(&m);
+        const u16 accel = m.accel ? m.accel : CELL_PAD_CTRL_R2, brake = m.brake ? m.brake : CELL_PAD_CTRL_L2;
+        const u16 up = m.up ? m.up : CELL_PAD_CTRL_R1, down = m.down ? m.down : CELL_PAD_CTRL_L1;
+        const u16 made = accel | brake | up | down;
+        u16 left = 0, right = 0;
+        if ((m.jobs & CELL_PAD_CTRL_L1) && !(made & CELL_PAD_CTRL_L1)) left = CELL_PAD_CTRL_L1;
+        else if ((m.jobs & CELL_PAD_CTRL_L2) && !(made & CELL_PAD_CTRL_L2)) left = CELL_PAD_CTRL_L2;
+        if ((m.jobs & CELL_PAD_CTRL_R1) && !(made & CELL_PAD_CTRL_R1)) right = CELL_PAD_CTRL_R1;
+        else if ((m.jobs & CELL_PAD_CTRL_R2) && !(made & CELL_PAD_CTRL_R2)) right = CELL_PAD_CTRL_R2;
+        if (bit == up) return CELL_PAD_SYM_RB;
+        if (bit == down) return CELL_PAD_SYM_LB;
+        if (bit == accel && (bit & shoulders)) return CELL_PAD_SYM_RT;
+        if (bit == brake && (bit & shoulders)) return CELL_PAD_SYM_LT;
+        if (left && bit == left) return CELL_PAD_SYM_LS;
+        if (right && bit == right) return CELL_PAD_SYM_RS;
+        if (bit & shoulders) return 0;   /* nothing on the controller presses it in this layout */
+    }
+    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof k_std / sizeof k_std[0]; i++)
+        if (k_std[i].bit == bit) return k_std[i].sym;
+    return 0;
+}
+
+int cellPad_symbol_key(unsigned bit, char* buf, int cap)
+{
+    if (!buf || cap < 1) return 0;
+    buf[0] = 0;
+    char nb[8];
+    const char* name = NULL;
+#ifdef _WIN32
+    for (int b = 0; b < KB_COUNT && !name; b++)
+        if (kb_btn[b].btn && kb_btn[b].btn == bit && s_kb_keys[b][0]) name = kb_vk_name(s_kb_keys[b][0], nb);
+#elif PAD_BACKEND_SDL2 && !defined(__ANDROID__)
+    for (int b = 0; b < KBS_COUNT && !name; b++)
+        if (kbs_btn[b].btn && kbs_btn[b].btn == bit && s_kbs_keys[b][0]) name = kbs_key_name(s_kbs_keys[b][0], nb);
+#else
+    (void)bit; (void)nb;
+#endif
+    if (name) snprintf(buf, (size_t)cap, "%s", name);
+    return (int)strlen(buf);
+}
