+/* One test for every diagnostic on the DMA path.
+ *
+ * mfc_submit and mfc_do_transfer carry some thirty environment-gated
+ * diagnostics, each of which loaded and tested a flag of its own on every MFC
+ * command and every transfer. They now sit between MFC_DIAG_BEGIN and
+ * MFC_DIAG_END, and those regions are entered only when one of the variables
+ * below is set at the first DMA of the process. Inside, each block still reads
+ * its own variable as before, so with any of them set every block runs exactly
+ * as it did. SPU_DMA_FASTPATH=0 enters the regions always: today's behaviour.
+ *
+ * Every getenv name used inside a region must be in this list: a variable
+ * read in a region but missing here would silently stop working. What is
+ * NOT a diagnostic stays outside: the malformed-transfer rule (SPU_DMA_LAX),
+ * the repeat watchdog, the policy-module trace, the barrier and poison watches
+ * that other code arms at run time. */
+__attribute__((unused)) static const char* const mfc_diag_env_names[] = {
+    "SPU_DMA_WATCH", "SPU_ORDER", "SPU_DMA_RANGE", "SPU_DMACHK", "SPU_GETHIST", "SPU_PUTHIST",
+    "SPU_MFC_TRACE", "SPU_STACKEA_WATCH", "SPU_DMATRACE_ALL", "YDKJ_DMA_IMG", "SPU_DUMP_GET",
+    "SPU_DSP_IMAGE_EA", "LBP_SKIP_NULL_DMA", "SPU_OVL_DIAG", "SPU_SMC_WATCH", "SPU_SMC_LO",
+    "SPU_SMC_HI", "SPU_PUT_WATCH", "SPU_LOCKGUARD", "SPU_CMDHIST", "SPU_WATCHEA",
+    "SPU_WATCHEA_EVERY", "SPU_WATCHLSA", "SPU_ROWCOV", "SPU_VRAMPC", "SPU_H2LSRC", "SPU_PUTEA",
+    "SPU_DMATRACE", "SPU_DMATRACE_RAW",
+};
+__attribute__((unused)) static int s_mfc_diag = -1;
+static inline int mfc_diag_probe(void)
+{
+    int on = 0;
+    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof mfc_diag_env_names / sizeof mfc_diag_env_names[0]; i++)
+        if (getenv(mfc_diag_env_names[i])) on = 1;
+    { const char* e = getenv("SPU_DMA_FASTPATH"); if (e && *e == '0') on = 1; }
+    s_mfc_diag = on;
+    return on;
+}

+#define MFC_DIAG_BEGIN  if (__builtin_expect(mfc_diag, 0)) {
+#define MFC_DIAG_END    }

+/* A guest wait loop that yields (GT5 waits for SPU results like this) spins at 100% of a core on a
+ * small CPU: SwitchToThread hands over only to a thread queued on the same processor, and there is
+ * usually none. On a laptop that is power the other game threads lose. So when a thread has yielded 16
+ * times in a row, less than 50 us apart, it naps 50 us on a high-resolution timer instead, while the
+ * process may use 12 logical CPUs or fewer (the count is checked again every second, so an affinity
+ * change counts). PS3_YIELD_NAP=0 never naps, =1 always may. Hookshot (Switch 2 recomp) measured +9%
+ * frame rate and 14% less CPU per frame at 4 threads with the same change.
+ * Round 9 (15 Nov 2026) widened "small" from 8 to 12 logical CPUs, the 6-core/12-thread CPUs many players
+ * have (Ryzen 5 3600/5600X, i5-10400F): on 6 P-cores with hyper-threading the policy (this nap and the
+ * pollers' sleep below) kept the same game fps (-0.3% +- 2.8%, +0.4% +- 1.7%) at 4.9% and 14.4% less CPU
+ * in two races; on 16 threads it was within noise (fps -1.1% +- 2.5%, CPU -4.0% +- 2.5%), so 16 stays big.
+ * PS3_SMALL_HOST_CPUS=<n> sets the limit; PS3_AB_WHAT=small alternates the whole policy off and on. */
+int ps3_ab_on(const char* what);
+static int ps3_ab_state(void);
+#ifdef _WIN32
+static int ppu_yield_nap_enabled(void)
+{
+    static int forced = -1; static unsigned set_gen;   /* -1 = not set; the in-game menu can change it */
+    if (set_gen != gt5_settings_gen()) { set_gen = gt5_settings_gen(); const int v = gt5_setting_int("PS3_YIELD_NAP", -1); forced = v < 0 ? -1 : v != 0; }
+    if (forced >= 0) return forced;
+    { /* PS3_AB_WHAT=small: whether the key is listed is worked out once, this runs on every yield */
+      static signed char listed = -1;
+      if (listed < 0) listed = (signed char)(ps3_ab_on("small") >= 0);
+      if (listed) { const int ab = ps3_ab_state(); if (ab >= 0) return ab; } }
+    static int small_max = -1;
+    if (small_max < 0) { const char* e = getenv("PS3_SMALL_HOST_CPUS"); small_max = (e && *e) ? atoi(e) : 12; }
+    static volatile long small_host = -1;
+    static volatile long long checked_ms = 0;
+#ifdef _WIN32
+    const long long now = (long long)GetTickCount64();
+    if (small_host < 0 || now - checked_ms > 1000) {
+        DWORD_PTR pm = 0, sm = 0; int n = 0;
+        if (GetProcessAffinityMask(GetCurrentProcess(), &pm, &sm))
+            for (; pm; pm &= pm - 1) n++;
+        small_host = (n > 0 && n <= small_max) ? 1 : 0;
+        checked_ms = now;
+    }
+#endif
+    return (int)small_host;
+}
+#else
+/* POSIX: the same small-host test as Windows (12 logical CPUs or fewer, PS3_SMALL_HOST_CPUS=<n>,
+ * PS3_AB_WHAT=small), for ps3_host_spin_sleep; the yield nap above stays Windows only. The CPUs
+ * counted are the ones this process may run on (sched_getaffinity on Linux, so taskset counts as
+ * Windows' affinity mask does), checked again every second. It was 8 CPUs here until v0.1.65's
+ * Windows measurements moved the line to 12. */
+static __attribute__((unused)) int ppu_small_host(void)   /* no caller since every host sleeps (17 Nov); kept for its test */
+{
+    { /* PS3_AB_WHAT=small: whether the key is listed is worked out once */
+      static signed char listed = -1;
+      if (listed < 0) listed = (signed char)(ps3_ab_on("small") >= 0);
+      if (listed) { const int ab = ps3_ab_state(); if (ab >= 0) return ab; } }
+    static int small_max = -1;
+    if (small_max < 0) { const char* e = getenv("PS3_SMALL_HOST_CPUS"); small_max = (e && *e) ? atoi(e) : 12; }
+    static volatile long small_host = -1;
+    static volatile long long checked_s = 0;
+    struct timespec ts; clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &ts);
+    if (small_host < 0 || (long long)ts.tv_sec - checked_s >= 1) {
+        long n = 0;
+#if defined(__linux__)
+        cpu_set_t set;
+        CPU_ZERO(&set);
+        if (sched_getaffinity(0, sizeof set, &set) == 0) n = CPU_COUNT(&set);
+#endif
+        if (n <= 0) n = sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN);
+        const long was = small_host;
+        small_host = (n > 0 && n <= small_max) ? 1 : 0;
+        checked_s = (long long)ts.tv_sec;
+        static int logs;
+        if (was != small_host && logs < 4) {
+            logs++;
+            fprintf(stderr, "[ppu] %ld logical CPUs for this process: %s (the line is %d, PS3_SMALL_HOST_CPUS)\n",
+                    n, small_host ? "small, waiting threads sleep" : "big, waiting threads spin", small_max);
+        }
+    }
+    return (int)small_host;
+}
+#endif

+static void ppu_yield_or_nap(void)
+{
+#ifdef _WIN32
+    static __declspec(thread) unsigned run;
+    static __declspec(thread) LONGLONG last;
+    static __declspec(thread) HANDLE timer;
+    static LONGLONG qpf;
+    LARGE_INTEGER t; QueryPerformanceCounter(&t);
+    if (!qpf) { LARGE_INTEGER f; QueryPerformanceFrequency(&f); qpf = f.QuadPart; }
+    run = (last && (t.QuadPart - last) * 20000 < qpf) ? run + 1 : 0;   /* < 50 us since the last yield */
+    last = t.QuadPart;
+    if (run >= 16 && ppu_yield_nap_enabled()) {
+        if (!timer) timer = CreateWaitableTimerExW(NULL, NULL, 0x00000002 /* HIGH_RESOLUTION */, TIMER_ALL_ACCESS);
+        if (timer) {
+            LARGE_INTEGER due; due.QuadPart = -500;   /* 50 us, relative, in 100 ns units */
+            if (SetWaitableTimer(timer, &due, 0, NULL, NULL, FALSE)) { WaitForSingleObject(timer, INFINITE); return; }
+        }
+    }
+    SwitchToThread();
+#else
+    sched_yield();
+#endif
+}

+/* For the runtime's own polling waits (the SPU repeated-DMA back-off): a 50 us timer nap on a small
+ * host, a plain yield elsewhere. */
+void ps3_host_nap_or_yield(void)
+{
+#ifdef _WIN32
+    static __declspec(thread) HANDLE timer;
+    if (ppu_yield_nap_enabled()) {
+        if (!timer) timer = CreateWaitableTimerExW(NULL, NULL, 0x00000002 /* HIGH_RESOLUTION */, TIMER_ALL_ACCESS);
+        if (timer) {
+            LARGE_INTEGER due; due.QuadPart = -500;
+            if (SetWaitableTimer(timer, &due, 0, NULL, NULL, FALSE)) { WaitForSingleObject(timer, INFINITE); return; }
+        }
+    }
+    SwitchToThread();
+#else
+    sched_yield();
+#endif
+}

+/* Host threads that poll for work (the RSX walker parked on a command-buffer word, the D3D12 record
+ * thread between batches) spin, which on a 4-8 thread CPU takes a core from the game threads doing the
+ * work they wait for, and on a laptop spends the shared power budget. ps3_host_spin_sleep() says whether
+ * such a poller should sleep after a short spin: on a small host as above, or PS3_SPIN_SLEEP=0/1.
+ * ps3_host_sleep_on() then waits for `ev` (may be NULL) or `us` microseconds on a high-resolution
+ * timer, whichever comes first, and returns 1 if `ev` fired. */
+/* PS3_AB_PERIOD=<s> (tests): the switches named in PS3_AB_WHAT (default "spin,slot,pace": the pollers'
+ * sleep below, SPURS_SLOT_WAKE, SPURS_PROBE_PACE) are off for <s> seconds, then on, and so on, so one race
+ * measures both under the same load. ps3_ab_frame(), called once a game frame, logs a line per segment:
+ * "[ab] on|off: N game frames in T s, F a second, C cores busy". ps3_ab_on("spin") is -1 when that
+ * switch is not being alternated, else 0 (off) or 1 (on). */
+static double ab_now_s(void)
+{
+#ifdef _WIN32
+    static LARGE_INTEGER f; if (!f.QuadPart) QueryPerformanceFrequency(&f);
+    LARGE_INTEGER c; QueryPerformanceCounter(&c);
+    return (double)c.QuadPart / (double)f.QuadPart;
+#else
+    struct timespec ts; clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &ts);
+    return (double)ts.tv_sec + ts.tv_nsec * 1e-9;
+#endif
+}
+static double s_ab_period = -1.0, s_ab_t0;
+static char s_ab_what[64];
+static int ps3_ab_state(void)
+{
+    if (s_ab_period < 0) {
+        const char* e = getenv("PS3_AB_PERIOD");
+        const char* w = getenv("PS3_AB_WHAT");
+        snprintf(s_ab_what, sizeof s_ab_what, ",%s,", w && *w ? w : "spin,slot,pace");
+        s_ab_period = e ? atof(e) : 0.0;
+    }
+    if (s_ab_period <= 0) return -1;
+    const double now = ab_now_s();
+    if (s_ab_t0 == 0) s_ab_t0 = now;
+    return (int)((long long)((now - s_ab_t0) / s_ab_period) & 1);
+}
+int ps3_ab_on(const char* what)
+{
+    const int st = ps3_ab_state();
+    if (st < 0) return -1;
+    /* Whether `what` is listed, worked out once per name: the SPURS workers ask for about ten names
+     * on every run (24 k runs a second), and a snprintf + strstr each was load on both arms of the very
+     * A/B it serves. Callers pass string literals, so the pointer is the key; a name seen through
+     * another pointer just gets its own slot. */
+    static const char* volatile memo_p[32];
+    static signed char memo_v[32];
+    static volatile long memo_n;
+    const long n = memo_n < 32 ? memo_n : 32;
+    for (long i = 0; i < n; i++)
+        if (__atomic_load_n(&memo_p[i], __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) == what) return memo_v[i] ? st : -1;
+    char key[32]; snprintf(key, sizeof key, ",%s,", what);
+    const int listed = strstr(s_ab_what, key) != NULL;
+    if (__atomic_load_n(&memo_n, __ATOMIC_RELAXED) < 32) {   /* full: overshoots by at most the racing threads */
+        const long slot = __atomic_fetch_add(&memo_n, 1, __ATOMIC_ACQ_REL);
+        if (slot < 32) { memo_v[slot] = (signed char)listed; __atomic_store_n(&memo_p[slot], what, __ATOMIC_RELEASE); }
+    }
+    return listed ? st : -1;
+}
+void ps3_ab_frame(void)
+{
+    const int st = ps3_ab_state();
+    if (st < 0) return;
+    static double seg_t0, cpu0; static unsigned long long frames; static int seg = -1;
+    const double now = ab_now_s();
+    if (st != seg) {
+        double cpu = 0;
+#ifdef _WIN32
+        { FILETIME a, b, k, u; if (GetProcessTimes(GetCurrentProcess(), &a, &b, &k, &u))
+              cpu = ((double)(((unsigned long long)k.dwHighDateTime << 32) | k.dwLowDateTime) +
+                     (double)(((unsigned long long)u.dwHighDateTime << 32) | u.dwLowDateTime)) * 1e-7; }
+#else
+        { struct rusage ru; if (getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF, &ru) == 0)
+              cpu = (double)ru.ru_utime.tv_sec + ru.ru_utime.tv_usec * 1e-6 +
+                    (double)ru.ru_stime.tv_sec + ru.ru_stime.tv_usec * 1e-6; }
+#endif
+        if (seg >= 0 && now > seg_t0)
+            fprintf(stderr, "[ab] %s: %llu game frames in %.2f s, %.2f a second, %.2f cores busy\n",
+                    seg ? "on" : "off", frames, now - seg_t0, frames / (now - seg_t0), (cpu - cpu0) / (now - seg_t0));
+        seg = st; seg_t0 = now; frames = 0; cpu0 = cpu;
+    }
+    frames++;
+}

+int ps3_host_spin_sleep(void)
+{
+#ifdef _WIN32
+    static int forced = -1; static unsigned set_gen;   /* -1 = not set; the in-game menu can change it */
+    if (set_gen != gt5_settings_gen()) { set_gen = gt5_settings_gen(); const int v = gt5_setting_int("PS3_SPIN_SLEEP", -1); forced = v < 0 ? -1 : v != 0; }
+    if (forced >= 0) return forced;
+    { const int ab = ps3_ab_on("spin"); if (ab >= 0) return ab; }
+    static int forced_nap = -2;   /* PS3_YIELD_NAP=1 tests the small-host behaviour on a big one */
+    { static unsigned nap_gen;
+      if (nap_gen != gt5_settings_gen()) { nap_gen = gt5_settings_gen(); const int v = gt5_setting_int("PS3_YIELD_NAP", -1); forced_nap = v < 0 ? -1 : v != 0; } }
+    if (forced_nap >= 0) return forced_nap;
+    /* Every host since 17 Nov 2026, not only small ones. Round 9 left 16+ logical CPUs spinning because the
+     * frame rate was within noise either way; in CPU it is the largest single cost on a big host: the RSX
+     * walker and the record thread kept most of a core each busy doing nothing. Alternated inside one race
+     * on 32 logical CPUs (PS3_AB_WHAT=spin): cores busy -22.2% +-2.8% (3.53 -> 2.96), frame rate +0.7% +-0.3%.
+     * PS3_SPIN_SLEEP=0 spins as before. The yield nap above stays a small-host matter. */
+    return 1;
+#else
+    /* The same switches; PS3_YIELD_NAP only steers this here, the yield nap itself being Windows only. */
+    static int forced = -1; static unsigned set_gen;   /* -1 = not set; the in-game menu can change it */
+    if (set_gen != gt5_settings_gen()) { set_gen = gt5_settings_gen(); const int v = gt5_setting_int("PS3_SPIN_SLEEP", -1); forced = v < 0 ? -1 : v != 0; }
+    if (forced >= 0) return forced;
+    { const int ab = ps3_ab_on("spin"); if (ab >= 0) return ab; }
+    static int forced_nap = -2;
+    { static unsigned nap_gen;
+      if (nap_gen != gt5_settings_gen()) { nap_gen = gt5_settings_gen(); const int v = gt5_setting_int("PS3_YIELD_NAP", -1); forced_nap = v < 0 ? -1 : v != 0; } }
+    if (forced_nap >= 0) return forced_nap;
+    return 1;   /* every host, as on Windows (measured there; PS3_SPIN_SLEEP=0 spins) */
+#endif
+}

+int ps3_host_sleep_on(void* ev, unsigned us)
+{
+#ifdef _WIN32
+    static __declspec(thread) HANDLE timer;
+    if (!timer) timer = CreateWaitableTimerExW(NULL, NULL, 0x00000002 /* HIGH_RESOLUTION */, TIMER_ALL_ACCESS);
+    if (timer) {
+        LARGE_INTEGER due; due.QuadPart = -(LONGLONG)us * 10;   /* relative, 100 ns units */

+/* s_lwc_lock held. The lock goes to the first waiter queued on it: held=1, the caller holds it and lets go
+ * (it passes on without ever being free); held=0, only if it can be taken now. 1 = handed over. */
+static int lwm_grant_locked(struct LwmSlot* sl, int held)
+{
+    LwcWaiter* const w = sl->handoff;
+    if (!w || !(held || lwm_try(sl))) return 0;
+    sl->handoff = w->hnext;
+    w->granted = true;
+    w->cv.notify_one();
+    return 1;

+static int lwm_handoff(struct LwmSlot* sl, int held)
+{

+    return lwm_grant_locked(sl, held);

+/* lwm_release for a caller that holds s_lwc_lock (sys_lwcond_wait giving its lwmutex up). */
+static void lwm_release_locked(struct LwmSlot* sl)

+/* s_lwc_lock held: a signalled waiter queues for its lwmutex, last in line, and the first in line takes it at
+ * once if it is free. The append comes before that try: a holder letting go meanwhile looks at the list again
+ * after its release (lwm_release), so one of the two sides always hands it over. */
+static void lwc_queue_on_lock(LwcWaiter* w)
+{
+    struct LwmSlot* const sl = w->sl;
+    w->hnext = nullptr;
+    if (!sl->handoff) sl->handoff = w;
+    else { LwcWaiter* p = sl->handoff; while (p->hnext) p = p->hnext; p->hnext = w; }
+    lwm_grant_locked(sl, 0);

+static int lwcond_wake(uint32_t lwcond, int all, uint64_t tid)

+ * making all sockets alias one id in the game's tables.
+ *
+ * Each offline socket also remembers the address it was bound to, so
+ * getsockname can give it back. GT5's comm library (func_009D9B10) makes a UDP
+ * socket, binds it to "127.0.0.1:0" and asks getsockname which port it got, to
+ * send itself wake-up datagrams. Datagrams still go nowhere offline (sendto
+ * below), and nothing is ever readable, exactly as before. */
+#define NET_OFF_SOCKS 1024
+struct net_off_sock { uint8_t bound; uint8_t addr[4]; uint16_t port; };
+static net_off_sock      s_off_sock[NET_OFF_SOCKS];
+static std::mutex        s_off_sock_mu;
+static std::atomic<uint32_t> s_off_next_fd{3};
+static uint16_t          s_off_next_port = 49152;   /* BSD's first automatic port */
+static void hle_net_socket(ppu_context* ctx)
+{
+    const uint32_t fd = s_off_next_fd.fetch_add(1);
+    if (fd < NET_OFF_SOCKS) {
+        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(s_off_sock_mu);
+        s_off_sock[fd] = net_off_sock{};
+    }
+    ctx->gpr[3] = fd;
+}
+static int net_off_fd_valid(uint32_t fd) { return fd >= 3 && fd < s_off_next_fd.load(); }
+/* bind(s, addr, len): still answers 0, as the offline model always has; now it
+ * also notes the address, and hands out a port when the caller asked for 0. */
+static void hle_net_bind(ppu_context* ctx)
+{
+    const uint32_t fd = (uint32_t)ctx->gpr[3], ea = (uint32_t)ctx->gpr[4];
+    if (ea && fd < NET_OFF_SOCKS && net_off_fd_valid(fd)) {
+        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(s_off_sock_mu);
+        net_off_sock& k = s_off_sock[fd];
+        if (!k.bound) {
+            const uint8_t* a = vm_base + ea;
+            k.port = (uint16_t)((a[2] << 8) | a[3]);
+            memcpy(k.addr, a + 4, 4);
+            if (!k.port) {
+                k.port = s_off_next_port;
+                s_off_next_port = (uint16_t)(s_off_next_port == 65535 ? 49152 : s_off_next_port + 1);
+            }
+            k.bound = 1;
+        }
+    }
+    ctx->gpr[3] = 0;
+}
+static void hle_net_close(ppu_context* ctx)
+{
+    const uint32_t fd = (uint32_t)ctx->gpr[3];
+    if (fd < NET_OFF_SOCKS) {
+        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(s_off_sock_mu);
+        s_off_sock[fd] = net_off_sock{};
+    }
+    ctx->gpr[3] = 0;

+/* errno lives where _sys_net_errno_loc put it (nowhere yet: nothing to set). */
+static int32_t net_off_fail(int32_t err)
+{

+/* getsockname (sys_net NID 0x13EFE7F5): a BSD sockaddr_in -- length 16,
+ * AF_INET, port, address, eight zero bytes -- and *addrlen = 16. An unbound
+ * socket reads as 0.0.0.0 port 0. Was unregistered: the call answered 0 and
+ * left the caller's struct as it was. */
+static void hle_net_getsockname(ppu_context* ctx)
+{
+    const uint32_t fd = (uint32_t)ctx->gpr[3], ea = (uint32_t)ctx->gpr[4];
+    const uint32_t len_ea = (uint32_t)ctx->gpr[5];
+    if (!net_off_fd_valid(fd)) { ctx->gpr[3] = (uint64_t)(int64_t)net_off_fail(9);  return; } /* EBADF */
+    if (!ea || !len_ea)        { ctx->gpr[3] = (uint64_t)(int64_t)net_off_fail(14); return; } /* EFAULT */
+    net_off_sock k{};
+    if (fd < NET_OFF_SOCKS) { std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(s_off_sock_mu); k = s_off_sock[fd]; }
+    uint8_t* p = vm_base + ea;
+    memset(p, 0, 16);
+    p[0] = 16;
+    p[1] = 2;                              /* AF_INET */
+    p[2] = (uint8_t)(k.port >> 8); p[3] = (uint8_t)k.port;
+    memcpy(p + 4, k.addr, 4);
+    vm_write32(len_ea, 16);
+    ctx->gpr[3] = 0;
+}

+ * the call answered 0, which the game takes as success, and the address stayed

+ * address (dst untouched), -1 with errno for a family other than AF_INET (the

+/* Set by cellGcmSys once a FIFO exists: nonzero while the RSX has not reached put. */
+int (*g_sys_cond_rsx_behind)(void);
+
+/* A real RSX never stops, so a title can guard a frame fence with a long timeout and
+ * treat its expiry as a lost GPU. Ours does stop: it compiles shaders and pipelines
+ * inline, for many seconds on a new scene. GT5 waits 5 s for the RSX to reach the
+ * previous frame, then starts the next frame regardless and rebuilds command blocks
+ * the RSX has yet to run, which deadlocks the RSX and the SPU jobs for good. So a wait
+ * of one to five seconds outlasts its timeout while the RSX is still catching up, within
+ * a bound that a really stuck RSX cannot exceed. SYS_COND_RSX_HOLD=0 turns this off.
+ * Every host: on Linux with a software Vulkan driver (and on phones) a race load ran
+ * past the 5 s and froze with the RSX parked and GT5 spinning on its GPUSyncArray. */
+static int cond_hold_for_rsx(uint32_t id, uint64_t duration, uint64_t elapsed)
+{
+    static int on = -1;
+    if (on < 0) { const char* e = getenv("SYS_COND_RSX_HOLD"); on = !e || atoi(e) != 0; }
+    if (!on || duration < 1000 || duration > 5000 || elapsed >= duration + 120000 ||
+        !g_sys_cond_rsx_behind || !g_sys_cond_rsx_behind())
+        return 0;
+    if (elapsed < duration + 20) {
+        static volatile long logged;
+#ifdef _WIN32
+        if (InterlockedIncrement(&logged) <= 16)
+#else
+        if (__atomic_add_fetch(&logged, 1, __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST) <= 16)
+#endif
+            fprintf(stderr, "[sys_cond] cond %u: held past its %llu ms timeout for the RSX\n",
+                    id, (unsigned long long)duration);
+    }
+    return 1;
+}

+#if defined(__linux__)
+/* The Windows build's vm_commit_veh, for Android: an access to a no-access page inside the guest's
+ * 4 GB -- the guard page vm_stack_allocate() leaves below every guest thread's stack -- makes that
+ * 64 KB block read-write and lets the access run again. On Windows the same handler commits the
+ * block, so a title that runs a little past a small stack (GT5's 24 KB "MtiFn" thread, right after
+ * the first dialog) never noticed; here it was a SIGSEGV that closed the app. Anything else goes
+ * to the handler that was there before (Android's crash reporter). */
+extern "C" uint8_t* vm_base;
+static struct sigaction s_vm_prev_segv, s_vm_prev_bus;
+static void vm_commit_sig(int sig, siginfo_t* si, void* uc)
+{
+    static uintptr_t last_page;
+    const uintptr_t fault = (uintptr_t)si->si_addr, base = (uintptr_t)vm_base;
+    if (vm_base && fault >= base && fault - base < 0x100000000ull) {
+        const uintptr_t page = fault & ~(uintptr_t)0xFFFF;
+        /* The same block again right after opening it: not a protection fault, so not ours. */
+        if (page != __atomic_load_n(&last_page, __ATOMIC_RELAXED) &&
+            mprotect((void*)page, 0x10000, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE) == 0) {
+            __atomic_store_n(&last_page, page, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
+            return;
+        }
+    }
+    const struct sigaction* prev = sig == SIGBUS ? &s_vm_prev_bus : &s_vm_prev_segv;
+    if ((prev->sa_flags & SA_SIGINFO) && prev->sa_sigaction) { prev->sa_sigaction(sig, si, uc); return; }
+    if (!(prev->sa_flags & SA_SIGINFO) && prev->sa_handler != SIG_DFL && prev->sa_handler != SIG_IGN &&
+        prev->sa_handler) { prev->sa_handler(sig); return; }
+    signal(sig, SIG_DFL);
+    raise(sig);
+}
+static void vm_commit_sig_install(void)
+{
+    struct sigaction sa;
+    memset(&sa, 0, sizeof sa);
+    sa.sa_sigaction = vm_commit_sig;
+    sa.sa_flags = SA_SIGINFO | SA_ONSTACK | SA_RESTART;
+    sigemptyset(&sa.sa_mask);
+    sigaction(SIGSEGV, &sa, &s_vm_prev_segv);
+    sigaction(SIGBUS, &sa, &s_vm_prev_bus);
+}

+/* The file name of the module that holds addr ("?" when none does): a crash in a graphics driver,

+{

+extern "C" void cellGcm_frame_counters(unsigned long long*, unsigned long long*);

+static void timed_present(void)
+{
+    /* Nothing new to show. Still present now and then, so a title that only blits can't freeze the window. */
+    { static ULONGLONG last_shown;
+      const ULONGLONG t = GetTickCount64();
+      if (!rsx_live_draw_present_needed() && t - last_shown < 250) return;
+      last_shown = t; }
+    static int stat = -1;
+    if (stat < 0) { const char* fl = getenv("PS3_FRAME_LOG"); stat = getenv("GCM_DRAIN_STAT") || !(fl && *fl == '0'); }
+    if (!stat) { present_guest_frame(); return; }
+    static LARGE_INTEGER f; if (!f.QuadPart) QueryPerformanceFrequency(&f);
+    static long long sum, t_last; static unsigned n;
+    LARGE_INTEGER a, c;
+    QueryPerformanceCounter(&a);
+    /* Time between frames. An average frame rate hides what makes motion look choppy. */
+    static long long prev_frame; static float gaps[4096]; static unsigned n_gaps;
+    if (prev_frame && n_gaps < 4096) gaps[n_gaps++] = (float)(1000.0 * (a.QuadPart - prev_frame) / f.QuadPart);
+    /* LD_FRAME_TRACE=1: 300 frames in a row, every 2000: where each one's time went. */
+    { static int tr = -1; static unsigned fno;
+      if (tr < 0) tr = getenv("LD_FRAME_TRACE") ? 1 : 0;
+      if (tr) {
+          static unsigned long long pw, pq, pd, pf, pfw;
+          unsigned long long w, q, d, fw, fwu;
+          cellGcm_frame_counters(&w, &q);
+          rsx_live_draw_frame_counters(&d, &fw, &fwu);
+          if ((fno++ % 2000) < 300 && n_gaps)
+              fprintf(stderr, "[ft] gap=%.1f walk=%.1f idle=%.1f gpuwait=%.1f draws=%llu fullwaits=%llu\n", gaps[n_gaps - 1],
+                      (w - pw) / 1000.0, (q - pq) / 1000.0, (fwu - pfw) / 1000.0, d - pd, fw - pf);
+          pw = w; pq = q; pd = d; pf = fw; pfw = fwu;
+      } }
+    prev_frame = a.QuadPart;
+    present_guest_frame();
+    QueryPerformanceCounter(&c);
+    sum += c.QuadPart - a.QuadPart; n++;
+    if (!t_last) t_last = c.QuadPart;
+    if (c.QuadPart - t_last >= 5 * f.QuadPart) {
+        fprintf(stderr, "[present] %u presents in 5 s, %.1f ms each, %.0f ms per second\n", n,
+                1000.0 * sum / f.QuadPart / (n ? n : 1), 1000.0 * sum / (c.QuadPart - t_last));
+        if (n_gaps > 4) {
+            qsort(gaps, n_gaps, sizeof gaps[0], [](const void* x, const void* y) -> int {
+                const float p = *(const float*)x, q = *(const float*)y; return p < q ? -1 : p > q; });
+            unsigned b0 = 0, b1 = 0, b2 = 0, b3 = 0, b4 = 0;
+            for (unsigned i = 0; i < n_gaps; i++) {
+                const float g = gaps[i];
+                if (g < 20.f) b0++; else if (g < 37.f) b1++; else if (g < 54.f) b2++; else if (g < 100.f) b3++; else b4++;
+            }
+            fprintf(stderr, "[pacing] ms p50=%.1f p90=%.1f p99=%.1f max=%.1f | <20:%u <37:%u <54:%u <100:%u more:%u\n",
+                    gaps[n_gaps / 2], gaps[n_gaps * 9 / 10], gaps[n_gaps * 99 / 100], gaps[n_gaps - 1], b0, b1, b2, b3, b4);
+        }
+        n_gaps = 0;
+        sum = 0; n = 0; t_last = c.QuadPart;
+    }

+/* [hang] The guest function a host code address is in (function_table, as dump_threads maps stack returns),
+ * or 0 when it is not lifted code or the extent is unknown. */
+static uint32_t hang_guest_func(uintptr_t v, uintptr_t* off)
+{
+    uint32_t bestGuest = 0;
+    uintptr_t bestHost = 0, maxHost = 0;
+    for (uint64_t q = 0; q < function_table_count; q++) {
+        const uintptr_t h = (uintptr_t)function_table[q].func;
+        if (h > maxHost) maxHost = h;
+        if (h <= v && h > bestHost) { bestHost = h; bestGuest = function_table[q].addr; }
+    }
+    if (!bestHost || bestHost == maxHost || v - bestHost > 0x4000u) return 0;
+    *off = v - bestHost;
+    return bestGuest;
+}
+/* [hang] The two threads of the process that used the most CPU over one second (at least a fifth of a core),
+ * and where 32 samples of each one's instruction pointer fell, 10 ms apart: the guest function (lifted code),
+ * else the module. Nothing is printed while a thread is suspended (it may hold the CRT's stream lock). */
+static void hang_busy_threads(HMODULE self, const char* tag)   /* tag: "[HANG]" or "[SLOW]", each line's start */
+{
+    enum { MAXT = 512, NS = 32 };
+    static DWORD tids[MAXT];
+    static ULONGLONG c0[MAXT], c1[MAXT];
+    const DWORD me = GetCurrentThreadId(), pid = GetCurrentProcessId();
+    int n = 0;
+    HANDLE snap = CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(TH32CS_SNAPTHREAD, 0);
+    THREADENTRY32 te; te.dwSize = sizeof te;
+    if (snap != INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE && Thread32First(snap, &te)) {
+        do {
+            if (te.th32OwnerProcessID == pid && te.th32ThreadID != me && n < MAXT) tids[n++] = te.th32ThreadID;
+        } while (Thread32Next(snap, &te));
+    }
+    if (snap != INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) CloseHandle(snap);
+    struct cpu_of { static ULONGLONG get(DWORD tid) {
+        HANDLE h = OpenThread(THREAD_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, FALSE, tid);
+        if (!h) return 0;
+        FILETIME c, e, k, u; ULONGLONG r = 0;
+        if (GetThreadTimes(h, &c, &e, &k, &u))
+            r = (((ULONGLONG)k.dwHighDateTime << 32) | k.dwLowDateTime) + (((ULONGLONG)u.dwHighDateTime << 32) | u.dwLowDateTime);
+        CloseHandle(h);
+        return r; } };
+    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) c0[i] = cpu_of::get(tids[i]);
+    Sleep(1000);
+    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) c1[i] = cpu_of::get(tids[i]);
+    int top[2] = { -1, -1 };
+    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
+        const ULONGLONG d = c1[i] - c0[i];
+        if (top[0] < 0 || d > c1[top[0]] - c0[top[0]]) { top[1] = top[0]; top[0] = i; }
+        else if (top[1] < 0 || d > c1[top[1]] - c0[top[1]]) top[1] = i;
+    }
+    for (int k = 0; k < 2; k++) {
+        if (top[k] < 0) continue;
+        const ULONGLONG d = c1[top[k]] - c0[top[k]];   /* 100 ns units over ~1 s */
+        if (d < 2000000ull) continue;
+        const DWORD tid = tids[top[k]];
+        uintptr_t rip[NS]; int got = 0;
+        HANDLE th = OpenThread(THREAD_GET_CONTEXT | THREAD_SUSPEND_RESUME, FALSE, tid);
+        if (th) {
+            for (int s = 0; s < NS; s++) {
+                if (SuspendThread(th) != (DWORD)-1) {
+                    CONTEXT ctx; ctx.ContextFlags = CONTEXT_CONTROL;
+                    if (GetThreadContext(th, &ctx)) rip[got++] = (uintptr_t)ctx.Rip;
+                    ResumeThread(th);
+                }
+                Sleep(10);
+            }
+            CloseHandle(th);
+        }
+        dbg_printf("%s host thread %lu used %.0f%% of a core; %d samples of where it runs:\n",
+                   tag, (unsigned long)tid, (double)d / 1e5, got);
+        /* by guest function (or module), most samples first */
+        char lab[NS][96]; int cnt[NS]; int nl = 0;
+        for (int s = 0; s < got; s++) {
+            char l[96];
+            HMODULE m = NULL;
+            GetModuleHandleExA(GET_MODULE_HANDLE_EX_FLAG_FROM_ADDRESS | GET_MODULE_HANDLE_EX_FLAG_UNCHANGED_REFCOUNT,
+                               (LPCSTR)rip[s], &m);
+            uintptr_t off = 0;
+            const uint32_t gf = m == self ? hang_guest_func(rip[s], &off) : 0;
+            if (gf) snprintf(l, sizeof l, "func_%08X", gf);
+            else if (m == self) snprintf(l, sizeof l, "gt5.exe rva=0x%llX", (unsigned long long)(rip[s] - (uintptr_t)self));
+            else {
+                char path[MAX_PATH] = "?";
+                if (m) GetModuleFileNameA(m, path, sizeof path);
+                const char* b = strrchr(path, '\\');
+                snprintf(l, sizeof l, "%s", b ? b + 1 : path);
+            }
+            int j = 0;
+            for (; j < nl; j++) if (!strcmp(lab[j], l)) break;
+            if (j == nl) { snprintf(lab[nl], sizeof lab[nl], "%s", l); cnt[nl++] = 0; }
+            cnt[j]++;
+        }
+        for (int shown = 0; shown < 8; shown++) {
+            int b = -1;
+            for (int j = 0; j < nl; j++) if (cnt[j] > 0 && (b < 0 || cnt[j] > cnt[b])) b = j;
+            if (b < 0) break;
+            dbg_printf("%s     %2d  %s\n", tag, cnt[b], lab[b]);
+            cnt[b] = 0;
+        }
+    }
+}

+/* Lanes outside the host float range on the round-toward-zero paths below, redone in double
+ * precision without a branch per lane (spu__x8_*_fixv). Game data has vectors whose last lane is
+ * not a float at all, so those paths can leave the host range on every call; the lane-by-lane
+ * routines above (spu__x8_*_fix) were 3.8% of an SPU worker's time. Each operand is widened to a
+ * double the SPU way, the operation is done once in double precision, and the result is narrowed
+ * the SPU way:
+ *  - widen: biased exponent 0 is +0.0; anything else is the double with the same sign, the same
+ *    power of two and the 23 fraction bits on top, so biased exponent 255 is one more binade
+ *    (cvtps2pd would read it as Inf/NaN). Every nonzero operand is a normal double in
+ *    [2^-126, 2^129).
+ *  - the operation, under MXCSR round toward zero: a sum is truncated at 53 bits; a product of
+ *    two 24-bit significands is exact; x*y + z is the exact product plus z truncated once at 53
+ *    bits (fused or not: the product is exact either way). A nonzero result is a multiple of
+ *    2^-298 below 2^259, a normal double, so flush-to-zero and denormals-are-zero never act, and
+ *    an exact zero sum is +0 in this rounding mode.
+ *  - narrow: the top 24 significand bits are kept. Truncating the exact value v at 53 bits gives
+ *    the largest 53-bit number t with |t| <= |v|; the largest 24-bit number not above |v| is
+ *    itself a 53-bit number, so it is <= |t| <= |v| and in the same binade: truncating t at 24
+ *    bits gives the same number as truncating v at 24 bits. A magnitude from 2^129 up saturates
+ *    to Smax, one below 2^-126 (zero included) is +0.
+ * So a lane computed here is the exact SPU result (what spu__fa_lane / spu__fm_lane /
+ * spu__fma_lane give) whether or not it was in the host range. Only for the round-toward-zero
+ * mode: under round to nearest the 53-bit rounding is not a truncation.
+ * The same code at two widths. When the lanes out of range are all in one half of the vector
+ * (the usual case: the last lane), that half alone is redone, as two doubles in 128-bit
+ * registers, and the other half keeps the host result; otherwise all four lanes are redone as
+ * four doubles. Redoing one half is cheaper on cores that split 256-bit operations in two (Intel
+ * E-cores: about a third less) and costs the same elsewhere.
+ * Arguments, in registers: the operands as the host operation took them (sign changes of

+ * sign of a zero, which the widening drops), the host result (-0 already +0) and its in-range
+ * mask.

+/* The same accesses for lifted code made with spu_lifter.py's register locals (the default):
+ * the local-store base and the two diagnostic gates arrive in the function's own locals, read
+ * once at its entry. spu_ls_read128/write128 reload ctx->ls and the gate words at every access,
+ * because each SPU register write was a store to ctx->gpr[] that might alias them; with the
+ * registers in C locals nothing aliases, and the access is a load, a byte swap and a store. A
+ * diagnostic armed in the middle of a function starts at the next one. */
+#if defined(__clang__) || defined(__GNUC__)
+#  define SPU_LS_INLINE static inline __attribute__((always_inline))
+#else
+#  define SPU_LS_INLINE static __forceinline
+#endif
+SPU_LS_INLINE u128 spu_ls_lq(const spu_context* ctx, const uint8_t* ls, int rdiag, uint32_t lsa)
+{
+    u128 v;
+    if (__builtin_expect(rdiag != 0, 0))
+        spu_ls_read_diag(ctx, lsa);
+    const uint8_t* p = ls + (lsa & (SPU_LS_MASK & ~0xFu));
+#if defined(__ARM_NEON)
+    vst1q_u8(v._u8, vrev32q_u8(vld1q_u8(p)));
+#elif SPU_LS_VEC
+    _mm_storeu_si128((__m128i*)v._u8, spu_ls_bswap_words(_mm_loadu_si128((const __m128i*)p)));
+#else
+    (void)p;
+    v = spu_ls_read128(ctx, lsa);
+#endif
+    return v;

+/* lqd/lqx in a read-modify-write loop (spu_lifter.py, its store forwarding): fa/fv are the
+ * function's most recent quadword store (fa its 16-byte aligned address, 1 when unknown). A load
+ * of that quadword takes the stored value instead of a round trip through the byte-swapped
+ * local store, which the next pass of a loop that stores the quadword it loads waits on. */
+SPU_LS_INLINE u128 spu_ls_lq_fwd(const spu_context* ctx, const uint8_t* ls, int rdiag, uint32_t lsa,
+                                 uint32_t fa, u128 fv)
+{

+        if (__builtin_expect(rdiag != 0, 0))
+            spu_ls_read_diag(ctx, lsa);
+        return fv;
+    }
+    return spu_ls_lq(ctx, ls, rdiag, lsa);

+/* Lifted functions made with register locals (spu_lifter.py, the default) come in two
+ * forms: NAME_sv, the code, and NAME, a thunk that calls it -- the one registered for
+ * dispatch, stored in g_spu_trampoline_fn and called by the runtime. On 64-bit Windows the
+ * code uses the System V convention: the Windows one makes xmm6-xmm15 callee-saved, so every
+ * lifted function that held SPU registers in more than six vector registers saved and
+ * restored up to ten of them, and most lifted functions are a basic block long. Lifted code
+ * calls and tail-calls the _sv forms directly; the thunk saves the registers once, on entry
+ * from the runtime. Elsewhere SPU_SV is empty and NAME_sv is the platform's own convention. */
+#if defined(_WIN64) && (defined(__clang__) || defined(__GNUC__)) && \
+    (defined(__x86_64__) || defined(_M_X64)) && !defined(SPU_NO_SYSV)
+#  define SPU_SV __attribute__((sysv_abi))
+#else
+#  define SPU_SV
+#endif
+/* Keep each thunk a call, not a second copy of the code. */
+#if defined(__clang__) && __clang_major__ >= 15

+#endif
+#ifdef SPU_DIRECT_TAILCALLS
+#define SPU_DIRECT_SV(ctx, PC, FN) do {                                       \

+        if (__builtin_expect(g_spu_direct > 0, 1) && (_dpc & SPU_LS_MASK) &&  \

+            !((ctx)->int_enable && ((ctx)->event_status & (ctx)->event_mask))) \

+/* ---- SPU_WWSPROF: where the Wws job time goes ------------------------------
+ * SPU_WWSPROF=<seconds> (unset or 0 = off): every <seconds>, per Wws workload
+ * and per job image, how many jobs ran, the host time spent inside them, the
+ * bytes they read (GET) and wrote (PUT), and where the writes went: main
+ * memory the RSX cannot read, main memory mapped for the RSX (IO), or RSX
+ * local memory. Per workload also the policy-module runs, the runs that found
+ * no job, the job manager's own time (run time minus job time) and the SPU
+ * interrupts taken.
+ *
+ * Jobs are found where the WWS job manager (marker "WWSJ" at LS 0x15E8, the
+ * `bisl` 0x35240280 at LS 0x327C) calls them: the lifted code brackets that
+ * call as spu_drain_call(ctx, 0x3280). The job's image is the resident code
+ * region its entry pc lies in. A job's time is host TSC around its drain, so it
+ * includes the job's own DMA copies, channel calls and any interrupt taken
+ * inside it: everything the worker did for that job.
+ *
+ * Counters are per host thread; the thread that finds the period over sums
+ * all of them and prints the difference to the last print. Off: one load and
+ * a branch per drain call, per PUT (gcm_note_spu_put) and per GET
+ * (g_spu_get_hook). Self-contained (libc only): unit tests
+ * that link this file need nothing more. */

+    struct timespec ts; timespec_get(&ts, TIME_UTC);   /* C11; the period only needs ms */
+    return (uint64_t)ts.tv_sec * 1000000000ull + (uint64_t)ts.tv_nsec;
+}
+
+int spu_wwsprof_enabled(void)
+{
+    if (g_spu_wwsprof_on < 0) {
+        const char* e = getenv("SPU_WWSPROF");
+        int s = e && *e ? atoi(e) : 0;
+        if (s < 0) s = 0;
+        if (s) {
+            s_wp_tsc0 = wp_tsc(); s_wp_ns0 = wp_ns();
+            s_wp_next_ms = (long long)(s_wp_ns0 / 1000000ull) + 1000ll * s;
+            fprintf(stderr, "[wwsprof] on: Wws jobs by workload and image every %d s "
+                    "(SPU_WWSPROF); times are host time inside the job\n", s);
+        }
+        __atomic_store_n(&g_spu_wwsprof_on, s, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
+    }
+    return g_spu_wwsprof_on;
+}
+
+static wp_thread* wp_self(void)
+{
+    wp_thread* t = t_wp;
+    if (__builtin_expect(t != 0, 1) || t_wp_full) return t;
+    const long i = __atomic_fetch_add(&s_wp_nthreads, 1, __ATOMIC_ACQ_REL);
+    if (i >= WP_THREADS) { t_wp_full = 1; return 0; }
+    t = (wp_thread*)calloc(1, sizeof *t);
+    if (!t) { t_wp_full = 1; return 0; }
+    __atomic_store_n(&s_wp_threads[i], t, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
+    return t_wp = t;
+}
+
+static inline uint32_t wp_be32(const uint8_t* p)
+{
+    return ((uint32_t)p[0] << 24) | ((uint32_t)p[1] << 16) | ((uint32_t)p[2] << 8) | p[3];
+}
+
+/* The WWS job manager this profiler knows: its marker and its job-entry bisl. */
+static int wp_is_wws(const spu_context* ctx)
+{
+    const uint8_t* l = ctx->ls;
+    return ctx->policy_mode && l[0x15E8] == 'W' && l[0x15E9] == 'W' && l[0x15EA] == 'S' &&
+           l[0x15EB] == 'J' && wp_be32(l + 0x327C) == 0x35240280u;
+}
+
+static void wp_close_job(wp_thread* t, uint64_t now)
+{
+    t->cell[t->jw][t->ji].tsc += now - t->jt0;
+    t->jopen = 0; t->jctx = 0;
+}
+
+static void wp_print(uint64_t now_tsc, uint64_t now_ns);
+
+static void wp_maybe_print(void)
+{
+    const uint64_t ns = wp_ns();
+    const long long ms = (long long)(ns / 1000000ull);
+    const long long next = s_wp_next_ms;
+    if (ms < next) return;
+    if (__atomic_exchange_n(&s_wp_printing, 1, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) return;
+    if (s_wp_next_ms == next) {
+        s_wp_next_ms = ms + 1000ll * g_spu_wwsprof_on;
+        wp_print(wp_tsc(), ns);
+    }
+    __atomic_store_n(&s_wp_printing, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
+}
+
+/* spu_drain_call(ctx, 0x3280): the manager is calling a job. */
+void spu_wwsprof_job_enter(spu_context* ctx)
+{
+    if (!wp_is_wws(ctx)) return;
+    wp_thread* t = wp_self();
+    if (!t) return;
+    const uint64_t now = wp_tsc();
+    if (t->jopen) { wp_close_job(t, now); t->unclosed++; }   /* its end was never seen */
+    const uint32_t pc = (uint32_t)ctx->pc & SPU_LS_MASK;
+    int img = 0; uint32_t ea = 0;
+    for (unsigned s = 0; s < 4; s++)
+        if (ctx->resident_code[s].image_id && pc - ctx->resident_code[s].lsa < ctx->resident_code[s].size) {
+            img = ctx->resident_code[s].image_id; ea = ctx->resident_code[s].source_ea; break;
+        }
+    if (!img) img = ctx->resident_ovl;
+    const int ii = (img >= 100 && img < 100 + WP_IMGS - 1) ? img - 100 : WP_IMGS - 1;
+    if (ea && !s_wp_img_ea[ii]) s_wp_img_ea[ii] = ea;
+    const int w = (t->ropen && t->rctx == ctx) ? t->rw : (int)(wp_be32(ctx->ls + 0x1DC) & (WP_WIDS - 1));
+    t->jctx = ctx; t->jdepth = ctx->host_depth; t->jt0 = now; t->jw = w; t->ji = ii; t->jopen = 1;
+    t->cell[w][ii].jobs++;
+    if (t->ropen && t->rctx == ctx) t->rjobs++;
+}
+
+/* The same drain returning: the job has gone back to the manager. */
+void spu_wwsprof_job_leave(spu_context* ctx)
+{
+    wp_thread* t = t_wp;
+    if (!t || !t->jopen || t->jctx != ctx || t->jdepth != ctx->host_depth) return;
+    wp_close_job(t, wp_tsc());
+}
+
+/* spu_run_policy_module, around one run of a policy module. */
+void spu_wwsprof_run_begin(spu_context* ctx, uint32_t wid)
+{
+    if (!wp_is_wws(ctx)) return;
+    wp_thread* t = wp_self();
+    if (!t) return;
+    t->rctx = ctx; t->rt0 = wp_tsc(); t->rjobs = 0; t->rw = (int)(wid & (WP_WIDS - 1)); t->ropen = 1;
+}
+
+void spu_wwsprof_run_end(spu_context* ctx)
+{
+    wp_thread* t = t_wp;
+    if (!t || !t->ropen || t->rctx != ctx) return;
+    const uint64_t now = wp_tsc();
+    if (t->jopen && t->jctx == ctx) { wp_close_job(t, now); t->unclosed++; }
+    wp_wcell* w = &t->w[t->rw];
+    w->runs++;
+    if (!t->rjobs) w->empty++;
+    w->run_tsc += now - t->rt0;
+    t->ropen = 0; t->rctx = 0;
+    wp_maybe_print();
+}
+
+/* spu_take_interrupt: an interrupt was taken on this context. */
+void spu_wwsprof_irq(const spu_context* ctx)
+{
+    wp_thread* t = t_wp;
+    if (!t || !t->ropen || t->rctx != ctx) return;
+    t->w[t->rw].irqs++;
+    if (t->jopen && t->jctx == ctx) t->w[t->rw].irqs_in_job++;
+}
+
+/* Every GET (spu_overlay_note_get through g_spu_get_hook) and every PUT
+ * (gcm_note_spu_put): cls 0 main memory the RSX cannot read, 1 IO-mapped
+ * main memory, 2 RSX local memory. Charged to the thread's open job, else to
+ * its open run's manager. */
+void spu_wwsprof_get(uint32_t size)
+{
+    wp_thread* t = t_wp;
+    if (!t) return;
+    if (t->jopen) t->cell[t->jw][t->ji].get += size;
+    else if (t->ropen) t->w[t->rw].mgr_get += size;
+}
+
+void spu_wwsprof_put(uint32_t size, int cls)
+{
+    wp_thread* t = t_wp;
+    if (!t) return;
+    if (t->jopen) {
+        wp_cell* c = &t->cell[t->jw][t->ji];
+        if (cls == 2) c->put_local += size; else if (cls == 1) c->put_io += size; else c->put_main += size;
+    } else if (t->ropen) t->w[t->rw].mgr_put += size;
+}
+
+/* ---- printing ---- */
+typedef struct { wp_cell cell[WP_WIDS][WP_IMGS]; wp_wcell w[WP_WIDS]; uint64_t unclosed; } wp_sum;
+static wp_sum s_wp_prev;
+static uint64_t s_wp_prev_tsc, s_wp_prev_ns;
+
+static void wp_print(uint64_t now_tsc, uint64_t now_ns)
+{
+    static wp_sum cur;      /* only the printing thread is here */
+    memset(&cur, 0, sizeof cur);
+    const long n = s_wp_nthreads < WP_THREADS ? s_wp_nthreads : WP_THREADS;
+    for (long i = 0; i < n; i++) {
+        const wp_thread* t = __atomic_load_n(&s_wp_threads[i], __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
+        if (!t) continue;
+        for (int w = 0; w < WP_WIDS; w++) {
+            for (int k = 0; k < WP_IMGS; k++) {
+                const wp_cell* a = &t->cell[w][k]; wp_cell* b = &cur.cell[w][k];
+                b->jobs += a->jobs; b->tsc += a->tsc; b->get += a->get;
+                b->put_main += a->put_main; b->put_io += a->put_io; b->put_local += a->put_local;
+            }
+            const wp_wcell* a = &t->w[w]; wp_wcell* b = &cur.w[w];
+            b->runs += a->runs; b->empty += a->empty; b->run_tsc += a->run_tsc; b->irqs += a->irqs;
+            b->irqs_in_job += a->irqs_in_job; b->mgr_get += a->mgr_get; b->mgr_put += a->mgr_put;
+        }
+        cur.unclosed += t->unclosed;
+    }
+    const uint64_t n0 = s_wp_prev_ns ? s_wp_prev_ns : s_wp_ns0;
+    const double secs = (double)(now_ns - n0) * 1e-9;
+    /* TSC ticks per ms, from the whole time the profiler has been on. */
+    const double tpms = (now_ns > s_wp_ns0 && now_tsc > s_wp_tsc0)
+                      ? (double)(now_tsc - s_wp_tsc0) / ((double)(now_ns - s_wp_ns0) * 1e-6) : 1e6;
+    /* The window's rows, biggest job time first. */
+    struct { int w, k; double ms; } rows[WP_WIDS * WP_IMGS];
+    int nr = 0;
+    uint64_t runs = 0, empty = 0, jobs = 0, irqs = 0; double jms = 0, rms = 0;
+    for (int w = 0; w < WP_WIDS; w++) {
+        const wp_wcell* a = &cur.w[w]; const wp_wcell* p = &s_wp_prev.w[w];
+        runs += a->runs - p->runs; empty += a->empty - p->empty; irqs += a->irqs - p->irqs;
+        rms += (double)(a->run_tsc - p->run_tsc) / tpms;
+        for (int k = 0; k < WP_IMGS; k++) {
+            const wp_cell* c = &cur.cell[w][k]; const wp_cell* q = &s_wp_prev.cell[w][k];
+            if (c->jobs == q->jobs && c->tsc == q->tsc) continue;
+            const double ms = (double)(c->tsc - q->tsc) / tpms;
+            jobs += c->jobs - q->jobs; jms += ms;
+            rows[nr].w = w; rows[nr].k = k; rows[nr].ms = ms; nr++;
+        }
+    }
+    for (int i = 1; i < nr; i++)            /* insertion sort, descending */
+        for (int j = i; j > 0 && rows[j].ms > rows[j - 1].ms; j--) {
+            const int tw = rows[j].w, tk = rows[j].k; const double tm = rows[j].ms;
+            rows[j] = rows[j - 1]; rows[j - 1].w = tw; rows[j - 1].k = tk; rows[j - 1].ms = tm;
+        }
+    fprintf(stderr, "[wwsprof] %.2f s: runs %llu (empty %llu), jobs %llu, in jobs %.1f ms, manager %.1f ms, "
+            "interrupts %llu, unclosed %llu\n", secs, (unsigned long long)runs, (unsigned long long)empty,
+            (unsigned long long)jobs, jms, rms - jms, (unsigned long long)irqs,
+            (unsigned long long)(cur.unclosed - s_wp_prev.unclosed));
+    for (int w = 0; w < WP_WIDS; w++) {
+        const wp_wcell* a = &cur.w[w]; const wp_wcell* p = &s_wp_prev.w[w];
+        if (a->runs == p->runs) continue;
+        uint64_t wj = 0; double wms = 0;
+        for (int k = 0; k < WP_IMGS; k++) {
+            wj += cur.cell[w][k].jobs - s_wp_prev.cell[w][k].jobs;
+            wms += (double)(cur.cell[w][k].tsc - s_wp_prev.cell[w][k].tsc) / tpms;
+        }
+        const double run_ms = (double)(a->run_tsc - p->run_tsc) / tpms;
+        fprintf(stderr, "[wwsprof] wid %d: runs %llu (empty %llu), jobs %llu, in jobs %.1f ms, manager %.1f ms, "
+                "interrupts %llu (%llu in jobs), manager get %.2f MB put %.2f MB\n", w,
+                (unsigned long long)(a->runs - p->runs), (unsigned long long)(a->empty - p->empty),
+                (unsigned long long)wj, wms, run_ms - wms, (unsigned long long)(a->irqs - p->irqs),
+                (unsigned long long)(a->irqs_in_job - p->irqs_in_job),
+                (double)(a->mgr_get - p->mgr_get) / 1e6, (double)(a->mgr_put - p->mgr_put) / 1e6);
+    }
+    for (int i = 0; i < nr; i++) {
+        const int w = rows[i].w, k = rows[i].k;
+        const wp_cell* c = &cur.cell[w][k]; const wp_cell* q = &s_wp_prev.cell[w][k];
+        const uint64_t nj = c->jobs - q->jobs;
+        char name[16];
+        if (k == WP_IMGS - 1) snprintf(name, sizeof name, "other");
+        else if (s_wp_img_ea[k]) snprintf(name, sizeof name, "w%08X", (unsigned)s_wp_img_ea[k]);
+        else snprintf(name, sizeof name, "image%d", 100 + k);
+        fprintf(stderr, "[wwsprof] wid %d %s: jobs %llu, %.2f ms (%.1f us a job), get %.2f MB, "
+                "put %.2f MB main + %.2f MB rsx-io + %.2f MB rsx-local\n", w, name,
+                (unsigned long long)nj, rows[i].ms, nj ? rows[i].ms * 1000.0 / (double)nj : 0.0,
+                (double)(c->get - q->get) / 1e6, (double)(c->put_main - q->put_main) / 1e6,
+                (double)(c->put_io - q->put_io) / 1e6, (double)(c->put_local - q->put_local) / 1e6);
+    }
+    memcpy(&s_wp_prev, &cur, sizeof cur);
+    s_wp_prev_tsc = now_tsc; s_wp_prev_ns = now_ns;
+}
