 static ld_state g;
 
+/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ * Internal resolution scale
+ *
+ * LD_RES_SCALE=<s> (or LD_RES_TARGET=<lines>, s = lines / the video mode's height) draws the game's
+ * screen-sized targets at s times their guest size while every guest-side number (clip, viewport,
+ * scissor, texture sizes, memory offsets, readbacks) stays what the game set. It is the antialias
+ * sample grid's mechanism taken one step further: a surface already could be larger than its pixel
+ * size (clip x aa grid); now its D3D12 texture can be larger than that again, by surface_t.rs.
+ *
+ *   - which surfaces: ld_rs_pick (screen-sized ones only; shadow maps, cube faces, the bloom and
+ *     particle targets stay at guest size);
+ *   - viewport / scissor / WPOS of a draw follow its colour target's rs (sink_end_impl, get_pso);
+ *   - the zeta a scaled target draws with is an entry of its own at that scale (zdepth_get);
+ *   - copies between surfaces of different scale, readbacks into guest memory and the final copy to
+ *     the window go through one filtering draw (ld_rs_draw);
+ *   - ld_set_res_scale changes it while running: applied at the next flip (ld_rs_apply).
+ *
+ * With no scale asked for, g_rs_on is 0, every rs is exactly 1.0f, ld_hs / ld_he return their
+ * argument, the float products are x * 1.0f, and none of the new branches is taken.
+ * -----------------------------------------------------------------------*/
+#define LD_RS_MAX_DIM     16384u                    /* D3D12's 2D texture limit */
+#define LD_RS_MAX_TEXELS  (7680ull * 4320ull)       /* one texture: no more than an 8K frame */
+#define LD_RS_MIN_SCALE   0.25f
+#define LD_RS_MAX_SCALE   8.0f
+#define LD_RS_LOC_SCRATCH 0xFFFFFFF0u               /* surface_t.location of the renderer's own targets */
+#define LD_RS_LOC_DEAD    0xFFFFFFFFu               /* a hidden surface or a released zeta entry */
+
+static float g_rs_user = 1.0f;            /* the scale in force */
+static int   g_rs_on;                     /* g_rs_user != 1.0f */
+static volatile LONG g_rs_request;        /* ld_set_res_scale: float bits for the next flip, 0 = none */
+static int   g_rs_aa_mul;                 /* LD_RES_AA=1: the scale multiplies the 2x2 sample grid too */
+static u32   g_rs_min_w, g_rs_min_h;      /* LD_RES_MIN=<w>x<h>: smallest guest pixel size that is scaled */
+static float g_rs_draw = 1.0f;            /* the scale of the colour target of the draw being set up */
+static u32   g_rs_dead_zetas;             /* zeta entries released by a scale change, free for reuse */
+static u32   g_rs_out_w, g_rs_out_h;      /* LD_RES_OUT=<w>x<h>: the back buffer size, instead of the window's */
+static u32   g_rs_cycle_ms;               /* LD_RES_CYCLE=<seconds>: tests, see ld_rs_flip */
+static float g_rs_cycle_scale = 2.0f;
+static void  ld_rs_out_size(u32* w, u32* h);
+/* [up] The 3D scene at a scale of its own, for a temporal upscaler that draws it smaller than it is
+ * shown (LD_AA=dlss_q / dlss_b / dlss_p; see the [up] blocks): while g_rs_scene_on, the surface at
+ * this address and guest size is made at g_rs_scene_rs whatever ld_rs_pick says, and passes into it
+ * with the clip cw x ch run at that scale. g_rs_on is then 1 even with no scale asked for: every
+ * other surface still gets exactly what it got. Never on unless such a mode is selected. */
+static int   g_rs_scene_on;
+static float g_rs_scene_rs = 1.0f;
+static u32   g_rs_scene_loc, g_rs_scene_off, g_rs_scene_w, g_rs_scene_h, g_rs_scene_cw, g_rs_scene_ch;
+/* [shadow2] Shadow maps at a higher resolution than the PS3's (the "Shadows" setting, LD_SHADOWS; the
+ * [shadow2] block before zdepth_get has the rule and the rest). While g_sm_on, the passes into a shadow
+ * map found by that rule run at its scale (2 or 4) whatever their colour target's is, and g_rs_on is 1
+ * as with the upscaler's scene scale: every other surface and zeta still gets exactly what it got. */
+static int   g_sm_on;                     /* an identified map is drawn at a scale above 1 */
+static int   g_sm_soft;                   /* ... and read through the soft filter */
+static float ld_sm_pass_scale(const rsx_dsp_surface* sf);   /* 0 = not a pass into a scaled shadow map */
+#define LD_RS_ON_NOW() (g_rs_user != 1.0f || g_rs_scene_on || g_sm_on)
+/* [aa3d] Who set the scene's own scale: 1 the upscaler, 2 LD_RES_SCENE (below), 0 nobody.
+ * LD_RES_SCENE (default 1; 0 = today's): with a resolution scale above 1 and no upscaler running, the
+ * 3D picture of the last 3D frame is drawn at the scale that makes it as sharp as the rectangle of the
+ * window it is copied into, when ld_rs_pick would leave it smaller (it goes by size and leaves small
+ * targets alone). GT5's Photo Mode and Photo Travel draw their 3D view as a small window (542x361 in
+ * 720p mode, 542x541 / 643x542 in 1080p mode) that today stays at guest size under any scale. Races and
+ * car select get exactly what ld_rs_pick gives them already (the two agree there). */
+static int   g_rs_scene_owner;
+static int   g_rs_scene_follow = 1;
+
+/* Guest size -> host size of a surface dimension at scale rs. */
+static u32 ld_hs(u32 v, float rs)
+{
+    if (rs == 1.0f) return v;
+    const u32 r = (u32)((float)v * rs + 0.5f);
+    return r ? r : (v ? 1u : 0u);
+}
+/* Guest edge -> host edge (the same rounding for every edge, so neighbouring rects still meet). */
+static LONG ld_he(LONG v, float rs)
+{
+    if (rs == 1.0f) return v;
+    return v <= 0 ? v : (LONG)((float)v * rs + 0.5f);
+}
+static float ld_rs_clamp(float s)
+{
+    if (!(s > 0.0f)) return 1.0f;                    /* 0, negative, NaN */
+    if (s < LD_RS_MIN_SCALE) s = LD_RS_MIN_SCALE;
+    if (s > LD_RS_MAX_SCALE) s = LD_RS_MAX_SCALE;
+    if (s > 0.999f && s < 1.001f) s = 1.0f;
+    return s;
+}
+/* The scale a NEW surface of guest size w x h is made at; aa_sx x aa_sy is its sample grid.
+ *
+ * Scaled: a target at least four fifths as tall as the video mode and at least half as wide, counted
+ * in pixels (GT5: the display buffers, the antialiased scene, the 2048-wide post-processing targets
+ * that hold the full-size picture). Not the mode's full size: GT5 draws its 3D view inside the
+ * display margin, 1728x972 of 1920x1080 (as 1152x972 with a 2x1 grid in a race) and 1152x648 of
+ * 1280x720, and a threshold of the full height left exactly the scene at guest size. Not scaled:
+ * anything smaller (bloom and blur chains at half size and below, particle buffers, the mirror,
+ * exposure strips, thumbnails, text strips), and anything whose width and height are both powers of
+ * two (shadow maps such as GT5's 1024x2048, cube faces, lookup tables), and the renderer's own scratch
+ * targets. LD_RES_MIN=<w>x<h> sets the threshold.
+ *
+ * A 2x2 antialiased target already holds 2x the pixels each way, so by default the scale counts from
+ * pixels there: at 2x such a target keeps its size and it is the resolve target that grows
+ * (LD_RES_AA=1: multiply the sample grid as well, i.e. supersample). A 2x1 grid is multiplied as is.
+ *
+ * No texture is made wider or taller than LD_RS_MAX_DIM or larger than LD_RS_MAX_TEXELS: a surface
+ * that would be gets the largest scale that fits. */
+static float ld_rs_pick(u32 location, u32 w, u32 h, u32 aa_sx, u32 aa_sy)
+{
+    if (!g_rs_on || location >= LD_RS_LOC_SCRATCH || !w || !h) return 1.0f;
+    if (!aa_sx) aa_sx = 1u;
+    if (!aa_sy) aa_sy = 1u;
+    const u32 pw = w / aa_sx, ph = h / aa_sy;
+    const u32 min_w = g_rs_min_w ? g_rs_min_w : g.width / 2u;
+    const u32 min_h = g_rs_min_h ? g_rs_min_h : g.height * 4u / 5u;
+    if (pw < min_w || ph < min_h) return 1.0f;
+    if (!(pw & (pw - 1u)) && !(ph & (ph - 1u))) return 1.0f;
+    float rs = g_rs_user;
+    if (rs > 1.0f && !g_rs_aa_mul && aa_sx > 1u && aa_sy > 1u) {
+        rs /= (float)(aa_sx < aa_sy ? aa_sx : aa_sy);
+        if (rs < 1.0f) rs = 1.0f;
+    }
+    const float side = (float)LD_RS_MAX_DIM / (float)(w > h ? w : h);
+    if (rs > side) rs = side;
+    const float texels = (float)w * (float)h;
+    if (rs * rs * texels > (float)LD_RS_MAX_TEXELS) rs = sqrtf((float)LD_RS_MAX_TEXELS / texels);
+    if (g_rs_user > 1.0f && rs < 1.0f) rs = 1.0f;    /* the limits never shrink a surface */
+    if (rs > 0.999f && rs < 1.001f) rs = 1.0f;
+    return rs;
+}
+/* The same for a surface at a given address. Two test switches, to find which target an artefact
+ * comes from: LD_RES_SKIP=<hex offset>[,<hex offset>...] keeps the surfaces at those offsets at guest
+ * size, LD_RES_ONLY=<...> keeps every surface but those (both lists empty normally). */
+static u32 g_rs_skip[16], g_rs_n_skip, g_rs_only[16], g_rs_n_only;
+static float ld_rs_pick_at(u32 location, u32 offset, u32 w, u32 h, u32 aa_sx, u32 aa_sy)
+{
+    if (!g_rs_on) return 1.0f;
+    if (g_rs_scene_on && location == g_rs_scene_loc && offset == g_rs_scene_off && w == g_rs_scene_w && h == g_rs_scene_h)
+        return g_rs_scene_rs;                          /* [up] the upscaler's render size */
+    for (u32 i = 0; i < g_rs_n_skip; i++)
+        if (g_rs_skip[i] == offset) return 1.0f;
+    if (g_rs_n_only) {
+        u32 i = 0;
+        while (i < g_rs_n_only && g_rs_only[i] != offset) i++;
+        if (i == g_rs_n_only) return 1.0f;
+    }
+    return ld_rs_pick(location, w, h, aa_sx, aa_sy);
+}
+/* The scale a draw or a clear runs at (its viewport, scissor and zeta entry): its colour target's,
+ * with one exception. A pass that writes no colour is not sized by the surface its colour registers
+ * happen to name: GT5 leaves an address of the display or post-processing buffers there for shadow
+ * maps and other depth- or stencil-only passes (the glyph polygons of a text it composes off screen),
+ * whose clips fit inside that scaled surface, and taking the surface's scale put such a pass's depth
+ * or stencil in a zeta entry of its own, apart from the passes at guest size the game shares that
+ * buffer with. Such a pass keeps the target's scale only when it looks like part of a scaled picture:
+ * its clip is a size ld_rs_pick scales, and its zeta is one scaled passes draw with: it has an entry
+ * at that scale that a pass writing colour used (a depth pre-pass or the glyphs of on-screen text,
+ * under the scene's or the display's zeta), or it has no entry at guest size yet (the first clear of
+ * a scene). Otherwise it runs at guest size. LD_RES_DEPTH_RULE=0: always the target's scale. */
+static int g_rs_depth_rule = 1, g_rs_zsync = 1;
+static float ld_rs_pass(const rsx_dsp_surface* sf, float target_rs, int writes_colour)
+{
+    /* [shadow2] a pass into an identified shadow map (no colour written): that map's scale */
+    if (g_sm_on && !writes_colour) { const float sm = ld_sm_pass_scale(sf); if (sm > 0.0f) return sm; }
+    if (target_rs == 1.0f || writes_colour || !g_rs_depth_rule) return target_rs;
+    /* [up] A depth-only pass of the upscaled scene (its depth pre-pass) runs where the scene's colour
+     * draws run: its clip is not a size ld_rs_pick scales when no scale was asked for. */
+    if (g_rs_scene_on && sf->color_location[0] == g_rs_scene_loc && sf->color_offset[0] == g_rs_scene_off &&
+        sf->clip_w == g_rs_scene_cw && sf->clip_h == g_rs_scene_ch) return target_rs;
+    if (ld_rs_pick(sf->color_location[0], sf->clip_w ? sf->clip_w : g.width,
+                   sf->clip_h ? sf->clip_h : g.height, sf->aa_sx, sf->aa_sy) == 1.0f) return 1.0f;
+    int at_guest_size = 0;
+    for (u32 i = 0; i < g.n_zdepths; i++) {
+        const zdepth_t* z = &g.zdepths[i];
+        if (!z->tex || z->location != sf->zeta_location || z->offset != sf->zeta_offset) continue;
+        if (z->rs == target_rs && z->with_colour) return target_rs;
+        if (z->rs == 1.0f) at_guest_size = 1;
+    }
+    return at_guest_size ? 1.0f : target_rs;
+}
+static u32 ld_rs_parse_offsets(const char* e, u32* out, u32 cap)
+{
+    u32 n = 0;
+    while (e && *e && n < cap) {
+        char* end = NULL;
+        const unsigned long v = strtoul(e, &end, 16);
+        if (end == e) break;
+        out[n++] = (u32)v;
+        e = end;
+        while (*e == ',' || *e == ' ' || *e == ';') e++;
+    }
+    return n;
+}
+
+/* ---- [scene] begin ------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ * The 3D scene, the HUD, and the line between them; dumps of the scene; camera jitter.
+ * (State and the per-draw test here; the rest is in the second [scene] block, after
+ * ld_dump_surface_ppm.)
+ *
+ * A temporal upscaler (DLSS, FSR 2/3) works on the finished 3D picture before any HUD is drawn
+ * over it, needs that picture's depth, and needs the camera moved by a different fraction of a
+ * pixel every frame. GT5 draws its 3D view into a target of its own and then copies it, with
+ * bloom, into the display buffer, where the HUD follows. That copy is the line:
+ *
+ *   the boundary = the first draw of a frame that writes colour into a registered display buffer,
+ *   if it has depth test and blending off and its fragment program samples a colour surface that
+ *   was drawn into with depth testing earlier in the same frame, with the zeta those draws used
+ *   still bound. That surface is the scene, that zeta its depth.
+ *   [aa3d] That is LD_SCENE_RULE=0. By default (rule 1, g_scn_rule) the boundary is the first
+ *   display draw of the frame that is such a copy, whatever 2D was drawn into the display buffer
+ *   before it, and a surface new to the role needs draws with depth write in perspective: every 3D
+ *   screen, not only races.
+ *
+ * A frame is judged when it ends (ld_scn_frame_end, at the first draw or clear after a flip):
+ *   scene    the boundary was found;
+ *   held     the display buffer's first draw samples the scene of an earlier frame, which was not
+ *            drawn again (a still picture under a menu): the scene stays remembered;
+ *   bypass   anything else: 2D menus, a frame that draws HUD first (GT5's Photo Mode), movies.
+ * The scene of the last "scene" frame is remembered by address and guest size (s_scn.sig), so the
+ * draws of the NEXT frame can be recognised as scene draws while they happen; the frame after a
+ * bypass frame has no scene until its own boundary is found.
+ *
+ * None of this runs, and nothing is logged, unless one of these is set:
+ *   LD_SCENE_LOG=1            only the "[scene]" line, printed whenever the judgement changes
+ *   LD_SCENE_DUMP=<dir>       at the boundary write the scene's colour (PPM), its depth (raw
+ *                             float32 and a small PGM), the display buffer right after the
+ *                             boundary draw (PPM) and a text file with the sizes, for
+ *                             LD_SCENE_DUMP_FRAMES=<n> scene frames (2) from present number
+ *                             LD_SCENE_DUMP_AT=<n> on, or from when the file
+ *                             LD_SCENE_DUMP_FILE=<path> appears (again each time it reappears);
+ *                             with neither, the first scene frames
+ *   LD_SCENE_CONSTS=<file>    for the same frames, one CSV row per draw into the scene: state,
+ *                             viewport, the transform the vertex shader gets, c[0..7], c[467]
+ *   LD_JITTER=<n>             (a setting: followed live) move the perspective scene draws by a
+ *                             Halton(2,3) offset of n phases, within +-0.5 host pixel of the scene
+ *                             target. Without an upscaler this only makes the picture shimmer.
+ *   LD_JITTER_RULE=<0|1|2>    which scene draws count as perspective, see ld_jit_moves
+ *   LD_JITTER_TEST=<1|2>      a capture (needs LD_SCENE_DUMP) of six scene frames: no offset, the
+ *                             four quarter-pixel offsets of a 2x2 grid, no offset. 1: first one
+ *                             frame at resolution scale 1, then the six at 0.5, then the scale is
+ *                             put back; 2: the six at the scale in force.
+ *                             dlss2\tools\jitter_check.py puts the four together and compares.
+ * ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ */
+enum { LD_SCN_NONE = 0, LD_SCN_SCENE, LD_SCN_HELD, LD_SCN_BYPASS };
+enum { LD_SCN_R_NONE = 0,
+       LD_SCN_R_NO_DISPLAY,   /* no colour draw into a display buffer */
+       LD_SCN_R_NOT_A_COPY,   /* the first one is blended or depth-tested: 2D, or HUD first */
+       LD_SCN_R_NO_SCENE,     /* it samples no surface drawn with depth this frame */
+       LD_SCN_R_ZETA,         /* it does, but another zeta is bound */
+       LD_SCN_R_HELD };       /* it samples the remembered scene, which was not drawn this frame */
+/* loc, off, w, h: the surface (guest size); cw, ch: the clip the scene's draws use, which is what NDC
+ * spans. The two differ when a draw's clip fits inside a larger surface at the same address (GT5 at
+ * 1080p: a clip of 2304x972 in a 2560x972 surface), and other passes may draw into that surface too. */
+typedef struct { u32 loc, off, w, h, zloc, zoff, cw, ch; u8 ax, ay; } ld_scn_sig;
+static struct {
+    int on;                              /* something asked for it: the per-draw bookkeeping runs */
+    u32 frame;                           /* game frames counted here (ld_scn_frame_end) */
+    u32 present_no;                      /* g_ld_frames when the frame being drawn started */
+    /* the frame being drawn */
+    u32 draws;                           /* draws recorded so far */
+    u32 scene_draws;                     /* of them, into the remembered scene */
+    u32 depth_frame[MAX_SURFACES];       /* frame + 1 of the last depth-tested draw into a surface */
+    u32 depth_draws[MAX_SURFACES];       /* how many, that frame */
+    u32 depth_zslot[MAX_SURFACES];       /* the zeta entry they used (zdepth_get's slot) ... */
+    u32 depth_zloc[MAX_SURFACES], depth_zoff[MAX_SURFACES];   /* ... and its guest address */
+    u32 depth_cw[MAX_SURFACES], depth_ch[MAX_SURFACES];       /* the clip of the last such draw */
+    int disp_seen;                       /* a colour draw into a display buffer has been seen */
+    int held_seen;                       /* [aa3d] rule 1: a display draw read the remembered scene, not drawn again */
+    u32 depth3d[MAX_SURFACES];           /* [aa3d] of a surface's depth-tested draws this frame: those writing depth
+                                          * and colour with a perspective projection (c[3].xyz not zero) */
+    int probe_best;                      /* the candidate draw's sampled surface with most depth draws, or -1 */
+    int probe_stale;                     /* it samples the remembered scene, not drawn this frame */
+    int found, reason;                   /* the boundary was found; else why not (LD_SCN_R_*) */
+    u32 b_draw;                          /* the boundary draw's number in the frame */
+    u32 b_scene, b_display, b_zslot;     /* surface indices and the zeta slot, as of that draw */
+    u32 b_depth_draws;
+    ld_scn_sig b_sig;                    /* the scene of this frame */
+    float b_rs, b_disp_rs;               /* resolution scale of the scene and of the display buffer */
+    u32 b_vp[4];                         /* the boundary draw's guest viewport: where the 3D picture goes */
+    u32 b_disp_loc, b_disp_off;
+    /* projection of the first perspective scene draw at the full viewport, for the dump's estimates */
+    int proj_have; float proj_c[3][4]; float proj_sz, proj_tz;
+    /* remembered from the frames before */
+    int kind;                            /* LD_SCN_*: the last frame that drew anything */
+    int sig_valid; ld_scn_sig sig; float sig_rs;
+} s_scn;
+static struct {
+    int   phases;                        /* LD_JITTER: 0 = off, else the sequence's length */
+    int   rule;                          /* LD_JITTER_RULE */
+    int   on;                            /* the scene draws of the frame being drawn are moved ... */
+    float x, y;                          /* ... by this, in host pixels of the scene target (x right, y down) */
+    u32   index, phase;                  /* frames jittered so far; this frame's place in the sequence */
+    int   used;                          /* a draw of this frame was moved */
+} s_jit;
+/* The capture the dump switches ask for: a list of steps walked one per scene frame. */
+enum { LD_CAP_FRAME = 1, LD_CAP_SCALE, LD_CAP_SETTLE };
+typedef struct { u8 kind; signed char jit; char tag[6]; float scale; u32 frames; } ld_cap_step;
+static struct {
+    const char* dir; const char* consts_path; const char* trigger;
+    long at; u32 frames; int test;
+    FILE* consts;
+    ld_cap_step steps[24]; u32 n_steps, step;
+    int running;                         /* a capture is walking its steps */
+    int active;                          /* the frame being drawn is one to capture */
+    int pending;                         /* its boundary was found: the dump runs before the next draw */
+    int trigger_seen, at_done;
+    u32 tries, seq;
+    float user_scale; int scale_changed;
+} s_cap;
+
+/* [aa3d] Which draw is the line between the 3D picture and what is drawn over it (LD_SCENE_RULE):
+ *   1 (default)  any 3D screen: the first draw of the frame into a display buffer that writes colour,
+ *                has no depth test, and reads (as a texture its fragment program samples, not a cube)
+ *                a surface drawn into this frame with depth test and depth write in perspective, that
+ *                surface's zeta still bound. Display draws before it are allowed: GT5 puts a 2D quad
+ *                there first on its 3D menu screens (Arcade car select: hl3 1616, lc2 8701; Photo
+ *                Mode and Photo Travel: ph1, ph2, pm1, pr1, pr2, pz1), which today's rule took for "2D".
+ *                The copy may be blended (none seen so far: every copy in 39 captures is opaque).
+ *                A race is judged exactly as before: its copy is the first display draw.
+ *   0            today's: the frame's FIRST colour draw into a display buffer has to be that copy. */
+static int g_scn_rule = 1;
+static void ld_scn_frame_end(void);
+static void ld_scn_pending_run(void);
+static int  ld_scn_draw_begin(u32 target, const rsx_dsp_surface* sf, int writes_colour, u32 zslot);
+static void ld_scn_probe_end(const rsx_dsp_surface* sf, const rsx_dsp_viewport* vp);
+static void ld_scn_consts_row(u32 target, const rsx_dsp_surface* sf, const rsx_dsp_viewport* vp,
+                              const float* xf, float trs, u32 prim, u32 n_tri, int moves, int moved);
+
+static int ld_scn_sig_is(const ld_scn_sig* q, const surface_t* s)
+{
+    return s->location == q->loc && s->offset == q->off && s->w == q->w && s->h == q->h;
+}
+/* The boundary candidate samples surface si (the draw path found it for one of the units its
+ * fragment program reads). */
+static void ld_scn_probe_sample(u32 si)
+{
+    if (si >= MAX_SURFACES) return;
+    /* [aa3d] rule 1: a surface that was not the scene before counts only when real 3D went into it
+     * (depth written, perspective); the remembered scene is judged as rule 0 judges it. */
+    if (s_scn.depth_frame[si] == s_scn.frame + 1u &&
+        (!g_scn_rule || s_scn.depth3d[si] || (s_scn.sig_valid && ld_scn_sig_is(&s_scn.sig, &g.surfaces[si])))) {
+        if (s_scn.probe_best < 0 || s_scn.depth_draws[si] > s_scn.depth_draws[s_scn.probe_best])
+            s_scn.probe_best = (int)si;
+    } else if (s_scn.sig_valid && ld_scn_sig_is(&s_scn.sig, &g.surfaces[si])) {
+        s_scn.probe_stale = 1;
+    }
+}
+/* Is this draw one the camera jitter moves? Only a draw whose colour target is the remembered scene
+ * surface (same address, same guest size), and of those only the perspective ones:
+ *   rule 0 (default)  depth test on AND the w row of its projection, c[3].xyz, not zero;
+ *   rule 1            depth test on;
+ *   rule 2            c[3].xyz not zero.
+ * GT5's vertex programs all form the position from c[0..3], so c[3] = (0,0,0,k) is a 2D or
+ * orthographic draw; the depth test is asked for as well because a program that does not read c[3]
+ * leaves the last draw's value there. So, left alone on purpose: everything drawn into another
+ * target (shadow maps, the reflection cube, mirror and instrument textures, the particle buffer,
+ * the exposure meter and bloom chain, the display buffer with the HUD), and inside the scene the
+ * full-viewport passes without depth test (the particle composite): moved by up to half a pixel
+ * they would uncover an edge column. Moved with the rest: the mirror views drawn in sub-viewports
+ * of the scene, and depth-only draws into the scene (colour mask 0): the colour draws that follow
+ * are depth-tested against them and must line up. */
+static int ld_jit_moves(u32 target, const rsx_dsp_surface* sf)
+{
+    if (!s_scn.sig_valid || !ld_scn_sig_is(&s_scn.sig, &g.surfaces[target])) return 0;
+    if (sf->clip_w != s_scn.sig.cw || sf->clip_h != s_scn.sig.ch) return 0;     /* another pass into the same surface */
+    const float* c3 = (const float*)g.rsx.constants[3];
+    const int persp = c3[0] != 0.0f || c3[1] != 0.0f || c3[2] != 0.0f;
+    const int dtest = (rsx_dsp_reg(&g.rsx, 0x0A74u /* M_DEPTH_TEST_ENABLE */) & 1u) != 0;
+    return s_jit.rule == 1 ? dtest : s_jit.rule == 2 ? persp : (dtest && persp);
+}
+/* ---- [scene] end (first block) ------------------------------------------------------------- */
+
+/* ---- [fill] begin ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ * LD_FILL (default 1; 0 = today's): the picture fills the window.
+ *
+ * GT5 draws everything it shows, 3D, HUD, menus and loading screens alike, inside a display margin:
+ * 1728x972 at 96,54 of 1920x1080 in 1080p mode, 1152x648 at 64,36 of 1280x720 in 720p mode (the 90 %
+ * of its option display_margin_hd, applied through MSystemConfiguration::SetDisplayMargin and chosen
+ * on the first boot's "adjust screen" page), and last one strip of 10 vertices over the whole frame
+ * that paints that margin black (no texture read, no blending). For a television that hides its edges
+ * that was the safe area; on a PC it is a black border on all four sides.
+ *
+ * What the picture occupies is read from what lands in a display buffer every frame: the union of the
+ * rects (viewport within scissor, guest pixels) of the colour draws into a display buffer and of the
+ * copies and blits into one, leaving out draws that cover the whole frame without reading a texture
+ * (that strip; a full-frame fill or fade, which has nothing to show but its colour). That rect, widened
+ * to the frame's shape about its centre, is what the window gets: the filtering draw scales it to the
+ * back buffer (magnified with a Catmull-Rom filter, reduced with the resolution scale's box filter),
+ * its taps kept inside the rect so nothing of the border bleeds in at the edges.
+ *
+ * It never crops and it does not flicker:
+ *   - a frame that draws outside the rect in force widens it at once, in that very frame (Photo
+ *     Travel's full-height viewfinder, 0,0 1620x1080, does; nothing else in 39 captures);
+ *   - it narrows only when every frame of a run of LD_FILL_FRAMES frames (60) that drew anything
+ *     stayed inside a smaller rect, and then to the union of that run;
+ *   - frames that draw nothing into a display buffer (a paused flip, host-decoded movies) do not
+ *     count; a rect within half a percent of the whole frame is the whole frame.
+ * It starts as the whole frame: the border shows for the first second after start, once.
+ *
+ * Only the step into the window uses it. The display buffers, the frame dumps (LD_FRAME_DUMP: the
+ * picture check compares what it always compared), LD_RECORD, the F8 snapshot and the upscaler's
+ * rectangle are the game's frame as before. Frame generation is handed the filled frame, and the 3D
+ * rectangle it is told about is mapped through the same rect. A "[fill]" line says each change.
+ * ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
+static struct {
+    int   mode;                 /* LD_FILL: -1 not read yet, 0 off, 1 on */
+    u32   frames;               /* LD_FILL_FRAMES */
+    int   have;                 /* the frame being drawn put something into r */
+    float r[4];                 /* its union: x0, y0, x1, y1 in guest pixels of the display buffer */
+    float cur[4];               /* the rect in force; the whole frame when not filling */
+    u32   fw, fh;               /* the frame size cur belongs to */
+    int   win_have;
+    float win[4];               /* the union over the run being counted ... */
+    u32   win_n;                /* ... and its length in frames that drew something */
+    int   on;                   /* cur is smaller than the frame: the present scales it */
+    u32   gen;                  /* changes of cur so far */
+} s_fill = { .mode = -1 };
+static void ld_fill_note(float x0, float y0, float x1, float y1);
+static void ld_fill_draw(u32 target, const rsx_dsp_viewport* vp, int writes_colour);
+static void ld_fill_blit(u32 di, u32 dx, u32 dy, u32 w, u32 h);
+/* ---- [fill] end (first block) ------------------------------------------------------------- */
+
+/* ---- [win] begin ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ * PS3_PRESENT_FIT (default 1; 0 = as before): the picture always reaches the window through the
+ * filtering draw (ld_rs_present_draw), into a back buffer of the window's own size (its client area,
+ * followed at the flips by ld_rs_flip, so a window made larger or smaller, F11, a move to another
+ * monitor all resize it without a restart), in the picture's own shape: the largest rectangle of the
+ * frame's shape (g.width : g.height) centred in the back buffer, with black bars on the sides that are
+ * left over. Bars only when the window's shape differs from the picture's by more than 1 %: a 16:10 or
+ * 4:3 screen, an ultrawide one this release of the game can't draw for. Before, with no resolution scale
+ * the back buffer was the frame's size and DXGI stretched it to the window: soft, and out of shape on
+ * any other shape. A magnification takes the filter's cubic, as LD_FILL's does; a reduction its tent.
+ * Frame generation gets the frame as the window does, bars included, and its 3D rectangle mapped into
+ * the bars' inside; when the window's size changes its presenter is stopped, the swap chain resized and
+ * the presenter started again (rsx_fg_size_reset), where before the back buffer kept its size.
+ * ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
+static int  ld_win_fit_on(void);
+static void ld_win_rect(float* x, float* y, float* w, float* h);
+static int  s_ld_fg_started;    /* the presenter: 0 not started, 1 running, -1 could not start (was a static in the present) */
+/* ---- [win] end (first block) -------------------------------------------------------------- */
+
+/* ---- [mv] begin -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ * Motion vectors of the 3D scene: for every pixel of the scene target, where the thing it shows was
+ * in the frame before. The third input of a temporal upscaler, with the scene's colour and depth.
+ * (State here; the rest is in the second [mv] block, after the second [scene] block.)
+ *
+ * The vectors are in host pixels of the scene target, point from this frame's position to the
+ * previous one (current + vector = previous), and are free of the camera jitter of both frames.
+ * They end up in s_mv.out_tex (R16G16_FLOAT, the scene target's host size), made right after the
+ * scene / HUD boundary (ld_mv_resolve), from two sources:
+ *
+ *   LD_MV=1  camera only. One full-screen pass over the scene's depth: each pixel is taken back
+ *            through this frame's view-projection and forward through the previous one. Right for
+ *            everything that stands still in the world, wrong for what moves in it (cars).
+ *   LD_MV=2  per object as well. GT5's vertex programs all form the position from c[0..3] (object to
+ *            clip), and every object keeps one c[0..3] for all its draws of a frame. Each such
+ *            transform is an "object" here; the object's transform of the frame before is found
+ *            again (ld_mv_match), and its draws write their own vector into a second render target
+ *            (s_mv.obj_tex): the vertex shader also outputs where the vertex was in the previous
+ *            frame, the fragment shader the difference. The full-screen pass then only fills the
+ *            pixels no such draw wrote (and those of objects with no previous transform).
+ *
+ * The view-projection of a frame is c[0..3] * inverse(c[4..6]) of its largest object: c[4..6] is the
+ * object-to-world matrix, and that product is the same matrix for every object of a viewport
+ * (measured: to 1e-7 on the world, the player's car, its wheels and the other cars alike). A mirror
+ * drawn into the scene through its own viewport has its own.
+ *
+ * With LD_MV unset nothing here runs: no target, no shader variant, no pipeline, no pass.
+ *   LD_MV=<0|1|2>        (a setting: followed live)
+ *   LD_MV_VIEW=<n>       show the vectors in place of the 3D picture (hue = direction, full
+ *                        brightness at n host pixels; 1 = 16) (a setting: followed live)
+ *   LD_MV_DUMP=1         a scene dump (LD_SCENE_DUMP) also writes ..._mv.f32 (two float32 per host
+ *                        pixel: x, y), ..._mv.ppm (the same as colours) and, with LD_MV=2,
+ *                        ..._mvobj.f32 (the second render target: 30000 where no draw wrote)
+ *   LD_MV_LOG=1          a "[mv]" line of counts every 300 resolved frames
+ * ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ */
+#define LD_RT_MV        0x100u      /* render_state_t.rt_count: one more target, the motion vectors */
+#define LD_MV_SENTINEL  30000.0f    /* in s_mv.obj_tex: no draw wrote a vector here */
+#define LD_MV_MAX_OBJ   512u        /* a frame seen so far has 41 to 66; sixteen cars in two viewports need more */
+#define LD_MV_REGIONS   3u          /* viewports with a camera of their own: the main one and two more */
+#define LD_MV_GATE      4.0         /* an object further than this from every candidate has no match */
+typedef struct {
+    u32   c[16];                    /* c[0..3] as the draws had them: what makes it one object */
+    u32   vp[4];                    /* guest viewport */
+    float xf[8];                    /* the viewport transform the vertex shader gets, without jitter */
+    float m46[12];                  /* c[4..6] of its first draw: object to world */
+    float vel[3];                   /* how far it moved in the world since the frame before */
+    u64   progs[4];                 /* one bit of 256 per vertex program that drew it */
+    u64   sig0;                     /* its first draw: vertex program and vertex count */
+    u32   draws, verts;
+    int   prev;                     /* its transform in the table of the frame before, or -1 */
+    u8    taken, rows_ok;
+    float ndc_w, ndc_h;             /* host pixels NDC -1..1 spans for its draws: their clip at the target's scale */
+    float rows[12];                 /* guest clip position -> previous host pixel x * w, y * w, w */
+} ld_mv_obj;
+typedef struct { u32 vp[4]; float xf[8]; double m[16]; int ok; float ndc_w, ndc_h; } ld_mv_region;   /* m: view-projection */
+static struct {
+    int   mode;                     /* LD_MV */
+    int   view, dump, log;
+    float view_px;
+    int   tracking;                 /* this frame's perspective scene draws are entered in the table */
+    int   live;                     /* ... and may be drawn with the motion-vector pipeline */
+    u32   frame;                    /* frames tracked: a constant block's rows are of one frame */
+    ld_mv_obj obj[2][LD_MV_MAX_OBJ];   /* [cur]: this frame's objects; [cur ^ 1]: the frame before's */
+    u32   n_obj[2], cur;
+    ld_mv_region reg[2][LD_MV_REGIONS];
+    u32   n_reg[2];
+    int   last_obj;                 /* the object of the last draw (most draws repeat it) */
+    int   prev_valid;               /* [cur ^ 1] is the frame directly before, of the same scene */
+    /* for whoever uses the vectors (the upscaler): */
+    int   out_ok;                   /* out_tex holds this frame's vectors */
+    int   reset;                    /* nothing of earlier frames belongs to this one: a new scene, a
+                                     * cut, a frame after a bypass frame, a change of size */
+    ID3D12Resource* obj_tex;        /* the second render target of scene draws; RENDER_TARGET at rest */
+    ID3D12Resource* out_tex;        /* the frame's vectors; RENDER_TARGET at rest */
+    u32   w, h;                     /* host size of both: the scene target's */
+    ID3D12DescriptorHeap* rtv_heap;
+    D3D12_CPU_DESCRIPTOR_HANDLE obj_rtv, out_rtv;
+    ID3D12RootSignature* rootsig;
+    ID3D12PipelineState* fill_pso;
+    ID3D12PipelineState* view_pso;
+    u32   obj_cleared;              /* frame + 1 in which obj_tex was last cleared */
+    u32   st_obj, st_match, st_exact, st_miss, st_full, st_resolved;
+    /* [fgv] The main viewport's camera of this frame, for a vendor's frame generator (ld_fg_camera):
+     * cam_f takes a world position to the host's clip space (x, y in -1..1 over cam_ndc_w x cam_ndc_h
+     * host pixels of the scene target, y up, depth 0..1), as a matrix for column vectors; cam_r takes
+     * this frame's clip position to the frame before's (the product the fill pass's rows are made of). */
+    int    cam_ok, cam_prev_ok;
+    double cam_f[16], cam_r[16];
+    float  cam_ndc_w, cam_ndc_h;
+} s_mv;
+static int  ld_mv_object(const rsx_dsp_viewport* vp, const float* xf, float host_w, float host_h, u32 n_tri);
+static void ld_mv_draw_target(void);
+static void ld_mv_resolve(int after_boundary);
+static void ld_mv_frame_begin(void);
+static void ld_mv_frame_end(int kind);
+static void ld_mv_dump(const char* base, FILE* info);
+static int  ld_mv_pipeline_wanted(const rsx_dsp_surface* sf, int depth_test, int depth_write, u32 rt_count);
+/* ---- [mv] end (first block) ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
+
+/* ---- [up] begin -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ * The temporal upscaler's evaluation step (NVIDIA DLSS through the optional plug-in, gt5_upscale.h):
+ * anti-aliasing at the scene's own size (DLAA), or the scene drawn smaller and rebuilt at the size
+ * it would have had. (State here; the rest is in the second [up] block, after the second [mv] block.)
+ *
+ * The setting LD_AA selects it, followed live: "" off, "dlaa", "dlss_q", "dlss_b", "dlss_p"; the
+ * setting LD_DLSS_PRESET the model ("" the back end's default, "K", "M", "J", "L"). While it is on
+ * it turns on what it needs: the scene detection, motion vectors per object (as LD_MV=2), and the
+ * camera jitter with the phase count that fits the mode (LD_JITTER, when set, still says how many).
+ *
+ * Where it sits in a frame. The game copies the finished 3D scene into the display buffer with one
+ * draw, the boundary (see [scene]). When that draw is being set up and has been recognised:
+ *   1. this frame's motion vectors are made (ld_mv_resolve);
+ *   2. the back end is given the scene's colour, depth snapshot and vectors and writes s_up.out, on
+ *      the real command list with the recording thread idle (ld_up_boundary);
+ *   3. the boundary draw's texture unit that reads the scene is given s_up.out instead of the scene
+ *      (the slot SRV_UP_BASE in its descriptor table). So the game's own exposure, bloom and colour
+ *      work run on the upscaled picture, and the HUD is drawn over that as always.
+ * The substitution is one slot of one draw's table and nothing else: there is nothing to undo. It is
+ * made only for a draw that reads the scene as a texture of exactly the scene's clip, and only in a
+ * frame whose evaluation succeeded (s_up.frame_ok); any later draw of that frame that reads the
+ * scene the same way gets it too. A bypass frame (menus, 2D) never comes here. In a held frame (the
+ * scene not drawn again: a pause) the display's first draw gets the output of the last evaluated
+ * frame, which is still that scene. When the evaluation fails the frame is shown as the game drew
+ * it; after LD_UP_MAX_FAILS failures in a row the upscaler is switched off until the setting is
+ * changed, with the reason in ld_upscale_state.
+ *
+ * Sizes. The output is the display rectangle the boundary draw fills, at the display buffer's scale
+ * (720p mode: 1152x648 times the resolution scale): the upscaler takes the place of the game's own
+ * supersampling. One scale serves both axes of the scene, the larger of the two ratios, so the 2x1
+ * grid of 1080p mode keeps its shape (out = the clip at the display's scale, 1.33 times the
+ * rectangle's width). LD_UP_OUT=scene: the output is the scene's clip at its ordinary scale, the
+ * supersampling stays (what stage 4 did). The render size is the output's for dlaa, what the back
+ * end asks for in dlss_q/b/p/u, and LD_DLSS_SCALE percent of it in dlss_c. The scene surface and its
+ * zeta are held at the scale that gives the render size (g_rs_scene_*, through the resolution-scale
+ * code), and put back when the mode goes or no 3D scene has been seen for two frames.
+ *
+ * The game's copy and a texture of another size. At 720p the copy takes one tap per display pixel at
+ * a coordinate normalised by the declared size, which lands on a texel centre of an output as large
+ * as the rectangle: an exact copy. At 1080p it takes two taps a guest pixel apart at positions from
+ * floor() of the coordinate, a resample of 1152 columns whatever the texture holds; that draw gets a
+ * variant of its fragment shader in which the resolve is one tap at the continuous coordinate
+ * (LD_RT_UPRES, ld_up_apply_resolve; LD_UP_RESOLVE=0 keeps the game's).
+ *
+ * With LD_AA unset nothing here runs; the plug-in is looked for once at start-up so the menu can
+ * show whether the choices can be had.
+ *   LD_UP_VIEW=<1|2>       (a setting) 1: the left half of the 3D picture is the upscaler's input,
+ *                          the right half its output (in = out size only; else as 2); 2: input and
+ *                          output alternate every second
+ *   LD_UP_JITTER_SIGN=x,y  (a setting) +1 or -1 each: the sign the jitter is handed over with
+ *   LD_UP_OUT=scene        (a setting) the output at the scene's own size, see above
+ *   LD_DLSS_SCALE=<33..100> (a setting) dlss_c: the render height in percent of the output's
+ *   LD_UP_RESOLVE=0        the 1080p copy keeps the game's two-tap resolve
+ *   LD_UP_LOD=0            no texture LOD bias on the scene's draws (log2(render / output), in quarter
+ *                          steps, while the scene is drawn below the output's size)
+ *   LD_UP_LOG=1            a "[upscale]" line of counts every 300 evaluated frames
+ *   LD_UP_COPY=1           the back end is handed copies of the scene's colour, depth and vectors
+ *                          of exactly the render size, not the textures themselves, of which the
+ *                          frame is the top-left part (the scene surface is larger than its clip)
+ *   a scene dump (LD_SCENE_DUMP) gains ..._up.ppm, the upscaled picture, and up_* lines
+ * ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ */
+#define LD_UP_MAX_FAILS 8u         /* evaluation failures in a row before it is switched off */
+#define LD_UP_MAX_WAITS 240u       /* scene frames in a row without what it needs, likewise */
+#define LD_RT_UPRES     0x200u     /* render_state_t.rt_count: the boundary draw with its resolve made one tap */
+enum { LD_UP_S_OFF = 0, LD_UP_S_UNAVAILABLE, LD_UP_S_RUNNING, LD_UP_S_HELD, LD_UP_S_NO_SCENE, LD_UP_S_WAITING,
+       LD_UP_S_FAILED, LD_UP_S_GAVE_UP };
+static struct {

+/* Four independent lanes of 8 bytes, so the multiplies overlap instead of waiting on each other:
+ * about four times the speed of fnv1a's word loop. Only for keys and change checks that live in
+ * memory for one run; anything saved to disk keeps fnv1a. */
+static u64 ld_fast_hash(const void* data, u32 n, u64 seed)
+{
+    const u8* p = (const u8*)data;
+    u64 a = seed ^ 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15ull, b2 = seed + 0xC2B2AE3D27D4EB4Full,
+        c = seed ^ 0x165667B19E3779F9ull, d = seed - 0x27D4EB2F165667C5ull;
+    u32 i = 0;
+    for (; i + 32 <= n; i += 32) {
+        u64 w0, w1, w2, w3;
+        memcpy(&w0, p + i, 8); memcpy(&w1, p + i + 8, 8); memcpy(&w2, p + i + 16, 8); memcpy(&w3, p + i + 24, 8);
+        a = (a ^ w0) * 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15ull; a ^= a >> 29;
+        b2 = (b2 ^ w1) * 0xC2B2AE3D27D4EB4Full; b2 ^= b2 >> 29;
+        c = (c ^ w2) * 0x165667B19E3779F9ull; c ^= c >> 29;
+        d = (d ^ w3) * 0xD6E8FEB86659FD93ull; d ^= d >> 29;
+    }
+    for (; i + 8 <= n; i += 8) { u64 w; memcpy(&w, p + i, 8); a = (a ^ w) * 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15ull; a ^= a >> 29; }
+    for (; i < n; i++) { b2 = (b2 ^ p[i]) * 0xC2B2AE3D27D4EB4Full; b2 ^= b2 >> 29; }
+    u64 h = a ^ (b2 * 31u) ^ (c * 961u) ^ (d * 29791u) ^ (u64)n;
+    h ^= h >> 33; h *= 0xff51afd7ed558ccdull; h ^= h >> 33; h *= 0xc4ceb9fe1a85ec53ull; h ^= h >> 33;
+    return h;
+}
+/* [draw-calls] Work a draw no longer does on the CPU (D3D12). Each switch is looked at once a present
+ * (ld_dc_refresh), so PS3_AB_WHAT=drawcpu can alternate them all in one race; =0 turns one off:
+ *   LD_SMP_SAMPLED  a sampler only for the units the fragment program samples. The others are bound
+ *                   white already, and their samplers made every draw look up ~12 more sampler states and
+ *                   made far more distinct sampler tables: the ring holds 128 between GPU waits.
+ *   LD_SRV_REUSE    a texture table with the same 16 views as one already in the ring, made since the
+ *                   last view was (re)written, is used again: no copy of 16 descriptors, no ring table.
+ *   LD_STATE_DEDUP  the root constant buffers and tables, stencil reference, blend factor and the vertex
+ *                   and index buffer views are not set again when the open list already has them.
+ *   LD_CB_RANGE     the vertex constant block gets only the constants the vertex program reads (all 512
+ *                   when it indexes them), and the last block is used again when those hold the same values.
+ *   LD_VC_HULL      a cached draw's guest pages are checked for writes with one system call over all its
+ *                   spans, not one per span (see ld_vc_clean; the number is how many pages between them).
+ *   LD_SRV_WRAP     a present that finds the texture-table ring (or the vertex, index, constant or upload
+ *                   ring) past half full still overlaps the next frame, and the ring starts over under the
+ *                   part still in flight (see srv_table), instead of waiting for all the GPU's work.
+ * The picture is the same either way: only repeated or unread work, and waits, are left out. */
+static struct { int smp, srv, state, cbr, vc_hull, wrap; } s_dc = { 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1 };
+enum { DC_SMP_LOOK, DC_SMP_SKIP, DC_SMP_TABLE, DC_SMP_FULL, DC_SRV_REUSE, DC_SRV_MADE, DC_SET, DC_SKIP,

+       DC_CB_UPLOADS, DC_CB_SAME, DC_WW_CALLS, DC_WW_PAGES, DC_WW_SAVED, DC_SRV_WRAP, DC_RETIRED_FREED, DC_N };
+static unsigned long long g_dc[DC_N];
+/* The walker's flushes and its waits for the GPU in them (us): [0] presents, [1] a descriptor ring full,
+ * [2] anything else. Every flush but a present's waits for all the GPU's work. */
+static unsigned long long g_dc_wait[3][2];
+/* LD_SRV_WRAP: retired textures [0] and pipelines [1] that were retired before the last flush */

+/* [shadow] Polygon offset (NV4097_SET_POLYGON_OFFSET_{POINT,LINE,FILL}_ENABLE 0x0A60/0x0A64/0x0A68,
+ * SCALE_FACTOR 0x0A78, BIAS 0x0A7C, both floats). The D3D12 path never read them, so every pass the game
+ * offsets -- a shadow map's casters pushed away from the light, decals and contact shadows laid on the road
+ * -- was drawn without: self-shadowing "acne" (stair-stepped bands on surfaces the light grazes, crawling
+ * as things move) and z-fighting decals. The Vulkan engine has honoured it since v0.1.49.
+ *   o = factor * m + units * r   (window depth; m = max |dz/dx|, |dz/dy| in pixels)
+ * The slope part is D3D12's SlopeScaledDepthBias (format independent; times the pass's resolution scale,
+ * because a host pixel is 1/scale of a guest pixel, so the slope per host pixel is m/scale). The constant
+ * part is added to the viewport transform's z
+ * translate, which is window depth exactly: D3D12's own DepthBias would scale by the exponent of each
+ * primitive's depth on our D32_FLOAT zetas, not by the guest's fixed step r = 2^-16 (Z16: GT5's 1024x2048
+ * shadow map is DEPTH16) or 2^-24 (Z24S8). LD_POLY_OFFSET=0: none, as before. */
+static int ld_poly_offset_on(void)
+{
+    static int on = -1;
+    if (on < 0) { const char* e = getenv("LD_POLY_OFFSET"); on = !(e && atoi(e) == 0); }
+    return on;
+}
+/* The guest's offset for what the current primitive rasterises as; 0 when it is off. */
+static int ld_poly_offset(float* slope, float* units)
+{
+    *slope = *units = 0.0f;
+    if (!ld_poly_offset_on()) return 0;
+    const u32 prim = g.rsx.current_primitive;
+    const u32 en = prim == 1u ? 0x0A60u : (prim >= 2u && prim <= 4u) ? 0x0A64u : 0x0A68u;
+    if (!(rsx_dsp_reg(&g.rsx, en) & 1u)) return 0;
+    const u32 fb = rsx_dsp_reg(&g.rsx, 0x0A78u), ub = rsx_dsp_reg(&g.rsx, 0x0A7Cu);
+    float f, u;
+    memcpy(&f, &fb, sizeof f);
+    memcpy(&u, &ub, sizeof u);
+    if (!(f == f) || f > 1e6f || f < -1e6f) f = 0.0f;   /* NaN, or nothing a game means */
+    if (!(u == u) || u > 1e9f || u < -1e9f) u = 0.0f;
+    *slope = f; *units = u;
+    return f != 0.0f || u != 0.0f;
+}
+/* LD_DEPTH_CLIP=1 (an experiment, off): clip at the near and far planes when ZMIN_MAX_CONTROL (0x1D78)

+ * for clipping is printed by LD_SHADOW_LOG ("zminmax="). */
+static int ld_depth_clip_on(void)
+{
+    static int on = -1;
+    if (on < 0) { const char* e = getenv("LD_DEPTH_CLIP"); on = e && atoi(e) != 0; }
+    return on;
+}

+/* [shadow] SET_TEXTURE_BORDER_COLOR (0x1A1C + unit * 0x20), for the BORDER address mode. The D3D12 samplers
+ * never set it, so a border read gave transparent black: for a depth texture that is depth 0, the near

+ * texture takes its low 24 bits (DEPTH24) or 16 bits (DEPTH16) as the depth, as the shared draw engine does
+ * (eng_border_class: inFAMOUS 2's sun shadow maps set 0x00FFFFFF, the far plane, so beyond the map is lit).
+ * Returns 0 when the texture has no BORDER address mode (the sampler is then exactly what it was), else a
+ * key for the sampler cache. LD_BORDER=0: transparent black, as before. */
+static int ld_border_on(void)
+{
+    static int on = -1;
+    if (on < 0) { const char* e = getenv("LD_BORDER"); on = !(e && atoi(e) == 0); }
+    return on;

+static u64 ld_border_key(const rsx_dsp_texture* t)
+{
+    if (!ld_border_on()) return 0;
+    if ((t->wrap & 0xFu) != 4u && ((t->wrap >> 8) & 0xFu) != 4u && ((t->wrap >> 16) & 0xFu) != 4u) return 0;
+    const u32 base = t->format & 0x9Fu;
+    const u64 cls = (base == 0x90u || base == 0x91u) ? 1u : (base == 0x92u || base == 0x93u) ? 2u : 0u;
+    return (1ull << 40) | (cls << 32) | (u64)t->border_color;
+}
+static void ld_border_color(u64 key, FLOAT out[4])
+{
+    const u32 b = (u32)key, cls = (u32)(key >> 32) & 3u;
+    if (cls) {
+        const float d = cls == 1u ? (float)(b & 0xFFFFFFu) / 16777215.0f : (float)(b & 0xFFFFu) / 65535.0f;
+        out[0] = out[1] = out[2] = d;
+        out[3] = 1.0f;
+        return;
+    }
+    out[0] = (float)((b >> 16) & 0xFFu) / 255.0f;
+    out[1] = (float)((b >> 8) & 0xFFu) / 255.0f;
+    out[2] = (float)(b & 0xFFu) / 255.0f;
+    out[3] = (float)(b >> 24) / 255.0f;
+}

+/* Held around every use of the swap chain's current back buffer and its Present: frame generation's
+ * presenter thread (rsx_framegen.c) presents too. Set up with the swap chain. */
+static CRITICAL_SECTION s_ld_swap_lock;
+
+/* The window belongs to the thread that presents here (boot_main's ticker pumps its messages), and a
+ * Present on the presenter thread can wait for that thread to answer a window message. So whoever waits
+ * for the presenter -- for this lock, or for it to take a frame -- answers the window's messages while
+ * it waits; blocking outright froze the picture for good (seen when frame generation was switched off
+ * while the presenter was in Present). */
+extern int rsx_null_backend_pump_messages(void);
+static void ld_pump_while_waiting(void)
+{
+    static int quit_seen;
+    RSX_FG_WAIT(w);                              /* [fgv3] a window message handler can block */
+    if (rsx_null_backend_pump_messages() != 0 && !quit_seen) {
+        quit_seen = 1;
+        PostQuitMessage(0);   /* the ticker's own pump must still see it */
+    }
+    rsx_fg_wait_end("renderer: window messages while waiting", &w);
+}
+static void ld_swap_lock_enter(void)
+{
+    if (TryEnterCriticalSection(&s_ld_swap_lock)) return;
+    RSX_FG_WAIT(w);                              /* [fgv3] the presenter holds it (its Present) */
+    while (!TryEnterCriticalSection(&s_ld_swap_lock)) {
+        ld_pump_while_waiting();
+        Sleep(1);
+    }
+    rsx_fg_wait_end("renderer: swap chain lock", &w);
+}

+/* [draw-calls] LD_SRV_REUSE: what each ring table holds -- the 16 view slots srv_table copied, and the
+ * view generation they were copied at (0: a table of another kind, never reused) -- and an index by
+ * content. A table is taken again only when it lies below srv_ring_used (written since the ring last
+ * started over), holds the same slots, and no view has been written since it was made; an index entry
+ * of an older generation counts as empty, so the index never needs clearing. Only a table the open
+ * command list took itself is taken again (s_srv_list_lo up), so what a submitted list reads is always
+ * its own tables, which LD_SRV_WRAP relies on.
+ *
+ * LD_SRV_WRAP: the ring used to start over only after a wait for all the GPU's work, so a present that
+ * found it past half full could not overlap the next frame (the [present-parts] "srv" count, 15-41
+ * presents in 5 s of a race). Now such a present, after its usual wait for the frame before, starts the
+ * ring over below the tables of the list it just submitted, the only ones still in flight: s_srv_cap
+ * keeps the next list under them, and the next flush (which waits for that list) lifts the cap. A list
+ * that reaches the cap makes room as one that reached the end always did. */

+/* Before every take from a ring: its use below the last take means it started over (after a wait for

+static void ld_ring_note(u32 used, u32 hi, u32* list_lo)
+{

+/* At the end of every flush: the list before the one just submitted is done (an overlapped present

+static void ld_ring_after(u32* used, u32 size, u32* cap, u32* list_lo, u32* hi, int overlapped)

+/* The ring's tables by content. sampler_table looked for its table with a memcmp against every one
+ * in the ring -- up to 128 a draw, and sampler_table_needs_flush did it again once the ring was
+ * full. A table is appended only when it is not there, so each content is in the ring once and the
+ * index answers what the scan did. Only sampler_table appends, after a lookup, so the index catches
+ * up on lookup, and a ring that is smaller than what it holds was reset. LD_SMP_INDEX=0: the scan. */
+#define SMP_INDEX_SLOTS 512u
+static u16 s_smp_index[SMP_INDEX_SLOTS];   /* ring table + 1, 0 = empty */
+static u32 s_smp_indexed;
+static u32 smp_index_slot(const u32 slots[SMP_TABLE_SIZE])
+{
+    return (u32)ld_fast_hash(slots, SMP_TABLE_SIZE * sizeof(u32), 0x534D5054u) & (SMP_INDEX_SLOTS - 1u);
+}
+static int smp_find(const u32 slots[SMP_TABLE_SIZE])
+{
+    static int on = -1;
+    if (on < 0) { const char* e = getenv("LD_SMP_INDEX"); on = !(e && atoi(e) == 0); }
+    if (!on) {
+        for (u32 i = 0; i < g.smp_ring_used; i++)
+            if (memcmp(g.smp_ring_slots[i], slots, sizeof(g.smp_ring_slots[i])) == 0)
+                return (int)i;
+        return -1;
+    }
+    if (g.smp_ring_used < s_smp_indexed) {
+        memset(s_smp_index, 0, sizeof s_smp_index);
+        s_smp_indexed = 0;
+    }
+    for (; s_smp_indexed < g.smp_ring_used; s_smp_indexed++) {
+        u32 h = smp_index_slot(g.smp_ring_slots[s_smp_indexed]);
+        while (s_smp_index[h]) h = (h + 1u) & (SMP_INDEX_SLOTS - 1u);
+        s_smp_index[h] = (u16)(s_smp_indexed + 1u);
+    }
+    for (u32 h = smp_index_slot(slots);; h = (h + 1u) & (SMP_INDEX_SLOTS - 1u)) {
+        const u32 e = s_smp_index[h];
+        if (!e) return -1;
+        if (memcmp(g.smp_ring_slots[e - 1u], slots, sizeof(g.smp_ring_slots[0])) == 0)
+            return (int)(e - 1u);
+    }
+}

+/* LD_GPU_TIME=1: GPU time of each draw, and of whatever ran between two draws (copies, barriers),
+ * summed by pipeline key and printed every five seconds. The key is what LD_PS_DUMP names shader
+ * files by. This is for finding what a slow scene spends its GPU on; CPU profiles can't see it. */
+#define LDT_DRAWS 8192
+#define LDT_KEYS  1024
+typedef struct { u64 key; u32 verts, target; } ldt_draw;
+typedef struct { u64 key; u32 target; u64 ticks, gap, n, verts; } ldt_sum;
+static struct {
+    int on;   /* 0 unknown, 1 on, -1 off */
+    ID3D12QueryHeap* heap;
+    ID3D12Resource* rb;
+    u32 n;
+    u64 freq;
+    u32 flips_at;
+    ULONGLONG printed_at;
+    u32 n_sum;
+    ldt_draw d[LDT_DRAWS];
+    ldt_sum sum[LDT_KEYS];
+} g_ldt;
+
+static int ldt_ready(void)
+{
+    if (g_ldt.on) return g_ldt.on > 0;
+    g_ldt.on = -1;
+    if (!getenv("LD_GPU_TIME")) return 0;
+    D3D12_QUERY_HEAP_DESC qd;
+    memset(&qd, 0, sizeof qd);
+    qd.Type = D3D12_QUERY_HEAP_TYPE_TIMESTAMP;
+    qd.Count = 2 * LDT_DRAWS;
+    D3D12_HEAP_PROPERTIES hp;
+    memset(&hp, 0, sizeof hp);
+    hp.Type = D3D12_HEAP_TYPE_READBACK;
+    D3D12_RESOURCE_DESC rd;
+    memset(&rd, 0, sizeof rd);
+    rd.Dimension = D3D12_RESOURCE_DIMENSION_BUFFER;
+    rd.Width = 16u * LDT_DRAWS;
+    rd.Height = 1;
+    rd.DepthOrArraySize = 1;
+    rd.MipLevels = 1;
+    rd.SampleDesc.Count = 1;
+    rd.Layout = D3D12_TEXTURE_LAYOUT_ROW_MAJOR;
+    if (FAILED(g.dev->lpVtbl->CreateQueryHeap(g.dev, &qd, &IID_ID3D12QueryHeap, (void**)&g_ldt.heap)) ||
+        FAILED(LD_CCR(g.dev, &hp, D3D12_HEAP_FLAG_NONE, &rd, D3D12_RESOURCE_STATE_COPY_DEST,
+                                                      NULL, &IID_ID3D12Resource, (void**)&g_ldt.rb)) ||
+        FAILED(g.queue->lpVtbl->GetTimestampFrequency(g.queue, &g_ldt.freq)) || !g_ldt.freq) {
+        fprintf(stderr, "[gpu-time] could not set up timestamps\n");
+        return 0;
+    }
+    g_ldt.on = 1;
+    return 1;
+}
+
+static void ldt_begin(u64 key, u32 verts, u32 target)
+{
+    if (!ldt_ready() || g_ldt.n >= LDT_DRAWS) return;
+    ldt_draw* d = &g_ldt.d[g_ldt.n];
+    d->key = key;
+    d->verts = verts;
+    d->target = target;
+    g.list->lpVtbl->EndQuery(g.list, g_ldt.heap, D3D12_QUERY_TYPE_TIMESTAMP, 2 * g_ldt.n);
+}
+
+static void ldt_end(void)
+{
+    if (g_ldt.on <= 0 || g_ldt.n >= LDT_DRAWS) return;
+    g.list->lpVtbl->EndQuery(g.list, g_ldt.heap, D3D12_QUERY_TYPE_TIMESTAMP, 2 * g_ldt.n + 1);
+    g_ldt.n++;
+}
+
+static void ldt_resolve(void)
+{
+    if (g_ldt.on > 0 && g_ldt.n)
+        g.list->lpVtbl->ResolveQueryData(g.list, g_ldt.heap, D3D12_QUERY_TYPE_TIMESTAMP, 0, 2 * g_ldt.n, g_ldt.rb, 0);
+}
+
+static int ldt_cmp(const void* a, const void* b)
+{
+    const u64 x = ((const ldt_sum*)a)->ticks + ((const ldt_sum*)a)->gap;
+    const u64 y = ((const ldt_sum*)b)->ticks + ((const ldt_sum*)b)->gap;
+    return x < y ? 1 : x > y ? -1 : 0;
+}

+/* After the fence: the list that wrote them has finished. */
+static void ldt_collect(void)
+{
+    if (g_ldt.on <= 0) return;
+    if (g_ldt.n) {
+        void* map = NULL;
+        D3D12_RANGE r;
+        r.Begin = 0;
+        r.End = 16u * g_ldt.n;
+        if (SUCCEEDED(g_ldt.rb->lpVtbl->Map(g_ldt.rb, 0, &r, &map))) {
+            const u64* t = (const u64*)map;
+            for (u32 i = 0; i < g_ldt.n; i++) {
+                const ldt_draw* d = &g_ldt.d[i];
+                u32 k = 0;
+                while (k < g_ldt.n_sum && (g_ldt.sum[k].key != d->key || g_ldt.sum[k].target != d->target)) k++;
+                if (k == g_ldt.n_sum) {
+                    if (k == LDT_KEYS) continue;
+                    memset(&g_ldt.sum[k], 0, sizeof g_ldt.sum[k]);
+                    g_ldt.sum[k].key = d->key;
+                    g_ldt.sum[k].target = d->target;
+                    g_ldt.n_sum++;
+                }
+                g_ldt.sum[k].ticks += t[2 * i + 1] - t[2 * i];
+                if (i) g_ldt.sum[k].gap += t[2 * i] - t[2 * i - 1];
+                g_ldt.sum[k].n++;
+                g_ldt.sum[k].verts += d->verts;
+            }
+            D3D12_RANGE none;
+            none.Begin = none.End = 0;
+            g_ldt.rb->lpVtbl->Unmap(g_ldt.rb, 0, &none);
+        }
+        g_ldt.n = 0;
+    }
+    const ULONGLONG now = GetTickCount64();
+    if (now - g_ldt.printed_at < 5000) return;
+    g_ldt.printed_at = now;
+    const u32 flips = g_ld_frames - g_ldt.flips_at ? g_ld_frames - g_ldt.flips_at : 1;
+    g_ldt.flips_at = g_ld_frames;
+    qsort(g_ldt.sum, g_ldt.n_sum, sizeof g_ldt.sum[0], ldt_cmp);
+    const double ms = 1000.0 / (double)g_ldt.freq / flips;
+    u64 draw_t = 0, gap_t = 0, n = 0;
+    for (u32 k = 0; k < g_ldt.n_sum; k++) { draw_t += g_ldt.sum[k].ticks; gap_t += g_ldt.sum[k].gap; n += g_ldt.sum[k].n; }
+    fprintf(stderr, "[gpu-time] %u flips: %.1f ms/flip in draws, %.1f between draws, %llu draws/flip, %u shader+target pairs\n",
+            flips, draw_t * ms, gap_t * ms, (unsigned long long)(n / flips), g_ldt.n_sum);
+    for (u32 k = 0; k < g_ldt.n_sum && k < 14; k++) {
+        const ldt_sum* m = &g_ldt.sum[k];
+        const surface_t* ts = m->target < MAX_SURFACES ? &g.surfaces[m->target] : NULL;
+        fprintf(stderr, "[gpu-time]   K=%016llX draw %6.2f gap %6.2f ms/flip, %5llu draws %8llu verts, target %u:0x%07X %ux%u\n",
+                (unsigned long long)m->key, m->ticks * ms, m->gap * ms, (unsigned long long)(m->n / flips),
+                (unsigned long long)(m->verts / flips), ts ? ts->location : 0, ts ? ts->offset : 0, ts ? ts->w : 0, ts ? ts->h : 0);
+    }
+    g_ldt.n_sum = 0;
+}

+/* GCM_DRAIN_STAT=1: where a present's time goes: before the flush (copies, dumps), the flush (the
+ * GPU finishing the frame), and the swap chain's Present. LD_PRESENT_SYNC=0 presents without
+ * waiting for vblank. */
+static LONGLONG lps_now(void) { LARGE_INTEGER t; QueryPerformanceCounter(&t); return t.QuadPart; }
+static UINT lps_sync_interval(void)
+{
+    static int v = 1; static unsigned gen;   /* the in-game menu can change it while the game runs */
+    if (gen != gt5_settings_gen()) {

+        if (v < 0) v = 0;
+        if (v > 4) v = 4;
