+/* Known-committed guest pages: the DMA engine's cache of them (spu_vm_pagemap.c). A set bit is a
+ * page some SPU transfer has already touched, which every page of a job list the manager has
+ * walked is. A page not in it is not read from here. */
+extern unsigned char g_vm_page_bitmap[65536 / 8];
+static int spurs_guest_readable(u32 ea, u32 size)
+{
+    if (!ea || !size || (uint64_t)ea + size > 0x100000000ull) return 0;
+    const u32 p0 = ea >> 16, p1 = (ea + size - 1u) >> 16;
+    return ((g_vm_page_bitmap[p0 >> 3] >> (p0 & 7)) & 1) && ((g_vm_page_bitmap[p1 >> 3] >> (p1 & 7)) & 1);
+}
+
+/* The job the Wws job manager would look at first, read from the workload's job-list header as
+ * the manager's claim reads it (GetJobFromJobList; layout from the policy module's disassembly):
+ *
+ *     array  = be32(header + 0x08)                    which of the four job-header arrays
+ *     taken  = be16(header + 0x40 + 16*array + 2)     index of the next job to hand out
+ *     jh     = be32(header + 0x30 + 4*array) + 8*taken
+ *     cmd    = be16(jh + 2)                           0 = kNoJobYet: nothing published there
+ *
+ * Returns 1 only for "nothing published at the next index": the claim's own answer for "no job".
+ * Returns 0 for anything else, including every case this cannot judge: not this job manager
+ * (the image's "WWSJ" marker and version at LS 0x15E8), an array id out of range, memory not
+ * known to be readable, or a header that changed while it was being read. A barrier, a Nop or a
+ * SetNextActiveArray at the next index is "may have work": the manager has to run to pass it.
+ * *taken_out receives the index looked at. */
+#define SPURS_WWS_MARK_OFFSET (0x15E8u - 0xA00u)
+static int spurs_wws_list_empty(u32 pm_ea, u32 pm_size, u64 data, u32* taken_out)
+{
+    static const u8 mark[8] = { 'W', 'W', 'S', 'J', 0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x80 };
+    if (!pm_ea || pm_size < SPURS_WWS_MARK_OFFSET + 8u) return 0;
+    if (memcmp(vm_base + pm_ea + SPURS_WWS_MARK_OFFSET, mark, 8) != 0) return 0;
+    const u32 hdr = (u32)data;
+    if ((hdr & 127u) || !spurs_guest_readable(hdr, 128)) return 0;
+    const u32 array = vm_read32(hdr + 0x08);
+    if (array > 3u) return 0;
+    const u32 seq   = vm_read32(hdr + 0x0C);
+    const u32 base  = vm_read32(hdr + 0x30 + 4u * array);
+    const u32 taken = vm_read16(hdr + 0x40 + 16u * array + 2u);
+    if (!base || (base & 7u)) return 0;
+    const u32 jh = base + 8u * taken;
+    if (jh < base || !spurs_guest_readable(jh, 8)) return 0;
+    const u32 cmd = vm_read16(jh + 2u);
+    /* The header is one lock line that SPUs commit as a whole; if any word used moved, do not judge. */
+    if (vm_read32(hdr + 0x08) != array || vm_read32(hdr + 0x0C) != seq ||
+        vm_read32(hdr + 0x30 + 4u * array) != base || vm_read16(hdr + 0x40 + 16u * array + 2u) != taken)
+        return 0;
+    if (taken_out) *taken_out = taken;
+    return cmd == 0;
+}
+
+static unsigned long long spurs_now_us(void)
+{
+    static LARGE_INTEGER f;
+    if (!f.QuadPart) QueryPerformanceFrequency(&f);
+    LARGE_INTEGER c; QueryPerformanceCounter(&c);
+    return (unsigned long long)(c.QuadPart / f.QuadPart) * 1000000ull +
+           (unsigned long long)(c.QuadPart % f.QuadPart) * 1000000ull / (unsigned long long)f.QuadPart;
+}
+
+static int spurs_prio_select(void)
+{
+    static int v = -1;
+    if (v < 0) { const char* e = getenv("SPURS_PRIO_SELECT"); v = e ? (atoi(e) != 0) : 2; }
+    if (v != 2) return v;
+    const int ab = ps3_ab_on("prio");
+    return ab >= 0 ? ab : 1;
+}
+
+/* One selection pass over the free slots: the coordinator's timed and kicked passes, and with
+ * SPURS_HANDOFF bit 0 the pass a worker makes at the end of its run. Under si->lock and the registry
+ * lock. self: that worker's slot, looked at first (NULL: the coordinator, from slot 0). Each slot filled
+ * is published and its worker woken, except self. Returns 1 if self was filled. */
+static int spurs_select_pass(struct SpursInst* si, int kick_pass, struct SpursPmSlot* self)
+{
+    u32 ea = si->ea;
+    if (!kick_pass) si->pass_no++;
+    SPURS_HS(si, self ? SPURS_HS_PASS_W : SPURS_HS_PASS_C);
+    u32 enabled = vm_read32(ea + SPURS_WKL_ENABLED);
+    /* SPURS_STARVE=1: every 5 s, how often each kicked workload found every SPU
+     * slot taken, and what held them. There is no preemption here, so a workload
+     * that holds its slots starves the rest. */
+    { static int st = -1; if (st < 0) st = getenv("SPURS_STARVE") ? 1 : 0;
+      if (st) {
+          static unsigned long long passes, starve[16], held[16]; static ULONGLONG t0;
+          u32 busy = 0;
+          for (u32 sn = 0; sn < si->host_spus; sn++)
+              if (si->slots[sn].busy) { busy++; held[si->slots[sn].wid & 15]++; }
+          passes++;
+          if (busy == si->host_spus)
+              for (u32 w = 0; w < 16; w++)
+                  if ((enabled & (0x80000000u >> w)) &&
+                      (vm_read8(ea + SPURS_WKL_READY1 + w) || (vm_read16(ea + SPURS_WKL_SIGNAL1) & (0x8000u >> w))))
+                      starve[w]++;
+          const ULONGLONG now = GetTickCount64();
+          if (!t0) t0 = now;
+          if (now - t0 >= 5000) {
+              fprintf(stderr, "[spurs-starve] passes=%llu", passes);
+              for (u32 w = 0; w < 16; w++)
+                  if (starve[w] || held[w])
+                      fprintf(stderr, " w%u:waited=%llu,held=%llu%%,max=%u", w, starve[w], held[w] * 100 / (passes ? passes : 1), vm_read8(ea + SPURS_WKL_MAXCONT + w));
+              fputc(10, stderr);
+              passes = 0; memset(starve, 0, sizeof starve); memset(held, 0, sizeof held); t0 = now;
+          }
+      } }
+    int self_filled = 0;
+    const u32 first = self ? (u32)(self - si->slots) : 0u;
+    for (u32 i = 0; i < si->host_spus; i++) {
+        const u32 sn = first + i < si->host_spus ? first + i : first + i - si->host_spus;
+        struct SpursPmSlot* slot = &si->slots[sn];
+        if (slot->busy) continue;
+        /* SPURS_PRIO_SELECT (default on; 0 = the plain round robin of before 23 Nov 2026; PS3_AB_WHAT=prio
+         * alternates): among the workloads that stand requested and may run on this SPU, the best priority
+         * goes first, as the real kernel chooses (1 is the highest, 15 the lowest). The round robin took
+         * whichever came next at the cursor, a probe of an idle workload included: in a 16-car race GT5's
+         * priority-1 workload found every SPU taken 1,500-2,000 times a second while its priority-6 and
+         * priority-7 job lists held 2.6 of them. Equal priorities still take turns by the cursor. */
+        u32 best_prio = 0;
+        if (spurs_prio_select()) {
+            const u32 sig0 = vm_read16(ea + SPURS_WKL_SIGNAL1);
+            const u32 pspu = sn < si->nspus ? sn : slot->spu_num;
+            for (u32 w = 0; w < 16; w++) {
+                if (!(enabled & (0x80000000u >> w))) continue;
+                if (!(vm_read8(ea + SPURS_WKL_READY1 + w) || (sig0 & (0x8000u >> w)) || spurs_wkl_flagged(ea, w))) continue;
+                if (vm_read8(ea + SPURS_WKL_STATE1 + w) != 2 || !s_workloads[w].in_use || s_workloads[w].spurs_ea != ea) continue;
+                const u32 p = vm_read8(ea + SPURS_WKL_INFO1 + w * SPURS_WKL_INFO_SZ + 0x18 + pspu);
+                if (!p || (best_prio && p >= best_prio)) continue;
+                const u32 mc = vm_read8(ea + SPURS_WKL_MAXCONT + w);
+                if (!mc || si->active[w] >= mc) continue;
+                int clash = 0;
+                for (u32 o = 0; o < si->host_spus; o++)
+                    if (o != sn && si->slots[o].busy && si->slots[o].wid == w && si->slots[o].spu_num == slot->spu_num) clash = 1;
+                if (clash || !spurs_resolve_pm(w)) continue;
+                best_prio = p;
+            }
+        }
+        for (u32 checked = 0; checked < 16; checked++) {
+            u32 wid = si->cursor;
+            si->cursor = (wid + 1) & 15;
+            if (!(enabled & (0x80000000u >> wid)) ||
+                vm_read8(ea + SPURS_WKL_STATE1 + wid) != 2 ||
+                !s_workloads[wid].in_use || s_workloads[wid].spurs_ea != ea)
+                continue;
+            /* The priority byte of the SPU number this run will CLAIM. An extra slot (SPURS_EXTRA_SPUS)
+             * runs as SPU sn % nspus, but was checked against SPU 0's byte: slot 6 of a 5-SPU instance
+             * could run, as SPU 1, a workload that SPU 1 may never run, and leave that SPU's lane of a
+             * job list at a progress nothing advances again (the game waits for the LOWEST lane).
+             * SPURS_EXTRA_PRIO=0: the old check. */
+            static int s_extra_prio = -1;
+            if (s_extra_prio < 0) { const char* e = getenv("SPURS_EXTRA_PRIO"); s_extra_prio = !(e && *e == '0'); }
+            const u32 prio_spu = sn < si->nspus ? sn : (s_extra_prio ? slot->spu_num : 0u);
+            if (!vm_read8(ea + SPURS_WKL_INFO1 + wid * SPURS_WKL_INFO_SZ + 0x18 + prio_spu))
+                continue; /* priority zero makes this physical lane ineligible */
+            u32 maxcont = vm_read8(ea + SPURS_WKL_MAXCONT + wid);
+            if (!maxcont || si->active[wid] >= maxcont) continue;
+            { /* Two runs of one workload can't share an SPU number: same context. */
+              int clash = 0;
+              for (u32 o = 0; o < si->host_spus; o++)
+                  if (o != sn && si->slots[o].busy && si->slots[o].wid == wid &&
+                      si->slots[o].spu_num == slot->spu_num) clash = 1;
+              if (clash) continue; }
+            WklPm* pm = spurs_resolve_pm(wid);
+            if (!pm) continue;
+            u32 signal = vm_read16(ea + SPURS_WKL_SIGNAL1);
+            u32 ready = vm_read8(ea + SPURS_WKL_READY1 + wid);
+            int kicked = ready || (signal & (0x8000u >> wid)) || spurs_wkl_flagged(ea, wid);
+            /* a requested workload of a better priority may run here: this one waits, and so does a probe */
+            if (best_prio && (!kicked || vm_read8(ea + SPURS_WKL_INFO1 + wid * SPURS_WKL_INFO_SZ + 0x18 + prio_spu) > best_prio))
+                continue;
+            if (kicked) si->idle[wid] = 0;
+            if (!kicked && (kick_pass || (si->pass_no & ((1u << si->idle[wid]) - 1))))
+                continue;
+            if (!kicked && si->probe_next_us[wid] && spurs_probe_pace_us() &&
+                spurs_now_us() < si->probe_next_us[wid])
+                continue;
+            slot->said_empty = 0;
+            if (!kicked) {
+                /* An idle probe is about to run a job manager to see whether its list has a
+                 * job. For a Wws list the first thing that run reads can be read from here. */
+                const int native = spurs_native_work_mode();
+                u32 taken = 0;
+                if (native && spurs_wws_list_empty((u32)(uintptr_t)s_workloads[wid].pm, s_workloads[wid].sizePm,
+                                                   vm_read64(ea + SPURS_WKL_INFO1 + wid * SPURS_WKL_INFO_SZ + 8), &taken)) {
+                    if (native == 1 && spurs_now_us() - si->run_start_us[wid] < spurs_native_work_recheck_us()) {
+                        if (spurs_dstat_on()) s_dstat[wid].nskip++;
+                        continue;               /* nothing to hand out; really probed again within the re-check time */
+                    }
+                    if (native == 2) { slot->said_empty = 1; slot->said_taken = taken; if (spurs_dstat_on()) s_dstat[wid].nskip++; }
+                }
+            }
+            if (spurs_native_work_mode()) si->run_start_us[wid] = spurs_now_us();
+            if (spurs_dstat_on()) { if (kicked) s_dstat[wid].kick++; else s_dstat[wid].probe++; }
+            /* SPURS_HANDOFF bit 0 also takes the request line's lock once for the request consumed and
+             * the contention count raised (one update of the line, as the real kernel's), not twice:
+             * in D65's [lockline] this pass's two holds and the run end's one were 3 of the lock-line
+             * lock's top 4 callers, 38.6 k a second each. */
+            const int one_hold = spurs_handoff_mode() & 1;
+            spu_lockline_lock_line(ea);
+            ready = vm_read8(ea + SPURS_WKL_READY1 + wid);
+            signal = vm_read16(ea + SPURS_WKL_SIGNAL1);
+            if (ready) vm_base[ea + SPURS_WKL_READY1 + wid] = (u8)(ready - 1);
+            if (signal & (0x8000u >> wid))
+                ef_w16(ea + SPURS_WKL_SIGNAL1, (u16)(signal & ~(0x8000u >> wid)));
+            if (spurs_wkl_flagged(ea, wid))
+                memset(vm_base + ea + SPURS_WKL_FLAG_WORD, 0xFF, 4);
+            if (one_hold) {
+                si->active[wid]++;
+                vm_base[ea + SPURS_WKL_CURCONT + wid] = si->active[wid];
+            }
+            ef_line_end_line(ea);
+            slot->fn = pm->fn; slot->image_id = pm->image_id;
+            slot->pm = vm_base + (u32)(uintptr_t)s_workloads[wid].pm;
+            slot->pm_size = s_workloads[wid].sizePm;
+            slot->data = vm_read64(ea + SPURS_WKL_INFO1 + wid * SPURS_WKL_INFO_SZ + 8);
+            slot->wid = wid; slot->ea = ea;
+            if (!one_hold) {
+                si->active[wid]++;
+                spu_lockline_lock_line(ea);
+                vm_base[ea + SPURS_WKL_CURCONT + wid] = si->active[wid];
+                ef_line_end_line(ea);
+            }
+            slot->probe = !kicked;
+            if (spurs_hang_spurs_on()) {   /* [HANG] (tl5) */
+                const unsigned long long now_ms = GetTickCount64();
+                slot->run_t0 = now_ms;
+                if (kicked) si->t_kick[wid] = now_ms; else si->t_probe[wid] = now_ms;
+            }
+            SPURS_HS(si, kicked ? SPURS_HS_KICKED : SPURS_HS_PROBE);
+            SPURS_HS(si, slot == self ? SPURS_HS_SELF : self ? SPURS_HS_OTHER : SPURS_HS_CFILL);
+            spurs_slot_publish(si, slot, slot == self);
+            if (slot == self) self_filled = 1;
+            break;
+        }
+    }
+    return self_filled;
+}
+
+/* SPURS_HANDOFF bit 0: at the end of a run on `slot`, the pass the coordinator was woken to make for
+ * it, made by this worker. Under si->lock. Returns 1 if it gave this worker its next run. */
+static int spurs_worker_pass(struct SpursInst* si, struct SpursPmSlot* slot)
+{
+    if (si->stopping || spurs_pm_disabled()) return 0;
+    int kick_pass = 0;
+    if (spurs_wake_filter_on()) {
+        /* The coordinator was woken (as a kick) only while a workload stood requested. */
+        if (!spurs_request_standing(si->ea)) return 0;
+        kick_pass = ++si->kick_run < 16;
+    }
+    if (!kick_pass) si->kick_run = 0;
+    AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&s_workload_registry_lock);
+    const int mine = spurs_select_pass(si, kick_pass, slot);
+    ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&s_workload_registry_lock);
+    return mine;
+}

+/* [HANG] (tl5): the SPURS state, for the hang report (boot_main.cpp hang_watchdog prints it after the guest
+ * registers when the game has asked for no flip for PS3_HANG_S seconds). The idea is Project Tourline 5's
+ * stall dump (patches/incremental/v211-freeze-flag-kick.patch, MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Ned Heller /
+ * sp00nznet): each Wws job list's rows and the jobs around them, which is how they found GT5 2.11's
+ * GPUSyncArray jobs left unrun. Our kernel cannot lose a request that way (requests are consumed only by the
+ * run they start, and idle job managers are probed anyway), so this answers the other questions about a stall
+ * like the 1.00 colour-screen hang, where the main thread spins: does a job list hold published jobs, is a
+ * job manager stuck inside a run (and for how long), or are they all idle with nothing to do.
+ *   instance: workloads enabled, signal bits, the workload flag and its receiver, runs ended so far, full passes
+ *   slot:     busy or idle; the workload, how long the run has lasted, and whether it was an idle probe
+ *   workload: ready count, contention (the instance byte / ours / maximum), state, idle back-off, and how long
+ *             ago it last ran on a request, was probed, and did work
+ *   Wws list: the 128-byte header (array in use at +0x08, list bases at +0x30, a 16-byte row per array at
+ *             +0x40), then per array its row: +0 the head (jobs published), +2..+E one progress halfword per SPU
+ *             (FFFF unused), their lowest, and the 8-byte jobs from two before the lowest to five after the
+ *             highest of them, at most 24; a published job is nonzero in its second halfword (0 = kNoJobYet).
+ *             GT5 1.00's main thread waits on exactly that lowest progress: func_00953700 -> func_00953680 ->
+ *             func_00CD1BC8 takes the unsigned minimum of row +2..+E of the GPUSyncArray list (wid 4) and returns
+ *             whether it has reached its target; those three are where the colour-screen hang spins (shc1 r4).
+ * Read-only: guest memory only where an SPU transfer has already touched the page, the instance lock only if
+ * it is free (else read without it, said so). PS3_HANG_SPURS=0: nothing. */
+static void spurs_hang_hex(char* out, size_t cap, const u8* p, u32 n)
+{
+    size_t k = 0;
+    for (u32 i = 0; i < n && k + 4 < cap; i++)
+        k += (size_t)snprintf(out + k, cap - k, "%s%02X", (i && !(i & 3)) ? " " : "", p[i]);
+    if (k < cap) out[k] = 0;
+}
+void cellSpurs_hang_report(void);   /* called from boot_main.cpp's hang watchdog */
+void cellSpurs_hang_report(void)
+{
+    if (!spurs_hang_spurs_on()) return;
+    const unsigned long long now = GetTickCount64();
+    char line[768];
+    for (int k = 0; k < MAX_SPURS_INST; k++) {
+        struct SpursInst* si = &s_inst[k];
+        const u32 ea = __atomic_load_n(&si->ea, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
+        if (!ea || !__atomic_load_n(&si->kernel_live, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) continue;
+        const int locked = TryAcquireSRWLockExclusive(&si->lock) ? 1 : 0;
+        const int reg = TryAcquireSRWLockShared(&s_workload_registry_lock) ? 1 : 0;
+        const u32 enabled = vm_read32(ea + SPURS_WKL_ENABLED);
+        fprintf(stderr, "[HANG] spurs \"%.15s\" ea=0x%08X spus %u (+%u): enabled 0x%08X signal 0x%04X flag %08X recv %02X; "
+                        "runs ended %llu, full passes %u%s\n",
+                si->prefix, ea, si->nspus, si->host_spus - si->nspus, enabled, vm_read16(ea + SPURS_WKL_SIGNAL1),
+                vm_read32(ea + SPURS_WKL_FLAG_WORD), vm_base[ea + SPURS_WKL_FLAG_RECV],
+                (unsigned long long)__atomic_load_n(&si->hs[SPURS_HS_ENDS], __ATOMIC_RELAXED), si->pass_no,
+                locked ? "" : " (instance lock busy: read without it)");
+        for (u32 sn = 0; sn < si->host_spus && sn < 8; sn++) {
+            const struct SpursPmSlot* s = &si->slots[sn];
+            if (__atomic_load_n(&s->busy, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE))
+                fprintf(stderr, "[HANG] spurs   slot %u (spu %u): wid %u, running %llu ms%s\n", sn, s->spu_num, s->wid,
+                        s->run_t0 ? (unsigned long long)(now - s->run_t0) : 0ull, s->probe ? " (an idle probe)" : "");
+            else
+                fprintf(stderr, "[HANG] spurs   slot %u (spu %u): idle\n", sn, s->spu_num);
+        }
+        for (u32 wid = 0; wid < 16; wid++) {
+            if (!(enabled & (0x80000000u >> wid))) continue;
+            const SpursWorkload* w = &s_workloads[wid];
+            const int mine = w->in_use && w->spurs_ea == ea;
+            const u32 wea = ea + SPURS_WKL_INFO1 + wid * SPURS_WKL_INFO_SZ;
+            const u32 hdr = (u32)vm_read64(wea + 8);
+            char ago[3][24];
+            const unsigned long long t[3] = { si->t_kick[wid], si->t_probe[wid], si->t_work[wid] };
+            for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
+                if (t[i]) snprintf(ago[i], sizeof ago[i], "%llu ms ago", (unsigned long long)(now - t[i]));
+                else snprintf(ago[i], sizeof ago[i], "never");
+            }
+            const u8* pr = vm_base + wea + 0x18;   /* priority per SPU number */
+            fprintf(stderr, "[HANG] spurs   wid %u: ready %u, contention %u (ours %u, max %u), state %u, priority %02X %02X %02X %02X "
+                            "%02X %02X, idle level %u, data 0x%08X; on a request %s, probed %s, did work %s%s\n",
+                    wid, vm_base[ea + SPURS_WKL_READY1 + wid], vm_base[ea + SPURS_WKL_CURCONT + wid], si->active[wid],
+                    vm_base[ea + SPURS_WKL_MAXCONT + wid], vm_base[ea + SPURS_WKL_STATE1 + wid],
+                    pr[0], pr[1], pr[2], pr[3], pr[4], pr[5], si->idle[wid], hdr,
+                    ago[0], ago[1], ago[2], mine ? "" : " (not in the workload table)");
+            if (!mine || !reg) continue;
+            const u32 pm_ea = (u32)(uintptr_t)w->pm;
+            static const u8 mark[8] = { 'W', 'W', 'S', 'J', 0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x80 };
+            if (!pm_ea || w->sizePm < SPURS_WWS_MARK_OFFSET + 8u ||
+                memcmp(vm_base + pm_ea + SPURS_WWS_MARK_OFFSET, mark, 8) != 0) continue;
+            if ((hdr & 127u) || !spurs_guest_readable(hdr, 128)) {
+                fprintf(stderr, "[HANG] spurs     wws list 0x%08X: not readable from here\n", hdr);
+                continue;
+            }
+            u8 h[128];
+            memcpy(h, vm_base + hdr, sizeof h);
+            for (u32 r = 0; r < 128; r += 32) {
+                spurs_hang_hex(line, sizeof line, h + r, 32);
+                fprintf(stderr, "[HANG] spurs     wws list 0x%08X +%02X: %s\n", hdr, r, line);
+            }
+            for (u32 a = 0; a < 4; a++) {
+                const u32 base = ((u32)h[0x30 + 4 * a] << 24) | ((u32)h[0x31 + 4 * a] << 16) |
+                                 ((u32)h[0x32 + 4 * a] << 8) | h[0x33 + 4 * a];
+                if (!base || (base & 7u)) continue;
+                u32 hw[8];
+                for (u32 i = 0; i < 8; i++) hw[i] = ((u32)h[0x40 + 16 * a + 2 * i] << 8) | h[0x41 + 16 * a + 2 * i];
+                /* The halfwords that can be job indices (FFFF = an unused lane, per Tourline's reading). */
+                u32 lo0 = 0xFFFFFFFFu, hi0 = 0;
+                for (u32 i = 0; i < 8; i++)
+                    if (hw[i] <= 0x1000u) { if (hw[i] < lo0) lo0 = hw[i]; if (hw[i] > hi0) hi0 = hw[i]; }
+                const u32 from = lo0 > hi0 ? 0u : lo0 >= 2u ? lo0 - 2u : 0u;
+                u32 to = lo0 > hi0 ? 0u : hi0 + 6u;
+                if (to - from > 24u) to = from + 24u;
+                u32 lowest = 0xFFFFu;   /* the game's own test: the unsigned minimum of +2..+E */
+                for (u32 i = 1; i < 8; i++) if (hw[i] < lowest) lowest = hw[i];
+                int n = snprintf(line, sizeof line, "array %u%s at 0x%08X: head %u, progress %04X %04X %04X %04X %04X %04X %04X "
+                                 "(lowest %u); jobs %u..%u:",
+                                 a, ((u32)h[0x0B] == a && !h[0x08] && !h[0x09] && !h[0x0A]) ? " (in use)" : "", base,
+                                 hw[0], hw[1], hw[2], hw[3], hw[4], hw[5], hw[6], hw[7], lowest, from, to ? to - 1u : 0u);
+                if (to <= from) { if (n > 0 && (size_t)n + 8 < sizeof line) snprintf(line + n, sizeof line - (size_t)n, " none"); }
+                else if ((uint64_t)base + 8ull * to <= 0x100000000ull && spurs_guest_readable(base + 8u * from, 8u * (to - from)))
+                    for (u32 j = from; j < to && n > 0 && (size_t)n + 20 < sizeof line; j++)
+                        n += snprintf(line + n, sizeof line - (size_t)n, " %08X%08X", vm_read32(base + 8u * j), vm_read32(base + 8u * j + 4u));
+                else if (n > 0 && (size_t)n + 24 < sizeof line)
+                    snprintf(line + n, sizeof line - (size_t)n, " not readable from here");
+                fprintf(stderr, "[HANG] spurs     %s\n", line);
+            }
+        }
+        if (reg) ReleaseSRWLockShared(&s_workload_registry_lock);
+        if (locked) ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&si->lock);
+    }
+    fflush(stderr);
+}

+/* The workload flag's address (spurs + 0x60). Unregistered, this import faked CELL_OK and left
+ * the game's pointer unset. */
+s32 cellSpursGetWorkloadFlag(CellSpurs* spurs, u32* flag)
+{
+    if (!spurs || !flag) return CELL_SPURS_CORE_ERROR_NULL_POINTER;
+    if ((u32)(uintptr_t)spurs & 127) return CELL_SPURS_CORE_ERROR_ALIGN;
+    vm_write32((u32)(uintptr_t)flag, (u32)(uintptr_t)spurs + SPURS_WKL_FLAG);
+    return CELL_OK;
+}
+
+/* Make wid the workload the flag wakes (is_set) or stop it being that. Policy-module error codes. */
+s32 _cellSpursWorkloadFlagReceiver(CellSpurs* spurs, CellSpursWorkloadId wid, u32 is_set)
+{
+    if (!spurs) return (s32)0x80410811;                       /* POLICY_MODULE_ERROR_NULL_POINTER */
+    if ((u32)(uintptr_t)spurs & 127) return (s32)0x80410810;  /* ..._ALIGN */
+    if (wid >= CELL_SPURS_MAX_WORKLOAD) return (s32)0x80410802; /* ..._INVAL */
+    const u32 ea = (u32)(uintptr_t)spurs;
+    if (!(vm_read32(ea + SPURS_WKL_ENABLED) & (0x80000000u >> wid))) return (s32)0x80410805; /* ..._SRCH */
+    s32 rc = CELL_OK;
+    spu_lockline_lock_line(ea);
+    const u8 recv = vm_base[ea + SPURS_WKL_FLAG_RECV];
+    if (is_set ? recv != 0xFF : recv != wid) {
+        rc = is_set ? (s32)0x8041080A : (s32)0x80410809;      /* ..._BUSY / ..._PERM */
+    } else {
+        memset(vm_base + ea + SPURS_WKL_FLAG_WORD, 0xFF, 4);
+        vm_base[ea + SPURS_WKL_FLAG_RECV] = is_set ? (u8)wid : 0xFF;
+    }
+    ef_line_end_line(ea);
+    {   static int _n = 0;
+        if (_n++ < 16) printf("[cellSpurs] WorkloadFlagReceiver(wid=%u, set=%u) -> 0x%08X\n", wid, is_set, (u32)rc);
+    }
+    return rc;
+}

-/* Enumerate files in a save directory. Returns count, fills fileList up to max. */
+/* Which files were written as SECUREFILE. A real save records them in
+ * PARAM.PFD; ours keeps one name per line there, and the file stays hidden
+ * from the guest's list (savedata_system_file). Without it every file came
+ * back as NORMALFILE, and a title that looks for its secure payload in the
+ * stat list (The Simpsons Arcade Game) called its own fresh save corrupt. */
+static void pfd_path(const char* save_path, char* out, size_t n)
+{
+    snprintf(out, n, "%s/PARAM.PFD", save_path);
+#ifdef _WIN32
+    for (char* p = out; *p; p++) if (*p == '/') *p = '\\';
+#endif
+}
+
+/* The name as a whole word in the PFD: ours is one name per line, a real one (a save from a PS3, or one an
+ * earlier build appended our lines to) keeps each name NUL-padded in its entry table. Reading it line by line
+ * missed both a real PFD's names and the first line glued to the end of one, so a save brought over from a PS3
+ * listed its payload as a NORMALFILE. */
+static int pfd_has(const char* save_path, const char* name)
+{
+    char path[1024];
+    pfd_path(save_path, path, sizeof(path));
+    FILE* fp = fopen(path, "rb");
+    if (!fp) return 0;
+    static unsigned char buf[64 * 1024];
+    size_t n = fread(buf, 1, sizeof buf, fp);
+    fclose(fp);
+    size_t nl = strlen(name);
+    if (!nl || nl > n) return 0;
+    for (size_t i = 0; i + nl <= n; i++) {
+        if (memcmp(buf + i, name, nl)) continue;
+        unsigned char after = i + nl < n ? buf[i + nl] : 0;
+        unsigned char before = i ? buf[i - 1] : 0;
+        int word_end = after == 0 || after == '\n' || after == '\r';
+        int word_start = !i || !(isalnum(before) || before == '.' || before == '_' || before == '-');
+        if (word_end && word_start) return 1;
+    }
+    return 0;
+}
+
+/* RPCS3 marks a save's secure files in PARAM.SFO instead: an INT32 key "*<name>" set to 1. A save made in RPCS3
+ * and copied over has no PFD at all, so read those marks too. */
+static int sfo_marks_secure(const char* save_path, const char* name)
+{
+    char path[1024];
+    snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "%s/PARAM.SFO", save_path);
+#ifdef _WIN32
+    for (char* p = path; *p; p++) if (*p == '/') *p = '\\';
+#endif
+    FILE* fp = fopen(path, "rb");
+    if (!fp) return 0;
+    uint8_t buf[8192];
+    size_t n = fread(buf, 1, sizeof buf, fp);
+    fclose(fp);
+    if (n < 0x14 || buf[0] != 0 || buf[1] != 'P' || buf[2] != 'S' || buf[3] != 'F') return 0;
+    uint32_t ktab = ps3_psf_get32(buf + 8), dtab = ps3_psf_get32(buf + 12), cnt = ps3_psf_get32(buf + 16);
+    if (cnt > 256 || ktab > n || dtab > n || 0x14 + 16ull * cnt > n) return 0;
+    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < cnt; i++) {
+        const uint8_t* e = buf + 0x14 + 16 * i;
+        uint32_t ko = ps3_psf_get16(e), fmt = ps3_psf_get16(e + 2), len = ps3_psf_get32(e + 4), dof = ps3_psf_get32(e + 12);
+        if (ktab + (uint64_t)ko >= n || dtab + (uint64_t)dof + len > n) continue;
+        if (!memchr(buf + ktab + ko, 0, n - (ktab + (size_t)ko))) continue;
+        const char* key = (const char*)buf + ktab + ko;
+        if (key[0] == '*' && !strcmp(key + 1, name) && fmt == PS3_PSF_INT32 && len == 4)
+            return ps3_psf_get32(buf + dtab + dof) != 0;
+    }
+    return 0;
+}
+
+static void pfd_add(const char* save_path, const char* name)
+{
+    if (pfd_has(save_path, name)) return;
+    char path[1024];
+    pfd_path(save_path, path, sizeof(path));
+    FILE* fp = fopen(path, "ab");
+    if (fp) { fprintf(fp, "%s\n", name); fclose(fp); }
+}

+/* Mixing thread, every pass: a device that went away (a USB or Bluetooth device gone, ALSA without a
+ * sound server, Android's output disconnected) is closed and the default one opened again; with none
+ * there, once a second. SDL keeps a lost device "open" but stopped, and feeds it nothing: it never
+ * comes back by itself. Meanwhile the mixing thread runs on the clock (no device), so the game's sound
+ * clock keeps going. The open runs on this thread: with a sound server it takes milliseconds, and an
+ * open that fails (none there) fails at once. AUDIO_FOLLOW=0: never (the old behaviour). */
+static int s_follow = -1;
+static void audio_backend_follow(long long now_ns)
+{
+    static long long next_look, retry_at;
+    static int lost;
+    if (s_follow < 0) { const char* e = getenv("AUDIO_FOLLOW"); s_follow = !(e && *e == '0'); }
+    if (!s_follow || !s_sdl_up || now_ns < next_look) return;
+    next_look = now_ns + 100000000LL;   /* ten times a second */
+    if (s_sdl_audio_dev) {
+        if (SDL_GetAudioDeviceStatus(s_sdl_audio_dev) != SDL_AUDIO_STOPPED) return;
+        fprintf(stderr, "[cellAudio] sound device lost: the sound clock runs on, looking for a device\n");
+        SDL_CloseAudioDevice(s_sdl_audio_dev);
+        s_sdl_audio_dev = 0;
+        lost = 1;
+        retry_at = now_ns;
+    }
+    if (now_ns < retry_at) return;
+    if (audio_sdl_open() < 0) { retry_at = now_ns + 1000000000LL; return; }
+    /* Four blocks of silence first: the lead the mixing thread keeps, so it goes on at its pace. */
+    { static const float zero[CELL_AUDIO_BLOCK_SAMPLES * 2];
+      for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) SDL_QueueAudio(s_sdl_audio_dev, zero, sizeof zero); }
+    fprintf(stderr, "[cellAudio] sound device %s\n", lost ? "back" : "found");
+    lost = 0;
+}

+/* ---- The output device ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ *
+ * It used to be opened once, at Init: a headset or Bluetooth device connected later left the sound on
+ * the speakers, and once the device in use went away (unplugged, an HDMI TV asleep, the default
+ * switched to another) the game was silent until restart. Now (AUDIO_FOLLOW, on unless 0):
+ *  - A device thread ("audio device") listens to Windows' device notifications. When the default
+ *    output device changes, or the one in use is lost, it opens the default one -- Activate,
+ *    Initialize, and half a buffer of silence, which can take a while on Bluetooth or HDMI -- and
+ *    hands it over. The mixing thread only swaps it in and starts it: it never waits for a device, so
+ *    the game's sound clock (a block and a tick every 5.33 ms, which paces the game) never stops.
+ *    With no device it runs on the performance counter, as it always did.
+ *  - The device switched away from is handed back and closed by the device thread once it has played
+ *    what it still held, while the new one plays the half buffer of silence it was opened with (the
+ *    lead the mixer keeps anyway): a switch between two working devices drops nothing.
+ *  - A device that fails (AUDCLNT_E_DEVICE_INVALIDATED and the like) or takes no sound for 250 ms is
+ *    lost: the mixing thread drops it and goes on on the clock. With no device to open, the device
+ *    thread tries again every second and at every device notification; a device lost again within
+ *    3 s of being opened is tried again after 0.5, 1, 2, then 4 s.
+ * AUDIO_FOLLOW=0: the device opened at Init is the only one, as before. AUDIO_FOLLOW_TEST=<s> (tests):
+ * every <s> seconds the device in use is dropped as if lost, and the default one opened <s>/2 s later. */
+
+typedef struct audio_dev {
+    IAudioClient*       client;
+    IAudioRenderClient* render;
+    HANDLE              event;          /* NULL: the mixing thread polls */
+    UINT32              buf_frames;
+    UINT32              drain_frames;   /* handed back: what it still had to play */
+    ULONGLONG           back_ms;        /* handed back: when */
+    LONG                gen;            /* 1, 2, ...: which opening this is */
+    WCHAR               id[256];        /* the endpoint's id */
+    char                name[160];      /* its name (UTF-8), for the log */
+} audio_dev;
+
+/* The device the mixing thread plays to: only the mixing thread changes it (and Init / Quit, while

+static audio_dev* volatile s_dev_next;         /* opened by the device thread, for the mixing thread */
+static audio_dev* volatile s_dev_back[4];      /* handed back by the mixing thread, for the device thread to close */
+static HANDLE              s_dev_wake;         /* auto-reset: the device thread has something to do */

+enum { DEV_DEFAULT = 1, DEV_CHANGED = 2, DEV_LOST = 4 };

+static void audio_dev_poke(LONG why)
+{
+    if (why) InterlockedOr(&s_dev_why, why);
+    if (s_dev_wake) SetEvent(s_dev_wake);

+/* Windows' device notifications: they arrive on a thread of the audio service's and must not wait
+ * for anything, so they only wake the device thread. Static object, no reference counting. */
+static HRESULT STDMETHODCALLTYPE nc_query(IMMNotificationClient* self, REFIID riid, void** out)
+{
+    if (IsEqualIID(riid, &ps3r_IID_IUnknown) || IsEqualIID(riid, &ps3r_IID_IMMNotificationClient)) {
+        *out = self;
+        return S_OK;
+    }
+    *out = NULL;
+    return E_NOINTERFACE;
+}
+static ULONG STDMETHODCALLTYPE nc_addref(IMMNotificationClient* self) { (void)self; return 1; }
+static ULONG STDMETHODCALLTYPE nc_release(IMMNotificationClient* self) { (void)self; return 1; }
+static HRESULT STDMETHODCALLTYPE nc_state(IMMNotificationClient* self, LPCWSTR id, DWORD state)
+{ (void)self; (void)id; (void)state; audio_dev_poke(DEV_CHANGED); return S_OK; }
+static HRESULT STDMETHODCALLTYPE nc_added(IMMNotificationClient* self, LPCWSTR id)
+{ (void)self; (void)id; audio_dev_poke(DEV_CHANGED); return S_OK; }
+static HRESULT STDMETHODCALLTYPE nc_removed(IMMNotificationClient* self, LPCWSTR id)
+{ (void)self; (void)id; audio_dev_poke(DEV_CHANGED); return S_OK; }
+static HRESULT STDMETHODCALLTYPE nc_default(IMMNotificationClient* self, EDataFlow flow, ERole role, LPCWSTR id)
+{
+    (void)self; (void)id;
+    /* One for each role: the game plays as a console (game) stream, the role it opened with. */
+    if (flow == eRender && role == eConsole) audio_dev_poke(DEV_DEFAULT);
+    return S_OK;
+}
+static HRESULT STDMETHODCALLTYPE nc_property(IMMNotificationClient* self, LPCWSTR id, const PROPERTYKEY key)
+{ (void)self; (void)id; (void)key; return S_OK; }

+static void audio_dev_free(audio_dev* d)
+{
+    if (!d) return;
+    if (d->client) d->client->lpVtbl->Stop(d->client);
+    if (d->render) d->render->lpVtbl->Release(d->render);
+    if (d->client) d->client->lpVtbl->Release(d->client);
+    if (d->event) CloseHandle(d->event);
+    free(d);
+}

+static audio_dev* audio_dev_open_default(IMMDeviceEnumerator* en, int prefill, const char** step, HRESULT* err)
+{
+    IMMDevice* device = NULL;
+    *step = "GetDefaultAudioEndpoint";
+    *err = en->lpVtbl->GetDefaultAudioEndpoint(en, eRender, eConsole, &device);
+    if (FAILED(*err) || !device) return NULL;
+    audio_dev* d = audio_dev_open(device, prefill, step, err);
+    device->lpVtbl->Release(device);
+    return d;
+}

+/* The default device's id into out (256); 0 when there is none. */
+static int audio_dev_default_id(IMMDeviceEnumerator* en, WCHAR* out)
+{
+    IMMDevice* device = NULL;
+    LPWSTR id = NULL;
+    out[0] = 0;
+    if (FAILED(en->lpVtbl->GetDefaultAudioEndpoint(en, eRender, eConsole, &device)) || !device) return 0;
+    if (SUCCEEDED(device->lpVtbl->GetId(device, &id)) && id) { lstrcpynW(out, id, 256); CoTaskMemFree(id); }
+    device->lpVtbl->Release(device);
+    return out[0] != 0;

+/* Mixing thread: a device it no longer plays to goes to the device thread to be closed, after playing
+ * out what it still holds unless it was lost. */
+static void audio_dev_give_back(audio_dev* d, int drain)
+{
+    UINT32 pad = 0;
+    if (!d) return;
+    if (drain && SUCCEEDED(d->client->lpVtbl->GetCurrentPadding(d->client, &pad))) d->drain_frames = pad;
+    d->back_ms = GetTickCount64();
+    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++)
+        if (!InterlockedCompareExchangePointer((PVOID volatile*)&s_dev_back[i], d, NULL)) { audio_dev_poke(0); return; }
+    audio_dev_free(d);   /* the device thread is four behind: close it here */
+}
+
+/* Mixing thread: the device in use failed (or takes no sound): play on the clock, ask for another. */
+static void audio_dev_lost(HRESULT hr, const char* what)
+{
+    audio_dev* d = s_dev;
+    if (!d) return;
+    s_dev = NULL;
+    fprintf(stderr, "[cellAudio] sound device lost (%s, %s 0x%08lX): the sound clock runs on, looking for a device\n",
+            d->name, what, (unsigned long)hr);
+    InterlockedExchange(&s_dev_lost_gen, d->gen);
+    audio_dev_give_back(d, 0);
+    audio_dev_poke(DEV_LOST);
+}
+
+/* Mixing thread, every pass: takes the device the device thread opened (or drops its own for a test). */
+static void audio_dev_take(void)
+{
+    if (!s_follow) return;
+    if (s_dev_drop && InterlockedExchange(&s_dev_drop, 0)) audio_dev_lost(S_OK, "AUDIO_FOLLOW_TEST");
+    audio_dev* n = (audio_dev*)InterlockedExchangePointer((PVOID volatile*)&s_dev_next, NULL);
+    if (!n) return;
+    audio_dev* old = s_dev;
+    s_dev = n;
+    n->client->lpVtbl->Start(n->client);
+    audio_dev_give_back(old, 1);
+}
+
+/* Device thread: close what was handed back, each once it has played out. */
+static void audio_dev_close_back(int now_all)
+{
+    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
+        audio_dev* d = s_dev_back[i];
+        if (!d) continue;
+        if (!now_all && d->drain_frames) {
+            const ULONGLONG until = d->back_ms + d->drain_frames * 1000ull / CELL_AUDIO_SAMPLE_RATE + 5;
+            const ULONGLONG now = GetTickCount64();
+            if (now < until) Sleep((DWORD)(until - now > 200 ? 200 : until - now));
+        }
+        InterlockedExchangePointer((PVOID volatile*)&s_dev_back[i], NULL);
+        audio_dev_free(d);
+    }
+}
+
+static unsigned __stdcall audio_dev_thread_func(void* arg)
+{
+    (void)arg;
+    ps3_thread_name("audio device");
+    const HRESULT co = CoInitializeEx(NULL, COINIT_MULTITHREADED);
+    IMMDeviceEnumerator* en = NULL;
+    HRESULT hr = CoCreateInstance(&CLSID_MMDeviceEnumerator, NULL, CLSCTX_ALL,
+                                  &IID_IMMDeviceEnumerator, (void**)&en);
+    if (FAILED(hr) || !en) {
+        fprintf(stderr, "[cellAudio] device thread: no device enumerator (0x%08lX): the device stays as it is\n",
+                (unsigned long)hr);
+        if (SUCCEEDED(co)) CoUninitialize();
+        return 0;
+    }
+    hr = en->lpVtbl->RegisterEndpointNotificationCallback(en, &s_nc);
+    const int listening = SUCCEEDED(hr);
+    if (!listening)
+        fprintf(stderr, "[cellAudio] no device notifications (0x%08lX): looking at the default device every 2 s\n",
+                (unsigned long)hr);
+
+    int test_s = 0;
+    { const char* e = getenv("AUDIO_FOLLOW_TEST"); test_s = e ? atoi(e) : 0; if (test_s < 0) test_s = 0; }
+    ULONGLONG now = GetTickCount64();
+    ULONGLONG test_at = test_s ? now + (ULONGLONG)test_s * 1000 : 0;
+    ULONGLONG next_try = now, opened_ms = now, lost_ms = 0;
+    int want = !s_dev_playing[0];           /* open the default device: none playing (Init found none) */
+    int streak = 0, failures = 0;
+    const char* reason = "found";
+
+    while (!s_dev_quit) {
+        now = GetTickCount64();
+        DWORD wait = INFINITE;
+        if (want) wait = next_try > now ? (DWORD)(next_try - now) : 0;
+        if (!listening && wait > 2000) wait = 2000;
+        if (test_at && wait > (test_at > now ? test_at - now : 0)) wait = (DWORD)(test_at > now ? test_at - now : 0);
+        WaitForSingleObject(s_dev_wake, wait);
+        if (s_dev_quit) break;
+        audio_dev_close_back(0);
+        now = GetTickCount64();
+        const LONG why = InterlockedExchange(&s_dev_why, 0);
+
+        if (test_at && now >= test_at) {               /* AUDIO_FOLLOW_TEST: drop the device in use */
+            test_at = now + (ULONGLONG)test_s * 1000;
+            InterlockedExchange(&s_dev_drop, 1);       /* the loss comes back as DEV_LOST */
+        }
+        if ((why & DEV_LOST) && s_dev_lost_gen == s_dev_gen) {
+            /* The device last handed over is gone (an older one going doesn't matter: the mixing
+             * thread is about to take the newer one). */
+            s_dev_playing[0] = 0;
+            want = 1;
+            lost_ms = now;
+            streak = now - opened_ms < 3000 ? streak + 1 : 0;
+            next_try = now + (streak ? (250ull << (streak < 4 ? streak : 4)) : 0);
+            if (test_s) next_try = now + (ULONGLONG)test_s * 500;
+            reason = "back";
+        }
+        if (!want && (!listening || (why & (DEV_DEFAULT | DEV_CHANGED)))) {
+            WCHAR def[256];
+            if (audio_dev_default_id(en, def) && lstrcmpW(def, s_dev_playing) != 0) {
+                want = 1;
+                next_try = now;
+                reason = "Windows default";
+            }
+        }
+        /* While waiting to try again, a device that turns up (or a new default) is tried at once. */
+        if (want && (why & (DEV_DEFAULT | DEV_CHANGED)) && !(why & DEV_LOST) && !test_s) next_try = now;
+        if (!want || now < next_try) continue;
+
+        const char* step = "";
+        audio_dev* d = audio_dev_open_default(en, 1, &step, &hr);
+        if (!d) {
+            if (failures++ == 0)
+                fprintf(stderr, "[cellAudio] no sound device to open (%s 0x%08lX): the sound clock runs on, "
+                        "trying again\n", step, (unsigned long)hr);
+            next_try = now + 1000;
+            continue;
+        }
+        d->gen = ++s_dev_gen;
+        lstrcpynW(s_dev_playing, d->id, 256);
+        audio_dev* prev = (audio_dev*)InterlockedExchangePointer((PVOID volatile*)&s_dev_next, d);
+        audio_dev_free(prev);              /* one opened before but never taken: superseded */
+        if (!strcmp(reason, "back") && lost_ms)
+            fprintf(stderr, "[cellAudio] sound device back: %s (%.0f ms after it was lost)\n", d->name,
+                    (double)(GetTickCount64() - lost_ms));
+        else
+            fprintf(stderr, "[cellAudio] sound device now %s (%s)\n", d->name, reason);
+        want = 0; failures = 0; opened_ms = now; lost_ms = 0;
+    }
+
+    if (listening) en->lpVtbl->UnregisterEndpointNotificationCallback(en, &s_nc);
+    en->lpVtbl->Release(en);
+    audio_dev_close_back(1);
+    if (SUCCEEDED(co)) CoUninitialize();
+    return 0;
+}
+
+/* Init, after the first device: start following the default one. */
+static void audio_follow_start(void)
+{
+    const char* e = getenv("AUDIO_FOLLOW");
+    s_follow = !(e && *e == '0');
+    if (!s_follow) return;
+    s_dev_why = 0; s_dev_quit = 0; s_dev_drop = 0; s_dev_lost_gen = 0;
+    s_dev_wake = CreateEventW(NULL, FALSE, FALSE, NULL);
+    s_dev_thread = s_dev_wake ? (HANDLE)_beginthreadex(NULL, 0, audio_dev_thread_func, NULL, 0, NULL) : NULL;
+    if (!s_dev_thread) {
+        fprintf(stderr, "[cellAudio] no device thread: the device stays as it is\n");
+        s_follow = 0;
+    }
+}

+/* Periods spent waiting for a late block: in all, and the longest wait (for the log). */
+static unsigned long long s_audio_holds, s_audio_hold_runs;

+/* Mix one block from all active ports into s_mix_buffer (stereo float). Returns 1 when the period
+ * was spent waiting for a late writer instead: silence, nothing read, and no notify to send. */
+static int audio_mix_one_block(void)
 {
     memset(s_mix_buffer, 0, sizeof(s_mix_buffer));
 
     mutex_lock(&s_audio_mutex);
+
+    /* A writer that is late gets its block waited for. GT5 writes its blocks in order, one per
+     * notify event, two blocks ahead of the reader. When the SPU job chain that makes them lost the
+     * CPU for longer than that (every core busy), the reader read the empty slot and moved on, the
+     * late blocks landed behind the reader, the whole ring played out empty before it came round to
+     * them (an 85 ms hole), and from then on the sound ran up to 80 ms late. Now, while a port that
+     * was playing finds its next block not yet written, the period plays silence and nothing moves:
+     * no block read, the read index unchanged, no notify sent, so when the writer catches up its
+     * lead is what it was. At most AUDIO_HOLD_MAX periods in a row (default 16, one ring of GT5's;
+     * 0 = never wait, the old behaviour), so a port that went quiet by writing zeros is read on.
+     * PS3_AB_WHAT=audhold alternates it with the old behaviour. */
+    {
+        static int hold_max = -1;
+        /* Capped at 64 (340 ms): no tick goes out while waiting, and GT5's tick thread gives up on
+         * its queue after a second without one. */
+        if (hold_max < 0) { const char* e = getenv("AUDIO_HOLD_MAX"); hold_max = e && *e ? atoi(e) : 16;
+                            if (hold_max > 64) hold_max = 64; }
+        extern int ps3_ab_on(const char* what);

+/* Once a minute, if the reader had to wait for late blocks: how often. Many waits mean the title's
+ * sound work runs short of CPU (on GT5, its SPU job chain): in play.err for reports. */
+static void audio_hold_report(void)
+{
+    static unsigned n;
+    static unsigned long long h0, r0;
+    if (++n < 11250) return;   /* 60 s of blocks */
+    n = 0;
+    if (s_audio_holds != h0)
+        fprintf(stderr, "[audio] waited for late sound blocks %llu times in the last minute, %llu periods "
+                "(%.0f ms) in all, longest %u\n", s_audio_hold_runs - r0, s_audio_holds - h0,
+                (double)(s_audio_holds - h0) * CELL_AUDIO_BLOCK_SAMPLES * 1000.0 / CELL_AUDIO_SAMPLE_RATE,
+                (unsigned)s_audio_hold_longest);
+    h0 = s_audio_holds; r0 = s_audio_hold_runs; s_audio_hold_longest = 0;
+}
+
+/* ---- The player's volume, and "mute when in the background" (the in-game menu's Sound page) ------
+ * GT5_VOLUME (0-100, not set = 100) and GT5_MUTE_BACKGROUND (1 = on), read from the settings registry
+ * whenever it changes, so both work at once. Applied to what the device gets, not to the mix itself
+ * (AUDIO_PEAK, AUDIO_WAV and AUDIO_RATE keep seeing the game's own sound). Volume goes by its square
+ * (50 = -12 dB, the way a volume slider sounds even); a change, and the mute, glide over a few blocks
+ * (no click). */
+
+/* 1: a window of this process is in front; 0: another one is; -1: can't tell (keep what it was). */
+static int audio_window_in_front(void)
+{
+#ifdef _WIN32
+    HWND fg = GetForegroundWindow();
+    if (!fg) return -1;            /* between two windows taking the focus */
+    DWORD pid = 0;
+    GetWindowThreadProcessId(fg, &pid);
+    return pid == GetCurrentProcessId();
+#elif AUDIO_BACKEND_SDL2
+    if (!SDL_WasInit(SDL_INIT_VIDEO)) return -1;   /* no SDL window to ask about */
+    return SDL_GetKeyboardFocus() != NULL;
+#else
+    return -1;
+#endif
+}
+
+/* Returns what the device gets: the mix itself at full volume, else a copy with the gain on it (the
+ * mix stays the game's own for AUDIO_PEAK / AUDIO_WAV / AUDIO_RATE). */
+static float s_out_buffer[CELL_AUDIO_BLOCK_SAMPLES * 2];
+static const float* audio_apply_volume(const float* mix, u32 frames)
+{
+    float* const stereo = s_out_buffer;
+    static unsigned gen = ~0u;
+    static float vol = 1.0f, gain = 1.0f;
+    static int bg = 0, front = 1, n = 0;
+    if (gen != gt5_settings_gen()) {
+        gen = gt5_settings_gen();
+        int v = gt5_setting_int("GT5_VOLUME", 100);
+        if (v < 0) v = 0;
+        if (v > 100) v = 100;
+        const int was_bg = bg; const float was_vol = vol;
+        vol = (float)(v * v) / 10000.0f;
+        bg = gt5_setting_bool("GT5_MUTE_BACKGROUND", 0);
+        if (vol != was_vol || bg != was_bg) {
+            static int said = 0;
+            if (PS3_LOG_FIRST(said, 32))
+                fprintf(stderr, "[cellAudio] volume %d%%, mute when in the background %s\n", v, bg ? "on" : "off");
+        }
+        n = 0;
+    }
+    if (bg) {
+        if ((n++ & 15) == 0) {                      /* every 16 blocks, 85 ms */
+            const int f = audio_window_in_front();
+            if (f >= 0 && f != front) {
+                static int said = 0;
+                if (PS3_LOG_FIRST(said, 32))
+                    fprintf(stderr, "[cellAudio] %s\n", f ? "in front: sound on" : "in the background: muted");
+                front = f;
+            }
+        }
+    } else {
+        front = 1;
+    }
+    float target = front ? vol : 0.0f;
+#if AUDIO_BACKEND_SDL2
+    { static int mute = -1; if (mute < 0) mute = getenv("PS3_MUTE") ? 1 : 0;   /* as at the WASAPI device */
+      if (mute) target = 0.0f; }
+#endif
+    if (target == 1.0f && gain == 1.0f) return mix;  /* full volume: nothing to do */
+    /* At most a fifth of full scale per block: a whole change takes ~27 ms. */
+    float next = target;
+    if (next > gain + 0.2f) next = gain + 0.2f;
+    if (next < gain - 0.2f) next = gain - 0.2f;
+    const float step = (next - gain) / (float)frames;
+    float g = gain;
+    for (u32 i = 0; i < frames; i++) {
+        g += step;
+        stereo[i * 2 + 0] = mix[i * 2 + 0] * g;
+        stereo[i * 2 + 1] = mix[i * 2 + 1] * g;
+    }
+    gain = next;
+    return stereo;
+}

+/* AUDIO_STALL_TEST=<s>,<ms> (tests): <s> seconds after the mixing thread starts, it stops for <ms> ms
+ * once, as a stall of the PC held it: no block, no tick. With AUDIO_TICK_GUARD=0, 1500 is enough for
+ * GT5 to drop its tick queue (one-second bursts after it); with the guard the sound just comes back. */
+static void audio_stall_test(void)
+{
+    static int at_s = -1, ms;
+    static u64 t0;
+    if (at_s < 0) {
+        const char* e = getenv("AUDIO_STALL_TEST");
+        at_s = 0;
+        if (e && *e) { at_s = atoi(e); const char* c = strchr(e, ','); ms = c ? atoi(c + 1) : 1500; }
+        t0 = audio_now_us();
+    }
+    if (at_s <= 0 || audio_now_us() - t0 < (u64)at_s * 1000000ull) return;
+    at_s = 0;
+    fprintf(stderr, "[cellAudio] AUDIO_STALL_TEST: the mixing thread stops for %d ms\n", ms);
+#ifdef _WIN32
+    Sleep((DWORD)ms);
+#else
+    usleep((useconds_t)ms * 1000u);
+#endif
+}

+/* ---- A stall doesn't end GT5's sound (AUDIO_TICK_GUARD, on unless 0) ------------------------------
+ * GT5's sound tick thread (func_00C0E35C in the lifted code) is, in full:
+ *     cellAudioSetNotifyEventQueue(key);
+ *     while (obj->running)                                                  // obj+4
+ *         if (sys_event_queue_receive(obj->queue, &ev, 1000000) != 0) break; // 1 s, any error: out
+ *         else { lock; for each listener: listener->vtbl[2](listener); unlock; }  // the next block
+ *     cellAudioRemoveNotifyEventQueue(key);                                 // and the thread ends
+ * Its start function (func_00C0E17C) makes the queue and the thread only while the thread id it keeps
+ * (obj+0) is 0, and only the stop function (func_00C0E11C: running = 0, destroy the queue, join) sets
+ * it back to 0. So a thread that left on a timeout is never started again, and the sound comes in
+ * one-second bursts for the rest of the session. On the PS3 the audio clock never stops while cellAudio
+ * runs, so that timeout means the sound system is gone; here it fired whenever the host held the
+ * mixing thread for a second (a stall of the whole PC, a driver, paging: "the last 1001.5 ms ago").
+ * So sys_event.c asks before a timed wait on an event queue runs out: for a queue ticked here, while
+ * the mixing thread runs, a tick is surely coming, and the wait goes on.
+ * Not ticks from another clock: GT5 writes one block per tick, in order, into a 16-block ring, so ticks
+ * without the reads that go with them run its writer round the ring onto blocks not yet played, and in
+ * a stall of the whole PC another thread stops too (after it, the waiter's timeout and the first tick
+ * race). Not re-arming the queue: the thread is gone, and GT5 would only start another after its stop
+ * function cleared obj+0. Called with the queue's lock held: no locks taken here. */
+static unsigned long s_tick_guard_saves;
+static int audio_tick_guard(uint64_t key)
+{
+    if (!s_audio_initialized || !s_mix_thread_running) return 0;
+    for (int i = 0; i < CELL_AUDIO_MAX_NOTIFY_EVENT_QUEUES; i++) {
+        const AudioNotifySlot* s = &s_notify_queues[i];
+        if (!s->in_use || s->key != key) continue;
+        const unsigned long n = ++s_tick_guard_saves;
+        if (n <= 8 || (n & (n - 1)) == 0)
+            fprintf(stderr, "[cellAudio] a wait for a sound tick on queue 0x%llX ran out, the last tick %.1f ms ago: "
+                    "it waits on (%lu times so far)\n", (unsigned long long)key,
+                    s->pushed ? (double)(audio_now_us() - s->last_us) / 1000.0 : -1.0, n);
+        return 1;
+    }
+    return 0;
 }

+/* cellAudioSetPortLevel(port, level): the level comes in f1, which only the context
+ * can reach. Zero is a real level here, unlike the port parameter's. */
+static void hle_audio_set_port_level(ppu_context* ctx)
+{
+    const u32 port = (u32)ctx->gpr[3];
+    const float level = (float)ctx->fpr[1];
+    if (!s_audio_initialized) { ctx->gpr[3] = (u64)(int64_t)(s32)CELL_AUDIO_ERROR_NOT_INIT; return; }

+        ctx->gpr[3] = (u64)(int64_t)(s32)CELL_AUDIO_ERROR_PORT_NOT_OPEN;
+        return;
+    }
+    mutex_lock(&s_audio_mutex);
+    s_ports[port].set_level = level < 0.0f ? 0.0f : level > 4.0f ? 4.0f : level;
+    s_ports[port].level_set = 1;
+    mutex_unlock(&s_audio_mutex);
+    { static int n = 0; if (PS3_LOG_FIRST(n, 16))
+        printf("[cellAudio] SetPortLevel(port=%u, level=%.3f)\n", port, level); }
+    ctx->gpr[3] = CELL_OK;
+}

+/*
+ * ps3recomp - the PC steering wheel behind the emulated G27 (see wheel.h)
+ *
+ * Windows: DirectInput 8, which every wheel driver (Logitech G HUB / LGS,
+ * Thrustmaster, Fanatec) serves, force feedback included. One thread owns the
+ * device: it looks for a wheel every few seconds until one is there, polls it
+ * every millisecond, publishes a WheelInput, and keeps the wheel's effects in
+ * step with the four force slots and default spring the G27 decoder holds.
+ *
+ * Settings (environment):
+ *   PS3_WHEEL            unset/auto: use the first wheel found.  off: never.
+ *                        (The game controllers seen are listed once in the log.)
+ *                        virtual: a G27 with no PC device behind it, for testing
+ *                        the game side; PS3_WHEEL_VIRTUAL=steer=-1,throttle=1,delay=190
+ *                        holds the rim and pedals there from that second on.
+ *                        anything else: a wheel whose name or VID:PID contains it.
+ *   PS3_WHEEL_RANGE      degrees of rotation the PC wheel is set to (900).
+ *   PS3_WHEEL_FFB        force feedback strength in percent (100; 0 = off).
+ *   PS3_WHEEL_FFB_INVERT 1 = the game's constant forces push the other way.
+ *   PS3_WHEEL_PEDALS     e.g. throttle=Y,brake=RZ,clutch=Z (axes X Y Z RX RY RZ S0 S1);
+ *                        add inv to a pedal (brake=RZinv) if it reads backwards.
+ *                        Throttle and brake on one axis (older wheels: it rests in the
+ *                        middle and there's no brake axis; or throttle=Y,brake=Y) are
+ *                        split where it rests: below is throttle, throttle=Yinv swaps.
+ *   PS3_WHEEL_STEER      steering axis (X).
+ *   PS3_WHEEL_BUTTONS    e.g. cross=1,circle=3,start=10, by the numbers Windows'
+ *                        Game Controllers panel shows (1 = first button);
+ *                        up/down/left/right put the d-pad on buttons, and
+ *                        throttle/brake/clutch a pedal (brake=4: button 4 brakes fully).
+ *   PS3_WHEEL_MENU       how a wheel with no d-pad moves through menus. Unset: at the
+ *                        game's menus (it plays its menu centring spring there),
+ *                        turning the rim is d-pad left/right and the throttle / brake
+ *                        are down / up. off: never. on: also on a wheel with a d-pad.
+ *   PS3_WHEEL_PEDAL_DEVICE   pedals that are a USB device of their own (a direct-drive base with
+ *                        separate pedals): its name or VID:PID, or part of it, as the "[wheel] found"
+ *                        lines list it. The pedals are read from it; PS3_WHEEL_PEDALS then names its
+ *                        axes (unset: the axes it has, in order X Y Z RX ..., are throttle, brake,
+ *                        clutch). The wheel keeps the steering and the force feedback.
+ *   PS3_WHEEL_BUTTON_DEVICE  the same for the buttons (a rim or a button box on its own USB): the
+ *                        buttons, the d-pad (its hat, else the wheel's) and PS3_WHEEL_BUTTONS' numbers
+ *                        are that device's. The in-game menu's wheel page sets both.
+ *   PS3_WHEEL_THROTTLE_DEVICE / _BRAKE_DEVICE / _CLUTCH_DEVICE  one pedal on a device of its own (unset: the
+ *                        pedals' device, else the wheel; "wheel": the wheel's own). Its axis is still the
+ *                        PS3_WHEEL_PEDALS one (unset: that device's first axis). The wheel page's pedal rows
+ *                        set these to the device the pedal is pushed on.
+ *   PS3_WHEEL_SHIFTER    1/0: report an H-shifter attached or not (default: once
+ *                        a gear is engaged).
+ *   PS3_WHEEL_TRACE      1 = log what the wheel and the game exchange.
+ *
+ * Or the mouse steers the G27 (PS3_MOUSE_STEER=1, off by default; see "Mouse steering" below).
+ */
+#include "wheel.h"
+#include "gt5_menu.h"          /* gt5_menu_input_captured */
+#include "gt5_settings.h"      /* force feedback and mouse steering follow the settings registry */
+#include <stdio.h>
+#include <stdlib.h>
+#include <string.h>
+#include <ctype.h>
+#include <math.h>

+    return s_trace;

+typedef struct {
+    int  steer;

+    int  pedal_inv[3];      /* -1 = released where it rests (see pedal()), 2 = the other end */
+    int  btn[WHEEL_BTN_COUNT];  /* host button index (0-based) per G27 button, -1 = none */

+/* Pedals and buttons on a device of their own (PS3_WHEEL_PEDAL_DEVICE / PS3_WHEEL_BUTTON_DEVICE): a
+ * direct-drive base with USB pedals, a rim or a button box that is its own USB device, as RPCS3's G27
+ * lets each part come from any device (Discord, 23 Nov 2026). The wheel keeps the steering and the
+ * force feedback; this device is only read, never held exclusively.
+ * One pedal can be on a device of its own too (PS3_WHEEL_THROTTLE_DEVICE / _BRAKE_DEVICE / _CLUTCH_DEVICE):
+ * a player's throttle and clutch are one USB device and his brake another (Discord, 24 Nov 2026). */
+enum { XD_PEDALS, XD_BUTTONS, XD_THROTTLE, XD_BRAKE, XD_CLUTCH, XD_COUNT };
+typedef struct {
+    const char*           what;              /* "pedals" / "buttons" / "throttle" ..., for the log */
+    char                  match[128];        /* lower case; "" = the wheel's own */
+    int                   on_wheel;          /* match names the wheel itself: read from it as usual */
+    int                   forced_wheel;      /* one pedal's device set to "wheel": that pedal is the wheel's own */
+    LPDIRECTINPUTDEVICE8W dev;
+    char                  name[260];
+    unsigned short        vid, pid;
+    int                   axis_present[AX_COUNT];
+    int                   has_hat;
+    unsigned long         buttons;
+    ULONGLONG             next_look;         /* not there: looked for again then */
+    unsigned              looks;             /* looks since the wheel was opened */
+    int                   said_missing;
+    ULONGLONG             last_good;         /* last reading taken (GetTickCount64) */
+    ULONGLONG             fail_since;
+    DIJOYSTATE2           js;                /* the last reading */
+    int                   ok;                /* js is recent enough to use */
+    /* pedals only: where the axes rest, as for the wheel (see dev_poll) */
+    int                   rest_known, rest_have;
+    unsigned short        rest_vid, rest_pid;
+    LONG                  rest[AX_COUNT];
+} XDev;
+static XDev s_xd[XD_COUNT] = { { "pedals" }, { "buttons" }, { "throttle" }, { "brake" }, { "clutch" } };
+/* The pedals / buttons come from a device of their own (configured and not the wheel itself). */
+static int xd_separate(const XDev* d) { return d->match[0] && !d->on_wheel; }
+/* A device the pedals (or one of them) are read from. */
+static int xd_is_pedal(int x) { return x == XD_PEDALS || x >= XD_THROTTLE; }
+/* Where pedal p (0 throttle, 1 brake, 2 clutch) is read from: its own device, else the pedals' device,
+ * else the wheel (-1). */
+static int pedal_src(int p)
+{
+    const XDev* own = &s_xd[XD_THROTTLE + p];
+    if (own->forced_wheel) return -1;
+    if (xd_separate(own)) return XD_THROTTLE + p;
+    if (xd_separate(&s_xd[XD_PEDALS])) return XD_PEDALS;
+    return -1;
+}

+static void lower(char* s) { for (; *s; s++) *s = (char)tolower((unsigned char)*s); }

+static void read_settings(void)
+{
+    if (s_mode >= 0) return;
+    const char* e = getenv("PS3_WHEEL");
+    char v[128] = "";
+    if (e) { snprintf(v, sizeof v, "%s", e); lower(v); }
+    if (!*v || !strcmp(v, "auto") || !strcmp(v, "1") || !strcmp(v, "on")) s_mode = MODE_AUTO;
+    else if (!strcmp(v, "off") || !strcmp(v, "0") || !strcmp(v, "no")) s_mode = MODE_OFF;
+    else if (!strcmp(v, "list")) s_mode = MODE_AUTO;   /* kept: the list is always printed once now */
+    else if (!strcmp(v, "virtual")) s_mode = MODE_VIRTUAL;
+    else { s_mode = MODE_MATCH; snprintf(s_match, sizeof s_match, "%s", v); }
+    /* Mouse steering takes the G27 over: a PC wheel isn't looked for while it's on. */
+    e = getenv("PS3_MOUSE_STEER");
+    if (e && *e) {
+        char m[16]; snprintf(m, sizeof m, "%s", e); lower(m);
+        if (!strcmp(m, "1") || !strcmp(m, "on") || !strcmp(m, "yes")) s_mode = MODE_MOUSE;
+    }
+    e = getenv("PS3_WHEEL_FFB");
+    if (e && *e) { s_gain = atoi(e); if (s_gain < 0) s_gain = 0; if (s_gain > 100) s_gain = 100; }
+    e = getenv("PS3_WHEEL_FFB_INVERT");
+    if (e && *e == '1') s_ffb_sign = -1.f;
+    e = getenv("PS3_WHEEL_SHIFTER");
+    if (e && *e) s_shifter_cfg = (*e == '1');
+    e = getenv("PS3_WHEEL_MENU");
+    if (e && *e) {
+        char m[16]; snprintf(m, sizeof m, "%s", e); lower(m);
+        if (!strcmp(m, "off") || !strcmp(m, "0") || !strcmp(m, "no")) s_menu_cfg = 0;
+        else if (!strcmp(m, "on") || !strcmp(m, "1") || !strcmp(m, "yes")) s_menu_cfg = 1;
+    }
+    static const char* const xkey[XD_COUNT] = { "PS3_WHEEL_PEDAL_DEVICE", "PS3_WHEEL_BUTTON_DEVICE",
+        "PS3_WHEEL_THROTTLE_DEVICE", "PS3_WHEEL_BRAKE_DEVICE", "PS3_WHEEL_CLUTCH_DEVICE" };
+    for (int x = 0; x < XD_COUNT; x++) {
+        s_xd[x].match[0] = 0;
+        s_xd[x].forced_wheel = 0;
+        e = getenv(xkey[x]);
+        if (!e) continue;
+        while (*e == ' ') e++;   /* a name typed with spaces around it */
+        snprintf(s_xd[x].match, sizeof s_xd[x].match, "%s", e);
+        size_t n = strlen(s_xd[x].match);
+        while (n && s_xd[x].match[n - 1] == ' ') s_xd[x].match[--n] = 0;
+        lower(s_xd[x].match);
+        if (!strcmp(s_xd[x].match, "wheel")) {   /* "wheel": the wheel's own (for one pedal: even with a pedals' device) */
+            s_xd[x].match[0] = 0;
+            s_xd[x].forced_wheel = x >= XD_THROTTLE;
+        }
+    }
+}

+static int axis_by_name(const char* s, int* inv)
+{
+    char n[16]; int i = 0;
+    while (s[i] && s[i] != ',' && i < 15) { n[i] = (char)toupper((unsigned char)s[i]); i++; }
+    n[i] = 0;
+    *inv = -1;
+    char* p = strstr(n, "INV");
+    if (p) { *p = 0; *inv = 2; }   /* 2 = flip whatever the default is */
+    for (int a = 0; a < AX_COUNT; a++) if (!strcmp(n, k_axis_name[a])) return a;
+    if (!strcmp(n, "SLIDER") || !strcmp(n, "SLIDER0")) return AX_S0;
+    if (!strcmp(n, "NONE")) return AX_NONE;
+    return -2;
+}

+/* PS3_WHEEL_PEDALS over whatever the pedals' axes are by default. */
+static void pedals_override(WheelMap* m)
+{
+    const char* e = getenv("PS3_WHEEL_PEDALS");
+    if (!e || !*e) return;
+    static const char* const pn[3] = { "throttle", "brake", "clutch" };
+    char buf[256]; snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, "%s", e); lower(buf);
+    for (int p = 0; p < 3; p++) {
+        const char* at = strstr(buf, pn[p]);
+        if (!at || at[strlen(pn[p])] != '=') continue;
+        int inv;
+        int a = axis_by_name(at + strlen(pn[p]) + 1, &inv);
+        if (a == -2) continue;
+        m->pedal[p] = a;
+        if (inv == 2) m->pedal_inv[p] = 2;
+    }
+}

+/* Defaults by model, then the PS3_WHEEL_* overrides. */
+static void build_map(WheelMap* m, u16 vid, u16 pid)
+{
+    m->steer = AX_X;
+    for (int i = 0; i < WHEEL_BTN_COUNT; i++) m->btn[i] = i;   /* G29/G923 order */
+    for (int d = 0; d < 4; d++) m->dpad[d] = -1;
+    for (int p = 0; p < 3; p++) m->pbtn[p] = -1;
+    /* Pedals rest at the top of their range on Logitech wheels. Axis usage
+     * differs: G29 / G923 (PlayStation) put the clutch on Z and the brake on
+     * Rz, the G920 / G923 (Xbox) the other way round. */
+    m->pedal[0] = AX_Y; m->pedal[1] = AX_RZ; m->pedal[2] = AX_Z;
+    m->pedal_inv[0] = m->pedal_inv[1] = m->pedal_inv[2] = -1;
+    if (vid == 0x044F) {
+        /* Thrustmaster, pedals "separate" (their control panel's normal mode): accelerator on
+         * Rz, brake on Y, clutch on the first slider, as Thrustmaster's manuals list them. A
+         * T-GT under the Logitech layout had the throttle and the brake swapped (a player, 15
+         * Nov 2026). In "combined" mode both share Y: see the rest-point check in dev_poll. */
+        m->pedal[0] = AX_RZ; m->pedal[1] = AX_Y; m->pedal[2] = AX_S0;
+    }
+    if (vid == 0x046D) {
+        if (pid == 0xC262 || pid == 0xC26D || pid == 0xC26E) {   /* G920, G923 Xbox */
+            static const int xb[] = {
+                WHEEL_BTN_CROSS, WHEEL_BTN_CIRCLE, WHEEL_BTN_SQUARE, WHEEL_BTN_TRIANGLE,
+                WHEEL_BTN_R1, WHEEL_BTN_L1, WHEEL_BTN_START, WHEEL_BTN_SELECT,
+                WHEEL_BTN_R3, WHEEL_BTN_L3 };
+            for (int i = 0; i < WHEEL_BTN_COUNT; i++)
+                if (i < WHEEL_BTN_GEAR1) m->btn[i] = -1;
+            for (int h = 0; h < 10; h++) m->btn[xb[h]] = h;
+            m->pedal[1] = AX_Z; m->pedal[2] = AX_RZ;
+        } else if (pid == 0xC299 || pid == 0xC29A || pid == 0xC29B || pid == 0xC298 || pid == 0xC294) {
+            m->pedal[1] = AX_Z; m->pedal[2] = AX_RZ;              /* G25 / DFGT / G27 / DFP */
+        }
+    }
+    const char* e = getenv("PS3_WHEEL_STEER");
+    int inv;
+    if (e && *e) { int a = axis_by_name(e, &inv); if (a >= 0) m->steer = a; }
+    pedals_override(m);
+    e = getenv("PS3_WHEEL_BUTTONS");
+    if (e && *e) {
+        char buf[512]; snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, "%s", e); lower(buf);
+        int set[WHEEL_BTN_COUNT] = { 0 };
+        for (char* tok = strtok(buf, ",; "); tok; tok = strtok(NULL, ",; ")) {
+            char* eq = strchr(tok, '=');
+            if (!eq) continue;
+            *eq = 0;
+            for (int i = 0; i < WHEEL_BTN_COUNT; i++)
+                if (!strcmp(tok, k_btn_name[i])) { m->btn[i] = atoi(eq + 1) - 1; set[i] = 1; }   /* 1-based, 0 = none */
+            for (int d = 0; d < 4; d++)
+                if (!strcmp(tok, k_dpad_name[d])) m->dpad[d] = atoi(eq + 1) - 1;
+            /* A pedal on a button, for a wheel whose pedals are missing or broken. */
+            static const char* const pn[3] = { "throttle", "brake", "clutch" };
+            for (int p = 0; p < 3; p++)
+                if (!strcmp(tok, pn[p])) m->pbtn[p] = atoi(eq + 1) - 1;
+        }
+        /* A button given a job here leaves the one it had by default only: start=8 on an
+         * eight-button wheel makes button 8 Start, not Start and L2. */
+        for (int i = 0; i < WHEEL_BTN_COUNT; i++) {
+            if (set[i] || m->btn[i] < 0) continue;
+            int taken = 0;
+            for (int j = 0; j < WHEEL_BTN_COUNT; j++) if (set[j] && m->btn[j] == m->btn[i]) taken = 1;
+            for (int d = 0; d < 4; d++) if (m->dpad[d] == m->btn[i]) taken = 1;
+            for (int p = 0; p < 3; p++) if (m->pbtn[p] == m->btn[i]) taken = 1;
+            if (taken) m->btn[i] = -1;
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ * Published state
+ * -------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
+static SRWLOCK      s_pub_lock = SRWLOCK_INIT;
+static WheelInput   s_pub;
+static ULONGLONG    s_pub_ms;   /* when the device thread last published (GetTickCount64) */
+static HANDLE       s_thread;
+static volatile LONG s_stop;
+static volatile LONG s_ffb_dirty = 1;
+static int          s_started;
+
+/* Called on the USB worker thread only (cellUsbd.c). */
+int wheel_host_read(WheelInput* out)
+{
+    AcquireSRWLockShared(&s_pub_lock);
+    *out = s_pub;
+    const ULONGLONG at = s_pub_ms;
+    ReleaseSRWLockShared(&s_pub_lock);
+    /* The device thread publishes every millisecond or two. When it stops (stuck in the
+     * wheel's driver, or the PC too busy to run it) the game must not keep the last rim and
+     * pedal positions, which steers the car into a wall with the throttle held: the rim is
+     * centred and the pedals released until the thread is back. */
+    static int stale;
+    static unsigned said;
+    if (out->connected && at) {
+        const ULONGLONG age = GetTickCount64() - at;
+        if (age >= 250) {
+            const int shifter = out->shifter;
+            memset(out, 0, sizeof *out);
+            out->connected = 1; out->hat = -1; out->shifter = shifter;
+            if (!stale && said < 20) {
+                said++;
+                fprintf(stderr, "[wheel] no reading from the PC wheel for %llu ms: rim centred, pedals released "
+                                "until it answers\n", age);
+            }
+            stale = 1;
+        } else if (stale) {
+            stale = 0;
+            if (said < 20) { said++; fprintf(stderr, "[wheel] reading the PC wheel again\n"); }
+        }
+    }
+    /* The in-game menu has the input: the game gets a centred rim and released pedals, as it gets a
+     * controller at rest. */
+    if (out->connected && gt5_menu_input_captured()) {
+        const int shifter = out->shifter;
+        memset(out, 0, sizeof *out);
+        out->connected = 1; out->hat = -1; out->shifter = shifter;
+    }
+    return out->connected;
+}
+
+void wheel_host_ffb_changed(void) { InterlockedExchange(&s_ffb_dirty, 1); }
+
+unsigned wheel_host_pad_buttons(void)
+{
+    AcquireSRWLockShared(&s_pub_lock);
+    const WheelInput in = s_pub;
+    const ULONGLONG at = s_pub_ms;
+    ReleaseSRWLockShared(&s_pub_lock);
+    if (!in.connected || !at || GetTickCount64() - at >= 250) return 0;
+    /* CELL_PAD_CTRL_*: select 1<<0, l3 1<<1, r3 1<<2, start 1<<3, up 1<<4, right 1<<5, down 1<<6,
+     * left 1<<7, l2 1<<8, r2 1<<9, l1 1<<10, r1 1<<11, triangle 1<<12, circle 1<<13, cross 1<<14,
+     * square 1<<15 */
+    static const struct { int wheel; unsigned pad; } k[] = {
+        { WHEEL_BTN_CROSS, 1u << 14 }, { WHEEL_BTN_SQUARE, 1u << 15 }, { WHEEL_BTN_CIRCLE, 1u << 13 },
+        { WHEEL_BTN_TRIANGLE, 1u << 12 }, { WHEEL_BTN_R1, 1u << 11 }, { WHEEL_BTN_L1, 1u << 10 },
+        { WHEEL_BTN_R2, 1u << 9 }, { WHEEL_BTN_L2, 1u << 8 }, { WHEEL_BTN_SELECT, 1u << 0 },
+        { WHEEL_BTN_START, 1u << 3 }, { WHEEL_BTN_R3, 1u << 2 }, { WHEEL_BTN_L3, 1u << 1 } };
+    unsigned b = 0;
+    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof k / sizeof k[0]; i++)
+        if (in.buttons & (1u << k[i].wheel)) b |= k[i].pad;
+    /* The hat: 0 up, then clockwise in eighths (the rim at the game's menus makes one too: menu_dpad). */
+    static const unsigned hat[8] = { 1u << 4, (1u << 4) | (1u << 5), 1u << 5, (1u << 6) | (1u << 5),
+                                     1u << 6, (1u << 6) | (1u << 7), 1u << 7, (1u << 4) | (1u << 7) };
+    if (in.hat >= 0 && in.hat < 8) b |= hat[in.hat];
+    return b;
+}
+
+static void publish(const WheelInput* in)
+{
+    AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&s_pub_lock);
+    s_pub = *in;
+    s_pub_ms = GetTickCount64();
+    ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&s_pub_lock);
+}
+
+/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ * Device
+ * -------------------------------------------------------------------------*/
+static LPDIRECTINPUT8W       s_di;
+static LPDIRECTINPUTDEVICE8W s_dev;
+static HWND                  s_hwnd;
+static int                   s_has_ffb;
+static u16                   s_vid, s_pid;
+static char                  s_name[260];
+static GUID                  s_inst;         /* the wheel's DirectInput instance */
+static int                   s_base_has_hat; /* the wheel itself has a d-pad (s_has_hat may come from a button device) */
+/* Every game controller the last look listed, for the in-game menu's "Pedals from" / "Buttons from". */
+static char                  s_devlist[GT5_MENU_WHEEL_DEVICES][64];
+static int                   s_devlist_n;
+static WheelMap              s_map;
+static int                   s_rest_known;
+static ULONGLONG             s_rest_wait;    /* when the wait for the wheel's first report began */
+static LONG                  s_rest[AX_COUNT];
+/* Rest points survive the same wheel dropping out and coming back: measured again then, a pedal
+ * or the rim held at that moment would become "rest" (a held throttle staying on afterwards). */
+static int                   s_rest_have;
+static u16                   s_rest_vid, s_rest_pid;
+static ULONGLONG             s_lost_at;      /* when the wheel last stopped answering for good, 0 = never */
+static int                   s_axis_present[AX_COUNT];
+static int                   s_shifter_seen;
+static ULONGLONG             s_ffb_retry_at;
+/* Throttle and brake on one axis (see pedal()), decided once its rest point is known. */
+static int                   s_split;
+static LONG                  s_split_at;
+static int                   s_split_swap;   /* 1 = above the rest point is the throttle */
+
+typedef struct {
+    GUID inst;
+    char name[260];
+    u16  vid, pid;
+    int  score;
+} Cand;
+
+static void utf8(const WCHAR* w, char* out, int cap)
+{
+    if (!WideCharToMultiByte(CP_UTF8, 0, w, -1, out, cap, NULL, NULL)) out[0] = 0;
+}
+
+static int contains_ci(const char* hay, const char* needle)
+{
+    char h[300]; snprintf(h, sizeof h, "%s", hay); lower(h);
+    return strstr(h, needle) != NULL;
+}
+
+static int s_enum_count;
+
+/* A device's name or VID:PID ("046d:c24f") contains this (lower case) text. */
+static int dev_matches(const char* name, u16 vid, u16 pid, const char* match)
+{
+    if (!match || !*match) return 0;
+    char vp[16]; snprintf(vp, sizeof vp, "%04x:%04x", vid, pid);
+    return contains_ci(name, match) || strstr(vp, match) != NULL;
+}
+
+static void devlist_add(const char* name)
+{
+    for (int i = 0; i < s_devlist_n; i++) if (!strncmp(s_devlist[i], name, sizeof s_devlist[i] - 1)) return;
+    if (s_devlist_n < GT5_MENU_WHEEL_DEVICES) snprintf(s_devlist[s_devlist_n++], sizeof s_devlist[0], "%s", name);
+}
+
+static BOOL CALLBACK enum_cb(LPCDIDEVICEINSTANCEW di, LPVOID ctx)
+{
+    Cand* best = (Cand*)ctx;
+    s_enum_count++;
+    Cand c; memset(&c, 0, sizeof c);
+    c.inst = di->guidInstance;
+    utf8(di->tszProductName, c.name, sizeof c.name);
+    c.vid = LOWORD(di->guidProduct.Data1);
+    c.pid = HIWORD(di->guidProduct.Data1);
+    static const u8 zero[sizeof(GUID)];
+    const int ff = memcmp(&di->guidFFDriver, zero, sizeof(GUID)) != 0;
+    const int driving = GET_DIDEVICE_TYPE(di->dwDevType) == DI8DEVTYPE_DRIVING;
+    char vp[16]; snprintf(vp, sizeof vp, "%04x:%04x", c.vid, c.pid);
+    devlist_add(c.name);
+    if (s_list)
+        fprintf(stderr, "[wheel] found %s \"%s\"%s%s\n", vp, c.name,
+                driving ? " (wheel)" : "", ff ? " (force feedback)" : "");
+    /* The device named for the pedals or the buttons is not the wheel, unless it is the one with
+     * force feedback (the player named the wheel itself there): some pedal sets call themselves
+     * a driving device and could outscore a base that doesn't. */
+    int extra = 0;
+    for (int x = 0; x < XD_COUNT; x++) if (dev_matches(c.name, c.vid, c.pid, s_xd[x].match)) extra = 1;
+    if (extra && !ff && !(s_mode == MODE_MATCH && dev_matches(c.name, c.vid, c.pid, s_match)))
+        return DIENUM_CONTINUE;
+    if (s_mode == MODE_MATCH) {
+        c.score = (contains_ci(c.name, s_match) || strstr(vp, s_match)) ? 10 : 0;
+    } else {
+        if (driving) c.score += 4;
+        if (ff) c.score += 1;
+        /* Force feedback on anything but a gamepad is a wheel base nearly always: a MOZA R5 Base calls
+         * itself neither a driving device nor a wheel, and was passed over (a player, 24 Nov 2026). Pads'
+         * rumble isn't DirectInput force feedback, but a pad that has it is still no wheel. */
+        if (ff && GET_DIDEVICE_TYPE(di->dwDevType) != DI8DEVTYPE_GAMEPAD) c.score += 3;
+        /* Some wheels call themselves a joystick and have no force feedback (the
+         * Genius Speed Wheel 3 Vibration): "wheel" in the name is enough. */
+        if (contains_ci(c.name, "wheel") || contains_ci(c.name, "driving force"))
+            c.score += 3;
+        else if (contains_ci(c.name, "racing"))
+            c.score += 2;
+        if (c.score < 3) c.score = 0;   /* a pad with rumble is not a wheel */
+    }
+    if (c.score > best->score) *best = c;
+    return DIENUM_CONTINUE;
+}
+
+static void dev_prop_dword(LPDIRECTINPUTDEVICE8W dev, REFGUID prop, DWORD how, DWORD obj, DWORD value)
+{
+    DIPROPDWORD p;
+    p.diph.dwSize = sizeof(DIPROPDWORD);
+    p.diph.dwHeaderSize = sizeof(DIPROPHEADER);
+    p.diph.dwObj = obj;
+    p.diph.dwHow = how;
+    p.dwData = value;
+    IDirectInputDevice8_SetProperty(dev, prop, &p.diph);
+}
+static void set_prop_dword(REFGUID prop, DWORD how, DWORD obj, DWORD value) { dev_prop_dword(s_dev, prop, how, obj, value); }
+
+/* Every axis 0..65535, no dead zone, as the wheel's (a pedal's travel is all its own). */
+static void dev_full_range(LPDIRECTINPUTDEVICE8W dev)
+{
+    DIPROPRANGE r;
+    r.diph.dwSize = sizeof(DIPROPRANGE);
+    r.diph.dwHeaderSize = sizeof(DIPROPHEADER);
+    r.diph.dwObj = 0;
+    r.diph.dwHow = DIPH_DEVICE;
+    r.lMin = 0; r.lMax = 65535;
