`GT5/scripts/install_pkg.ps1`:

```ps1
# Installs GT5 game updates and DLC from their .pkg files, for the port, by itself (no RPCS3):
#   powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File GT5\scripts\install_pkg.ps1 <file.pkg or folder> [more ...]
#                [-Gt5 <GT5 folder>]
# (The launcher's Help page has a button for it.)
#
# 1. Each package is unpacked straight into GT5\hdd0\game\<title ID> by ps3_unlock.py (the port's own
#    tool), the way a PS3 installs it. Its own checksum is checked before anything is written. Updates go
#    in version order (1.05, 1.06 ... 2.17): each one goes on top of the one before it; ones that are
#    installed already are skipped.
# 2. update_exe.ps1 unlocks the newest update's EBOOT.BIN into GT5\input\EBOOT.elf.
# Then setup.bat (or setup.ps1) generates and builds the game for that version once (about an hour).
#
# DLC: a DLC package installs its voucher; the game still needs that licence's key in
# GT5\hdd0\home\00000001\exdata (README, DLC). Nothing here makes or holds keys.
#
# -Rpcs3 is still accepted and ignored (older launchers pass it). For testing: GT5_PKG_NOPAUSE=1 doesn't
# wait for Enter at the end.
param([Parameter(Position = 0, ValueFromRemainingArguments = $true)][string[]]$Paths,
      [string]$Gt5 = "", [string]$Rpcs3 = "", [int]$TimeoutMinutes = 30)
$ErrorActionPreference = "Continue"
if (-not $Gt5) { $Gt5 = Split-Path $PSScriptRoot -Parent }   # (empty in this param block's defaults)
$base = Split-Path $Gt5 -Parent

function Say([string]$s, [string]$c = "Gray") { Write-Host $s -ForegroundColor $c }
function Fail([string]$s) { Say $s Yellow; if ($env:GT5_PKG_NOPAUSE -ne "1") { Read-Host "Press Enter to close" | Out-Null }; exit 2 }

# ---- The packages: content ID from each header, updates sorted by version, DLC after ----------------------
$files = @()
foreach ($p in $Paths) {
    if (-not $p) { continue }
    $p = $p.Trim('"')
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $p -PathType Container) { $files += @(Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $p -Filter *.pkg -File | ForEach-Object FullName) }
    elseif (Test-Path -LiteralPath $p) { $files += (Resolve-Path -LiteralPath $p).Path }
    else { Say "  not found: $p" Yellow }
}
if (-not $files) { Fail "No .pkg files given. Usage: install_pkg.ps1 <file.pkg or folder> [more ...]" }

$pkgs = @()
foreach ($f in ($files | Select-Object -Unique)) {
    $fs = $null
    try {
        $fs = [IO.File]::OpenRead($f); $h = New-Object byte[] 0x60; [void]$fs.Read($h, 0, $h.Length)
    } catch { Say "  can't read $f" Yellow; continue } finally { if ($fs) { $fs.Close() } }
    if ($h[0] -ne 0x7F -or $h[1] -ne 0x50 -or $h[2] -ne 0x4B -or $h[3] -ne 0x47) { Say "  not a PS3 package: $f" Yellow; continue }
    $cid = [Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetString($h, 0x30, 0x24).TrimEnd([char]0)
    $title = if ($cid.Length -ge 16) { $cid.Substring(7, 9) } else { "" }
    # Game updates are named ...-A<version>-V<pkg version>-...; their content ID ends in zeros.
    $ver = ""
    if ([IO.Path]::GetFileName($f) -match '-A(\d\d)(\d\d)-V\d{4}') { $ver = "$($Matches[1]).$($Matches[2])" }
    $isUpdate = [bool]$ver -and $cid -match '-0{16}$'
    $pkgs += [pscustomobject]@{ File = $f; Cid = $cid; Title = $title; Ver = $ver; IsUpdate = $isUpdate
                                Order = $(if ($isUpdate) { [double]$ver } else { 1000 }) }
}
if (-not $pkgs) { Fail "None of those is a PS3 package (.pkg)." }
$pkgs = @($pkgs | Sort-Object Order, File)
$titles = @($pkgs | ForEach-Object Title | Select-Object -Unique)
Say "Packages ($($pkgs.Count)):" White
foreach ($k in $pkgs) { Say ("  {0}  {1}" -f $(if ($k.IsUpdate) { "update $($k.Ver)" } else { "DLC/other " }), [IO.Path]::GetFileName($k.File)) }

# ---- The port's own tool and Python ------------------------------------------------------------------------
$tool = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "ps3_unlock.py"
$py = @((Join-Path $base "tools\python\python.exe"), (Join-Path $base "venv\Scripts\python.exe")) | Where-Object { Test-Path -LiteralPath $_ } | Select-Object -First 1
if (-not $py) { $c = Get-Command python.exe -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; if ($c) { $py = $c.Source } }
if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $tool) -or -not $py) { Fail "This install is missing a part it needs to unpack packages (GT5\scripts\ps3_unlock.py, or its Python). Run Update.bat, then try again." }
$keys = Join-Path $base "tools\ps3_keys"
$hddGame = Join-Path $Gt5 "hdd0\game"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $hddGame | Out-Null

function Read-Sfo([string]$path) {
    try { $b = [IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($path) } catch { return $null }
    if ($b.Length -lt 20 -or $b[1] -ne 0x50 -or $b[2] -ne 0x53 -or $b[3] -ne 0x46) { return $null }
    $keyT = [BitConverter]::ToUInt32($b, 8); $dataT = [BitConverter]::ToUInt32($b, 12)
    $n = [BitConverter]::ToUInt32($b, 16); $r = @{}
    for ($i = 0; $i -lt $n; $i++) {
        $e = 20 + $i * 16
        if ($e + 16 -gt $b.Length) { break }
        $ko = [BitConverter]::ToUInt16($b, $e); $fmt = [BitConverter]::ToUInt16($b, $e + 2)
        $len = [BitConverter]::ToUInt32($b, $e + 4); $do = [BitConverter]::ToUInt32($b, $e + 12)
        $k = ""; $p = $keyT + $ko
        while ($p -lt $b.Length -and $b[$p] -ne 0) { $k += [char]$b[$p]; $p++ }
        if ($dataT + $do + $len -gt $b.Length) { continue }
        if ($fmt -eq 0x0404) { $r[$k] = [BitConverter]::ToUInt32($b, $dataT + $do) }
        else { $r[$k] = [Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetString($b, $dataT + $do, $len).TrimEnd([char]0) }
    }
    return $r
}
function Installed-Ver([string]$title) {
    $s = Read-Sfo (Join-Path $hddGame "$title\PARAM.SFO")
    if ($s -and $s["APP_VER"]) { return ([string]$s["APP_VER"]).Trim() }
    return ""
}

# ---- Updates go in order: a gap is said plainly before anything is written ----------------------------------
# An update goes on top of the one before it (a player picked 2.01 to 2.11 without 1.05 to 2.00, 23 Nov 2026).
# gt5_updates.txt lists every official update in order.
$chainFile = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "gt5_updates.txt"
if (Test-Path $chainFile) {
    $csv = @(Get-Content -LiteralPath $chainFile | Where-Object { $_ -and -not $_.StartsWith("#") } | ForEach-Object { ,($_.Split(",")) })
    foreach ($t in $titles) {
        $chain = @($csv | Where-Object { $_[0] -eq $t } | ForEach-Object { $_[1] } | Sort-Object { [double]$_ })
        if (-not $chain) { continue }
        $have = Installed-Ver $t
        $given = @($pkgs | Where-Object { $_.IsUpdate -and $_.Title -eq $t -and (-not $have -or [double]$_.Ver -gt [double]$have) } | ForEach-Object Ver)
        if (-not $given) { continue }
        $missing = @($chain | Where-Object { (-not $have -or [double]$_ -gt [double]$have) -and [double]$_ -lt [double]$given[-1] -and $given -notcontains $_ })
        if ($missing) {
            $from = if ($have) { "$t $have is installed, so" } else { "Nothing of $t is installed yet, so" }
            Say "Updates install only in order, one after the other. $from these are missing before $($given[-1]): $($missing -join ', ')." Yellow
            Say "Pick those packages too (all of them from $($missing[0]) up to $($given[-1])), or use the launcher's Help > Game version and DLC, which downloads every update it needs from Sony." Yellow
            Fail "Nothing was installed."
        }
    }
}

# ---- Unpack each package into GT5\hdd0\game\<title ID> -----------------------------------------------------
$failed = @()
$updOk = 0   # updates that are in place now (installed in this run, or there already)
foreach ($k in $pkgs) {
    $name = [IO.Path]::GetFileName($k.File)
    if ($k.IsUpdate) {
        $have = Installed-Ver $k.Title
        if ($have -and [double]$have -ge [double]$k.Ver) { Say "  update $($k.Ver): $have is installed already, skipped"; $updOk++; continue }
    }
    Say "Installing $name ..." White
    $why = ""; $skipped = $false; $lastPct = -1
    & $py -I $tool pkg $k.File $hddGame --keys-dir $keys 2>&1 | ForEach-Object {
        $l = "$_"
        if ($l -match '^PKG_PROGRESS\s+(\d+)\s+(\d+)') {
            $pct = if ([double]$Matches[2] -gt 0) { [int]([math]::Floor(100.0 * [double]$Matches[1] / [double]$Matches[2] / 10) * 10) } else { 100 }
            if ($pct -gt $lastPct -and $pct -lt 100) { $lastPct = $pct; Say "  $pct %" }
        }
        elseif ($l -match '^PS3_UNLOCK_FAIL\s+\d+\s+\w+:\s*(.*)$') { $why = $Matches[1].Trim() }
        elseif ($l -match '^PKG_SKIP') { $skipped = $true }
    }
    $code = $LASTEXITCODE
    if ($code -eq 0) {
        if ($skipped) { Say "  it is installed already, skipped" }
        else { Say "  installed$(if ($k.IsUpdate) { ": $($k.Title) is now at $($k.Ver)" })" Green }
        if ($k.IsUpdate) { $updOk++ }
    } else {
        Say "  not installed: $(if ($why) { $why } else { "the unpacker stopped (code $code)" })" Yellow
        $failed += $name
        if ($k.IsUpdate) { Say "  The updates after it need it, so stopping here." Yellow; break }
    }
}
foreach ($t in $titles) {
    $v = Read-Sfo (Join-Path $hddGame "$t\PARAM.SFO")
    if ($v -and $v['APP_VER']) { Say "GT5\hdd0 now holds $t version $($v['APP_VER'])." Green }
}

# ---- The update's executable --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
& powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "update_exe.ps1") -Gt5 $Gt5
$code = $LASTEXITCODE

Say ""
if ($failed) { Say "Not installed: $($failed -join ', ')" Yellow }
# Only when an update is in place now: with none installed nothing changed, and there is nothing to build.
if ($code -eq 2) { Say "The update's data is in place, but its executable couldn't be unlocked (see above)." Yellow }
elseif ($updOk -gt 0) { Say "Next: run setup.bat (or setup.ps1) once. It generates and builds the game for this version (about an hour)." Green }
if ($pkgs | Where-Object { -not $_.IsUpdate }) { Say "DLC: the vouchers are in place; each still needs its licence key in GT5\hdd0\home\00000001\exdata (README, DLC)." }
if ($env:GT5_PKG_NOPAUSE -ne "1") { Read-Host "Press Enter to close" | Out-Null }
exit $(if ($failed) { 1 } else { 0 })
```

`GT5/scripts/joblist.py`:

```py
"""List GPUSyncArray jobs from gmem.py dumps: joblist.py <lists.bin> <lists ea> <jobs.bin> <jobs ea> <list ea> [--find ea]

Each entry is {u16 size, u16 valid, u32 job}. Prints index, job address and the segment each job writes (the
job's first pointer into the command area 0x61xxxxxx). --find names the job holding a given address.
"""
import struct
import sys

find = None
if "--find" in sys.argv:
    i = sys.argv.index("--find")
    find = int(sys.argv[i + 1], 16)
    del sys.argv[i:i + 2]
lists = open(sys.argv[1], "rb").read()
lists_ea = int(sys.argv[2], 16)
jobs = open(sys.argv[3], "rb").read()
jobs_ea = int(sys.argv[4], 16)
list_ea = int(sys.argv[5], 16)
off = list_ea - lists_ea
prev = None
idx = 0
entries = []
while off + 8 <= len(lists):
    size, valid, job = struct.unpack_from(">HHI", lists, off)
    if valid == 0:
        break
    entries.append((idx, size, valid, job))
    off += 8
    idx += 1
print("entries:", len(entries))
for idx, size, valid, job in entries:
    o = job - jobs_ea
    segs = []
    if 0 <= o < len(jobs) - 0x300:
        words = struct.unpack_from(">192I", jobs, o)
        segs = [w for w in words if 0x61000000 <= w < 0x61400000][:3]
    note = ""
    if find is not None and job <= find < job + size * 8:
        note = "  <== holds %08X" % find
    if find is None or note:
        print("%3d (0x%02X) size=%04X job=%08X segs=%s%s" % (idx, idx, size, job, " ".join("%08X" % s for s in segs), note))
```

`GT5/scripts/jobsegs.py`:

```py
import os as _gt5_os  # this clone's folders, wherever it was cloned to
GT5_DIR = _gt5_os.path.dirname(_gt5_os.path.dirname(_gt5_os.path.abspath(__file__)))
BASE_DIR = _gt5_os.path.dirname(GT5_DIR)
"""State of each GPUSyncArray job's command segment in a running gt5.exe: jobsegs.py <list ea, hex>

A job's segment starts with a jump to itself until the job has finished. Prints runs of parked and done jobs,
then each done segment's way out (the last jump in it) when --walk is given.
"""
import ctypes
import ctypes.wintypes as w
import re
import struct
import subprocess
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, (GT5_DIR + r"\scripts"))
out = subprocess.run(["python", (GT5_DIR + r"\scripts\gmem.py"), "save %s,0x800,E:/Games/gt5-recomp/GT5/logs/_list.bin" % sys.argv[1], "save 60600000,0x400000,E:/Games/gt5-recomp/GT5/logs/_jobs.bin", "save 61000000,0x1000000,E:/Games/gt5-recomp/GT5/logs/_seg.bin"], capture_output=True, text=True)
lst = open((GT5_DIR + r"\logs\_list.bin"), "rb").read()
jobs = open((GT5_DIR + r"\logs\_jobs.bin"), "rb").read()
seg = open((GT5_DIR + r"\logs\_seg.bin"), "rb").read()
rows = []
for i in range(0, len(lst), 8):
    size, valid, job = struct.unpack_from(">HHI", lst, i)
    if not valid:
        break
    o = job - 0x60600000
    if not 0 <= o < len(jobs) - 0x300:
        continue
    start = None
    for w_ in struct.unpack_from(">64I", jobs, o):
        if 0x61000000 <= w_ < 0x62000000:
            start = w_
            break
    first = struct.unpack_from(">I", seg, start - 0x61000000)[0] if start else 0
    parked = first == (0x20000000 | (start - 0x60000000)) if start else None
    rows.append((i // 8, job, start, first, parked))
print("jobs", len(rows))
run = None
for r in rows:
    state = "parked" if r[4] else "done"
    if run and run[0] == state:
        run[2] = r[0]
    else:
        if run:
            print("%-7s %3d..%3d" % (run[0], run[1], run[2]))
        run = [state, r[0], r[0]]
if run:
    print("%-7s %3d..%3d" % (run[0], run[1], run[2]))
for r in rows:
    print("%3d job=%08X seg=%08X first=%08X %s" % (r[0], r[1], r[2] or 0, r[3], "PARKED" if r[4] else ""))
```

`GT5/scripts/jobtime.py`:

```py
"""Audio job timing from a run with SPU_ORDER set: jobtime.py <err log> [from sec] [to sec]

Per notify on the sound guard: time until the job's event (job), and from that event to the next
notify (PPU). Times are host microseconds, seconds count from the first logged line.
"""
import re
import sys

rows = []
for line in open(sys.argv[1], errors="replace"):
    m = re.search(r"\[spu-order\] t=(\d+) (notify|event)(.*)", line)
    if m:
        rows.append((int(m.group(1)), m.group(2), m.group(3)))
t0 = rows[0][0]
a = float(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 0
b = float(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 1e9
job = []
ppu = []
last_notify = None
last_event = None
per_block = []
for t, k, x in rows:
    s = (t - t0) / 1e6
    if s < a or s > b:
        continue
    if k == "notify" and "0x60040180" in x:
        if last_event is not None:
            ppu.append(t - last_event)
        last_notify = t
    elif k == "event" and "q=4" in x:
        if last_notify is not None:
            job.append(t - last_notify)
        last_event = t


def show(name, v):
    if not v:
        print(name, "none")
        return
    v = sorted(v)
    n = len(v)
    print("%-4s n=%d mean=%.0f p50=%d p90=%d p99=%d max=%d" % (name, n, sum(v) / n, v[n // 2], v[n * 9 // 10], v[n * 99 // 100], v[-1]))


show("job", job)
show("ppu", ppu)
span = b - a if b < 1e8 else (rows[-1][0] - t0) / 1e6
print("span %.1f s, jobs per second %.1f" % (span, len(job) / span))
```

`GT5/scripts/kcalls.py`:

```py
"""Which win32u and ntdll calls a prof.ps1 capture sits in, for its busiest renderer thread: kcalls.py <prof.txt> [--tid n]

win32u.dll is mostly thin kernel-call stubs (NtGdiDdDDI* is the D3D kernel interface), so naming the export names the
kernel call. Prints each thread's share of samples per call; a thread is picked by its nvwgf driver samples.
"""
import collections
import re
import struct
import sys


def exports(path):
    d = open(path, "rb").read()
    pe = struct.unpack("<I", d[0x3C:0x40])[0]
    nsec = struct.unpack("<H", d[pe + 6:pe + 8])[0]
    optsz = struct.unpack("<H", d[pe + 20:pe + 22])[0]
    opt = pe + 24
    exp_rva = struct.unpack("<I", d[opt + 112:opt + 116])[0]
    secs = []
    for i in range(nsec):
        s = pe + 24 + optsz + i * 40
        vsz, va, rsz, ptr = struct.unpack("<IIII", d[s + 8:s + 24])
        secs.append((va, max(vsz, rsz), ptr))

    def off(rva):
        for va, sz, ptr in secs:
            if va <= rva < va + sz:
                return rva - va + ptr
        raise ValueError(hex(rva))

    e = off(exp_rva)
    nfun, nnames, afun, aname, aord = struct.unpack("<IIIII", d[e + 20:e + 40])
    funcs = struct.unpack("<%dI" % nfun, d[off(afun):off(afun) + 4 * nfun])
    names = struct.unpack("<%dI" % nnames, d[off(aname):off(aname) + 4 * nnames])
    ords = struct.unpack("<%dH" % nnames, d[off(aord):off(aord) + 2 * nnames])
    out = []
    for n, o in zip(names, ords):
        p = off(n)
        out.append((funcs[o], d[p:d.index(b"\0", p)].decode()))
    out.sort()
    return out


def name(table, rva):
    lo, hi = 0, len(table)
    while lo < hi:
        m = (lo + hi) // 2
        if table[m][0] <= rva:
            lo = m + 1
        else:
            hi = m
    return table[lo - 1][1] if lo else "?"


tables = {"win32u.dll": exports(r"C:\Windows\System32\win32u.dll"), "ntdll.dll": exports(r"C:\Windows\System32\ntdll.dll")}
rows = collections.defaultdict(collections.Counter)
total = collections.Counter()
for line in open(sys.argv[1], errors="replace"):
    p = line.split()
    if line.startswith("#") or len(p) < 4:
        continue
    tid, mod, rva, cnt = p[0], p[1], p[2], int(p[3])
    total[tid] += cnt
    base = mod.split("\\")[-1].lower()
    if base in tables:
        rows[tid][base.split(".")[0] + ":" + name(tables[base], int(rva, 16))] += cnt
    else:
        rows[tid][base] += cnt
for tid, c in sorted(rows.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1].get("nvwgf2umx.dll", 0))[:2]:
    print("thread", tid, "samples", total[tid])
    for k, n in c.most_common(22):
        print("  %5.1f%%  %s" % (100.0 * n / total[tid], k[:70]))

```

`GT5/scripts/labelcmds.py`:

```py
"""Find RSX semaphore commands that write given labels, in dumps saved by gmem.py: labelcmds.py <file> <ea, hex> [low hex] [high hex]

Looks for method 0x1D6C (offset) with a following 0x1D70/0x1D74 release, in any command header shape, and
prints the address, label offset and value. Reports only offsets in low..high (default 0x480..0x4F0).
"""
import struct
import sys

d = open(sys.argv[1], "rb").read()
base = int(sys.argv[2], 16)
low = int(sys.argv[3], 16) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 0x480
high = int(sys.argv[4], 16) if len(sys.argv) > 4 else 0x4F0
n = len(d) // 4
w = struct.unpack(">%dI" % n, d[:n * 4])
hits = 0
i = 0
while i < n - 3:
    x = w[i]
    if x & 0xE0030003 == 0 and x & 0xFFFC == 0x1D6C:
        cnt = (x >> 18) & 0x7FF
        off = w[i + 1]
        if low <= off <= high and cnt:
            if cnt >= 2:
                print("%08X off=%X value=%08X (m=1D70, one header)" % (base + i * 4, off, w[i + 2]))
                hits += 1
            else:
                y = w[i + 2]
                m = y & 0xFFFC
                print("%08X off=%X next header %08X value=%08X" % (base + i * 4, off, y, w[i + 3]))
                hits += 1
    i += 1
print("hits", hits)
```

```py
"""Each thread's last lwcond wait, from a run with PS3_LWC_BT=0: lastwaits.py <err log> [tid ...]"""
import re
import sys

last = {}
count = {}
tid = None
for line in open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"):
    m = re.match(r"\[GSTACK:lwc\] sp=\S+ .*tid=(\d+)", line)
    if m:
        tid = int(m.group(1))
        count[tid] = count.get(tid, 0) + 1
    elif line.startswith("[GSTACK:lwc] chain:") and tid is not None:
        last[tid] = line.split("chain:", 1)[1].strip()
want = {int(a) for a in sys.argv[2:]}
for t in sorted(last):
    if not want or t in want:
        print(f"tid {t:3d} waits={count[t]:6d}: {last[t][:330]}")
```

`GT5/scripts/lift_spu_jobs.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Lift every captured raw SPU image and regenerate src/gen/spu_jobs.c.

GT5's job binaries and its Wws_Job policy module are raw code+data blobs, not the
ELFs build_spu_workloads.py discovers. Capture them first, then lift and rebuild:

    run.ps1 -Env @{SPU_DUMP_MISS="...\\analysis\\spu_miss"}
    python scripts/lift_spu_jobs.py

The dump name carries the fingerprint the runtime computed, which is the value to
register. Run again after each round: a job only dumps once it gets dispatched,
and earlier jobs have to work for later ones to be reached.

The Wws_Job policy module streams a second family of jobs into LS 0x4000 from the
EBOOT's own data. Those are found by scanning the EBOOT (wws_jobs below) and registered
as overlays, so they run compiled instead of through the interpreter.
"""
import concurrent.futures
import hashlib
import re
import shutil
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
TOOLS = ROOT.parent / "ps3recomp" / "tools"
DUMPS = ROOT / "analysis" / "spu_miss"
OUT = ROOT / "spu" / "jobs"
REG = ROOT / "src" / "gen" / "spu_jobs.c"

# Policy modules run at LS 0xA00 (spurs_policy.c); jobs load at LS 0 (spurs_job.c).
PM_BASE = {"75BFE68AE96D7577": 0xA00}  # Wws_Job, embedded in the EBOOT at 0x0177F200

# A Wws job: 16 bytes of `ila $r2` fingerprint, then {entry, text, data, bss}, then
# {0xC0DEC0DE, ?, link base, 5}. The DMA covers text - 0x20 bytes when there's no data.
EBOOT = ROOT / "input" / "EBOOT.elf"
WWS_DIR = ROOT / "analysis" / "spu_wws"
WWS_BASE = 0x4000
WWS_IMAGE0 = 100
WWS_SAMPLE = 64  # code bytes checked at first dispatch; pins the overlay to its load address

NAME_RE = re.compile(r"^spujob_([0-9A-Fa-f]{16})_(\d+)\.bin$")

# Branches whose target is known when lifting (the interrupt window around each DMA, `bid`/`bie` to the
# next instruction, and the like) go there directly instead of through the dispatcher; the pc getter
# `brsl $rX, .+4` no longer splits a function; code entered only from outside gets a C function of its
# own; jump tables become switches; the interrupt test at labels reads the event word first. See the
# options' help in spu_lifter.py. The Wws jobs (lift_wws) and their job manager (PM_OPTS, lift); not
# the SPURS jobs. Natives (src/native/natives.txt) keep what they rely on: the functions
# of an image with a lift-sha1 pin are lifted exactly as before (--frozen-funcs), the others stay
# entered as their own functions (--keep-entries).
LIFT_OPTS = ["--const-branches", "--getpc-inline", "--seed-entries", "--jump-switch", "--irq-macro", "--irq-oneword"]
PM_OPTS = ["--const-branches", "--jump-switch", "--irq-macro", "--irq-oneword"]
# n_static, 22 Nov 2026: every image also gets its any-address form (spu_anyaddr.c: every instruction address
# enterable, used by the runtime only where the lift above has no function), registered from spu_jobs.c right
# after the image's own functions, so no address of a known image is ever interpreted.
ANY_OPTS = ["--any-address", "spu_anyaddr.c"]   # no merged groups there: the rest do nothing
NATIVES = ROOT / "src" / "native" / "natives.txt"


def native_opts(image):
    """--frozen-funcs / --keep-entries for one image, from natives.txt."""
    addrs, pinned = set(), False
    if NATIVES.exists():
        for ln in NATIVES.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
            p = ln.split()
            if len(p) < 2 or p[0] != image:
                continue
            if p[1] == "lift-sha1":
                pinned = True
            elif re.fullmatch(r"[0-9A-Fa-f]{8}", p[1]):
                addrs.add(int(p[1], 16))
    if not addrs:
        return []
    return ["--frozen-funcs" if pinned else "--keep-entries", ",".join(hex(a) for a in sorted(addrs))]


# Addresses reached only through a computed branch (scripts/spu_static_entries.txt: `<image> <address> ...`),
# lifted as entries so the runtime never has to interpret the bytes there (spu_lifter.py --entries).
STATIC_ENTRIES = ROOT / "scripts" / "spu_static_entries.txt"


# The Wws jobs' entry stub builds its own return point at 0x40C8, `ila $r0,0xDC ; a $r0,$r0,$r126`, and
# branches to the job's main, whose `bi $r0` lands at 0x40DC with no caller waiting: an entry in every job that
# has the stub, whatever the release (the list names it for the European disc's jobs).
WWS_STUB = bytes.fromhex("42006E00181F8000")


def static_entries(image, blob=None):
    addrs = set()
    if blob is not None and blob[0xC8:0xD0] == WWS_STUB:
        addrs.add(WWS_BASE + 0xDC)
    if STATIC_ENTRIES.exists():
        for ln in STATIC_ENTRIES.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
            p = ln.split("#", 1)[0].split()
            if len(p) >= 2 and p[0] == image and re.fullmatch(r"[0-9A-Fa-f]{1,8}", p[1]):
                addrs.add(int(p[1], 16))
    return ["--entries", ",".join(hex(a) for a in sorted(addrs))] if addrs else []


# A Wws job image is named after its address in the EBOOT (w<address>), and that address differs between
# releases: the game updates keep some of the disc's images byte for byte, somewhere else. The lists that go
# by name (spu_static_entries.txt, src/native/natives.txt and the native code's symbols) would then miss them.
# `<image> = <SHA-1 of the image's bytes>` lines in spu_static_entries.txt give those bytes that name in
# every release, so the same code gets the same entries and the same native functions wherever it sits.
def known_names():
    names = {}
    if STATIC_ENTRIES.exists():
        for ln in STATIC_ENTRIES.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
            p = ln.split("#", 1)[0].split()
            if len(p) >= 3 and p[1] == "=" and re.fullmatch(r"[0-9A-Fa-f]{40}", p[2]):
                names.setdefault(p[2].lower(), p[0])
    return names


def name_jobs(jobs):
    """(name, ea, entry, code, blob) for each Wws job: the listed name of its bytes, else w<its address>."""
    known = known_names()
    own = {f"w{ea:08X}" for ea, *_ in jobs}
    out, taken = [], set()
    for ea, entry, code, blob in jobs:
        name = f"w{ea:08X}"
        alias = known.get(hashlib.sha1(blob).hexdigest())
        # never a name another image of this EBOOT has by its own address, nor one given out already
        if alias and alias != name and alias not in own and alias not in taken:
            name = alias
        taken.add(name)
        out.append((name, ea, entry, code, blob))
    return out


def run(*args):
    r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, *map(str, args)], capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=ROOT)
    if r.returncode:
        print(r.stdout[-2000:], r.stderr[-2000:], sep="\n", file=sys.stderr)
        raise SystemExit(f"failed: {' '.join(map(str, args))}")
    return r.stdout


def lift(blob, fp):
    base = PM_BASE.get(fp, 0)
    outdir = OUT / f"j{fp[:8]}"
    outdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    funcs = OUT / f"j{fp[:8]}_funcs.json"
    out = run(TOOLS / "find_spu_functions.py", "--raw", "--base", hex(base), "--out", funcs, blob)
    m = re.search(r"Detected ([\d,]+) function", out)
    # The Wws job manager (the policy module) opens its interrupt window the same way (`ila $rX, next ;
    # bie $rX`, then `bid` to the next), between functions: those become direct tail calls (PM_OPTS). The
    # SPURS jobs are left as they were.
    run(TOOLS / "spu_lifter.py", blob, "--base", hex(base), "--functions", funcs,
        "--symbol-prefix", f"gt5_j{fp[:8]}", "--output", outdir, "--source-name", "spu_recomp.c", *ANY_OPTS,
        *(PM_OPTS if fp in PM_BASE else []), *static_entries(f"j{fp[:8]}"))
    return int(m.group(1).replace(",", "")) if m else 0


def wws_jobs():
    """Every Wws job in the EBOOT, as (ea, entry offset, code size, blob)."""
    d = EBOOT.read_bytes()
    phoff = struct.unpack(">Q", d[0x20:0x28])[0]
    phnum = struct.unpack(">H", d[0x38:0x3A])[0]
    jobs = []
    for i in range(phnum):
        kind, _, off, va, _, size, _, _ = struct.unpack(">IIQQQQQQ", d[phoff + i * 56:phoff + i * 56 + 56])
        if kind != 1:
            continue
        for o in range(off, off + size - 0x40, 16):
            w = struct.unpack(">12I", d[o:o + 0x30])
            if w[8] == 0xC0DEC0DE and all((x >> 25) == 0x21 and (x & 0x7F) == 2 for x in w[:4]):
                code = w[5] - 0x20
                jobs.append((va + o - off, w[4], code, d[o:o + code]))
    return jobs


def lift_wws(job):
    name, ea, entry, code, blob = job
    WWS_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path = WWS_DIR / f"{name}.bin"
    path.write_bytes(blob)
    outdir = OUT / name
    outdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    funcs = OUT / f"{name}_funcs.json"
    out = run(TOOLS / "find_spu_functions.py", "--raw", "--base", hex(WWS_BASE), "--entry", hex(WWS_BASE + entry),
              "--out", funcs, path)
    m = re.search(r"Detected ([\d,]+) function", out)
    run(TOOLS / "spu_lifter.py", path, "--base", hex(WWS_BASE), "--functions", funcs, "--code-end", hex(WWS_BASE + code),
        "--return-entries", "--merge-chunks", "--symbol-prefix", f"gt5_{name}", "--output", outdir, "--source-name", "spu_recomp.c", *ANY_OPTS,
        *LIFT_OPTS, *native_opts(name), *static_entries(name, blob))
    return int(m.group(1).replace(",", "")) if m else 0


def main():
    dumps = sorted(p for p in DUMPS.glob("spujob_*.bin") if NAME_RE.match(p.name))
    if not dumps:
        raise SystemExit(f"no spujob_*.bin in {DUMPS} -- run with SPU_DUMP_MISS first")
    fps = [NAME_RE.match(p.name).group(1).upper() for p in dumps]
    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(8) as ex:
        counts = list(ex.map(lift, dumps, fps))
    for p, n in zip(dumps, counts):
        print(f"  {p.name}: {n} functions")

    jobs = name_jobs(wws_jobs())
    # a name's folder from an earlier lift of another release would be compiled in as well: only this lift's stay
    names = {j[0] for j in jobs}
    for old in OUT.glob("w????????"):
        if old.is_dir() and old.name not in names:
            shutil.rmtree(old, ignore_errors=True)
    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(8) as ex:
        wcounts = list(ex.map(lift_wws, jobs))
    print(f"  {len(jobs)} Wws jobs, {sum(wcounts)} functions, {sum(j[3] for j in jobs)} bytes of code")
    moved = [(j[0], j[1]) for j in jobs if j[0] != f"w{j[1]:08X}"]
    if moved:
        print("  known by another release's name: " + ", ".join(f"{n} (here at 0x{ea:08X})" for n, ea in moved))

    externs, regs = [], []
    for img, (p, fp) in enumerate(zip(dumps, fps), start=2):
        pre = f"gt5_j{fp[:8]}"
        entry = f"{pre}_spu_func_{PM_BASE.get(fp, 0):08X}"
        externs += [f"extern void {entry}(spu_context*);", f"extern void {pre}_spu_recomp_register(void);", f"extern void {pre}_any_register(void);"]
        regs += [f"    /* {p.name} */",
                 f"    spu_begin_image({img});",
                 f"    {pre}_spu_recomp_register();", f"    {pre}_any_register();",
                 f'    spu_workload_register_img(0x{fp}ULL, {entry}, {img}, "j{fp[:8]}");']
    for img, (name, ea, entry, code, blob) in enumerate(jobs, start=WWS_IMAGE0):
        pre = f"gt5_{name}"
        sample = blob[0x30:0x30 + WWS_SAMPLE]
        externs += [f"extern void {pre}_spu_recomp_register(void);", f"extern void {pre}_any_register(void);",
                    f"static const uint8_t {pre}_sample[{len(sample)}] = {{{', '.join(str(b) for b in sample)}}};"]
        regs += [f"    spu_begin_image({img});",
                 f"    {pre}_spu_recomp_register();", f"    {pre}_any_register();",
                 f"    {{ spu_overlay_code_segment s = {{0x{WWS_BASE + 0x30:X}, {len(sample)}, {pre}_sample}};",
                 f"      spu_overlay_register_verified_region(0x{ea:08X}u, 0x{WWS_BASE:X}u, 0x{code:X}u, {img}, &s, 1); }}"]
    REG.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    REG.write_text(TEMPLATE.format(externs="\n".join(externs), regs="\n".join(regs), n=len(dumps)), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"{len(dumps)} images, {sum(counts)} SPU functions -> {REG.relative_to(ROOT)}")


TEMPLATE = """/* Raw SPU images (SPURS jobs + the Wws_Job policy module), GENERATED by
 * scripts/lift_spu_jobs.py. The runtime matches an image by content fingerprint;
 * without a match it logs `dispatch MISS`, and that job never runs. */
#include <stdint.h>
#include "spu_workload.h"
#include "spu_overlay_residency.h"

extern void spu_begin_image(int image_id);

{externs}

/* {n} images. Image ids 2.. leave room for build_spu_workloads.py's hashed ids. */
__attribute__((constructor)) static void gt5_spu_jobs_register(void)
{{
{regs}
    spu_begin_image(0);
}}
"""

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

`GT5/scripts/lift_stamp.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Fingerprint of everything the generated code is made from, so an update knows when to re-lift.

    python scripts/lift_stamp.py           prints the current fingerprint
    python scripts/lift_stamp.py --write   records it as the fingerprint of the last lift (relift.ps1 does)
    python scripts/lift_stamp.py --check   exit 0 when the last lift is still current, 1 when a re-lift is due

The fingerprint covers the lift tools in ps3recomp/tools, the GT5 lift scripts, the game-code mods and
this copy's EBOOT.elf. Runtime-only changes (graphics, sound, input) leave it alone: those need a
rebuild, not a re-lift.
"""
import hashlib
import sys
from pathlib import Path

GT5 = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
BASE = GT5.parent
STAMP = GT5 / "analysis" / "lift_stamp.txt"
SCRIPTS = ["relift.ps1", "filter_functions.py", "setjmp_patch.py", "version_addrs.py", "mods.py",
           "lift_spu_jobs.py", "spu_jobs_from_eboot.py", "spu_static_entries.txt"]


def inputs():
    files = sorted((BASE / "ps3recomp" / "tools").glob("*.py"))
    files += [GT5 / "scripts" / s for s in SCRIPTS]
    files += sorted((GT5 / "mods").glob("*/mod.json")) if (GT5 / "mods").is_dir() else []
    files += [GT5 / "input" / "EBOOT.elf"]
    return files


def fingerprint():
    h = hashlib.sha1()
    for f in inputs():
        h.update(str(f.relative_to(BASE)).replace("\\", "/").encode())
        h.update(b"\0")
        # Line endings don't change what the tools do.
        h.update(f.read_bytes().replace(b"\r\n", b"\n") if f.exists() else b"<missing>")
        h.update(b"\0")
    return h.hexdigest()


def main():
    fp = fingerprint()
    if "--write" in sys.argv:
        STAMP.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        STAMP.write_text(fp + "\n")
        print(f"lift stamp written: {fp[:12]}")
    elif "--check" in sys.argv:
        last = STAMP.read_text().strip() if STAMP.exists() else ""
        if last == fp:
            print("lift is current")
            sys.exit(0)
        print("re-lift needed" + ("" if last else " (no record of a lift)"))
        sys.exit(1)
    else:
        print(fp)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

`GT5/scripts/methodfind.py`:

```py
"""Tally arguments of an RSX method in a gmem.py dump: methodfind.py <file> <ea hex> <method hex> [method hex ...]

Scans for one-argument headers of each method (a cheap pattern; it can catch look-alike data) and counts values.
"""
import collections
import struct
import sys

d = open(sys.argv[1], "rb").read()
base = int(sys.argv[2], 16)
n = len(d) // 4
w = struct.unpack(">%dI" % n, d[:n * 4])
for ms in sys.argv[3:]:
    m = int(ms, 16)
    head = (1 << 18) | m
    c = collections.Counter(w[i + 1] for i in range(n - 1) if w[i] == head)
    first = [base + i * 4 for i in range(n - 1) if w[i] == head][:3]
    print("%04X: %d hits, first at %s" % (m, sum(c.values()), " ".join("%08X" % a for a in first)))
    for v, k in c.most_common(10):
        print("   %08X x%d" % (v, k))
```

`GT5/scripts/mods.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Collect the game-code mods in GT5/mods into the lifter's --insn-patches file and their switches.

    python scripts/mods.py            (relift.ps1 runs it before the lifter)

A mod is a folder GT5/mods/<name>/ with a mod.json:

    {
      "name": "unlock-fps",
      "description": "What it does, in a sentence.",
      "default": false,
      "patches": {
        "<SHA-1 of the decrypted EBOOT.elf it was written for>": [
          {"addr": "0x008CFFB4", "orig": "0x8089001C", "new": "0x38800000", "note": "why"}
        ]
      }
    }

Each patch replaces one 32-bit PowerPC instruction. The lifter emits both versions,
`if (g_mod_<name>) { new } else { original }`, so a mod built in costs nothing while it is off and
is switched at start-up by the environment variable GT5_MOD_<NAME> (1 on, 0 off; unset: "default").
Patches are listed per release because addresses differ between them; a mod with no list for
this copy's EBOOT is skipped. Every "orig" is checked against the EBOOT before anything is written.

A list under "*" is for every release. Its patches name the place by the code around it instead of
an address: {"find": "8089001C 88A90019 7C8407B4", "new": "0x38800002"} replaces the first word of that
run of instruction words, which must turn up exactly once in the EBOOT (otherwise the mod is skipped
for this copy). "at" picks another word of the run (0 = the first). A list for this copy's own SHA-1
wins over "*".

Two mods may replace the same instruction (unlock-fps and half-rate both set the frame pacer's wait):
the lifter builds every version in, and when both are switched on the one whose name sorts first wins.

Writes analysis/insn_patches.json and src/gen/mods.cpp when at least one mod applies; otherwise
removes them, so a build without mods is exactly a build without this script.
"""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import re
import struct
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


def eboot_words(path):
    """vaddr -> 32-bit word reader for the ELF's loadable segments."""
    d = path.read_bytes()
    e_phoff = struct.unpack(">Q", d[32:40])[0]
    e_phentsize, e_phnum = struct.unpack(">HH", d[54:58])
    segs = []
    for i in range(e_phnum):
        o = e_phoff + i * e_phentsize
        p_type, _, p_offset, p_vaddr, _, p_filesz, _ = struct.unpack(">IIQQQQQ", d[o:o + 48])
        if p_type == 1 and p_filesz:
            segs.append((p_vaddr, p_offset, p_filesz))

    def word(addr):
        for va, off, size in segs:
            if va <= addr < va + size - 3:
                return struct.unpack(">I", d[off + addr - va:off + addr - va + 4])[0]
        return None
    def find(words):
        """Addresses where this run of 32-bit words stands, on a 4-byte boundary."""
        pat = b"".join(struct.pack(">I", w) for w in words)
        out = []
        for va, off, size in segs:
            i = d.find(pat, off, off + size)
            while i >= 0:
                if (i - off) % 4 == 0:
                    out.append(va + i - off)
                i = d.find(pat, i + 1, off + size)
        return out
    return hashlib.sha1(d).hexdigest().upper(), word, find


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--elf", default=str(ROOT / "input" / "EBOOT.elf"))
    ap.add_argument("--mods", default=str(ROOT / "mods"))
    ap.add_argument("--patches-out", default=str(ROOT / "analysis" / "insn_patches.json"))
    ap.add_argument("--cpp-out", default=str(ROOT / "src" / "gen" / "mods.cpp"))
    a = ap.parse_args()

    sha1, word, find = eboot_words(Path(a.elf))
    patches, switches, seen, errors = [], [], {}, []
    mod_dirs = sorted(p for p in Path(a.mods).glob("*/mod.json")) if Path(a.mods).is_dir() else []
    for mj in mod_dirs:
        try:
            m = json.loads(mj.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except ValueError as e:
            errors.append(f"{mj}: not valid JSON ({e})")
            continue
        name = str(m.get("name") or mj.parent.name)
        if not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*", name):
            errors.append(f"{mj}: name {name!r} must be lowercase letters, digits and dashes")
            continue
        mine = (m.get("patches") or {}).get(sha1) or (m.get("patches") or {}).get("*")
        if not mine:
            print(f"[mods] {name}: no patches for this EBOOT ({sha1[:12]}...), skipped")
            continue
        # "find" patches: the place by its code. Not found exactly once = this mod has no place here.
        resolved, lost = [], None
        for p in mine:
            if "find" not in p:
                resolved.append(p)
                continue
            try:
                words = [int(w, 16) for w in str(p["find"]).split()]
                at = int(p.get("at", 0))
                if not words or not 0 <= at < len(words):
                    raise ValueError
            except ValueError:
                errors.append(f"{name}: \"find\" is a run of hex instruction words, \"at\" an index into it")
                lost = "bad"
                break
            hits = find(words)
            if len(hits) != 1:
                lost = f"its code turns up {len(hits)} times in this EBOOT, not once"
                break
            q = dict(p)
            q["addr"] = f"0x{hits[0] + 4 * at:08X}"
            q["orig"] = f"0x{words[at]:08X}"
            resolved.append(q)
        if lost:
            if lost != "bad":
                print(f"[mods] {name}: {lost}, skipped")
            continue
        mine = resolved
        ident = name.replace("-", "_")
        guard = f"g_mod_{ident}"
        ok = True
        for p in mine:
            try:
                addr, orig, new = (int(str(p[k]), 0) for k in ("addr", "orig", "new"))
            except (KeyError, ValueError):
                errors.append(f"{name}: each patch needs addr, orig and new as numbers")
                ok = False
                break
            have = word(addr)
            if have is None:
                errors.append(f"{name}: 0x{addr:08X} is not in the EBOOT")
                ok = False
            elif have != orig:
                errors.append(f"{name}: 0x{addr:08X} holds 0x{have:08X}, the mod expects 0x{orig:08X}")
                ok = False
            elif addr in seen and seen[addr][1] != orig:
                errors.append(f"{name}: 0x{addr:08X} is also patched by {seen[addr][0]}, from another original word")
                ok = False
            else:
                seen.setdefault(addr, (name, orig))
                patches.append({"addr": f"0x{addr:08X}", "orig": f"0x{orig:08X}", "new": f"0x{new:08X}",
                                "guard": guard, "note": f"{name}: {p.get('note', '')}".strip()})
        if ok:
            switches.append((name, guard, f"GT5_MOD_{ident.upper()}", bool(m.get("default", False)),
                             str(m.get("description", ""))))
            print(f"[mods] {name}: {len(mine)} patch(es), switch GT5_MOD_{ident.upper()}"
                  f" (default {'on' if m.get('default') else 'off'})")
    if errors:
        for e in errors:
            print("[mods] ERROR:", e)
        sys.exit(1)

    pout, cout = Path(a.patches_out), Path(a.cpp_out)
    if not switches:
        for f in (pout, cout):
            if f.exists():
                f.unlink()
        print("[mods] no mods for this EBOOT")
        return
    pout.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    cout.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    pout.write_text(json.dumps({"patches": patches}, indent=2) + "\n")
    lines = ["// Generated by scripts/mods.py from GT5/mods: one start-up switch per mod.",
             "#include <stdio.h>", "#include <stdlib.h>", "",
             "static int gt5_mod_switch(const char* env, int on_by_default, const char* name)", "{",
             "    const char* e = getenv(env);",
             "    const int on = e ? atoi(e) != 0 : on_by_default;",
             "    fprintf(stderr, \"[mods] %s %s (%s)\\n\", name, on ? \"on\" : \"off\", env);",
             "    return on;", "}", ""]
    for name, guard, env, default, desc in switches:
        if desc:
            lines.append("// " + desc.replace("\n", " "))
        lines.append(f'extern "C" {{ int {guard} = gt5_mod_switch("{env}", {int(default)}, "{name}"); }}')
    cout.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    print(f"[mods] {len(patches)} patch(es) from {len(switches)} mod(s) -> {pout.name}, {cout.name}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

`GT5/scripts/moviecmp.py`:

```py
import os as _gt5_os  # this clone's folders, wherever it was cloned to
GT5_DIR = _gt5_os.path.dirname(_gt5_os.path.dirname(_gt5_os.path.abspath(__file__)))
BASE_DIR = _gt5_os.path.dirname(GT5_DIR)
"""Are the pictures the game decoded the same as an independent decode of the same stream?
moviecmp.py <stream from DMUX_DUMP> <dir from VDEC_DUMP>   (FFmpeg demuxes and decodes the stream itself)
"""
import glob
import hashlib
import os
import subprocess
import sys

FF = (BASE_DIR + r"\ffmpeg\ffmpeg-n9.0-latest-win64-lgpl-shared-9.0\bin\ffmpeg.exe")
stream, dumps = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
out = subprocess.run([FF, "-hide_banner", "-loglevel", "error", "-f", "mpeg", "-i", stream, "-map", "0:v:0", "-fps_mode", "passthrough",
                      "-f", "framemd5", "-"], capture_output=True, text=True)
errors = [x for x in out.stderr.splitlines() if x.strip()]
print("independent decode: %d log lines; first: %s" % (len(errors), errors[:3]))
frames = {}
n = 0
for line in out.stdout.splitlines():
    if line.startswith("#") or not line.strip():
        continue
    f = [x.strip() for x in line.split(",")]
    frames[f[-1]] = n
    n += 1
print("frames in the stream: %d, distinct: %d" % (n, len(frames)))
hit = miss = 0
offsets = []
missed = []
for path in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(dumps, "*.yuv"))):
    tok = int(os.path.basename(path).split("_")[0])
    h = hashlib.md5(open(path, "rb").read()).hexdigest()
    if h in frames:
        hit += 1
        offsets.append(frames[h] - tok)
    else:
        miss += 1
        missed.append(tok)
print("game pictures found in it: %d, not found: %d %s" % (hit, miss, missed[:12]))
if offsets:
    print("display index minus AU number: min %d max %d" % (min(offsets), max(offsets)))

```

`GT5/scripts/moviefind.py`:

```py
import os as _gt5_os  # this clone's folders, wherever it was cloned to
GT5_DIR = _gt5_os.path.dirname(_gt5_os.path.dirname(_gt5_os.path.abspath(__file__)))
BASE_DIR = _gt5_os.path.dirname(GT5_DIR)
"""Find a displayed frame in the movie stream by an independent decode: moviefind.py <stream> <shot.png> <out.png> [x0 y0 x1 y1]

The box is where the picture sits in the shot. Writes the shot and the best matching movie frame side by side.
"""
import subprocess
import sys

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

FF = (BASE_DIR + r"\ffmpeg\ffmpeg-n9.0-latest-win64-lgpl-shared-9.0\bin\ffmpeg.exe")
stream, shot, out = sys.argv[1:4]
box = tuple(int(x) for x in sys.argv[4:8]) if len(sys.argv) > 7 else (64, 37, 1216, 684)
W, H = 240, 135
want = np.asarray(Image.open(shot).convert("RGB").crop(box).resize((W, H)), dtype=np.float32)
p = subprocess.Popen([FF, "-hide_banner", "-loglevel", "error", "-f", "mpeg", "-i", stream, "-map", "0:v:0", "-fps_mode", "passthrough",
                      "-vf", "scale=%d:%d" % (W, H), "-f", "rawvideo", "-pix_fmt", "rgb24", "-"], stdout=subprocess.PIPE)
best = (1e9, -1)
n = 0
size = W * H * 3
while True:
    d = p.stdout.read(size)
    if len(d) < size:
        break
    a = np.frombuffer(d, dtype=np.uint8).reshape(H, W, 3).astype(np.float32)
    e = float(np.abs(a - want).mean())
    if e < best[0]:
        best = (e, n)
    n += 1
print("frames %d, best frame %d, mean difference %.2f" % (n, best[1], best[0]))
tmp = out + ".ref.png"
subprocess.run([FF, "-hide_banner", "-loglevel", "error", "-y", "-f", "mpeg", "-i", stream, "-map", "0:v:0", "-vf",
                "select='eq(n\\,%d)',scale=960:540" % best[1], "-fps_mode", "passthrough", "-frames:v", "1", tmp])
sheet = Image.new("RGB", (1920, 540))
sheet.paste(Image.open(shot).convert("RGB").crop(box).resize((960, 540)), (0, 0))
sheet.paste(Image.open(tmp).convert("RGB"), (960, 0))
sheet.save(out)
print(out)
```

`GT5/scripts/native_by_name.py`:

```py
import os as _gt5_os  # this clone's folders, wherever it was cloned to
GT5_DIR = _gt5_os.path.dirname(_gt5_os.path.dirname(_gt5_os.path.abspath(__file__)))
BASE_DIR = _gt5_os.path.dirname(GT5_DIR)
"""Which native is registered under a script name? native_by_name.py WaitAdvertiseEnd ...

Finds the string, the TOC slots pointing at it, the lifted code loading them, and every
OPD loaded nearby, since registration passes the name and the OPD together.
"""
import glob
import re
import struct
import sys

d = open((GT5_DIR + r"\input\EBOOT.elf"), "rb").read()
SEGS = [(65536, 0, 24585320), (24707072, 24641536, 1363804)]
TOCS = [0x1846AF0, 0x1866624, 0x18765B0, 0x185682C]


def u32(va):
    for v, o, f in SEGS:
        if v <= va < v + f - 3:
            return struct.unpack(">I", d[o + va - v:o + va - v + 4])[0]
    return None


base, off, size = SEGS[1]
words = struct.unpack(f">{size // 4}I", d[off:off + size // 4 * 4])
load = re.compile(r"vm_read32\(ctx->gpr\[2\] \+ (-?0x[0-9A-F]+)\)")
files = {p: open(p, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").readlines()
         for p in sorted(glob.glob((GT5_DIR + r"\generated\ppu_recomp_0*.cpp")))}
head = re.compile(r"^void func_([0-9A-F]{8})\(")
for name in sys.argv[1:]:
    pat = name.encode() + b"\0"
    i = -1
    while True:
        i = d.find(pat, i + 1)
        if i < 0:
            break
        if d[i - 1] != 0:  # part of a longer string
            continue
        va = 0x10000 + i
        slots = [base + k * 4 for k, w in enumerate(words) if w == va]
        print(f"== {name} string {va:#x} slots {[hex(s) for s in slots]}")
        for slot in slots:
            for toc in TOCS:
                disp = slot - toc
                if abs(disp) >= 0x8000:
                    continue
                tag = f"ctx->gpr[2] + {'-' if disp < 0 else ''}0x{abs(disp):X})"
                for path, src in files.items():
                    for n, l in enumerate(src):
                        if tag in l and "vm_read32" in l:
                            fn = next((head.match(src[k]).group(1) for k in range(n, 0, -1) if head.match(src[k])), "?")
                            found = []
                            for w in src[n:n + 10]:
                                m = load.search(w)
                                if m:
                                    v = u32(toc + int(m.group(1), 16))
                                    c = u32(v) if v else None
                                    if c and 0x10200 <= c < 0x111C684:
                                        found.append(f"opd {v:#x} code {c:08X}")
                            print(f"   in func_{fn} ({path[-8:-4]}:{n}): {found[:3]}")
```

`GT5/scripts/native_name.py`:

```py
import os as _gt5_os  # this clone's folders, wherever it was cloned to
GT5_DIR = _gt5_os.path.dirname(_gt5_os.path.dirname(_gt5_os.path.abspath(__file__)))
BASE_DIR = _gt5_os.path.dirname(GT5_DIR)
"""What script-visible name is a native function registered under? native_name.py 00747C28 ...

Finds the OPD for the code address, the TOC slots holding that OPD, and the lifted
code that loads those slots, then prints the strings loaded just before each one.
"""
import glob
import re
import struct
import sys

d = open((GT5_DIR + r"\input\EBOOT.elf"), "rb").read()
SEGS = [(65536, 0, 24585320), (24707072, 24641536, 1363804)]
TOCS = [0x1846AF0, 0x1866624, 0x18765B0, 0x185682C]


def u32(va):
    for v, o, f in SEGS:
        if v <= va < v + f - 3:
            return struct.unpack(">I", d[o + va - v:o + va - v + 4])[0]
    return None


def cstr(va):
    for v, o, f in SEGS:
        if v <= va < v + f:
            e = d.find(b"\0", o + va - v)
            s = d[o + va - v:e]
            if 2 <= len(s) < 80 and all(32 <= c < 127 for c in s):
                return s.decode()
    return None


base, off, size = SEGS[1]
words = struct.unpack(f">{size // 4}I", d[off:off + size // 4 * 4])
load = re.compile(r"vm_read32\(ctx->gpr\[2\] \+ (-?0x[0-9A-F]+)\)")
files = {}


def lines(path):
    if path not in files:
        files[path] = open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").readlines()
    return files[path]


for arg in sys.argv[1:]:
    code = int(arg, 16)
    opds = [base + i * 4 for i, w in enumerate(words) if w == code]
    print(f"== {code:08X}: OPDs {[hex(o) for o in opds]}")
    for opd in opds:
        slots = [base + i * 4 for i, w in enumerate(words) if w == opd]
        for slot in slots:
            for toc in TOCS:
                disp = slot - toc
                if abs(disp) >= 0x8000:
                    continue
                tag = f"ctx->gpr[2] + {'-' if disp < 0 else ''}0x{abs(disp):X})"
                for path in sorted(glob.glob((GT5_DIR + r"\generated\ppu_recomp_0*.cpp"))):
                    src = lines(path)
                    for n, l in enumerate(src):
                        if tag in l and "vm_read32" in l:
                            near = []
                            for w in src[max(0, n - 14):n + 15]:
                                m = load.search(w)
                                if m:
                                    s = cstr(u32(toc + int(m.group(1), 16)) or 0)
                                    if s:
                                        near.append(s)
                            print(f"   slot {slot:#x} toc {toc:#x} {path[-8:-4]}:{n} strings near: {near[:8]}")
```

`GT5/scripts/ntwaits.py`:

```py
"""Which ntdll calls a prof.ps1 capture sits in, per thread: ntwaits.py <prof.txt> [--threads N] [--log err]

Names come from ntdll's export table, so internal functions show as the nearest export before them.
"""
import bisect
import collections
import struct
import sys


def exports(path):
    d = open(path, "rb").read()
    pe = struct.unpack("<I", d[0x3C:0x40])[0]
    nsec = struct.unpack("<H", d[pe + 6:pe + 8])[0]
    optsz = struct.unpack("<H", d[pe + 20:pe + 22])[0]
    opt = pe + 24
    exp_rva = struct.unpack("<I", d[opt + 112:opt + 116])[0]
    secs = []
    for i in range(nsec):
        s = pe + 24 + optsz + i * 40
        vsz, va, rsz, ptr = struct.unpack("<IIII", d[s + 8:s + 24])
        secs.append((va, max(vsz, rsz), ptr))

    def off(rva):
        for va, sz, ptr in secs:
            if va <= rva < va + sz:
                return rva - va + ptr
        raise ValueError(hex(rva))

    e = off(exp_rva)
    nfun, nnames, afun, aname, aord = struct.unpack("<IIIII", d[e + 20:e + 40])
    funcs = struct.unpack("<%dI" % nfun, d[off(afun):off(afun) + 4 * nfun])
    names = struct.unpack("<%dI" % nnames, d[off(aname):off(aname) + 4 * nnames])
    ords = struct.unpack("<%dH" % nnames, d[off(aord):off(aord) + 2 * nnames])
    out = []
    for n, o in zip(names, ords):
        p = off(n)
        out.append((funcs[o], d[p:d.index(b"\0", p)].decode()))
    out.sort()
    return out


def arg(name, default):
    return sys.argv[sys.argv.index(name) + 1] if name in sys.argv else default


ex = exports(r"C:\Windows\System32\ntdll.dll")
rvas = [e[0] for e in ex]


def name(rva):
    i = bisect.bisect_right(rvas, rva) - 1
    return ex[i][1] if i >= 0 else "?"


guest = {}
log = arg("--log", None)
if log:
    import re
    for line in open(log, encoding="utf8", errors="replace"):
        m = re.match(r"\[THREAD (\d+)\] host thread started.*hosttid=(\d+)", line)
        if m:
            guest[int(m.group(2))] = m.group(1)
cpu = {}
per = collections.defaultdict(collections.Counter)
tot = collections.Counter()
for line in open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf8", errors="replace"):
    p = line.split()
    if line.startswith("#cpu"):
        cpu[int(p[1])] = int(p[2])
    elif len(p) >= 4:
        n = int(p[-1])
        lab = name(int(p[-2], 16)) if " ".join(p[1:-2]).lower() == "ntdll.dll" else "(other code)"
        per[int(p[0])][lab] += n
        tot[lab] += n
for t in sorted(cpu, key=lambda x: -cpu[x])[:int(arg("--threads", 12))]:
    all_n = sum(per[t].values()) or 1
    print("thread %d guest %s cpu %d%%: %s" % (t, guest.get(t, "-"), cpu[t],
          ", ".join("%s %.0f%%" % (k, 100.0 * v / all_n) for k, v in per[t].most_common(5))))
print("all:", ", ".join("%s %.0f%%" % (k, 100.0 * v / sum(tot.values())) for k, v in tot.most_common(10)))

```

`GT5/scripts/opdrefs.py`:

```py
import os as _gt5_os  # this clone's folders, wherever it was cloned to
GT5_DIR = _gt5_os.path.dirname(_gt5_os.path.dirname(_gt5_os.path.abspath(__file__)))
BASE_DIR = _gt5_os.path.dirname(GT5_DIR)
"""Where a function's address is stored: opdrefs.py <hex addr>... lists OPDs naming it and the vtable slots naming each OPD."""
import struct
import sys

d = open((GT5_DIR + r"\input\EBOOT.elf"), "rb").read()
BASE = 0x10000


def find_all(b):
    i = d.find(b)
    while i >= 0:
        yield i
        i = d.find(b, i + 1)


for a in sys.argv[1:]:
    ea = int(a, 16)
    for i in find_all(struct.pack(">I", ea)):
        print("%08X stored at %08X (next word %08X)" % (ea, i + BASE, struct.unpack(">I", d[i + 4:i + 8])[0]))
        for j in find_all(struct.pack(">I", i + BASE)):
            w = struct.unpack(">8I", d[(j & ~31):(j & ~31) + 32])
            print("   slot at %08X; around: %s" % (j + BASE, " ".join("%08X" % x for x in w)))
```
