`GT5/scripts/profsym.py`:

```py
import os as _gt5_os  # this clone's folders, wherever it was cloned to
GT5_DIR = _gt5_os.path.dirname(_gt5_os.path.dirname(_gt5_os.path.abspath(__file__)))
BASE_DIR = _gt5_os.path.dirname(GT5_DIR)
"""Name a prof.ps1 capture: profsym.py <prof.txt> [--threads N] [--top M] [--log <run .err>]

Prints the busiest functions overall, then the top functions for each busy thread, with the
guest thread id where the run's log gives one.
"""
import collections
import re
import subprocess
import sys

SYM = r"C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\Community\VC\Tools\Llvm\x64\bin\llvm-symbolizer.exe"
EXE = (GT5_DIR + r"\build\gt5.exe")
BASE = 0x140000000


def arg(name, default):
    return sys.argv[sys.argv.index(name) + 1] if name in sys.argv else default


nthreads = int(arg("--threads", 10))
top = int(arg("--top", 12))
log = arg("--log", None)
guest = {}
if log:
    for line in open(log, encoding="utf8", errors="replace"):
        m = re.match(r"\[THREAD (\d+)\] host thread started.*hosttid=(\d+)", line)
        if m:
            guest[int(m.group(2))] = m.group(1)

cpu = {}
rows = []
for line in open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf8", errors="replace"):
    p = line.split()
    if line.startswith("#cpu"):
        cpu[int(p[1])] = int(p[2])
    elif len(p) >= 4:
        rows.append((int(p[0]), " ".join(p[1:-2]), int(p[-2], 16), int(p[-1])))

addrs = sorted({r[2] for r in rows if r[1].lower() == "gt5.exe"})
names = {}
if addrs:
    text = "\n".join(hex(BASE + a) for a in addrs) + "\n"
    out = subprocess.run([SYM, "--obj=" + EXE, "--no-inlines", "--output-style=GNU", "--basenames"],
                         input=text, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split("\n")
    # GNU style prints two lines per address: function, then file:line.
    for i, a in enumerate(addrs):
        names[a] = out[i * 2].strip() if i * 2 < len(out) else "?"


def label(mod, rva):
    if mod.lower() == "gt5.exe":
        return names.get(rva, "?")
    return "[" + mod + "]"


total = collections.Counter()
per = collections.defaultdict(collections.Counter)
for tid, mod, rva, n in rows:
    per[tid][label(mod, rva)] += n
    # Idle threads sit in ntdll/kernel waits; those samples say nothing about load.
    total[label(mod, rva)] += n

busy = sorted(cpu, key=lambda t: -cpu[t])[:nthreads]
print("total cpu %d%% of one core across %d threads above 5%%" % (sum(v for v in cpu.values()), sum(1 for v in cpu.values() if v > 5)))
print("\n== busiest threads")
for t in busy:
    print("\nthread %d  guest %s  cpu %d%%" % (t, guest.get(t, "-"), cpu[t]))
    all_n = sum(per[t].values()) or 1
    for name, n in per[t].most_common(top):
        print("  %5.1f%%  %s" % (100.0 * n / all_n, name[:90]))
print("\n== across the busy threads")
merged = collections.Counter()
for t in cpu:
    if cpu[t] > 20:
        merged.update(per[t])
all_n = sum(merged.values()) or 1
for name, n in merged.most_common(top * 3):
    print("  %5.1f%%  %s" % (100.0 * n / all_n, name[:90]))

```

`GT5/scripts/ps3_unlock.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""ps3_unlock.py - unlock a PS3 game executable and Sony's firmware file for the PC port, without RPCS3.

    python ps3_unlock.py eboot    <EBOOT.BIN>     <out.elf>           a game's executable (disc or update)
    python ps3_unlock.py firmware <PS3UPDAT.PUP>  <dev_flash folder>  Sony's firmware file, as RPCS3 installs it
    python ps3_unlock.py pkg      <file.pkg>      <hdd0\\game folder>  a game update or DLC package, into
                                                                      <that folder>\\<title ID>, as a PS3 installs it
    python ps3_unlock.py keys                                         only fetch + check the keys

An EBOOT.BIN that is already a plain ELF is copied as it is. Free-licence NPDRM executables (game
updates) are handled; ones that need a licence file (.rap) and system modules (.sprx) are not.

pkg: retail PS3 packages. The package's own checksum is checked before anything is written. A file that
is there already is replaced only where the package says so. An update is skipped when that version (or
a newer one) is installed, and refused when the version it goes on top of is not: updates go in order.
--info prints the package's line (content, folder, versions) and writes nothing. Progress is printed as
"PKG_PROGRESS <done> <total>" about once a second.

Options (before or after the command):
    --keys-dir DIR   where the fetched key source files are kept (default: ./ps3_keys next to this file,
                     or $PS3_UNLOCK_KEYS). Files already there are reused when their SHA-256 matches.
    --offline        never download; use only --keys-dir.

No keys are in this file. At run time it downloads two public text files from RPCS3's source on GitHub
at a pinned commit, checks each against the SHA-256 written below, and reads the key constants out of
the text. The code here is written from the published file-format descriptions (psdevwiki: SELF / SCE
header, Certified File, PUP, ustar), not from RPCS3's code.

Exit codes - the installer falls back to RPCS3 on anything but 0:
    0  done
    1  bad command line
    2  KEYS: the key files could not be fetched, or did not match their pinned SHA-256, or did not parse
    3  INPUT: the input is not something this tool can unlock (unknown format / no key for it / bad hash)
    4  OUTPUT: could not write the result
    5  INTERNAL: anything unexpected (a traceback is printed first)
The last line printed on failure always starts with "PS3_UNLOCK_FAIL <code> <KEYS|INPUT|OUTPUT|INTERNAL>:".
Nothing is left at the output path after a failure: the ELF is written as <out>.part and renamed, the
firmware is unpacked into <dev_flash>.part and moved into place only when every package unpacked.

Standard library only. AES: Windows bcrypt.dll, else OpenSSL's libcrypto (ctypes), else pure Python (slow).
"""
import ctypes
import ctypes.util
import hashlib
import hmac
import os
import re
import shutil
import struct
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
import zlib

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Where the keys come from (public RPCS3 source, pinned). Only these bytes are trusted.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
KEY_COMMIT = "29108e1cb4dc884ff88295831aed790278b7e75b"   # RPCS3 v0.0.37-18154
KEY_FILES = {
    # local name          (path in the repository,              SHA-256 of the exact bytes)
    "key_vault.cpp": ("rpcs3/Crypto/key_vault.cpp", "048b03adde6f79d564d5002afaa32f69c90bcb6ec5b8dc535b631dca5417e8d1"),
    "key_vault.h":   ("rpcs3/Crypto/key_vault.h",   "7e2830a930127ab8b0291e3e940df50329cf486b7fb7566fdb8438648948f54a"),
}
KEY_URL = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RPCS3/rpcs3/{commit}/{path}"


class UnlockError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, code, kind, msg):
        super().__init__(msg)
        self.code, self.kind = code, kind


def keys_fail(msg):
    return UnlockError(2, "KEYS", msg)


def input_fail(msg):
    return UnlockError(3, "INPUT", msg)


def fetch_key_sources(keys_dir, offline=False):
    """Return {local name: text}. Every file is checked against its pinned SHA-256."""
    os.makedirs(keys_dir, exist_ok=True)
    out, fetched = {}, 0
    for name, (path, want) in KEY_FILES.items():
        local = os.path.join(keys_dir, name)
        data = None
        if os.path.isfile(local):
            with open(local, "rb") as f:
                data = f.read()
            if hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() != want:
                data = None
        if data is None:
            if offline:
                raise keys_fail(f"{name} is not in {keys_dir} (or differs from the pinned file) and --offline was given")
            url = KEY_URL.format(commit=KEY_COMMIT, path=path)
            try:
                req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "ps3-unlock"})
                with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as r:
                    data = r.read()
            except Exception as e:  # network, TLS, HTTP errors
                raise keys_fail(f"could not download {url}: {e}")
            got = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
            if got != want:
                raise keys_fail(f"{url} has SHA-256 {got}, expected {want}")
            fetched += len(data)
            with open(local, "wb") as f:
                f.write(data)
        out[name] = data.decode("utf-8", "replace")
    return out, fetched


# Program types of a SELF (psdevwiki "SELF - SPRX", program identification header)
PROGRAM_TYPES = {"KEY_LV0": 1, "KEY_LV1": 2, "KEY_LV2": 3, "KEY_APP": 4, "KEY_ISO": 5,
                 "KEY_LDR": 6, "KEY_UNK7": 7, "KEY_NPDRM": 8}


class Keys:
    """The constants read out of the fetched text: SELF keysets plus a few fixed keys."""

    def __init__(self, texts):
        cpp, hdr = texts["key_vault.cpp"], texts["key_vault.h"]
        self.selfkeys = []          # (program type, version start, version end, revision, erk, riv)
        rx = re.compile(r'emplace_back\(\s*(0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+)\s*,\s*(0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+)\s*,\s*(0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+)\s*,\s*(KEY_\w+)\s*,'
                        r'\s*"([0-9A-Fa-f]*)"\s*,\s*"([0-9A-Fa-f]*)"')
        for m in rx.finditer(cpp):
            ptype = PROGRAM_TYPES.get(m.group(4))
            if ptype is None:
                raise keys_fail(f"unknown key type {m.group(4)}")
            erk, riv = bytes.fromhex(m.group(5)), bytes.fromhex(m.group(6))
            if len(erk) != 32 or len(riv) != 16:
                raise keys_fail("a SELF keyset has the wrong length")
            self.selfkeys.append((ptype, int(m.group(1), 16), int(m.group(2), 16), int(m.group(3), 16), erk, riv))
        if len(self.selfkeys) != cpp.count("emplace_back(") or len(self.selfkeys) < 50:
            raise keys_fail("could not read every SELF keyset from key_vault.cpp")
        self.arrays = {}
        for m in re.finditer(r'constexpr\s+u8\s+(\w+)\s*\[[^\]]*\]\s*=\s*\{(.*?)\};', hdr, re.S):
            body = re.sub(r'//[^\n]*', '', m.group(2))
            self.arrays[m.group(1)] = bytes(int(x, 16) for x in re.findall(r'0x([0-9A-Fa-f]{2})', body))
        need = {"SCEPKG_ERK": 32, "SCEPKG_RIV": 16, "NP_KLIC_FREE": 16, "NP_KLIC_KEY": 16, "PUP_KEY": 64}
        for n, ln in need.items():
            if len(self.arrays.get(n, b"")) != ln:
                raise keys_fail(f"could not read {n} from key_vault.h")

    def find_self_key(self, ptype, revision):
        """Keyset of a game executable: application (4) or NPDRM (8) program, picked by key revision."""
        for (t, _v0, _v1, rev, erk, riv) in self.selfkeys:
            if t == ptype and rev == revision:
                return erk, riv
        return None


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# AES (ECB primitives; CBC and CTR are built on them here)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
class _BCrypt:
    name = "Windows bcrypt"

    def __init__(self):
        self.b = ctypes.WinDLL("bcrypt.dll")
        self.alg = ctypes.c_void_p()
        if self.b.BCryptOpenAlgorithmProvider(ctypes.byref(self.alg), ctypes.c_wchar_p("AES"), None, 0):
            raise OSError("BCryptOpenAlgorithmProvider")
        mode = ctypes.create_unicode_buffer("ChainingModeECB")
        if self.b.BCryptSetProperty(self.alg, ctypes.c_wchar_p("ChainingMode"), mode, ctypes.sizeof(mode), 0):
            raise OSError("BCryptSetProperty")
        self.b.BCryptEncrypt.argtypes = self.b.BCryptDecrypt.argtypes = [
            ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_char_p, ctypes.c_ulong, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_ulong,
            ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_ulong, ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_ulong), ctypes.c_ulong]

    def _run(self, key, data, enc):
        h = ctypes.c_void_p()
        kb = ctypes.create_string_buffer(key, len(key))
        if self.b.BCryptGenerateSymmetricKey(self.alg, ctypes.byref(h), None, 0, kb, len(key), 0):
            raise OSError("BCryptGenerateSymmetricKey")
        try:
            out = ctypes.create_string_buffer(len(data))
            n = ctypes.c_ulong()
            fn = self.b.BCryptEncrypt if enc else self.b.BCryptDecrypt
            if fn(h, data, len(data), None, None, 0, out, len(data), ctypes.byref(n), 0):
                raise OSError("BCryptEncrypt/Decrypt")
            return out.raw[:n.value]
        finally:
            self.b.BCryptDestroyKey(h)

    def ecb_encrypt(self, key, data):
        return self._run(key, data, True)

    def ecb_decrypt(self, key, data):
        return self._run(key, data, False)


class _OpenSSL:
    name = "OpenSSL libcrypto"

    def __init__(self):
        path = ctypes.util.find_library("crypto")
        names = [path] if path else []
        names += ["libcrypto.so.3", "libcrypto.so.1.1", "libcrypto.dylib"]
        if os.name == "nt":                            # the libcrypto python.org's Windows builds ship with
            import glob
            for d in (os.path.join(sys.base_prefix, "DLLs"), sys.base_prefix, os.path.dirname(sys.executable)):
                names += sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(d, "libcrypto*.dll")))
        last = None
        for n in names:
            try:
                self.c = ctypes.CDLL(n)
                break
            except OSError as e:
                last = e
        else:
            raise OSError(f"libcrypto not found ({last})")
        c = self.c
        c.EVP_CIPHER_CTX_new.restype = ctypes.c_void_p
        c.EVP_CIPHER_CTX_free.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p]
        for f in ("EVP_aes_128_ecb", "EVP_aes_256_ecb"):
            getattr(c, f).restype = ctypes.c_void_p
        c.EVP_CipherInit_ex.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_char_p,
                                        ctypes.c_char_p, ctypes.c_int]
        c.EVP_CIPHER_CTX_set_padding.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_int]
        c.EVP_CipherUpdate.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_int),
                                       ctypes.c_char_p, ctypes.c_int]

    def _run(self, key, data, enc):
        c = self.c
        ctx = c.EVP_CIPHER_CTX_new()
        try:
            cipher = c.EVP_aes_256_ecb() if len(key) == 32 else c.EVP_aes_128_ecb()
            if c.EVP_CipherInit_ex(ctx, cipher, None, key, None, 1 if enc else 0) != 1:
                raise OSError("EVP_CipherInit_ex")
            c.EVP_CIPHER_CTX_set_padding(ctx, 0)
            out = ctypes.create_string_buffer(len(data) + 32)
            res, pos, step = [], 0, 1 << 28
            while pos < len(data):
                chunk = data[pos:pos + step]
                n = ctypes.c_int()
                if c.EVP_CipherUpdate(ctx, out, ctypes.byref(n), chunk, len(chunk)) != 1:
                    raise OSError("EVP_CipherUpdate")
                res.append(out.raw[:n.value])
                pos += step
            return b"".join(res)
        finally:
            c.EVP_CIPHER_CTX_free(ctx)

    def ecb_encrypt(self, key, data):
        return self._run(key, data, True)

    def ecb_decrypt(self, key, data):
        return self._run(key, data, False)


class _PurePython:
    """FIPS-197 AES, table driven. Correct but slow (a large firmware takes many minutes)."""
    name = "pure Python (slow)"

    def __init__(self):
        sbox = [0] * 256
        p = q = 1
        while True:                                    # build the S-box from GF(2^8) inverses
            p = p ^ ((p << 1) & 0xFF) ^ (0x1B if p & 0x80 else 0)
            q ^= q << 1
            q ^= q << 2
            q ^= q << 4
            q &= 0xFF
            if q & 0x80:
                q ^= 0x09
            x = q ^ ((q << 1 | q >> 7) & 0xFF) ^ ((q << 2 | q >> 6) & 0xFF) ^ ((q << 3 | q >> 5) & 0xFF) ^ ((q << 4 | q >> 4) & 0xFF)
            sbox[p] = x ^ 0x63
            if p == 1:
                break
        sbox[0] = 0x63
        inv = [0] * 256
        for i, v in enumerate(sbox):
            inv[v] = i
        self.sbox, self.inv = sbox, inv

        def mul(a, b):
            r = 0
            while b:
                if b & 1:
                    r ^= a
                a = ((a << 1) ^ 0x1B) & 0xFF if a & 0x80 else a << 1
                b >>= 1
            return r
        self.te = [[0] * 256 for _ in range(4)]
        self.td = [[0] * 256 for _ in range(4)]
        for i in range(256):
            s, t = sbox[i], inv[i]
            e = (mul(s, 2) << 24) | (s << 16) | (s << 8) | mul(s, 3)
            d = (mul(t, 14) << 24) | (mul(t, 9) << 16) | (mul(t, 13) << 8) | mul(t, 11)
            for r in range(4):
                self.te[r][i] = ((e >> (8 * r)) | (e << (32 - 8 * r))) & 0xFFFFFFFF
                self.td[r][i] = ((d >> (8 * r)) | (d << (32 - 8 * r))) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        self._cache = {}

    def _expand(self, key):
        if key in self._cache:
            return self._cache[key]
        nk = len(key) // 4
        nr = nk + 6
        w = list(struct.unpack(">%dI" % nk, key))
        rcon = 1
        sb = self.sbox
        for i in range(nk, 4 * (nr + 1)):
            t = w[i - 1]
            if i % nk == 0:
                t = ((t << 8) | (t >> 24)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
                t = (sb[t >> 24] << 24) | (sb[(t >> 16) & 255] << 16) | (sb[(t >> 8) & 255] << 8) | sb[t & 255]
                t ^= rcon << 24
                rcon = ((rcon << 1) ^ 0x11B) if rcon & 0x80 else rcon << 1
            elif nk > 6 and i % nk == 4:
                t = (sb[t >> 24] << 24) | (sb[(t >> 16) & 255] << 16) | (sb[(t >> 8) & 255] << 8) | sb[t & 255]
            w.append(w[i - nk] ^ t)
        ek = [w[4 * r:4 * r + 4] for r in range(nr + 1)]
        # decryption schedule (equivalent inverse cipher)
        dk = [ek[nr]]
        for r in range(nr - 1, 0, -1):
            row = []
            for x in ek[r]:
                row.append(self.td[0][sb[x >> 24]] ^ self.td[1][sb[(x >> 16) & 255]] ^
                           self.td[2][sb[(x >> 8) & 255]] ^ self.td[3][sb[x & 255]])
            dk.append(row)
        dk.append(ek[0])
        self._cache[key] = (nr, ek, dk)
        return self._cache[key]

    def _blocks(self, key, data, enc):
        nr, ek, dk = self._expand(key)
        ks = ek if enc else dk
        t0, t1, t2, t3 = self.te if enc else self.td
        sb = self.sbox if enc else self.inv
        out = bytearray(len(data))
        unpack, pack = struct.unpack_from, struct.pack_into
        for off in range(0, len(data), 16):
            s0, s1, s2, s3 = unpack(">4I", data, off)
            k = ks[0]
            s0 ^= k[0]; s1 ^= k[1]; s2 ^= k[2]; s3 ^= k[3]
            for r in range(1, nr):
                k = ks[r]
                if enc:
                    a0 = t0[s0 >> 24] ^ t1[(s1 >> 16) & 255] ^ t2[(s2 >> 8) & 255] ^ t3[s3 & 255] ^ k[0]
                    a1 = t0[s1 >> 24] ^ t1[(s2 >> 16) & 255] ^ t2[(s3 >> 8) & 255] ^ t3[s0 & 255] ^ k[1]
                    a2 = t0[s2 >> 24] ^ t1[(s3 >> 16) & 255] ^ t2[(s0 >> 8) & 255] ^ t3[s1 & 255] ^ k[2]
                    a3 = t0[s3 >> 24] ^ t1[(s0 >> 16) & 255] ^ t2[(s1 >> 8) & 255] ^ t3[s2 & 255] ^ k[3]
                else:
                    a0 = t0[s0 >> 24] ^ t1[(s3 >> 16) & 255] ^ t2[(s2 >> 8) & 255] ^ t3[s1 & 255] ^ k[0]
                    a1 = t0[s1 >> 24] ^ t1[(s0 >> 16) & 255] ^ t2[(s3 >> 8) & 255] ^ t3[s2 & 255] ^ k[1]
                    a2 = t0[s2 >> 24] ^ t1[(s1 >> 16) & 255] ^ t2[(s0 >> 8) & 255] ^ t3[s3 & 255] ^ k[2]
                    a3 = t0[s3 >> 24] ^ t1[(s2 >> 16) & 255] ^ t2[(s1 >> 8) & 255] ^ t3[s0 & 255] ^ k[3]
                s0, s1, s2, s3 = a0, a1, a2, a3
            k = ks[nr]
            if enc:
                o = (s0, s1, s2, s3, s1, s2, s3, s0, s2, s3, s0, s1, s3, s0, s1, s2)
            else:
                o = (s0, s3, s2, s1, s1, s0, s3, s2, s2, s1, s0, s3, s3, s2, s1, s0)
            words = []
            for j in range(4):
                a, b, c, d = o[4 * j:4 * j + 4]
                words.append(((sb[a >> 24] << 24) | (sb[(b >> 16) & 255] << 16) | (sb[(c >> 8) & 255] << 8) | sb[d & 255]) ^ k[j])
            pack(">4I", out, off, *words)
        return bytes(out)

    def ecb_encrypt(self, key, data):
        return self._blocks(key, data, True)

    def ecb_decrypt(self, key, data):
        return self._blocks(key, data, False)


def make_aes():
    force = os.environ.get("PS3_UNLOCK_AES", "")       # bcrypt | openssl | pure (for testing)
    order = {"bcrypt": (_BCrypt,), "openssl": (_OpenSSL,), "pure": ()}.get(force)
    if order is None:
        order = (_BCrypt, _OpenSSL) if os.name == "nt" else (_OpenSSL,)
    for cls in order:
        try:
            a = cls()
            if a.ecb_encrypt(bytes(16), bytes(16)).hex() == "66e94bd4ef8a2c3b884cfa59ca342b2e":  # FIPS-197 check
                return a
        except Exception:
            pass
    return _PurePython()


def _xor(a, b):
    n = len(a)
    return (int.from_bytes(a, "little") ^ int.from_bytes(b[:n], "little")).to_bytes(n, "little")


def cbc_decrypt(aes, key, iv, data):
    plain = aes.ecb_decrypt(key, data)
    return _xor(plain, iv + data[:-16]) if data else b""


def ctr_crypt(aes, key, iv, data):
    """AES-CTR with a 128-bit big-endian counter starting at iv."""
    if not data:
        return b""
    n = (len(data) + 15) // 16
    c = int.from_bytes(iv, "big")
    mask = (1 << 128) - 1
    stream = bytearray()
    step = 1 << 16
    for base in range(0, n, step):
        cnt = min(step, n - base)
        ctr = b"".join(((c + base + i) & mask).to_bytes(16, "big") for i in range(cnt))
        stream += aes.ecb_encrypt(key, ctr)
    return _xor(data, stream)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Certified file (SCE header) - common to SELF and to the firmware's update packages
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def u32(b, o):
    return struct.unpack_from(">I", b, o)[0]


def u64(b, o):
    return struct.unpack_from(">Q", b, o)[0]


class CertifiedFile:
    """SCE header (0x20), encrypted metadata info (0x40), metadata header (0x20), section headers (0x30
    each), then the data keys. psdevwiki: "Certified File"."""

    def __init__(self, data):
        if data[:4] != b"SCE\0":
            raise input_fail("not an SCE (signed / encrypted) file")
        self.data = data
        self.version = u32(data, 4)
        self.key_revision = struct.unpack_from(">H", data, 8)[0]
        self.category = struct.unpack_from(">H", data, 10)[0]      # 1 SELF, 2 RVK, 3 PKG, 4 SPP
        self.meta_offset = u32(data, 12)
        self.header_len = u64(data, 16)
        self.data_len = u64(data, 24)

    def is_debug(self):
        return (self.key_revision & 0x8000) != 0

    def open_metadata(self, aes, erk, riv, pre=None):
        """Decrypt the metadata. `pre` optionally strips an extra layer (NPDRM) from the 0x40-byte info."""
        d = self.data
        start = 0x20 + self.meta_offset
        info = d[start:start + 0x40]
        hdrs = d[start + 0x40:self.header_len]
        if not self.is_debug():
            if pre:
                info = pre(info)
            info = cbc_decrypt(aes, erk, riv, info)
        key, key_pad, iv, iv_pad = info[0:16], info[16:32], info[32:48], info[48:64]
        if key_pad != bytes(16) or iv_pad != bytes(16):   # both pads are all zero in a good file
            raise input_fail("metadata did not decrypt (no key for this file, or a damaged file)")
        hdrs = ctr_crypt(aes, key, iv, hdrs)
        sig_len, _unk, nsec, nkeys, opt_size = struct.unpack_from(">QIIII", hdrs, 0)
        if nsec > 4096 or 0x20 + nsec * 0x30 + nkeys * 0x10 > len(hdrs):
            raise input_fail("metadata did not decrypt (section table out of range)")
        self.sections = []
        for i in range(nsec):
            off, size, typ, pidx, hashed, sha_idx, enc, kidx, ividx, comp = struct.unpack_from(">QQIIIIIIII", hdrs, 0x20 + 0x30 * i)
            self.sections.append(dict(offset=off, size=size, type=typ, index=pidx, enc=enc, key=kidx, iv=ividx, comp=comp))
        kstart = 0x20 + 0x30 * nsec
        self.keys = [hdrs[kstart + 16 * j:kstart + 16 * j + 16] for j in range(nkeys)]

    def section_plain(self, aes, s):
        raw = self.data[s["offset"]:s["offset"] + s["size"]]
        if len(raw) != s["size"]:
            raise input_fail("file is shorter than its section table says")
        if s["enc"] == 3:
            if s["key"] >= len(self.keys) or s["iv"] >= len(self.keys):
                raise input_fail("section key index out of range")
            raw = ctr_crypt(aes, self.keys[s["key"]], self.keys[s["iv"]], raw)
        return raw


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SELF -> ELF
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def self_to_elf(data, keys, aes):
    if data[:4] == b"\x7fELF":
        return data                                    # already plain
    if len(data) < 0x70 or data[:4] != b"SCE\0":
        raise input_fail("not a SELF or ELF file")
    cf = CertifiedFile(data)
    if cf.category != 1:
        raise input_fail(f"SCE file of category {cf.category}, not a SELF")
    # Extended header (psdevwiki "SELF - SPRX"): offsets of the parts that are stored in the clear
    (_hdr_type, appinfo_off, elf_off, phdr_off, shdr_off, _segext_off, _ver_off,
     ctrl_off, ctrl_size) = struct.unpack_from(">9Q", data, 0x20)
    auth_id, vendor, ptype, sce_version = struct.unpack_from(">QIIQ", data, appinfo_off)
    e_type = struct.unpack_from(">H", data, elf_off + 0x10)[0]
    if ptype not in (4, 8) or e_type != 2:
        # Only game executables: application or NPDRM programs whose ELF is an executable (ET_EXEC),
        # the kind proven byte for byte against RPCS3. Modules (.sprx, ELF type PRX) and system
        # programs are refused: the port uses the firmware's files as they are, still locked.
        raise input_fail(f"not a game executable (program type {ptype}, ELF type 0x{e_type:x}); only EBOOT.BIN files are handled")
    elf32 = data[elf_off + 4] == 1
    if elf32:
        ehsize, phentsize, shentsize = 0x34, 0x20, 0x28
        phnum, shnum = struct.unpack_from(">H", data, elf_off + 0x2C)[0], struct.unpack_from(">H", data, elf_off + 0x30)[0]
        phoff, shoff = u32(data, elf_off + 0x1C), u32(data, elf_off + 0x20)
        def ph(i):
            p = phdr_off + i * phentsize
            return u32(data, p + 4), u32(data, p + 16)          # p_offset, p_filesz
    else:
        ehsize, phentsize, shentsize = 0x40, 0x38, 0x40
        phnum, shnum = struct.unpack_from(">H", data, elf_off + 0x38)[0], struct.unpack_from(">H", data, elf_off + 0x3C)[0]
        phoff, shoff = u64(data, elf_off + 0x20), u64(data, elf_off + 0x28)
        def ph(i):
            p = phdr_off + i * phentsize
            return u64(data, p + 8), u64(data, p + 32)
    # NPDRM layer: a control-info entry of type 3 holds the NPD header
    npd_license = None
    pos, end = ctrl_off, ctrl_off + ctrl_size
    while pos < end:
        ctype, csize = struct.unpack_from(">II", data, pos)
        if csize == 0:
            break
        if ctype == 3 and data[pos + 0x10:pos + 0x14] == b"NPD\0":
            npd_license = u32(data, pos + 0x18)
        pos += csize
    pre = None
    if npd_license is not None:
        if npd_license != 3:
            raise input_fail("NPDRM executable that needs a licence file (RAP); only free-licence ones are supported")
        klic = aes.ecb_decrypt(keys.arrays["NP_KLIC_KEY"], keys.arrays["NP_KLIC_FREE"])
        pre = lambda info: cbc_decrypt(aes, klic, bytes(16), info)
    ks = keys.find_self_key(ptype, cf.key_revision)
    if ks is None:
        raise input_fail(f"no key for program type {ptype}, key revision 0x{cf.key_revision:x}")
    cf.open_metadata(aes, ks[0], ks[1], pre)
    # The ELF: its header, the program header table at e_phoff, each segment at its p_offset, then the
    # section header table at e_shoff (when the SELF carries one).
    out = bytearray()

    def put(off, blob):
        if len(out) < off + len(blob):
            out.extend(bytes(off + len(blob) - len(out)))
        out[off:off + len(blob)] = blob
    put(0, data[elf_off:elf_off + ehsize])
    put(phoff, data[phdr_off:phdr_off + phnum * phentsize])
    for s in cf.sections:
        if s["type"] != 2:                              # 2 = a program segment
            continue
        if s["index"] >= phnum:
            raise input_fail("segment index out of range")
        p_offset, p_filesz = ph(s["index"])
        blob = cf.section_plain(aes, s)
        if s["comp"] == 2:
            try:
                blob = zlib.decompressobj().decompress(blob, p_filesz) if p_filesz else b""
            except zlib.error as e:
                raise input_fail(f"segment {s['index']} did not decompress ({e}): wrong key?")
            blob = blob.ljust(p_filesz, b"\0")
        put(p_offset, blob)
    if shdr_off:
        put(shoff, data[shdr_off:shdr_off + shnum * shentsize])
    return bytes(out)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PUP -> dev_flash
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def read_pup(path, keys, check_hashes=True):
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        pup = f.read()
    if pup[:8] != b"SCEUF\0\0\0":
        raise input_fail("not a PUP file")
    _pkg_ver, _img_ver, count, hdr_len, data_len = struct.unpack_from(">5Q", pup, 8)
    if len(pup) < hdr_len + data_len or not count or 0x30 + count * 0x40 > len(pup):
        raise input_fail("PUP file is incomplete")
    entries = {}
    for i in range(count):
        eid, off, ln = struct.unpack_from(">QQQ", pup, 0x30 + 0x20 * i)
        if off + ln > len(pup):
            raise input_fail("PUP file table points outside the file")
        hoff = 0x30 + 0x20 * count + 0x20 * i
        heid, digest = u64(pup, hoff), pup[hoff + 8:hoff + 28]
        if check_hashes and hmac.new(keys.arrays["PUP_KEY"], pup[off:off + ln], hashlib.sha1).digest() != digest:
            raise input_fail(f"PUP entry 0x{eid:x} fails its hash check (damaged download?)")
        entries[eid] = pup[off:off + ln]
    return entries


def tar_entries(blob):
    """ustar reader: returns [(name, type, mtime, data)] in archive order."""
    out, pos = [], 0
    while pos + 512 <= len(blob):
        h = blob[pos:pos + 512]
        if h[257:262] != b"ustar":
            break
        name = h[0:100].split(b"\0")[0]
        prefix = h[345:500].split(b"\0")[0]
        if not name and not prefix:
            break
        size = int(h[124:136].split(b"\0")[0].strip() or b"0", 8)
        mtime = int(h[136:148].split(b"\0")[0].strip() or b"0", 8)
        typ = h[156:157]
        full = (prefix + b"/" + name) if prefix else name
        out.append((full.decode("utf-8"), typ, mtime, blob[pos + 512:pos + 512 + size]))
        pos += 512 + (size + 511) // 512 * 512
    return out


def install_firmware(pup_path, dest, keys, aes, log=print):
    entries = read_pup(pup_path, keys)
    version = entries.get(0x100, b"").split(b"\n")[0].decode("ascii", "replace")
    if 0x300 not in entries:
        raise input_fail("PUP has no update_files.tar (entry 0x300)")
    outer = tar_entries(entries[0x300])
    pkgs = [(n, d) for (n, t, m, d) in outer if "dev_flash_" in n]
    if not pkgs:
        raise input_fail("PUP holds no dev_flash_* packages")
    log(f"  firmware {version}: {len(pkgs)} packages")
    erk, riv = keys.arrays["SCEPKG_ERK"], keys.arrays["SCEPKG_RIV"]
    dest = os.path.abspath(dest)
    files = {}                                        # later entries of the same name replace earlier ones
    for name, pkg in pkgs:
        cf = CertifiedFile(pkg)
        cf.open_metadata(aes, erk, riv)
        blob = None
        for s in cf.sections:                          # the package's content: the section holding a ustar archive
            b = cf.section_plain(aes, s)
            if s["comp"] == 2:
                try:
                    b = zlib.decompress(b)
                except zlib.error as e:
                    raise input_fail(f"{name}: a section did not decompress ({e})")
            if b[257:262] == b"ustar":
                blob = b
                break
        if blob is None:
            raise input_fail(f"{name}: no file archive inside the package")
        for (n, t, mtime, d) in tar_entries(blob):
            if not n.startswith("dev_flash/") and n != "dev_flash":
                raise input_fail(f"{name}: unexpected path {n!r}")
            if t not in (b"0", b"\0", b"5"):
                raise input_fail(f"{name}: unsupported tar entry type {t!r} for {n}")
            files[n] = (t, mtime, d)
    # Everything is unpacked into <dest>.part first; only a complete tree is moved to <dest>.
    part = dest.rstrip("\\/") + ".part"
    nfiles = 0
    try:
        if os.path.exists(part):
            shutil.rmtree(part)
        os.makedirs(part)
        for n, (t, mtime, d) in sorted(files.items()):
            rel = n[len("dev_flash"):].strip("/")
            parts = [p for p in rel.split("/") if p]
            if any(p in (".", "..") or ":" in p or "\\" in p for p in parts):
                raise input_fail(f"unsafe path in firmware: {n!r}")
            target = os.path.join(part, *parts) if parts else part
            if t == b"5":
                os.makedirs(target, exist_ok=True)
            else:
                os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(target), exist_ok=True)
                with open(target, "wb") as f:
                    f.write(d)
                os.utime(target, (mtime, mtime))
                nfiles += 1
        if not os.path.exists(dest):
            os.rename(part, dest)
        else:                                          # merge into an existing folder, replacing same-named files
            for dp, dn, fn in os.walk(part):
                tdir = os.path.join(dest, os.path.relpath(dp, part))
                os.makedirs(tdir, exist_ok=True)
                for f in fn:
                    os.replace(os.path.join(dp, f), os.path.join(tdir, f))
            shutil.rmtree(part)
    except OSError as e:
        shutil.rmtree(part, ignore_errors=True)
        raise UnlockError(4, "OUTPUT", f"could not write the firmware files to {dest}: {e}")
    except BaseException:
        shutil.rmtree(part, ignore_errors=True)
        raise
    return version, nfiles


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Package (.pkg) -> the game's folder on the hard disk (psdevwiki "PKG files": header, metadata
# packets, item table). Retail PS3 packages only: the data area is AES-128-CTR, the key a fixed one,
# the counter the header's 16 bytes plus the 16-byte block number.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
_LOW16 = None


def _counter_blocks(c0, n):
    """n consecutive 16-byte big-endian counters from c0, built 65,536 at a time by one join."""
    global _LOW16
    if _LOW16 is None:
        _LOW16 = [i.to_bytes(2, "big") for i in range(65536)]
    out = []
    while n > 0:
        low = c0 & 0xFFFF
        run = min(n, 65536 - low)
        pre = ((c0 >> 16) & ((1 << 112) - 1)).to_bytes(14, "big")
        out.append(pre + pre.join(_LOW16[low:low + run]))
        c0 = (c0 + run) & ((1 << 128) - 1)
        n -= run
    return b"".join(out)


def read_sfo(blob):
    """PARAM.SFO -> {key: text or int}; {} when it is not one."""
    out = {}
    if len(blob) < 20 or blob[1:4] != b"PSF":
        return out
    key_t, data_t, n = struct.unpack_from("<III", blob, 8)
    for i in range(n):
        e = 20 + i * 16
        if e + 16 > len(blob):
            break
        ko, fmt, ln, _mx, do = struct.unpack_from("<HHIII", blob, e)
        end = blob.find(b"\0", key_t + ko)
        key = blob[key_t + ko:end].decode("ascii", "replace")
        if data_t + do + ln > len(blob):
            continue
        raw = blob[data_t + do:data_t + do + ln]
        out[key] = struct.unpack_from("<I", raw)[0] if fmt == 0x0404 and ln >= 4 else raw.split(b"\0")[0].decode("utf-8", "replace")
    return out


def _ver(s):
    """'02.11' -> 2.11; None when it is no version."""
    m = re.match(r"^\s*(\d{1,2})\.(\d{2})\s*$", s or "")
    return int(m.group(1)) + int(m.group(2)) / 100.0 if m else None


class Package:
    def __init__(self, path, keys, aes):
        self.path, self.aes = path, aes
        try:
            self.f = open(path, "rb")
            self.size = os.path.getsize(path)
            h = self.f.read(0xC0)
        except OSError as e:
            raise input_fail(f"cannot read {path}: {e}")
        if len(h) < 0xC0 or h[:4] != b"\x7fPKG":
            raise input_fail("not a PS3 package (.pkg)")
        rev, ptype = struct.unpack_from(">HH", h, 4)
        meta_off, meta_count, _meta_size, self.items = struct.unpack_from(">IIII", h, 8)
        total, self.data_off, self.data_size = struct.unpack_from(">QQQ", h, 0x18)
        if rev != 0x8000:
            raise input_fail("this package is not a finished retail one (a debug package): not handled")
        if ptype != 1:
            raise input_fail(f"not a PS3 package (type {ptype})")
        if total != self.size or self.data_off + self.data_size > self.size or self.items > 1000000:
            raise input_fail("the package is cut off or damaged (its sizes do not fit the file)")
        self.content_id = h[0x30:0x54].split(b"\0")[0].decode("ascii", "replace")
        self.key = keys.arrays.get("PKG_AES_KEY", b"")
        if len(self.key) != 16:
            raise keys_fail("could not read PKG_AES_KEY from key_vault.h")
        self.iv = int.from_bytes(h[0x70:0x80], "big")
        # Metadata packets (in the clear): 0x0A = the folder it installs into, after 8 other bytes.
        self.folder = ""
        try:
            self.f.seek(meta_off)
            for _ in range(min(meta_count, 64)):
                pid, psize = struct.unpack(">II", self.f.read(8))
                body = self.f.read(psize)
                if pid == 0x0A and psize > 8:
                    self.folder = body[8:].split(b"\0")[0].decode("ascii", "replace")
        except (OSError, struct.error):
            pass
        if not re.match(r"^[A-Z0-9_\-]{4,32}$", self.folder or ""):
            self.folder = self.content_id[7:16]
        if not re.match(r"^[A-Z]{4}\d{5}$", self.folder):
            raise input_fail(f"could not tell which game this package belongs to (content {self.content_id!r})")
        self.entries = None

    def close(self):
        try:
            self.f.close()
        except OSError:
            pass

    def plain(self, off, size):
        """size bytes of the data area at off, unlocked."""
        if off < 0 or off + size > self.data_size:
            raise input_fail("the package's own tables point outside it (damaged)")
        a = off & ~15
        n = (off + size - a + 15) // 16
        self.f.seek(self.data_off + a)
        enc = self.f.read(n * 16)
        ks = self.aes.ecb_encrypt(self.key, _counter_blocks((self.iv + a // 16) & ((1 << 128) - 1), n))
        return _xor(enc, ks)[off - a:off - a + size]

    def check_footer(self, tick=None):
        """The last 32 bytes are the SHA-1 of everything before them, then 12 zero bytes."""
        sha, left = hashlib.sha1(), self.size - 32
        self.f.seek(0)
        while left > 0:
            b = self.f.read(min(8 << 20, left))
            if not b:
                break
            sha.update(b)
            left -= len(b)
            if tick:
                tick(len(b))
        tail = self.f.read(32)
        if left or tail != sha.digest() + bytes(12):
            raise input_fail("the package is damaged (its own checksum does not match): download it again")

    def read_table(self):
        if self.entries is not None:
            return self.entries
        tbl = self.plain(0, self.items * 0x20)
        out = []
        for i in range(self.items):
            name_off, name_size, d_off, d_size, flags, _pad = struct.unpack_from(">IIQQII", tbl, i * 0x20)
            if name_size == 0 or name_size > 1024:
                raise input_fail("the package's file table is damaged (or it is not a PS3 retail package)")
            name = self.plain(name_off, name_size).split(b"\0")[0].decode("utf-8", "strict").replace("\\", "/")
            parts = [p for p in name.split("/") if p]
            if not parts or any(p in (".", "..") or ":" in p for p in parts) or name.startswith("/"):
                raise input_fail(f"the package holds a file name that is not allowed ({name!r})")
            out.append(("/".join(parts), d_off, d_size, flags))
        self.entries = out
        return out

    def sfo(self):
        for name, d_off, d_size, flags in self.read_table():
            if name == "PARAM.SFO" and d_size < (1 << 20):
                return read_sfo(self.plain(d_off, d_size))
        return {}


def install_package(pkg_path, game_root, keys, aes, info_only=False, log=print):
    """Unpack a package into <game_root>/<its title folder>, as a PS3 (or RPCS3) installs it:
    files that are there are replaced only where the package says so; an update is refused unless
    the version it builds on is installed. Returns (folder name, files written, files kept)."""
    p = Package(pkg_path, keys, aes)
    try:
        table = p.read_table()
        s = p.sfo()
        app, target, cat = str(s.get("APP_VER", "")), str(s.get("TARGET_APP_VER", "")), str(s.get("CATEGORY", ""))
        dest = os.path.join(game_root, p.folder)
        have = ""
        try:
            with open(os.path.join(dest, "PARAM.SFO"), "rb") as f:
                have = str(read_sfo(f.read()).get("APP_VER", ""))
        except OSError:
            pass
        files = [e for e in table if (e[3] & 0xFF) not in (4, 0x12)]
        total = sum(e[2] for e in files)
        log(f"PKG content={p.content_id} dir={p.folder} files={len(files)} bytes={total} app_ver={app or '-'}"
            f" target={target or '-'} category={cat or '-'} installed={have or '-'}", flush=True)
        if info_only:
            return p.folder, 0, 0
        # A game update: its own PARAM.SFO with a version, category "GD" (the first one names no
        # version to go on top of: it goes on the disc's 01.00).
        is_update = _ver(app) is not None and cat == "GD"
        if is_update:
            now = _ver(have) or 1.00            # nothing installed = the disc's 01.00
            if now >= _ver(app):
                log(f"PKG_SKIP update {app}: {have or '01.00'} is installed already", flush=True)
                return p.folder, 0, 0
            if _ver(target) is not None and now < _ver(target):
                raise input_fail(f"update {app} goes on top of {target}, and {have or '01.00'} is installed: install the updates in order")
        done = [0]
        last = [time.time()]

        def tick(n, scale=1):
            done[0] += n
            if time.time() - last[0] >= 1.0:
                last[0] = time.time()
                log(f"PKG_PROGRESS {done[0] // scale} {total_work}", flush=True)
        total_work = p.size + total
        p.check_footer(tick)
        written = kept = 0
        made = set()
        for name, d_off, d_size, flags in table:
            path = os.path.join(dest, *name.split("/"))
            if (flags & 0xFF) in (4, 0x12):
                os.makedirs(path, exist_ok=True)
                continue
            parent = os.path.dirname(path)
            if parent not in made:
                os.makedirs(parent, exist_ok=True)
                made.add(parent)
            if os.path.exists(path) and not (flags & 0x80000000):
                kept += 1                       # there already, and the package does not ask to replace it
                tick(d_size)
                continue
            if d_off + d_size > p.data_size or (d_off & 15):
                raise input_fail(f"the package's entry for {name} is damaged")
            part = path + ".pkgpart"
            try:
                with open(part, "wb") as o:
                    pos = 0
                    while pos < d_size:
                        n = min(8 << 20, d_size - pos)
                        o.write(p.plain(d_off + pos, n))
                        pos += n
                        tick(n)
                os.replace(part, path)
            except OSError as e:
                try:
                    os.remove(part)
                except OSError:
                    pass
                raise UnlockError(4, "OUTPUT", f"cannot write {path}: {e}")
            written += 1
        log(f"PKG_PROGRESS {total_work} {total_work}", flush=True)
        return p.folder, written, kept
    finally:
        p.close()


def main(argv):
    args, keys_dir, offline, info_only = [], os.environ.get("PS3_UNLOCK_KEYS") or os.path.join(
        os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "ps3_keys"), False, False
    it = iter(argv)
    for a in it:
        if a == "--keys-dir":
            keys_dir = next(it, "")
        elif a == "--offline":
            offline = True
        elif a == "--info":
            info_only = True
        else:
            args.append(a)
    if not args or args[0] not in ("eboot", "firmware", "keys", "pkg") or len(args) != (1 if args[0] == "keys" else 3):
        print(__doc__)
        return 1
    t0 = time.time()
    try:
        texts, fetched = fetch_key_sources(keys_dir, offline)
        try:
            keys = Keys(texts)
        except UnlockError:
            raise
        except Exception as e:
            raise keys_fail(f"key files did not parse: {e}")
        aes = make_aes()
        print(f"keys: RPCS3 {KEY_COMMIT[:8]}, {len(keys.selfkeys)} SELF keysets"
              f" ({'downloaded %d bytes' % fetched if fetched else 'cached'}); AES: {aes.name}")
        if args[0] == "keys":
            return 0
        src, dst = args[1], args[2]
        if args[0] == "eboot":
            try:
                with open(src, "rb") as f:
                    data = f.read()
            except OSError as e:
                raise input_fail(f"cannot read {src}: {e}")
            elf = self_to_elf(data, keys, aes)
            try:
                os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(dst)), exist_ok=True)
                with open(dst + ".part", "wb") as f:
                    f.write(elf)
                os.replace(dst + ".part", dst)
            except OSError as e:
                try:
                    os.remove(dst + ".part")
                except OSError:
                    pass
                raise UnlockError(4, "OUTPUT", f"cannot write {dst}: {e}")
            print(f"done: {dst} ({len(elf)} bytes, SHA-1 {hashlib.sha1(elf).hexdigest().upper()}) in {time.time() - t0:.1f} s")
        elif args[0] == "pkg":
            folder, written, kept = install_package(src, dst, keys, aes, info_only)
            if not info_only:
                print(f"done: {written} files written, {kept} kept, in {os.path.join(dst, folder)} in {time.time() - t0:.1f} s")
        else:
            version, n = install_firmware(src, dst, keys, aes)
            print(f"done: firmware {version}, {n} files in {dst} in {time.time() - t0:.1f} s")
        return 0
    except UnlockError as e:
        print(f"PS3_UNLOCK_FAIL {e.code} {e.kind}: {e}", flush=True)
        return e.code
    except Exception as e:                              # a damaged or unexpected file, or a bug here
        import traceback
        traceback.print_exc()
        print(f"PS3_UNLOCK_FAIL 5 INTERNAL: {type(e).__name__}: {e}", flush=True)
        return 5


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
```

`GT5/scripts/racefps.py`:

```py
"""Frame rate against draw load in a run's race: racefps.py <err log> ... [--last n]

Takes the last n windows of each log (default 30, about 150 s), so a menu before the race doesn't count. Prints the
median frame rate per band of draws per flip, and overall.
"""
import re
import sys

last = 30
if "--last" in sys.argv:
    i = sys.argv.index("--last")
    last = int(sys.argv[i + 1])
    del sys.argv[i:i + 2]


def rows(path):
    out, fps = [], None
    for line in open(path, errors="replace"):
        m = re.match(r"\[fps\] ([\d.]+)", line)
        if m:
            fps = float(m[1])
        m = re.match(r"\[gpu-work\] per flip: draws=(\d+) verts=(\d+)", line)
        if m and fps is not None:
            out.append((int(m[1]), int(m[2]), fps))
    return out[-last:]


for path in sys.argv[1:]:
    r = rows(path)
    bands = {}
    for d, _, f in r:
        bands.setdefault(min(d // 200 * 200, 1200), []).append(f)
    med = lambda v: sorted(v)[len(v) // 2]
    print(path.split("\\")[-1].split("/")[-1], "windows", len(r), "median fps %.1f" % med([x[2] for x in r]), "median draws %d" % med([x[0] for x in r]),
          {k: (len(v), med(v)) for k, v in sorted(bands.items())})
```

```ps1
# A race test with a CPU profile of its middle: raceprof.ps1 -Tag x [-Env @{...}] [-ProfSeconds 25]
# Starts racerun.ps1 hidden (muted, behind windows), waits until screendrive says "accelerate", lets the race
# settle, samples every thread with prof.ps1 into logs\prof_<Tag>.txt, then waits for the run to end.
param([string]$Tag = "rp", [hashtable]$Env = @{}, [int]$ProfSeconds = 25, [int]$Settle = 20)
$root = "$(Split-Path $PSScriptRoot -Parent)"
Remove-Item "$root\logs\$Tag.drive" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
# Screenshots stop once the race is reached, so the measured frame rate is the game's own.
$stop = "$root\logs\$Tag.nodump"
Remove-Item $stop -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
$Env["LD_FRAME_DUMP_STOP"] = $stop
$pairs = ($Env.GetEnumerator() | ForEach-Object { "$($_.Key)='$($_.Value)'" }) -join ";"
$cmd = "& '$root\scripts\racerun.ps1' -Tag $Tag -Seconds 640 -EndAfter $($Settle + $ProfSeconds + 30) -Env @{$pairs}"
$run = Start-Process powershell -WindowStyle Hidden -PassThru -ArgumentList "-NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command `"$cmd`""
$t0 = Get-Date
while (((Get-Date) - $t0).TotalSeconds -lt 560) {
    Start-Sleep 3
    $d = Get-Content "$root\logs\$Tag.drive" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    if ($d -match "accelerate") { break }
    if ($run.HasExited) { break }
}
if (-not ($d -match "accelerate")) { "no race reached"; return }
Set-Content -Path $stop -Value "race" -Encoding ascii
Start-Sleep $Settle
# -ProfSeconds 0: no sampling (it suspends threads and costs frames), just a clean measurement.
if ($ProfSeconds -gt 0) { & "$root\scripts\prof.ps1" -Seconds $ProfSeconds -Hz 60 -Out "$root\logs\prof_$Tag.txt" | Out-Null }
$run.WaitForExit(240000) | Out-Null
"race at $([int]((Get-Date) - $t0).TotalSeconds) s, profile in logs\prof_$Tag.txt"
```

`GT5/scripts/racerun.ps1`:

```ps1
# One full test: run gt5.exe, follow its screen to a race with screendrive.py, sample it with prof.ps1.
#   racerun.ps1 -Tag p2 [-Seconds 900] [-EndAfter 120] [-Env @{...}]
# Frames land in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\gt5_frames_<Tag>, samples in logs\prof_<Tag>_car.txt and _race.txt, the route in logs\<Tag>.drive.
# -Capture car|race|both writes logs\<Tag>.csv (RSX_DRAW_CSV) and analysis\surf_<Tag> (LD_SURF_DUMP) at that point.
param([string]$Tag = "rr", [int]$Seconds = 900, [int]$EndAfter = 120, [hashtable]$Env = @{}, [string]$Capture = "", [int]$SkipMovie = 50, [string]$DriveArgs = "")
$root = "$(Split-Path $PSScriptRoot -Parent)"
$s = "$root\scripts"
Set-Content -Path "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Temp\gt5_pad.txt" -Value "" -Encoding ascii -NoNewline
$frames = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Temp\gt5_frames_$Tag"   # C:, because a 6.6 MB dump on the USB drive stalls the RSX thread
$e = @{ PAD_FILE = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Temp\gt5_pad.txt"; PS3_VERBOSE = "0"
        LD_FRAME_DUMP = $frames; LD_FRAME_DUMP_MS = "1000"; LD_GPU_WORK = "1"; SPU_DMA_REPEAT_SECS = "100000" }
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $frames | Out-Null
$extra = ""
if ($Capture) {
    $gate = "$root\logs\$Tag.gate"
    Remove-Item $gate -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "$root\analysis\surf_$Tag", "$root\analysis\ps_$Tag" | Out-Null
    $e["RSX_DRAW_CSV"] = "$root\logs\$Tag.csv"; $e["RSX_DRAW_CSV_GATE"] = $gate
    $e["LD_SURF_DUMP"] = "$root\analysis\surf_$Tag"; $e["LD_SURF_DUMP_GATE"] = $gate
    $e["LD_FRAME_BURST"] = $gate
    $e["LD_PS_DUMP"] = "$root\analysis\ps_$Tag"
    $extra = "--gate `"$gate`" --capture $Capture"
}
# -DriveArgs passes more screendrive.py options, e.g. "--track-keys up,right,down" for another track.
if ($DriveArgs) { $extra = "$extra $DriveArgs" }
if ($env:FS_HIDE) { $e["FS_HIDE"] = $env:FS_HIDE }
foreach ($k in $Env.Keys) { $e[$k] = $Env[$k] }
# A run wider than 16:9 (PS3_ASPECT or PS3_WINDOW_SIZE) has the menus drawn squeezed; screendrive stretches them back.
$shape = if ($e["PS3_ASPECT"]) { $e["PS3_ASPECT"] } elseif ($e["PS3_WINDOW_SIZE"]) { $e["PS3_WINDOW_SIZE"] } else { "" }
if ($shape -match '^([\d.]+)[xX:]([\d.]+)$') {
    $widen = ([double]$Matches[1] / [double]$Matches[2]) / (16.0 / 9.0)
    if ($widen -gt 1.005) { $extra = "$extra --widen $($widen.ToString([cultureinfo]::InvariantCulture))" }
}
$drive = Start-Process python -WindowStyle Hidden -PassThru -ArgumentList "`"$s\screendrive.py`" --dir `"$frames`" --pad `"$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Temp\gt5_pad.txt`" --race --log `"$root\logs\$Tag.drive`" --prof `"$root\logs\prof_$Tag`" --end-after $EndAfter --timeout $Seconds --skip-movie $SkipMovie $extra"
& "$s\run.ps1" -Seconds $Seconds -Tag $Tag -Env $e
if (-not $drive.HasExited) { Stop-Process -Id $drive.Id -Force -Confirm:$false }
Get-Content "$root\logs\$Tag.drive" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
```

```py
"""Turn raw guest frame dumps into PNGs: rawview.py <file> <out.png> <w> <h> <rgba|argb|y> [--stride n] [--scale n]"""
import sys

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

path, out, w, h, kind = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3]), int(sys.argv[4]), sys.argv[5]
stride = int(sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--stride") + 1]) if "--stride" in sys.argv else None
scale = int(sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--scale") + 1]) if "--scale" in sys.argv else 2
raw = np.fromfile(path, dtype=np.uint8)
if kind == "y":
    s = stride or w
    a = raw[: s * h].reshape(h, s)[:, :w]
    print("luma min %d mean %.1f max %d" % (a.min(), a.mean(), a.max()))
    im = Image.fromarray(a)
else:
    s = stride or w * 4
    a = raw[: s * h].reshape(h, s)[:, : w * 4].reshape(h, w, 4)
    print("channels mean", [round(float(a[:, :, i].mean()), 1) for i in range(4)], "max", [int(a[:, :, i].max()) for i in range(4)])
    rgb = a[:, :, :3] if kind == "rgba" else a[:, :, 1:4]
    im = Image.fromarray(rgb)
im.resize((w // scale, h // scale)).save(out)
print(out)
```

```ps1
# Rebuild gt5.exe, optionally re-lifting first: rebuild.ps1 [-Lift] [-Jobs 10]
param([switch]$Lift, [int]$Jobs = 10)
$root = "$(Split-Path $PSScriptRoot -Parent)"
$ErrorActionPreference = "Continue"
if ($Lift) {
    $t = Get-Date
    & "$root\scripts\relift.ps1" *> "$root\analysis\relift.log"
    "relift: $([int]((Get-Date) - $t).TotalSeconds) s"
    Select-String -Path "$root\analysis\relift.log" -Pattern "failed|Traceback" | Select-Object -First 10 | ForEach-Object { $_.Line }
}
$t = Get-Date
$env:GT5_JOBS = "$Jobs"
cmd /c "$root\scripts\build.cmd gt5 > $root\analysis\build_gt5.log 2>&1"
$built = $LASTEXITCODE
"build exit $built in $([int]((Get-Date) - $t).TotalSeconds) s"
Select-String -Path "$root\analysis\build_gt5.log" -Pattern "error:|FAILED|LNK\d+" | Select-Object -First 15 | ForEach-Object { $_.Line }
# A freshly linked exe can stall on first launch, so run it once now: silent, behind other windows.
if ($built -eq 0) {
    $env:PS3_MUTE = "1"; $env:PS3_WINDOW_BEHIND = "1"
    $p = Start-Process "$root\build\gt5.exe" -ArgumentList "--help" -PassThru -NoNewWindow -RedirectStandardOutput "$root\logs\h.out" -RedirectStandardError "$root\logs\h.err"
    Start-Sleep -Seconds 4
    if (-not $p.HasExited) { Stop-Process -Id $p.Id -Force -Confirm:$false }
}
```

```ps1
# One command for a full lift: functions, PPU C++, setjmp patch, NID table, SPU images.
# Run from anywhere; generated/ and spu/ are rebuilt wholesale.
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
$root = Split-Path $PSScriptRoot -Parent
$tk   = Join-Path $root "..\ps3recomp\tools"
$py   = Join-Path $root "..\venv\Scripts\python.exe"

Set-Location $root

function Run($label, [string[]]$a) {
    Write-Output "== $label"
    & $py @a
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "$label failed ($LASTEXITCODE)" }
}

$ErrorActionPreference = "Continue"
# Everything the lift needs, checked first so a missing piece gives one clear message instead of a
# cascade of errors. setup.ps1 makes the first two; the last is the player's own file.
$missing = @()
if (-not (Test-Path $py)) { $missing += "the Python environment (venv\Scripts\python.exe): setup.ps1 makes it" }
if (-not (Test-Path (Join-Path $tk "ppu_lifter.py"))) { $missing += "ps3recomp with the patch (ps3recomp\tools): setup.ps1 fetches it" }
if (-not (Test-Path "input\EBOOT.elf")) { $missing += "GT5\input\EBOOT.elf, your decrypted game executable (README, Setup)" }

    Write-Host "relift.ps1 can't start. Missing:" -ForegroundColor Red
    $missing | ForEach-Object { Write-Host "  - $_" -ForegroundColor Red }
    Write-Host "Run setup.ps1 from the gt5-recomp folder (not from GT5\scripts): it lists everything still missing,"
    Write-Host "and once it's all in place it runs this lift and the build for you."
    exit 1
}
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "analysis" | Out-Null

# The addresses that differ between GT5 releases (code end, setjmp/longjmp, a computed goto),
# found in this copy's EBOOT by version_addrs.py. Europe 01.00: 0x111c684, 00D00D74/00D00E98.
Write-Output "== version_addrs"
& $py "scripts\version_addrs.py" "input\EBOOT.elf"
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Write-Warning "version_addrs.py did not find everything; see its NOT FOUND lines" }
if (-not (Test-Path "analysis\version.json")) {
    Write-Host "version_addrs.py couldn't read GT5\input\EBOOT.elf (see the message above). Is it the decrypted file?" -ForegroundColor Red
    exit 1
}
$ver = Get-Content "analysis\version.json" -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
$codeEnd = $ver.code_end
Run "ppu_loader"     @("$tk\ppu_loader.py", "input\EBOOT.elf", "-o", "analysis\")
Run "find_functions" @("$tk\find_functions.py", "input\EBOOT.elf", "--seed-json", "analysis\EBOOT.functions.json", "--output", "analysis\functions.json")
Run "filter"         @("scripts\filter_functions.py", "input\EBOOT.elf", "analysis\functions.json", "analysis\functions_code.json")

# Game-code mods in GT5\mods (see MODDING.md): their instruction patches go to the lifter, each
# behind a start-up switch. With no mod for this EBOOT, mods.py writes nothing and the lift is plain.
Run "mods"           @("scripts\mods.py")
$liftArgs = @("$tk\ppu_lifter.py", "input\EBOOT.elf", "--functions", "analysis\functions_code.json",
              "--hle-stubs", "analysis\EBOOT.imports.json", "--code-end", $codeEnd,
              "--label-jumps", "analysis\label_jumps.json",
              "--jobs", "16", "--chunks", "48", "--output", "generated")
if (Test-Path "analysis\insn_patches.json") { $liftArgs += @("--insn-patches", "analysis\insn_patches.json") }
Run "ppu_lifter"     $liftArgs
Run "setjmp_patch"   @("scripts\setjmp_patch.py")

# The SPU code (the PS3's co-processors: physics, sound, graphics set-up), compiled like the main code:
# the SPU programs and the SPURS jobs this copy's EBOOT carries. An SPU program not found runs in the
# SPU interpreter, many times slower; a SPURS job not found can't run at all, and the game stalls when
# it needs it (spu_jobs_from_eboot.py names any it misses).
# A GT5\spu from an older version may have a closed permission list: fix_spu_access.ps1 puts it right.
& (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "fix_spu_access.ps1")
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit 1 }
Run "spu_programs"   @("$tk\build_spu_workloads.py", "--input", "input\EBOOT.elf", "--lifted", "spu",
                       "--out", "spu\spu_workloads.c", "--constructor", "--allow-partial")
Run "spu_jobs_find"  @("scripts\spu_jobs_from_eboot.py")
if (Get-ChildItem "analysis\spu_miss\spujob_*.bin" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
    Run "spu_jobs"   @("scripts\lift_spu_jobs.py")
}

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force src\gen | Out-Null
Run "gen_hle_nids"   @("$tk\gen_hle_nids.py", "--all", "--out", "src\gen\ppu_hle_nids.cpp")
# Record what this lift was made from, so update.ps1 re-lifts only when that changes.
Run "lift_stamp"     @("scripts\lift_stamp.py", "--write")
```

```sh
# Linux version of relift.ps1: one command for a full lift (functions, PPU C++, setjmp patch, NID
# table, SPU images), made from your own GT5/input/EBOOT.elf. setup.sh runs it when the game code is

                   --out spu/spu_workloads.c --constructor --allow-partial

    run spu_jobs   scripts/lift_spu_jobs.py
```

`GT5/scripts/ringlog.py`:

```py
"""Read an AUDIO_RINGLOG file: ringlog.py <file> [--port n] [--from sec] [--to sec] [--dump a,b]

Prints the writer's lead over the read cursor, the time between blocks, and every run of
blocks read while empty. --dump prints the raw lines around those times (seconds from start).
"""
import collections
import sys


def arg(n, d=None):
    return sys.argv[sys.argv.index(n) + 1] if n in sys.argv else d


rows = []
for line in open(sys.argv[1]):
    f = line.split()
    if len(f) < 5:
        continue
    rows.append((int(f[0]), int(f[1]), int(f[2]), int(f[3]), int(f[4]), f[5] if len(f) > 5 else ""))
ports = collections.Counter(r[1] for r in rows)
print("ports", dict(ports))
want = int(arg("--port", ports.most_common(1)[0][0]))
rows = [r for r in rows if r[1] == want]
t0 = rows[0][0]
lo, hi = float(arg("--from", 0)), float(arg("--to", 1e9))
rows = [r for r in rows if lo <= (r[0] - t0) / 1e6 <= hi]
print("blocks", len(rows), "span %.1f s" % ((rows[-1][0] - rows[0][0]) / 1e6), "ring", len(rows[0][5]))
leads = collections.Counter(r[4] for r in rows)
print("lead", " ".join("%d:%.1f%%" % (k, 100.0 * leads[k] / len(rows)) for k in sorted(leads)))
gaps = [b[0] - a[0] for a, b in zip(rows, rows[1:])]
hist = collections.Counter(min(g // 1000, 40) for g in gaps)
print("ms between blocks", " ".join("%d:%d" % (k, hist[k]) for k in sorted(hist)))
runs = []
i = 0
while i < len(rows):
    if rows[i][4] == 0:
        j = i
        while j + 1 < len(rows) and rows[j + 1][4] == 0:
            j += 1
        runs.append((i, j))
        i = j + 1
    else:
        i += 1
lens = collections.Counter(b - a + 1 for a, b in runs)
print("empty runs", len(runs), "lengths", " ".join("%d:%d" % (k, lens[k]) for k in sorted(lens)))
print("empty blocks %.1f%%" % (100.0 * sum(b - a + 1 for a, b in runs) / len(rows)))
for a, b in runs[:12]:
    print("  at %.3f s, %d blocks, slot %d..%d, lead before: %s" % (
        (rows[a][0] - t0) / 1e6, b - a + 1, rows[a][3], rows[b][3], " ".join(str(r[4]) for r in rows[max(0, a - 12):a])))
if "--dump" in sys.argv:
    x, y = [float(v) for v in arg("--dump").split(",")]
    for r in rows:
        if x <= (r[0] - t0) / 1e6 <= y:
            print("%9.3f r=%d slot=%2d lead=%2d %s" % ((r[0] - t0) / 1e6, r[2], r[3], r[4], r[5]))

```

```py
import os as _gt5_os  # this clone's folders, wherever it was cloned to
GT5_DIR = _gt5_os.path.dirname(_gt5_os.path.dirname(_gt5_os.path.abspath(__file__)))
BASE_DIR = _gt5_os.path.dirname(GT5_DIR)
"""Scripted menu routes for a live session, each step checked only by timing: route.py <name> [name ...]

    home    from a fresh boot through the dialog and movie to My Home
    sunday  from My Home into the first Sunday Cup race's grid screen
    bspec   from My Home into the first B-Spec Sunday Cup race, started
    rain    from My Home to driving a Practice free run at High Speed Ring in the rain
    photo   from that free run through its replay to Photo Mode, and take a shot
"""
import subprocess
import sys
import time

GP = (GT5_DIR + r"\scripts\gp.py")


def step(button, wait, polls=None):
    a = ["python", GP]
    if button:
        a.append(button)
    if polls:
        a += ["--polls", str(polls)]
    a += ["--wait", str(wait)]
    subprocess.run(a, capture_output=True)


ROUTES = {
    "home": [(None, 40), ("cross", 14), ("cross", 8), ("cross", 20), ("cross", 18)],
    "rain": [("right", 2, 16), ("right", 2, 16), ("down", 2, 16), ("cross", 10), ("right", 3, 16), ("cross", 6),
             ("cross", 8), ("cross", 60), ("cross", 25), ("cross", 12, 1500)],
    "photo": [("start", 4, 30), ("right", 1.6, 16), ("right", 1.6, 16), ("right", 1.6, 16), ("cross", 8), ("right", 2.5, 16),
              ("cross", 14), ("start", 4, 30), ("left", 3, 16), ("cross", 10), ("cross", 5), ("cross", 30)],
    "bspec": [("right", 2, 24), ("right", 2, 24), ("cross", 9, 30), ("cross", 8, 30), ("cross", 8, 30), ("cross", 40, 30), ("cross", 3, 24),
              ("down", 2, 24), ("cross", 40, 30), ("cross", 30, 30)],
    "sunday": [("right", 2, 16), ("cross", 8), ("cross", 4), ("cross", 10), ("cross", 6), ("cross", 60)],
}
for name in sys.argv[1:]:
    t = time.time()
    for s in ROUTES[name]:
        step(*s)
    print(name, "done in %.0f s" % (time.time() - t))
```

`GT5/scripts/rpcs3_mods.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Turn RPCS3 game patches (patch.yml) into the port's game-code mods (GT5/mods), where they fit.

    python scripts/rpcs3_mods.py <patch.yml>                        list the patches for this copy
    python scripts/rpcs3_mods.py <patch.yml> --add "Disable Dithering" [--add "..."]

RPCS3 patches are listed per game executable under "PPU-<hash>"; this works out that hash for the
EBOOT the port was lifted from (GT5/input/EBOOT.elf, the same one relift.ps1 and mods.py read), so
only the patches written for exactly this release and update are offered.

A patch fits when every write in it swaps one instruction in the game's code (be32 into an
executable segment) for one that doesn't branch: the same shape a mod has (scripts/mods.py). RPCS3
writes its patches into the game's code while it runs; here the code was turned into PC code ahead
of time, so a patch that adds new code of its own (most long ones), changes data, takes a
configurable value or branches somewhere new can't be brought over this way, and is left out whole.

--add writes GT5/mods/rpcs3-<name>/mod.json, on by default (GT5_MOD_RPCS3_<NAME>=0 turns it off),
with each instruction's original read from your EBOOT. Then run scripts\\relift.ps1 and
scripts\\build.cmd gt5 (as for any mod, see MODDING.md). The patches stay RPCS3's authors' work:
the mod names them, and you get them from your own patch.yml; don't put the generated mods in a
repository of your own without their permission.
"""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import re
import struct
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent

OP_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*-\s*\[\s*([A-Za-z0-9_]+)\s*(?:,\s*([^,\]]+?)\s*)?(?:,\s*(.+?)\s*)?\]\s*(?:#.*)?$")
PATCH_NAME_RE = re.compile(r'^  "(.+)":\s*(?:#.*)?$')
FIELD_RE = re.compile(r'^    (Author|Notes):\s*(.*?)\s*$')


def read_elf(path):
    """The ELF's file SHA-1 (mods.py's key), RPCS3's PPU hash, and a reader for code words."""
    d = path.read_bytes()
    phoff = struct.unpack(">Q", d[0x20:0x28])[0]
    es, n = struct.unpack(">HH", d[0x36:0x3A])
    h = hashlib.sha1()
    code = []
    for i in range(n):
        o = phoff + i * es
        p_type, p_flags, p_offset, p_vaddr, _, p_filesz, p_memsz = struct.unpack(">IIQQQQQ", d[o:o + 48])
        # RPCS3's PPU hash (ppu_load_exec): type and flags of every program header, then the
        # address, size and file bytes of each loadable one.
        h.update(struct.pack(">II", p_type, p_flags))
        if p_type == 1 and p_memsz:
            h.update(struct.pack(">QQ", p_vaddr, p_memsz))
            h.update(d[p_offset:p_offset + p_filesz])
            if p_flags & 1 and p_filesz:          # executable: the code the lifter turned into C++
                code.append((p_vaddr, p_offset, p_filesz))

    def code_word(addr):
        for va, off, size in code:
            if va <= addr <= va + size - 4:
                return struct.unpack(">I", d[off + addr - va:off + addr - va + 4])[0]
        return None
    return hashlib.sha1(d).hexdigest().upper(), "PPU-" + h.hexdigest(), code_word


def parse_anchors(lines):
    """{anchor: {"ops": [...], "text": "..."}}: the shared write lists and notes patches refer to
    with `- [ load, *name ]` and `Notes: *name`."""
    anchors, cur, indent = {}, None, 0
    for line in lines:
        if not line.strip() or line.lstrip().startswith("#"):
            continue
        ind = len(line) - len(line.lstrip(" "))
        m = re.match(r"^(\s*)[^\s:]+:\s*&(\S+)\s*(?:#.*)?$", line)
        if m:
            cur, indent = anchors.setdefault(m.group(2), {"ops": [], "text": ""}), len(m.group(1))
            continue
        if cur is None or ind <= indent:
            cur = None
            continue
        m = OP_RE.match(line)
        if m:
            cur["ops"].append((m.group(1).lower(), m.group(2) or "", m.group(3) or ""))
        elif line.strip().startswith('"') and not cur["text"]:
            cur["text"] = line.strip()[1:-1].replace('\\"', '"') if line.strip().endswith('"') else ""
    return anchors


def parse_patches(path, ppu):
    """{patch name: {"author", "notes", "ops": [(op, addr_text, value_text)]}} for one PPU hash,
    with `load` writes replaced by the anchor's own (moved by the load's offset, if any)."""
    lines = [raw.rstrip() for raw in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines()]
    anchors = parse_anchors(lines)
    out, cur, in_block, in_patch = {}, None, False, False
    for line in lines:
        if not line.strip() or line.lstrip().startswith("#"):
            continue
        if not line.startswith(" "):                       # a top-level key: PPU-..., Anchors:, ...
            in_block = line.split(":")[0].strip().lower() == ppu.lower()
            cur, in_patch = None, False
            continue
        if not in_block:
            continue
        m = PATCH_NAME_RE.match(line)
        if m:
            cur = out.setdefault(m.group(1), {"author": "", "notes": "", "ops": []})
            in_patch = False
            continue
        if cur is None:
            continue
        m = FIELD_RE.match(line)
        if m:
            v = m.group(2)
            if v.startswith('"') and v.endswith('"') and len(v) >= 2:
                cur[m.group(1).lower()] = v[1:-1].replace('\\"', '"')
            elif v.startswith("*") and v[1:] in anchors:
                cur[m.group(1).lower()] = anchors[v[1:]]["text"]
            in_patch = False
            continue
        if re.match(r"^    Patch:\s*$", line):
            in_patch = True
            continue
        if re.match(r"^    \S", line):                     # another field of this patch
            in_patch = False
            continue
        if in_patch:
            m = OP_RE.match(line)
            if not m:
                cur["ops"].append(("?", line.strip(), ""))
            elif m.group(1).lower() == "load":
                name = (m.group(2) or "").lstrip("*")
                shift = number(m.group(3)) if m.group(3) else 0
                if name not in anchors or shift is None:
                    cur["ops"].append(("?", line.strip(), ""))
                    continue
                for op, a, v in anchors[name]["ops"]:
                    addr = number(a)
                    cur["ops"].append((op, hex(addr + shift) if addr is not None and op != "load" else a, v))
            else:
                cur["ops"].append((m.group(1).lower(), m.group(2) or "", m.group(3) or ""))
    return out


def number(text):
    try:
        return int(text.strip().strip('"'), 0)
    except ValueError:
        return None


def convert(patch, code_word):
    """(list of (addr, orig, new), None) when the patch fits; (None, reason) when it doesn't."""
    ops = patch["ops"]
    if not ops:
        return None, "has no writes"
    words = {}                      # instruction address -> its new word, writes applied in order
    for op, a, v in ops:
        size = {"be32": 4, "be16": 2, "byte": 1}.get(op)
        if size is None:
            return None, f"has a '{op}' write (only changes to instructions fit)"
        addr, val = number(a), number(v)
        if addr is None or val is None:
            return None, "takes a configurable value"
        if addr % size:
            return None, f"writes {size} bytes at 0x{addr:08X}, not aligned"
        base = addr & ~3
        orig = code_word(base)
        if orig is None:
            return None, f"writes outside the game's code (0x{addr:08X}: data, or new code of its own)"
        shift = (4 - size - (addr & 3)) * 8              # big-endian: the bytes' place in the word
        mask = ((1 << (size * 8)) - 1) << shift
        cur = words.get(base, orig)
        words[base] = (cur & ~mask & 0xFFFFFFFF) | ((val << shift) & mask)
    swaps = []
    for base, new in sorted(words.items()):
        orig = code_word(base)
        if new == orig:
            continue
        # A branch can't be the replacement (the lifter has no labels for new targets), nor the
        # original when it never falls through (b, blr, bctr): the code after it may not be lifted
        # as reachable from there. A conditional branch (bc) may become a plain instruction.
        if (new >> 26) in (16, 17, 18, 19) or (orig >> 26) in (17, 18, 19):
            return None, f"changes a branch at 0x{base:08X} (new code paths can't be added after lifting)"
        swaps.append((base, orig, new))
    if not swaps:
        return None, "changes nothing in this EBOOT"
    return swaps, None


def taken(mods_dir, sha1, skip):
    """{instruction address: mod name} already patched by the mods in mods_dir for this EBOOT."""
    out = {}
    for mj in sorted(Path(mods_dir).glob("*/mod.json")) if Path(mods_dir).is_dir() else []:
        if mj.parent.name == skip:
            continue
        try:
            m = json.loads(mj.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            for p in (m.get("patches") or {}).get(sha1, []):
                out[int(str(p["addr"]), 0)] = str(m.get("name") or mj.parent.name)
        except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):
            continue
    return out


def slug(name):
    s = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", name.lower()).strip("-")
    return ("rpcs3-" + s)[:48].rstrip("-")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("patch_yml", help="RPCS3's patch.yml (or imported_patch.yml)")
    ap.add_argument("--add", action="append", default=[], metavar="NAME", help="patch name to turn into a mod")
    ap.add_argument("--elf", default=str(ROOT / "input" / "EBOOT.elf"))
    ap.add_argument("--mods", default=str(ROOT / "mods"))
    a = ap.parse_args()

    sha1, ppu, code_word = read_elf(Path(a.elf))
    patches = parse_patches(Path(a.patch_yml), ppu)
    print(f"This copy's EBOOT: {ppu} (file SHA-1 {sha1[:12]}...)")
    if not patches:
        print("The patch file has no patches for it.")
        return 1 if a.add else 0
    results = {name: convert(p, code_word) for name, p in patches.items()}
    if not a.add:
        for name, (swaps, why) in results.items():
            by = f" ({patches[name]['author']})" if patches[name]["author"] else ""
            if swaps:
                print(f"  fits:    {name}{by}: {len(swaps)} instruction(s)")
            else:
                print(f"  doesn't: {name}{by}: {why}")
        print('Add one with --add "<name>", then run scripts\\relift.ps1 and scripts\\build.cmd gt5.')
        return 0

    status = 0
    for want in a.add:
        name = next((n for n in patches if n.lower() == want.lower()), None)
        if name is None:
            print(f"'{want}': no patch by that name for this EBOOT")
            status = 1
            continue
        swaps, why = results[name]
        if not swaps:
            print(f"'{name}' doesn't fit: {why}")
            status = 1
            continue
        p = patches[name]
        mod = slug(name)
        clash = taken(a.mods, sha1, mod)
        both = sorted({clash[ad] for ad, _, _ in swaps if ad in clash})
        if both:
            print(f"'{name}' changes an instruction that {', '.join(both)} already changes: use that mod instead")
            status = 1
            continue
        desc = f"{name}: RPCS3 patch" + (f" by {p['author']}" if p["author"] else "") + \
               (f". {p['notes']}" if p["notes"] else "")
        doc = {"name": mod, "description": desc, "default": True,
               "patches": {sha1: [{"addr": f"0x{ad:08X}", "orig": f"0x{o:08X}", "new": f"0x{n:08X}",
                                   "note": f"from RPCS3's patch.yml ({ppu})"} for ad, o, n in swaps]}}
        out = Path(a.mods) / mod / "mod.json"
        out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        out.write_text(json.dumps(doc, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        env = "GT5_MOD_" + mod.replace("-", "_").upper()
        print(f"'{name}': {len(swaps)} instruction(s) -> {out} (on; {env}=0 turns it off)")
    if status == 0:
        print("Now run scripts\\relift.ps1, then scripts\\build.cmd gt5.")
    return status


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

`GT5/scripts/rsxwhere.py`:

```py
import os as _gt5_os  # this clone's folders, wherever it was cloned to
GT5_DIR = _gt5_os.path.dirname(_gt5_os.path.dirname(_gt5_os.path.abspath(__file__)))
BASE_DIR = _gt5_os.path.dirname(GT5_DIR)
"""What the RSX thread is doing right now, sampled: rsxwhere.py [samples] [gap seconds]

Runs hoststack.py several times and tallies the top frames of the thread running vblank_ticker.
"""
import collections
import subprocess
import sys
import time

n = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 8
gap = float(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 0.5
tally = collections.Counter()
for _ in range(n):
    out = subprocess.run(["python", "-I", (GT5_DIR + r"\scripts\hoststack.py"), "--all", "--depth", "24"],
                         capture_output=True, text=True, errors="replace").stdout
    for block in out.split("== ")[1:]:
        lines = [l.strip() for l in block.splitlines()[1:]]
        if any("vblank_ticker" in l for l in lines):
            top = [l.split("  ")[0].split("+")[0] for l in lines[:6]]
            tally[" < ".join(top)] += 1
    time.sleep(gap)
for k, v in tally.most_common():
    print(v, k[:170])
```
