```ps1
# Run gt5.exe for a fixed time and keep its output. -Window opens the D3D12 window;
# otherwise it runs headless. -Env sets extra variables, e.g. -Env @{PS3_ARGV="boot_from=x"}.
param([int]$Seconds = 60, [switch]$Window, [hashtable]$Env = @{}, [string]$Tag = "run")
$root = "$(Split-Path $PSScriptRoot -Parent)"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "$root\hdd0", "$root\hdd1", "$root\logs" | Out-Null
$env:PS3_VFS_ROOT = "$root\vfs"
# Test runs use their own copy of the saves and caches, so the real save (play.bat) stays untouched.
$env:PS3_HDD0_ROOT = "$root\test_save\hdd0"
$env:PS3_GAMEDATA_ROOT = "$root\test_save\gamedata"
$env:PS3_HDD1_ROOT = "$root\test_save\hdd1"
$env:PS3_DEV_FLASH = "$(Split-Path $PSScriptRoot -Parent)\dev_flash"
$env:RSX_LIVE_DRAW = "1"
$env:PS3_TITLE = "Gran Turismo 5"
# GT5's SPU jobs fill self-JUMP holes in the FIFO, slowly during loads. Real RSX just waits.
$env:GCM_PARK_GRACE_MS = "600000"
$env:SPU_DMA_REPEAT_SECS = "100000"
$env:SPURS_EXTRA_SPUS = "2"
# Test runs stay silent on the speakers; audiolevel.py checks what would have played.
$env:PS3_MUTE = "1"
$env:AUDIO_WAV = "$root\logs\audio_last.f32"
if (-not $Window) { $env:PS3_HEADLESS = "1"; $env:PS3_WINDOW_BEHIND = "1" }
foreach ($k in $Env.Keys) { Set-Item "env:$k" $Env[$k] }
$out = "$root\logs\$Tag.out"; $err = "$root\logs\$Tag.err"
$t0 = Get-Date
# GT5_TEST_EXE=<path>: run another build (e.g. one made from the published source) with the same data.
$exe = if ($env:GT5_TEST_EXE) { $env:GT5_TEST_EXE } else { "$root\build\gt5.exe" }
# GT5_TEST_ELF=<path>: the EBOOT.elf that build was lifted from (another release or update).
$elf = if ($env:GT5_TEST_ELF) { $env:GT5_TEST_ELF } else { "$root\input\EBOOT.elf" }
$p = Start-Process $exe -ArgumentList "`"$elf`"" -WorkingDirectory $root `
    -PassThru -NoNewWindow -RedirectStandardOutput $out -RedirectStandardError $err
$h = $p.Handle  # keeps ExitCode readable after exit
$peak = 0
while (-not $p.HasExited -and ((Get-Date) - $t0).TotalSeconds -lt $Seconds) {
    try { $p.Refresh(); if ($p.PeakWorkingSet64 -gt $peak) { $peak = $p.PeakWorkingSet64 } } catch {}
    Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 500
}
$alive = -not $p.HasExited
if ($alive) { Stop-Process -Id $p.Id -Force -Confirm:$false; "still running after $Seconds s, stopped it" }
else { "exited by itself after $([int]((Get-Date) - $t0).TotalSeconds) s, code $($p.ExitCode) (0x$('{0:X8}' -f $p.ExitCode))" }
"peak RAM $([math]::Round($peak / 1GB, 2)) GB"
"stdout $([math]::Round((Get-Item $out).Length / 1MB, 2)) MB, stderr $([math]::Round((Get-Item $err).Length / 1MB, 2)) MB"
```

`GT5/scripts/scan_computed.py`:

```py
import os as _gt5_os  # this clone's folders, wherever it was cloned to
GT5_DIR = _gt5_os.path.dirname(_gt5_os.path.dirname(_gt5_os.path.abspath(__file__)))
BASE_DIR = _gt5_os.path.dirname(GT5_DIR)
"""List lifted `bctr`s that are computed jumps inside a function, not tail calls.

A tail call through an OPD reloads r2 first. One that doesn't is either a jump through
a label table the lifter couldn't see, or a tail call through a plain code pointer.
"""
import glob
import re

head = re.compile(r"^void (?:gt5_orig_)?func_([0-9A-F]{8})\(")
tail = re.compile(r"ps3_indirect_call\(ctx\); return;")
sites = []
for path in sorted(glob.glob((GT5_DIR + r"\generated\ppu_recomp_0*.cpp"))):
    cur = None
    prev = []
    for line in open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"):
        m = head.match(line)
        if m:
            cur = m.group(1)
        if tail.search(line) and "switch (" not in line:
            ctx = prev[-6:]
            if not any("ctx->gpr[2] = vm_read" in p for p in ctx):
                sites.append((cur, [p.strip()[:80] for p in ctx]))
        prev.append(line)
        prev = prev[-6:]
print(len(sites), "sites")
seen = {}
for fn, ctx in sites:
    seen.setdefault(fn, []).append(ctx)
for fn, lst in seen.items():
    print(f"func_{fn}: {len(lst)}")
    for l in lst[0][-4:]:
        print("    ", l)
```

`GT5/scripts/screendrive.py`:

```py
"""Follow gt5.exe's screen and press pad buttons when the expected menu is up.

    screendrive.py --dir <LD_FRAME_DUMP dir> --pad logs/pad.txt [--race] [--log file]
    screendrive.py --check <dir of old PNG frames>     shows which frames match each step
    screendrive.py --make-refs <analysis dir>          cuts scripts/refs/*.png from a good run

Each step waits for a crop of the screen to match its reference, presses, and moves on once
the screen has left that state. Run with LD_FRAME_DUMP_MS so frames keep coming in slow
scenes. Dumps are read and deleted, keeping a PNG per step and one every --keep seconds, so
a run leaves a record without filling the disk.
"""
import argparse
import glob
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import time

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
REFS = os.path.join(HERE, "refs")
CROSS, RIGHT = 0x4000, 0x0020
MASK = {"cross": 0x4000, "circle": 0x2000, "square": 0x8000, "triangle": 0x1000, "start": 0x0008, "select": 0x0001,
        "up": 0x0010, "right": 0x0020, "down": 0x0040, "left": 0x0080, "l2": 0x0100, "r2": 0x0200, "l1": 0x0400, "r1": 0x0800}
# name, source frame for the reference, crop in the 1280x720 picture, press, polls, largest difference
STEPS = [
    ("dialog", "frames_p1/frame_000097.png", (360, 184, 920, 544), CROSS, 16, 10),
    ("top_gt", "frames_p1/frame_000582.png", (280, 530, 420, 680), RIGHT, 16, 24),
    ("top_arc", "frames_p1/frame_000776.png", (280, 530, 560, 680), CROSS, 16, 24),
    ("arcade", "frames_p1/frame_001164.png", (360, 500, 920, 640), CROSS, 16, 5),
    ("level", "frames_p1/frame_001940.png", (360, 500, 920, 640), CROSS, 16, 5),
    ("track", "frames_p1/frame_002522.png", (0, 620, 1280, 720), CROSS, 16, 3),
    ("car", "frames_p1/frame_003104.png", (0, 620, 1280, 720), CROSS, 16, 3),
    ("color", "frames_ref/color.png", (480, 640, 900, 690), CROSS, 16, 6),
    # The AT/MT question. Only the two buttons: the car's reflection runs behind them, so a wider crop
    # (the old "car_ok", 500,500,780,610) matched only the usual car and stalled any other (a G27 run's Fiat).
    ("atmt", "frames_p1/frame_003201.png", (540, 565, 745, 603), CROSS, 16, 8),
    ("prerace", "frames_live2/frame_005141.png", (440, 600, 840, 690), CROSS, 16, 12),
]
REF_CACHE = {}


def thumb(img):
    return np.asarray(img.convert("L"), dtype=np.int16)[::2, ::2]


# The top menu's selected icon sits on an orange base; the 3D scene behind it changes, this doesn't.
ICON_BASE = {"top_gt": (320, 622, 376, 660), "top_arc": (434, 622, 490, 660)}


def orange(img, box):
    a = np.asarray(img.convert("RGB").crop(box), dtype=np.int16)
    hit = (a[..., 0] > 170) & (a[..., 1] > 80) & (a[..., 1] < 190) & (a[..., 2] < 90)
    return float(hit.mean())


def diff(img, step):
    if step[0] in ICON_BASE:
        # A difference score, so the callers treat it like the others: small when selected.
        # Only one icon is ever selected: an orange scene behind the menu lights up both.
        other = ICON_BASE["top_gt" if step[0] == "top_arc" else "top_arc"]
        return 0.0 if orange(img, ICON_BASE[step[0]]) > 0.07 and orange(img, other) < 0.02 else 30.0
    ref = REF_CACHE.get(step[0])
    if ref is None:
        ref = REF_CACHE[step[0]] = thumb(Image.open(os.path.join(REFS, step[0] + ".png")))
    return float(np.abs(thumb(img.crop(step[2])) - ref).mean())


def make_refs(analysis):
    os.makedirs(REFS, exist_ok=True)
    for s in STEPS:
        Image.open(os.path.join(analysis, s[1])).convert("L").crop(s[2]).save(os.path.join(REFS, s[0] + ".png"))
    print("refs written")


def read_ppm(path):
    d = open(path, "rb").read()
    fields, pos = [], 0
    while len(fields) < 4:
        while d[pos] in b" \t\r\n":
            pos += 1
        end = pos
        while d[end] not in b" \t\r\n":
            end += 1
        fields.append(d[pos:end])
        pos = end
    w, h = int(fields[1]), int(fields[2])
    if len(d) - pos - 1 < w * h * 3:
        raise ValueError("partial")
    return Image.frombuffer("RGB", (w, h), d[pos + 1:pos + 1 + w * h * 3], "raw", "RGB", 0, 1)


def newest(dirname):
    """The newest complete frame; older dumps are deleted."""
    fs = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(dirname, "frame_*.ppm")))
    for f in fs[:-1]:
        try:
            os.remove(f)
        except OSError:
            pass
    if not fs:
        return None
    try:
        return read_ppm(fs[-1])
    except (ValueError, OSError, IndexError):
        return None


def unsqueeze(img, widen, content_w=0):
    """A run wider than 16:9 (PS3_ASPECT, PS3_WINDOW_SIZE) has the game draw a wider picture with its
    menus as a 16:9 block in the middle. Cut that block out at 1280x720 so the references still match.
    content_w is how many pixels across the whole picture spans in the dump: the game draws 720 lines
    at the wide shape, a multiple of 8 across, at most 1920 (display_aspect.c); a wider shape than
    that is squeezed into the 1920 and the block with it, so it is stretched back here."""
    if widen <= 1.001:
        return img
    cw = content_w or min(8 * round(1280 * widen / 8), 1920)
    cx, half = cw / 2, cw / 2 / widen
    return img.crop((round(cx - half), 0, round(cx + half), 720)).resize((1280, 720), Image.BILINEAR)


TEST_EXE = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(HERE), "build", "gt5.exe")


def stop_test_game():
    """Stop only the test build (GT5\build\gt5.exe here); a gt5.exe from anywhere else is the player's own game."""
    ps = ("Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter \"Name='gt5.exe'\" | "
          "Where-Object { $_.ExecutablePath -and $_.ExecutablePath -ieq '%s' } | "
          "ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force }" % TEST_EXE)
    subprocess.run(["powershell", "-NoProfile", "-Command", ps], capture_output=True)


def press(pad, mask, polls):
    with open(pad, "w") as f:
        f.write("0x%04X %d" % (mask, polls))


def drive(a):
    log = open(a.log, "a", buffering=1) if a.log else sys.stdout
    t0 = time.time()

    def say(msg):
        log.write("%6.0f %s\n" % (time.time() - t0, msg))

    def profile(name):
        say("profile " + name)
        subprocess.Popen(["powershell", "-NoProfile", "-ExecutionPolicy", "Bypass", "-File", os.path.join(HERE, "prof.ps1"),
                          "-Seconds", "12", "-Out", "%s_%s.txt" % (a.prof, name)], stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL)

    def capture(name):
        # The runtime's RSX_DRAW_CSV_GATE / LD_SURF_DUMP_GATE act while this file exists.
        say("capture " + name)
        open(a.gate, "w").close()
        time.sleep(a.gate_secs)
        os.remove(a.gate)

    i, pressed_at, last_keep, armed, done_at = 0, 0.0, 0.0, False, 0.0
    captured = False
    race_at, profiled = 0.0, False
    tries = {}
    left_at = 0.0
    skipped = 0.0
    while time.time() - t0 < a.timeout:
        time.sleep(0.25)
        img = newest(a.dir)
        if img is None:
            continue
        now = time.time()
        if now - last_keep >= a.keep:
            last_keep = now
            img.save(os.path.join(a.dir, "frame_t%05d.png" % (now - t0)))
        cw = a.content_width
        if img.size == (1920, 1080):
            # 1080p mode (PS3_VIDEO_MODE=1080): the whole picture, at any shape, fills the 1920x1080.
            img = img.resize((1280, 720), Image.BILINEAR)
            cw = cw or 1280
        img = unsqueeze(img, a.widen, cw)
        # The opening movie's frames can look like a menu (an orange steel mill matches the selected
        # icon), so past the first dialog nothing is read until the movie has been skipped.
        if a.skip_movie and i > 0 and not skipped:
            # Counted from the dialog as well as from launch: a slow boot shows the dialog as late as 60 s, a press
            # before the movie has started is lost, and its orange frames then fool the icon test below.
            if now - t0 >= a.skip_movie and now - left_at >= 35:
                say("skip the movie, press 0x%04X" % CROSS)
                press(a.pad, CROSS, 16)
                skipped = now
                pressed_at = now
            continue
        if skipped and now - skipped < 12:  # the movie stays up while the player stops
            continue
        # A skip press that landed before the movie took input is lost, and the movie then plays for
        # minutes (its frames capture black). Still black 20 s after a press, with no step reached:
        # press again, up to three more times.
        if skipped and i == 1 and tries.get("reskip", 0) < 3 and now - pressed_at >= 20:
            if float(np.asarray(img.convert("L"), dtype=np.float32).mean()) < 2.0:
                tries["reskip"] = tries.get("reskip", 0) + 1
                say("still black after the skip, press 0x%04X again" % CROSS)
                press(a.pad, CROSS, 16)
                pressed_at = now
                continue
        if i < len(STEPS):
            s = STEPS[i]
            d = diff(img, s)
            if i + 1 < len(STEPS) and diff(img, STEPS[i + 1]) <= STEPS[i + 1][5]:
                say("at %s already, past %s" % (STEPS[i + 1][0], s[0]))
                i, armed, pressed_at = i + 1, False, 0.0
                continue
            # A press lost during a load: the screen came back to the previous step.
            if i and s[0] != "top_gt" and d > s[5] and diff(img, STEPS[i - 1]) <= STEPS[i - 1][5] and now - left_at >= 8:
                say("back at %s" % STEPS[i - 1][0])
                i, armed, pressed_at = i - 1, False, 0.0
                continue
            # The top menu ignores input while it animates in, and then idles into the attract demo.
            # Only while the cursor still sits on GT Mode, and never after Cross has gone in: a late Right
            # overwrites the Cross in the pad file or pushes the cursor past Arcade.
            if (s[0] == "top_arc" and not armed and d > s[5] and now - left_at >= 15 and tries.get("top_arc_right", 0) < 2
                    and diff(img, STEPS[i - 1]) <= STEPS[i - 1][5]):
                tries["top_arc_right"] = tries.get("top_arc_right", 0) + 1
                say("top_arc not reached, press right again")
                press(a.pad, RIGHT, 16)
                left_at = now
                continue
            if d <= s[5] and a.stop_at == s[0]:
                # --stop-at: arrived; press nothing more (the top menu then idles into its attract demo).
                if not tries.get("stopped"):
                    tries["stopped"] = 1
                    say("at %s, stopping here (--stop-at)" % s[0])
                    img.save(os.path.join(a.dir, "step_%02d_%s.png" % (i, s[0])))
                continue
            if d <= s[5]:
                # The top menu's icon bar fades about 10 s after the last press, so don't wait out the usual gap there.
                if now - pressed_at >= (3 if s[0] == "top_arc" else a.gap):
                    say("%s matched (%.1f), press 0x%04X" % (s[0], d, s[3]))
                    if s[0] == "color" and a.gate and a.capture in ("car", "both"):
                        capture("car")
                    if s[0] == "atmt" and a.prof:
                        profile("car")
                        time.sleep(14)
                    img.save(os.path.join(a.dir, "step_%02d_%s.png" % (i, s[0])))
                    tries[i] = tries.get(i, 0) + 1
                    if tries[i] in (5, 9) and a.prof:
                        # The game isn't taking this press: record what every thread is doing.
                        say("stuck at %s, recording stacks" % s[0])
                        with open(a.prof + "_stuck%d.txt" % tries[i], "w") as out:
                            subprocess.run([sys.executable, os.path.join(HERE, "gstack.py"), "--depth", "12"], stdout=out, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
                        profile("stuck%d" % tries[i])
                    if s[0] == "track" and a.track_keys and not tries.get("track_keys"):
                        # Another track: move the cursor first, keeping a frame after each press.
                        tries["track_keys"] = 1
                        for n, key in enumerate(a.track_keys.split(",")):
                            say("track key %s" % key)
                            if key != "wait":   # "wait": a pause, e.g. while the list first appears and ignores input
                                press(a.pad, MASK[key], 16)
                            time.sleep(a.key_gap)
                            shot = newest(a.dir)
                            if shot is not None:
                                shot.save(os.path.join(a.dir, "step_05_key%02d_%s.png" % (n, key)))
                        if a.explore:
                            say("explored the track list, stopping the game")
                            stop_test_game()
                            return
                    press(a.pad, s[3], s[4])
                    pressed_at, armed = now, True
                    if s[3] == RIGHT:  # stays on the same screen, with the cursor moved
                        i, armed = i + 1, False
                        left_at = now
            elif armed and d > s[5] + 4:
                say("%s left (%.1f)" % (s[0], d))
                left_at = now
                i, armed = i + 1, False
                pressed_at = 0.0
                if i == len(STEPS):
                    done_at = now
        elif a.race and now - done_at >= 30 and now - pressed_at >= 30:
            # Past the start flag: hold the accelerator, repeating so the hold survives loads.
            say("accelerate")
            press(a.pad, CROSS, 4000)
            pressed_at = now
            race_at = race_at or now
        if race_at and a.race_keys:
            # --race-keys: in the race, press a button (with the accelerator still held) at a set time,
            # e.g. to change the camera, then go back to holding the accelerator.
            for n, item in enumerate(a.race_keys.split(",")):
                secs, _, keys = item.partition(":")
                if tries.get("race_key%d" % n) or now - race_at < float(secs):
                    continue
                tries["race_key%d" % n] = 1
                mask = CROSS
                for key in keys.split("+"):
                    mask |= MASK[key]
                say("race key %s" % keys)
                press(a.pad, mask, 6)
                time.sleep(1.5)
                press(a.pad, CROSS, 4000)
                pressed_at = now
                time.sleep(2.0)
                shot = newest(a.dir)
                if shot is not None:
                    shot.save(os.path.join(a.dir, "race_key%02d_%s.png" % (n, keys)))
                break
        if race_at and a.gate and a.capture in ("race", "both") and not captured and now - race_at >= a.capture_at:
            capture("race")
            captured = True
        if race_at and a.prof and not profiled and now - race_at >= 30:
            profile("race")
            profiled = True
        if race_at and a.end_after and now - race_at >= a.end_after:
            say("done, stopping the game")
            stop_test_game()
            return


def check(dirname):
    print("             " + " ".join(s[0][:5].rjust(5) for s in STEPS))
    for f in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(dirname, "frame_*.png"))):
        img = Image.open(f).convert("RGB")
        ds = [diff(img, s) for s in STEPS]
        best = int(np.argmin(ds))
        mark = STEPS[best][0] if ds[best] <= STEPS[best][5] else "-"
        print(os.path.basename(f)[6:-4], mark.ljust(8)[:8], " ".join("%5.1f" % x for x in ds))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument("--dir")
    p.add_argument("--pad")
    p.add_argument("--log")
    p.add_argument("--race", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--check")
    p.add_argument("--make-refs")
    p.add_argument("--keep", type=float, default=10.0)
    p.add_argument("--gap", type=float, default=12.0, help="seconds between presses of one step")
    p.add_argument("--timeout", type=float, default=900.0)
    p.add_argument("--prof", help="prefix for prof.ps1 samples of car select and the race")
    p.add_argument("--gate", help="file to create while capturing")
    p.add_argument("--gate-secs", type=float, default=6.0)
    p.add_argument("--skip-movie", type=float, default=0, help="press Cross at this many seconds to skip the opening movie; menus are not read before it")
    p.add_argument("--capture", default="", help="car, race or both")
    p.add_argument("--end-after", type=float, default=0, help="stop the game this long after the race starts")
    p.add_argument("--race-keys", default="", help="in the race, <seconds>:<button>[+<button>] presses with the"
                   " accelerator held, e.g. 15:select to change the camera; a frame is kept after each")
    p.add_argument("--capture-at", type=float, default=20, help="seconds into the race for --capture race")
    p.add_argument("--track-keys", default="", help="buttons pressed on the track list before Cross, e.g. up,right,down;"
                   " wait pauses. The first press only wakes the cursor. Tsukuba: wait,wait,up,wait,select,right,cross,wait,wait,select,right,right,right,right")
    p.add_argument("--key-gap", type=float, default=2.5, help="seconds after each --track-keys press")
    p.add_argument("--explore", action="store_true", help="stop the game after the --track-keys presses")
    p.add_argument("--stop-at", default="", help="a step name (e.g. top_gt) to stop pressing at; top_gt then shows the attract demo")
    p.add_argument("--content-width", type=float, default=0, help="pixels across the whole wide picture in a dump, see unsqueeze")
    p.add_argument("--widen", type=float, default=1.0, help="the run's picture shape over 16:9 (2560x1080: 1.333), see unsqueeze")
    a = p.parse_args()
    if a.make_refs:
        make_refs(a.make_refs)
    elif a.check:
        check(a.check)
    else:
        drive(a)
```

`GT5/scripts/setjmp_patch.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Make guest setjmp/longjmp transfer control instead of returning.

Adapted from the GT5 Prologue port (sp00nznet/GT5P). ppu_lifter emits longjmp's
final `blr` as `return;`, so the lifted longjmp restores the guest register file
and then returns to its own caller rather than to the setjmp site.

Two edits, both in generated/:

  * every call site of the guest setjmp gets a real host setjmp wrapped around
    it, so the landing point is a live frame on the host stack;
  * the guest longjmp keeps its original body -- which is what restores the
    guest registers -- and then fires the host longjmp.

Run after every re-lift; generated/ is rebuilt wholesale.

GT5 addresses, found by scripts/find_setjmp.py and show_jmp.py: both routines
open with addi r3,r3,15; setjmp has 2 bl callers, longjmp has 3.

    python scripts/setjmp_patch.py
"""
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

GEN = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "generated"

# This copy's routines, as scripts/version_addrs.py found them (relift.ps1 runs it first);
# Europe 01.00's when it has not run.
SETJMP, LONGJMP = "00D00D74", "00D00E98"
_ver = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "analysis" / "version.json"
if _ver.exists():
    import json as _json
    _v = _json.loads(_ver.read_text())
    if _v.get("setjmp") and _v.get("longjmp"):
        SETJMP, LONGJMP = _v["setjmp"], _v["longjmp"]

DECLS = """
/* ---- setjmp_patch.py ------------------------------------------------- */
#include <setjmp.h>
#include <stdint.h>
struct gt5_jmp;
extern "C" gt5_jmp* gt5_jmp_push(uint32_t buf_ea);
extern "C" jmp_buf* gt5_jmp_host(gt5_jmp* e);
extern "C" int      gt5_jmp_depth(void);
extern "C" void     gt5_jmp_unwind(int depth);
extern "C" void     gt5_jmp_fire(uint32_t buf_ea, int value);
"""

LONGJMP_WRAPPER = """
/* ---- setjmp_patch.py: guest longjmp ---------------------------------- */
void func_%(lj)s(ppu_context* ctx)
{
    /* Capture the arguments before the original body overwrites the register
     * file with the saved state. */
    uint32_t buf = (uint32_t)ctx->gpr[3];
    int      val = (int)(int32_t)ctx->gpr[4];

    /* The original restores r1, r2, r13-r31, LR, CR and the FPRs from the
     * guest buffer -- exactly the state the guest expects to resume with. */
    gt5_orig_func_%(lj)s(ctx);
    DRAIN_TRAMPOLINE(ctx);

    /* Then actually go there. Returns only if nothing is armed, in which case
     * this degrades to the old (wrong, but no worse) behaviour. */
    gt5_jmp_fire(buf, val);
}
"""

# The lifted call site looks like:
#     ctx->lr = 0x00BC8A0C; func_00D00D74(ctx); DRAIN_TRAMPOLINE(ctx);
# In the game updates (2.xx) the code needs more than one TOC, so the callers reach setjmp through a
# linker stub that saves r2, switches it and branches on (std r2,40(r1); addis; addi; b setjmp):
#     ctx->lr = 0x00CB11DC; func_00E43010(ctx); DRAIN_TRAMPOLINE(ctx);
# A call to such a stub is a setjmp call too: the stub makes no frame, so setjmp still saves the
# caller's r1 and return address.
SETJMP_CALLEES = ["func_" + SETJMP]
STUB_RE = re.compile(
    r"^void (func_[0-9A-F]{8})\(ppu_context\* ctx\) \{\n"
    r"(?:[^\n]*\n){0,6}?"
    r"[^\n]*\{ g_trampoline_fn = \(void\(\*\)\(void\*\)\)func_" + SETJMP + r"; return; \}\n\}", re.M)


def call_re():
    return re.compile(r"( *)ctx->lr = (0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+); (" + "|".join(SETJMP_CALLEES) +
                      r")\(ctx\); DRAIN_TRAMPOLINE\(ctx\);")


def find_stubs(chunks):
    """TOC stubs in front of setjmp: tiny functions saving r2 and tail-branching to it."""
    stubs = []
    for chunk in chunks:
        text = chunk.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        for m in STUB_RE.finditer(text):
            if "vm_write64(ctx->gpr[1] + 0x28, ctx->gpr[2]);" in m.group(0):
                stubs.append(m.group(1))
    return stubs


def patch_call_sites(text):
    """Put a host setjmp in the frame that calls the guest setjmp.

    setjmp has to appear lexically in the frame that will be jumped back into,
    so this cannot live behind a helper -- it is expanded at each site.
    """
    def repl(m):
        ind, lr, callee = m.group(1), m.group(2), m.group(3)
        return (
            f"{ind}{{ gt5_jmp* _j = gt5_jmp_push((uint32_t)ctx->gpr[3]);\n"
            f"{ind}  if (setjmp(*gt5_jmp_host(_j)) == 0) {{\n"
            f"{ind}      ctx->lr = {lr}; {callee}(ctx); DRAIN_TRAMPOLINE(ctx);\n"
            f"{ind}  }} }}")
    return call_re().subn(repl, text)


def guard_callers(text, names):
    """Restore the buffer stack depth when a setjmp-calling function returns.

    Without this a buffer stays armed after its frame is gone, and a later
    longjmp would jump into a dead frame.
    """
    n = 0
    for name in names:
        define = f"void {name}(ppu_context* ctx) {{"
        if define not in text or f"gt5_orig_{name}" in text:
            continue
        text = text.replace(define, f"void gt5_orig_{name}(ppu_context* ctx) {{", 1)
        text += (
            f"\n/* ---- setjmp_patch.py: {name} arms a setjmp buffer ---- */\n"
            f"void {name}(ppu_context* ctx)\n{{\n"
            f"    int _d = gt5_jmp_depth();\n"
            f"    gt5_orig_{name}(ctx);\n"
            f"    gt5_jmp_unwind(_d);\n"
            f"}}\n")
        n += 1
    return text, n


def main():
    total_sites, total_guards, did_longjmp = 0, 0, False
    chunks = sorted(GEN.glob("ppu_recomp_*.cpp"))
    stubs = find_stubs(chunks)
    if stubs:
        print(f"  setjmp is also reached through TOC stubs: {', '.join(stubs)}")
        SETJMP_CALLEES.extend(stubs)
    for chunk in chunks:
        text = chunk.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        original = text

        if "setjmp_patch.py" not in text:
            # find which functions contain a setjmp call before rewriting them
            owners = []
            calls = [f"{c}(ctx);" for c in SETJMP_CALLEES]
            if any(c in text for c in calls):
                for m in re.finditer(r"^void (func_[0-9A-F]{8})\(ppu_context\* ctx\) \{", text, re.M):
                    end = text.find("\nvoid ", m.end())
                    body = text[m.start():end if end > 0 else len(text)]
                    if m.group(1) not in SETJMP_CALLEES and any(c in body for c in calls):
                        owners.append(m.group(1))

            text, sites = patch_call_sites(text)
            total_sites += sites
            if sites:
                print(f"  {chunk.name}: setjmp sites {sites}, owners {owners}")
                text = DECLS + text
                text, guards = guard_callers(text, owners)
                total_guards += guards

            define = f"void func_{LONGJMP}(ppu_context* ctx) {{"
            if define in text:
                text = text.replace(define, f"void gt5_orig_func_{LONGJMP}(ppu_context* ctx) {{", 1)
                if DECLS not in text:
                    text = DECLS + text
                text += LONGJMP_WRAPPER % {"lj": LONGJMP}
                did_longjmp = True

        if text != original:
            chunk.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
            print(f"  patched {chunk.name}")

    print(f"setjmp call sites wrapped: {total_sites}")
    print(f"arming functions guarded:  {total_guards}")
    print(f"longjmp rewritten:         {did_longjmp}")
    return 0 if (total_sites and did_longjmp) else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

`GT5/scripts/shaderdiff.py`:

```py
import os as _gt5_os  # this clone's folders, wherever it was cloned to
GT5_DIR = _gt5_os.path.dirname(_gt5_os.path.dirname(_gt5_os.path.abspath(__file__)))
BASE_DIR = _gt5_os.path.dirname(GT5_DIR)
"""Why does a shader miss the disk cache? shaderdiff.py <minutes> [count]

Takes files written in the last <minutes>, finds the older file whose HLSL is closest, and prints the lines that
differ. If the same text comes back with small changes, something run-specific has got into the text.
"""
import difflib
import os
import struct
import sys
import time

D = (GT5_DIR + r"\scratch\rsx_shader_cache_v2")
minutes = float(sys.argv[1])
count = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 4
now = time.time()
HEADER = 32


def source(path):
    d = open(path, "rb").read()
    # header: magic, version, stage, source_length, blob_length, pad, hash
    fields = struct.unpack_from("<5I", d)
    for off in (24, 32, 40):
        n = fields[3]
        text = d[off:off + n]
        if text[:64].isascii() and b"\0" not in text[:64]:
            return text.decode("latin1")
    return ""


new, old = [], []
for e in os.scandir(D):
    if not e.name.endswith(".bin"):
        continue
    (new if now - e.stat().st_mtime < minutes * 60 else old).append(e)
print("new", len(new), "old", len(old))
olds = {}
for e in old:
    if e.name[0] == "P":
        olds[e.name] = source(e.path)
shown = 0
exact = 0
for e in sorted(new, key=lambda x: x.name):
    if e.name[0] != "P":
        continue
    s = source(e.path)
    same = [n for n, t in olds.items() if t == s]
    if same:
        exact += 1
        continue
    lines = s.splitlines()
    best, best_r = None, 0
    cands = sorted(olds.items(), key=lambda kv: abs(len(kv[1]) - len(s)))[:150]
    for n, t in cands:
        r = difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, lines, t.splitlines(), autojunk=False).quick_ratio()
        if r > best_r:
            best, best_r = n, r
    if shown < count and best:
        print("==", e.name, "closest", best, "ratio %.3f" % best_r, "lengths", len(s), len(olds[best]))
        for l in list(difflib.unified_diff(olds[best].splitlines(), lines, lineterm="", n=0))[:14]:
            print("  ", l[:150])
        shown += 1
print("identical text under another name:", exact)

```

`GT5/scripts/shaderkeys.py`:

```py
"""The made-ahead lists by program (rsx_shader_prep.inc): look at them, merge players' lists, make the one
that ships with the port.

A record names one pipeline by its two programs' keys (hashes of their own bytes) and every input of
their translation; it holds no game code or data. A player's game writes them to
GT5\\scratch\\shader_keys\\shader_keys.lst; the launcher's "Save logs for a report" writes the same records
as base64 text (gt5-shader-keys.txt), which this reads too.

  shaderkeys.py stats <list>...                    what is in them, by release and settings kind
  shaderkeys.py releases <list>...                 the releases in them (disc id + EBOOT size)
  shaderkeys.py merge -o <out.lst> <list>...       one list, each record once (first copy kept)
  shaderkeys.py ship [-o <out.lst>] <list>...      the shipped list (default share_docs/GT5/shaders/known_d3d12.lst):
                                                   merged, damaged and old ones dropped, sorted so a new version
                                                   of the list diffs small
  shaderkeys.py text -o <out.txt> <list>           as the launcher saves it (base64, a record a line)

merge / ship take --release ID[:EBOOTSIZE] (repeatable; records of no known release, from version-1 lists,
go with any release unless --strict) and --min-version N (default: the current record version, so a list
made before a change of the translation's inputs is left out; --min-version 1 keeps old records, which are
converted).

Versions. A record's version is the version of its set of translation inputs (LD_PREP_VERSION in
rsx_shader_prep.inc), not of the generator: the HLSL may change freely and records stay good, because the
game translates them again and uses the result only when a draw makes the same text. When the sibling work
on the cache key adds an input to the translation, LD_PREP_VERSION goes up; records of the old version are
either converted (when the new input has a value meaning "as before"; add the conversion here and in
ld_prep_add_list) or dropped (ship's --min-version). The game reads version-1 records (round 1's test
lists) as "made under any settings".

The game reads the shipped list from GT5\\shaders\\known_d3d12.lst and uses records of any release (their
programs are matched by content, so another release's records cost nothing when their programs never
come). Records made under other settings are skipped by kind (Shadows; render scale / upscaler; motion
vectors; the upscaler's resolve), only for records whose text depends on that kind; `stats` shows the mix.
"""
import argparse
import base64
import collections
import os
import struct
import sys

REC = 512
REC_V1 = 496
MAGIC = 0x31504B53        # "SKP1"
VERSION = 2
CHECK_AT = 504
FNV_OFF = 1469598103934665603
FNV_PRIME = 1099511628211
MASK64 = (1 << 64) - 1
KINDS = ("Shadows", "render scale / upscaler", "motion vectors", "upscaler resolve", "render scale (pipeline only)")
FLAGS = {1: "masked layout", 2: "packed", 4: "motion vectors", 8: "one-tap resolve", 16: "WPOS grid", 32: "WPOS scale",
         64: "branch bits"}


def fnv1a(data, h=FNV_OFF):
    for b in data:
        h = ((h ^ b) * FNV_PRIME) & MASK64
    return h


def from_v1(b):
    """A version-1 record (496 bytes) as version 2: any settings, no release (as the game reads it)."""
    magic, ver, size = struct.unpack_from("<III", b, 0)
    if magic != MAGIC or ver != 1 or size != REC_V1 or struct.unpack_from("<Q", b, 488)[0] != fnv1a(b[:488]):
        return None
    r = bytearray(REC)
    r[:488] = b[:488]
    struct.pack_into("<II", r, 4, VERSION, REC)
    flags, = struct.unpack_from("<I", r, 12)
    struct.pack_into("<I", r, 12, flags & 0xFF)
    struct.pack_into("<I", r, 92, 0)          # cfg: any
    struct.pack_into("<Q", r, CHECK_AT, fnv1a(bytes(r[:CHECK_AT])))
    return bytes(r)


def valid(b):
    magic, ver, size = struct.unpack_from("<III", b, 0)
    if magic != MAGIC or ver != VERSION or size != REC:
        return False
    return struct.unpack_from("<Q", b, CHECK_AT)[0] == fnv1a(b[:CHECK_AT])


def read_records(path):
    """Records (version 2, converted from version 1 when need be) from a binary list or the launcher's
    base64 text; (records, damaged, version-1 count)."""
    raw = open(path, "rb").read()
    blobs = []
    text_like = raw[:1] != b"S" and all(32 <= c < 127 or c in (9, 10, 13) for c in raw[:4096])
    if text_like:
        for line in raw.decode("ascii", "replace").splitlines():
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            try:
                blobs.append(base64.b64decode(line, validate=True))
            except Exception:
                blobs.append(None)
    else:
        size = REC
        if len(raw) >= 12:
            ver, sz = struct.unpack_from("<II", raw, 4)
            if ver == 1 and sz == REC_V1:
                size = REC_V1
        for i in range(len(raw) // size):
            blobs.append(raw[i * size:(i + 1) * size])
    good, bad, v1 = [], 0, 0
    for b in blobs:
        if b is not None and len(b) == REC_V1:
            b = from_v1(b)
            if b is not None:
                v1 += 1
                good.append((b, 1))
                continue
        if b is None or len(b) != REC or not valid(b):
            bad += 1
        else:
            good.append((b, VERSION))
    return good, bad, v1


def rec_id(b):
    return fnv1a(b[:CHECK_AT]) or 1


def fields(b):
    flags, = struct.unpack_from("<I", b, 12)
    vp_key, fp_key = struct.unpack_from("<QQ", b, 16)
    vp_instrs, vp_start, fp_size = struct.unpack_from("<III", b, 32)
    cfg, = struct.unpack_from("<I", b, 92)
    fp_head, vp_head = struct.unpack_from("<II", b, 104)
    title = b[488:500].split(b"\0", 1)[0].decode("ascii", "replace")
    eboot, = struct.unpack_from("<I", b, 500)
    return dict(flags=flags, vp_key=vp_key, fp_key=fp_key, fp_size=fp_size, cfg=cfg, deps=(flags >> 8) & 0x1F,
                fp_head=fp_head, vp_head=vp_head, title=title, eboot=eboot)


def release_of(b):
    f = fields(b)
    return (f["title"], f["eboot"])


def release_name(rel):
    t, e = rel
    return "%s:%d" % (t, e) if t or e else "(none: version-1 list)"


def parse_releases(args):
    out = []
    for a in args or []:
        t, _, e = a.partition(":")
        out.append((t, int(e) if e else None))
    return out


def merge(paths, releases=None, strict=False, min_version=VERSION):
    out, seen, bad, old, other = [], set(), 0, 0, 0
    per_file = []
    for p in paths:
        recs, b, v1 = read_records(p)
        bad += b
        added = 0
        for r, ver in recs:
            if ver < min_version:
                old += 1
                continue
            if releases:
                t, e = release_of(r)
                if not t and not e:
                    if strict:
                        other += 1
                        continue
                elif not any(t == rt and (re is None or e == re) for rt, re in releases):
                    other += 1
                    continue
            i = rec_id(r)
            if i in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(i)
            out.append(r)
            added += 1
        per_file.append((p, len(recs), added, b, v1))
    return out, dict(damaged=bad, old=old, other_release=other), per_file


def cmd_stats(a):
    recs, drop, per = merge(a.lists, min_version=1)
    for p, n, added, b, v1 in per:
        print("%s: %d records (%d new to the merge, %d of version 1), %d damaged" % (p, n, added, v1, b))
    if not recs:
        print("no records")
        return
    f = [fields(r) for r in recs]
    vps = set(x["vp_key"] for x in f)
    fps = set(x["fp_key"] for x in f)
    pairs = collections.Counter((x["vp_key"], x["fp_key"]) for x in f)
    print("%d pipelines, %d vertex programs, %d fragment programs, %d program pairs (pipelines per pair: max %d, mean %.2f)" % (
        len(recs), len(vps), len(fps), len(pairs), max(pairs.values()), len(recs) / len(pairs)))
    rel = collections.Counter(release_of(r) for r in recs)
    print("releases: " + ", ".join("%s %d" % (release_name(k), v) for k, v in rel.most_common()))
    print("text depends on no setting: %d" % sum(1 for x in f if not x["deps"]))
    for k, name in enumerate(KINDS):
        dep = [x for x in f if x["deps"] & (1 << k)]
        if not dep:
            continue
        byte = k if k < 4 else 1   # the pipeline-only scale kind uses the scale byte
        vals = collections.Counter((x["cfg"] >> (8 * byte)) & 0xFF for x in dep)
        print("  depends on %s: %d (settings values: %s)" % (
            name, len(dep), ", ".join("%s %d" % ("any" if v == 0 else "%02X" % v, n) for v, n in vals.most_common())))
    fl = collections.Counter()
    for x in f:
        for bit, n in FLAGS.items():
            if x["flags"] & bit:
                fl[n] += 1
    print("  " + ", ".join("%s %d" % kv for kv in fl.most_common()))
    print("size %.1f MB (%d bytes a record)" % (len(recs) * REC / 1e6, REC))


def cmd_releases(a):
    recs, drop, per = merge(a.lists, min_version=1)
    rel = collections.Counter(release_of(r) for r in recs)
    for k, v in rel.most_common():
        print("%-28s %d" % (release_name(k), v))


def write_list(path, recs):
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path)), exist_ok=True)
    tmp = path + ".tmp"
    with open(tmp, "wb") as o:
        for r in recs:
            o.write(r)
    os.replace(tmp, path)


def drop_words(d):
    return "%d damaged, %d of an older version, %d of other releases left out" % (d["damaged"], d["old"], d["other_release"])


def cmd_merge(a):
    recs, d, per = merge(a.lists, parse_releases(a.release), a.strict, a.min_version)
    write_list(a.out, recs)
    print("%s: %d records from %d lists (%s)" % (a.out, len(recs), len(a.lists), drop_words(d)))


def cmd_ship(a):
    recs, d, per = merge(a.lists, parse_releases(a.release), a.strict, a.min_version)
    recs.sort(key=lambda r: (struct.unpack_from("<Q", r, 24)[0], struct.unpack_from("<Q", r, 16)[0], rec_id(r)))
    out = a.out or os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "..", "..", "share_docs", "GT5", "shaders", "known_d3d12.lst")
    write_list(out, recs)
    print("%s: %d records, %.1f MB (%s)" % (os.path.normpath(out), len(recs), len(recs) * REC / 1e6, drop_words(d)))


def cmd_text(a):
    recs, d, per = merge(a.lists, min_version=1)
    with open(a.out, "w", newline="\n") as o:
        for r in recs:
            o.write(base64.b64encode(r).decode("ascii") + "\n")
    print("%s: %d records" % (a.out, len(recs)))


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    sp = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    s = sp.add_parser("stats"); s.add_argument("lists", nargs="+"); s.set_defaults(fn=cmd_stats)
    s = sp.add_parser("releases"); s.add_argument("lists", nargs="+"); s.set_defaults(fn=cmd_releases)
    for name, fn, need_out in (("merge", cmd_merge, True), ("ship", cmd_ship, False)):
        s = sp.add_parser(name)
        s.add_argument("-o", "--out", required=need_out)
        s.add_argument("--release", action="append", help="ID[:EBOOTSIZE], e.g. BCES00569:26029448 (repeatable)")
        s.add_argument("--strict", action="store_true", help="with --release: leave out records of no known release")
        s.add_argument("--min-version", type=int, default=VERSION)
        s.add_argument("lists", nargs="+")
        s.set_defaults(fn=fn)
    s = sp.add_parser("text"); s.add_argument("-o", "--out", required=True); s.add_argument("lists", nargs="+"); s.set_defaults(fn=cmd_text)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    a.fn(a)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

`GT5/scripts/shadowinfo.py`:

```py
"""What draws into the shadow map in a capture: shadowinfo.py <csv> [frame]"""
import collections
import csv
import sys

rows = [r for r in csv.DictReader(open(sys.argv[1])) if r.get("frame") and r["frame"].isdigit()]
frames = collections.Counter(r["frame"] for r in rows)
want = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else max(frames, key=lambda k: frames[k])
c = collections.Counter()
for r in rows:
    if r["frame"] != want or not r.get("zeta_off"):
        continue
    try:
        if int(r["zeta_off"], 16) != 0x5380000:
            continue
    except ValueError:
        continue
    c[(r["surf"], r["vpx"], r["vpy"], r["vpw"], r["vph"], r["clipw"], r["cliph"], r["zeta_pitch"], r["dwrite"], r["dfunc"], r["cmask"])] += int(r["verts"])
print("frame", want)
for k, v in sorted(c.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1])[:12]:
    print(v, k)
```

```py
"""Contact sheet of frame dumps: sheet.py <dir> <out.png> [--every N] [--from K] [--max M] [--cols C]"""
import glob, os, sys
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
def arg(n, d): return int(sys.argv[sys.argv.index(n) + 1]) if n in sys.argv else d
fs = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(sys.argv[1], "frame_*.png")))
fs = fs[arg("--from", 0)::arg("--every", 1)][:arg("--max", 40)]
cols = arg("--cols", 6)
W, H = 320, 180
rows = (len(fs) + cols - 1) // cols
sheet = Image.new("RGB", (cols * W, rows * (H + 14)), "black")
d = ImageDraw.Draw(sheet)
for i, f in enumerate(fs):
    im = Image.open(f).convert("RGB").crop((0, 0, 1280, 720)).resize((W, H))
    x, y = (i % cols) * W, (i // cols) * (H + 14)
    sheet.paste(im, (x, y + 14))
    d.text((x + 2, y + 1), os.path.basename(f)[6:-4], fill="yellow")
sheet.save(sys.argv[2])
print(len(fs), "frames")
```

`GT5/scripts/show_jmp.py`:

```py
"""Dump the setjmp/longjmp region and every bl into the entry points it finds."""
import struct
import sys

d = open(sys.argv[1], "rb").read()
lo, hi = int(sys.argv[2], 0), int(sys.argv[3], 0)
code_end = 0x111c684
BASE = 0x10000
n = (code_end - BASE) // 4
words = struct.unpack(f">{n}I", d[:n * 4])

ENTRY_MARK = 0x3863000F  # addi r3,r3,15 -- both routines align the buffer first
BLR = 0x4E800020
entries = []
for a in range(lo, hi, 4):
    w = words[(a - BASE) // 4]
    tag = ""
    if w == ENTRY_MARK:
        tag = "  <-- addi r3,r3,15 (entry)"
        entries.append(a)
    if w == BLR:
        tag = "  <-- blr"
    print(f"{a:08X}: {w:08X}{tag}")


def callers(target):
    out = []
    for i, w in enumerate(words):
        if w >> 26 == 18 and w & 3 == 1:
            li = w & 0x03FFFFFC
            if li & 0x02000000:
                li -= 0x04000000
            if BASE + i * 4 + li == target:
                out.append(BASE + i * 4)
    return out


for e in entries:
    cs = callers(e)
    print(f"entry 0x{e:08X}: {len(cs)} bl callers: " + " ".join(f"0x{c:08X}" for c in cs[:20]))
```

```py
import os as _gt5_os  # this clone's folders, wherever it was cloned to
GT5_DIR = _gt5_os.path.dirname(_gt5_os.path.dirname(_gt5_os.path.abspath(__file__)))
BASE_DIR = _gt5_os.path.dirname(GT5_DIR)
"""Print lifted functions by address, without the noise: showfn.py 00010230 000105A8 [--max N]"""
import glob
import re
import sys

args = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if not a.startswith("--")]
maxl = 120
if "--max" in sys.argv:
    maxl = int(sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--max") + 1])
    args.remove(str(maxl))
want = {a.upper().rjust(8, "0") for a in args}
head = re.compile(r"^void func_([0-9A-F]{8})\(ppu_context\* ctx\) \{")
cr = re.compile(r"\{ int64_t a = \(.*?\)ctx->gpr\[(\d+)\]; int64_t b = (.*?); uint32_t cr_val.*?\(0xFu << (\d+)\)\).*")
for path in sorted(glob.glob((GT5_DIR + r"\generated\ppu_recomp_0*.cpp"))):
    on = False
    n = 0
    for line in open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"):
        m = head.match(line)
        if m:
            on = m.group(1) in want
            n = 0
            if on:
                print(f"--- {path[-18:]} func_{m.group(1)}")
        if on:
            n += 1
            if n <= maxl:
                s = line.rstrip()[4:]
                s = cr.sub(lambda c: f"cmp r{c.group(1)}, {c.group(2)} -> cr<<{c.group(3)}", s)
                s = s.replace("ctx->gpr[", "r[").replace("DRAIN_TRAMPOLINE(ctx);", "").replace("(ctx);", "()")
                print(s[:170])
            if line.startswith("}"):
                on = False
```

`GT5/scripts/spu_jobs_from_eboot.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Find GT5's SPU job images in this copy's EBOOT, for lift_spu_jobs.py to compile.

GT5 hands most of its SPU work (physics, sound, graphics set-up) to SPURS as raw job images
stored inside EBOOT.elf. Each one is found here by its hashes (no game data is stored in this
script) and written to analysis/spu_miss under the name the runtime would have dumped it with,
the fingerprint the runtime registers it by. lift_spu_jobs.py then lifts them to C, and the build
compiles them in. A job that isn't compiled in can't run: the runtime drops it, and whatever
waits on it stalls (a black screen after the logos, for one in the game updates).

The list is the European release (BCES00569, disc 01.00), which the other discs share, plus the
versions the game updates (2.xx) changed. A copy needs one version of each job; the summary says
how many it has.

    python scripts/spu_jobs_from_eboot.py [input/EBOOT.elf]
"""
import hashlib
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
OUT = ROOT / "analysis" / "spu_miss"
PREFIX = 64   # bytes hashed at each candidate offset
STEP = 16     # SPU images are at least quadword aligned

# (runtime fingerprint, size, SHA-1 of the first PREFIX bytes, SHA-1 of the whole image)
JOBS = [
    ("1B6BDAC375C5438D", 13840, "1dcbe5569e3ff030af74a4ee4a6bc68dc34b5916", "6428d06556207eb480f5f6f53d2b4637bc47a959"),
    ("48AF2BC79A72CB50", 25232, "d059dbdc8f7bc5bb07edd875d17cd28d34d172a4", "a33efe337060b6984fbe0d5c4b8ffcd83be6ae4f"),
    ("49C1D6C47E80AF43", 24720, "a5ca7ca714dfd3d42f6d2791c52e0aabe91d9fe5", "bab6bc8bd1c240db96c648e01ab549958fb5998e"),
    ("5DA195169669A5FF", 72464, "912583737f277c4b255face079ae6ce444b5d295", "724e11c2b86807bc4e7858f39a86dc010271c2f5"),
    ("650EE1A07AEBB151", 22032, "9a05ed1196c433d422230bbe2c81492c5d014ce8", "600792fb187ca897f81879dea87b6fbec6aa8163"),
    ("75BFE68AE96D7577", 12032, "3e6a0b4551e424a7315f2dca03bb8a202ff47486", "3cad156b9d0d985e4788140db9728da0bf8cd734"),
    ("80435D36E623FAA0", 19488, "7928e1212b01f0881edfa032020cca4068960679", "8c77e02b4b9bbb84e492f37ac2c332ab1985d485"),
    ("82D0BE145EC28AEE", 17424, "49b0dff67aa20024f04415f899cb6c82b3ad8dc1", "2e1a55c099adba1ce3f2ac1bb8dd7e815bec546b"),
    ("9804ABA84566F431", 20624, "7b875f4adf8082ec22cc4cf0ed3b4a23430da201", "ec458520f805b66025656eda6431d0fdff7bc144"),
    ("ABD49FC58F53F368", 9488, "8ebad749fab419a62a8db9bd90d817e3a4a758b4", "1ba431ca767a4016eab4c06218a0bcca0e60bf30"),
    ("D58063CD2A0236B5", 53408, "078fd4721b87c3870605f474cbab013c6ae0154e", "e934703d61aca2e7f025503e3326dd8d57c21f01"),
    ("EB79FDFCD7112702", 22288, "7276512751ce9dfae150210e4029aa03592499de", "38b144965d2b3a89bc29cc8a6e1970ea26424120"),
    ("F523F26F69764538", 64912, "f767a6c12afd282eb9a9997df10760a79138ba7e", "eb871a28c52e2f5d430fc93145ca3e51291e2fae"),
    ("FDFFAAC1BCD5352E", 34704, "6282b2e494736583faf042793e20804657c901b0", "61d01493b972923284dad53ece6c80516b0af794"),
    ("FE031AF67ED048DE", 46928, "6872f373fae3b3578750a555b2dbf54d3ad2a5da", "65c1baa23a23c6a15eed04ae15137270fcc4d86c"),
]

# Versions changed by game updates: (fingerprint, size, prefix SHA-1, whole SHA-1, the job above it replaces).
UPDATED = [
    ("C2A031BC164B4A45", 21952, "c7f26544a13fbe51db2e9f71e56d8c08ea06f0e3", "7ea77243d007ad477175d54ceae94d25297741dc", "650EE1A07AEBB151"),  # 2.01
    ("E3FDDA10963A6130", 22544, "2a759a61e4fa122c5344b18265352c9ac4836e40", "fe409a4e6c7f4e72c21021aaadd47cd0d7a0eefb", "EB79FDFCD7112702"),  # 2.01
    ("CB9BD0241BB0DE67", 53280, "a3a0364d94ae6bc5a96fc5fd54b803ac72850c11", "7276beb17d4929a04954b77c87f24f07534be190", "D58063CD2A0236B5"),  # 2.17 (US)
    # New in 2.17, no 01.00 counterpart (the second job table, with the two below it).
    ("0B07CA3DA8C030C2", 29920, "73d23dc69f344dfc689b779d8217e0bc9f55db21", "d7bc0a42a7418b6f40478a794d40968473901382", None),  # 2.17 (US)
    ("18DE371921B1A751", 13200, "a4e9776a48878b1eab752497422034a251f27860", "3c24724fb099b4cefc0878905982adf1f8aa3f0b", None),  # 2.17 (US)
    ("CF6352633FE351E3", 24000, "2ecaeef90de6ee0e0ecba183e65005f3e0c44dd9", "26b9d37ca05af1e4cc50fe4d325e2ecccce445be", None),  # 2.17 (US)
]


def main():
    eboot = Path(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else ROOT / "input" / "EBOOT.elf"
    data = eboot.read_bytes()
    by_prefix = {}
    for job in JOBS + UPDATED:
        by_prefix.setdefault(job[2], []).append(job[:4])
    found = {}
    sha1 = hashlib.sha1
    for off in range(0, len(data) - PREFIX, STEP):
        cands = by_prefix.get(sha1(data[off:off + PREFIX]).hexdigest())
        if not cands:
            continue
        for fp, size, _, full in cands:
            if fp not in found and sha1(data[off:off + size]).hexdigest() == full:
                found[fp] = (off, data[off:off + size])
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for fp, (off, blob) in sorted(found.items()):
        (OUT / f"spujob_{fp}_{len(blob)}.bin").write_bytes(blob)
    have = set(found) | {old for fp, *_, old in UPDATED if fp in found}
    missing = [fp for fp, *_ in JOBS if fp not in have]
    new = [fp for fp, *_, old in UPDATED if old is None and fp in found]
    print(f"SPU jobs found in {eboot.name}: {len(JOBS) - len(missing)} of {len(JOBS)}"
          + (f", plus {len(new)} that only game updates have" if new else ""))
    for fp in missing:
        print(f"  not found: {fp} (or a version of it this script doesn't know yet; the game stalls when it needs it)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

`GT5/scripts/spu_native_patch.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Switch hand-written native functions in for lifted SPU functions, and take a lifted job image's
branches to its own entries directly, at build time (no re-lift).

    spu_native_patch.py <lifted spu_recomp.c> <patched copy> <image> [<natives list>...] [--direct-bi <spu_jobs.c>]

GT5/src/native/natives.txt lists the replacements, one a line:

    <image> <address> <native symbol or -> <source file> [pure] [hooked]

For each line of this image the lifted definition `SPU_SV void gt5_<image>_spu_func_<ADDR>_sv(...)`
is renamed to `gt5_<image>_lifted_<ADDR>_sv`, and a function with the old name is added that picks
one at run time (GT5_SPU_NATIVE: 1 = native, the default; 0 = lifted; 2 = run both and compare,
only for lines marked `pure`: functions that touch nothing but their context and local store).
Every caller, the thunk and the function table keep using the old name, so nothing else changes.
A line marked `hooked` only renames the lifted definition to `..._orig_sv`: its source file defines
the old name itself (built with NATIVE_HOOKED) and has its own switch.
A line whose function is not in this lift is an error: a native function must never be linked in
for code it was not written against.
Further lists (the build passes GT5/src/native/natives_prof.txt only when its option is on) are read
the same way, after natives.txt. With no list (--direct-bi alone) the image only gets the direct branches.

--direct-bi <spu_jobs.c> (the build passes it for every job image) rewrites the image's returns to the
dispatcher (`ctx->pc = spu_w0(rN); g_spu_trampoline_fn = spu_indirect_branch; return;` -- a `bi`, `biz`,
`binz`, `bie`/`bid` to a register: loop back edges chosen with selb, interrupt toggles to the next
instruction) and its calls through a register (`ctx->pc = _tg; ctx->host_depth++; spu_indirect_branch(ctx);`
-- a `bisl`: the opcode handlers of a job's program, function pointers) so that, when the register holds
one of the image's entries and the dispatcher would choose that entry's function and nothing else
(gt5_dbi_ready, src/native/gt5_direct_bi.h / .c, with the reasons), the function is called directly; in
every other case the code is the lift's own (the dispatcher). The entries: the image's function table
(`{ 0x<ADDR>u, gt5_<image>_spu_func_<ADDR>, ...}`), less the return points (`spu_link(0x...)`,
`spu_drain_call(ctx, 0x...)`: where a waiting host frame must see the branch), the runtime's service
addresses (LS 0, 0x9C0, 0x9D0, 0xA00, 0xA2C, 0xA70, 0x3FEC0, 0x3FF00), and, for a WWS job's code, anything
outside the span it is registered with. Which images: the WWS jobs' code, registered in spu_jobs.c as
resident regions (spu_overlay_register_verified_region), and every image registered as a job binary
(spu_workload_register_img: the WWS job manager entered at 0xA00, the SPURS job binaries entered at LS 0;
n_static, 22 Nov 2026, before only the job manager): those run as the context's own image (spurs_job.c /
spu_workload.c set ctx->image_id to it), which is what gt5_dbi_confirm's kind 0 checks -- no resident code
slot over the target, the context's image, no overlay, no task -- so a branch goes direct only where the
dispatcher resolves the same function. A waiting host frame inside such an image is at one of its own
return points (spu_link / spu_drain_call: never in a switch) or at a service address (the job return
0x3FF00, LS 0: never in a switch). Other lifts (not in spu_jobs.c) are copied unchanged.
n_jobmgr, 22 Nov 2026: a target outside the image's own entries goes on to the switch of the image the
dispatcher would resolve it in (gt5_dbi_route: a WWS job's calls of the job manager's API, the manager's call of
a job), and the policy module's call of its interrupt handler's register stub (0x3FEC0) runs the stub natively
(spu_wws_irq_stub_direct) where the dispatcher's checks before it could not act. GT5_DIRECT_BI_XIMAGE=0 at run
time: own entries only.
Lift text this depends on (a re-lift that changes it leaves those branches with the dispatcher: the
counts printed show it): the two statements above, the table entry form, `spu_link(0x...)`,
`spu_drain_call(ctx, 0x...)`, `#include "spu_recomp.h"`, and `SPU_SV void gt5_<image>_spu_func_<ADDR>_sv(`
(each table entry's code, called by that name).
"""
import re
import sys

SERVICE = {0x0, 0x9C0, 0x9D0, 0xA00, 0xA2C, 0xA70, 0x3FEC0, 0x3FF00}


def image_info(jobs_c, image):
    """(image id, kind, lsa, size, policy module) from src/gen/spu_jobs.c, or None when the image gets no direct
    branches. The policy module is the image registered with its entry at 0xA00 (the WWS job manager)."""
    t = open(jobs_c, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
    m = re.search(r"spu_begin_image\((\d+)\);\s*gt5_%s_spu_recomp_register\(\);(.*?)(?=spu_begin_image|\Z)" % image, t, re.S)
    if not m:
        return None
    iid, rest = int(m.group(1)), m.group(2)
    r = re.search(r"spu_overlay_register_verified_region\(0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+u, 0x([0-9A-Fa-f]+)u, 0x([0-9A-Fa-f]+)u, (\d+)", rest)
    if r and int(r.group(3)) == iid:
        return iid, 1, int(r.group(1), 16), int(r.group(2), 16), False
    r = re.search(r"spu_workload_register_img\([^,]+, gt5_%s_spu_func_([0-9A-F]{8}), %d," % (image, iid), rest)
    if r:
        return iid, 0, 0, 0x40000, int(r.group(1), 16) == 0xA00
    return None


def transform_direct_bi(text, image, info):
    iid, kind, lsa, size, pm = info
    tab = [(int(a, 16), f) for a, f in re.findall(r"\{ 0x([0-9A-F]{8})u, gt5_%s_spu_func_([0-9A-F]{8}), \"" % image, text)]
    # each entry's code by its _sv name: defined here, or (a hooked native) named here and defined by the native
    have = set(re.findall(r"\bgt5_%s_spu_func_([0-9A-F]{8})_sv\b" % image, text))
    rets = set(int(x, 16) for x in re.findall(r"spu_link\(0x([0-9A-Fa-f]+)\)", text))
    rets |= set(int(x, 16) for x in re.findall(r"spu_drain_call\(ctx, 0x([0-9A-Fa-f]+)\)", text))
    ents = sorted(set(a for a, f in tab
                      if int(f, 16) == a and not (a & 3) and a not in rets and a not in SERVICE and lsa <= a < lsa + size
                      and f in have))
    first = text.find('#include "spu_recomp.h"')
    heads = re.search(r"^SPU_SV void gt5_%s_spu_func_" % image, text, re.M)
    if not ents or first < 0 or not heads:
        return text, 0, 0
    d = f"gt5_{image}_dbi"
    disp, dchk = f"gt5_{image}_direct_bi_sv", f"gt5_{image}_direct_bi_check_sv"
    call, cchk = f"gt5_{image}_direct_call_sv", f"gt5_{image}_direct_call_check_sv"
    site_re = re.compile(r"ctx->pc = spu_w0\((r\d+)\); g_spu_trampoline_fn = spu_indirect_branch; return;")
    text, sites = site_re.subn(
        lambda m: (f"ctx->pc = spu_w0({m.group(1)}); {{ const int _db = {d}.mode; "
                   f"if (__builtin_expect(_db == 1, 1)) {{ __attribute__((musttail)) return {disp}(ctx); }} "
                   f"if (_db == 2) {{ __attribute__((musttail)) return {dchk}(ctx); }} }} "
                   "g_spu_trampoline_fn = spu_indirect_branch; return;"), text)
    call_old = "ctx->pc = _tg; ctx->host_depth++; spu_indirect_branch(ctx);"
    calls = text.count(call_old)
    text = text.replace(call_old, f"ctx->pc = _tg; ctx->host_depth++; {{ const int _db = {d}.mode; "
                                  f"if (__builtin_expect(_db == 1, 1)) {call}(ctx); else if (_db == 2) {cchk}(ctx); "
                                  "else spu_indirect_branch(ctx); }")
    decl = ("\n/* spu_native_patch.py --direct-bi: a branch or call to a register holding one of this image's entries goes\n"
            " * there directly when the dispatcher would choose the same (src/native/gt5_direct_bi.h) */\n"
            '#include "gt5_direct_bi.h"\n'
            f"static gt5_dbi_image {d};\n"
            f"SPU_SV void {disp}(spu_context* ctx);\nSPU_SV void {dchk}(spu_context* ctx);\n"
            f"SPU_SV void {call}(spu_context* ctx);\nSPU_SV void {cchk}(spu_context* ctx);\n"
            + ("int spu_pm_service(spu_context* ctx);   /* spu_channels.c */\n" if pm else ""))
    # The policy module (n_static, 22 Nov 2026) calls the SPURS kernel's two services through the kernel context
    # (`lqa $r2, 0x1E0; bisl $r0, $r2`: exitToKernel 0x9C0, selectWorkload 0x9D0). The dispatcher serves them
    # with spu_pm_service after nothing but its interrupt-return check, which only acts while an interrupt's
    # registers are saved: so a call there is served directly in a policy-module run with none saved.
    svc = ("    if (__builtin_expect((ctx->pc == 0x9C0u || ctx->pc == 0x9D0u) && ctx->policy_mode && !ctx->irq_saved, 0) &&\n"
           "        spu_pm_service(ctx)) return;\n") if pm else ""
    # The policy module's interrupt handler calls the register save / restore stub the job manager writes at
    # 0x3FEC0 (`brsl $r79, 0x3FEC0`: the lift has a function there that only hands the address to the
    # dispatcher, which runs the stub natively). n_jobmgr, 22 Nov 2026: the stub runs right there, with the
    # dispatcher's result (ctx->pc = its return, the trampoline set: the waiting drain takes it), where the
    # dispatcher's own checks before it could not act (gt5_dbi_step_ok: not the interrupt-return point, no
    # interrupt pending, not a first step); else the dispatcher as before.
    nstub = 0
    if pm:
        stub_re = re.compile(r"(SPU_SV void gt5_%s_spu_func_0003FEC0_sv\(spu_context\* ctx\) \{\r?\n    )"
                             r"ctx->pc = 0x3FEC0u; g_spu_trampoline_fn = spu_indirect_branch; return;" % image)
        text, nstub = stub_re.subn(
            lambda m: m.group(1) + (f"ctx->pc = 0x3FEC0u; if (__builtin_expect({d}.mode != 0, 1) && ctx->policy_mode && "
                                    "gt5_dbi_step_ok(ctx)) (void)spu_wws_irq_stub_direct(ctx); "
                                    "g_spu_trampoline_fn = spu_indirect_branch; return;"), text)
    pos = heads.start()
    text = text[:pos] + decl + text[pos:]
    rows = ",\n".join(f"    {{ 0x{a:X}u, gt5_{image}_spu_func_{a:08X} }}" for a in ents)
    bcases = "\n".join(f"            case 0x{a:X}u: __attribute__((musttail)) return gt5_{image}_spu_func_{a:08X}_sv(ctx);" for a in ents)
    ccases = "\n".join(f"            case 0x{a:X}u: gt5_{image}_spu_func_{a:08X}_sv(ctx); return;" for a in ents)
    lo, hi = ents[0], ents[-1] + 4
    # n_jobmgr, 22 Nov 2026: a target outside this image's entries goes on to the image the dispatcher would
    # resolve it in (gt5_dbi_route: a WWS job's call of the job manager's API, the manager's call of a job),
    # through that image's own switch and confirmation; anything else is the dispatcher's, as before.
    route = (f"        const gt5_dbi_image* _r = gt5_dbi_route(ctx, {kind});\n"
             "        if (_r) {\n"
             "            if (_r->mode == 1) { %s }\n"
             "            if (_r->mode == 2) { %s }\n"
             "        }\n")
    text += (f"\n/* spu_native_patch.py --direct-bi: this image's entries (image {iid}, "
             + (f"resident code at 0x{lsa:X}+0x{size:X}" if kind == 1 else "the context's own image") + ") */\n"
             f"static const gt5_dbi_ent {d}_tab[] = {{\n{rows}\n}};\n"
             f"static gt5_dbi_image {d} = {{ .mode = 0, .name = \"{image}\", .image_id = {iid}, .kind = {kind}, "
             f".lsa = 0x{lsa:X}u, .size = 0x{size:X}u, .lo = 0x{lo:X}u, .hi = 0x{hi:X}u, .tab = {d}_tab, .n = {len(ents)}u, "
             f".branch_sv = {disp}, .branch_chk_sv = {dchk}, .call_sv = {call}, .call_chk_sv = {cchk} }};\n"
             f"__attribute__((constructor)) static void {d}_init(void) {{ gt5_dbi_register(&{d}); }}\n"
             "/* a branch: ctx->pc holds the target */\n"
             f"SPU_SV void {disp}(spu_context* ctx) {{\n"
             f"    if (__builtin_expect(ctx->pc - 0x{lo:X}u < 0x{hi - lo:X}u, 1)) {{\n"
             f"        if (__builtin_expect(gt5_dbi_ready(ctx, &{d}), 1)) {{\n"
             "            switch (ctx->pc) {\n" + bcases + "\n            default: break;\n            }\n        }\n"
             "    } else {\n"
             + route % ("__attribute__((musttail)) return _r->branch_sv(ctx);", "__attribute__((musttail)) return _r->branch_chk_sv(ctx);")
             + "    }\n"
             "    g_spu_trampoline_fn = spu_indirect_branch;\n}\n"
             f"SPU_SV void {dchk}(spu_context* ctx) {{\n"
             f"    if (gt5_dbi_ready(ctx, &{d}) && !gt5_dbi_check(ctx, &{d})) {{ g_spu_trampoline_fn = spu_indirect_branch; return; }}\n"
             f"    __attribute__((musttail)) return {disp}(ctx);\n}}\n"
             "/* a call (host_depth already counted): the entry's function as the dispatcher's fast path calls it */\n"
             f"SPU_SV void {call}(spu_context* ctx) {{\n" + svc +
             f"    if (__builtin_expect(ctx->pc - 0x{lo:X}u < 0x{hi - lo:X}u, 1)) {{\n"
             f"        if (__builtin_expect(gt5_dbi_ready(ctx, &{d}), 1)) {{\n"
             "            switch (ctx->pc) {\n" + ccases + "\n            default: break;\n            }\n        }\n"
             "    } else {\n"
             + route % ("_r->call_sv(ctx); return;", "_r->call_chk_sv(ctx); return;")
             + "    }\n"
             "    spu_indirect_branch(ctx);\n}\n"
             f"SPU_SV void {cchk}(spu_context* ctx) {{\n"
             f"    if (gt5_dbi_ready(ctx, &{d}) && !gt5_dbi_check(ctx, &{d})) {{ spu_indirect_branch(ctx); return; }}\n"
             f"    __attribute__((musttail)) return {call}(ctx);\n}}\n")
    return text, sites + calls + nstub, len(ents)


def main():
    args = sys.argv[1:]
    jobs_c = None
    if "--direct-bi" in args:
        i = args.index("--direct-bi")
        jobs_c = args[i + 1]
        del args[i:i + 2]
    src, dst, image = args[:3]
    listings = args[3:]
    text = open(src, encoding="latin-1", newline="").read()
    nl = "\r\n" if "\r\n" in text else "\n"
    tail = []
    for listing in listings:
        for line in open(listing, encoding="utf-8"):
            f = line.split("#", 1)[0].split()
            if len(f) < 4 or f[0] != image:
                continue
            addr, native = f[1].upper().rjust(8, "0"), f[2]
            pure = "pure" in f[4:]
            hooked = "hooked" in f[4:]
            if not hooked and not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z_]\w*", native):
                sys.exit(f"[spu-native] {listing}: {native!r} is not a C identifier")
            old = f"gt5_{image}_spu_func_{addr}_sv"
            new = f"gt5_{image}_lifted_{addr}_sv"
            head = f"SPU_SV void {old}(spu_context* ctx) {{"
            if text.count(head) != 1:
                sys.exit(f"[spu-native] {image}: `{head}` stands {text.count(head)} times in {src}, not once")
            if hooked:
                # The native source defines the old name itself and calls ..._orig_sv for what it leaves.
                text = text.replace(head, f"SPU_SV void gt5_{image}_spu_func_{addr}_orig_sv(spu_context* ctx) {{")
                n_hooked = locals().get("n_hooked", 0) + 1
                continue
            text = text.replace(head, f"SPU_SV void {new}(spu_context* ctx) {{")
            tail += [f"/* native replacement of {image} 0x{addr} (GT5/src/native) */",
                     f"extern void {native}(spu_context* ctx);",
                     f"SPU_SV void {old}(spu_context* ctx) {{",
                     "    const int m = g_gt5_spu_native;",
                     f"    if (m == 1) {{ {native}(ctx); return; }}",
                     (f"    if (m == 2) {{ gt5_spu_native_compare(ctx, {native}, {new}, \"{image}:{addr}\"); return; }}"
                      if pure else "    /* not pure: compare mode runs the lifted function */"),
                     f"    {new}(ctx);",
                     "}"]
    if listings and not tail and not locals().get("n_hooked"):
        sys.exit(f"[spu-native] {' '.join(listings)} has no line for {image}")
    done = []
    if jobs_c:
        info = image_info(jobs_c, image)
        if info:
            text, n, ne = transform_direct_bi(text, image, info)
            done.append(f"direct branches: {n} dispatcher branches and calls, {ne} entries")
        else:
            done.append("no direct branches (not a WWS job's code or the job manager)")
    if tail:
        text += nl + '#include "spu_native.h"' + nl + nl.join(tail) + nl
    open(dst, "w", encoding="latin-1", newline="").write(text)
    print(f"[spu-native] {image}: {len(tail) // 8 + locals().get('n_hooked', 0)} function(s) switched"
          + (f", {', '.join(done)}" if done else ""))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

`GT5/scripts/spuregs.py`:

```py
"""SPU state of a running gt5.exe, from outside: spuregs.py [--name "spurs pm"] [--reg a,b,c] [--ls hexaddr,hexlen]

Finds each host thread's spu_context by scanning its stack for a pointer whose `ls` field points at its own
ls_store, then prints image, pc, link register and the MFC staging registers.
"""
import ctypes
import ctypes.wintypes as w
import struct
import subprocess
import sys

LS_FIELD = 0x40800


def opt(name, default=None):
    if name in sys.argv:
        i = sys.argv.index(name)
        v = sys.argv[i + 1]
        del sys.argv[i:i + 2]
        return v
    return default


name = opt("--name", "spurs")
ls_dump = opt("--ls")
regs = [int(x) for x in opt("--reg", "3,11,14,15,16,18,55,61,63,70").split(",")]
k = ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32", use_last_error=True)
for fn in (k.OpenProcess, k.OpenThread, k.CreateToolhelp32Snapshot):
    fn.restype = w.HANDLE
k.ReadProcessMemory.argtypes = [w.HANDLE, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_size_t, ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_size_t)]
k.SuspendThread.argtypes = k.ResumeThread.argtypes = k.CloseHandle.argtypes = [w.HANDLE]
k.GetThreadContext.argtypes = [w.HANDLE, ctypes.c_void_p]
k.Thread32First.argtypes = k.Thread32Next.argtypes = [w.HANDLE, ctypes.c_void_p]
k.GetThreadDescription.argtypes = [w.HANDLE, ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_wchar_p)]
k.LocalFree.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p]


class THREADENTRY32(ctypes.Structure):
    _fields_ = [("dwSize", w.DWORD), ("cntUsage", w.DWORD), ("th32ThreadID", w.DWORD), ("th32OwnerProcessID", w.DWORD),
                ("tpBasePri", w.LONG), ("tpDeltaPri", w.LONG), ("dwFlags", w.DWORD)]


out = subprocess.run(["tasklist", "/FI", "IMAGENAME eq gt5.exe", "/FO", "CSV", "/NH"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
pid = int(out.split('","')[1])
proc = k.OpenProcess(0x1F0FFF, False, pid)


def read(addr, n):
    buf = ctypes.create_string_buffer(n)
    got = ctypes.c_size_t()
    if not k.ReadProcessMemory(proc, addr, buf, n, ctypes.byref(got)):
        return buf.raw[:got.value]
    return buf.raw[:got.value]


snap = k.CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(4, 0)
te = THREADENTRY32()
te.dwSize = ctypes.sizeof(te)
tids = []
ok = k.Thread32First(snap, ctypes.byref(te))
while ok:
    if te.th32OwnerProcessID == pid:
        tids.append(te.th32ThreadID)
    ok = k.Thread32Next(snap, ctypes.byref(te))
k.CloseHandle(snap)

raw = ctypes.create_string_buffer(4096 + 16)
ctx_addr = (ctypes.addressof(raw) + 15) & ~15
for tid in tids:
    h = k.OpenThread(0x1FFFFF, False, tid)
    if not h:
        continue
    desc = ctypes.c_wchar_p()
    title = ""
    if k.GetThreadDescription(h, ctypes.byref(desc)) >= 0 and desc.value:
        title = desc.value
        k.LocalFree(desc)
    if name not in title:
        k.CloseHandle(h)
        continue
    k.SuspendThread(h)
    ctypes.memset(ctx_addr, 0, 1232)
    ctypes.c_uint32.from_address(ctx_addr + 0x30).value = 0x10001F
    rsp = 0
    if k.GetThreadContext(h, ctx_addr):
        rsp = ctypes.c_uint64.from_address(ctx_addr + 0x98).value
    stack = read(rsp, 0x4000) if rsp else b""
    seen = set()
    for i in range(0, len(stack) - 8, 8):
        p = struct.unpack_from("<Q", stack, i)[0]
        if p < 0x10000 or p >> 47 or p & 15 or p in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(p)
        field = read(p + LS_FIELD, 0x30)
        if len(field) == 0x30 and struct.unpack_from("<Q", field)[0] == p + 0x800:
            pc, status, stop, spu, group, img = struct.unpack_from("<IIIIIi", field, 8)
            gp = read(p, 0x800)
            r = lambda n: struct.unpack_from("<I", gp, n * 16)[0]
            print("%d %s ctx=%X img=%d pc=%05X lr=%05X sp=%05X status=%X spu=%X" % (tid, title, p, img, pc & 0x3FFFF, r(0) & 0x3FFFF, r(1), status, spu))
            print("   " + " ".join("r%d=%08X" % (n, r(n)) for n in regs))
            if ls_dump and status == 1:
                a, n = [int(x, 16) for x in ls_dump.split(",")]
                d = read(p + 0x800 + a, n)
                for o in range(0, len(d), 32):
                    print("   %05X: %s" % (a + o, " ".join("%08x" % x for x in struct.unpack_from("<8I", (d + bytes(32)), o))))
            break
    k.ResumeThread(h)
    k.CloseHandle(h)

```

`GT5/scripts/stacksum.py`:

```py
import os as _gt5_os  # this clone's folders, wherever it was cloned to
GT5_DIR = _gt5_os.path.dirname(_gt5_os.path.dirname(_gt5_os.path.abspath(__file__)))
BASE_DIR = _gt5_os.path.dirname(GT5_DIR)
"""Add up host call stacks of a running gt5.exe: stacksum.py [samples] [gap s] [--name text]

Runs hoststack.py repeatedly and, for each kind of thread, counts where it was: the ntdll leaf it sat in and the
first frame above ntdll. Shows whether "ntdll time" is idle waiting or contention on a lock.
"""
import collections
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import time

HS = (GT5_DIR + r"\scripts\hoststack.py")
n = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 20
gap = float(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 0.7
NT = re.compile(r"^(Zw|Nt|Rtl|Ldr|_NLG|KiUser|Wait|Sleep|Enter|Leave|Cnd_|Mtx_|Switch|Query|BaseThread|Etw|Tp)")
by_kind = collections.defaultdict(collections.Counter)
by_kind_top = collections.defaultdict(collections.Counter)
samples = collections.Counter()
for s in range(n):
    out = subprocess.run(["python", HS, "--all", "--depth", "12"], capture_output=True, text=True, errors="replace").stdout
    blocks = re.split(r"^== ", out, flags=re.M)[1:]
    for b in blocks:
        lines = b.splitlines()
        head = lines[0].split(None, 1)
        kind = head[1].strip() if len(head) > 1 else "(unnamed)"
        kind = re.sub(r"\d+$", "", kind).strip() or "(unnamed)"
        frames = [l.strip().split("  ")[0] for l in lines[1:] if l.strip()]
        if not frames:
            continue
        samples[kind] += 1
        leaf = re.sub(r"\+[0-9A-Fa-f]+$", "", frames[0])
        first = next((re.sub(r"\(.*$", "", f) for f in frames if not NT.match(f)), "?")
        by_kind[kind][(leaf if NT.match(frames[0]) else "(running)") + " <- " + first] += 1
    time.sleep(gap)
for kind, c in sorted(samples.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]):
    print("== %s  (%d thread samples)" % (kind, c))
    for what, k in by_kind[kind].most_common(12):
        print("   %5.1f%%  %s" % (100.0 * k / c, what[:96]))

```

```py
"""Print strings from the ELF that match regexes, with their guest address (rodata maps file off + 0x10000)."""
import re
import sys

d = open(sys.argv[1], "rb").read()
BASE = 0x10000
strs = list(re.finditer(rb"[\x20-\x7e]{3,200}", d))
for pat in sys.argv[2:]:
    rx = re.compile(pat.encode())
    print(f"== {pat}")
    n = 0
    for m in strs:
        if rx.search(m.group(0)):
            print(f"  0x{m.start() + BASE:08X} {m.group(0).decode('latin1')}")
            n += 1
            if n > 60:
                print("  ...")
                break
```
