         stbtt_uint16 ch2 = s2[2]*256 + s2[3];
         if (i+3 >= len1) return -1;
         c = ((ch - 0xd800) << 10) + (ch2 - 0xdc00) + 0x10000;
         if (s1[i++] != 0xf0 + (c >> 18)) return -1;
         if (s1[i++] != 0x80 + ((c >> 12) & 0x3f)) return -1;
         if (s1[i++] != 0x80 + ((c >>  6) & 0x3f)) return -1;
         if (s1[i++] != 0x80 + ((c      ) & 0x3f)) return -1;
         s2 += 2; // plus another 2 below
         len2 -= 2;
      } else if (ch >= 0xdc00 && ch < 0xe000) {
         return -1;
      } else {
         if (i+2 >= len1) return -1;
         if (s1[i++] != 0xe0 + (ch >> 12)) return -1;
         if (s1[i++] != 0x80 + ((ch >> 6) & 0x3f)) return -1;
         if (s1[i++] != 0x80 + ((ch     ) & 0x3f)) return -1;
      }
      s2 += 2;
      len2 -= 2;
   }
   return i;
}

static int stbtt_CompareUTF8toUTF16_bigendian_internal(char *s1, int len1, char *s2, int len2)
{
   return len1 == stbtt__CompareUTF8toUTF16_bigendian_prefix((stbtt_uint8*) s1, len1, (stbtt_uint8*) s2, len2);
}

// returns results in whatever encoding you request... but note that 2-byte encodings
// will be BIG-ENDIAN... use stbtt_CompareUTF8toUTF16_bigendian() to compare
STBTT_DEF const char *stbtt_GetFontNameString(const stbtt_fontinfo *font, int *length, int platformID, int encodingID, int languageID, int nameID)
{
   stbtt_int32 i,count,stringOffset;
   stbtt_uint8 *fc = font->data;
   stbtt_uint32 offset = font->fontstart;
   stbtt_uint32 nm = stbtt__find_table(fc, offset, "name");
   if (!nm) return NULL;

   count = ttUSHORT(fc+nm+2);
   stringOffset = nm + ttUSHORT(fc+nm+4);
   for (i=0; i < count; ++i) {
      stbtt_uint32 loc = nm + 6 + 12 * i;
      if (platformID == ttUSHORT(fc+loc+0) && encodingID == ttUSHORT(fc+loc+2)
          && languageID == ttUSHORT(fc+loc+4) && nameID == ttUSHORT(fc+loc+6)) {
         *length = ttUSHORT(fc+loc+8);
         return (const char *) (fc+stringOffset+ttUSHORT(fc+loc+10));
      }
   }
   return NULL;
}

static int stbtt__matchpair(stbtt_uint8 *fc, stbtt_uint32 nm, stbtt_uint8 *name, stbtt_int32 nlen, stbtt_int32 target_id, stbtt_int32 next_id)
{
   stbtt_int32 i;
   stbtt_int32 count = ttUSHORT(fc+nm+2);
   stbtt_int32 stringOffset = nm + ttUSHORT(fc+nm+4);

   for (i=0; i < count; ++i) {
      stbtt_uint32 loc = nm + 6 + 12 * i;
      stbtt_int32 id = ttUSHORT(fc+loc+6);
      if (id == target_id) {
         // find the encoding
         stbtt_int32 platform = ttUSHORT(fc+loc+0), encoding = ttUSHORT(fc+loc+2), language = ttUSHORT(fc+loc+4);

         // is this a Unicode encoding?
         if (platform == 0 || (platform == 3 && encoding == 1) || (platform == 3 && encoding == 10)) {
            stbtt_int32 slen = ttUSHORT(fc+loc+8);
            stbtt_int32 off = ttUSHORT(fc+loc+10);

            // check if there's a prefix match
            stbtt_int32 matchlen = stbtt__CompareUTF8toUTF16_bigendian_prefix(name, nlen, fc+stringOffset+off,slen);
            if (matchlen >= 0) {
               // check for target_id+1 immediately following, with same encoding & language
               if (i+1 < count && ttUSHORT(fc+loc+12+6) == next_id && ttUSHORT(fc+loc+12) == platform && ttUSHORT(fc+loc+12+2) == encoding && ttUSHORT(fc+loc+12+4) == language) {
                  slen = ttUSHORT(fc+loc+12+8);
                  off = ttUSHORT(fc+loc+12+10);
                  if (slen == 0) {
                     if (matchlen == nlen)
                        return 1;
                  } else if (matchlen < nlen && name[matchlen] == ' ') {
                     ++matchlen;
                     if (stbtt_CompareUTF8toUTF16_bigendian_internal((char*) (name+matchlen), nlen-matchlen, (char*)(fc+stringOffset+off),slen))
                        return 1;
                  }
               } else {
                  // if nothing immediately following
                  if (matchlen == nlen)
                     return 1;
               }
            }
         }

         // @TODO handle other encodings
      }
   }
   return 0;
}

static int stbtt__matches(stbtt_uint8 *fc, stbtt_uint32 offset, stbtt_uint8 *name, stbtt_int32 flags)
{
   stbtt_int32 nlen = (stbtt_int32) STBTT_strlen((char *) name);
   stbtt_uint32 nm,hd;
   if (!stbtt__isfont(fc+offset)) return 0;

   // check italics/bold/underline flags in macStyle...
   if (flags) {
      hd = stbtt__find_table(fc, offset, "head");
      if ((ttUSHORT(fc+hd+44) & 7) != (flags & 7)) return 0;
   }

   nm = stbtt__find_table(fc, offset, "name");
   if (!nm) return 0;

   if (flags) {
      // if we checked the macStyle flags, then just check the family and ignore the subfamily
      if (stbtt__matchpair(fc, nm, name, nlen, 16, -1))  return 1;
      if (stbtt__matchpair(fc, nm, name, nlen,  1, -1))  return 1;
      if (stbtt__matchpair(fc, nm, name, nlen,  3, -1))  return 1;
   } else {
      if (stbtt__matchpair(fc, nm, name, nlen, 16, 17))  return 1;
      if (stbtt__matchpair(fc, nm, name, nlen,  1,  2))  return 1;
      if (stbtt__matchpair(fc, nm, name, nlen,  3, -1))  return 1;
   }

   return 0;
}

static int stbtt_FindMatchingFont_internal(unsigned char *font_collection, char *name_utf8, stbtt_int32 flags)
{
   stbtt_int32 i;
   for (i=0;;++i) {
      stbtt_int32 off = stbtt_GetFontOffsetForIndex(font_collection, i);
      if (off < 0) return off;
      if (stbtt__matches((stbtt_uint8 *) font_collection, off, (stbtt_uint8*) name_utf8, flags))
         return off;
   }
}

#if defined(__GNUC__) || defined(__clang__)
#pragma GCC diagnostic push
#pragma GCC diagnostic ignored "-Wcast-qual"
#endif

STBTT_DEF int stbtt_BakeFontBitmap(const unsigned char *data, int offset,
                                float pixel_height, unsigned char *pixels, int pw, int ph,
                                int first_char, int num_chars, stbtt_bakedchar *chardata)
{
   return stbtt_BakeFontBitmap_internal((unsigned char *) data, offset, pixel_height, pixels, pw, ph, first_char, num_chars, chardata);
}

STBTT_DEF int stbtt_GetFontOffsetForIndex(const unsigned char *data, int index)
{
   return stbtt_GetFontOffsetForIndex_internal((unsigned char *) data, index);
}

STBTT_DEF int stbtt_GetNumberOfFonts(const unsigned char *data)
{
   return stbtt_GetNumberOfFonts_internal((unsigned char *) data);
}

STBTT_DEF int stbtt_InitFont(stbtt_fontinfo *info, const unsigned char *data, int offset)
{
   return stbtt_InitFont_internal(info, (unsigned char *) data, offset);
}

STBTT_DEF int stbtt_FindMatchingFont(const unsigned char *fontdata, const char *name, int flags)
{
   return stbtt_FindMatchingFont_internal((unsigned char *) fontdata, (char *) name, flags);
}

STBTT_DEF int stbtt_CompareUTF8toUTF16_bigendian(const char *s1, int len1, const char *s2, int len2)
{
   return stbtt_CompareUTF8toUTF16_bigendian_internal((char *) s1, len1, (char *) s2, len2);
}

`MODDING.md`:

```md
# Modding

There are four ways into the port, from no code at all to changing the PC side itself. Whatever you
make, share **your own work only**: never the game's files, `gt5.exe` builds or the generated code.
When you've made something, tell us with the
[fork/mod form](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/issues/new?template=4-my-fork-or-mod.yml)
or in the [Workshop Discord](https://discord.gg/9cVPS7r5Ha) (#dev-chat).

## 1. Your own game files

The game reads its data from `GT5\vfs\PS3_GAME` exactly as the disc lays it out, so changing a file
there changes the game on your PC. Keep a backup of anything you replace. To share such a mod, share
your new content and instructions or a tool, never files that came off the disc.

## 2. Textures and HD texture packs

GT5's textures can be written out as files and swapped for your own, at any size, the way HD texture
packs are made for GT4 on PCSX2. This works with the DirectX 12 renderer (the default); the Vulkan
renderer, and so Linux, doesn't do it yet.

**Dumping.** Add `set "PS3_TEX_DUMP=1"` to `GT5\settings.bat` (or `play.bat`) and play: every texture
the game shows is written once to `GT5\textures\dump\`, on a background thread. Drive the tracks and
cars you want, then take the line out again. A texture is written once it has stayed the same for 20
frames, so movies, the menus' animated backgrounds and anything else the game keeps rewriting are left
out, as are render targets (pictures the game draws itself, like mirrors), cube maps and 3D textures.
Files already in the folder aren't written again.

Each file is named `<hash>_<width>x<height>_<format>.<dds|png>`, for example
`543D80602521D493_1024x1024_dxt5.dds`:

- The hash (the first 16 characters) is worked out from the texture's pixels, so a texture gets the
  same name every time, on every PC, wherever the game happens to keep it in video memory.
- DXT1, DXT3 and DXT5 textures (nearly everything on tracks and cars) are written as **DDS**: the
  compressed data exactly as the game has it, nothing lost. Paint.NET, GIMP, Photoshop (with Intel's
  Texture Works plugin) and Microsoft's `texconv` open them.
- Everything else (A8R8G8B8 and the 16-bit formats, mostly menus and the HUD) is written as **PNG**
  with alpha, in the colours the game reads.
- `_rect` at the end of a name: the game reads that texture by pixel position, so a replacement has to
  keep exactly its size.
- Some textures are stored upside down or mirrored; that's how the game uses them, so keep them that way.

**Replacing.** Put your file in `GT5\textures\replace\` (sub-folders are fine, say one per pack) with
the same 16-character hash at the start of its name; the rest of the name is up to you. At the next
start the game uses it instead of its own.

- **Any size.** 2x or 4x the original is usual; keep the proportions. `_rect` textures only at their
  own size (`play.err` says so when a file is skipped for that).
- **Formats:** PNG (RGBA or RGB), or DDS in BC1/DXT1, BC2/DXT3, BC3/DXT5, BC7 or uncompressed 32-bit
  RGBA/BGRA. Compressed DDS sizes must be multiples of 4. No cube maps or arrays.
- **Mipmaps:** a DDS's own are used; otherwise they're made when the file loads (except for a BC7 DDS,
  which then shimmers in the distance; save BC7 with mipmaps).
- **For a big pack, use DDS with mipmaps** (BC1 for opaque textures, BC3 or BC7 with alpha). A PNG,
  or a BC1/BC3 DDS without mipmaps, is unpacked to 32-bit colour: 4 to 8 times the video memory, and
  slower to load.
- Files load in the background the first time their texture shows up (the game's own is shown for
  that moment) and are kept for the rest of the session. Changes to the folder are read at the next start.
- For DXT textures the file holds the channels as the game stores them, and the game's channel
  mapping still applies on top (normal maps, for instance, keep working). For the other formats the
  PNG is the finished picture and is used as it is.
- `set "PS3_TEX_REPLACE=0"` turns replacement off without moving any files, and
  `set "PS3_TEX_DIR=<folder>"` uses another folder instead of `GT5\textures` (it holds `dump\` and
  `replace\`).
- `logs\play.err` shows how many files were found (`[texpack] replace: N texture file(s)`), each file
  where it's first used, any file it can't use and why, and what it did every 10 s.

**Sharing.** Dumped textures come off the game disc: never share them, not even a few as examples or
"originals for comparison". Share only textures you made yourself, as your own download, and never on
this project's GitHub (no textures in issues, pull requests, releases or forks of it), the same rule
as for every other mod here.

## 3. Game-code mods (`GT5\mods`)

A game-code mod changes instructions in the game's own code. It lives in a folder with a `mod.json`:

```json
{
  "name": "unlock-fps",
  "description": "What it does, in a sentence.",
  "default": false,
  "patches": {
    "1535B865EC7DD58E7704B378B8621532ECF844E1": [
      {"addr": "0x008CFFB4", "orig": "0x8089001C", "new": "0x38800000", "note": "why this works"}
    ]
  }
}
```

- Each patch replaces one 32-bit PowerPC instruction at `addr`. `orig` is the instruction there now
  (checked against your EBOOT, so a mod can't land in the wrong place), and `new` is its replacement.
- Patches are listed per release, under the SHA-1 of the decrypted `EBOOT.elf` that
  `scripts\version_addrs.py` prints. A mod has no effect on a release it has no list for.
- `relift.ps1` collects every mod (`scripts\mods.py`) and builds both versions of each patched
  instruction into the game, so a mod costs nothing while it's off. It is switched at start-up by the
  environment variable `GT5_MOD_<NAME>` (`set "GT5_MOD_UNLOCK_FPS=1"` in `play.bat`), or by
  `"default"` when that isn't set. `logs\play.err` lists each mod as on or off.
- After adding or changing a mod, run `scripts\relift.ps1` and `scripts\build.cmd gt5` again.

A patch can also name its place by the code around it, for every release at once: put it in a list
under `"*"` as `{"find": "8089001C 88A90019 7C8407B4", "new": "0x38800002"}`. The first word of that run of
instruction words is replaced (`"at"` picks another), and the run must turn up exactly once in the EBOOT,
or the mod is left out for that copy. Two mods may replace the same instruction; with both on, the one
whose name sorts first wins. `GT5\mods\half-rate` works this way: it makes the game draw 30 frames a
second at real speed (it steps its simulation twice a frame), for about half the frames' work.

`GT5\mods\unlock-fps` is the example of the format, and of what a one-instruction change can and can't
do. It takes out the game's own wait for the next screen refresh (RPCS3's "Unlock FPS" patch is the same
change), and that alone does **not** make the game run faster than 60 frames a second here: the port
finishes a frame's flip no more than 60 times a second, and GT5 also follows the PS3's 60-a-second
vertical blank in other places. Measured on 17 Nov 2026 with the mod on: 60.0 frames a second, the same
race clock; with the port's own limit lifted as a test, still 60.0; with the vertical blank at 120 a
second the game fell to 8-18 frames a second and never reached the race. So the mod is kept as a
harmless example, off by default (its own description in the launcher's mod list still promises more;
that text changes with the next version that re-lifts, since a changed `mod.json` means a re-lift). For
more frames on a fast screen use the launcher's **Frame rate multiplier** (frame generation), which
leaves the game at 60.

Checked on v0.1.100 (17 Nov 2026): `half-rate` gives 29.97 game frames a second at the unmodded race
clock's speed with about 40% less CPU, and 60 frames on screen with frame generation; the in-game
menu (F1) keeps `GT5_MOD_...` lines and your own lines when it saves `settings.bat`.

**RPCS3 patches.** RPCS3's game patches (`patch.yml`, from RPCS3's patch manager) can become mods
when they only change instructions in place. `scripts\rpcs3_mods.py` finds the patches written for
exactly your copy (release and update) and says which ones fit:

```
venv\Scripts\python.exe GT5\scripts\rpcs3_mods.py "C:\path\to\patch.yml"
venv\Scripts\python.exe GT5\scripts\rpcs3_mods.py "C:\path\to\patch.yml" --add "Disable Dithering"
```

`--add` writes `GT5\mods\rpcs3-<name>\mod.json` (on by default; it shows in the launcher's mod list),
then run `scripts\relift.ps1` and `scripts\build.cmd gt5`. RPCS3 writes its patches into the game's
code while the game runs, but here the code was turned into PC code ahead of time, so patches that
add code of their own (most long ones), change data, take a configurable value or point a branch
somewhere new don't fit and are left out whole. The patches are their authors' work: keep the
generated mods on your PC.

Some changes are data rather than instructions, such as a constant the game reads. Try one without
building anything with `set "PS3_POKE32=<address>=<value>"` (hex, big-endian 32-bit words, comma
separated; `logs\play.err` shows the old values). To keep one, do as `GT5\src\gt5_widescreen.cpp`
does for ultrawide: a function registered with `ps3_on_loaded` runs once the EBOOT is loaded and
before the game starts, checks the values it expects, and writes the new ones.

Finding what to change: the lifted code in `GT5\generated` is readable C++ with one function per game
function (`func_<address>`), and the scripts help you watch the running game:

| Script | Use |
|---|---|
| `gstack.py`, `hoststack.py` | Where each game thread is right now (game and PC call stacks). |
| `gwatch.py`, `gmem.py`, `gvar.py` | Watch or read the game's memory while it runs. |
| `showfn.py`, `opdrefs.py` | Show a game function, and who refers to it. |
| `profsym.py` (with `prof.ps1`) | Where the CPU time goes, per thread. |

## 4. The PC side (ps3recomp)

Everything that stands in for the PS3's hardware and system software is C/C++ in `ps3recomp`, patched
by `GT5\patches\ps3recomp.patch`:

| Area | Where |
|---|---|
| Graphics (the RSX drawn with Direct3D 12) | `libs/video/rsx_live_draw.c`, `rsx_dispatch.c`, `rsx_fp_decompiler.c` (shaders) |
| Texture dumps and packs | `libs/video/rsx_texpack.c` (files, hashes), `rsx_live_draw.c` (`ld_tp_*`) |
| Controller | `libs/input/cellPad.c` |
| Sound | `libs/audio/cellAudio.c` |
| Movies | `libs/codec/` |
| SPU (the PS3's co-processors) | `runtime/spu/` |
| Files and saves | `runtime/ppu/ppu_fs.cpp`, `libs/system/cellSaveData.c` |

Change the files in `ps3recomp\`, then `GT5\scripts\build.cmd gt5`. Put anything that might not suit
everyone behind an environment-variable switch (`getenv`), as the existing changes are. To share it,
fork this repository and refresh the patch from your `ps3recomp` folder:

```
git -C ps3recomp diff --output=../GT5/patches/ps3recomp.patch
```

## Ideas people would like

Tuning the new steering-wheel support (button and pedal defaults for more wheels, rev lights), a
resolution or render-scale setting, a wider field of view,
a frame-rate unlock that keeps the clock at real time, HUD toggles for screenshots, and anything that
makes setup easier. If you start on one, say so in the
[discussions](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/discussions) so work isn't doubled.

# GT5 Recomp

An unofficial PC port of **Gran Turismo 5** (PS3) made by static recompilation: the game's
PowerPC and SPU code is translated into C++ that is compiled for Windows x64, and the PS3's graphics,
sound, input and system calls are reimplemented on Windows (Direct3D 12 for the RSX). A native
[Linux build](#linux) (Vulkan) is new and early.

It is built on [ps3recomp](https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp) and borrows from the
[GT5 Prologue port](https://github.com/sp00nznet/GT5P), both by Ned Heller (sp00nznet).

> **Game version required:** your own **Gran Turismo 5** Blu-ray disc, using the disc's own
> executable (version **01.00**, with **no game update** installed):
>
> - **Europe, BCES00569**: tested. This is the copy the port was built from.
> - **North America, BCUS98114**: works; players have raced on it (thanks!). The lift finds the few addresses
>   that differ between releases in your own executable.
>
> See [Which copy of GT5](#which-copy-of-gt5) for how to check your files.

<a id="install"></a>

## ⬇️ Install

**The easy way, on Windows 10 or 11:**

1. Download **[GT5-Installer.bat](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/releases/latest/download/GT5-Installer.bat)**
   and double-click it. If Windows warns about a downloaded file, choose **Run** (or **More info**, then
   **Run anyway**).
2. In its window, pick **your GT5 game** (the folder of your disc dump, the one with `PS3_GAME` in it, or
   an `.iso`) and press **Install**. Nothing else is needed: no PS3 system software file and no RPCS3.

That's all, and it all happens in that one window: the steps, a progress bar, and what went wrong if
something does. Nothing is installed into Windows. It downloads this code and, into the install folder,
its own copies of Git (38 MB, only when the PC has none), Python (17 MB) and the compiler tools
(about 1.5 GB, into the install folder: **no Visual Studio is installed or changed**), unlocks your game's executable (with the port's own small tool; RPCS3 is not used:
the game itself runs natively as `gt5.exe`, not in an emulator), builds the game (about an hour the
first time) with both renderers (DirectX 12 and Vulkan), adds AMD FSR 3 frame generation and, on a PC with
an NVIDIA RTX card, NVIDIA DLSS, and puts **Gran Turismo 5 (PC)** on your desktop, which opens the
[launcher](#launcher). Nothing from the game is ever uploaded or shared. Some of what it downloads comes
under another company's licence (Microsoft's C++ libraries in the compiler tools, when it fetches those;
NVIDIA DLSS): the line by the **Install** button names them, with links, and pressing Install accepts them.

Rather do it by hand? See [Setup](#setup). On Linux? See [Linux](#linux).

<a id="launcher"></a>

## 🎛️ The launcher

<p align="center">
  <img src="docs/launcher.png" alt="The GT5 launcher: Display settings, with a big Play button" width="80%">
</p>

**Gran Turismo 5 (PC)** on your desktop (or `GT5Launcher.exe` in your `gt5-recomp` folder) opens the
launcher: every setting in one window, then **Play**. No more editing `play.bat`.

- **Display:** the renderer, resolution, anti-aliasing (NVIDIA DLSS, on an RTX card), shadows, frame
  generation, **borderless full screen** (the default), a maximized window or a window size, screen shape
  (ultrawide), the frame rate (60 or 30 fps) and [asynchronous shader loading](#shaders). The rows say
  what the game's own menu says; a row that
  means nothing with another setting's value is left out, as in the game (no Multiplier while frame
  generation is off), and with Vulkan chosen the rows it can't do yet are greyed.
- **Controls:** the controller's triggers (throttle and brake, or as on a PS3 pad), steering wheel on/off,
  wheel rotation, force feedback strength and direction, pad in the background, mouse clipping,
  [mouse steering](#mouse-steering), keyboard keys.
- **Game:** the [cockpit view](#cockpit-view) (field of view, seat position), the game's language (as far as
  your disc has it), the volume and muting in the background, your mods from `GT5\mods`, the launcher's
  own language (English or 中文).

The game's own settings menu (**F1** in the game, or **Select + Start** held on a controller) has the same
settings and writes the same file; the launcher reads it again when the game ends.
- **Updates:** shows your version and the newest one with what's new, and **Update now** does the
  whole update for you in its own window (your newest Photo Mode pictures behind it, a car on the
  progress bar, **Details** for the full text) and opens the launcher again.
- **Help:** **Save logs for a report** puts one report file (`GT5-report-<date>.zip`) on the desktop,
  plus the logs folder, the problem form, this FAQ and **Clear the shader cache** (also
  `ClearShaders.bat` in the install folder; see the FAQ).
- **After a crash or a freeze** the line at the bottom says so, with **Save a report** (the same file,
  shown in Explorer) and **Open the report page** (the problem form with your version and PC filled in:
  drag the file into it). The report holds the parts of the logs that matter, your settings and your
  PC's parts; your Windows user name, PC name and every folder outside the game's are taken out, and
  there's no save data or game file in it. Nothing is sent by itself.

It's built on your PC from [`launcher/GT5Launcher.cs`](launcher/GT5Launcher.cs) with the C# compiler that
comes with Windows, every time the game is built, so it updates with the game; its picture is the logo
from your own disc. Settings are saved in `GT5\settings.bat`, which `play.bat` reads, so `play.bat`
still works and starts the game the same way. (`GT5Launcher.exe --play` starts the game straight away.)

<a id="updating"></a>

## 🔄 Updating

Every change to the port comes out as a numbered version (v0.1.0, v0.1.1, ...) on the
[Releases page](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/releases), with what changed. To hear
about new ones, click **Watch** at the top of this page, then **Custom** and tick **Releases**.

### The easy way

- **The launcher** checks for a new version when it opens: its **Updates** page shows what's new, and
  **Update now** does everything below in an update window and opens the launcher again. If the update
  stops, the window shows why and keeps the full text in `GT5\logs\update.log` for a report.
- Or **double-click `Update.bat`** in your `gt5-recomp` folder.

Both run `update.ps1`, so everything below applies. (No launcher or `Update.bat` yet? Your next update
brings them: run the command below once.)

### Are you out of date?

Close the game, open PowerShell in your `gt5-recomp` folder and run:

```
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1 -List
```

It lists every version and marks the one you have (`<- installed`) and the newest (`[newest]`).
If they're different, you're out of date.

### Update to the newest version

```
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1
```

That one command does everything:

1. It downloads the new version.
2. It swaps the old ps3recomp patch for the new one.
3. It re-generates the game code only if that version needs it (about 10 minutes).
4. It rebuilds only what changed.

Kept as they are:
- your saves (`GT5\gamedata`), a game update's data (`GT5\hdd0`) and game files (`GT5\input`, `GT5\vfs`);
- the shader cache;
- edits you made to files such as `play.bat`.

The previous `gt5.exe` is kept as `GT5\build\gt5.previous.exe`. If one of your edits clashes with a
change in the new version, the new version's file is used and your edit is saved in `backups\` so
you can copy it back.

**If you're several versions behind,** run the same command. It goes straight to the newest version;
there's no need to step through the ones in between.

### Installed before update.ps1 existed?

If your folder has no `update.ps1` (you set up before v0.1.0), get it first, then update:

```
git pull
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1
```

If `git pull` says your local changes would be overwritten (usually `play.bat`), run `git stash`,
then `git pull`, then `git stash pop`, then the update. Your first update re-generates the game code
once (about 10 minutes), because older installs have no record of what their code was made from.

### Downloaded the ZIP instead of cloning?

A ZIP download can't update itself. Clone the repository fresh as in [Setup](#setup), step 1. Then
move these folders over from your old copy and run `update.ps1`:
- your game files: `GT5\input`, `GT5\vfs`;
- your saves: `GT5\gamedata` (and `GT5\hdd0`, if you set up a game update).

### Go back to an older version

If a new version gives you trouble, switch back to the one that worked (see `-List` for the names):

```
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1 -Version v0.1.0
```

To play the previous build right away instead, copy `GT5\build\gt5.previous.exe` over
`GT5\build\gt5.exe` (the last update kept it). Please also
[report what went wrong](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/issues/new?template=2-problem.yml).

<a id="test-builds"></a>

### Test builds

Changes still being tried out go to a **test build** first: the `test` branch of this repository, with
no version number and no release. Releases, new installs and the launcher's Update never use it. To try it:

```
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1 -Test
```

A plain update (`update.ps1`, `Update.bat` or the launcher's **Update now**) goes back to the newest
release. What the current test build changes is at the top of
[its CHANGELOG](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/blob/test/CHANGELOG.md) (the entries above
the newest "Released as" line), and each new one is announced in
[Announcements](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/discussions/categories/announcements) and in
the Discord's releases channel. Expect rough edges, and say "test build" and its date when you report
something.

### Other options

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `update.ps1 -Test` | The [test build](#test-builds): changes still being tried out. A plain update goes back. |
| `update.ps1 -Dev` | The newest changes, before they're released. |
| `update.ps1 -NoBuild` | Switch versions without building; build later with `GT5\scripts\build.cmd gt5`. |
| `update.ps1 -Force` | Re-generate and rebuild everything, even when nothing changed. |

<a id="controls"></a>

## 🎮 Controls

A DualSense, DualShock 4 or XInput pad works, and so does the keyboard, with a pad connected or without one.

**On a pad** the buttons are the game's own, as on a PS3 pad: ✕ / A accelerates, □ / X brakes, R2 / L2
shift (change them in the game's own options). The in-game menu's Controls page has **Triggers**:
*Throttle and brake* makes the right trigger the throttle and the left the brake while you drive, both
by how far you pull them, with the bumpers shifting up and down, the left stick press looking back and
the right one working the lights; the face buttons still accelerate and brake fully, and it follows the
buttons you set in the game's own options. At the menus, in replays and in the in-game menu the pad is
always laid out as a PS3 pad. Every pad gets the same small round dead zone on its sticks.

The game's menus show PlayStation symbols. The Controls page has **Button symbols**: *Xbox* shows
A / B / X / Y, LB / RB, LT / RT in their place, *Keyboard* shows the keys you have bound, and
*Automatic* follows what you used last (checked on the European 1.00 release; a release whose
pictures differ keeps the game's own).

**Keyboard**: Z = Cross, X = Circle, A = Square, S = Triangle, arrow keys = D-pad, Enter = Start, Tab = Select.
An arrow-key tap moves one place in the menus, and in a race Left/Right steer as the D-pad does on a PS3
pad, eased in by the game (`PS3_KEYS_ARROWS` under [Switches](#switches) has the other ways).
Esc quits the game, after asking (`set "PS3_ESC_CONFIRM=0"` in `play.bat` quits at once).

<a id="keyboard-keys"></a>

**Your own keys** (new): the launcher's Controls page has a **Keyboard keys** list, one row per PS3
button, labelled with what that button does in GT5. Click a row and press the key you want (Esc
cancels); right-click a row to give it a second key, **×** to clear it, **Reset to defaults** to start
over. A key that's already used moves to the row you picked. Or put it in `GT5\settings.bat` (or
`play.bat`) yourself, `button:key` pairs split by commas:

```bat
set "PS3_KEYS=cross:W,square:Space,l2:Q,r2:E,circle:LAlt"
```

That one is W = accelerate, Space = brake, Q / E = shift down / up, Left Alt = handbrake. A bound
button takes only its new keys, and a key you bind stops doing its old job (above, W no longer works
the headlights and Z no longer accelerates). Two keys for one button: `cross:W/Up`; no key: `l1:none`.
With nothing set, the keys above are unchanged. On Linux the same line goes in `GT5/settings.sh`:
`export PS3_KEYS="cross:W,square:Space,l2:Q,r2:E,circle:LAlt"` (letters are where they are on a US
keyboard there).

- **Buttons:** `cross` `circle` `square` `triangle` `l1` `r1` `l2` `r2` `l3` `r3` `start` `select`,
  the D-pad `up` `down` `left` `right`, and the sticks pushed all the way: `lstick_up` `lstick_down`
  `lstick_left` `lstick_right` `rstick_up` `rstick_down` `rstick_left` `rstick_right`.
- **Keys:** `A`-`Z`, `0`-`9`, `F1`-`F24`, `Space` `Enter` `Tab` `Backspace` `CapsLock`, `LShift` `RShift`
  `LCtrl` `RCtrl` `LAlt` `RAlt`, `Up` `Down` `Left` `Right`, `Insert` `Delete` `Home` `End` `PageUp`
  `PageDown`, the number pad `Num0`-`Num9` `NumPlus` `NumMinus` `NumMultiply` `NumDivide` `NumDecimal`,
  `Comma` `Period` `Slash` `Semicolon` `Apostrophe` `LBracket` `RBracket` `Backslash` `Minus` `Equals`
  `Grave` `IntlBackslash` (the extra key next to Left Shift on European keyboards), and the mouse's side
  buttons `Mouse4` `Mouse5`. Any case. Esc stays the quit key. A name the game doesn't know is left out,
  with a `[keys]` line in `logs\play.err`.
- With Alt or F10 bound, the game window no longer opens its window menu (or beeps) on them; Alt+Tab and
  Alt+F4 work as before.

What each button does is GT5's own setting (in the game: **Options > Hardware > Change Button
Assignments**). Its defaults, as the game shows them:

| Button | GT5 does (default) | Default key |
|---|---|---|
| Cross | Accelerate (OK in the menus) | Z |
| Square | Brake | A |
| R2 / L2 | Shift up / Shift down | 2 / 1 |
| Circle | Handbrake (Back in the menus) | X |
| Triangle | Reverse | S |
| L1 | Rear view (look back) | Q |
| R1 | Flash and toggle high/low beam | W |
| L3 / R3 | Horn / Windscreen wipers | none |
| Select / Start | Change view / Pause | Tab / Enter |
| D-pad up | Ghost | Up |
| D-pad left/right, left stick left/right | Steering | Left / Right |
| Right stick up / down | Accelerate / Brake | none |

Left View, Right View, Flash Lights (on its own) and Toggle High/Low Beam have no pad button by
default: give one of the free buttons (D-pad down, the left stick's up/down, the right stick's
left/right) that action in GT5's Change Button Assignments, then bind a key to that button here. The
keys press the pad's buttons, so they follow whatever you set there. With mouse steering (below) GT5
still takes the pad's buttons, so the keys work the same.

A steering wheel works too, with force feedback (new; one real wheel tried so far): see the
[FAQ](#faq).

<a id="mouse-steering"></a>

**Mouse steering** (new, off unless you turn it on): tick *Steer with the mouse* on the launcher's
Controls page, or `set "PS3_MOUSE_STEER=1"` in `play.bat`. In races, move the mouse left and right to
steer: **left button = throttle, right button = brake, middle button = straighten the wheel**. The
keyboard and pads keep working alongside (Z still accelerates). While you steer, the cursor is hidden
and kept inside the window. At the menus and when paused the mouse doesn't steer: there **left click = OK
(Cross), right click = back (Circle) and the mouse wheel moves the cursor up and down**, and the keyboard
and pads work as before (`set "PS3_MOUSE_MENU=0"` leaves the mouse out of the menus). Alt+Tab frees the
mouse at any time. The game sees a steering wheel
(the same emulated G27 a real wheel uses, with its fine steering), so a real wheel isn't used while
mouse steering is on.

| Setting (launcher, or `play.bat`) | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Mouse steering speed, `PS3_MOUSE_STEER_SENS` | 100 | Percent, 1 to 1000, decimals allowed (2.5); the launcher steps it by 0.5. At 100, mouse movement about the width of a 1080p screen (at Windows' default pointer speed) turns the wheel from straight ahead to full lock; 200 is twice as quick. GT5 turns sharply on little wheel, so small movements go a long way. Windows' pointer speed and acceleration don't change it. |
| Wheel straightens by itself, `PS3_MOUSE_STEER_CENTER` | off | Once you stop moving the mouse, the wheel goes back to straight ahead, at this percent of full lock a second (the launcher's Slowly / Medium / Quickly are 50 / 100 / 200). Off: it stays where you left it. |

## 📋 Current state

<p align="center">
  <img src="docs/status.png" alt="Playable: 45 to 58 fps in races on an i9-14900KF and RTX 4070 Ti SUPER" width="100%">

board (tested rig, what works, what's being worked on, known issues, recent changes) is in
