<a id="feedback"></a>

## 🏁 Try it, then tell me how it went

If you own the game, please set it up and play. Every result helps decide what gets fixed next,
whether it runs great, half works, or doesn't build at all. Laptops, integrated graphics and AMD cards
especially: the port was tuned on one desktop with an NVIDIA card.

| You want to... | Go here |
|---|---|
| Say how it went (takes two minutes, mostly quick picks) | [Tried it: here's how it went](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/issues/new?template=1-tried-it.yml) |
| Report something broken | [Something's broken](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/issues/new?template=2-problem.yml) |
| Ask for a change | [Suggest a change](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/issues/new?template=3-idea.yml) |
| Post quick results, screenshots of it running, or ask for help | [Discussions](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/discussions/1) |
| Chat, get help live, share results | **[The Workshop Discord](https://discord.gg/9cVPS7r5Ha)**: #gt5-help, #gt5-test-reports, #gt5-chat (I'm **mormonftp** there) |

<a id="faq"></a>

## ❓ FAQ

| Question | Short answer |
|---|---|
| Steering wheels? | 🧪 New. First real wheel: a Genius Speed Wheel 3 Vibration (`0458:3017`, tested by brocolison, [#29](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/pull/29)) attaches as an emulated G27; since 13 Nov it's found by itself and its one-axis pedals work as throttle and brake (a full race on v0.1.39). Logitech, Thrustmaster and Fanatec wheels are picked up by themselves but still untried: [wheel owners wanted](#faq) |
| Force feedback? | 🧪 New, with wheel support, also untried on a real wheel |
| Widescreen (16:9)? | ✅ Yes, GT5 is a 16:9 game |
| Ultrawide (21:9, 32:9)? | ✅ New: a wider view, with the HUD kept 16:9 in the middle |
| Wider cockpit view, seat position? | ✅ New: the launcher's Game > Cockpit view ([more](#cockpit-view)) |
| Which controllers? | ✅ DualSense, DualShock 4, Xbox pads, keyboard; new: [keys of your choice](#keyboard-keys), [steering with the mouse](#mouse-steering) |
| US copy (BCUS98114)? | ✅ Yes, players have raced on it |
| Version 1.02, or a game update (2.xx)? | 🧪 New: game updates run: 2.17 (the last) tested on the US and European releases, 2.01 on the Asian one, 2.11 with the Master Mod on the US one by a player ([how to set one up](#game-updates)); 1.02 untried |
| Settings without editing files? | ✅ New: the [launcher](#launcher) |
| Full screen? | ✅ New: borderless full screen in the launcher (Alt+Enter is switched off since v0.1.17: it used to freeze the picture) |
| Vulkan instead of DirectX 12? | 🧪 The launcher's Display > Renderer: built in, slower than DirectX 12 for now ([more](#faq)) |
| Higher than 1080p (4K)? | ⚠️ The game's top mode is its 1080p one (races drawn at 1728x972), scaled up to your window; drawing above that isn't there yet |
| Japanese or Asian release (BCJS, BCAS)? | ✅ Hong Kong / Asia (BCAS20108) runs, reported by a player, and its disc 01.00 and update 2.01 race in tests too; Japanese untried, please report |
| Slow PC or laptop? | 🛠️ Laptops now use their dedicated graphics card. On most PCs the CPU sets the pace (the game's own threads), so the launcher's **Speed: 30 fps** rarely helps: it's for a graphics card at its limit. **On a laptop:** plug it in and set Windows' power mode to *Best performance* (and the maker's performance mode, e.g. in HP Command Center or Lenovo Vantage): a tester's i5-1135G7 ran into its power limit 88% of the time, which held its cores at 2.9 GHz instead of 4.2, while its graphics were only 30% busy. Speed-ups for 4-6 core CPUs are being worked on |
| Linux? | 🧪 New and early: a [native Linux build](#linux). First test (no graphics card) reached the race start; races on a real GPU untested |
| Steam Deck, Proton, Wine? | 🟡 Steam Deck: the Linux build in a distrobox runs (menus ~25-30 fps, races ~8-10; [Steam Deck](#steam-deck)). Proton and Wine not tried. Reports welcome |
| Android? | 🛠️ Being worked on |
| Online? | ❌ No |
| Is it legal? | ✅ No game files here: you build it from your own disc |
| Ready-made download? | ❌ No, but [GT5-Installer.bat](#install) builds it for you |
| Errors during setup? | 🛠️ Use [GT5-Installer.bat](#install), or run `setup.ps1` (see below) |
| Black screen, `draws: 0`? | 🛠️ Fixed: update; if it's still black, `GT.VOL` may be missing or in pieces (see below) |
| Clear or refresh the shaders? | ✅ New: launcher **Help > Clear the shader cache**, or double-click `ClearShaders.bat` (see below) |

**Q: Does it support steering wheels and force feedback?**

**A: Yes, new in v0.1.2, and one real wheel has been tried so far.** On a PS3, GT5 talks to its
Logitech wheels directly over USB, for both steering and force feedback. The port now plays that
part: your PC wheel appears to the game as a **Logitech G27** (900°, three pedals, paddles and an
H-shifter), and the game's force-feedback commands (the centring spring, the steering forces in a race)
are played on your wheel through DirectInput, which Logitech, Thrustmaster, Fanatec and other wheels
support. Plug the wheel in before you start the game; it's picked up by itself, and pads work as before.

What has been checked, without a wheel: the game accepts the emulated G27, a race steers from it, and
the force-feedback commands the game sends are decoded and logged.

The first real wheel (thanks to brocolison, [#29](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/pull/29)):
a **Genius Speed Wheel 3 Vibration** attaches as the G27, and the game sends it its wheel commands in a
race. It has no force feedback, and both pedals sit on one axis. Since 13 Nov the port finds it by
itself (Windows calls it a joystick, so before that it needed `set "PS3_WHEEL=0458:3017"`) and splits
that axis where it rests: one way is throttle, the other is brake. If they're the wrong way round:
`set "PS3_WHEEL_PEDALS=throttle=Yinv"`. Other wheels with pedals on one axis get the same. On v0.1.39
brocolison raced a full 16-car field with it, throttle and brake both working, with the keyboard for
the menus: GT5's menus move with the d-pad, and that wheel has none. Since 15 Nov a wheel with no d-pad
moves through the menus by itself: **at the menus, turn the rim for left / right and press the throttle
/ brake for down / up** (hold to scroll); Cross (button 1) chooses and Circle (button 3) goes back. In a
race the rim and pedals only drive. A pad or the keyboard works alongside any wheel.

What hasn't been checked: force feedback on a real wheel, including which way the forces push. So
**wheel owners are wanted**: please
[tell us how it went](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/issues/new?template=1-tried-it.yml)
(or [report a problem](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/issues/new?template=2-problem.yml)),
and attach `GT5\logs\play.err`: its `[wheel]` lines say which wheel was found, its axes, and what the
game asked of it.

If something is off, add a line to `GT5\settings.bat` (right-click it > Edit; updates replace
`play.bat`, and the launcher keeps lines you add to `settings.bat`, anywhere in it, since v0.1.86):

| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| The wheel isn't found (`play.err` lists it in a `[wheel] found` line, then says "no steering wheel found") | `set "PS3_WHEEL=<part of its name>"`, e.g. `set "PS3_WHEEL=MOZA"`. Since v0.1.113 any device with force feedback that isn't a gamepad is taken as a wheel by itself |
| The forces push the wrong way (the wheel pulls away from the centre) | `set "PS3_WHEEL_FFB_INVERT=1"` |
| Forces too strong or too weak | `set "PS3_WHEEL_FFB=60"` (percent, 0 = off) |
| Steering too quick or too slow | set your wheel's rotation to 900° in its software (G HUB, ...), or tell the port what it is: `set "PS3_WHEEL_RANGE=1080"` |
| Pedals, or the wheel's buttons, plug in with their own USB cable (a direct-drive base with separate pedals, a rim or button box of its own) | in the game, **F1** > **Controls** > **Wheel buttons and pedals**: **Pedals from** and **Buttons from** pick that device (Enter or Cross steps through the controllers found), then the rows below set its pedals and buttons by pressing them. Or in `settings.bat`: `set "PS3_WHEEL_PEDAL_DEVICE=<part of its name>"` and `set "PS3_WHEEL_BUTTON_DEVICE=<part of its name>"`, as the `[wheel] found` lines of `play.err` list them (its `VID:PID` works too). The base keeps the steering and the force feedback. Since v0.1.111 |
| The pedals are on different devices (the throttle and clutch on one, the brake on another) | in the game, on the same page, press Enter on each pedal's row and push that pedal: the pedal keeps the device it was pushed on (the row shows its name). Or in `settings.bat`, a device per pedal over `PS3_WHEEL_PEDAL_DEVICE`: `set "PS3_WHEEL_BRAKE_DEVICE=<part of its name>"` (also `PS3_WHEEL_THROTTLE_DEVICE`, `PS3_WHEEL_CLUTCH_DEVICE`; `wheel` = the wheel's own), with each pedal's axis on its own device in `PS3_WHEEL_PEDALS`. Since v0.1.113 |
| A pedal does nothing, or the wrong thing | `set "PS3_WHEEL_TRACE=1"`, press each pedal, and see which axis moves in the `[wheel] axes` lines of `play.err`; then e.g. `set "PS3_WHEEL_PEDALS=throttle=Y,brake=RZ,clutch=Z"` (add `inv` to one that works backwards: `brake=RZinv`) |
| Throttle and brake swapped on a wheel whose pedals share one axis | `set "PS3_WHEEL_PEDALS=throttle=Yinv"` (`play.err` names the shared axis: `[wheel] throttle and brake share the Y axis`) |
| A button is wrong | `set "PS3_WHEEL_BUTTONS=cross=1,circle=3,start=10"`, with button numbers as Windows' *Set up USB game controllers* window (`joy.cpl`) shows them; names: cross square circle triangle r1 l1 r2 l2 select start r3 l3 gear1..gear6 gearr plus minus dialcw dialccw, and up down left right for the d-pad |
| No d-pad on the wheel, and you'd rather move through menus with buttons | `set "PS3_WHEEL_BUTTONS=up=7,down=8"` (any spare buttons; left= and right= too). Without it, the rim and pedals move through menus on such a wheel; `set "PS3_WHEEL_MENU=off"` turns that off |
| No Start button on the wheel (to pause) | give Start a spare button: `set "PS3_WHEEL_BUTTONS=start=8"` (the defaults put Start on button 10, which smaller wheels don't have) |
| No pedals plugged in, or a broken one | a button can be a pedal: `set "PS3_WHEEL_BUTTONS=brake=4"` brakes fully while button 4 is held (`throttle=` and `clutch=` too) |
| No H-shifter, and you want reverse | `set "PS3_WHEEL_BUTTONS=gearr=6"`: holding button 6 is the shifter's R. GT5 takes it with the manual gearbox (MT): hold it and accelerate to back up, then a shift-up paddle puts you in 1st again. With the automatic gearbox GT5 ignores it |
| Several of these | one line, commas between: `set "PS3_WHEEL_BUTTONS=cross=1,circle=3,brake=4,gearr=6"`. A button given a job here loses its default one |
| The wrong device is used, or none | `set "PS3_WHEEL=G29"` (part of its name, or its `046d:c24f` VID:PID); `play.err` lists every controller it saw |
| You don't want it | `set "PS3_WHEEL=off"` |

Buttons and pedals are set up for Logitech's G29 / G923 / G920 out of the box; other wheels steer and
get force feedback the same way but may need the pedal and button lines above. Thrustmaster wheels get
Thrustmaster's pedal layout (accelerator, brake, clutch), in the control panel's normal pedal mode and in
combined mode alike; their buttons still follow the G29's numbers.

**Q: Does it support widescreen and ultrawide?**

**A: Yes, both; ultrawide is new.** GT5 is a 16:9 game, so a normal widescreen monitor (1920×1080,
2560×1440, 4K) is filled edge to edge, as on a PS3. On an ultrawide monitor (21:9 or 32:9) the game now
draws a wider picture itself: races and replays show more of the track at the sides (nothing is
stretched), the 3D scenes behind the menus widen the same way, and the HUD and menus stay a 16:9 block
in the middle of the screen. `play.bat` sets `PS3_ASPECT=auto`, the shape of your monitor; the window
opens at that shape, so maximize it or drag it to the size you like.

| In `play.bat` | What you get |
|---|---|
| `set "PS3_ASPECT=auto"` | the shape of your monitor (the default; on a 16:9 monitor nothing changes) |
| `set "PS3_ASPECT=21:9"` (or `32:9`, `3440x1440`, `2.37`) | that shape, whatever the monitor |
| `set "PS3_ASPECT=16:9"` | the PS3's own 16:9 picture, as before |
| `set "PS3_WINDOW_SIZE=2560x1080"` | the window opens at exactly that size (and shape, unless `PS3_ASPECT` says otherwise) |

The game draws 720 lines at the wider shape, as many pixels across as it needs up to 1920: about
1700×720 for 21:9, as sharp as its usual 1280×720. Shapes wider than 8:3 (32:9) are drawn at 1920×720
and spread sideways to fill the window, so they're a little softer side to side. The window title shows
the size it draws at. This works on the European release (BCES00569, disc 01.00); on any other release
the picture stays 16:9 for now, and `logs\play.err` says so in a `[widescreen]` line.

<a id="cockpit-view"></a>
**Q: Can I widen the cockpit view, or move the seat?**

**A: Yes, new: the [launcher](#launcher)'s Game page, under Cockpit view.** On a PS3 the view from
the driver's seat is fixed: GT5 shows every car's cockpit at 52.4° from the top of the screen to the
bottom, with the eye where the car's own data puts the driver. The port can widen (or narrow) that view
and move the eye forward, back, up or down. Only the cockpit view changes: the chase, bumper and roof
views and the menus stay as they are. All three are off by default, and then nothing changes.

| In `play.bat` (or `settings.bat`) | What you get |
|---|---|
| `set "PS3_COCKPIT_FOV=20"` | the cockpit view 20° wider, top to bottom (72.4° instead of 52.4°; the sides widen with it); negative is narrower |
| `set "PS3_COCKPIT_SEAT=10"` | the eye 10 cm further forward, toward the windscreen; negative moves it back |
| `set "PS3_COCKPIT_HEIGHT=5"` | the eye 5 cm higher; negative is lower |

`logs\play.err` has a `[cockpit]` line with the game's number and the new one. The in-car camera is found
by its name in the game's code, so this isn't tied to one release: tested on the European disc, and the
same camera code is in the 2.17 update and the Asian disc and 2.01.

**Q: What resolution does it render at?**

**A: GT5's own 1080p mode, as on a PS3 connected to a 1080p TV, scaled to fit your window.** Races are
drawn at 1728×972 (the game keeps a black border around them for TVs that cut off the edges), the HUD
and menus at 1920×1080. Choose it in the [launcher](#launcher) (Display, Resolution), or in `play.bat`:

| In `play.bat` | |
|---|---|
| `set "PS3_VIDEO_MODE=1080"` | the 1080p mode (the default since v0.1.12) |
| `set "PS3_VIDEO_MODE=720"` | the 720p mode, races at 1152×648: for a slow graphics chip |

On the tested rig both run at the same speed, since the CPU is the limit; on a laptop's built-in
graphics 720 may be faster, but often the CPU is the limit there too (an Iris Xe laptop's graphics were
30% busy at 1080p). (v0.1.10 had the 1080p mode on too, but its window showed only the top-left
part of the picture; v0.1.11 went back to 720 until v0.1.12 fixed it.) On an ultrawide monitor the 720p
mode draws the wider view pixel for pixel (about 1700×720), and the 1080p mode draws it into 1920×1080
and spreads it sideways. Rendering above the PS3's resolutions is on the list.

**Q: Can I use Vulkan instead of DirectX 12?**

**A: Yes: the [launcher](#launcher)'s Display > Renderer.** DirectX 12 is the port's main renderer and stays
the default. Vulkan is the renderer the Linux build and the Android work use. On Windows it's slower for
now (see the numbers in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md), 15 Nov), some effects may look different, and some
settings do nothing with it yet (render resolution, DLSS, the frame generator and multiplier, texture dumps:
the launcher greys them while Vulkan is chosen). The game is built with both renderers: setup (so the
installer) fetches the source code of SDL2 and glslang (about 60 MB, from GitHub, checked against the exact
releases) and builds them before the game's first build, and an update does the same for an install made
before that. If they can't be had (no internet at that moment, say), the game is built with DirectX 12
alone, the launcher doesn't list Vulkan, and the next update tries again. By hand: `add_vulkan.ps1
-Prepare` gets them for the next build, `add_vulkan.ps1` also rebuilds `gt5.exe` with Vulkan now, and
`add_vulkan.ps1 -Remove` builds it without (and setup and updates then leave it out until you add it
again). Vulkan's shaders are kept in `GT5\shadercache` (cleared by ClearShaders.bat with the rest).

**Q: Which controllers work?**

**A: DualSense and DualShock 4 (USB or Bluetooth), Xbox and other XInput pads, and the keyboard.** See
[Controls](#controls) for the keyboard layout. The mouse can steer in races too (off by default): see
[Mouse steering](#mouse-steering).

**Q: Can I use a US copy?**

**A: Yes.** Players have raced on the US disc. Its executable has the same layout as the European one,
and the tools find the few spots that could differ between releases in your own copy anyway (see
[Which copy of GT5](#which-copy-of-gt5)). Only ultrawide is still Europe-only.

**Q: My copy says version 1.02, or I have a game update (2.xx). Does that work? What about the Master Mod?**

**A: Game updates work now, as far as they've been tried.** 2.17, the last update, runs on the US
release (menus, GT Mode and a full 16-car Arcade race at 60 fps) and on the European one (its first-start
questions, the opening movie, Arcade and a 16-car race). The Asian release's 2.01 boots,
loads a career save and races. An update needs its executable and its data: the launcher gets and installs both, see
[Game updates](#game-updates).

**The GT5 Master Mod runs too** (Nenkai's and ddm's; 2.0.0a on Europe 2.11 on the test PC, and players
run it on the US release): its menus and news, its SELECT debug menu, Arcade's Master level and races.
Bring the game to update 2.11, then the launcher installs the mod's zip by itself: see
[Game mods](#game-mods). The update's data with the disc's executable gives a black screen before the
main menu, so the launcher builds the game for the update right after installing it.

The Asian 2.17 hasn't been tried yet: each update can change the game's SPU programs again, so please
report what setup prints (`version_addrs.py`'s lines and `SPU jobs found in EBOOT.elf: N of 15`; 2.17
shows 13 of 15 plus 3 of its own, and that is complete). Another disc version, like 1.02, hasn't been tried either; the same lines tell us how
close it is.

**Q: Does online work?**

**A: No.** GT5's online services were shut down, and the port doesn't connect to anything.

**Q: Is there a ready-to-go build I can just download?**

**A: No, and there can't be.** A built `gt5.exe` contains GT5's own code converted for PC, so
sharing one would be sharing the game itself. That's what gets projects like this taken down, and
it's why this one only works from your own disc. Please don't ask for builds or share them. What we
can do is make building easy: [GT5-Installer.bat](#install) asks for your game and Sony's PS3 system
software file and does all the rest, ending with a shortcut on your desktop. If you get stuck, post its output in the
[discussions](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/discussions) and someone will help.

**Q: I get errors like "venv\Scripts\python.exe is not recognized" or "cannot find analysis\version.json". What's wrong?**

**A: Setup hasn't finished, so the tools that later steps use aren't there yet.** `venv` is the Python
environment `setup.ps1` makes. `analysis\version.json` is made by the build itself from your EBOOT.elf,
so it isn't a file you add. Open PowerShell in the `gt5-recomp` folder (the one with `setup.ps1`, not
`GT5\scripts`) and run `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File setup.ps1`. It installs what's
missing, lists any of your files that are missing or in the wrong place, and once everything is there
it generates and builds the game for you. If Python itself is missing (the download of the port's own copy failed), run `setup.ps1` again or install Python 3.11 or newer
from python.org with "Add python.exe to PATH" ticked, then run setup again.

**Q: The game starts but the window stays black, and the title says `draws: 0`. What's wrong?**

**A: Builds made before 10 November did that; it's fixed.** Setup didn't compile the game's SPU code
(the PS3's co-processors), so the game waited forever for work that never ran. Update and it's
rebuilt with that code: in the `gt5-recomp` folder run `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1`
(or double-click `setup.bat`; if you downloaded the ZIP, download it again and move your `input`
and `vfs` folders into the new `GT5` folder). While it builds, it prints
`SPU jobs found in EBOOT.elf: N of 15`.

**Still black on a new version?** Look in `GT5\logs\play.err` for `open FAIL '/dev_bdvd/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/GT.VOL'`.
That means the game's data file, `GT.VOL` (about 12 GB), isn't in `GT5\vfs\PS3_GAME\USRDIR`. Dumps made
to a FAT32 USB drive split it into pieces (`GT.VOL.66600`, `GT.VOL.66601`, ...); since v0.1.19 they're
joined automatically by `Update.bat`, setup and the launcher's **Play**. If there's no `GT.VOL` at all,
copy it from `PS3_GAME\USRDIR` in your dump. Otherwise attach the whole `GT5\logs\play.err` to a
[problem report](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/issues/new?template=2-problem.yml), with
that line.

**Q: The picture froze on one screen, but the menu sounds still react when I press buttons. What now?**

**A: Restart the game, and send us the log of the frozen run.** The game kept running; only the picture
stopped. Before v0.1.17, **Alt+Enter** always did this (Windows switched the window to exclusive full
screen behind the port's back); it's switched off now, so update, and use the launcher's **borderless
full screen** for full screen. If it froze without Alt+Enter, the graphics driver most likely reset or
refused a frame. (A frozen opening movie at the first start, the Earth from space, was another cause;
since v0.1.21 that movie is skipped.) Attach that run's log to
[issue #10](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/issues/10), with your graphics card: it's
`GT5\logs\play.err` until you start the game again, then `GT5\logs\play.prev.err` (each start keeps the
previous log under that name; builds before v0.1.10 didn't, so there copy `play.err` before restarting). A
line in it starting with `[d3d-fail]` says what failed, and that decides the fix. If no new picture came
for 8 seconds, a `[HANG]` report in the same log says what each busy thread was doing at that moment. If
it kept drawing but crawled (under 6 frames a second for 6 seconds), a `[SLOW]` report says the same.

**Q: How do I attach my log to an issue? GitHub won't take it.**

**A: Let the launcher make the file.** **Help** > **Save logs for a report** (or **Save a report** in the
line that comes up after a crash or a freeze) puts a `.zip` on your desktop that GitHub takes, with your
Windows user name, PC name and folders taken out; drag it into the issue. By hand: GitHub refuses `.err`
files, so rename `GT5\logs\play.err` to `play.err.txt` (or put it in a `.zip`); it names your Windows user
in its paths. The installer's `GT5-Installer.log` attaches as it is. For a
graphics problem, also say the mode, the track and its time or weather (for example Arcade, Chamonix,
snow): some problems show on one track and not another.

**Q: How do I clear the shader cache?**

**A: Launcher, Help, Clear the shader cache, or double-click `ClearShaders.bat` in your install
folder (close the game first).** The game turns each of GT5's shaders into a PC shader the first time
it's needed and keeps the result in `GT5\scratch\rsx_shader_cache_v2` (on Linux `GT5/shadercache`), so
the next visit doesn't stutter. Clearing it frees the space (it grows with every car and track you
see) and gives a fresh start; the first visit to each menu, car and track then stutters again for a
while. It can't fix or cause a wrong picture: a cached shader is only used for exactly the same
source, so a game update, a mod or a new version of the port never picks up an old one by mistake.
Saves, settings and game files are not touched. On Linux, delete `GT5/shadercache` by hand.

<a id="shaders"></a>

**Q: What are "Preparing shaders" and "Asynchronous shader loading"?**

**A: Two ways of keeping new shaders from stopping the game.** The first time a car, track or menu is
drawn, its shaders are built for your graphics card, and the picture used to pause for that.
- **Preparing shaders:** after an update, or after a graphics setting that changes the shaders (DLSS or
  frame generation on or off, Shadows, the render resolution), the launcher first builds everything your
  game has drawn before, plus a general stand-in, in a short step before the game starts. Updates do the
  same. Details are in `GT5\logs\prepare.log`.
- **Asynchronous shader loading** (Display, **On** by default, DirectX 12): a part whose shader isn't
  ready yet is drawn at once with the stand-in and switched over when its own is done, instead of the
  picture pausing. On a PC that has never played, about one part in fifty can still be missing for a
  moment in the first race. **Off** waits for each new shader, as before. Vulkan always builds new
  shaders in the background, so it has no such row.

<a id="saves"></a>

**Q: Where are my saves? Can I bring a save over from RPCS3?**

**A: In a folder named after your disc, inside `GT5\gamedata`:**

```
GT5\gamedata\dev_hdd0\home\00000001\savedata\BCUS98114-GAME     (US disc)
GT5\gamedata\dev_hdd0\home\00000001\savedata\BCES00569-GAME     (European disc)
```

That's the same place a PS3 and RPCS3 keep it, so a save comes over by copying that **whole folder**:
1. Close the game, and keep a copy of the port's own `<title ID>-GAME` folder if you have one.
2. In RPCS3's own folder, open `dev_hdd0\home\00000001\savedata` and copy the `<title ID>-GAME` folder
   (and `<title ID>-BKUP`, its backup, if there is one) into the port's `savedata` folder above.

Copy the folder itself, not the files inside it: files put straight into `savedata` aren't seen. The title
ID has to match your disc (a European save doesn't show up in the US game, and the other way round).
Updates never touch `GT5\gamedata`.

**Q: Is this legal? Do I need the game?**

**A: You need your own copy of GT5, and nothing from the game is in this repository.** It holds only
code written for the port. You build the game yourself from your own disc, and builds must never be
shared (see below).

<a id="linux"></a>

## 🐧 Linux

A native x86-64 build using Vulkan and SDL2. See [Requirements](#requirements) for hardware and
build dependencies, and [Which copy of GT5](#which-copy-of-gt5) for supported game releases.

**Experimental:** it runs, races included, on a Radeon RX 7900 XTX, but with picture bugs there that
are still open. See [Linux testing status](#linux-testing-status).

### Set it up

After cloning, run all commands from `gt5-recomp`. Replace `/path/to/...` with your own paths.

**1. Install the build dependencies**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp
cd gt5-recomp
bash setup.sh --install-deps
```

`--install-deps` installs packages using apt, dnf, pacman or zypper and may ask for your password.
Without it, setup prints the install command. Two `[missing]` game-file entries are normal on
the first run: the next step supplies them.

**2. Copy the game data**

Copy the whole `PS3_GAME` folder from your disc dump:

```bash
mkdir -p GT5/vfs/PS3_GAME
cp -a "/path/to/your/disc/PS3_GAME/." GT5/vfs/PS3_GAME/
```

Setup unlocks the game's executable (`PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN`) into `GT5/input/EBOOT.elf` by itself,
with the port's own tool: no RPCS3 and no PS3 system software file are needed.
For a game update, follow [Game updates](#game-updates-2xx) to keep the executable and data matched.

**3. Check and build**

Check these paths exist, without an extra `PS3_GAME` folder nested inside:

```text
GT5/vfs/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN
GT5/vfs/PS3_GAME/PARAM.SFO
GT5/vfs/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/GT.VOL
```

Check the files and build only if the check succeeds:

```bash
bash setup.sh --no-build && bash setup.sh
```

If setup reports `[missing]`, follow its message and rerun the command.
The first build takes about 20 to 60 minutes and produces `GT5/build-linux/gt5`.

### Play

```
bash GT5/play.sh
```

Logs go to `GT5/logs` (`play.err` is the one to attach to a report). Settings: the switches in
`GT5/play.sh` (full screen, resolution, watch mode), or your own `export NAME=value` lines in
`GT5/settings.sh`, which win and survive updates.

Full screen, kept across updates (thanks, melroy89):

```bash
echo 'export PS3RECOMP_VK_FULLSCREEN=1' >> GT5/settings.sh
```

Or just once: `PS3RECOMP_VK_FULLSCREEN=1 bash GT5/play.sh`.

Controls: any controller SDL2 knows (DualSense, DualShock 4, Xbox, 8BitDo, the Steam Deck's own
controls through Steam Input), or the keyboard as on Windows: Z = Cross, X = Circle, A = Square,
S = Triangle, Q/W = L1/R1, 1/2 = L2/R2, arrows = D-pad, Enter = Start, Tab = Select, Esc = quit.
[Your own keys](#keyboard-keys) work too, with `export PS3_KEYS=...` in `GT5/settings.sh`.

### Updating

```
git pull
bash setup.sh
```

It re-patches ps3recomp, re-generates the game code only when the new version needs it, and rebuilds
only what changed. Your saves (`GT5/gamedata`, `GT5/hdd0`) and game files stay.

### Linux testing status

**How far it's been tested (12 Nov 2026):** on Ubuntu 24.04 with no graphics card at all (Mesa's
software Vulkan driver, on a virtual display), so speed and the picture on a real GPU are untested.
`setup.sh` ran the whole setup from a fresh clone: tools, ps3recomp, the game code (the same code the
Windows setup generates, checked file by file) and the build. The game boots, does the first-start
screens and saves them, and reaches the top menu with its 3D scene, GT Mode (My Home), and Arcade
through track select, car select (the 3D car), colour and the pre-race screen with the 3D track.
**The race itself stayed black** in that test. The same race does draw with this renderer on a real
graphics card (checked on Windows), so that was the software driver.

**First test on a real graphics card (13 Nov 2026, melroy89, [#20](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/issues/20)):**
Linux Mint 22.3, Threadripper 7960X, Radeon RX 7900 XTX. `setup.sh` and the build went through, the
menus draw correctly, an Xbox controller works out of the box, and there were no crashes or frame drops.
Still wrong there at first: races drew in the top half of the picture, the intro's 3D scene looked
white, and sound effects played late. The squashed races and the late sound are fixed since 13 Nov
(see the changelog); the white city is how GT5 draws that scene.

**Second report (14 Nov 2026, melroy89, v0.1.43, the same PC):** races and licence tests run, mostly
at a steady 60 frames per second. Wrong there: freezes of 0.3 to 0.7 s (once 1.7 s) whenever something
new came on screen, fixed since 14 Nov (new shaders now build in the background); car bodies whose
lighting flickers; in the B-2 licence intro on Tokyo R246, flickering parts and a road you can see
through; most textures missing in a braking licence test; a dark title-screen scene. None of those
last four showed on an NVIDIA card here, so they may be specific to AMD's driver: being looked into
on #20.

If you have a Linux PC with a graphics card, please
[tell us how it goes](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/issues/new?template=1-tried-it.yml)
(attach `GT5/logs/play.err`).

### Not there yet on Linux

- No launcher and no installer: setup is `setup.sh`, settings are in `play.sh` / `settings.sh`.
- Steering wheels and force feedback (Windows only so far).
- Ultrawide (21:9, 32:9): the Linux renderer draws 16:9.
- The Vulkan renderer is younger than the Windows one; picture bugs the Windows build fixed may
  still show here. Please report them with a screenshot.
- The first time a car, track or menu needs new shaders, something can be missing for a few frames
  while they build (instead of the whole game freezing). `export PS3RECOMP_VK_ASYNC_SHADERS=0` in
  `GT5/settings.sh` goes back to freezing.
- The title screen's white model city is meant to be white (the Windows build draws it the same),
  but its depth-of-field blur and darker roads may still be missing on Linux.
- Movies and the on-screen keyboard (naming a save, Course Maker) are untried on Linux.

<a id="steam-deck"></a>

### Steam Deck

**Tried on a Steam Deck OLED** (SteamOS 3.9, update 2.17 with DLC, the build in an Arch distrobox;
the Ubuntu box below is the same route): it builds, boots, races and plays sound in time. More reports
welcome. The route is the Linux build in a distrobox. SteamOS keeps its system files read-only, so `setup.sh` can't install the build tools there
(it says so and stops). Distrobox, part of SteamOS 3.5 and later, gives you an Ubuntu container that
shares your home folder, screen, sound and graphics. In desktop mode, in Konsole:

```
distrobox create --name gt5 --image ubuntu:24.04
distrobox enter gt5
git clone https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp
cd gt5-recomp
bash setup.sh --install-deps
```

(`sudo` inside the box needs no password.) Then copy your files in as above and run `bash setup.sh`
again, still inside the box. Keep `gt5-recomp` on the internal drive: it needs about 30 GB. The first
setup is slow on the Deck's 4 cores: expect one to two hours for generating the code and building
(an estimate; it runs one compile per 2 GB of free memory).

To play from Game Mode: in desktop mode, Steam > *Add a Non-Steam Game*, browse to
`/usr/bin/distrobox-enter`, and in its properties set the launch options to
`-n gt5 -- bash /home/deck/gt5-recomp/GT5/play.sh` (setup prints the exact line). Started from
Steam, the Deck's controls reach the game as a controller; from a terminal they act as mouse and
keyboard. Leave full screen off in `play.sh`: Game Mode fits the 16:9 window onto the 16:10 screen
with bars, while full screen would stretch it.

Play from Game Mode. In desktop mode Steam's desktop controller layout turns the Deck's buttons into
keys, and the menu button becomes Esc, which quits the game.

What to expect, measured on the Deck: the main menu at about 25-30 frames a second and races at about
8-10 (100-130 ms a frame). GT5's pace is set by the CPU: in a race the GPU is mostly idle (locking its
clock at 1600 MHz changed nothing), and the game's own threads set the frame rate. The first races
after an update recompile their shaders once and stutter. B-Spec races and replays in watch mode
(`export LD_WATCH=1` in `GT5/settings.sh`) are the realistic use. Suspend and resume are untested:
quit the game first.

The Windows build under **Proton** is untried too. Direct3D 12 would go through vkd3d-proton; start
`GT5\play.bat` (it sets the game's switches), not `gt5.exe` on its own.

<a id="requirements"></a>

## 🧰 Requirements

- **Windows:** Windows 10 or 11 (x64) and a Direct3D 12 graphics card. The compiler is the
  [standalone tools](#no-visual-studio) (what the installer fetches), or a Visual Studio 2022 you already
  have with *Desktop development with C++*, *C++ Clang tools for Windows* and a Windows SDK.
- **Linux (experimental):** an x86-64 distribution with FFmpeg 6.1 or newer (such as Ubuntu 24.04
  or Linux Mint 22), and a Vulkan-compatible GPU with a Vulkan driver. Follow the
  [Linux setup](#linux) to install build dependencies and prepare the game.
- An AVX2-capable CPU and 16 GB of RAM for the first build.
- Git and Python are not needed: `setup.ps1` fetches the port's own copies into `tools\git` (MinGit,
  only when the PC has no Git) and `tools\python` (python.org's 3.11.9, 17 MB) and runs every tool on
  them; nothing is installed in Windows.
- About 25 GB free on Windows or 30 GB on Linux, including about 17 GB of game files.
- Your own GT5 disc (BCES00569, BCUS98114 or BCAS20108) and the means to dump it. Nothing else of Sony's:
  no PS3 system software file, and no RPCS3 (since v0.1.115).

<a id="pc-check"></a>

### A processor that calculates wrongly

The game is built on your PC by long calculations, and they assume every processor gives the right
answer. On some PCs one or two logical processors don't (seen on a 14th generation Intel desktop
processor: two of its 28 failed a fixed job most of the time, the other 26 never). The signs are tools
stopping with errors that make no sense, compiler crashes, or a game that misbehaves.

Setup checks for this before it generates and builds the game: a small fixed job runs on every
processor, and any processor that gives an error or a different result is left out of the whole install.
You are told which. The result is kept for 30 days in `.gt5\pc-check.json`. To run the check by hand:

```
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File pc-check.ps1
```

Leaving processors out gets the game built, but the PC still has the fault, and other programs (and the
game itself) can hit it. What usually cures it: the newest BIOS for your motherboard (for Intel 13th and
14th generation processors it carries Intel's fix), the processor maker's default settings in the BIOS
instead of the motherboard's "performance" ones, memory at its standard speed, and current drivers.

<a id="no-visual-studio"></a>

### No Visual Studio needed

`GT5-Installer.bat` never installs or changes Visual Studio. When the PC has no Visual Studio with the
Clang tools and a Windows SDK, it runs `get-toolchain.ps1`, which puts the same compiler tools in the
install folder (`tools\toolchain`). By hand, the script puts them in one folder you choose, on any drive.
In the `gt5-recomp` folder, in PowerShell:

```
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File get-toolchain.ps1
```

- It suggests a `toolchain` folder next to `gt5-recomp`. Type another folder to put it somewhere else,
  for example on a second drive.
- It downloads about 1.5 GB and keeps about 1.5 GB: LLVM 19.1.5 (clang-cl), CMake and Ninja from
  their official GitHub pages, and Microsoft's C++ libraries and Windows SDK, fetched from Microsoft by
  [mmozeiko's portable-msvc.py](https://gist.github.com/mmozeiko). Every download is checked.
- Microsoft's part comes under Microsoft's licence. The script shows you the link and only goes on when
  you type `yes`.
- No administrator rights, and nothing is installed into Windows. To remove the tools, delete the folder.

Then run `setup.ps1` as usual (it also offers to run `get-toolchain.ps1` when it finds no Visual Studio).
When there's no Visual Studio, the build uses these tools.

<a id="which-copy-of-gt5"></a>

## Which copy of GT5

Use the Blu-ray disc's own executable, `PS3_GAME\USRDIR\EBOOT.BIN`, application version **01.00**
(the `APP_VER` in `PS3_GAME\PARAM.SFO`), or the executable of a game update together with that
update's data (see [Game updates](#game-updates)).

| Release | Title ID | Status | SHA-1 of the disc's files |
|---|---|---|---|
| Europe / PAL | **BCES00569** | tested | `EBOOT.BIN` `1FFABF4C029CF3099579B73425C91C1FD48CAFCA`, decrypted `EBOOT.elf` `1535B865EC7DD58E7704B378B8621532ECF844E1` |
| North America | **BCUS98114** | works (run by players) | decrypted `EBOOT.elf` `40126D2D14B0A95B9601BB11E3A6E778186067AC` |
| Hong Kong / Asia | **BCAS20108** | tested (and run by a player) | decrypted `EBOOT.elf` `49A3662D4B541BB4E0C2E72D2602F89FEB710E71` |
| Hong Kong / Asia, update 2.01 | **BCAS20108** | tested: menus, career save, Arcade race | decrypted update `EBOOT.elf` `96DEA35B194AA80E993CAD9EBE42E96072F3A3D5` |
| North America, update 2.17 | **BCUS98114** | tested: menus, GT Mode, 16-car Arcade race | decrypted update `EBOOT.elf` `12EF249F9B95591E08251AC85F103B1451DA23BF` |
| Europe, update 2.17 | **BCES00569** | tested: first-start questions, opening movie, 16-car Arcade race | decrypted update `EBOOT.elf` `306F86C62B9F03041C903BE96AC59E5C3F130452` |

Almost everything in the port works for any release, because the recompiled code is generated from
your own executable. Only three things are tied to where the code sits in one executable: the end of
the code, the game's setjmp/longjmp routines, and one jump table the game builds while it runs.
`GT5\scripts\relift.ps1` starts by running `GT5\scripts\version_addrs.py`, which finds all three in
your EBOOT by what the code looks like, not by address, and prints your EBOOT's SHA-1:

- If every line is found, carry on: your release should work.
- If it prints `NOT FOUND`, that release differs in those places. Please open an issue with that
  output (the text only, never any game file).

Check a file's hash with `Get-FileHash <file> -Algorithm SHA1` in PowerShell.

<a id="game-updates"></a>

### Game updates (2.xx)

A game update brings a new executable and data the game reads from the PS3's hard disk (for 2.01,
about 2.2 GB of files in `PDIPFS`). The port needs both.

<a id="game-version"></a>

**The easiest way: pick the version (since v0.1.112).** In the launcher, *Help > Game version and DLC*
shows the version your game is at and lets you change it to any other: **1.00** (the disc), any official
update up to **2.17** (the newest), or **2.11** for the [Master Mod](#game-mods). The launcher downloads the
updates it needs straight from Sony's update server (the same packages a PS3 gets), checks each one
against Sony's own list (size and SHA-1, kept in `GT5\scripts\gt5_updates.txt`), installs them and builds the
game for that version (about 20 minutes once they're downloaded; 1.05 to 2.17 is about 4.6 GB in all).
- Going to an older version installs the updates from 1.05 on again; going to 1.00 removes the update data.
  If anything fails, the game is put back as it was.
- Downloaded packages are kept in `downloads\game-updates` in the install folder for the next change (delete
  them if you need the space).
- The packages are checked and unpacked by the port's own tool (no RPCS3). Your saves aren't touched.
- Not while a game mod is installed: remove the mod first (an update would overwrite part of it).
- Europe (`BCES00569`), North America (`BCUS98114`), Asia (`BCAS20108`) and Japan (`BCJS30001`).
- Without the launcher: `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File GT5\scripts\game_version.ps1 -To 2.11`.

DLC is bought content, so it can't be downloaded this way: see [DLC](#dlc) (the same window has a button for
your DLC packages).

**From your update's `.pkg` files (since v0.1.45):** in the launcher, *Help > Install a game
update or DLC (.pkg)*, and pick the update packages. Pick all of them from the first one (1.05, 1.06
... up to the version you want): updates install only in order, and the ones already installed are
skipped. This runs `GT5\scripts\install_pkg.ps1`. It checks each package, unpacks it into `GT5\hdd0` and
unlocks the new executable, all with the port's own tool (no RPCS3, no other window): steps 1 and 2 below.
The launcher then builds the game for the update by itself (step 3, about 20 minutes; done by script
instead, run `Update.bat` or `setup.bat` afterwards). Without the launcher:
`powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File GT5\scripts\install_pkg.ps1 <folder with the .pkg files>`.

By hand:

1. **The update's files** go into `GT5\hdd0\game\<title ID>` (for example `GT5\hdd0\game\BCES00569`),
   all of them, `USRDIR\EBOOT.BIN` included. Either copy that folder from your PS3's hard disk
   (`dev_hdd0\game\<title ID>`), or unpack each package in order with the port's own tool:
   `venv\Scripts\python GT5\scripts\ps3_unlock.py pkg <the .pkg> GT5\hdd0\game`.
   Without the data the game starts, but Arcade Mode has no courses to choose.
2. **The executable**: `setup.ps1` (and `Update.bat`) unlocks the update's `EBOOT.BIN` from that folder into
   `GT5\input\EBOOT.elf` by itself and keeps the disc's as `GT5\input\EBOOT.disc-01.00.elf`.
   The two must match: with the update's data but the disc's executable, the game stops before the main
   menu (a black screen).
3. Run `setup.ps1` again: it lifts and builds the new executable (about an hour).

If your disc folder's `PS3_GAME\PARAM.SFO` already says version 02.xx, it holds the update's
executable, but usually not its data: step 1 is still needed. `GT5-Installer.bat` doesn't do these
steps; the launcher's *Help > Game version and DLC* does.

<a id="game-mods"></a>

### Game mods (the GT5 Master Mod)

A mod that comes as a zip of `PDIPFS` files, like the [GT5 Master Mod](https://gt5mm.gt-mod.site/),
installs straight into the port. No RPCS3 step is needed for the mod itself.

1. **Bring the game to the update the mod needs.** The Master Mod needs **2.11 exactly**, not higher and
   not lower: in the launcher, *Help > Game version and DLC*, pick 2.11 ([Game version](#game-version)), or
   install the update packages from 1.05 up to 2.11 as in [Game updates](#game-updates). The launcher builds
   the game for the update right after (about 20 minutes).
2. **Download the mod's zip for your release of the game** from the mod's own site: the one named for
   your game's ID (Europe `BCES00569`, North America `BCUS98114`, and so on). The game's files are locked
   per release, so another release's zip doesn't work.
3. In the launcher: *Help > Install a game mod (.zip)*, and pick the zip. Without the launcher:
   `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File GT5\scripts\install_mod.ps1 <the zip>`.

What it does: it checks that the zip fits the installed game (the Master Mod's zip brings the game's two
original files it was made from; they must be the same as yours, so a wrong version or region is refused
before anything is changed), then copies the mod's `PDIPFS` files into
`GT5\hdd0\game\<title ID>\USRDIR\PDIPFS`. Nothing in the zip is run. The game files it replaces are kept
in `USRDIR\PDIPFS_before_mod`, and `USRDIR\mod_installed.txt` lists what was added.

- **The first start afterwards takes longer**, and the first visit to each track or car can stutter for a
  few seconds: the game rebuilds its lists and copies files from the disc again.
- **To remove it:** the same button (it reads *Remove the game mod* while one is installed), or
  `install_mod.ps1 -Remove`. The game's own files come back. A save made with the mod may not load
  without it, so keep a copy of your save from before.
- Extras inside a mod's zip (the Master Mod's `Debug_Cam_Addon` folder) aren't installed by this.
- Checked with the Master Mod 2.0.0a on Europe 2.11: its menus and news, Arcade's Master level, a 16-car
  race and a time trial at Rome. The North America zip is checked the same way by the script; the game
  itself with it hasn't been run here (no North America disc on the test PC).

<a id="dlc"></a>

### DLC

GT5's DLC works once it's installed, with update 2.17 (tested on the US release): the Racing Car
Pack, Car Packs 2 and 3, the 2012 car packs, the Course Pack, Speed Test, Twin Ring Motegi and the
gift cars. Each DLC item is a small "voucher" file the game unlocks it from; the cars and tracks
themselves come with the updates. Only DLC you bought unlocks: a voucher opens only with the key of
its licence.

1. **The vouchers**: pick the DLC `.pkg` files in the launcher's *Help > Install a game update or DLC
   (.pkg)*, which puts them in place. Or use your PS3's hard disk and copy `dev_hdd0\game\<title ID>\USRDIR\vou` to
   `GT5\hdd0\game\<title ID>\USRDIR\vou`.
2. **The licence keys**: for each voucher, the 16-byte key of its licence, saved as
   `GT5\hdd0\home\00000001\exdata\<content ID>.rifkey`. The content ID is the name of the licence
   file (`<content ID>.rap`), for example `UP9000-BCUS98114_00-TWINRINGMOTEGI00`. The key comes from your
   licence; this repository holds no keys and doesn't make it for you.
3. Start the game. The gift cars arrive in the garage at the first start ("The following Gift Cars have
   been added to your garage"); the packs are in **Downloadable Content** on the main menu, under
   Purchased Content, each with *Install*. That screen wants a PSN sign-in: when `play.bat` finds
   vouchers, it tells the game it's signed in, with a local profile and no connection to anything.

A voucher without its key stays locked, and the game shows nothing for it.

<a id="setup"></a>

## 🚦 Setup

**`setup.ps1` does almost everything.** Run it as often as you like. Each time it does what's still
to do, checks your files, and tells you exactly what's missing and how to fix it. Once everything is
in place it builds the game for you. You never need to run the scripts in `GT5\scripts` yourself.

1. Install the tools from [Requirements](#-requirements): Git (Python is fetched by `setup.ps1`; if you would rather use your own: 3.11 or newer, tick "Add
   python.exe to PATH"), and Visual Studio 2022 with C++ and the Clang tools.
2. Get the port and run setup once. In PowerShell:

   ```
   git clone https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp
   cd gt5-recomp
   powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File setup.ps1
   ```

   Or, without typing commands: after the `git clone`, double-click **`setup.bat`** in the
   `gt5-recomp` folder. It runs the same setup and keeps the window open so you can read the result.

   It fetches and patches ps3recomp, makes the Python environment and downloads FFmpeg. Then it lists
   the game files you still need to add, marked `[missing]`. Use Git rather than the ZIP download, so
   you can update later.
3. Add your own game files (setup checks each one and catches the usual mistakes):
   - **Game data:** dump your own GT5 disc (BCES00569 or BCUS98114) and copy its `PS3_GAME` folder to
     `GT5\vfs`, so that `GT5\vfs\PS3_GAME\USRDIR` exists.
   - **The executable:** nothing to do. Setup unlocks your disc's `PS3_GAME\USRDIR\EBOOT.BIN` into
     `GT5\input\EBOOT.elf` by itself, with the port's own tool (no RPCS3). The PS3's system software is
     not needed.
4. Run setup again (the same command, or double-click `setup.bat`):

   ```
   powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File setup.ps1
   ```

   When nothing is missing, it generates the game code from your EBOOT.elf (about 10 minutes) and
   builds `gt5.exe` (20 to 50 minutes the first time, depending on your PC).
5. Play: `GT5\play.bat`. Saves go to `GT5\gamedata`; logs go to `GT5\logs`.

If setup stops with an error, post its whole output in the
[discussions](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/discussions) or the
[problem form](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/issues/new?template=2-problem.yml).

When it is set up, the folder looks like this (the parts you add are marked):

```
gt5-recomp\
  setup.bat, setup.ps1, update.ps1, README.md, LICENSE
  ps3recomp\          fetched and patched by setup.ps1
  ffmpeg\             fetched by setup.ps1
  venv\               made by setup.ps1
  GT5\
    input\            made by setup.ps1: EBOOT.elf, unlocked from your disc's EBOOT.BIN
    vfs\PS3_GAME\     YOU ADD: the PS3_GAME folder from your disc
    generated\, src\gen\, analysis\   made by setup.ps1 from your EBOOT.elf
    build\            made by setup.ps1 (gt5.exe)
    hdd0\, logs\      made when you play
```

Optional, for speed: GT5 runs many SPU jobs. They run in an interpreter until they are captured and
recompiled. Run the game once with `SPU_DUMP_MISS=<GT5 folder>\analysis\spu_miss` set, then run
`python GT5\scripts\lift_spu_jobs.py` and build again (see the comments at the top of that script).

<a id="switches"></a>

## ⚙️ Switches

`play.bat` sets the usual environment variables, then reads `settings.bat` (what the launcher saves),
so the launcher's settings win. Some useful ones:

| Variable | Effect |
|---|---|
| `PS3_VIDEO_MODE=1080` | The game's 1080p mode (default); `720` for its 720p mode on a slow graphics chip. See the [FAQ](#faq). |
| `PAD_BACKGROUND=1` | The pad keeps working when another window has focus. |
| `PS3_WHEEL=off` | Don't look for a steering wheel. The other `PS3_WHEEL_*` settings are in the [FAQ](#faq). |
| `PS3_MOUSE_STEER=1` | Steer with the mouse in races (left button throttle, right brake). Its other settings are under [Mouse steering](#mouse-steering). |
| `PS3_COCKPIT_FOV=20` | The cockpit view 20° wider (negative: narrower); `PS3_COCKPIT_SEAT` and `PS3_COCKPIT_HEIGHT` move the eye (cm forward, cm up). See [Cockpit view](#cockpit-view). |
| `PS3_KEYS=cross:W,square:Space,...` | Your own keyboard keys, `button:key` pairs (the launcher's Controls page writes it). Button and key names are under [Your own keys](#keyboard-keys). |
| `PS3_KEYS_ARROWS=split` | Where the arrow keys go. By default (without mouse steering or a wheel) the d-pad only: a tap moves one place in the menus, and in a race GT5 eases into the steering as it does with a PS3 pad's d-pad. `split`: Left/Right push the left stick (full lock at once), Up/Down press the d-pad, as before 18 Nov. With mouse steering or a wheel the default follows the game: d-pad only at the menus, d-pad and stick in a race. `both`: always both (a menu tap moves two places). |
| `PS3_KEYS_WITH_PAD=0` | The keyboard is off while a pad is connected (by default both work together). |
| `PAD_TRIGGERS=drive` | The in-game menu's **Triggers** setting writes it (*Throttle and brake*). By default a pad is as on a PS3 pad while driving too (R2 / L2 shift, the face buttons on and off for throttle and brake). With `drive`, while the game drives a car, the right trigger feeds the pressure of the button the game accelerates with and the left trigger that of the brake button (read from the game's own button assignment, so a layout changed in its options is followed), the bumpers press its shift buttons, and what the bumpers pressed before moves to the stick presses. `PAD_TRACE=2` logs what the game reads: `[pad] the game reads throttle 50%`. |
| `PAD_STICK_DEADZONE=8` | The round dead zone in the middle of every pad's sticks, in percent (0-30; default 8). A worn stick that drifts may want 12 or 15. `old`: XInput pads 24 % on each axis, other pads none, as before 18 Nov. |
| `PAD_MENU_ALL_PADS=0` | The in-game menu reads only the first connected controller, as before; by default it reads every pad and the wheel's buttons. |
| `PAD_RUMBLE_GUARD=0` | The pad's motors left as the game sets them. By default they stop while the in-game menu is open, when the game stops for half a second (the quit question) and when it ends. `PAD_DS_RUMBLE=0`: a DualSense or DualShock 4 read directly doesn't rumble (it does by default over USB, and a DualShock 4 over Bluetooth). |
| `LD_WATCH=1` (or **F9** in the game) | Watch mode for B-Spec races and replays: draws every other frame while the race keeps full speed, draws nothing while minimized, and lowers the game's priority. Off unless you turn it on; with `LD_WATCH=1` it comes on after 10 s without input and goes off when you touch the controls. |
| `PAD_CURSOR_CLIP=1` | Keep the mouse inside the window while the controller is in use (the old behaviour). By default the mouse is free, and only the mouse movement and clicks Steam makes from the controller are ignored. |
| `GCM_DRAIN_STAT=1` | Timing lines every 5 s in `logs\play.err`. |
| `PS3_THREAD_STATS=0` | Turns off the `[threads]` line written to `logs\play.err` every 5 s: how busy each kind of thread was (the game's own, its SPU jobs, the drawing threads, sound), where 100 is one core busy the whole time. A single thread near 100 is the one holding the frame rate back. A number sets another period in seconds (1 to 60). |
| `PS3_MUTE=1` | No sound. |
| `RSX_SHADER_CACHE_DIR=<dir>` | Where compiled shaders are cached (default `scratch\rsx_shader_cache_v2`). |
| `LD_ASYNC_SHADERS=0` | Compile new shaders one at a time on the graphics thread, as before 13 Nov, instead of on up to 8 threads alongside it. |
| `LD_SHADERS=wait` | Asynchronous shader loading off (the Display setting writes it): the picture waits for each new shader. See the [FAQ](#shaders). |
| `LD_FG_ALWAYS=0` | Frame generation only where the game draws a 3D scene, as before 19 Nov; by default it makes frames on every screen (menus, pause, the pre-race screen, replays). |
| `PS3_HANG_S=8` | After how many seconds without a new picture `logs\play.err` gets a `[HANG]` report (8 by default; `0` = none). |
| `PS3_SLOW_FPS=6` / `PS3_SLOW_S=6` | A `[SLOW]` report (the same, for a game that still draws) when it draws fewer than `PS3_SLOW_FPS` frames a second for `PS3_SLOW_S` seconds in a row; not in the first minute, at most three a run (`PS3_SLOW_FPS=0` = none). |
| `SPURS_SLOT_WAKE=0` | Wake every SPU worker thread for each job, as before v0.1.95 (by default only the one that gets the job). |
| `GT5_NATIVE_MIXER=0`, `GT5_NATIVE_SND=0`, `GT5_NATIVE_GEO=0` | Run the translated PS3 code instead of the native PC code: the sound mixer (v0.1.91), the reverb and the EQ (v0.1.92), the geometry jobs (v0.1.93). `=2` runs both and logs any difference (slow, for testing). |
| `GT5_MOD_<NAME>=1` | Turns on a game-code mod from `GT5\mods` (see [MODDING.md](MODDING.md)). |
| `PS3_TEX_DUMP=1` | Writes every texture the game shows to `GT5\textures\dump` (DDS and PNG), for making texture packs. See [MODDING.md](MODDING.md#2-textures-and-hd-texture-packs). DirectX 12 only for now. |
| `PS3_TEX_REPLACE=0` | Don't use the texture files in `GT5\textures\replace` (an HD texture pack); they're used whenever there are any. |

Most speed-ups in the patch can be switched off one by one to rule them out when something looks
wrong; each is described in a comment next to its `getenv` in the patch.

<a id="repo-contents"></a>

## ⚖️ What this repository contains, and what it does not

This repository holds only code and scripts written for the port:

- `GT5/patches/ps3recomp.patch`: the changes to ps3recomp (runtime, graphics, SPU, audio, input).
- `GT5/CMakeLists.txt`, `GT5/play.bat`, `GT5/src/`, `GT5/config/`: the GT5 build and launcher.
- `GT5/scripts/`: the lift, build, test and analysis tools.

It does **not** contain, and must never be given:

- any part of the game: the EBOOT, disc or installed files, music, textures, models, shaders,
  menu images, save data, or screenshots;
- code generated from the game (the recompiled `generated/` and `spu/` folders, `src/gen/`): every
  user produces these from their own copy;
- PS3 firmware, system modules, or any decryption key.

You need your own copy of Gran Turismo 5 (BCES00569 or BCUS98114), dumped from a console you own, and PS3 system
software installed from Sony's official update file. Use this only with games you own.

- **Never share what you build.** `gt5.exe`, the `generated/` folder and anything else made by the
  lift contain code recompiled from the game, so each person has to build them from their own copy.
  Don't upload them or a ready-to-play package, and don't ask for them.
- This repository does not include, link to, or explain how to obtain decryption keys or game files.
- Questions about downloaded copies of the game will not be answered.

**Gran Turismo** is a trademark of Sony Interactive Entertainment. This project is not affiliated
with, endorsed by, or connected to Sony Interactive Entertainment or Polyphony Digital.

## 🔧 Fork it, mod it

Forks are welcome; take whatever you like (MIT license). If you make something good, open a pull
request or [show it here](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/issues/new?template=4-my-fork-or-mod.yml)
so it can come back into the main repo. [MODDING.md](MODDING.md) covers the ways in: texture dumps
and HD texture packs, switchable game-code mods in `GT5\mods`, the graphics, controller and sound code, and the tools for finding
your way around. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) has the few rules.
