`setup.ps1`:

```ps1
# Set up and build GT5 Recomp with one command. Run it from the gt5-recomp folder:
#   powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File setup.ps1
# Run it as often as you like. It does whatever is still to do: fetches and patches ps3recomp, makes
# the Python environment, downloads FFmpeg (optional: the movies), then checks your game files and says exactly what's
# missing or wrong. When everything is in place it generates the game code and builds gt5.exe with both
# renderers, DirectX 12 and Vulkan (the first time takes 30 to 60 minutes), then adds AMD FSR 3 and, on a PC
# with an NVIDIA RTX card whose installer showed NVIDIA's licence, NVIDIA DLSS. Then play with
# GT5Launcher.exe or GT5\play.bat. -NoBuild stops after the checks. To update later, use update.ps1.
param([switch]$NoBuild)
# Errors are checked through exit codes: with "Stop", Windows PowerShell turns a native command's
# redirected stderr into a terminating error before the check can run.
$ErrorActionPreference = "Continue"
# Another Python's settings (Anaconda, QGIS and others set these for everyone) would make the port's own Python load
# that one's libraries: not for this run or anything it starts.
Remove-Item Env:PYTHONHOME, Env:PYTHONPATH -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
# On a drive that doesn't record who owns a file (exFAT, FAT32, many USB and network drives) git refuses
# to work in the install folder ("detected dubious ownership", #41). Trust it for git run from here and
# what this starts, through git's environment config; the player's own git settings stay as they are.
if ($env:GT5_GIT_SAFE -ne "1") {
    $gn = 0; if ("$env:GIT_CONFIG_COUNT" -match '^\d+$') { $gn = [int]$env:GIT_CONFIG_COUNT }
    Set-Item "env:GIT_CONFIG_KEY_$gn" "safe.directory"; Set-Item "env:GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_$gn" "*"
    $env:GIT_CONFIG_COUNT = "$($gn + 1)"; $env:GT5_GIT_SAFE = "1"
}
$base = $PSScriptRoot
# Git: the PC's own, else the port's own portable copy in tools\git (get-git.ps1; nothing installed in Windows).
$ownGit = Join-Path $base "tools\git\cmd"
if (-not (Get-Command git -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $ownGit "git.exe"))) { $env:Path = "$ownGit;$env:Path" }
$gt5 = Join-Path $base "GT5"
$rc = Join-Path $base "ps3recomp"
$venv = Join-Path $base "venv"
$py = Join-Path $venv "Scripts\python.exe"
$script:todo = 0

function Ok([string]$m) { Write-Host "  [ok]      $m" -ForegroundColor Green }
function Todo([string]$m, [string]$fix) {
    Write-Host "  [missing] $m" -ForegroundColor Yellow
    if ($fix) { Write-Host "            $fix" }
    $script:todo++
}
function Stop-Setup([string]$m) { Write-Host ""; Write-Host "setup stopped: $m" -ForegroundColor Red; exit 1 }
# PARAM.SFO's values by key (APP_VER, TITLE_ID, ...), or $null when it isn't one.
function Read-Sfo([string]$path) {
    try { $b = [IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($path) } catch { return $null }
    if ($b.Length -lt 20 -or $b[1] -ne 0x50 -or $b[2] -ne 0x53 -or $b[3] -ne 0x46) { return $null }
    $keyT = [BitConverter]::ToUInt32($b, 8); $dataT = [BitConverter]::ToUInt32($b, 12)
    $n = [BitConverter]::ToUInt32($b, 16); $r = @{}
    for ($i = 0; $i -lt $n; $i++) {
        $e = 20 + $i * 16
        if ($e + 16 -gt $b.Length) { break }
        $ko = [BitConverter]::ToUInt16($b, $e); $fmt = [BitConverter]::ToUInt16($b, $e + 2)
        $len = [BitConverter]::ToUInt32($b, $e + 4); $do = [BitConverter]::ToUInt32($b, $e + 12)
        $k = ""; $p = $keyT + $ko
        while ($p -lt $b.Length -and $b[$p] -ne 0) { $k += [char]$b[$p]; $p++ }
        if ($dataT + $do + $len -gt $b.Length) { continue }
        if ($fmt -eq 0x0404) { $r[$k] = [BitConverter]::ToUInt32($b, $dataT + $do) }
        else { $r[$k] = [Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetString($b, $dataT + $do, $len).TrimEnd([char]0) }
    }
    return $r
}

if (-not (Test-Path (Join-Path $gt5 "scripts\relift.ps1"))) {
    Stop-Setup "run this from the gt5-recomp folder (the one with setup.ps1, README.md and the GT5 folder)."
}
Write-Host "== GT5 Recomp setup in $base"
Write-Host ""

# ---- Can this PC run the game? Before anything long (GT5-Installer.bat asks the same on its first page) ----------
# The game is built for processors with AVX2 (GT5\CMakeLists.txt: -mavx2 -mfma ...): one without it stops the moment
# the game starts, after an hour of building. The first build also needs memory.
function Get-PcProblem {
    try {
        if (-not ("Gt5Pc.Cpu" -as [type])) {
            Add-Type -Namespace Gt5Pc -Name Cpu -MemberDefinition @'
[DllImport("kernel32.dll")] public static extern bool IsProcessorFeaturePresent(uint feature);
[DllImport("kernel32.dll")] public static extern ulong GetEnabledXStateFeatures();
[DllImport("kernel32.dll")] public static extern bool GetPhysicallyInstalledSystemMemory(out ulong kb);
'@
        }
        $avx2 = $true
        # No AVX state in use: no AVX, so no AVX2. A Windows that knows the AVX entries (39) answers AVX2 (40) directly;
        # an older one answers no to both, and the processor is given the benefit of the doubt.
        if (([Gt5Pc.Cpu]::GetEnabledXStateFeatures() -band 4) -eq 0) { $avx2 = $false }
        elseif ([Gt5Pc.Cpu]::IsProcessorFeaturePresent(39)) { $avx2 = [Gt5Pc.Cpu]::IsProcessorFeaturePresent(40) }
        if ($env:GT5_INSTALL_NOAVX2) { $avx2 = $false }
        if (-not $avx2) { return "this PC's processor is too old for the game (it has no AVX2)." }
        $kb = [uint64]0; $gb = 0
        if ([Gt5Pc.Cpu]::GetPhysicallyInstalledSystemMemory([ref]$kb)) { $gb = [int][math]::Round($kb / 1MB) }
        if ($env:GT5_INSTALL_RAMGB) { $gb = [int]$env:GT5_INSTALL_RAMGB }
        if ($gb -gt 0 -and $gb -lt 8) { return "this PC has $gb GB of memory; the game needs at least 8 GB." }
    } catch { }
    return ""
}
$pcProblem = Get-PcProblem
if ($pcProblem) { Stop-Setup $pcProblem }
Write-Host "Tools:"

# ---- Git ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
if (-not (Get-Command git -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) -and (Test-Path (Join-Path $base "get-git.ps1"))) {
    & powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File (Join-Path $base "get-git.ps1") | ForEach-Object { Write-Host "            $_" }
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $ownGit "git.exe")) { $env:Path = "$ownGit;$env:Path" }
}
if (Get-Command git -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) { Ok "Git" }
else { Todo "Git" "get-git.ps1 couldn't fetch the port's own Git (see above; is the internet connection up?). Run setup.ps1 again, or install Git for Windows (https://git-scm.com)."; Stop-Setup "Git is needed to fetch ps3recomp." }

# ---- Python: the port's own copy (get-python.ps1, in tools\python) ------------------------------------------
# The tools run in an environment (venv) made from python.org's Python 3.11.9 that get-python.ps1 puts in
# this folder: the version they are tested on, whatever Python the PC has or hasn't. An environment that
# already exists is kept as it is (an earlier setup made it from the PC's Python), unless GT5_OWN_PYTHON=1
# (GT5-Installer.bat sets it) asks for it to be made again from the port's own.
$ownPy = Join-Path $base "tools\python\python.exe"
function Get-PyVer([string]$p) { return "$(& $p -c "import sys; print('%d.%d.%d%s' % (sys.version_info[:3] + ('' if sys.version_info.releaselevel == 'final' else ' ' + sys.version_info.releaselevel,)))" 2>$null)".Trim() }
function Test-VenvIsOwn {
    $cfg = Join-Path $venv "pyvenv.cfg"
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $cfg)) { return $false }
    $h = (Get-Content -LiteralPath $cfg | Where-Object { $_ -match '^\s*home\s*=' } | Select-Object -First 1) -replace '^\s*home\s*=\s*', ''
    return ("$h".Trim().TrimEnd('\') -ieq (Split-Path $ownPy -Parent))
}
if (-not (Test-Path $py) -or ($env:GT5_OWN_PYTHON -eq "1" -and -not (Test-VenvIsOwn))) {
    if (-not (Test-Path $ownPy)) { & powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File (Join-Path $base "get-python.ps1") | ForEach-Object { Write-Host "            $_" } }
    if ((Test-Path $ownPy) -and (Test-Path $py) -and -not (Test-VenvIsOwn)) {
        Write-Host "            Making the Python environment again from the port's own Python (it was made from the PC's: Python $(Get-PyVer $py))."
        Remove-Item -LiteralPath $venv -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    }
}
if (Test-Path $py) { $pyVer = Get-PyVer $py; Ok "Python environment (venv, Python $pyVer)" }
else {
    # The port's own Python, else (the download failed) one already on the PC: 3.11 or newer, final releases only.
    $pyCmd = $null
    if (Test-Path $ownPy) { $pyCmd = @($ownPy) }
    else {
        foreach ($cand in @(@("py", "-3.11"), @("py", "-3.12"), @("py", "-3.13"), @("py", "-3"), @("python"), @("python3"))) {
            if (-not (Get-Command $cand[0] -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { continue }
            $rest = @($cand | Select-Object -Skip 1)
            $v = & $cand[0] @rest -c "import sys; print('%d.%d' % sys.version_info[:2] if sys.version_info.releaselevel == 'final' else 'pre-release')" 2>$null
            if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0 -and "$v" -match '^3\.(\d+)$' -and [int]$Matches[1] -ge 11) { $pyCmd = $cand; break }
        }
    }
    if (-not $pyCmd) {
        Todo "Python" "get-python.ps1 couldn't fetch the port's own Python (see above; is the internet connection up?). Run setup.ps1 again, or install Python 3.11 from https://www.python.org/downloads/ and tick 'Add python.exe to PATH'."
        Stop-Setup "Python is needed for the tools."
    }
    $rest = @($pyCmd | Select-Object -Skip 1)
    & $pyCmd[0] @rest -m venv $venv
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or -not (Test-Path $py)) { Stop-Setup "making the Python environment failed (see the message above)." }
    $pyVer = Get-PyVer $py
    Ok "Python environment (venv, Python $pyVer$(if (Test-VenvIsOwn) { ', the port''s own' } else { ', from the PC''s ' + ($pyCmd -join ' ') }))"
}

# ---- Visual Studio with the Clang tools (what GT5\scripts\build.cmd needs), or get-toolchain.ps1's tools ----
# A usable Visual Studio has both clang-cl and vcvars64.bat (build.cmd calls it): a folder an uninstall left
# behind can keep clang-cl alone, and then the build stopped with "The system cannot find the path specified" (#35).
function Test-VsFolder([string]$p) {
    $p -and (Test-Path (Join-Path $p "VC\Tools\Llvm\x64\bin\clang-cl.exe")) -and (Test-Path (Join-Path $p "VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvars64.bat"))
}
$vsOk = Test-VsFolder "$env:ProgramFiles\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\Community"
if (-not $vsOk) {
    $vswhere = "${env:ProgramFiles(x86)}\Microsoft Visual Studio\Installer\vswhere.exe"
    if (Test-Path $vswhere) {
        foreach ($vsPath in @(& $vswhere -sort -products * -requires Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.Llvm.Clang -property installationPath)) {
            if (Test-VsFolder $vsPath) { $vsOk = $true; break }
        }
    }
}
# The same tools without Visual Studio, where build.cmd looks: the folder get-toolchain.ps1 recorded, else
# "toolchain" next to this folder.
function Find-Toolchain {
    $rec = Join-Path $base ".gt5\toolchain-path.txt"
    $cands = @($env:GT5_TOOLCHAIN)
    if (Test-Path $rec) { $cands += [Console]::OutputEncoding.GetString([IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($rec)).Trim() }
    $cands += Join-Path (Split-Path $base -Parent) "toolchain"
    foreach ($c in $cands) { if ($c -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $c "gt5-toolchain.txt"))) { return $c } }
}
# The Windows SDK (kernel32.lib and the other Windows libraries), shared by every Visual Studio on the PC: one
# installed without it stopped the build with "could not open 'kernel32.lib'" (#35). get-toolchain.ps1's tools
# bring their own.
$sdkOk = $false
foreach ($r in @("${env:ProgramFiles(x86)}\Windows Kits\10\Lib", "$env:ProgramFiles\Windows Kits\10\Lib")) {
    foreach ($d in @(Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $r -Directory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
        if (Test-Path (Join-Path $d.FullName "um\x64\kernel32.lib")) { $sdkOk = $true }
    }
}
if ($vsOk -and -not $sdkOk -and -not (Find-Toolchain)) {
    Todo "Windows SDK" "Your Visual Studio has the Clang tools but no Windows SDK (kernel32.lib and the other Windows libraries the build needs). In the Visual Studio Installer choose Modify, tick 'Windows 11 SDK' under Individual components, then run setup.ps1 again. (GT5-Installer.bat fetches its own compiler tools instead in that case.)"
}
elseif ($vsOk -and $sdkOk) { Ok "Visual Studio with the C++ Clang tools" }
else {
    $tc = Find-Toolchain
    if (-not $tc) {
        Write-Host "            Visual Studio with the C++ Clang tools isn't installed. get-toolchain.ps1 can get the same" -ForegroundColor Yellow
        Write-Host "            compiler tools without it: about 1.5 GB in a folder you choose, on any drive (C: stays free)." -ForegroundColor Yellow
        $a = Read-Host "            Run get-toolchain.ps1 now? (Y/N)"
        if ("$a".Trim() -match '^[Yy]') { & powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File (Join-Path $base "get-toolchain.ps1") }
        $tc = Find-Toolchain
    }
    if ($tc) { Ok "Compiler tools from get-toolchain.ps1 (no Visual Studio needed), in $tc" }
    else { Todo "Visual Studio 2022 with 'Desktop development with C++' and 'C++ Clang tools for Windows'" "Install the free Community edition (https://visualstudio.microsoft.com), choose that workload and tick the Clang tools under Individual components. Not much space on C:? Run get-toolchain.ps1 instead (README.md: No Visual Studio)." }
}

# ---- ps3recomp, patched for this version (the same step update.ps1 uses) --------------------------------
$out = & powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File (Join-Path $base "update.ps1") -Here 2>&1
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { $out | ForEach-Object { Write-Host "            $_" }; Stop-Setup "the game's tools couldn't be fetched (is the internet connection up?)." }
Ok "ps3recomp, patched"
# The packages at the versions the tools are tested with (requirements.txt gives only lower bounds, so each install
# got whatever was newest that day). A later version of one of these comes with an update that names it here.
$pins = @("capstone==5.0.9", "construct==2.10.70", "pycryptodome==4.2.0", "tabulate==0.10.0", "tqdm==4.70.1")
& $py -m pip install --quiet --disable-pip-version-check -r (Join-Path $rc "requirements.txt") @pins
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Stop-Setup "the Python packages couldn't be installed (is the internet connection up?)." }
Ok "Python packages"

# ---- FFmpeg (plays the game's movies; optional) ------------------------------------------------------------
# get-ffmpeg.ps1 fetches a fixed release, checked by its SHA-256. Without it the game builds and runs, and only its
# movies don't play: a failed download is a note, never a stop, and the next update tries again.
$ffname = "ffmpeg-n9.0-latest-win64-lgpl-shared-9.0"
$ffdir = Join-Path $base "ffmpeg"
$getFf = Join-Path $base "get-ffmpeg.ps1"
if ((Test-Path -LiteralPath $getFf) -and -not (Test-Path (Join-Path $ffdir "$ffname\bin\avcodec-63.dll"))) {
    & powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $getFf | ForEach-Object { Write-Host "            $_" }
}
if (Test-Path (Join-Path $ffdir "$ffname\bin\avcodec-63.dll")) { Ok "FFmpeg (plays the game's movies)" }
else { Write-Host "  [note]    FFmpeg: not added this time, so the game's movies won't play. The next update tries again." -ForegroundColor Yellow }

# ---- Your game files ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Write-Host ""
Write-Host "Your files (see Setup in README.md for where each comes from):"
foreach ($d in "input", "vfs") { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force (Join-Path $gt5 $d) | Out-Null }

$elf = Join-Path $gt5 "input\EBOOT.elf"
$elfDisc = $false   # the disc's own version 01.00 executable (no update)
# The game's executable is locked as it comes on the disc (EBOOT.BIN). The port's own tool unlocks it
# (scripts\ps3_unlock.py: no RPCS3): from GT5\input\EBOOT.BIN, a locked file named EBOOT.elf, or the disc
# copy's own PS3_GAME\USRDIR\EBOOT.BIN.
function Unlock-Exe([string]$from) {
    $tool = Join-Path $gt5 "scripts\ps3_unlock.py"
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $tool) -or -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $py)) { return "this copy lacks the unlock tool" }
    $why = ""; $tmp = "$elf.unlock"
    Remove-Item -LiteralPath $tmp -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    & $py -I $tool eboot $from $tmp --keys-dir (Join-Path $base "tools\ps3_keys") 2>&1 | ForEach-Object {
        if ("$_" -match '^PS3_UNLOCK_FAIL\s+\d+\s+\w+:\s*(.*)$') { $why = $Matches[1].Trim() }
    }
    $global:LASTEXITCODE = 0
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $tmp) { Move-Item -LiteralPath $tmp -Destination $elf -Force; return "" }
    return $(if ($why) { $why } else { "it didn't work" })
}
$locked = $null
if (Test-Path $elf) {
    $fs = [IO.File]::OpenRead($elf); $magic = New-Object byte[] 4; [void]$fs.Read($magic, 0, 4); $fs.Close()
    if (($magic -join ",") -eq "83,67,69,0") { $locked = "$elf.locked"; Move-Item -LiteralPath $elf -Destination $locked -Force }
} else {
    $locked = @((Join-Path $gt5 "input\EBOOT.BIN"), (Join-Path $gt5 "vfs\PS3_GAME\USRDIR\EBOOT.BIN")) | Where-Object { Test-Path -LiteralPath $_ } | Select-Object -First 1
}
if ($locked -and -not (Test-Path $elf)) {
    $u = Unlock-Exe $locked
    if ($u) { Write-Host "  [note]    Unlocking the game's executable ($locked): $u" -ForegroundColor Yellow }
    else { Ok "GT5\input\EBOOT.elf: unlocked from $locked" }
}
if (-not (Test-Path $elf)) {
    Todo "GT5\input\EBOOT.elf (your game's executable)" "Copy your disc's PS3_GAME folder to GT5\vfs (so that GT5\vfs\PS3_GAME\USRDIR\EBOOT.BIN exists) and run setup again: it unlocks the executable by itself."
} else {
    $fs = [IO.File]::OpenRead($elf); $magic = New-Object byte[] 4; [void]$fs.Read($magic, 0, 4); $fs.Close()
    $sha1 = (Get-FileHash $elf -Algorithm SHA1).Hash
    if (($magic -join ",") -ne "127,69,76,70") {
        Todo "a valid GT5\input\EBOOT.elf" "This file isn't a PS3 executable. Delete it and run setup again: it is made from your disc's PS3_GAME\USRDIR\EBOOT.BIN."
    } elseif ($sha1 -eq "1535B865EC7DD58E7704B378B8621532ECF844E1") {
        Ok "GT5\input\EBOOT.elf: Europe BCES00569, version 01.00 (the tested one)"; $elfDisc = $true
    } elseif ($sha1 -eq "40126D2D14B0A95B9601BB11E3A6E778186067AC") {
        Ok "GT5\input\EBOOT.elf: North America BCUS98114, version 01.00 (players have raced on it)"; $elfDisc = $true
    } elseif ($sha1 -eq "49A3662D4B541BB4E0C2E72D2602F89FEB710E71") {
        Ok "GT5\input\EBOOT.elf: Hong Kong / Asia BCAS20108, version 01.00 (tested)"; $elfDisc = $true
    } elseif ($sha1 -eq "96DEA35B194AA80E993CAD9EBE42E96072F3A3D5") {
        Ok "GT5\input\EBOOT.elf: Hong Kong / Asia BCAS20108, update 2.01 (tested; needs the update's data in GT5\hdd0, README: Game updates)"
    } elseif ($sha1 -eq "12EF249F9B95591E08251AC85F103B1451DA23BF") {
        Ok "GT5\input\EBOOT.elf: North America BCUS98114, update 2.17 (tested; needs the update's data in GT5\hdd0, README: Game updates)"
    } elseif ($sha1 -eq "266EE27115B2AAC6318AD0122DAE56EDE94B797F") {
        Ok "GT5\input\EBOOT.elf: North America BCUS98114, update 2.11 with the GT5 Master Mod 1.9.2 (a player raced on it; needs 2.11's and the mod's data in GT5\hdd0, README: Game updates)"
    } elseif ($sha1 -eq "306F86C62B9F03041C903BE96AC59E5C3F130452") {
        Ok "GT5\input\EBOOT.elf: Europe BCES00569, update 2.17 (tested; needs the update's data in GT5\hdd0, README: Game updates)"
    } else {
        Ok "GT5\input\EBOOT.elf (SHA-1 $sha1)"
        Write-Host "            Not one tried yet. Another disc version may well work: please report how it goes. One from a game update (2.xx) also needs the update's data in GT5\hdd0 (README: Game updates)." -ForegroundColor Yellow
    }
}

# A game update's data in GT5\hdd0 needs the update's executable too. GT5 reads updated files from the
# hard disk whatever its own version, so the disc's 01.00 executable runs the update's newer scripts,
# which call code it doesn't have: the game stops before the main menu with a black screen (13 Nov 2026,
# US 2.11 with the Master Mod). The update's PARAM.SFO (APP_VER) or EBOOT.BIN in GT5\hdd0\game\<title ID>
# says an update is installed; the disc version writes neither there.
# scripts\update_exe.ps1 finds the update's EBOOT.BIN (GT5\hdd0), unlocks it with the port's own tool and
# swaps it in, keeping the disc's as EBOOT.disc-01.00.elf; the game code is then generated for it.
if ($elfDisc) {
    & powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File (Join-Path $gt5 "scripts\update_exe.ps1") -Gt5 $gt5
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 2) { Todo "GT5\input\EBOOT.elf from the game update in GT5\hdd0" "See the lines just above." }
    elseif ((Get-FileHash $elf -Algorithm SHA1).Hash -ne $sha1) { Ok "GT5\input\EBOOT.elf: switched to the installed update's executable" }
    $global:LASTEXITCODE = 0
}

$game = Join-Path $gt5 "vfs\PS3_GAME"
if (Test-Path (Join-Path $game "USRDIR")) {
    if (Test-Path (Join-Path $game "PARAM.SFO")) {
        # Joins a GT.VOL that a FAT32 dump split into pieces, and checks it's there at all.
        & (Join-Path $gt5 "scripts\fix_game_files.ps1") -Gt5 $gt5
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 2) {
            Todo "GT5\vfs\PS3_GAME\USRDIR\GT.VOL (the game's data, about 12 GB)" "Copy it from PS3_GAME\USRDIR in your disc dump (or its pieces GT.VOL.66600, .66601, ...: they're joined automatically)."
        } else { Ok "GT5\vfs\PS3_GAME (your disc's game data)" }
        $global:LASTEXITCODE = 0
    }
    else { Todo "GT5\vfs\PS3_GAME\PARAM.SFO" "Copy the whole PS3_GAME folder from your disc, including PARAM.SFO." }
} elseif (Test-Path (Join-Path $game "PS3_GAME\USRDIR")) {
    Todo "GT5\vfs\PS3_GAME at the right level" "It's one folder too deep: move the contents of GT5\vfs\PS3_GAME\PS3_GAME up into GT5\vfs\PS3_GAME."
} else {
    $nested = Get-ChildItem (Join-Path $gt5 "vfs") -Directory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
              Where-Object { Test-Path (Join-Path $_.FullName "PS3_GAME\USRDIR") } | Select-Object -First 1
    if ($nested) { Todo "GT5\vfs\PS3_GAME" "Found it inside GT5\vfs\$($nested.Name): move that PS3_GAME folder up so it's GT5\vfs\PS3_GAME." }
    else { Todo "GT5\vfs\PS3_GAME (your disc's game data, about 17 GB)" "Copy the PS3_GAME folder from your disc dump to GT5\vfs, so that GT5\vfs\PS3_GAME\USRDIR exists." }
}

# The PS3's system software (GT5\dev_flash) is not needed: the game never reads it, and every system
# function it calls is the port's own code. A folder left by an older install does no harm.

Write-Host ""
if ($script:todo -gt 0) {
    Write-Host "$($script:todo) thing(s) still to do (marked [missing] above). Sort them out, then run setup.ps1 again." -ForegroundColor Yellow
    exit 1
}
if ($NoBuild) { Write-Host "Everything is in place. Run setup.ps1 without -NoBuild to build the game." -ForegroundColor Green; exit 0 }

# ---- Generate the game code (only when it's missing or out of date), then build --------------------------
# Processors that calculate wrongly are left out of everything from here on (pc-check.ps1 says why).
$pcCheck = Join-Path $base "pc-check.ps1"
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $pcCheck) {
    . $pcCheck
    $pcNote = Use-GoodProcessors -Base $base -Py $py
    if ($pcNote) { Write-Host $pcNote -ForegroundColor Yellow }
}
Push-Location $gt5
& $py "scripts\lift_stamp.py" --check | Out-Null
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
    Write-Host "Generating the game code from your EBOOT.elf (about 10 minutes)..."
    & powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "scripts\relift.ps1"
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        # Seen on a player's PC: a step stopped with an error from inside Python itself that no line of the
        # tool can raise: two of its processors calculated wrongly. So the check is made again, now with
        # one of the lift's own jobs, any processor that fails is left out, and the lift starts again.
        if (Get-Command Use-GoodProcessors -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
            $pcNote = Use-GoodProcessors -Base $base -Py $py -Again
            if ($pcNote) { Write-Host $pcNote -ForegroundColor Yellow }
        }
        Write-Host "Generating the game code stopped (see above). Trying once more from the start..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
        & powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "scripts\relift.ps1"
    }
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Write-Host "Generating the game code failed twice (Python $pyVer)."; Pop-Location; Stop-Setup "converting the game's code didn't finish." }
} else {
    Write-Host "The game code is already generated and current."
}
Write-Host "Building gt5.exe (the first build takes 20 to 50 minutes)..."
# The parts the game is built with or gets next to it are set up here, not on first use: Vulkan (the second
# renderer) before the build, so this one build has both renderers; AMD FSR 3 and, on a PC with an NVIDIA RTX
# card, NVIDIA DLSS after it. Their scripts (GT5\scripts\add_*.ps1) write their whole text to GT5\logs and pass
# on only their progress lines (GT5_ADD ...). None of them can stop setup: without one, the launcher simply
# doesn't offer it, and the next update tries again.
$addCommon = Join-Path $gt5 "scripts\addon_common.ps1"
$addOns = Test-Path -LiteralPath $addCommon
if ($addOns) { . $addCommon }
$logs = Join-Path $gt5 "logs"
$cacheFile = Join-Path $gt5 "build\CMakeCache.txt"
function Test-VulkanInBuild { return (Test-Path -LiteralPath $cacheFile) -and [bool](Select-String -LiteralPath $cacheFile -Pattern '^PS3RECOMP_RSX_VULKAN:BOOL=ON' -Quiet) }
if ($addOns) {
    $r = Invoke-AddOn (Join-Path $gt5 "scripts\add_vulkan.ps1") @("-Prepare") "add_vulkan" $logs
    if ($r -eq 0) { Write-Host "  Vulkan: built in" } elseif ($r -eq 1) { Write-Host "  Vulkan: left out this time (DirectX 12 only; GT5\logs\add_vulkan.log says why). The next update tries again." }
}
cmd /c "scripts\build.cmd gt5"
$built = $LASTEXITCODE
if ($built -ne 0 -and $addOns -and (Test-VulkanInBuild)) {
    # The game must build even when Vulkan doesn't (a newer compiler that its code doesn't suit, say): once more
    # without it, which rebuilds only the runtime. The next update tries Vulkan again.
    Write-Host "The build stopped. Building once more without Vulkan..."
    $null = Invoke-AddOn (Join-Path $gt5 "scripts\add_vulkan.ps1") @("-Remove", "-Prepare") "add_vulkan-off" $logs
    cmd /c "scripts\build.cmd gt5"
    $built = $LASTEXITCODE
    if ($built -eq 0) { Write-Host "  Vulkan: left out this time (the build with it stopped; GT5\logs says why). The next update tries again." }
}
Pop-Location
if ($built -ne 0) { Stop-Setup "the build didn't finish." }
# The launcher (settings, Play, updates) is built after every good build (GT5\scripts\build_run.ps1). Without it the
# shortcut would start the game in a console window: once more, else the setup isn't done.
$launcherExe = Join-Path $base "GT5Launcher.exe"
$buildLauncher = Join-Path $base "launcher\build-launcher.ps1"
if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $launcherExe) -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath $buildLauncher)) {
    & powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $buildLauncher
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $launcherExe)) { Stop-Setup "the launcher couldn't be built." }
}
if ($addOns) {
    $r = Invoke-AddOn (Join-Path $gt5 "scripts\add_fsr.ps1") @() "add_fsr" $logs
    if ($r -eq 0) { Write-Host "  AMD FSR 3: added" } elseif ($r -eq 1) { Write-Host "  AMD FSR 3: not added this time (GT5\logs\add_fsr.log says why). The next update tries again." }
    # NVIDIA's licence: accepted with the installer's Install button, which showed it (GT5-Installer.bat writes
    # .gt5\installer-licences.txt), or when DLSS was added before. A setup.ps1 run by hand without either
    # leaves DLSS out without a word: the launcher's Display page can add it, with the same licence line.
    $licFile = Join-Path $base ".gt5\installer-licences.txt"
    $dlssShown = (Test-Path -LiteralPath $licFile) -and [bool](Select-String -LiteralPath $licFile -Pattern '^dlss\b' -Quiet)
    $dlssThere = Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $gt5 "build\gt5_upscale_dlss.dll")
    if (($dlssShown -or $dlssThere) -and (Test-RtxCard)) {
        $r = Invoke-AddOn (Join-Path $gt5 "scripts\add_dlss.ps1") @("-Accept") "add_dlss" $logs
        if ($r -eq 0) { Write-Host "  NVIDIA DLSS: added" } elseif ($r -eq 1) { Write-Host "  NVIDIA DLSS: not added this time (GT5\logs\add_dlss.log says why). The next update tries again." }
    }
}
# The shaders this PC's game has drawn before (a setup over an earlier install keeps them), made with this build
# (gt5.exe --prepare-shaders). On a first install there are none yet and it ends at once. Never a stop.
$gt5exe = Join-Path $gt5 "build\gt5.exe"
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $gt5exe) {
    $null = Start-Process -FilePath $gt5exe -ArgumentList "--prepare-shaders" -WorkingDirectory $gt5 -NoNewWindow -Wait -PassThru -RedirectStandardError (Join-Path $logs "prepare.log")
}
Write-Host ""
Write-Host "Done! Start GT5Launcher.exe in this folder (settings, Play, Updates), or GT5\play.bat directly." -ForegroundColor Green
Write-Host "Later, the launcher's Updates page or a double-click on Update.bat gets new versions." -ForegroundColor Green

```

`setup.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Set up and build GT5 Recomp on Linux with one command. Run it from the gt5-recomp folder:
#   bash setup.sh
# Run it as often as you like; it does whatever is still to do. It checks the tools (and with
# --install-deps installs the missing ones through your package manager, asking for your password),
# fetches and patches ps3recomp, makes the Python environment, then checks your game files and says
# exactly what's missing or wrong. When everything is in place it generates the game code from your
# EBOOT.elf and builds GT5/build-linux/gt5 (the first time takes 20 to 60 minutes). Then play with
# bash GT5/play.sh. --no-build stops after the checks.
#
# Updating later: git pull, then bash setup.sh again (it re-patches, re-lifts and rebuilds only what
# the new version changed).
set -u
BASE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
GT5="$BASE/GT5"
RC="$BASE/ps3recomp"
VENV="$BASE/venv"
PY="$VENV/bin/python"
STATE="$BASE/.gt5"
TODO=0
NOBUILD=0
INSTALL=0
for a in "$@"; do
    case "$a" in
        --no-build) NOBUILD=1 ;;
        --install-deps) INSTALL=1 ;;
        -h|--help) sed -n '2,12p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
        *) echo "setup.sh: unknown option $a (try --help)"; exit 1 ;;
    esac
done

if [ -t 1 ]; then G=$'\e[32m'; Y=$'\e[33m'; R=$'\e[31m'; N=$'\e[0m'; else G=; Y=; R=; N=; fi
ok()   { echo "  ${G}[ok]${N}      $1"; }
todo() { echo "  ${Y}[missing]${N} $1"; [ -n "${2:-}" ] && echo "            $2"; TODO=$((TODO + 1)); }
stop() { echo; echo "${R}setup stopped: $1${N}"; exit 1; }
have() { command -v "$1" > /dev/null 2>&1; }

[ -f "$GT5/scripts/relift.sh" ] && [ -f "$GT5/linux/CMakeLists.txt" ] ||
    stop "run this from the gt5-recomp folder (the one with setup.sh, README.md and the GT5 folder)."
[ "$(uname -s)" = Linux ] || stop "this is the Linux setup. On Windows use setup.ps1 (or GT5-Installer.bat)."
case "$(uname -m)" in x86_64|amd64) ;; *) stop "only x86-64 PCs are supported so far (this is $(uname -m))." ;; esac
grep -qw avx2 /proc/cpuinfo 2> /dev/null ||
    stop "this CPU has no AVX2. The game code is built for AVX2 CPUs (Intel 2013 Haswell / AMD 2015 and later)."
# SteamOS (Steam Deck): its system files are read-only and every update resets them, so the build tools
# can't be installed there. Inside a distrobox (an Ubuntu container) /etc/os-release is Ubuntu's.
if grep -qs '^ID=steamos' /etc/os-release; then
    echo "This is SteamOS: its system files are read-only, so build GT5 inside a distrobox (part of SteamOS"
    echo "3.5 and later). In desktop mode, in Konsole:"
    echo "  distrobox create --name gt5 --image ubuntu:24.04"
    echo "  distrobox enter gt5"
    echo "  cd \"$BASE\" && bash setup.sh --install-deps"
    echo "README.md, Steam Deck, has the rest (adding the game to Steam)."
    exit 1
fi
echo "== GT5 Recomp setup (Linux) in $BASE"
echo
echo "Tools:"

# ---- The packages the build needs, by package manager ----------------------------------------------------
PM=""; PKGS=""
if have apt-get; then
    PM="sudo apt-get install -y"
    PKGS="git python3 python3-venv python3-pip clang lld cmake ninja-build pkg-config libsdl2-dev libvulkan-dev glslang-dev glslang-tools libavcodec-dev libvulkan1 mesa-vulkan-drivers"
elif have dnf; then
    PM="sudo dnf install -y"
    PKGS="git python3 clang lld cmake ninja-build pkgconf-pkg-config SDL2-devel vulkan-headers vulkan-loader glslang-devel glslang ffmpeg-free-devel mesa-vulkan-drivers"
elif have pacman; then
    PM="sudo pacman -S --needed --noconfirm"
    PKGS="git python clang lld cmake ninja pkgconf sdl2 vulkan-headers vulkan-icd-loader glslang ffmpeg"
elif have zypper; then
    PM="sudo zypper install -y"
    PKGS="git python3 clang lld cmake ninja pkg-config libSDL2-devel vulkan-headers libvulkan1 glslang-devel ffmpeg-7-libavcodec-devel"
fi
if [ "$INSTALL" = 1 ]; then
    [ -n "$PM" ] || stop "no apt, dnf, pacman or zypper here: install the tools listed below by hand."
    echo "  installing: $PKGS"
    $PM $PKGS || stop "installing the packages failed (see above)."
fi

# Each check: its name, then how to see it is there.
missing_tools=0
check_tool() { if eval "$2" > /dev/null 2>&1; then ok "$1"; else todo "$1"; missing_tools=1; fi; }
check_tool "Git" "have git"
check_tool "Python 3.11 or newer, with venv" "python3 -c 'import sys, venv; sys.exit(sys.version_info < (3, 11))'"
check_tool "Clang (C/C++ compiler)" "have clang && have clang++"
check_tool "CMake 3.20 or newer" "printf '3.20\n%s\n' \"\$(cmake --version | awk 'NR==1 {print \$3}')\" | sort -V -C"
check_tool "Ninja" "have ninja || have ninja-build"
check_tool "SDL2 (development files)" "have sdl2-config || pkg-config --exists sdl2"
check_tool "Vulkan headers" "test -f /usr/include/vulkan/vulkan.h"
check_tool "glslang (development files)" "ls /usr/include/glslang/Public/ShaderLang.h"
check_tool "FFmpeg 6.1 or newer (libavcodec development files)" \
    "grep -qs AV_FRAME_FLAG_KEY /usr/include/libavutil/frame.h /usr/include/*/libavutil/frame.h /usr/include/ffmpeg/libavutil/frame.h"
check_tool "Vulkan loader (libvulkan.so.1)" "ldconfig -p | grep -q 'libvulkan.so.1 '"
if [ "$missing_tools" = 1 ]; then
    echo
    if [ -n "$PM" ]; then
        echo "Install them with:"
        echo "  $PM $PKGS"
        echo "or run: bash setup.sh --install-deps"
    else
        echo "Install them with your distribution's package manager (development packages of SDL2, Vulkan,"
        echo "glslang and FFmpeg's libavcodec, plus git, python3, clang, cmake and ninja)."
    fi
    stop "tools missing (see above)."
fi
if have vulkaninfo; then
    vulkaninfo --summary 2> /dev/null | grep -q "deviceName" && ok "a Vulkan graphics driver" ||
        echo "            ${Y}vulkaninfo found no Vulkan device: install your graphics card's Vulkan driver (Mesa for AMD/Intel, the NVIDIA driver).${N}"
fi

# ---- ps3recomp at this version's base commit, plus this version's patch (what update.ps1 does) ----------
mkdir -p "$STATE"
PATCH="$GT5/patches/ps3recomp.patch"
NEWBASE="$(tr -d '\r\n ' < "$GT5/patches/ps3recomp-base.txt")"
if [ ! -d "$RC/.git" ]; then
    # No line-ending conversion: the patch matches the files as stored upstream.
    git clone --quiet --config core.autocrlf=false https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp.git "$RC" ||
        stop "couldn't clone ps3recomp (is the internet reachable?)"
fi
OLDPATCH="$STATE/applied.patch"
OLDBASE="$(cat "$STATE/applied-base.txt" 2> /dev/null | tr -d '\r\n ')"
if [ -f "$OLDPATCH" ] && cmp -s "$OLDPATCH" "$PATCH" && [ "$OLDBASE" = "$NEWBASE" ] &&
   [ "$(git -C "$RC" rev-parse HEAD)" = "$NEWBASE" ]; then
    ok "ps3recomp, patched (already in place)"
else
    # 1. Take the old patch out, keeping anything else changed in ps3recomp (saved to backups/).
    if [ -n "$(git -C "$RC" status --porcelain)" ] && [ -f "$OLDPATCH" ] &&
       git -C "$RC" apply --whitespace=nowarn --reverse --check "$OLDPATCH" 2> /dev/null; then
        git -C "$RC" apply --whitespace=nowarn --reverse "$OLDPATCH"
    fi
    if [ -n "$(git -C "$RC" status --porcelain)" ]; then
        mkdir -p "$BASE/backups"
        own="$BASE/backups/ps3recomp-changes-$(date +%Y-%m-%d_%H%M).patch"
        git -C "$RC" add -A && git -C "$RC" diff --cached --binary > "$own" && git -C "$RC" reset --quiet
        echo "            ${Y}ps3recomp had changes besides the patch (your own edits?). Saved in backups/$(basename "$own").${N}"
    fi
    # 2. The ps3recomp commit this version's patch was made against.
    git -C "$RC" cat-file -e "$NEWBASE^{commit}" 2> /dev/null || git -C "$RC" fetch --quiet origin "$NEWBASE"
    git -C "$RC" checkout --quiet --force "$NEWBASE" || stop "couldn't check out ps3recomp $NEWBASE"
    git -C "$RC" clean -fdq
    # 3. This version's patch.
    git -C "$RC" apply --whitespace=nowarn --check "$PATCH" ||
        stop "this version's patch doesn't apply to ps3recomp $NEWBASE. Please report it."
    git -C "$RC" apply --whitespace=nowarn "$PATCH" || stop "applying the patch failed"
    cp -f "$PATCH" "$OLDPATCH"
    echo "$NEWBASE" > "$STATE/applied-base.txt"
    ok "ps3recomp, patched"
fi
if [ -d "$BASE/.git" ]; then
    { git -C "$BASE" describe --tags --exact-match HEAD 2> /dev/null ||
      echo "development build $(git -C "$BASE" describe --tags 2> /dev/null || git -C "$BASE" rev-parse --short HEAD)"; } > "$STATE/version.txt"
fi

# ---- Python environment and the tools' packages --------------------------------------------------------
if [ ! -x "$PY" ]; then
    python3 -m venv "$VENV" || stop "making the Python environment failed (Debian/Ubuntu: sudo apt install python3-venv)."
fi
"$PY" -m pip install --quiet --disable-pip-version-check -r "$RC/requirements.txt" ||
    stop "installing the Python packages failed (see above)."
ok "Python environment and packages"

# ---- Your game files -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo
echo "Your files (see Linux in README.md for where each comes from):"
mkdir -p "$GT5/input" "$GT5/vfs"
ELF="$GT5/input/EBOOT.elf"
# The game's executable is locked as it comes on the disc (EBOOT.BIN). The port's own tool unlocks it
# (scripts/ps3_unlock.py: no RPCS3): from GT5/input/EBOOT.BIN, a locked file named EBOOT.elf, or the disc
# copy's own PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN.
LOCKED=""
if [ -f "$ELF" ]; then
    if [ "$(head -c 4 "$ELF" | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')" = "53434500" ]; then LOCKED="$ELF.locked"; mv -f "$ELF" "$LOCKED"; fi
else
    for c in "$GT5/input/EBOOT.BIN" "$GT5/vfs/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN"; do
        if [ -f "$c" ]; then LOCKED="$c"; break; fi
    done
fi
if [ -n "$LOCKED" ] && [ ! -f "$ELF" ]; then
    if "$PY" -I "$GT5/scripts/ps3_unlock.py" eboot "$LOCKED" "$ELF" --keys-dir "$BASE/tools/ps3_keys" > "$BASE/unlock.log" 2>&1; then
        ok "GT5/input/EBOOT.elf: unlocked from $LOCKED"
    else
        echo "  [note]    Unlocking the game's executable ($LOCKED): $(grep '^PS3_UNLOCK_FAIL' "$BASE/unlock.log" | tail -1 | cut -d: -f2-)"
    fi
fi
if [ ! -f "$ELF" ]; then
    todo "GT5/input/EBOOT.elf (your game's executable)" "Copy your disc's PS3_GAME folder to GT5/vfs (so that GT5/vfs/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN exists) and run setup again: it unlocks the executable by itself."
else
    magic="$(head -c 4 "$ELF" | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')"
    sha1="$(sha1sum "$ELF" | cut -d' ' -f1 | tr a-f A-F)"
    if [ "$magic" != "7f454c46" ]; then
        todo "a valid GT5/input/EBOOT.elf" "This file isn't a PS3 executable. Delete it and run setup again: it is made from your disc's PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN."
    else
        case "$sha1" in
            1535B865EC7DD58E7704B378B8621532ECF844E1) ok "GT5/input/EBOOT.elf: Europe BCES00569, version 01.00 (the tested one)" ;;
            40126D2D14B0A95B9601BB11E3A6E778186067AC) ok "GT5/input/EBOOT.elf: North America BCUS98114 (players have raced on it)" ;;
            49A3662D4B541BB4E0C2E72D2602F89FEB710E71) ok "GT5/input/EBOOT.elf: Hong Kong / Asia BCAS20108, version 01.00 (tested)" ;;
            96DEA35B194AA80E993CAD9EBE42E96072F3A3D5) ok "GT5/input/EBOOT.elf: Hong Kong / Asia BCAS20108, update 2.01 (tested; needs the update's data in GT5/hdd0, README: Game updates)" ;;
            *) ok "GT5/input/EBOOT.elf (SHA-1 $sha1)"
               echo "            ${Y}Not one tried yet. Another disc version may well work: please report how it goes.${N}" ;;
        esac
    fi
fi

GAME="$GT5/vfs/PS3_GAME"
if [ -d "$GAME/USRDIR" ]; then
    if [ -f "$GAME/PARAM.SFO" ]; then
        # A dump made to a FAT32 drive splits files over 4 GB into <file>.66600, .66601, ...: join them.
        while IFS= read -r first; do
            whole="${first%.66600}"
            parts=(); i=0
            while [ -f "$(printf '%s.666%02d' "$whole" "$i")" ]; do parts+=("$(printf '%s.666%02d' "$whole" "$i")"); i=$((i + 1)); done
            echo "            joining ${whole#$GAME/} from ${#parts[@]} pieces (a few minutes)..."
            if cat "${parts[@]}" > "$whole.joining" && mv -f "$whole.joining" "$whole"; then
                rm -f "${parts[@]}"
            else
                rm -f "$whole.joining"; echo "            ${Y}couldn't join them (disk full?). Copy the whole file from your dump instead.${N}"
            fi
        done < <(find "$GAME" -type f -name '*.66600' 2> /dev/null)
        if [ -f "$GAME/USRDIR/GT.VOL" ]; then ok "GT5/vfs/PS3_GAME (your disc's game data)"
        else todo "GT5/vfs/PS3_GAME/USRDIR/GT.VOL (the game's data, about 12 GB)" "Copy it from PS3_GAME/USRDIR in your disc dump (or its pieces GT.VOL.66600, .66601, ...: they're joined automatically)."
        fi
    else
        todo "GT5/vfs/PS3_GAME/PARAM.SFO" "Copy the whole PS3_GAME folder from your disc, including PARAM.SFO."
    fi
elif [ -d "$GAME/PS3_GAME/USRDIR" ]; then
    todo "GT5/vfs/PS3_GAME at the right level" "It's one folder too deep: move the contents of GT5/vfs/PS3_GAME/PS3_GAME up into GT5/vfs/PS3_GAME."
else
    todo "GT5/vfs/PS3_GAME (your disc's game data, about 17 GB)" "Copy the PS3_GAME folder from your disc dump to GT5/vfs, so that GT5/vfs/PS3_GAME/USRDIR exists."
fi

# The PS3's system software (GT5/dev_flash) is not needed: the game never reads it.

echo
if [ "$TODO" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "${Y}$TODO thing(s) still to do (marked [missing] above). Sort them out, then run setup.sh again.${N}"
    exit 1
fi
if [ "$NOBUILD" = 1 ]; then echo "${G}Everything is in place. Run setup.sh without --no-build to build the game.${N}"; exit 0; fi

# ---- Generate the game code (only when it's missing or out of date), then build ---------------------------
cd "$GT5" || exit 1
if ! "$PY" scripts/lift_stamp.py --check > /dev/null 2>&1 || [ ! -f generated/ppu_recomp.h ]; then
    echo "Generating the game code from your EBOOT.elf (about 10 to 20 minutes)..."
    bash scripts/relift.sh ||
        stop "generating the game code failed (see above). Please report it with that output: https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/issues/new?template=2-problem.yml"
else
    echo "The game code is already generated and current."
fi

# Parallel jobs: one per core, but no more than one per 2 GB of free memory (the biggest files need that).
mem_gb=$(( $(awk '/MemAvailable/ {print $2}' /proc/meminfo) / 1048576 ))
JOBS=$(nproc); [ $((mem_gb / 2)) -lt "$JOBS" ] && JOBS=$((mem_gb / 2)); [ "$JOBS" -lt 1 ] && JOBS=1
[ -n "${GT5_JOBS:-}" ] && JOBS="$GT5_JOBS"
BUILD="$GT5/build-linux"
NINJA=ninja; have ninja || NINJA=ninja-build
if [ ! -f "$BUILD/build.ninja" ]; then
    cmake -S "$GT5/linux" -B "$BUILD" -G Ninja -DCMAKE_MAKE_PROGRAM="$(command -v $NINJA)" \
          -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++ ||
        stop "configuring the build failed (see above)."
fi
echo "Building GT5/build-linux/gt5 with $JOBS parallel jobs (the first build takes 20 to 60 minutes)..."
built=1
for try in 1 2 3 4; do
    if cmake --build "$BUILD" --target gt5 -j "$JOBS" 2>&1 | tee "$BUILD/last_build.log"; [ "${PIPESTATUS[0]}" -eq 0 ]; then
        built=0; break
    fi
    # A crashed compile (heavy parallel builds now and then) is simply redone, with fewer jobs.
    JOBS=$(( JOBS / 2 )); [ "$JOBS" -lt 1 ] && JOBS=1
    echo "${Y}The build stopped. Trying again with $JOBS parallel jobs; it carries on where it stopped...${N}"
done
[ "$built" = 0 ] || stop "the build failed (see above). Please report it with that output: https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/issues/new?template=2-problem.yml"
echo
echo "${G}Done! Play with: bash GT5/play.sh${N}"
if [ -n "${CONTAINER_ID:-}" ]; then
    # In a distrobox (the Steam Deck route): how to start it from Steam, where the Deck's controls work.
    echo "To play from Steam (Game Mode): Add a Non-Steam Game > /usr/bin/distrobox-enter, then set its"
    echo "launch options to:  -n $CONTAINER_ID -- bash \"$GT5/play.sh\""
fi

```

`update.ps1`:

```ps1
# Update this GT5 Recomp install to the newest version, or switch to any other version (older too).
# Run it in PowerShell from the folder you cloned:
#   powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1                     newest release
#   powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1 -List               list the versions
#   powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1 -Version v0.1.0     switch to that version
#   powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1 -Dev                newest changes not yet released
#   powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File update.ps1 -Test               the test build: changes still being
#                                                                           tried out, when there is one (plain
#                                                                           update.ps1 goes back to the release)
# -NoBuild switches without building (build later with GT5\scripts\build.cmd gt5); -Force re-lifts and
# rebuilds even when nothing changed. Easiest: the launcher's Updates page, or double-click Update.bat.
# (-Relaunch <exe>: the launcher's Update button; this opens it again when done.)
#
# Kept: your saves (GT5\hdd0), your game files, the shader cache, and edits you made to files such as
# play.bat (set aside during the switch and put back). The previous gt5.exe is kept as
# GT5\build\gt5.previous.exe. The slow re-lift only runs when a version changes the lift tools;
# otherwise only the changed code is rebuilt. The game is built with both renderers (Vulkan's libraries are
# fetched once, also for an install made before that), and its add-ons are built again for the new version.
# (-AfterSwitch -PrevVersion -NewLabel: used by update.ps1 itself. When the version it switched to has a different
# update.ps1, that one does the rest, so each update runs the new version's own steps.)
param([string]$Version, [switch]$List, [switch]$Dev, [switch]$Test, [switch]$NoBuild, [switch]$Force, [switch]$Here, [string]$Relaunch,
      [switch]$AfterSwitch, [string]$PrevVersion, [string]$NewLabel)
# This file as it was when it started: after the switch, a different one on disk is the new version's.
$selfHash = $null
try { $selfHash = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $PSCommandPath -Algorithm SHA256).Hash } catch {}
# Errors are checked through exit codes: with "Stop", Windows PowerShell turns git's progress messages
# on stderr into errors.
$ErrorActionPreference = "Continue"
# Another Python's settings (Anaconda, QGIS and others set these for everyone) would make the port's own Python load
# that one's libraries: not for this run or anything it starts.
Remove-Item Env:PYTHONHOME, Env:PYTHONPATH -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
# On a drive that doesn't record who owns a file (exFAT, FAT32, many USB and network drives) git refuses
# to work in the install folder ("detected dubious ownership", #41). Trust it for git run from here and
# what this starts, through git's environment config; the player's own git settings stay as they are.
if ($env:GT5_GIT_SAFE -ne "1") {
    $gn = 0; if ("$env:GIT_CONFIG_COUNT" -match '^\d+$') { $gn = [int]$env:GIT_CONFIG_COUNT }
    Set-Item "env:GIT_CONFIG_KEY_$gn" "safe.directory"; Set-Item "env:GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_$gn" "*"
    $env:GIT_CONFIG_COUNT = "$($gn + 1)"; $env:GT5_GIT_SAFE = "1"
}
$base = $PSScriptRoot
# Git: the PC's own, else the port's own portable copy in tools\git (get-git.ps1; nothing installed in Windows).
$ownGit = Join-Path $base "tools\git\cmd"
if (-not (Get-Command git -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $ownGit "git.exe"))) { $env:Path = "$ownGit;$env:Path" }
$gt5 = Join-Path $base "GT5"
$rc = Join-Path $base "ps3recomp"
$state = Join-Path $base ".gt5"
$backups = Join-Path $base "backups"
$py = Join-Path $base "venv\Scripts\python.exe"
$stamp = Get-Date -Format "yyyy-MM-dd_HHmm"
$fallbackBase = "4e8f3ca87a3e1d87bb83b8b7e9348fe2685cd514"   # versions from before ps3recomp-base.txt existed

# Started from the launcher: open it again at the end; after a failure, wait so the message can be read.
function Finish([int]$code) {
    if ($Relaunch) {
        if ($code -ne 0) { Write-Host ""; Read-Host "Press Enter to close this window" | Out-Null }
        if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Relaunch) { Start-Process -FilePath $Relaunch }
    }
    exit $code
}
function Fail([string]$m) { Write-Host "update: $m" -ForegroundColor Red; Finish 1 }
function Warn([string]$m) { Write-Host $m -ForegroundColor Yellow }
function Describe {
    if (-not (Test-Path (Join-Path $base ".git"))) { return "a downloaded copy (not a git clone)" }
    $t = git -C $base describe --tags --exact-match HEAD 2>$null
    if ($t) { return $t }
    $d = git -C $base describe --tags 2>$null
    if ($d) { return "development build $d" }
    return "development build $(git -C $base rev-parse --short HEAD)"
}
function Read-Base([string]$file) {
    if (Test-Path $file) { return (Get-Content $file -Raw).Trim() }
    return $fallbackBase
}

# -Here (setup.ps1's step) also works in a ZIP download; switching versions needs a git clone.
if (-not $Here -and -not (Test-Path (Join-Path $base ".git"))) {
    Fail "this folder isn't a git clone. Install with: git clone https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp (see README.md)"
}
if (Test-Path (Join-Path $base ".git\gt5-publish-repo")) { Fail "this is the publishing copy of the repository, not an install" }
if (-not (Test-Path (Join-Path $gt5 "scripts\relift.ps1"))) { Fail "GT5\scripts is missing: this isn't a full checkout" }
# Only this install's game matters (another copy elsewhere can keep running).
$mine = Get-Process gt5 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.Path -and $_.Path.StartsWith($base, [StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase) }
if ($mine) { Fail "close the game first" }

# ---- List the versions ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
if ($List) {
    git -C $base fetch --quiet --tags origin
    $cur = Describe
    $latest = git -C $base tag --list "v*" --sort=-v:refname | Select-Object -First 1
    Write-Host "Installed: $cur"
    Write-Host ""
    $rows = git -C $base for-each-ref "refs/tags/v*" --sort=-version:refname --format="%(refname:short)|%(creatordate:short)|%(subject)"
    if (-not $rows) { Write-Host "No releases yet: -Dev gets the newest changes." }
    foreach ($r in $rows) {
        $p = $r -split '\|', 3
        $mark = ""
        if ($p[0] -eq $latest) { $mark += "  [newest]" }
        if ($p[0] -eq $cur) { $mark += "  <- installed" }
        Write-Host ("{0,-9} {1}  {2}{3}" -f $p[0], $p[1], $p[2], $mark)
    }
    exit 0
}

$from = if ($AfterSwitch -and $PrevVersion) { $PrevVersion } else { Describe }
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $state | Out-Null

# The patch now in ps3recomp, saved before the switch replaces GT5\patches with the new version's.
$patch = Join-Path $gt5 "patches\ps3recomp.patch"
$baseFile = Join-Path $gt5 "patches\ps3recomp-base.txt"
$oldPatch = Join-Path $state "applied.patch"
$oldBase = Read-Base (Join-Path $state "applied-base.txt")
if (-not (Test-Path $oldPatch) -and (Test-Path (Join-Path $rc ".git")) -and (git -C $rc status --porcelain)) {
    # Installed before update.ps1 existed (maybe followed by a `git pull`, so this folder's patch can
    # already be newer than ps3recomp's): find which version's patch ps3recomp carries.
    $cand = Join-Path $state "pre-update.patch"
    foreach ($c in (git -C $base log --format=%H -n 40 -- GT5/patches/ps3recomp.patch)) {
        cmd /c "git -C `"$base`" show ${c}:GT5/patches/ps3recomp.patch > `"$cand`""
        git -C $rc apply --whitespace=nowarn --reverse --check $cand 2>$null
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) {
            $oldPatch = $cand
            $b = git -C $base show "${c}:GT5/patches/ps3recomp-base.txt" 2>$null
            if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0 -and $b) { $oldBase = "$b".Trim() } else { $oldBase = $fallbackBase }
            break
        }
    }
}

# ---- Switch this folder to the chosen version ---------------------------------------------------------
$label = if ($AfterSwitch -and $NewLabel) { $NewLabel } else { $from }
if (-not $Here -and -not $AfterSwitch) {
    git -C $base fetch --quiet --tags origin
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Fail "couldn't reach GitHub" }
    if ($Test) {
        # The test build: a branch of its own that releases never point at.
        git -C $base fetch --quiet origin "+refs/heads/test:refs/remotes/origin/test"
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Fail "there is no test build at the moment" }
        $target = "origin/test"; $label = "the test build"
    } elseif ($Dev) {
        $target = "origin/main"; $label = "the newest development build"
    } elseif ($Version) {
        if ($Version -notmatch '^v') { $Version = "v$Version" }
        git -C $base rev-parse -q --verify "refs/tags/$Version" | Out-Null
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Fail "there's no version $Version (see -List)" }
        $target = $Version; $label = $Version
    } else {
        $target = git -C $base tag --list "v*" --sort=-v:refname | Select-Object -First 1
        if ($target) { $label = $target } else { $target = "origin/main"; $label = "the newest development build" }
    }
    $targetCommit = git -C $base rev-parse "$target^{commit}"
    # Already on that version, but a game update was installed since the last build (the launcher's Help page, or
    # by hand): its executable is brought into GT5\input, and when the generated code no longer matches the
    # executable this run goes on to convert and build it instead of stopping at "Already on". Before, an
    # update here said "Already on ..." and the player had to know to run setup.bat.
    $staleLift = $false
    if ($targetCommit -eq (git -C $base rev-parse HEAD) -and -not $Force -and -not $NoBuild -and (Test-Path (Join-Path $state "applied.patch")) -and
        (Test-Path (Join-Path $gt5 "input\EBOOT.elf")) -and (Test-Path $py) -and (Test-Path (Join-Path $gt5 "scripts\lift_stamp.py"))) {
        if (Test-Path (Join-Path $gt5 "scripts\update_exe.ps1")) {
            & powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File (Join-Path $gt5 "scripts\update_exe.ps1") -Gt5 $gt5 *> $null
        }
        Push-Location $gt5
        & $py "scripts\lift_stamp.py" --check *> $null
        $staleLift = ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0)
        Pop-Location
    }
    if ($targetCommit -eq (git -C $base rev-parse HEAD) -and -not $Force -and -not $staleLift -and (Test-Path (Join-Path $state "applied.patch"))) {
        # Parts next to the game that an earlier updater did not know how to add (it brought this version in
        # with its own, older steps): added now, so nothing waits for the next version. Never a stop.
        $addCommonNow = Join-Path $gt5 "scripts\addon_common.ps1"
        if ((Test-Path -LiteralPath $addCommonNow) -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $gt5 "build\gt5.exe")) -and -not $Here -and -not $NoBuild) {
            . $addCommonNow
            $logsNow = Join-Path $gt5 "logs"
            if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $gt5 "build\gt5_upscale_fsr.dll"))) {
                Write-Host "Finishing up..."
                $r = Invoke-AddOn (Join-Path $gt5 "scripts\add_fsr.ps1") @() "add_fsr" $logsNow
                if ($r -eq 1) { Write-Host "  AMD FSR 3: not built this time (GT5\logs\add_fsr.log says why). The next update tries again." }
            }
            $licNow = Join-Path $state "installer-licences.txt"
            $dlssShownNow = (Test-Path -LiteralPath $licNow) -and [bool](Select-String -LiteralPath $licNow -Pattern '^dlss\b' -Quiet)
            if ($dlssShownNow -and -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $gt5 "build\gt5_upscale_dlss.dll")) -and (Test-RtxCard)) {
                $r = Invoke-AddOn (Join-Path $gt5 "scripts\add_dlss.ps1") @("-Accept") "add_dlss" $logsNow
                if ($r -eq 1) { Write-Host "  NVIDIA DLSS: not built this time (GT5\logs\add_dlss.log says why). The next update tries again." }
            }
        }
        Write-Host "Already on $label."
        Finish 0
    }
    if ($staleLift) { Write-Host "The game's executable changed (a game update was installed): converting and building the game for it." }
    elseif ($targetCommit -eq (git -C $base rev-parse HEAD)) { Write-Host "Reinstalling $label" }
    else { Write-Host "Switching from $from to $label" }

    # Edits the player made to tracked files (play.bat, say) are set aside and put back after.
    $dirty = git -C $base status --porcelain --untracked-files=no
    $stashed = $false
    if ($dirty) {
        git -C $base stash push --quiet -m "update.ps1 $stamp"
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { $stashed = $true }
    }
    if ($Dev) {
        git -C $base checkout --quiet main
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { git -C $base merge --quiet --ff-only origin/main }
    } else {
        git -C $base checkout --quiet --detach $targetCommit
    }
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        if ($stashed) { git -C $base stash pop --quiet }
        Fail "couldn't switch to $label"
    }
    if ($stashed) {
        $files = ($dirty | ForEach-Object { $_.Substring(3) }) -join ", "
        $null = git -C $base stash pop --quiet 2>&1
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) {
            Write-Host "Your edits to $files are back in place."
        } else {
            # The edits clash with this version's changes to the same lines: this version's files win,
            # and the edits are saved so nothing is lost.
            New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $backups | Out-Null
            $mine = Join-Path $backups "my-edits-$stamp.patch"
            git -C $base reset --quiet --hard HEAD
            cmd /c "git -C `"$base`" stash show -p stash@{0} > `"$mine`""
            git -C $base stash drop --quiet
            Warn "Your edits to $files clash with this version's own changes there. This version's files are in place; your edits are saved in backups\$(Split-Path $mine -Leaf) to copy back by hand."
        }
    }
    # The version switched to has its own update.ps1: when it differs from this one, it does the rest (patching
    # ps3recomp, the build, the add-ons), so a new step of an update already runs on the update that brings it.
    # Only a copy that knows -AfterSwitch: an older version's (a switch back with -Version) is left to this one.
    $now = $null
    try { $now = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $PSCommandPath -Algorithm SHA256).Hash } catch {}
    if ($selfHash -and $now -and $now -ne $selfHash -and (Select-String -LiteralPath $PSCommandPath -Pattern '\[switch\]\$AfterSwitch' -Quiet)) {
        $a = @("-NoProfile", "-ExecutionPolicy", "Bypass", "-File", $PSCommandPath, "-AfterSwitch", "-PrevVersion", $from, "-NewLabel", $label)
        if ($NoBuild) { $a += "-NoBuild" }
        if ($Force) { $a += "-Force" }
        if ($Relaunch) { $a += @("-Relaunch", $Relaunch) }
        & powershell @a
        exit $LASTEXITCODE
    }
}

# ---- ps3recomp: this version's base commit plus this version's patch -----------------------------------
$newBase = Read-Base $baseFile
if (-not (Test-Path (Join-Path $rc ".git"))) {
    # No line-ending conversion: the patch matches the files as stored upstream.
    git clone --quiet --config core.autocrlf=false https://github.com/sp00nznet/ps3recomp.git $rc
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Fail "couldn't clone ps3recomp" }
}
$same = (Test-Path $oldPatch) -and (Test-Path $patch) -and
        ((Get-FileHash $oldPatch).Hash -eq (Get-FileHash $patch).Hash) -and ($oldBase -eq $newBase) -and
        ((git -C $rc rev-parse HEAD) -eq $newBase)
if ($same) {
    Write-Host "ps3recomp: this version's patch is already in place"
} else {
    # 0. Every file either patch touches, with its content hash and timestamp now. Taking the old patch out
    #    and putting the new one in rewrites all of them, shared headers included, so the build saw them
    #    all as changed and recompiled every file of the game's generated code (20 to 50 minutes) even
    #    when an update changed a few runtime files. Below, the ones whose content comes out the same get
    #    their old timestamps back.
    $kept = @{}
    foreach ($pf in @($oldPatch, $patch)) {
        if (-not (Test-Path $pf)) { continue }
        foreach ($m in (Select-String -LiteralPath $pf -Pattern '^diff --git a/(\S+) b/')) {
            $rel = $m.Matches[0].Groups[1].Value
            $full = Join-Path $rc $rel
            if ($kept.ContainsKey($rel) -or -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $full -PathType Leaf)) { continue }
            $kept[$rel] = @((Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $full -Algorithm SHA1).Hash, (Get-Item -LiteralPath $full).LastWriteTimeUtc)
        }
    }
    # 1. Take the old patch out, keeping anything else changed in ps3recomp.
    $changes = git -C $rc status --porcelain
    if ($changes -and (Test-Path $oldPatch)) {
        git -C $rc apply --whitespace=nowarn --reverse --check $oldPatch 2>$null
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) {
            git -C $rc apply --whitespace=nowarn --reverse $oldPatch
            $changes = git -C $rc status --porcelain
        }
    }
    if ($changes) {
        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $backups | Out-Null
        $own = Join-Path $backups "ps3recomp-changes-$stamp.patch"
        git -C $rc add -A
        cmd /c "git -C `"$rc`" diff --cached --binary > `"$own`""
        git -C $rc reset --quiet
        Warn "ps3recomp had changes besides the old patch (your own edits?). They're saved in backups\$(Split-Path $own -Leaf)."
    }
    # 2. The ps3recomp commit this version's patch was made against.
    git -C $rc cat-file -e "$newBase^{commit}" 2>$null
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { git -C $rc fetch --quiet origin $newBase }
    git -C $rc checkout --quiet --force $newBase
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Fail "couldn't check out ps3recomp $newBase" }
    git -C $rc clean -fdq
    # 3. This version's patch.
    git -C $rc apply --whitespace=nowarn --check $patch
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Fail "this version's patch doesn't apply to ps3recomp $newBase. Please report it." }
    git -C $rc apply --whitespace=nowarn $patch
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Fail "applying the patch failed" }
    # 4. Files whose content is what it was before get their timestamps back (step 0), so only what this
    #    version really changed is recompiled.
    $unchanged = 0
    foreach ($rel in $kept.Keys) {
        $full = Join-Path $rc $rel
        if ((Test-Path -LiteralPath $full -PathType Leaf) -and
            (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $full -Algorithm SHA1).Hash -eq $kept[$rel][0]) {
            try { (Get-Item -LiteralPath $full).LastWriteTimeUtc = $kept[$rel][1]; $unchanged++ } catch { }
        }
    }
    Write-Host "ps3recomp: $($kept.Count - $unchanged) patched file(s) changed in this version, $unchanged unchanged"
    Copy-Item $patch (Join-Path $state "applied.patch") -Force
    Set-Content -Path (Join-Path $state "applied-base.txt") -Value $newBase -Encoding ascii
    Remove-Item (Join-Path $state "pre-update.patch") -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    Write-Host "ps3recomp: patched for $label"
}
Set-Content -Path (Join-Path $state "version.txt") -Value (Describe) -Encoding ascii
if (Test-Path $py) {
    # The versions the tools are tested with, as setup.ps1 pins them (nothing is fetched when they are in place).
    $pins = @("capstone==5.0.9", "construct==2.10.70", "pycryptodome==4.2.0", "tabulate==0.10.0", "tqdm==4.70.1")
    & $py -m pip install --quiet --disable-pip-version-check -r (Join-Path $rc "requirements.txt") @pins
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Warn "The Python packages couldn't be brought to this version's (see above): the tools run with the ones in place." }
}

if ($Here -or $NoBuild) {
    if (-not $Here) { Write-Host "Switched to $label. Build with GT5\scripts\build.cmd gt5 (or run update.ps1 -Force) when you're ready." }
    exit 0
}
if (-not (Test-Path (Join-Path $gt5 "input\EBOOT.elf")) -or -not (Test-Path $py)) {
    Write-Host "Switched to $label. Setup isn't finished (no GT5\input\EBOOT.elf or no venv), so nothing was built: see Setup in README.md."
    exit 0
}

# ---- A game update installed in GT5\hdd0 needs its executable in GT5\input (scripts\update_exe.ps1) -------
if (Test-Path (Join-Path $gt5 "scripts\update_exe.ps1")) {
    & powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File (Join-Path $gt5 "scripts\update_exe.ps1") -Gt5 $gt5
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 2) { Warn "The game update in GT5\hdd0 still needs its executable (see above): until then the game stops before the main menu." }
}

# ---- Re-lift only when this version changes what the generated code is made from, then build --------------
# Processors that calculate wrongly are left out of everything from here on (pc-check.ps1 says why).
$pcCheck = Join-Path $base "pc-check.ps1"
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $pcCheck) {
    . $pcCheck
    $pcNote = Use-GoodProcessors -Base $base -Py $py
    if ($pcNote) { Write-Host $pcNote -ForegroundColor Yellow }
}
Push-Location $gt5
& $py "scripts\lift_stamp.py" --check
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or $Force) {
    Write-Host "Re-lifting (about 10 minutes): this version changes the lift tools, mods or your EBOOT."
    & powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "scripts\relift.ps1"
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        # A step that stops inside Python itself: the processors are checked again with one of the lift's
        # own jobs, any that calculates wrongly is left out, and the lift starts again.
        if (Get-Command Use-GoodProcessors -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
            $pcNote = Use-GoodProcessors -Base $base -Py $py -Again
            if ($pcNote) { Write-Host $pcNote -ForegroundColor Yellow }
        }
        Write-Host "The re-lift stopped (see above). Trying once more from the start..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
        & powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "scripts\relift.ps1"
    }
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Pop-Location; Fail "the re-lift failed twice (see the messages above)" }
} else {
    # The runtime's HLE function list can change with any version.
    & $py "..\ps3recomp\tools\gen_hle_nids.py" --all --out "src\gen\ppu_hle_nids.cpp"
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Pop-Location; Fail "gen_hle_nids.py failed" }
}
if (Test-Path "build\gt5.exe") { Copy-Item "build\gt5.exe" "build\gt5.previous.exe" -Force }
# The parts the game is built with or gets next to it (GT5\scripts\add_*.ps1, through addon_common.ps1: their
# whole text goes to GT5\logs, their progress lines GT5_ADD ... are passed on). None of them can fail the update.
$addCommon = Join-Path $gt5 "scripts\addon_common.ps1"
$addOns = Test-Path -LiteralPath $addCommon
if ($addOns) { . $addCommon }
$logs = Join-Path $gt5 "logs"
$cacheFile = Join-Path $gt5 "build\CMakeCache.txt"
function Test-VulkanInBuild { return (Test-Path -LiteralPath $cacheFile) -and [bool](Select-String -LiteralPath $cacheFile -Pattern '^PS3RECOMP_RSX_VULKAN:BOOL=ON' -Quiet) }
# FFmpeg (the game's movies) when an earlier setup or update couldn't get it: optional, never a stop. When it arrives,
# get-ffmpeg.ps1 has the build folder configure again so the runtime is built with it.
$getFf = Join-Path $base "get-ffmpeg.ps1"
if ((Test-Path -LiteralPath $getFf) -and -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $base "ffmpeg\ffmpeg-n9.0-latest-win64-lgpl-shared-9.0\bin\avcodec-63.dll"))) {
    & powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $getFf
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Write-Host "  FFmpeg: not added this time, so the game's movies won't play. The next update tries again." }
}
# Vulkan, the second renderer, in this build: an install made before it was built in gets its two libraries
# now (once, a few minutes), and this build adds it to the runtime.
if ($addOns) {
    $r = Invoke-AddOn (Join-Path $gt5 "scripts\add_vulkan.ps1") @("-Prepare") "add_vulkan" $logs
    if ($r -eq 1) { Write-Host "  Vulkan: left out this time (DirectX 12 only; GT5\logs\add_vulkan.log says why). The next update tries again." }
}
Write-Host "Building (only what changed)..."
cmd /c "scripts\build.cmd gt5"
$built = $LASTEXITCODE
if ($built -ne 0 -and $addOns -and (Test-VulkanInBuild)) {
    # The game must build even when Vulkan doesn't: once more without it (only the runtime is rebuilt).
    Write-Host "The build stopped. Building once more without Vulkan..."
    $null = Invoke-AddOn (Join-Path $gt5 "scripts\add_vulkan.ps1") @("-Remove", "-Prepare") "add_vulkan-off" $logs
    cmd /c "scripts\build.cmd gt5"
    $built = $LASTEXITCODE
    if ($built -eq 0) { Write-Host "  Vulkan: left out this time (the build with it stopped; GT5\logs says why). The next update tries again." }
}
Pop-Location
if ($built -ne 0) { Fail "the build failed (see the messages above). The previous game is in GT5\build\gt5.previous.exe." }
# The add-ons follow the game: their small plug-ins are built for one version of it, so they are built again
# now. AMD FSR 3, which needs no agreement, always (added when it is missing); NVIDIA DLSS on an NVIDIA RTX card
# when it is there or the installer showed its licence by the Install button (.gt5\installer-licences.txt).
if ($addOns) {
    Write-Host "Finishing up..."
    $r = Invoke-AddOn (Join-Path $gt5 "scripts\add_fsr.ps1") @() "add_fsr" $logs
    if ($r -eq 1) { Write-Host "  AMD FSR 3: not built this time (GT5\logs\add_fsr.log says why). The next update tries again." }
    $licFile = Join-Path $state "installer-licences.txt"
    $dlssShown = (Test-Path -LiteralPath $licFile) -and [bool](Select-String -LiteralPath $licFile -Pattern '^dlss\b' -Quiet)
    $dlssThere = Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $gt5 "build\gt5_upscale_dlss.dll")
    if (($dlssShown -or $dlssThere) -and (Test-RtxCard)) {
        $r = Invoke-AddOn (Join-Path $gt5 "scripts\add_dlss.ps1") @("-Accept") "add_dlss" $logs
        if ($r -eq 1) { Write-Host "  NVIDIA DLSS: not built this time (GT5\logs\add_dlss.log says why). The next update tries again." }
    }
}
# The shaders: everything this PC's game has drawn is made again with the new version, on every processor, before
# the game starts (gt5.exe --prepare-shaders; its "GT5_SHADERS done total" lines are the progress, its words go to
# GT5\logs\prepare.log). Never a stop: a shader not made here is made when first drawn, as before.
$gt5exe = Join-Path $gt5 "build\gt5.exe"
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $gt5exe) {
    Write-Host "Preparing shaders..."
    $p = Start-Process -FilePath $gt5exe -ArgumentList "--prepare-shaders" -WorkingDirectory $gt5 -NoNewWindow -Wait -PassThru -RedirectStandardError (Join-Path $logs "prepare.log")
    if ($p.ExitCode -ne 0) { Write-Host "  Shaders: not all made this time (GT5\logs\prepare.log says why). The game makes the rest as it needs them." }
}
Write-Host ""
Write-Host "Done: $from -> $label. Saves, game files, settings and the shader cache were kept." -ForegroundColor Green
Write-Host "The previous build is GT5\build\gt5.previous.exe; to go back, run update.ps1 -Version <version> (see -List)."
if ($Relaunch) { Write-Host "Opening the launcher again..."; Start-Sleep -Seconds 2 }
Finish 0

```
